Peasant families linked to the League of Poor Peasants (LCP) occupied an area of the Santa Carmem farm, in the Nova Mutum region, district of Porto Velho, Rondônia, in January 2021, and built Camp Ademar Ferreira, named after one of the two peasants killed in Nova Mamoré in 2018. The locality is adjacent to the areas Tiago dos Santos and Dois Amigos. In August, a massacre victimized three camp peasants.
(Photo: LCP)
On July 13, according to reports presented by the League of Poor Peasants, the National Force, the PM of Rondônia and gunmen would have plagued the families of the camp Ademar Ferreira. The campers had put up roadblocks to prevent the arrival of three National Force vehicles, one of the PM and three of gunmen, who, when they saw the peasants filming them, made at least fifteen shots at them, using heavy weapons such as rifles, rifles and shotguns.
The police action of the National Force was carried out with the support of the Bolsonaro government, which had repeatedly condemned the action of peasant organizations in Rondônia in the fight for land. The LCP also pointed out the joint action of police forces with paramilitary groups, which present themselves as private security companies.
On August 5, once again, the federal and state police forces, together with gunmen, attacked the peasants of Camp Ademar Ferreira. According to LCP's report, the police shot drones, torched sheds and flew helicopter over the region.
On August 13, according to information, at least three peasants were murdered by the Special Operations Battalion (BOPE) of the PM of Rondônia and the National Security Force. Amarildo Aparecido Rodrigues, 49 years old, Amaral José Stoco Rodrigues, 17 years old and son of Amarildo, and Kevin Fernando Holanda de Souza, 21 years old. Kevin was murdered while trying to escape his tormentors who chased him and shot him out of the helicopter. The rifle shells fired by policemen crossed the peasant's body and motorcycle. Left his wife pregnant. Amarildo was married and, besides Amaral's father, he was the father of a small child. Amaral, 17 years old, was completing high school, besides working in the country.
There are still reports of five missing persons hiding in the woods so they don't get shot, and we don't know if they're alive. One of the people who ran away had a strong allergic reaction to the ant bite that attacked her when she got caught in the woods to get away from shooting. Five peasants were arrested in this action. The police still destroyed the community kitchen of the camp, including food, and several of the peasants' personal belongings.
According to the CCL report, the bodies were removed without forensics at the crime scene. State Public Security Secretary José Cysneiros Pachá initially stated that there was a confrontation, which was denied by the League. Then he stated that the police forces were serving a warrant for reinstatement, information that according to LCP does not support itself because there is no warrant issued.

On April 14, 2013, according to Funai, a conflict with firearms between Yanomami tribes left 05 indigenous people dead and 07 injured. The indigenous peoples of the Alto Alegre region (RR), told Funai at the time, that they were being armed by prospectors in exchange for permissions for illegal gold exploitation in the indigenous land, which would be invaded by at least 1,600 men.
For João Catalano, head of Funai's yanomami protection sector at the time, the conflict was 'serious' because it involved a newly contacted group. "The prospectors gradually arrive and introduce weapons and ammunition to impose the pace of gold exploration," he said.
According to Dário Kopenawa, vice president of the Yanomami Association, the conflict was motivated by dispute of pupou ( palm fruit). For him, the conflict is the result of a lack of supervision over illegal mining. In the previous year, the Federal Police withdrew about 600 prospectors from the region, but many returned. 'The prospectors are enticing Indians with firearms to kill all the Indians. The PF knows that,' he said at the time.
e3f1126ed0e9e3a2818e2d6c32f6e10ba49b595e:
On August 1, 1993, what became known as the Haximu Massacre occurs. This massacre is the result of tensions related to the gold rush since 1987 in Brazil, which include conflicts between Brazilian prospectors and the Yanomami people. The name of the village became known worldwide after the bloody massacre that victimized 5 children and 5 adults, among women and elderly of Haximu, caught by surprise at the beginning of a morning by a group of heavily armed prospectors.
The massacre took place in one of the gardens on the outskirts of the village Haximu-teri in the north of the state of Roraima. Haximu is the name of a Yanomami community on the border between Brazil and Venezuela, near the Demini River. It was Brazil's first and only crime to be tried as a genocide. There's a mismatch in the number of deaths between different sources. CPT registered 10 dead in this massacre.
In 1997, prospector Pedro Emiliano Garcia and four other defendants were sentenced to 20 years in prison for genocide by the Yanomami people. This was the first genocide sentence in Brazil. However, in 2011, the sentence was deemed extinct and all defendants were released

Yanomani Indians clash with 150 prospectors camped in the mountains of Couto Magalhães. The prospectors killed seven Indians and injured 47. The group was armed with rifles. The massacre of the Pineapple River took place on August 9, 2020, as a result of a conflict that began days earlier. The area of the massacre covers the region of the Pineapple River and the Coata-Larajal Indigenous Land, in the municipalities of Nova Olinda do Norte and Borba, state of Amazonas. After the police action, the death of three riverside people on the 9th was confirmed, and a Munduruku indigenous man was murdered two days earlier. The CPT then considers six deaths in this massacre. The deaths occurred due to the unfolding of police action initiated by the attempt of the executive secretary of the Social Promotion Fund of the Government of Amazonas, Saulo Moysés Rezende Costa, conduct sports fishing in the pineapple river, in an area inhabited by the indigenous people Maraguá, on July 24 of the same year. As a result of the conflict, besides two indigenous Munduruku and four dead riversidemen, one missing and six injured were also confirmed.
(photo: CNS)

In June 1985, 17 pawns were murdered at the Surubim Farm, in the town known as Barreiro, in the municipality of Xinguara, in the state of Pará. There were gunmen on the farm, including the 3 Guedes brothers, according to information from residents of the region. There's a chance that the Guedes were the contractors of the overthrows and also acted as gunmen.
A possum named Leonidas, who lived in an area next to Surubim, walking through a forest on the farm, came across the bodies of the 17 people. By learning of this crime, this worker was captured by gunmen and imprisoned in a shack to prevent any kind of complaint about what happened.
During his time in prison, Leonidas witnessed the murder of a 3-year-old child whose father was among the 17 dead. Since then, the child was in the possession of the gunmen, who constantly threatened her. One day, the squatter saw the threats come true. When the gunman told the boy that he would really kill him, the little man asked for his "pee" (the pacifier). Right after that, he was shot to death. After a time in prison, the squatter was released and returned to his land.

On March 24, 2019, three charred bodies were found on a farm located in the vicinity of the Martins vicinal, in the rural area of Baião, in southeastern Pará. The farm is 14 kilometers from the Salvador Allende settlement, where the first 2019 massacre took place on March 22nd. The victims were Marlete da Silva Oliveira and Raimundo de Jesus Ferreira, homeowners of the farm, and Venilson Da Silva Santos, tractorist of the property.
After the two massacres, a Civil Police task force was assembled, under the command of General Delegate Alberto Teixeira, from the order of the governor of the State, Helder Barbalho. As soon as the two witnesses were heard about the case, the civil police initiated Operation Fire, which served, at the beginning of the night of March 26, a temporary arrest warrant for the main suspect, Fernando Ferreira Rosa Filho, known as “Fernandinho”, who would be the boss of the two massacres. Fernandinho is accused of several crimes in the Southeast region of Pará, such as: involvement with drug trafficking, loan sharking, reception, bank robbery, murder and attempted murder, and land grabbing.
In the case of this massacre, according to the witnesses, the three employees of Fernandinho's farm were not satisfied that they did not have their labor rights respected, which could be claimed judicially. There is also the complaint that the accused would be building a clandestine airstrip for aircraft of drug traffickers, on the stage of the second massacre, and so perhaps he did not want to be disturbed by anyone, let alone by neighbors linked to social movements and dissatisfied officials.
The police also confirmed that the sender had direct contact with the executioners before, during and after the crimes. They would be four brothers: Marlon Alves, Cosme Francisco Alves, Alan Alves and Glaucimar Francisco Alves. Against Glaucimar there was already an open warrant for preventive arrest since 2015, issued by the County of Tucuruí, for murder. Marlon, on the other hand, is a fugitive from the prison system for criminal prosecution, also for murder. So far only the accused of being the boss of the two massacres, Fernandinho, has been arrested.
(Image: Gazette of Pará)

At the beginning of the night of March 26, 2019, the Civil Police arrested the main suspect, Fernando Ferreira Rosa Filho, known as “Fernandinho”, who would be the boss of the massacre. Still according to the police and according to the statements collected, Fernandinho did not like the “neighbourhood” and the fact that part of the settlement was in lands that he said were his. This would have motivated the order to assassinate Dilma, her husband and their friend.
There is also the complaint that the accused would be building a clandestine airstrip for aircraft of drug traffickers, on the stage of the second massacre, and so perhaps he did not want to be disturbed by anyone, let alone by neighbors linked to social movements and dissatisfied officials.

Area History
The old Piratininga Farm, today Salvador Alende Settlement, has a long history of conflicts. The site was occupied 12 years ago by more than 400 landless families. Since then, until it became a settlement, there were several attacks by gunmen and conflicts with loggers.
In 2007, approximately 480 families linked to the Landless Rural Workers Movement (MST) occupied the Farm Piratininga, located in the kilometer 50 of BR-422, known as Transcametá, in the municipality of Baião, Pará. The name given to the camp was Salvador Alende. Renato Lima was the purported owner of the area.
Also that year, on August 6, a group of four heavily armed men went to the camp and fired several shots - no one was injured. The gunmen were in a truck and on a motorcycle.
Days later, the families were victims of a second attack. A group of about 15 armed men arrived at the camp, fired several shots at the site, and physically assaulted men, women, youth and children. Some people even had broken arms and legs, others fled the attack and sheltered in a forest.
After this intense attack, the families were forced to leave the farm, and camped at the headquarters of the National Institute of Colonization of Agrarian Reform (INCRA) in Tucuruí. Some time later, the campers returned to the farm, even circulating rumors in the region that a group of gunmen were preparing for a new attack on families.
Already in 2009, in the month of November, the MST of Pará, during the Day of Struggle for Agrarian Reform, occupied the INCRA of Tucuruí to denounce the agrarian conflicts in the region and press the public agencies so that farms, such as Piratininga, would be inappropriate for the purposes of agrarian reform. According to the movement, the lands of the Piratininga Farm were, in fact, of the Union and had been grilled. About 220 workers participated in the action.
During this act, the movement also denounced the conflict between the squatters and loggers, who deforested the reserve areas, threatened and tried to expel families from those locations.
In 2010, in May, about 1,300 families from various areas occupied the INCRA headquarters in the municipality of Marabá, and the agenda of claims was not very different from the previous year. The families of Camp Salvador Allende denounced the violence by loggers, and that no authority manifested itself to solve the problem.
In 2011, about 50 families of the occupation in the Piratininga Farm camped in the Square of the Mogno, in Tucuruí, to claim the settlement in the area. That same year, the landless families, accompanied by the Federation of Workers in Family Agriculture (FETRAF/PA) and the MST, suffered a reintegration of ownership. However, after leaving the families, INCRA started measuring the lots. Some time later the camp became Salvador Allende settlement.
(Image: MAB)

On May 24, 2017, ten rural workers without land (nine men and one woman) were killed in an action by Milita Police (PM) and the Civil Police of the state of Pará, supposedly organized to serve arrest warrants against occupants of Santa Lucia Farm / Camp New Life. The operation was conducted by the Police Department of Agricultural Conflicts (DECA), with the support of the police contingent Redemption, Conceição do Araguaia and Xinguara. 15 police officers (13 military and 2 civilians) were arrested in September 2017, but were released by decision at the Court of Justice of the State of Pará (TJE-PA) on December 18, 2017.
Already on January 16, 2018, the president of the Supreme Court (STF), Minister Carmen Lucia, denied injunction of habeas corpus required by the defense of civil and military police. Carmen stated, in his decision, that “the decision of the President of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), Minister Laurita Vaz, who restored the arrest [in December 2017] is in accordance with the case law of the Supreme Court in the sense that the danger of the agent, evidenced by the risk of delitive reiteration, is an appropriate reason for the precautionary custody”.

On July 9, 2001, two gunmen shot the unionist José Pinheiro Lima, his wife Cleonice Campos Lima and the son of the couple Samuel Campos Lima. The crime occurred at the family residence in Morada Nova (PA). José was the director of the Marabá Rural Workers Union (STR) and two years ago accompanied the families camped on the São Raimundo farm. In 1999, the survey had declared the occupied land unproductive and had a decree of expropriation signed in January 2001, but the families had not been settled and the owner had not conformed to the expropriation, maintaining the conflict with the occupants.
Arrested preventively at the time of the crime and then released, the farmers denounced and recognized as rulers, who already threatened death the trade unionist, were tried and acquitted in 2016 by the justice of Marabá. The massacre became known as “Chacina de Morada Nova”.

After occupation of the São Francisco farm, of 3,500 hectares, by about 200 families, in Eldorado dos Carajás, on 21/08/1996, gunmen invaded the area and kidnapped four squatters, who were tied up, questioned and tortured at the farm headquarters. Three were shot in the head a few kilometers from there: Manoel Soares de Souza, Sebastião Paulo de Miranda and Manoel de Jesus Gonçalves. The other squatter pretended to be dead to survive, then fled and denounced what happened.
Months later, on January 4, 1997, two other squatters were killed with more than 20 shots. A third, who survived, reported it to the police. The survivors remained hidden and threatened with death. Even without convictions and with the delay in criminal investigations, the Ministry of Land Policy and Agrarian Reform directed the expropriation of the farm for being unproductive. INCRA reported that 70 families occupy the area.

The largest and best known massacre recorded in the struggle for land, the case of Eldorado dos Carajás refers to the murder of nineteen landless people killed by the Military Police of the State of Pará on April 17, 1996. The massacre occurred when 1500 landless camped in the region carried out a march obstructing the BR-155 in protest against the delay of land reform on site. Under the approval of the State Public Security Secretary (Paulo Sette Câmara), the colonel responsible for the operation (Mário Colares Pantoja) undertook acts of repression and violence that culminated in the deaths at close range and by cuts.
Despite the great national repercussions, the investigation did not arrest or identify the officers who fired. Propina would have been paid by farmers in the region, especially the owner of the Macaxeira farm, so the police would kill the landless leaders.

UPDATE 30/01/2019
The 1985 massacre boss in Pará is arrested during demonstrations of farmers against the arrest of the chiefs of the armed militia in the paraense camp
Governor Helder Barbalho sent a plane to Marabá (PA), on 24 January, to arrest the farmer convicted of the slaughter of Ubá Farm, 1985. José Edmundo Ortiz Vergolino is 82 years old and was sentenced to 152 years of imprisonment in 2017 for the murder of seven rural workers occupying the Ubá Farm in São João do Araguaia.
(With information from the site Zedudu and the team of the CPT of Marabá)
On the day that dozens of ranchers in the region made a demonstration in Marabá charging the state more rigorously against the occupations of rural properties, at the time of the arrest of José Iran dos Santos Lucena, his son Matheus da Silva Lucena and Hamilton Silva Ribeiro, for integrating the largest armed militia with activity in the countryside in the southeast of Pará, farmer José Edmundo Ortiz Vergolino, sentenced to more than 152 years in prison for the massacre of the Farm Ubah, he was arrested in his residence. The crime for which he was convicted occurred in 1985.
The arrest of José Vergolino occurred around 9 a.m. on January 24, in his residence in Marabá Pioneera. The delegate Marcelo Delgado, who arrived at the site around 6 a.m., was attended by the cattleman himself and gave a prison voice to the elderly, who did not outline any kind of reaction. He was taken to the Civil Police Superintendence, in Folha 30, New Marabá, where he testified. At about 5:00 p.m. he was taken to the Legal Medical Institute (IML), where he underwent a body crime examination. Then, already at night, it was taken to Marabá Airport, where a plane from the Air Safety Group Public awaited him, with police officers who made his escort to Bethlehem.
On the occasion, the farmer's lawyer, Gilberson dos Santos Santis, reported that he would join this Friday, 25, with a habeas corpus at the State Court of Justice asking for house or hospital arrest, due to health problems: urinary retention, osteoporosis and high pressure, for example. According to the lawyer, the arrest warrant against his client had been issued in 2017, but he had no knowledge and has only now been served.
Understand the case
José Vergolino, son of José Mendonça Vergolino, mayor of Marabá in the 1960s, is accused of being responsible for the execution, according to data from the Documentation Center of the CPT, of seven rural workers - one of the victims being a pregnant teenager - occupants of the Ubá Farm in 1985 in São João do Araguaia. He was tried and convicted by the Court of Justice of Pará and the International Court of Human Rights (ICHR), which also condemned Brazil and Pará for the episode. The rancher served time in 2006 at the Mariano Antunes Agricultural Recovery Center (Crama) in Marabá, but had granted house arrest. In 2007, the Reunited Criminal Chambers granted him provisional release. In 2010, an agreement was signed between the relatives of the victims, the Brazilian State and Pará on the case in the IACHR. But only in 2017 was a new arrest warrant issued by the 2nd Court of the Capital Jury.

On 28 September 2023, the 3rd Criminal Chamber of the Court of Cassation of Turkey upheld the sentences against four human rights defenders Osman Kavala, Çiğdem Mater, Mine Özerden and Tayfun Kahraman, and political activist Can Atalay while overturning the sentences of the remaining three defenders Mücella Yapıcı, Hakan Altınay and Yiğit Ekmekci on the Gezi Park case.
On 22 January 2021, the 3rd Penal Chamber of Istanbul Regional Appeals Court unanimously overturned the acquittals of the nine human rights defenders in the Gezi Park Trial. The case will be sent back to Istanbul 30th Heavy Penal Court for retrial.
On 18 February 2020, during the sixth and final hearing in the Gezi Park Trial, the 30th Heavy Penal Court in Istanbul acquitted nine human rights defenders, Osman Kavala, Mücella Yapıcı, Yiğit Aksakoğlu, Çiğdem Mater Utku, Ali Hakan Altınay, Mine Özerden, Şerafettin Can Atalay, Tayfun Kahraman and Yiğit Ali Ekmekçi.
On 16 July 2019 an access block was imposed on the “geziyisavunuyoruz.org” (“We Defend Gezi” in English) website, that was created to inform the public about the ongoing Gezi trial and contained photographs and videos of the Gezi protests, a summary of the indictment, court statements by defendants, illustrations from inside the courtroom, as well as a schedule of buses to the courthouse.
The second hearing in the trial of 16 human rights defenders who are accused of financing and organising the Gezi Park protests in 2013 in an “attempt to overthrow the government” was held on 18 July 2019 in Istanbul. If convicted, the HRDs face a possible sentence of life in prison without parole.

Front Line Defenders is deeply concerned by the arrest of human rights defender Arul Arumugam by the Tamil Nadu police on 4 November 2023, as well as his continued incarceration under multiple First Information Reports (FIRs) and preventive detention under the regressive Goonda's Act in Tamil Nadu. The human rights defender and 20 farmers/community leaders were arrested in connection with their involvement in a peaceful protest against the forcible acquisition of land by the State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu (SIPCOT) in the Tiruvannamalai district of Tamil Nadu. Arul Arumugam is currently being held in the Palayamkottai Central Prison, Tamil Nadu.
Arul Arumugam is a human rights defender from Tamil Nadu State and a vocal advocate on the rights of farmers and local communities impacted by develoment related displacement - especially the violation of rights to land and livelihood. Since 2 July 2023, local farmers have been engaged in a peaceful protest against the acquisition of 3,174 acres of wetlands by SIPCOT for an industrial park. The land to be acquired by SIPCOT stretches over nine agricultural villages, meaning its dispossession could severely impact the livelihood of the farmers who use the land for crop cultivation. Instead of engaging in a meaningful dialogue with the farmers regarding their concerns, the government of Tamil Nadu has responded with a crackdown on their peaceful protest and the criminalisaton of human rights defenders and leaders associated with it.
On 4 November 2023, at around 1am, the Tamil Nadu police arrested 21 farmers, including human rights defender Arul Arumugam. The farmers had been voicing their opposition to the acquisition of land by SIPCOT. The human rights defender and assembly of farmers were arrested under the FIR 324/23 file at Anakkavoor Police station which includes offences related to obstructing a public servant from discharging their functions, disturbing public order, preventing people from voluntarily selling land to the government, and damaging public assets. The FIR was filed on 29 August 2023 when human rights defender Arul Arumugam and farmers were walking together to attend a public hearing organized by the Tiruvannamalai district administration. They were obstructed by the police en route to the hearing and were charged with unlawful assembly and other related offences. Multiple FIRs have been filed against the farmers and Arul Arumugam between July and September 2023.
On 14 November 2023, senior civil society activists wrote to the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu demanding the immediate release of the arrested farmers and leaders of the protest.
In a disturbing development, on 15 November 2023, police invoked the Goonda's Act 1982 against seven of those arrested, including human rights defender Arul Arumugam. The Tamil Nadu Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Goonda's, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Forest Offenders, Sand Offenders, Slum-Grabbers and Video Pirates Act, 1982 - commonly referred to as the Goondas Act - is a draconian preventive law which makes it difficult to obtain bail court through detention. While charges under the Goonda's Act were subsequently withdrawn against six of the farmers, human rights defender Arul Arumugam continues to be detained under the regressive preventive detention law.
On 20 November 2023, the 20 farmers and leaders arrested in the context of the protest movement were granted conditional bail by the Tiruvannamalai District Court. There is concern that the arrest, multiple charges, and invoking of the preventive detention law were aimed at pressuring the farmers to stop their protest and silence those speaking out peacefully against rights violations in the area. A complaint filed to the National Human Rights Commission of India regarding the wrongful arrests and continued incarceration of human rights defender Arul Arumugam was dismissed by the Commission on 30 November 2023, directing the Superintendent of Police of Tiruvannamalai district to take appropriate action.
Front Line Defenders strongly condemns the repression of the peaceful protests by farmers in Tamil Nadu and the continued incarceration of human rights defender Arul Arumugam in reprisal for his peaceful and legitimate human rights work. We call upon the authorities in India to immediately release Arul Arumugam and quash the fabricated charges against him and the 20 other leaders of the protest.
179b20dde558277aa6d2d61f7e714899dcd70e06: Crew Against Torture is an informal union of human rights lawyers engaged in investigation of torture and inhumane treatment in the Russian Federation. Crew against Torture emerged after the shutdown of the Committee against Torture, as the lawyers who used to work for the Committee against Torture decided to continue their work without forming any legal entity. Crew against Torture carried the legacy of the Committee against Torture, and provides assistance to torture survivors and conducts independent investigation of torture cases. In addition, Crew against Torture publishes reports on systemic problems regarding the ineffectiveness of official investigations and prosecution of torture in Russia. Crew against Torture addresses human rights violations relying mostly upon legal mechanisms available at the national level. Crew against Torture promotes protection in various regions of Russia. As of 2022, Crew against Torture operates in six regions: Nizhny Novgorod region, Orenburg region, the North Caucasus, Moscow, Saint Petersburg and Krasnodar region.

5568a8d8e00a5bfa81e2b3b444cf6579883a3fad: Complaint requesting the investigation of the circumstances of the 20-year-old death of Crista Jamamadi for negligence in the care of the health team present in the area: “This is a request/denunciation whose purpose is to request the investigation of the circumstances of the death of Crista Jamamadi, indigenous of the Jamamadi ethnic group of the Middle Purus region, Amazonas. Crista Jamamadi, who at the time of his death was about 20 years old, was at the beginning of the pregnancy of his second son. Because of a small accident, she slipped and fell, Crista suffered pain in the abdomen region. At the time of their fall, the nurse was at the pole (in general, the teams that attend the Jamamadi are composed only of 1 nurse and 1 nursing technician), and refused to attend her at the site, even with the requests of the relatives. Crista ended up being medicated by the Indigenous Health Agent of the village where she lived, Embaúba (about 30 minutes of walking from the central center of São Francisco, located in the largest village of this people), which gave her, by indication of the nurse, omeprazole. Despite the structure of the pole, opened in 2014, rare are the times when there is a doctor composing the teams that enter the area. Anyway, the medication (which was for stomach pain) was not effective and pain persisted. The next day, the nurse attended her, but did not pay much attention to her picture, even though she was sick. Crista's relatives requested removal because they knew that the fall caused an abortion and that was the cause of pain. In the subsequent days, the nurse refused to serve her, simply delivering the medicines she thought were necessary without taking the trouble of personally evaluating her. After a few days, with the worsening of Crista's health, his desperate relatives went to the health center in the neighboring village, San Francisco, and said that if the nurse did not attend, he should not go back to work in their villages. Constrained by the ultimatum, the nurse finally accompanied them and decided to call the plane to remove it, because it was evident that the situation was serious. The nurse left in front, without leaving the nursing technician watching the patient, and before the plane arrived, Crista was already dead. The consequences of Crista's death continue to reinforce the practice of neglect, which is the rule of health care for indigenous peoples in the region, because there are not few cases already reported and reported of negligence and errors. A few days later, at the end of May 2017, a call from the nearby municipality Funai de Lábrea warned of her death, however, even this institution did not have the concern to investigate the case properly. They mistakenly informed that Cristina Jamamadi had died; because she did not correspond to the description presented, she immediately suspected the information and was able to correctly identify who had died. Minutes later, the general chief of this people, Jamamadi Abbeys, reported on what happened and stated that the health team procedure was incorrect. The following week, Abbeys Jamamadi arrived in Lábrea with a document signed by all the villages, demanding the immediate exit of the Sesai nurse and urgent improvements in health care, not only to the Jamamadi, but to the jurisdiction of the Dsei as a whole. The chief Abbeys had scheduled a meeting with Carlos Galvão, coordinator of the Dsei Médio Purus. At that meeting the Jamamadi document was handed over to the coordinator, who signed it, returned the original and kept a copy. It is worth remembering that there is a great discontent with the programs and with the representativeness of the present Condisi, which leaves communities without an adequate health service. In the following months, the Dsei Médio Purus did not continue the investigation of the case and only relocated the nurse to another center; now, he attends at the Crispim pole of the Paumari people, even though the Jamamadi do not tire of requesting their disconnection from indigenous health. At this moment, the case has already been forgotten by the responsible entities, except for the family of Crista who, in mourning, continues to ask that the case not fall into oblivion. At their request, especially from Crista's father, Arigo Jamamadi, and the chief general, Jamamadi Abbeys, this statement is made in the hope that there will be a proper investigation of the circumstances of his death and that the appropriate measures will be applied. Attention is drawn to the specificities of the Jamamadi context. The total population is around 400 people living in six permanent villages, all on land, scattered in the territory of the Jarawara Indigenous Land, Jamamadi, Kanamati, on the left bank of the Purus River. Rarely, the teams adapt to the indigenous social reality and their logistics ignores the organization of this group. Thus, the team remains practically the whole period in the main village, far away many hours of walking from the others, and circulate little through the other villages. Except the accidents of evident gravity are reason to move the team from the central village. In short, the central hub structure does not function adequately to the local reality. Moreover, the unpreparedness of professionals who enter the area is glaring, in the best case they ignore the indigenous reality, but, more often than not, they are at odds in the villages and express frank prejudice, when they do not directly interfere in their way of life. Many teams impose a mode of care that does not correspond to that effective for the Jamamadi. Finally, it has to be said that the Dsei gives a big look at the “polemic” cases, especially when it comes to a people like Jamamadi, with little influence on local politics. Medications are scarce; referrals are rare; exams are non-existent; the precariousness of care ends up reinforcing a dependency of missionaries who have been working for many decades in their area, to the point that there are few requests for them to be allowed to attend them in place of health teams. Any attempt to retrieve information from Middle Dsei Purus was in vain. Employees refuse to answer. Finally, it is important to remember that the plane that did not remove Crista for emergency care arrived without delay to remove Nurse Andrew from the village. Neither the Dsei Médio Purus nor the Funai de Lábrea held any meeting to forward the necessary arrangements to investigate the case.”

7841e93feff239f5b75d68dc96a3549dfc646dec: The pollution of the Cateté River by metals iron, copper, chromium and nickel persists without any measure of containment by the Onça-Puma Plant of the Vale miner, since the first reports mentioned by the indigenous before 2015. The fish, valued in the Xikrin diet, disappeared. Iron oxide was found at a level 30 times that allowed (by Conama), and copper three times (by UFPA). The Valley has transformed the Cateté River into a heavy metal dump channel at very high and dangerous levels for the health of the Xikrin. The communities drink water, bathe, wash their clothes and pans in this river, which has the reddish color of iron oxide and the greenish color of nickel, deposited on its banks, some darkened by copper oxide. The area surrounding the indigenous land is almost totally devastated by the farmers and by the mining of the Valley. The top of the mountains and the dry streams are not respected. The Itacaiúnas River, on the side of IT Cateté, is also polluted with heavy metals. This river is used in the same way by indigenous people (to prepare meals, wash clothes and drink their water), which causes diseases mainly in children and the elderly. Heavy metals are being investigated, but the scientific literature shows that they are hormonal disruptors and possible contributors to type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. According to Conama, they are still cancerous, responsible for damage to hereditary DNA, malformations, immunodepression and compromises of the various organs. Despite all the irreversible and serious impacts on the lives of the people, Vale wants to allocate the resources that would be for the Xikrin to other projects, removing from indigenous associations the monetary resource they received from the Ferro-Carajás Project.

176b06f24100c54bc7da8192c09d417359a0bee7: Contamination by pesticides; trafficking in animals; burning

0c4a8542f8e320bf8675fa6ce2f13c0f4e96dd4a: The indigenous denounce that the publication of Decree 1.969 by the governor of the state of Pará, January 24, 2018, is unconstitutional. Recognized in the Brazilian legal system, Convention 169 states that “Governments should consult the peoples concerned, through appropriate procedures and particularly through their representative institutions, each time legislative or administrative measures are provided that may affect them directly”.

14f6e75feab31fa2e5c2bf4c19202eef70ab5f42: The community suffered three violent attacks in October. On the 7th, the Indians were surprised by a large drive of trucks and tractors that destroyed shacks, set fire and fired fire to the community causing injury in 15 people. Using rubber, marble and lethal bullets, several indigenous people were injured in these attacks. According to Ava Kunã Te'e, every week there are attacks on the scene. Shots are constantly fired. They also close the road and let no one pass. They threatened to run over anyone who passed, including children. On October 28, the Indians were again attacked extremely aggressively. Gunmen approached the Indians and shot them with rubber and marble bullets. One of the Indians explained that gunmen arrived around six o'clock and started shooting. He added they weren't doing anything, just taking mate. The attackers shot everywhere and destroyed everything. On October 31st, a new attack by farmers. Indigenous leaders told of the new invasion, with the overthrow of shacks, without any willingness for dialogue. The community protected themselves in the woods and this time there were no injuries.
2691b88ac8fc2df103fb493dc9eea74611e66f58: During the visit of Commissioner Antônia Urrejola Nogueira, of the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (ICHR) of the Organization of American States (OAS), to the indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá, a community 2 km from Dourados, suffered attack by local farmers, with bullets from rubber. According to information from indigenous leaders, the shooting resulted in several indigenous wounded, shacks knocked down. In addition to these aggressions, poison was spilled which caused diarrhea and vomiting in children and adults for several days after the attack. The farmers closed the road that gave access to the place where the IACHR delegation was, preventing the leaders from participating in the meeting with the commissioner.
c3d524892073daa397496e3797cc55b0a959fc8b: The Indian was the victim of an attack when he left a meeting at Funai headquarters in Guaíra. He was shot in the back by an individual who was in a dark vehicle. The motive and the author were neither clarified nor disclosed by the police. The Indian will be paraplegic. This attack was denounced to the IACHR (Inter-American Commission on Human Rights), when he visited Brazil.
528dfee771ddc5140144cdec1a45bce4a64ec6a6: The indigenous was shot after a disagreement during the election to the new chief of the village. The victim was referred to the hospital. There's no information on the defendant.
0f62a3525d85a80f8ae221040462b0ed0db3765d: The community was preparing to celebrate the “day of the Indian”, when there was a disagreement between two indigenous people and one of them was wounded with stab wounds. The perpetrator of the assault wasn't located by the police.
48c2c785f48538b0f259967047e4abe596c07f29: Two weeks after the publication of the Funai dispatch with the delimitation of Tekoha Guasú Guarani, the indigenous was harassed by four armed men who forced him into a car. They insisted that he recognize, by photo, other indigenous in the region, asking about villages and location of houses. With each negative response, the victim was beaten with punches. Not satisfied with the answers, they took the victim to the banks of the Paraná River, instructing a Paraguayan to kill him. When he said he was Paraguayan, the shooter saved him from death. He managed to escape to Salto do Guaíra, Paraguay.
3d071aae133d1c914fad018265932569768c0166: The Indian was driving around the city on his motorcycle when he was hit by a truck. The victim was on the floor when the driver of the truck went backwards, throwing the vehicle back on him. He was helped by other bikers, also indigenous, who passed the site. The truck driver ran off unmarked.
8171839a847e2c4789dd4f1f4b76cfb8e1670f7a: The indigenous woman was attacked when she was on Avenida Brasil, central region of Cascavel, and asked for help from people who were in a nightclub. The police were triggered and she was taken to the Emergency Unit (UPA). There's no information on the circumstances of the assault.
45626e460044f3c42a18dcd80cf814408dff32bb: There was a conflict at the Light Indian Reserve in Charrua. Some Indians came in shooting and there was a firefight between the parties. According to family members, who are hospitalized, a group of approximately 50 indigenous people has been camped in the community of Crowned for about five months.
a2e9b2eed27e6cac6612d51fc0d23d6fad2fedc4: The victim was beaten with stab wounds by a man. The crime was witnessed by other indigenous people who helped her. Taken to the hospital, she underwent surgery due to the severity of her injuries. The attacker was located and immobilized until the arrival of the Military Police.
b2d2766520bf54701764aa9ea88fdf516433112a: The Indian was in the hospital where he had taken the newborn child who would be hospitalized. When seeking to leave the room he was sexually harassed by the nurse who had attended him.
152bb1ebe0261e9702c7ce86d64f15d48a1e954a: An operation led by a delegate from Tabatinga, arrested two men accused of rape of indigenous children between six and eleven years old. Rapes, reported by representatives of Sesai, were being committed between 2011 and 2017.
6b0c77094012cccfd5f4291d8d17f8c173862edc: The Indian was approached by a man who tried to take his clothes off by force. After screaming for help, the perp ran away undetected. The victim was rescued by community residents who heard the cries for help.
b3a1bcae845a21be615768809c7212e4ff476afc: The girl was in the company of the accused, drinking alcohol. Later, she was taken to a forest where the crime occurred. After the act, he tied the victim's legs to a tree and threw gasoline at his body. She was rescued and taken to the hospital.
1f398ec9730420efcae8198c8349a85501ccb1fb: The mother reported to the police that the child left in the company of two uncles, who would have taken the niece into the bush. She was hospitalized in a serious state and needed to be transferred by plane to the city of Ariquemes, Rondônia.
16f97e8e2f7cb59d903911536ff5e7aa63fdcfcb: The indigenous woman was at St. Felix's birthday party in Araguaia. After a fight, the aggressor beat the indigenous, dragged her and raped her inside a house in São Félix do Araguaia. According to the police, another man who tried to defend her was assaulted by the suspect with punches, slaps and threatened with a knife.
72955add6cd66e7664d736c93f0ec2cd4a737d62: The mother reported that she left home to go into town, leaving her daughter in the company of two younger brothers and her neighbor. When he returned, he found his daughter with multiple bruises on her body.
33eaa15247951de9b0efc8b00fd5ac78f3cc53c6: In Dourados 70% of rape crimes against children happen in the Indian reserve. Victims are between 4 and 14 years old and in most cases are victims of parents, stepfathers and close people. Most are motivated by high alcohol consumption. Another serious problem is that several mothers end up being accomplices to their husbands. The information is from the coordinator of the Golden Court, Lucilene Leivas Leite Prudente.
c94ec6d6d1bc782e753a198ea34b475f25982755: The child told his mother that she was admonished by her father. The nine-year-old brother witnessed the case. Indian leaders and the victim's mother reported the case to the police. The suspect is under arrest.
b1f826dd261c259d2bbe36053e01b03bea4122b7: The State Public Ministry of Mato Grosso do Sul investigated a rape case of an indigenous adolescent. The accused would be brother-in-law of the village chief.
b89cb75e8c7e1bfd512f0ce923f38ce9bfff27bf: The indigenous woman said she was being threatened by the councilman after suffering sexual abuse and getting pregnant. According to the victim, the councilman, also indigenous, would have another family in the village and therefore threatened her.
61ba1814527f81a2d4e570998ce10921a118e42b: The girl would have gone out to the grandparents' house, which is next to her residence, when she was approached and raped. Suspect was identified, but not arrested.
0bcb7eec4619ad027f96e0032692074153257b52: The parents of the child went to the police to report rape against their adolescent cousin, because they reported that they caught the adolescent sexually abusing the child. The police were investigating the case.
84e05e776e5f4679dbb11bcab7ae3fa0b1e60769: The young woman was the victim of rape by two men arrested in the act. She was referred to Xanxerê hospital.
235dc786a95e0cb3b5b2378729d934d6b441dcca: Krahô women reported cases of sexual abuse practiced by some employees of the Dsei, working in the village where they live. According to one of the reports, in addition to trying to abuse the indigenous, they uttered words that left them embarrassed and disrespected.
00cf25f72178e9490abeef02d8703c1f8ed834c0: Chapter III – Violence by the Government’s Default
8f4f0ee54425b93e14c067b9d56366f45a52fea2: Drug traffickers worked in the indigenous land. Fifty search and seizure warrants and 21 arrests were issued.
1f2703b24c516eaf8386d862d2774ccaa02a3c2b: After denunciation, the Preventive and Integrated Control of the São Francisco River Basin (FPI) found that the residences of the federal government program “Minha Casa, Minha Vida”, delivered to the indigenous community in 2017, present cracks on the walls and sidewalks; irregularities in electrical installations; low quality construction material; floor sinking; termite in wood and doors without locks. According to the chief of the Kariri-Xocó, José Cicero Queiroz, when the community received the houses, there were no cracks, but over the months the problems arose. The chief says the community needs the houses because it has nowhere to go. The community triggered the MPF of Alagoas and denounced the irresponsibility of the federal government for the delivery of houses with foundation and structure problems.
30b6b5488e6108039da114e50363a789ad854175: It was determined by the 4th Class of the TRF of the 5th Region that Funai should provide basic baskets to the indigenous family, Macário/Salustiano, for a period of four months, until the indigenous could harvest their own plantations and acquire self-sufficiency to feed. However, the determination was not fulfilled.
c288e4f62027491fbcc5beb91eebd5a87fcfbfe0: Funai signed a Conduct Adjustment Term (TAC) with Aracruz (now Fibria). Only part of the TAC was fulfilled by Funai, missing to pass on to indigenous communities the payment of R $ 1,484,884. Funai should ensure resources in the annual budgets for projects and programs resulting from ethnoenvironmental studies and promoting self-sustainability. These activities should have been implemented between 2008 and 2011. According to the prosecutor of the Republic in Linhares, Paulo Henrique Trazzi, since the signature of the document, the MPF-ES tried to enforce the treaties in various ways. However, in 2018, it had no alternative but to request the judicial enforcement of the TAC.
013821344f173727cbf3c4a98cdd68e58c6f7c4a: After suffering a heart attack in the village and dying, the body of the indigenous had to be transferred to its original village in the municipality of Zé Doca. Those responsible for the preparation of the body did not use formaldehyde, which caused great embarrassment, in view of the delay to perform the burial and the long distance from the transfer because, at the time of the wake, the body was already entering a state of decomposition.
0536360ab8f61051fae4b01b1f9dae32175d05e3: The indigenous people have not yet had recognition of their traditional territory and are constantly threatened by farmers. The community is located in a border area where there is no assistance, supervision and protection agencies.
6c6259e1d0f2f032a9b5080965a045b885035819: The community is included in the Luz para Todos program, but was not attended because the company Energisa Mato Grosso-Energy Distributor claimed that the indigenous would need to prove that they were in possession of the territory. As explained by the MPF-MT, this claim does not proceed and hurts the Federal Constitution of 1988, which adopted the institute of indigenato, a primary source of territorial possession and not dependent on legitimacy. Second, the declaration of the MPF-MT, the lack of access of electricity to the community impairs the conservation of school meals, food and pharmaceutical supplies, such as insulin for diabetics.
f5a2ff84dba8d589e2a6e68b1eaae19f0cc9a4a6: According to Chief Sebastião, creator and coordinator of the Chiquetana Airport Organization (OCA), the chicanian population living in the Airport Garden is in a situation of extreme vulnerability, aggravated by the lack of public policies. The absence of territorial demarcation has contributed to increasing the number of indigenous population in urban peripheries. The situation faced by indigenous peoples in the rural area of the municipality is also critical, because families live in lots of approximately 60m x 80m, without conditions to plant and cultivate their traditions, forced to work on neighboring farms, with low wages and in poor conditions. In these cases, migration to the city is the only alternative. Two of the 50 families living on the periphery were visited by members of the Caracol Institute, along with the chief, in action supported by Cimi. One of the families consists of 15 people and adults are outside the formal labour market. One of them only gets paid when called and often goes weeks without work. Another works for a minimum wage in a sawmill, without a signed wallet and is out of work when the site paralyzes its activities. In the other family, when one of them gets a job it is to work with farmers who pay the minimum wage and collect food sold on their own farm, with an average of 300 reais left for the family to pay their expenses.
6b6e84993032a32b2fe95a141d361ee248801ad2: The neglect in the treatment of indigenous peoples in the Dourados Reserve motivated a Public Civil Action for governments, in the federal, state and municipal spheres, to implement policies to combat drug use. For the MPF, the indigenous population is treated with hostile indifference, based mostly on discriminatory reasons. This neglect is reflected in the high rates of domestic violence, drug and alcohol consumption, suicide mainly due to precariousness in education, food, housing and public safety. In a note, the MPF stated that despite the data explaining the need for public policies aimed at the indigenous population, public authorities avoid their responsibilities.
ddcd63d86b5ffb69513614fa878dc02ec82173c6: Criminals robbed and deprecated the Guatemalan health center. According to the Local Indigenous Health Council, it was the tenth criminal action recorded on site in three years. In addition to furniture, important items were taken for community health care, such as the pregnant women's care apparatus and the pressure measurement. The x-ray device was destroyed. The leaders point out as one of the factors for the wave of crime in the reserve, the growing increase in drug sales points, since those who command the traffic demand from users stolen products as payment. As a consequence, care was paralyzed until the responsible bodies took steps to ensure safety on the spot.
d735cdddba8f1fb882439d00d05a0ccf9a2476e2: About 3,000 children are under canvas shacks, vulnerable to intense cold, with temperatures of 7o degrees, in the villages of Dourados, the most populous in Brazil. There are reports that the indigenous burn wood inside the shacks to warm up from the cold. However, this situation is very dangerous and risky, because in addition to smoke inhalation, there can be fires. Funai estimates that about two thousand families live under tarps or improvised structures in the reserve. They are men, women, children and elderly in a situation of absolute vulnerability.
4ddc0d299bb5426d2da42f53706e523bac6e77f3: The water delivery service is through truck-pipe, but the supply is irregular and the community suffers from lack of water. As a result, indigenous people resort to non-drinking watercourses, water from nearby streams, often contaminated with pesticides and residues. In 2015 the MPF filed a public civil action against the Union, after finding the poor conditions of access to water by the community. Even after granting early protection, later confirmed by a court sentence that determined the supply of water to the village residents, the situation was not resolved.
f9d95f304235d3110bd7a7fe9ca23ce850eeacb0: According to the TRF of the 3rd Region, indigenous families were not receiving basic baskets. The problem had become worse because new families had not been registered, which prevented them from receiving even with regular delivery of baskets. One of the problems indicated is that many families are no longer entitled to this food and others, who need it, are not served. According to the determination of the TRF, the government of Mato Grosso do Sul must re-registrate and deliver the baskets to all indigenous families living in the state, both in regularized areas and in those that are pending regularization.
979fa069214670979e0fa453d17db8f1a877f6ec: The number of indigenous children and adolescents in shelters doubled from June 2014 to July 2018, according to data from the judicial social worker Ana Liége Charão Dias Borges who, at the request of the Thomson Reuters Foundation, did the research. The judge of the Court of Childhood and Youth in Dourados clarified that communities live in a state of misery, and this causes the destitution of families. In addition, there is an increase in alcoholism and drug use, further aggravating the situation. Funai denounces that children have been taken from their parents wrongly, without any warning, without motivation, without time for farewells, without speaking to the child in the mother tongue. In addition, when placed in shelters, children are forced to adapt to a new and unknown way of life, which makes their reintegration to the indigenous community difficult. The social worker reported that indigenous children account for more than half of the children in shelters in Dourados. A very significant increase, because four years ago it represented less than a third of the total number of sheltered children.
6e1707044fbce4f8f82919d91d1a8a4100f10926: According to the State Public Defender and a complaint by Cimi at the UN, it is estimated that 30% of Guarani-Kaiowá children remain unregistered. Factors such as the lack of registration of the parents themselves, the distance from the villages of the cities and the existence of lands close to the border areas worsen this stateless situation. According to the defender Neyle Ferreira Mendes, the interpretation of the law loaded with prejudice greatly aggravates this process. There are difficulties in notaries to perform this record because there is still no specific procedure for indigenous people.
9184dd6784ae20f53617d278e7ee4230edff1fe7: The duplication of the highway MS-156, which cuts stretches of the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, was performed without due attention to the compensation measures provided in anthropological and environmental studies, commissioned by the state government itself. Currently, the highway is in full operation, in total non-compliance with Brazilian legislation and conditions agreed by the state government with the indigenous. Faced with the intense traffic that cuts the roads, the MPF-MS required the competent bodies to ensure greater protection to communities.
b46aa0f939c8c04bb90bdef553d7b578f3b9b9dc: About 50 indigenous people occupied the headquarters of Funai - Regional Coordination of Lower Tocantins, in Marabá. The few activities that were still being developed were suspended. Due to large cuts in Funai's budget, employees hired by the agency were eventually exonerated. For more than 10 months, the unit has no one to answer for it. Since the departure of the last regional manager there has been no appointment for the post. According to Jopramré Parkatejê, people need help from Funai because there are many demands that need the support of the indigenous agency and there is no one to sign a document, nor to respond to the demands of communities. Also, according to the indigenous woman, in a meeting with the president of Funai, he asked them to indicate a name for the function. However, this was not taken into account.
447f3ad39c99e14e1f82fba75a019905420244e5: A group of Indians Tembé occupied the headquarters of the city of Tomé-Açu, demanding an audience to discuss improvements in the area of health and education, improvements in roads that give access to communities and payment of late wages. They report that indigenous workers working in community schools were dismissed without any explanation and those who remain working have been behind wages since July 2018. In addition, they claim that the funding for paving the roads giving access to the villages has already been released, but the works have not been started.
bc8a310f4baf15ef24facb2274f2b58436306532: One woman and three children were prevented from entering the Indigenous Passing House (Capai) and, because of this, spent the night in the open. In a note, the municipality claimed that the amount of indigenous people exceeded the limit of service of the unit.
dc99c9abf8592b9c4eaf42dace53d1f97bc80041: The community that has lived 40 years on the banks of BR-153, km 42, has no drinking water. Indigenous people are exposed to contamination and the risk of contracting diseases. Analysis carried out by the State Health Surveillance in water samples collected at the Camp on April 3, 2018, confirmed the contamination by the presence of the bacterium Escheríchia coli.
2e64e657558e867406c928b38f971e67ef60f1f9: The indigenous community was contemplated with support for the construction of 82 houses. The responsibility for the agreement and the construction of the houses was borne by the Association Amigo do Indio. According to the complaint, the contract was not fulfilled and the Federal Justice of Erechim determined the blocking of assets of the said association, since it did not meet the deadline of delivery of the houses to indigenous families in Votouro, which was December 2015. According to MPF, the entity received funds from Caixa Econômica Federal (CEF) to mediate the construction of housing units in the indigenous community, in an agreement signed in December 2012. An Association lawyer claims that CEF suspended the missing resources because of a conflict between the indigenous themselves. No indigenous leadership was consulted on the subject.
c5b904738ceae9fbd6ce1626962faf0d697ae0ff: The community, composed of 50 people, faces serious problems related to lack of drinking water, sanitation, health center, medical negligence and lack of transportation. Chief Estevan Garay has been in the occupation for 11 years, and claims that conditions are extremely precarious. Some time ago they needed to consume water from the Arroyo do Conde, where farmers wash equipment contaminated with pesticides. The Arroio water that reaches the community is also contaminated with poison used in rice plantations.
43f47c56147375b207cbfed7bf73d7d6889f99fc: The Guarani-Mbya resumed their ancestral lands at the Arado Velho in Porto Alegre. Since then, they have been threatened, including firearms, by the owners of an enterprise. They intend to kick them out of the area and build luxury condos there. In one of the violent actions, the community was even forbidden from having access to drinking water.
b3eb7d0a9a45ac4e0d67d2308b7bc67528984fd7: The community of Capivari do Sul lives for decades camped on the banks of RS-040, km 60 to 62 and claims the demarcation of its traditional land. However, the identification and delimitation work group has been paralyzed since 2012. Living in complete vulnerability, the situation worsened considerably during 2018 due to the lack of drinking water. Sesai, responsible for basic sanitation, claims that there is no way to provide water because the trucks are lacking documentation and maintenance. Due to this situation, the Guarani Mbya consume water from a polluted stream, where farm waste is dumped and agricultural equipment washed.
5709c201db84fc291a0b0e0bf7ab3fb7e7643cab: The community reports neglect in maintaining and opening the access road to the village Panorama, which has caused serious problems for health care in emergency cases. A document was forwarded to the DER and the MPF, demanding measures.
8b6e12be860f510bad229e4058f4cb0755ccdd03: Due to the lack of the Administrative Registry of Indigenous Birth (Rani), whose expedition is the responsibility of Funai, children, adolescents and adults are being deprived of adequate health and education care.
e73d10c6b00c1a1ef9fbe9f28035132f6255b9a0: The elderly died and their relatives had many difficulties to obtain the death certificate due to the lack of an identification document. Since 2012 Funai's community has been collecting documents.
530e4563a83fc82afee3ea6527f3e88f3e9960a7: The school was broken into and a 13 kg gas tank, a cell phone, thermal bottles and various food and working materials were stolen. To the cops, one of the defendants said he got some teenagers drunk and convinced them to break into school. The material was subsequently recovered.
7ef0b3dbd75cfc7ce01a285fe8bfd314cb2ddf3f: In the village Tabalada the structure is quite precarious. There is a lack of school supplies, lunch, transportation for students who live far from the village, as well as the devaluation of teachers who are behind wages. Students spend months without school, which hinders learning and causes delays in the school year. In health, there is no adequate transport for the removal of patients and the health centers have been unmaintained for years.
f7c60171049182927b47cda023ebb894a61532a3: Despite a judicial decision determining the construction of a Passage House for indigenous peoples to shelter when they go to Florianópolis to sell their crafts, it has not yet been fulfilled. Without shelter, they stay in an abandoned road terminal, without walls, full of leaks, without the minimum conditions to be protected and safe. The judge himself wrote in the sentence that determined the creation of a place to shelter them: “Indians cannot be treated as animals or second-class human beings”, “Indians live a flagrant case of public omission.”
e53a3cfb65b56b555567f9dce266cf4f6cb69411: The poor road conditions hinder medical care in the villages. According to a missionary from Cimi, there were cases where indigenous people died because of the delay in help. The justification for the organs is that the vehicles would be broken. There was the case of a woman who, in labor, gave birth on the way to the hospital, because transportation failed to arrive in time.
48bb4e22cd474068ceaafa5509010bb0900e6ae0: Residents of the House of the Indigenous Student of Araguaína denounced the precarious state of the property. They claim that the house has not been reformed in many years and the structure threatens to collapse. There are many infiltrations and wiring is old, which increases the risk of accidents and fires. According to them, when it rains hard the building trembles like it's going to collapse. The walls fell and often the police enter the property behind thieves, scaring the children.
4e344f6caa42434337af24e33f5100e3c066f279: The water used in the village to cook and drink is dark, reddish, apparently with high presence of iron and phosphate. Without receiving any treatment, it is collected directly in the ribeirãos that pass within the indigenous land, since there are no artesian wells in the villages. People have become constantly sick.
ce9d6a3e06e43b99b6bfa22d953ac071943261f6: The Karajá people of Xambioá have been facing problems of access to other villages due to a damaged bridge that offers no guarantee of security, as it is flooded in the rainy season. Lack of maintenance prevents health care, education and other types of locomotion.
81a85d4219312710b551a7cbfd85c7d47a4fd73b: People suffer from the lack of water treatment. Most of the population consumes water directly from rivers and streams near the villages. Without basic sanitation, waste is carried with rain to these rivers and streams, feeding a permanent cycle of viruses, diarrhea and skin diseases. There is no effective plan for water treatment and sanitation by Dsei.
a15a2635ed31f547b578a3d83cf0351ec6d662bc: There is discontinuity in the formation of indigenous teachers, for those who are, both of those who are attending the teaching school and of those who have already completed it. There is no pedagogical accompaniment from the teacher. The implementation of high school is lacking, which has led many young people to move from their community to live in the municipal headquarters. No school building, many teachers teach in their own homes.
876937196b20e6b82855d0f97025788155fbf820: There is discontinuity in the formation of teachers who still attend the indigenous teaching and in the continuing education of those who have already completed it. Teachers lack pedagogical support. The problem affects the indigenous lands Nawa (22 teachers) and Nukini (25 teachers).
02fefa79ee02863eeeb93fe3ec13a214449f71d5: Teacher training is neglected by responsible bodies, especially those who are still attending the indigenous teaching school, as well as those who have completed the course. There is also a lack of pedagogical support for the teacher.
f90d449215eca1ac70664d9369288996cbc21a52: Six years ago, a group of the Katukina people migrated from their area to the Gregório River Indigenous Land. Only one of the six communities has a school. In two communities, there is no building for the school to run and teachers teach in their own homes. On the other three, there's no teacher or school. The leaders have already charged the state government to enforce the right of children and young people to study, but so far the number of children who are not being literate has increased.
12d96c0d03e0381124f9e7c8f78160b281cb499d: Several indigenous people reported that the non-indigenous teacher receives the lunch for the students, but does not pass it on. Sometimes the snack doesn't even get to the village and is replaced by chickens. As for the teacher, according to the students, he uses food in evangelical cults, offering meals to his friends. This situation has been going on for years.
f32a1e6664e5b3523b569287351f9904b3d40b0c: Edileusa Shanenawa, a basic schoolteacher, denounced that the government “want to put our knowledge on the Western level.” She argues that it is necessary to learn Portuguese to enter the world of white people, but that it is necessary to respect the right of indigenous peoples to differentiated education, with specific teaching materials. “We don’t just want the book that comes from MEC, we want our own material”, he added the representative of the Organization of Indigenous Teachers of Acre (Opiacre).
3372a683afa3c54835079e2e236053f615dec5ad: Almost 200 students were enrolled in the indigenous community, divided into 16 classes, in the three shifts. Without any building for the operation of the school, the indigenous use several rented structures (including residences) and spaces built by the community itself. The State Department of Education has information about this reality, but, despite promoting enrollments, providing school transportation and hiring staff for the functioning of the school, it has been omitted by not building a teaching unit for another decade.
2e083ca89be4050acaa1960be3c6d6db54ce2c9a: Due to the lack of school in the community, adolescents and children need to move to the municipality, where they suffer racial discrimination because they are indigenous.

The Guarani registered a complaint of the truculent action with the MPF and demanded an investigation of the facts and threats received by the indigenous, as well as the identification and punishment of those responsible.
ec3e744442991061a81fc25bf3171c0f68e24fa9: The licensing project of the Hydroelectric Power Plant (UHE) Well Quer continued to advance in 2019 without any information being passed on to the indigenous communities, nor was any consultation procedure carried out, as the legislation provides. The company responsible for the Environmental Impact Study and Report (EIA/Rima) held information meetings at some municipal headquarters. The company responsible for the Study of Indigenous Component (ECI), with a contract in force since 2018, has not manifested or sought out indigenous communities and organizations at any time to inform about the progress of the study. Funai also did not inform indigenous communities and organizations, as required by its own Normative Instruction No. 2 of March 27, 2015. According to the Brazilian State, the construction of the UHE Bem Querer would affect nine indigenous lands: Tabalascada, Malacacheta, Manoá-Pium, Jabuti, Moskow, Canauanim, São Marcos and Yanomami. However, more indigenous lands are likely to be directly or indirectly affected. During 2019, President Jair Bolsonaro and other political representatives waved the idea that the project would be built immediately, ignoring all the procedures provided for by the licensing legislation and disregarding the right of indigenous peoples to prior, free and informed consultation. Peoples and their indigenous organisations have already publicly and at various times expressed that they do not accept the project. The communities of six indigenous lands, located in the Serra da Lua region, and the Yanomami IT people prepared two Consultation Protocols. The MPF has been informed.
5f4b35ca2e0e1c44cf96242a307a6721de77404d: In 2019 the federal government made several investments to accelerate the process of licensing the installation of the transmission network, known as Linhão de Tucuruí, which will cross the Waimiri-Atroari IT, without the necessary prior, free and informed consultation. In 2017, the Federal Court had determined the suspension of the Previous License of the undertaking precisely because of the lack of prior consultation with the communities. Since June 2019, the case has been before the Federal Regional Court of the 1st Region, which, even if it had not decided on the merits of the case, whether or not the licence was granted, has expressed its views on the need for consultation with the Waimiri-Atroari people. At various times, President Jair Bolsonaro, members of his government and parliamentarians, expressed the view that the works of Linhão would be started quickly, without the need to follow the procedures established by the law. On February 28, 2019, an order from Bolsonaro was published in the Official Gazette, declaring the work of Linhão de Tucuruí as an undertaking of “interest of the National Defense Policy”. In the interpretation of the government, this recognition would waive the guarantee of the right to consult indigenous peoples and accelerate the beginning of the works. The Waimiri-Atroari have prepared a Consultation Protocol and demand that it be respected. The MPF-AM denounced, in November 2019, illegalities in the procedures prior to the consultation and requested the translation of the documents, in addition to having asked Funai and Ibama to prepare a technical opinion to clarify whether there will be negative impacts on indigenous peoples, since the topography studies of the project were not carried out, considering that the places where the 250 transmission towers will be placed are unknown. The Joint Parliamentary Front in Defense of the Rights of Indigenous Peoples visited the Waimiri-Atroari community in April 2019 and undertook to work within the Legislative Power to effectively comply with the guarantee of the right to prior, free and informed consultation.
60e7ea75c3fa76a01a8b19e1b8dde0bc83153bf0: An energy distribution substation was built within the Sucuba IT, without due prior consultation process, free and informed. The community filed a complaint with the MPF.
7b1f9f5f650b4d9a2c01c7d355fa9c652586ab2c: Armed men with covered faces burned down the prayer house of the Guarani people. Leadership reports that there has been a significant increase in threats and pressures against the indigenous, both day and night. In addition to the explicit threats, they have still been constantly disturbed by the overflight of drones in the village, which causes them considerable apprehension.
4c26075123726da10f16a48ac0c32b78f3591bfa: Grinders, serving real estate speculators, invaded Tarumã IT and threatened the Indians. The invaders said: “You are Paraguayans; the earth is not yours; we are born here”. And, threatening them, they said: “If you step on this, we will shoot you”. Indigenous people report that this type of threat has been systematically increasing.
8a676c9bb5944d98d8a98b8a6043de9524e2bc35: Failure to comply with compensation agreement
86e82371c382fd31150f9aed25e69ec1f6d0c64e: In an unprecedented strategy in the country, indigenous Guarani acquired six actions (at R$ 17 each) of the Road Logistics Railway, the largest railway operator in the country and, as shareholders, filed a complaint about the lack of compliance with environmental measures and protection of their rights. Among the priority measures are the construction of houses, places of prayer and a bridge, the creation of community gardens and the acquisition of micro tractors. The indigenous say that of the 101 mitigation and compensation measures taken by the companies, 72 “are totally paralyzed at this time”. Funai and MPF-SP state that the railway is failing to comply with the terms of the Basic Environmental Plan formulated by the company itself in November 2013.
db10408be0750005ca7f98ae5bfce206e893c78e: The territory borders the border of Peru and it has become a route for drug trafficking, as well as being used by baggers, fishermen and loggers from Peru. The activities of the traffickers begin at the fall of the afternoon and go until the dawn. However, the traffickers continue to use the indigenous territory as a route of passage and the people Apolima-Arara remain vulnerable and threatened in this context.
83e6d2405ed5a62cce29d63375cf27389d4a7613: The leaders of the Yawanawá people denounce the company Radon Administração e Participação Ltda that, in 2010, obtained environmental license for logging in an area of 150 thousand hectares that is at the limit with the Indigenous Lands Rio Gregório, of the peoples Yawanawá and Katukina, and the IT Kaxinawá of Carapanã Beach, of the Kaxinawá people, in the municipality of Tarauacá. The devastation is overwhelming and the company is not respecting the damping zone. This destruction has put at risk the safe food breed of the peoples, due to the flight of hunting, for example. Despite the complaints, no action has been taken by the responsible bodies and communities remain threatened.
43194d4dfc8efbf942c75bd9f39d3174b97271d8: The surrounding of the indigenous land is occupied by farms and logging, which has increased deforestation of the area. f76450a364a0cc9fb0f9cb2d872a1fa39f19652c: The surroundings of the indigenous land are occupied by an Incra settlement; farmers, squatters and settlers are deforesting the area. e78b0c8c68b34b0d387ef63488d0aa0c61691a0d: In addition to the indigenous being suffering the consequences of deforestation around their territory, caused by farmers, squatters and settlers, the installation of electric transmission network with high voltage towers, from Eletrobrás, which will pass within the indigenous land is ongoing. The Environmental Impacts Study was carried out, as well as the consultation process; however, the company itself made the consultation, forcing the people to accept compensation. 870784bdf040eed45266b5251a41917ba2385eda: The indigenous territory limits the border of Peru and has been used as a route of drug trafficking and logging from Peru. cbfd35940857e9feaace7fbdbaddbdb32bfc7a01: The territory claimed has always been the target of invasions of farmers who occupied the land through the greasing. b1ef19d1dee58b57507f6f17dbaa6b5d65fc9920: The indigenous people have been impacted due to the duplication of BR 101 and the presence of invaders in the traditional land.
c41ce4c03a891c6c38b229530b890a26c15f9b10: Development of the Growth Acceleration Program (CAP) is being implemented without any process of study and mitigation by the government in relation to the demarcation of Karuazu IT. ac3e843a785dcd3be242ad2c358de5dfddb9bc9e: Duplicating works of highway BR 101 are reaching the indigenous and the environment. The people also suffer from the presence of invaders within the traditional land.

eab7cf326ac588190e62ab1baada0bc18b2b4051: The Articulation of the Peoples and Indigenous Organizations of Amapá and Norte do Pará (Apoianp) denounced the relaunch of the former Programa Calha Norte, with the new name of Projecto Barão do Rio Branco. b56ec0f22eace0df90722b7bb2ca30f43f0c8224: Invasion, hunting and predatory fishing, illegal logging

72a63688620c721b840edc175e69ddf3b387d8e9: The monitoring of satellite images by Inpe revealed an increase in deforestation in the Amazon in 2019 caused by illegal gold mining. President Jair Bolsonaro's statements, favorable to mineral exploitation in indigenous lands and that disqualify the work of Inpe, end up stimulating the invasions of indigenous lands and their resulting conflicts, generating fear and insecurity in indigenous populations.
56e12300951a5e32c148dece42d0078a4fe32578: The Association of the Kanamari of the Javari Valley denounced to the technical coordinator of Funai, in Eirunepé, the advance of mining activity in the Rio Jutaí, within the indigenous territory.
