The leaders counted at least ten dredges (ships designed to draw sand or mud from the bottom of watercourses), and identified the increase in ports. To get into the territory, the prospectors try to entice the indigenous with gifts and alcohol. One of them, armed with a shotgun, came to the village saying Funai didn't help the Indians. He committed to improving the village, including offering a 114 Hp light engine to the chief if the community allowed the prospect. In addition to the degradation of the river, the forest and all its biodiversity, mining severely threatens the way of life of the peoples, and may spread diseases and cause the consumption of alcohol and drugs, in addition to endangering the existence of the indigenous peoples isolated from the region. Indigenous women are often harassed by prospectors, who still threaten the indigenous who react to the harassment of their wives and daughters. Indigenous organizations have repeatedly denounced invasions of Javari Valley IT. Fishermen, hunters, traffickers and prospectors have been causing conflicts in various locations, affecting even peoples of little or no contact with the surrounding society. According to the coordination of the Etnoenvironmental Protection Front of the Javari Valley, there are at least 18 people in the region who remain without contact with non-indigenous society.
57b46a892c5ee70252877a63ca542149a3108780: In the southern region of the state, the indigenous people faced the arrival of fire for the first time in the forest areas of their territory, until then a “green belt” surrounded by illegal deforestation and land grabbing. According to Antônio Enesio Tenerim, “to this day the fire had not entered. But now it has come at once, in various places”. The smoke cloud covered the forest of the indigenous land, advanced through the Amazonian municipalities of Manicoré and Humaitá and moved to Porto Velho, Rondônia. With 80 kilometers of IT cut irregularly by the Transamazonic route, the people triggered all possible organs to try to contain the fires.
bb8d04774495adc9db0e3349290edacc8945a18f: Invasion, hunting and predatory fishing, environmental damage
a79147d2edd30cd5c6f8fb31cdf995cb8ac7f375: The Ethnoenvironmental Protection Base of the Ituí-Itacoaí River of Funai at the entrance of Javari Valley IT was attacked by clandestine hunters. Indigenous peoples confirmed that hunters of wild animals fired several shots at the base when indigenous peoples of various peoples and servants of Funai were inside. According to a statement by the leader Kora Kanamari, “their focus is to end the base of Ituí, especially now that the rights of indigenous peoples are under attack, with this government, which says it will release the mining”. After one of the attacks, a Funai team seized about 300 tracajás and 40,000 eggs with teams of illegal hunters inside the indigenous land. This was the fourth attack on the same base since last year. It serves as guardian of one of the main river entrances in the Javari Valley. 89d1ff489524543b08ae0d56017fd6617ca954bc: A man was arrested while making illegal landscaping on the ground of a pre-Colombian indigenous cemetery in Manaus, with area of about 20,000 square meters. The person responsible for the terraplanning made the opening of a road on site and the existence of environmental impacts in the area was observed.
64860e7d0f62fcebfbcf8f03c8185f3b61f42758: About 60 rafts were illegally dribbling near places where isolated indigenous people live. A joint operation of Funai agents, Federal Police and Ibama, entitled “Korubo”, disabled the equipment of the offenders. Territorial protection carried out through federal surveillance operations is essential to guarantee the autonomy and survival of these indigenous peoples.
46776079404b430a1f25cc6602a130629dd1b3cf: Indigenous people in the region reported that armed hunters once again attacked the surveillance base of Funai River Ituí, which is located in the Javari Valley IT. The Federal Police is investigating the cases, but already pointed out that the attacks were made by fishermen and illegal hunters of North Atalaia, financed by smuggling groups of animals of Tabatinga and Benjamin Constant, municipalities located in the state of Amazonas. Servers and indigenous peoples claim that illegal activities in the territory increased considerably after the Bolsonaro government began. They report that the dismantling of these bases and the lack of government support are favoring the increase of invasions, mainly due to the lack of supervision.

10655d808af955a9f8aecdb21a8ef4c77792d6a6: For years, the people have been waiting for the authorities to regulate their territory, removing the invaders. They are illegal prospectors and fishermen who work within the indigenous land, causing conflicts and destroying the environment.
ae798630476eacff5c043da6c6f874d9c359425c: President Jair Bolsonaro stated that the transmission line between Manaus (AM) and Boa Vista (RR) will be built "regardless of the manifestation of the Indians". The goal of the linion is to solve the energy problem of Roraima, since part of the state depends on energy coming from Venezuela. The linion focuses on the lands of the Waimiri-Atroari people and its construction will severely impact the community, with the destruction of structures and plantations.
e8e0cb8346cc6bdc450b267ad3abf33ff4d83e04: The invasion of prospectors grows frighteningly in Yanomami territory and already involves about 20,000 people. In March 2018, according to a complaint filed by indigenous associations in the MPF, this number was estimated at 5,000. According to David Kopenawa, the prospectors spread over four rivers of the region, building wooden houses, rafts, and landing strips. A partial report by the Federal Police in August 2019 denounces the performance of a criminal organization in illegal mining activity in IT, acting on the fronts of air and land logistics, radiophony centers and buying gold. One of those investigated by PF, Pedro Emiliano Garcia, was already sentenced to imprisonment for genocide in 1993 (due to the “Massacre of Haximu”, slaughter of dozens of Yanomami by prospectors). According to the investigations, Garcia even owns a plane, and one of his associates became a Sesai pilot. The advance of deforestation and environmental devastation in the Yanomami IT was confirmed by satellite monitoring by Inpe. The indigenous reported that the action of the prospectors increased dramatically after the deactivation of three Etnoenvironmental Protection Bases, Funai, and the departure of the Army from the region.
9387eb321386fe90958b44f738171ca55179f399: Operation Walopali-Curare XI ended up with 30 outbreaks of illegal mining at Yanomami IT. A helicopter and dozens of equipment such as engines, dredge pumps, generators and suction equipment were seized. The action lasted 12 days and involved 75 Funai, Army, Federal Police, Ibama, ICMBio and other state agencies. Garimpo causes enormous environmental destruction, deforestation, assorting rivers and mercury contamination in communities.
ab9a81691cc729ed59a07b82915edcb116d8caa9: The Hutukara Yanomami Association (HAY) has repeatedly denounced the presence of some 20,000 prospectors operating illegally within the Yanomami IT. This estimate was made by the communities themselves, who accompany the movement of boats and rafts that arrive in the regions of the so-called “tatuzão”. Clandestine landing lanes operate within Yanomami territory to secure the supplies needed for mining action and withdraw from the location the gold found. Among the impacts of the activity, HAY denounces the opening of large digs in the land and the contamination of soil and water by mercury, as well as the introduction of drugs, alcohol, firearms, the grooming of young people and prostitution in traditional territory. The mining invasion of the Yanomami IT has been taking place for many years, but it has not had such a vast scale since the 1980s. These are sophisticated mining operations, supported by schemes involving large-scale financing by entrepreneurs who provide earthmoving equipment, supplies and aircraft. The Army confirms that they have already been seized, in several operations in the region of the Rio Mucajaí, up to 70 vessels with equipment used in the mining work. According to a survey by the State Planning Secretariat of Roraima, in the first half of 2019 a total of 288 kg of gold (equivalent to R$ 48.7 million) was exported by the state, although there is no authorized mine for gold extraction in Roraima. This ore occupies the 4th position of products exported by the state, evidencing the lack of supervision and incidence on the existing commercial scheme from the mining. According to research by Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (Fiocruz) in communities Yanomami do Amazonas attended by Dsei Yanomami, 56% of the indigenous had mercury concentrations above the limit established by WHO. HAY filed complaints with the Army, the Federal Police and the MPF. Several withdrawal and prohibition operations were carried out during 2019.
e041eeb06b73f567370fb51d18744b9e1239b4f6: From an anonymous tip, a police operation of the Independent Environmental Police Company (CIPA) caught, in Boa Vista, a fuel transport scheme for mining in the Alto Uraricoera region, located in the Yanomami IT.
ab8f1b501fc248ddf9e15fbb41a8ece9f94184b0: Indigenous people observed the movement of people at night, with lanterns, in a mountain range around the village. The volunteers from the Territorial Indigenous Protection and Surveillance Group monitored the area and found mining equipment. Later, they identified the person responsible for the activity and led it to the community, where they asked him not to resume the activity of the mining. The Legal Advisory Office of the Indigenous Council of Roraima (CIR) registered the complaint, but the Federal Police never went to the community.
28a932473f071b48e2ec72424c62fa11d01f2ed0: In 2019, stimulated by the speeches of the federal and state governments and of Roraimense parliamentarians (federal representatives and senators), mining activities within the Raposa Serra do Sol IT were resumed. Throughout 2019, President Jair Bolsonaro publicly expressed his support for mineral exploration of indigenous territories, particularly the Yanomami and Raposa Serra do Sol territories in Roraima. With the support of Roraimense deputies and senators, he published videos in which indigenous Roraimenses, without any community representation, supported this proposal of the federal government, thus configuring a manipulation of the political position of indigenous communities and organizations in the state that continue to express their total opposition to mining and mining in indigenous lands.
6421dc51e6ced3d5323cec6e91a422a7546df441: Indigenous people denounce that an electric network, installed to benefit the Fazenda do Gaúcho, crossed the ITA Araçá. No prior consultation was made with the communities of this indigenous land.
07135daa01c214594bc1f7bae12f5f35ef661d4b: An illegal camp in the Good Jesus vicinal kept illegal products that would be taken and coming from the mining areas within the Yanomami IT. 451d77ca4270cf41b34d2fb7652c38575777bb55: A leadership denounced a criminal fire that began inside the Serra do Tabuleiro State Park and almost reached the village, if it were not for the collective work of the community to contain the fire. f1ee02c60c5f82af8598952a7843d0829469c4a2: Invaders attract indigenous people from the region for illegal logging, which is marketed on farms near Xerente IT. A diversity of trees is turning to fences.
014602769a22ea606b6871abf616f0076e2d1fd8: Leaderships denounced the involvement of an indigenous, resident of the Gorgulho region, in the extraction and illegal sale of wood.

3ae5b68ff1e7623cab02bacdeb3f6a9f8d202997: Since the 1970s, when Funai made forced contact with the Avá Canoeiro people, the indigenous people suffer various violence, such as the expulsion of their traditional territory known as Mata Azul. The Declaratory Ordinance was signed in May 2016 and the process is in the phase of disintrusion, for the removal of two settlements of the Incra and the Eletroenge farm. Meanwhile, indigenous leaders are threatened by the occupants of their territory. In 2018, the people won a Public Civil Action (PCA) proposed by the MPF for the removal of occupants during the period of one year. The Declaratory Ordinance suffered several attacks by politicians in the region, such as Senator Katia Abreu and Congressman Carlos Henrique, who tried to cancel it. Lawyers and anthropologist Edward Luz were hired by agribusiness to disqualify the earth's identification and delimitation report.
5bd2d91326fcf8f3c6afe73dd12e6ff5dc01cdbd: A family composed of seven people was in the House of Indigenous Health (Casai) due to the surgical recovery of a pregnant adolescent who had been shot in a shootout between two criminal factions, which occurred on September 19. After two days of foster care at Casai, a nurse spread a rumor that members of a criminal faction would have threatened to invade Casai to kill the entire family, which left the other patients and companions in panic. The person responsible for Casai demanded from the adolescent's father that the whole family withdraw from Casai, not taking into account that it was already late Saturday night, and that the adolescent was under post-surgical care and under medication. The family had to retire, and managed to be welcomed into the house of a leadership of another people living in Rio Branco. A complaint was lodged with the MPF and the Union Public Defender. The MPF did a syndicance at Casai and found that everything was just a rumor, made of bad faith by the nurse. There was a notification to Sesai, in which assistance was requested to the adolescent in the residence where she had been received.
44fbd06e09f46078ae0b37ef004fa5269acc48c2: Army soldiers prevented a leadership and five indigenous students from entering a territory to participate in an assembly of the Içana Basin Indigenous Organization (Oibi). After denouncing the fact, the public agencies came into contradiction regarding their justifications. The representative of Funai informed that the decision to ban the indigenous would not have left the agency, and that he had directed the ban only on non-indigenouss to enter that area. The Army, in turn, reported that the order came from the indigenist organ. The name of Maria Auxiliadora Cordeiro da Silva, of the Baré people, was one of those listed by the Army and Funai, where there were other names of people who should not enter the indigenous land. Mary was one of the guests to attend the assembly of the peoples - Baniwa and Kuripako. Baniwa people themselves. The Baniwa leaders report that the Army has acted authoritarianly with the people living in that region but, on the other hand, tolerates and favors the entry of entrepreneurs interested in mining within the indigenous areas, an activity that is prohibited. André Baniwa states that the case is unprecedented in the history of Oibi and that he has already filed a complaint about what happened at Funai. Funai's regional coordinator at Alto Rio Negro, Jackson Duarte, denied that the agency had given the order to bar the leaders, but said that the non-indigenous invited by Oibi needed prior authorization from the foundation.
516375f83af1841f21ce00c1e06165ee06978fce: The community has no electricity network due to the difficulties imposed by owners of farms located in the area of the village, according to the prosecutor of the Republic Fernando Zelada. The area was recognized in 2013 as indigenous territory by Funai, when it was proven that it belongs traditionally to the community. There is an action by the MPF in progress in the Federal Court against Funai and the Union, in which the demarcation procedure is requested. According to the MPF, “the Federal Constitution provides that the indigenous land is a public good of the Union and must be used exclusively by the Indians themselves, to guarantee their rights, including access to electricity, already recognized as a social right and necessary to the dignity of everyone”.
b387b4186b2bb40a3bd662de154a092aa6d7aaaa: The indigenous was subjected to serious embarrassment when put, only in their underwear, inside a cell at the police station, where he was about nine hours without water and without food.
a361037f171238e130a19145ec867ab853d8b3c6: Indigenous leaders reported that two police officers went to the village to pick up a motorcycle that had been seized by the indigenous when they were monitoring the territory. d082b467ff0c5c830ab078281052ff654491839e: Operation A’uwe (meaning “Xavante people” in the indigenous language) caught a gang of scammers who held Xavante indigenous cards. The investigations showed that the scammers lent money to the indigenous people with interest of up to 40% and, as a guarantee of the amount borrowed, kept the bank cards and passwords. The group managed to divert more than R$ 100,000 monthly from the victims, but no one was arrested.

439e2a9c710db1e63f1979ce61327bf285a220d2: Throughout the year 2019, bank agencies made committed loans - beyond the limits allowed by law - for many Retired Xavante, causing the drastic decrease of their receipts and compromising the survival of their families. 70cf04167cbc61cd3999d4c04bd348a619de6aa0: Three Mbya Guarani were arrested by Army soldiers on highway BR-116, in Barra do Ribeiro, and led to the Camaquã police station. Unlike the version given by the Army soldiers at the police station, this Indian denounced that he had been beaten by the soldiers. An examination of the body of offense was carried out in Camaquã that morning, and found that the indigenous had actually been physically assaulted. He also complained of anal pain, typical of post-sexual pain, but did not present injury or bleeding. The body crime tests performed on both adolescents confirmed that they were not sexually abused. 5b255bd0b2b8924f06aaa544b66d19c8de3784ba: The chief receives threats due to his performance in the fight for the land.

Since the murder of two leaders, in November 2019, there has been a lot of tension among the indigenous, since the veiled threats have grown within the Indigenous Land (IT) Arariboia, where more than 12 thousand Guajajara live, as well as isolated indigenous Awá-Guajá. After these crimes, the feeling of abandonment and insecurity in the villages of this territory increased, which has no basis for supervision by the federal government. Strangers come and go at any time and sometimes cross the motorcycle villages during the evenings and the mornings. The threats received, from inside and outside the indigenous land, led the government of Maranhão to withdraw for an indefinite time three members of the Guardians group from this site. The families of Jenipapo Village live apprehensive and the 50 children who study are taken without any security, in a truck, to the school that is 7 km from the village. Without the internet or another system of communication between the villages, the indigenous do not know what happens in their own territory. 62855d9a89e902b14de4a4628dd236973427884f: In March 2019, a group of Warao indigenous peoples who were homeless, without access to official shelters, peacefully occupied an abandoned public space with non-indigenous migrant families. 8acb8475c607e4c7a726fb9170d6f3b5abdc9304: About the Arara IT of the Amônia River focuses the Extractive Reserve Alto Juruá, where there was also an Incra settlement. Seven years ago, the process of paying compensation to the non-indigenous occupying families began and was completed between the end of 2018 and the beginning of 2019. However, six families refused to accept payment and remain in the indigenous area; in 2020 these families that remained brought more people into the territory. The fact continues to generate conflicts between indigenous and occupiers, and the indigenous ask for their immediate withdrawal from justice. In addition, the community strives for the competent bodies to complete the demarcatory process that is in the last phase.
68ad2d9cb4fe73194ce542eb3da8e65da97c8dfb: The Nawá IT is traditionally occupied by the indigenous people and focuses on the Serra do Divisor National Park, created in 1989. The claim for territory began in 2000. The study of Funai, conducted in 2003, was contested by Ibama, which resulted in the judicialization of the case. With the ICMBio taking over the Park, the process remained unresolved and on the part of the body began persecution of the people, with threat of expulsion, fine application and opening of proceedings against leaders. In December 2019, an inter-institutional GT was in the territory between ICMBio and Funai, collecting information and reviewing the limits of the area requested, but this report was never issued.
88ac27f7487e63469f7ca3a26423bef51bd29962: The Nukini IT was demarcated in 1991 without including the entire territory of the people, which is why, in 2000, the Nukini claimed to Funai the revision of IT limits. The area claimed is traditionally occupied by the indigenous and focuses on the Serra do Divisor National Park. After the 2nd Meeting of Peoples Without Demarcated Land, promoted by Cimi Regional Western Amazon in May 2019, and the incidence of Nukini leaders in Brasilia with the various agencies, Funai promised to send a specialized group to do an information survey, which was done in December 2019. However, so far, the people are awaiting provision.
cdb6307d2b51e92805691327b0fa463a2356a167: Reclaimed since 2002, the Kontanawa IT is traditionally occupied by the indigenous and overlapping by the High Juruá Extractive Reserve. In November 2017, a court sentence forced Funai to begin the demarcatory process, giving a period of two years and under daily fine for noncompliance. In December 2019, the deadline expired and no procedures have been taken by Funai so far.
fc888dec83c8103522cb9abd4b3364bf3150dc80: The claim for the demarcation of the Kaxinawá territory of the Curralinho Seringal began in October 2001. The process of demarcating this IT has remained “under study” over these years. While the Union, through Funai, does not assume its responsibility in compliance with the Federal Constitution, indigenous families constantly suffer from the invasion of the territory and the agricultural expansion of the municipality of Feijó.
8d203f45b742c18278f69b38e5875f8cee2197ae: In 2004, a preliminary study was conducted in the territory of the indigenous Jaminawá and Manchineri, which resulted in the creation, in 2013, of the GT of Identification and Delimitation of the territory by Funai, to study the claim of 319,000 hectares of land. Before 2018, this indigenous land was claimed separately, respectively, with the names Guajará and Seringal Guanabara, by each of the peoples. However, in 2019, the Jaminawá and Manchineri peoples, located in these lands, decided to join in the joint struggle for the demarcation of their territory, which is contiguous, and began to call them TI Boca do Riozinho. With this action, both peoples intended to expedite the progress of the demarcation process, considering that there have been invasions and removal of many wood from the indigenous territory. In December 2019, Funai went to this land to make a prior survey of the residents and the area, but so far, the indigenous people have not received the report.
ae15b4b1063fca103ae915f97debc4d6bf8eaabb: The preliminary study of the Jaminawá IT of the Caeté River was initiated in 2004, but was not completed. Later, as reported by the community, a Funai Working Group appeared in the territory in 2012, and later in 2014. However, since then, it has never been completed or informed the community about the progress of the process. In 2018, the ICMBio went to the territory and installed landmarks in two places, warning the population and neighbors that wood could not be removed in this place, because the land was under study. However, the community has repeatedly denounced that the wood is still being extracted, even with the ban.
4167d019f1343af835d73fe72ace1de757c0d6d7: The Identification and Delimitation Working Group, in charge of building the anthropological study report of this IT, was initiated in 2006 by Funai, but was never completed. In 2011, the community received a group of researchers, supposedly from the same GT. Since then, they have never received information about the progress of the demarcation process of their territory. Meanwhile, there is a constant confrontation between the Jaminawá people of this IT with non-indigenous occupants, mainly due to deforestation caused by the latter.
8012e452b2b7e50bb62938f1afc130d823b08aff: The Identification and Delimitation GT was created in 2004, but the professionals never appeared in the field to do the field work, nor was there information about the progress of the demarcation process. According to information from the community itself, in 2014 Funai went to the area and installed plates with demarcation information that do not correspond with the area that the population would be claiming. For this reason, there are currently conflicts with farmers that invade the territory and argue that these areas do not belong to the Jaminawá of the São Paulino Indigenous Land.
6f95ba0c5071b496e75b3ce8638c2488add28002: In 2012, Jaminawá and Madija communities received a visit from Funai, and never again had any information about their demarcation process. Every year, during the winter season, the territory where these families live is flooded, and the indigenous lose their plantations and creations, and are forced to consume contaminated water from the Purus River. The upper part of the territory, which does not suffer from flooding, is in the hands of six farmers. In addition, the region has several barriers to demarcation, such as the border line with Peru, an area for the Army and an Incra settlement.
61880c95eab9543984bca810a2a147ee7c8057e5: According to the warning of the “Informa Trinational Queimadas e Deforestamento em Territoriales com Registros de Peoples of Indigenous Peoples in Isolation”, these actions pose a threat to the survival of the isolated peoples of Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay, who inhabit the Amazon, Brazilian Cerrado and Great American Chaco. They report the danger caused by deforestation and fires, which cause displacement of these populations in search of safer places, which end up submitting to the approach with neighboring populations and possible contagion of diseases, aggravated by the pandemic of the coronavirus. This further increases the vulnerability of isolated groups, as they destroy the territories on which they depend and are the basis of their survival and culture. This Report warns of the risk of genocide of these indigenous groups. It emphasizes that the origin of the increase in fires is human action, through the practices of agribusiness and logging and mining, which rely on the lack of effective action of the government in the protection of isolated indigenous peoples.
86f0521f33035563ad70b5d4f40c8242b16247d2: The Valparaiso IT has been claimed since 1991. Currently, the demarcation process is judicialized. Even with the process being in Justice, the lands of the Apurinã people began to be invaded, having the forest torn down, transformed into a field and later into a cattle farm. The municipality of Boca do Acre has the second largest herd of cattle in the state of Amazonas, losing only to the neighboring city of Lábrea.
e259ce6d0dae2b9b1ee09789c8b6a9439eead5f3: Indigenous people denounce that they went through a day of terror within their territory in Castanhal of Ajaratuba, when city tractors invaded the land, without any judicial decision, destroying the swiddens and saying they were plotting the place. Chief Eronilde Omagua-Kambaba said: “The Department of Works invaded, batching, without our permission, destroying our garden, to give land in exchange for votes. In January the same thing happened, we denounced, but nobody did anything, so he felt right to do it again. He gives the land to non-indigenous. There'll be resistance, we won't give in. We need help. We're past our limit. They threatened to kill my father and my husband.” She also denounces that the local police do nothing to protect them; that the invaders have firearms and are encouraged to shoot the indigenous, following the orders of the mayor. Funai and the Public Prosecutor's Office were activated, but these problems are recurrent due to the omission and lack of measures in the regularization of the indigenous territory.
b014f169f33444595bee7ca4c0a0ad3b2e9f5fff: After denouncing indigenous leaders and Funai, reporting the invasion of American missionary Steve Campbell at Hi-Merimã IT, the MPF opened an investigation to investigate the case. The MPF notified the Etnoenvironmental Protection Front Madeira Purus to present updated information on Campbell's activities, which is linked to the Greene Baptist Church movement, and other missionaries in the region. Illegal entry of people into indigenous land endangers the physical integrity of isolated peoples, especially in the midst of the new coronavirus pandemic. Steve Campbell has been investigated since 2019 on suspicion of joining the Jarawara/Jamadi/Kanamati IT in Lábrea.
989e8abc00cd71c7f19773c1731f2685c03c71b8: In the worst performance since the end of the military dictatorship, alongside Michel Temer, the government of Jair Bolsonaro did not demarcate any indigenous land in two years of government. However, this was his plan before he even got to the chair of the presidency. When he was still a candidate, he said that in being elected, “he would not demarcate any centimeters of indigenous land”. The Bolsonaro government, as in other sectors, militarized Funai and appointed the federal delegate Marcelo Augusto Xavier da Silva to be the president of the indigenist agency, and has been disrupting all the surveillance and protection agencies of indigenous lands, in favor of the interests of the ruralist bench and other sectors of the capital.
a84a6d0dd4616260eae808f5b3b7c718826ab8ff: Based on false complaints from farmers who, at all costs, wanted to prevent the sanitary barrier of protection to indigenous land, military policemen in the municipality of Careiro da Várzea, invaded the territory with the intention of destroying the barrier. The police pointed weapons to the indigenous who were on duty at the barrier and entered the village Sissaíma without wearing protective masks, to avoid contagion of the community. In this operation, in addition to threatening people, they seized indigenous objects (hunches and arrows). Before that, the farmers had already destroyed the signs and tried to destroy the barrier, with threats to the Indians. As if this truculent action by the police is not enough, it is also observed the invasion of the indigenous territory in several places that were deforested, with the timber removed and marketed illegally; the deforested sites are used for new pasture areas. In addition to invasion and deforestation, illegal fishing and improper occupation are also taking place in the territory. Faced with such conflicts, the Mura had to suspend the protection barrier against Covid-19. With the pandemic, indigenous people saw persecution, diseases, neglect and invasions grow in their own territory. Leaderships have referred a complaint to the MPF and await action.
3434dffc78c3c6f66d8238e7aac5dddd53ba7a7a: During an illegal operation in August, the military police invaded the village of Pilão, threatening indigenous people who were there, turning houses and the historical church of the site. Work equipment and personal effects of the indigenous were thrown and destroyed. The church, of historical value, was turned over, and some objects that were in it, also of historical and cultural value to the indigenous people, were destroyed; because the door of the church was broken into, the entrance of animals was facilitated. The conflict took place in the context of the “massacre of the Pineapple River”, a police operation in the region of the Pineapple and Marimari rivers, in the municipalities of Nova Olinda do Norte and Borba (AM), which resulted in the murder of two indigenous people of the Munduruku people of the Coatá-Laranjal and four riversides, in addition to the disappearance of two other riversides and a series of human rights violations committed by the PM against local communities. Federal police are investigating the case.
6f20db16d91a9013dd4a8e2593d6b394ff4ba46c: Currian IT is located on the right bank of those who climb the Purus River. It is an area very rich in natural resources, which sharpens the desire of explorers. According to the chief, the riverside invaders known as Leandro and Alex were entering the indigenous territory through the Joari Igarapé, then began to invade the main lake of the village by Igarapé Curriã, which gives entrance to the village Bom Jesus and the village Curriã, challenging the indigenous people. The community instructed them to leave with all their equipment and not return. For more than 20 years, the Apurinã have been fighting for the demarcation of the area, but so far it is not even registered in Funai databases in Brasilia.

0bcf9283e6ab16823c6a0e84cd1acd0631ab7415: Since 1980, the indigenous peoples of Apurinã and Jamamadi from this IT have been fighting for the demarcation of their territories. Although the demarcation process started 17 years ago, and the Identification and Delimitation GT was shaped twice – 2003 and 2014 – the demarcation has not been completed so far. The Apurinã and Jamamadi communities request speed of the demarcation process initiated, since the actions that affect the territory only advance, such as invasions in the area, and deforestation by the Management and Settlement Plan, promoted by Incra. Since 2019, the Apurinã and Jamamadi peoples of Lourdes and Cajueiro have asked Funai for the unification of the process, in continuous territory, with the name of Massacury Kamapa, shared by both peoples. 968e45dd64f56cf0ecebf8e2bac5740da61bc08a: The Apurinã and Jamamadi peoples of this IT are constantly threatened by farmers who want to drive them out of this territory. Currently, families are confined in a small space. To date, only one preliminary study was conducted by Funai in 2003, and it was not continued. Later, in 2012, an anthropological study was conducted on the impacts of the construction of BR-317, which links Boca do Acre (AM) to Rio Branco (AC), which also did not advance much. The Jamamadi population requires the continuity of anthropological studies and the formation of the Identification and Delimitation GT to prevent farmers from continuing to buy lots inside and outside this indigenous land. Since 2019, the communities Apurinã and Jamamadi do Monte II, Iquirema and Goiaba have decided to unite in the search for demarcation of their contiguous territories, requesting the demarcation of a single indigenous land.
19ef0cdef07d4dfabe49995bf2ae0c9fd56ffd5c: The Jamamadi indigenous people have been asking Funai, repeatedly, to create the Working Group for Identification and Delimitation of their territory, but so far they have not been attended. This study did not continue.
c2ef3c5eb47b987af05e2c254918b9134c1210e8: The invasions in IT Patauá continued to occur in 2020. The fact that the whole country has experienced a pitiful pandemic situation due to the Covid-19 has not prevented invasions from advancing over indigenous lands. The Patauá TI is bordered by a farm, and the conflicts and threats to indigenous people are constant, because the farmer prevents the free transit of indigenous people in his own territory. Funai's delay in expediting the demarcatory processes of indigenous lands has favored that conflicts, invasions and violence of all kinds continue to be committed against indigenous people. This year, not only the indigenous people were threatened by the farmer, but also members of the Cimi team.
517af60481921d8efd0ce5ec4b75169fabfb1db8: Leaderships denounce the abandonment of interest of the Union/Funai in the defense of the Tupinambá people of Olivença in lawsuit of possession of traditional area located in Serra das Trempes. The action seeks to evict the indigenous from the property called Conjunto Santa Maria, incident on the indigenous land. In his order, the president of Funai, Marcelo Xavier, says that “it is up to the integrated Indians to answer for their actions, because it is about invasion of private property”, contrary to what the Federal Constitution provides. Funai has an obligation to defend its administrative acts – in this case, the demarcation of Tupinambá territory. The Union has an obligation to defend indigenous lands, which are public heritage.
af65216253310164628d4083b8865afa4222a32f: Pataxó Indians received an illegal eviction threat from the owners of Sky Dream Pilot School, through action that called for the withdrawal of about 27 families from the site. The area where these families meet is part of the land claimed by the indigenous peoples, in the process of demarcation at Funai. The leaders denounced that the perpetrators of the action do not have title of ownership of the land to claim it; they also denounced the omission of Funai that, instead of defending the indigenous and presenting the evidence about the situation of the land, tried to make them cooperate with the eviction. Due to the slowness of Funai and the Ministry of Justice in regulating its territory, the Pataxó people face several challenges in the region, with the predatory advance on their lands by tourism entrepreneurs, real estate companies, hotels, resorts, and the cellulose agroindustry. The Pataxó appealed to the Supreme Court.
252ac88beabdb910dbb7dd08c86e72f40b5be83a: Contrary to the determination of the Supreme Court, which suspended any reintegration of possessions during the pandemic, the Federal Court determined the eviction of the village Novos Guerreiros, located in the Red Crown Indigenous Land, of the Pataxó people, in Porto Seguro, southern Bahia coast. In the village live 24 families, and the area was resumed more than a year ago. According to chief Ararawe Pataxó, in the village live around 2,500 indigenous people, among adults, elders and children. “In time of pandemic, the judge wants to put us out of our village. We have nowhere to put our people. We're asking for help because if this eviction happens, we have nowhere to go. This is our land, consecrated. It is part of the traditional territory of the people”, said the chief. On August 27, the Federal Police was in the village New Warriors to summon the Pataxó families to withdraw from the area. The Federal Justice measure serves owners of an Aviation Club. The Pataxó were surprised to hear from the police that the village needed to be evicted because the indigenous occupy the airstrip of the Aviation Club. The Indians are in a nearby area, keeping distance from the runway. 92 entities, between social movements, universities, foundations and non-governmental organizations, signed a manifesto organized by Mupoiba, Apoinme and Finpat, in which they repudiated the decision of the Federal Court and asked the competent authorities to “provide for the rights of the Pataxó to be guaranteed and the ruling of the Supreme Court to be respected”.
b5633727567a26aec2bde3525352562f4dfe0be4: Leaderships denounce that the slowness of the government in regulating indigenous lands has favored criminal factions to invade the areas and recruit mainly young people to act in organized groups; that traffickers make use of real estate to store weapons and drugs, and that residents are being expelled from their homes. They report that schools and health centers are tarnished with threats and inscriptions concerning criminal factions. Residents fear to go out at night, claiming that the region is dominated by drug trafficking. The indigenous also report that there is no public safety in the region.
9a9c78ba15bdbd662393e95eda5fdc31d4fd2ab2: The Federation of Peoples and Indigenous Organizations of Ceará (Fepoince) denounces that 96% of indigenous territories in the state have no consolidated demarcation. The delay in demarcatory processes has been dragging for years and harming more than 35,000 indigenous people living there. Of the 25 Indigenous Lands, only the Córrego do João Pereira, of the people Tremembé do Capim Açu, in Itarema, is completed, and the IT of Anacé, in Caucaia, awaits only the registration. According to Weibe Tapeba, who is a legal advisor to Fepoince, the situation is critical and worrying, because most people in the region have no legal certainty.
8aec84d75769f92a99717ced0520e99a153ac6b8: According to chief Roberto Anacé, criminals set fire to the forest, which lies in an area of territorial pretension of the Anacé people, burning several sacred trees and animals. For years, the community has been struggling for the regularization of its traditional territory; tired of waiting for the demarcation of the area, the Mangabeira Village community has resumed the area, causing several threats by local squatters. Complaints have been made to MPF and Funai but, so far, no action has been taken.
3bed0b989adac6be10a4a39ce753b72e46ef88e5: Indigenous members of the “Guardians of the Forest” group discovered a cattle farm within IT. They reported that more than 140 hectares have been deforested in the area next to Lago Branco Village. They triggered several federal and state agencies of supervision and control, Funai, Environmental Police and Ibama, who were on site. The Guajajara suffer from invasions of their territory, destruction of natural resources and violence, awaiting measures regarding the regularization and supervision of their lands. The leaders denounce the omission of the federal government regarding the indigenous and environmental cause.
177b540495b5442c7403cd902687377468a47ddd: A marijuana plantation was found by police using a drone, which visualized about three hectares of deforested forest. The operation involved military police, Funai and indigenous leaders and found about 8,000 feet of marijuana planted by traffickers within the Caru IT. At the scene, in addition to marijuana feet, the police found 200 kilograms of pressed drugs and 60 kilograms of seed. The criminals responsible for the plantation, when they realize the movement, have fled through the woods and are being sought by the police. IT is a constant target of drug traffickers who invade the territory to plant drugs, and the dense forest helps hide the crops.
10171fd6a1672cf6c02a762ef1644fa6475d7bf9: Attack on the village with firearms
8b3046ab4a44ad720b1ea4982a312c160cae1c39: Leaderships of the Guajajara people denounced attack on Kwaxi Kamihaw village by more than 40 armed men. According to the Indians, the men were led and organized by Isaiah Tavares Albuquerque, who lives in the neighborhood Nova Grajaú, and by Abraham da Conceição Santos, who claims to be heir to the indigenous land. The Jagunços have already arrived in the village shooting at the houses, destroying them and burning them; they have also destroyed objects of personal use, nets, clothes, containers, food, motorcycles and everything they found ahead. The Indians, frightened, fled the place, leaving everything behind, including the animals raised to support families. The indigenous land has been declared permanent possession of the Guajajara people since June 30, 2008, by Ordinance 1234 of the Ministry of Justice, but the demarcation process has not been completed. An occurrence report was registered at the Grajaú Civil Police (MA) and a complaint at Funai.
fb7cc381d375d11015b8490b9860221f001f1c0c: In 2014, the municipality of Juína filed a lawsuit against Funai to request the nullity of the administrative procedure no. 08620000726200065 and its acts, which aims to review the demarcation to include the region of Adowina (Rio Preto) in the Enawenê-Nawê IT. In the same year, the federal judge of Juina granted injunction to suspend the procedure. On October 25, 2016, the judge gave a final sentence, confirming the nullity of the demarcation procedure for lack of subpoena of the municipality and ensuring the anticipation of guardianship. Funai and MPF filed an appeal appeal, which is in TRF-1. The community never participated in the lawsuit, so in 2018, the leaders asked Cimi to enable them in this action. Following that, the municipality was opposed to the entrance of the community, however MPF and AGU were favorable. There is still no decision on community entry or appeal.
87b037081b1105e0f3dba4366219d5fedd00d357: Hydropower construction (PCH); breach of prior consultation
66ba0f19c44052a6bf328a9ff1e93c65d2d9bd82: Negotiations for the construction of the Jesuit PCH and UHE Cachoeirão, both in the Juruena River basin, are taking place without obeying the process of Prior Consultation, Free and Informed to the indigenous populations, according to the ILO Convention 169. The licensing project provides for the installation of the PCH structure in the Juruena river, part of the Amazon river basin, located in the municipalities of Campos de Júlio and Sapezal, both in the state of Mato Grosso, and the electricity transmission system generated by the PCH, including transmission lines and existing substations and to be built and/or expanded. On August 26, 2020, through Dispatch no. 2,489, Aneel registered the “adequateness of UHE Cachoeirão inventory studies”, pleaded by Maggi Energia S.A.
f09b787852e8c6ecdd59e9818c8ad8a24b68ad3c: Leaderships denounce that an armed group threatened and shot against the resumption Ñu Verá. They report that two landlords were accompanied by the National Force. The motivation would be because the indigenous had questioned the use of the “venom forger”, as they call land vehicles that spread agrotoxic in large quantities in the areas of planting, and that affect the indigenous areas, the people who inhabit it and the whole environment. One indigenous was injured in the arm and the entire community, including children and the elderly, was terrified of such violence. On the same day, around 10:00 p.m., the Indians were again attacked by private security. In this region the conflicts intensified, especially after the election of Bolsonaro, and the site has been considered by the Guarani people as an area of war. Several complaints were made to the MPF, Federal Police and Funai, but the trend is that conflicts remain until the land issue is resolved.
288da80509c69205c617851e5f95ba2f5fb83ed0: Leaderships denounce that the community is threatened daily by private security, hired by ruralists; they also report that almost every day private security guards arrive by truck in the quiet of the night to take down their shacks, fire and assault the indigenous, to leave the houses and the area resumed. They report that the region has always been very violent, due to land conflicts and the omission of the government to regulate indigenous lands. In this episode, a group of private security guards arrived armed and shot at the retake. The authorities have been reported. Representatives of the National Human Rights Council heard the indigenous, who reported that security in the region became worse with the presence of the National Force; that when the troops appear it is to side with the ruralists. The community is apprehensive and under constant fear and threats, awaiting provision from the Public Prosecutor, Funai and other authorities.
d304bb6b996cd738eb83431ca1cf1d5e1d3f6030: Leaders denounce the brutal attack on the indigenous area by private security guards of ruralists and also by military police who have already arrived shooting. The attacks occurred at night and throughout the next day. Indigenous people report verbal and physical threats, destruction of their homes, gunshots from firearms, rubber bullets and even the use of light and sound grenades, considered nonlethal. One of these artifacts ended up exploding in the hands of a 12-year-old child, who lost three fingers in his left hand. At least four Indians were injured by gun and gun shots, one of them in the face. There live more than 50 indigenous families, including children and the elderly, claiming for years the regularization of their traditional territory. Due to Funai's omission to continue the demarcatory process, the region is constantly invaded and the indigenous peoples threatened and assaulted violently, in the intention of giving up the struggle and abandoning their territory. Conflicts are frequent and increasingly violent, including by the public force that should defend them. Several complaints were made in the MPF, Funai, Federal Police, among others, and the Guarani-Kaiowá people remain waiting for justice.
2843c1278b1b7767fcdf2a6769f074623d632a55: According to the community, a group of armed security guards from the area claimed as indigenous land, in the region bordering the Golden Reserve, attacked the community at dawn and burned the Oga Pysy – Casa de Reza, newly built by the community in the territory resumed. The week before, on April 9, the same armed group had attacked the community for the seventh time in the year, tearing down the shacks and burning their belongings. The leaders referred a complaint to the MPF and asked for measures.
73ce8d55897e2ed0238adc168232660e0e6e8de3: Leaders and representatives of the municipality were prevented from installing a water supply network to serve indigenous families, by a group of farmers and squatters who used force and threats. The area in question is in judicial dispute, and was resumed by the Xakriabá in September 2013; the Identification and Delimitation Report was published in the Official Gazette of the Union on October 6, 2014, but so far the process of regularization of the territory has not been completed. Indigenous families constantly suffer threats and acts of violence promoted and articulated by the organization of farmers who are supported by the ruralist and agribusiness bench.
f4433fc511d5c00c54c1c1bdfaf6b8b0a0d02dc7: Invasion and exploitation of unregulated area
45cf76b7f7cbf20eecc96d93e36fb8dd0a3075d3: In addition to the daily impact caused by the Vitória-Minas Railway (EFVM) and the Aimorés Hydroelectric Plant, both owned by Vale S.A mining company, as well as by the death of the Watu River – the Doce River, in the Krenak language – after the break of the Fundão dam in Mariana (MG), indigenous people suffer from the pressure of invaders on the Seven Halls region. Claimed as a sacred place by the indigenous peoples, the area was subtracted from the Krenak territory and transformed into a conservation unit, the Seven Halls State Park. The area, whose regularization as indigenous land is claimed by the people, suffers from the invasion of illegal hunters, indiscriminate withdrawal of palms and even the theft and destruction of the cave paintings of the sacred territory of the Krenak. Illegal extraction of ores and exploitation of mineral water by invading farmers, even using the name of the people for the commercialization of mineral water.
099f1650b3da3a54edb6e4d3f87d6ac1be875641: In 2014, Funai recognized, through the publication of the detailed report of identification and delimitation, the traditionality of the occupation of 43,357 hectares of Xakriabá territory, covering important resources of extraction, agricultural areas and access to the São Francisco River. About 21,000 hectares of this area have already been recovered by the people through resumption actions. The paralysis of the administrative process of demarcation and the delay in issuing the declaratory ordinance, however, causes the continuation of the devastation of the territory in the possession of non-indigenous people, who practice on a large scale the raising of beef cattle and the planting of soybeans, corn and bananas. As a consequence, the Xakriabá people are affected by the exploitation, pollution and poisoning of the waters of the São Francisco River, the area's grill, exploitation of indigenous labor, violence and criminalization resulting from the conflict, impoverishment of indigenous families, lack of access to water and insufficient food production due to the invasion processes.
399435db0073556d620bd33b99c6671d3e5f8906: The STF authorized direct negotiation between the City Hall of São Félix do Xingu and the Union, without consultation with the indigenous people or the MPF, on the reduction of Apyterewa IT. The rapporteur of the case at the Supreme Court, Minister Gilmar Mendes, welcomed the request of the city of São Félix do Xingu and farmers' associations against the act of the President of the Republic who, in 2007, demarcated the Apyterewa IT. The MPF expressed itself to review the decision of the Supreme Court Minister and to hold a public hearing with the public agencies involved, mainly representatives of indigenous peoples and the MPF.
d0cf3005e1a8f77fd8eac6ba2919b68f32f4ec90: False report aimed at reducing territory
31e53d37b2fd7f805e70218a84c15a4f9fd5b2f5: Report prepared by the Ministry of Women, Family and Human Rights contradicts decisions of Justice and attacks, without presenting evidence, the demarcation of the indigenous land Apyterewa, in southern Pará, one of the most deforested in the country in recent years. The report adopts the argument of ruralists and says that the process of demarcation of the area would have been “evicted” of irregularities, a thesis rejected by the Justice. The report was made after a trip from the ministry to the indigenous land, carried out at the request of the ruralist bench. The document was signed by the national secretary replacing policies to promote racial equality of the MMFDH, Esequiel Roque, who was in the indigenous land in October. He went to the site at the request of Senator Zequinha Marinho (PSC-PA), vice president of the Parliamentary Front of Agriculture (FPA), also known as ruralist bench. The aim of the trip was to verify possible human rights violations of the invaders of the indigenous land. Even without presenting concrete evidence, the MMFDH report adheres to the thesis of ruralists contrary to demarcation. According to him, these alleged irregularities “reduced from illegality the demarcatory process”. In the evaluation of Apib's lawyer, Luiz Eloy Terena, the report drew attention to the federal government's willingness to check the demarcation of an indigenous land. According to Eloy, this demarcation was made by the Brazilian State and the ministry commanded by Damares Alves is acting against an act of the State itself. This demarcation has already been finalized and questioned in Justice and decisions are favorable to indigenous people. Parakanan leaders living in Apyterewa territory report that invaders have tried to enlist important leaders of the village.
ae9ccaa72958950bf3d5fb479622079c00e6d7d0: Denial of MPF information on demarcations
856f2abce5843560bc8032ce3cce97ec9889d50e: The MPF in Santarém filed a security warrant with a request to grant an injunction, in the face of acts of the President and the Director of Territorial Protection (DPT) of Funai, before the negative access of the MPF to information and the records of administrative procedures for demarcation of indigenous lands in Pará, even after express ministerial request. Meanwhile, the various indigenous peoples of the region have been suffering from invasions of their territories, depredation of the environment, violence of all kinds, in the middle of the coronavirus pandemic.
76a428ff9d5d841278af2b8f66589ba7bf7e5cb3: Invasion and attempt to co-opt leaders
2ae2165f8446ee8303a0ec8533a2d2bcf35ed0b0: The Tato’a Indigenous Association issued a document to the MPF denouncing the surprise with the arrival of representatives of the Ministry of Women, Family and Human Rights, on October 18, 2020, at the farm headquarters irregularly located in the indigenous territory, in the region known as Paredão. They report that some of the leaders were called to attend a meeting at the Funai protection base, with the aim of dealing with the invasion of the indigenous land. In the middle of the way they were moved to the headquarters of this farm, where representatives of the Ministry of Human Rights, representatives of the invaders and the city of São Félix do Xingu were already present. At this moment, the objective of the meeting was clear: to pressure the leaders present to accept the proposal to reduce the limits of the territory. Not for another reason, the meeting was held in secret, at the farm headquarters of an irregular occupant, without the presence of the MPF or even the Funai, with a few leaders of the Parakanã people. According to the Association, it was “an additional ruse of the federal government, allied with the invaders and the City Hall of São Félix, to cause internal division and confuse the leaders of the Parakanã people, with the eternal promise that the reduction of the territory will resolve the conflicts and bring peace to the Parakanã people”. The indigenous denounce the invasion of their lands, the omission federal government and the bodies that should make their defense and protection and reiterate the need for the disintrusion of their territory.
7c642e62e73ba0eafe064c0ef0eb50f3267dae0b: The MPF in Pará proposed Public Civil Action against the National Mining Agency (ANM) asking that the mining processes overlapping with indigenous lands be cancelled or rejected, in the area of circumscription of the Santarém Judicial Subsection. The MPF points out that the request covers not only the declared and approved ITs, but also those identified and delimited. According to the MPF, there are mining processes overlapping with 13 ITs – in different stages of regularization – located in the Santarém Judicial Subsection region. The MPF points out that the cancellation or rejection of requests is necessary because these mining requirements are used to confer an apparent legitimacy to illegal exploitation, especially mining in indigenous lands, generating significant socio-environmental impacts. The Action was granted by the Federal Justice and the indigenous peoples living in the region expect compliance.
6a4f540ee45cf4d65274671e3c77e27462a76252: The MPF and the MPE of Pará filed environmental civil action against the state of Pará and Atem’s Petroleum Distributor Ltda, aiming at the nullity of the previous license and the license to install the construction of a port in Lake Maicá, both issued in February 2019 by the State Department of Environment and Sustainability of Pará (Sema). The MPF argues that the licenses were issued without prior consultation, free and informed to the indigenous, quilombolas and fishermen affected by the project, as determined by ILO Convention 169, there was no evaluation of the impacts of the work on these peoples and, moreover, there was an undue waiver of the elaboration of Environmental Impact Study and Environmental Impact Report (EIA/Rima). In addition, according to the MPF, the licensing was conducted by an incompetent body. The Federal Court granted the request of the MPF, suspending the licenses and determining that Atem’s paralyze the works. For years, indigenous and quilombolas have been questioning the construction of the port on site, which will directly affect the Lake and the streams that are the source of its food and indispensable element for the maintenance of its traditional way of life.
f140e7742d9cbc754cbe1088003da3263746c297: A Public Civil Action filed by the MPF against União, Ibama, Funai and Norte Energia asked for measures to redefine the Indigenous Component of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Plant and immediate intervention in the management, execution and control of the Basic Environmental Plan, with the aim of making viable the operation of the enterprise for indigenous peoples. The Federal Court has granted and determined that the Union and Funai present, within 90 days, a schedule for completion of the land regularization processes of the Paquiçamba Indigenous Lands (demarcation, approval and disintrusion) and Cachoeira Seca (disintrusion), for being conditions of the project. The Justice has determined that evidence of the completion of the physical demarcation of the IT Paquiçamba and guarantee of budget resource for the compensation of families of good faith occupants of the TI Cachoeira Seca. Indigenous communities await compliance with the judicial decision.
1b20915b7f42d2ccf8ca0296a70c9309d62835d7: In view of the seriousness of the situation experienced by the Parakanã, who have been waiting for years for the regularization of their territory, the MPF in Pará made a recommendation to the president of Funai, signed by 15 prosecutors, for immediate reconstruction of the GT “Operation Apyterewa”, as well as the immediate resumption of the disintrusion of the Apyterewa IT, traditionally occupied by the Parakanã people.
e3f5c999c4e23d354751cf9629f98a34a502937d: The MPF entered with eight lawsuits, in all sections of the Federal Court in Pará, to suspend the effects of the normative instruction 09/2020 of Funai, which released the certification of private properties on indigenous lands that were not approved by the Brazilian government, unprotecting and facilitating the greasing of 37 indigenous lands located in the territory of the state. In addition to Funai, Incra is also defendant in the actions of MPF. The lawsuits request, in an emergency regime, that the Justice compel Funai and Incra to maintain or include all indigenous lands of the state in the Fund Management System (Sigef) and the Rural Environmental Registry System (Sicar), regardless of the stage of its demarcatory process. According to the MPF, the Normative of Funai had as practical consequence to hide from Sigef all unapproved ITs, “allowing individuals to obtain statements, conduct legal business (without any mention of the nature of the area and overlap with indigenous lands) and put at indigenous risk and the environment”. For the prosecutors of the Republic who work in the municipalities of Santarém, Redenção, Altamira, Itaituba, Marabá, Tucuruí, Belém and Castanhal, if the ordinance is not suspended urgently, there will be an increase in land conflicts and the risk of spreading Covid-19 among indigenous peoples. The MPF, as soon as the publication of IN 09/2020 was published, forwarded a recommendation to the presidency of Funai that the rules be annulled and, to Incra, not to comply with it. The recommendation, signed by 49 prosecutors and prosecutors of the Republic of 23 states of the federation, was ignored by Funai. Given the non-compliance with the recommendation, the MPF had to trigger the Federal Court. The MPF explains that Funai’s ordinance “violates advertising and legal certainty by completely disregarding delimited indigenous lands, declared indigenous lands and physically demarcated indigenous lands, in addition to those banned, with restrictions on the use and entry of third parties, for the protection of indigenous peoples in voluntary isolation”. For prosecutors, the rules, among other aspects, contradict the originating character of the rights of indigenous peoples to their lands and the declaratory nature of the demarcation act, besides creating undue precedence of private property over indigenous lands, which is blatantly unconstitutional and contradicts even international treaties of which Brazil is a signatory, such as the ILO Convention 169, the UN Declaration On the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and the decisions of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights on the subject.
8ad76db8054524baad022df14b878829ed98249c: The MPF asked the Federal Court for Funai to be required to suspend the ordinance that changed the original composition of the Working Group (GT) responsible for the elaboration of the Circumstantial Report of Identification and Delimitation (RCID) of the territory claimed by the Munduruku indigenous people in the area known as the Santareno Plateau in Santarém, in the west of Pará. From September to December 2019, Funai unfulfilled three orders of the Federal Court for the provision of the second stage of the field work to be taken, and on the last day of that year, published in the Official Gazette of the Union a ordinance that changed the composition of the group. For the MPF, this change is “another chapter of the deliberate non-compliance of judicial decisions and undue political intervention in the administrative demarcation process by the president of Funai”. The MPF also requested that the Court determine the increase and execution of the personal fine to the Funai authorities responsible for non-compliance with judicial decisions, highlighting that the constitution of the GT “is not a discretionary administrative act that can be revoked by criteria of convenience and opportunity”. On February 20, 2020, the Federal Court annulled Funai's ordinance, complying with MPF's request.
72f7607a6584a09a738df3f54c956212d763b142: Ituna-Itatá IT, located in the Xingu River basin, is inhabited by an isolated indigenous people, who began to be seriously threatened by the construction of the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant. Funai has had news of its existence since 1989. Further studies, however, were only carried out in 2009 and culminated with the Order of Interdiction of IT by the indigenous agency. With the construction of the dam, the region became the target of the action of landowners and loggers, and there was an increase in deforestation, which exploded inside the indigenous territory in 2019, being 656% higher compared to 2018. Deforestation within IT increased by 60% in the first four months of 2020, according to the Deter system deforestation alerts from Inpe. Individuals declare themselves owners of 94% of the indigenous land through records in the Rural Environmental Register, the CAR. Given the extent of the invasion, the isolated Indians, in addition to being subjected to physical violence by the invaders, may be exposed to contagion by Covid-19.
2705f2abe394585aa603ecb33e159af27ad8dc9c: Since 2006, the Tabajara people have been fighting for the recognition and demarcation of their territory, located in the municipality of Conde - PB. The demarcation process was initiated by Funai, but the report of the Working Group (GT) has not even been published yet, so that the process can proceed. Even so, the people resist, occupying part of the territory claimed, organized in 3 villages: Village Vitória, Village Barra de Gramame and Village Nova Conquista with approximately 900 people in all.
710cba7c0a1064c216a6cba30573bfa02e9a7ee7: Since 2009, the process of demarcation of the Monte Mor IT has been paralyzed, with only the approval by the president of the republic. Meanwhile, the Potiguara community continues to face serious and constant conflicts with squatters.
a465221329b450bfa0c36bd5a7236a57dd0f0477: A decision of the judge Gustavo Chies Cignachi, of the Federal Justice of Guaíra, determined the suspension of any act of demarcation of indigenous lands in the municipalities of Guaíra and Terra Roxa and the annulment of the identification report and delimitation of the Indigenous Land Tekoha Guasu Guavirá, which comprises 14 Guarani villages located in both cities. The measure takes place amid recent reports of physical aggression, threats and attacks against indigenous peoples in the villages of the region. The decision of the Federal Court can further aggravate the conflicts that are already triggered in the western region of Paraná.
16261876d349dd5005a2c3105765ec7c214bfd4a: Nullity of demarcation of indigenous land
4c9de9f0c24a2026543047e563af0b742ddf5ae8: Funai published Ordinance 418, declaring the nullity of the administrative process of identification and delimitation of TI Tekohá Guasu Guavirá, heeding the decision of the Federal Justice in process moved by the municipality of Guaíra. The action called for the nullity of all acts committed by Funai in the demarcation procedure, because it was not guaranteed to participate in all phases of the procedure, instituted by Funai in 2009; however, the struggle of the indigenous goes back to the 1980s, always surrounded by conflicts with farmers and sufferings of indigenous families. Leadership reports that Funai is failing to fulfill its constitutional role in defending the rights of indigenous peoples.
53f69ef9710cdb8016d9af470248e8ede6921085: Destruction of the village entrance gate
38ac95992b5315cc2cbfea2e3f2c53b5eb85faf9: The indigenous couple of the Guarani people, Marilene Escobar and Vilson Moreira, reports that they found the entrance gate of the village knocked down and damaged. This gate was located on the road that gives access to the villas and where a new house is being built. This place, where the gate was, served as a sanitary barrier, for greater security for the indigenous who are building a new village.
c2f3c045c0861ec8221dcccd45d1243bc6167665: Since 2008, Pankará do Serrote dos Campos people have been suffering from the attacks by local politicians to build a nuclear power plant in their territory. This fact has generated fear and insecurity in the local population, and the leaders have been suffering persecution and threats for being contrary to the construction of the plant. Thus, the community has mobilized with the sectors of social movements in the struggle for demarcation of their claimed territory.
a711d9dd16e155fae231860114a64eb18239e065: Destruction of orchards; lack of supervision
f152510e381097d6ba89968eeab029020dc5da48: Since the mid-1980s, when the Miguelenos and Puruborá were expelled from their traditional territory, called Limoeiro, the community remained united. In the site the Biological Area of Guaporé was created, and the houses they had there were gradually destroyed. They remained in part of the territory, fighting for regularization, where they live according to their cultures and traditions. Families began to produce fruit trees, the fruits of which served as food for the community and the animals of the forest. In early 2020, the community was surprised to encounter ICMBio employees applying poison to exterminate the orchards. Leaderships have filed a complaint document to the MPF and await action. In the document, they also ask for measures regarding the delay in the land regularization process, lack of supervision on fishing activity in the region, and deforestation of fruit trees.
962d4382898e564408b1b18105a8e39c973a0f07: Leaderships report and the website “Keeping an eye on ruralists” confirms that the state of Rondônia registered 84 private properties through the Rural Environmental Register (CAR) to invading landowners, who are occupying the ITs Karipuna and Karitiana. With the CAR, in addition to seeking to legitimize the improper occupation of the land, the invaders are still destroying it; feeling legitimate, they are overthrowing the forest and planting grass inside the indigenous lands. Leaderships sent complaint document and request of actions to the MPF.

d8f8c68e94554d36035b5ad39e6ec750d1dc48f7: Wood removed from within the indigenous land was overthrown, transported and marketed illegally. A man was arrested by the Military Police in a truck, carrying a load of wood taken from the Parabubure IT.
860d240ac62eba9e90a5a5134ff65d081495d949: Leaderships have reported illegal invasion and logging within the Guaporé Valley IT. Military police accompanied by Funai servers were at the scene and found environmental crime; they saw that the woods were already processed and ready to be removed from the site. Six men were arrested and firearms, ammunition, chainsaws and others seized.
c67dffe7a82433ae14e2dc7394e383648412fbf8: Fire of grave proportions reached Tadarimana IT. Since the beginning of August, when the fires began, it is estimated that the devastation reaches 90% of the territory, equivalent to more than 5,000 hectares of destroyed vegetation. The area is difficult to access, which made it difficult to fight the flames by the Fire Department. The fires added to the pandemic situation by coronavirus and the lack of health care led the indigenous to even more suffering and difficulties in the struggle for survival.
60749427d76b454cfa4de6ae0f0a2a2c99acbac9: A fire of great proportions destroyed more than 20,000 hectares of vegetation within the Pareci Indigenous Land, reaching the Cerrado and Amazonian Forest biomes. Whole families were affected, requiring medical attention, especially children and elderly who, due to smoke, had respiratory diseases.
489064687f0c4283ba368047964a2dde845eda0f: Many outbreaks of fire have been verified in TI Tereza Cristina, where the Bororo people live. Much of the vegetation was destroyed and the indigenous were affected by severe respiratory problems.
2912881e4b94d46040bfa78270b7adca7d3088b1: Survey by the Public Agency, from satellite data from the National Institute of Space Research (INPE), identified that only in September, 164 outbreaks of fire advanced on indigenous lands in the Pantanal, and more than 200 occurred in August. Almost half of the indigenous lands regulated in the region faced fires and destruction of houses, gardens, forests, water sources and caused health damage, especially of the elderly and children, leading them to hospitalizations for respiratory problems. The data also shows that in some of the places that suffered the most from the fires, the outbreaks of fire appeared and multiplied first in private properties, then take the indigenous lands. And yet that part of the fire began in areas of legal reserve and native forest of landowners, which are protected by law and must be preserved. The situation is very serious.
d26dccc608f53e2646f55c887650eafca441ed28: The arsons have taken on frightening proportions this year. Reports based on scientific studies from the Instituto Centro de Vida (ICV) and the European Space Agency (ESA) found that one of the outbreaks of fire in Mato Grosso, which destroyed 90% of the Parque Encontro das Águas, the main refuge of ounces of Pantanal and the world, originated in a clandestine farm, which does not appear in official databases. The farm borders Bororo territory and is also close to the territory of the Guató, which was hit by the same fire in almost all of its 19,000 hectares. The crime is being investigated by the Federal Police and the MPF.
264a35bc26160e517463854fb4a8c006268c8d96: Deforestation of an area equivalent to more than 360 hectares was recorded within IT, where the last two survivors of the Piripkura people live, in a situation of voluntary isolation. This is an area that is invaded by landowners, which has been destroying the environment and threatening the survival of these people. The destruction was done by a shallow cut and the area was all torn down, a typical process associated with the greasing, in which the dematador cleans the area to consolidate its irregular property. The two Indians are survivors of a massacre of loggers in the 1980s. The surrounding area became pasture and soybean plantation. The FUNAI Normative Instruction 09/2020 is encouraging invaders to advance in the regularization of properties in indigenous lands still in the process of demarcation. According to data from the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), the Piripkura IT registered in 2020 at least 1,600 hectares of burning area, which is directly related to illegal deforestation.
86e041eaf4052b9421714de42b8f4c3bd1c77eac: Survey made Global Forest Watch points out that Indigenous Lands were devastated by more than 115,000 fires that occurred between the beginning of 2020 and October 29. Satellite data reveal that the ITs most affected in 2020 were the Xingu (MT), Araguaia Park (TO) and Kayapó (PA). Of the more than 724 ITs considered in the survey, 448 recorded fires in the period, i.e. 61%, according to data from NASA's active fires. The TI Parque do Xingu (MT), with 16 people and 500 villages, was the most affected, with 10,502 fires. Indigenous Brigadiers do not handle the fight, not only because of the number of outbreaks, but also because of the lack of more Brigadiers, adequate structure and equipment. TI Araguaia Park appears second in the survey, with 8,792 fires. The fire forces indigenous people to leave their homes and reaches even a group of indigenous people in voluntary isolation on Bananal Island. The suspicion is that the fire began purposely, with human action, to clean up pasture. Another location where other groups of isolates live was also hit by fires, the Tumucumaque Park, with 1,085 foci. Also hit were the IT San Marcos (RR), Kayapó (PA), Paresi (MT) and Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau (RO). The lack of positive actions of the federal government regarding environmental protection is the main cause of so many crimes and destruction of natural resources and the lives of indigenous peoples. The fires and the Covid-19 only expand the list of sufferings imposed on indigenous peoples, who already live under denial of rights, violence and threats by invasions of landowners, loggers and prospectors.
c49113fc650df7fe4c601b87ed47c6fcae0b0674: After numerous reports of indigenous leaders on invasions in IT, illegal exploitation of ores, felling of forests and other crimes, an operation was carried out by the Special Border Security Group, Funai, Ibama, PMMT, Environmental Police and Special Operations Battalion. Thirty-three suspects were arrested, camps, tools, boats and illegal mining equipment destroyed.
e6eaa8971b0f0b46673159d6977f89283fb71569: Reports that the owner of deforestation actions is known in the region by the nickname of Pezão, resident of the village of Veranópolis, in the rural area of Confresa. He manages the pawns who enter IT for illegal logging and trades the removed wood. The invaders who illegally occupy the northern part of IT also manage people for logging in the territory. The communities affected and threatened by environmental crimes committed are Tapi’itãwa, Tapiparanytãwa, Towajaatãwa, Wiriaotãwa, Inataotãwa, Myryxitãwa, Akara’ytãwa. After denunciation of the crimes, an operation was carried out by the Local Technical Coordination of Funai de Confresa, assisted by the Civil Police, from May 26 to June 2, when equipment used in deforestation and arrest of some suspects was seized. Two wooden shacks were found that served as housing and kitchen for the invaders, chainsaws and many logs of Brazilian wood cut. Apyãwa leaderships (Tapirapé) expressed their indignation at the fact that they were quarantined because of the coronavirus pandemic and were surprised by this new invasion of their territory. The indigenous peoples await compliance with the Supreme Court decision of July 28, 2020, which determined the withdrawal of the invaders from Urubu Branco IT. To date, however, the determination has not been fulfilled.
a2528dbe2c24f6d933f288414228e5a73962f6fd: The IT was hit by fires between August and October, affecting the few high forest spots that remained in the territory of the Apyãwa/Tapirapé. The fire is set by neighboring farmers, who use the practice of burning pastures; the fire then advances over the indigenous land. The damage is enormous, because fire destroys the few remaining forests of Cerrado and causes the death of many animals, besides the constant smoke that harms people's health. Many raw materials needed to perform rituals, such as the bacaba palm and the wild banana, are destroyed, making it difficult to perform ceremonies. Apyãwa groups fought the fire without any proper equipment.
