The general chief of the Apyãwa people, Ware’i (Kamoriwa’i Elber Tapirapé) asked the Department of the Environment of the Municipality of Confresa and Ibama. Since 2018, the Apyãwa have claimed the installation of a Prev Fire brigade for Urubu Branco IT.
e9f37acb90d903d11aa01a5a9463f9f00596ba99: Invasion; deforestation; illegal logging; indigenous land greasing
7c5e74cfcc28144556fa6444ec5ca97ca6ae7fd0: Even before its demarcation and approval (1998), IT was invaded by illegal occupants from the moment the Apyãwa (Tapirapé) began the resumption movement of their ancestral territory in 1993. From then on, these illegal occupants managed to remain in the northern area of the Urubu Branco IT through successive injunctions that guaranteed them the permanence, but not the bust of the indigenous land. The invaders not only deforested the region to deploy pastures, but have promoted illegal logging for commercialization. In 2020, the Urubu Branco IT continued to suffer depredation of its natural resources, but in a much faster way. Since the inauguration of the Bolsonaro government, the invaders and loggers have felt allowed to carry out more deforestation to deploy new pasture areas and more logging for illegal sale of pau-brasil stakes. In 2020 an Ibama operation against deforestation and illegal logging was carried out. The area has been “crowded” among several bosses who recruit pawns. Leandro da Silva, head of the Technical Unit of Ibama de Barra do Garças, said that, after the operation, he located a record of property in the Rural Environmental Registry (CAR), at the site of deforestation. The property, within IT, is in the name of Ailton de Paula Souza. In addition to suffering from the pandemic of the new coronavirus, the people have been suffering from the invasions and deforestation that is reaching sacred sites for the Apyawa, such as the Waterfall of the White Urubu. Leaders registered an occurrence report in the Confresa Civil Police and reported it to the MPF and the National Human Rights Council (CNDH). Cimi Regional Mato Grosso published a complaint note on May 25, 2020, on the Cimi website. On July 28, Minister Dias Toffoli of the STF issued determination to withdraw the invaders from the Urubu Branco IT, but it was not fulfilled.
bdc1e613e9166437a0bf28b4f70421b08a72eda2: Invasion; deforestation for cattle raising; use of pesticides
a78933e07bdb1eda0ce8b12a8b84eac7c3ecf827: Due to the slowness of the demarcation process of the Menku IT, in recent years deforestation has been accelerated for pasture and planting of soybeans and corn. It has also increased, around the territory and, mainly, in the area under demarcation process, the use of pesticides in soybean plantations only 25 km from the village Japuíra, by aerial spray. Areas of important cultural activities of collection and hunting, due to the non-demarcation, are restricted for the access of Myky by farmers, especially the areas of tucuszais, important raw material used for the making of strings for traditional networks.
81b0fba019f468c068b14e115026431fe78f5458: The Jarudori IT is demarcated and regularized, however, it is invaded by squatters. The community is apprehensive by the undefinition of the land situation and by the presence of invaders in their lands. The Bororo people are awaiting a court decision.
400b5e4fb91a9b7c12a475a43c3a544f0c8f9390: In 2013, Minister Luiz Fux, of the Supreme Court, received a request for anticipation of guardianship and suspended the registration in real estate registry of the area demarcated as Kayabi Indigenous Land, made by presidential decree dated April 24, 2013. The judicial request was made in Original Civil Action filed by the government of Mato Grosso and prevents the final transfer of property until the final trial of the issue. In 2020, the Attorney General of the Republic announced calling the parties for dialogue, but was suspended due to the pandemic. The then Prosecutor of the 6th Chamber, Antonio Bigonha, stated that the land must be de-intruded. So far, there has been no provision and the community remains apprehensive by the pandemic of the new coronavirus and the invasion of its territory.
a7b1393a9a71e26ae2fda17e11d08c68f591978c: Leadership reports that invasions, deforestation and illegal logging in IT are even more exacerbated. The invaders did not stop even in this pandemic period. On the contrary, invasions have increased, the violence and truculence of the invaders as well. Leadership believes that they felt more authorized with the attitude of neglect of the current government; there has been no supervision or punishment of environmental criminals. Complaints have already been made to the MPF and the community awaits provisions.
7061669bd07a4fb30767e7ae1040de96350f0c25: On October 2, 2020, a great fire, coming from a farm located at the entrance of the municipality of Serra Nova Dourada, reached the TI Marãiwatsédé and burned almost the only forest area that remained. IT only has this area of forest due to environmental destruction caused by farmers who occupied it illegally for more than 40 years, before the resumption process occurred in 2013.
699163bdc2ab434683d8abb3efc47c87023e4009: Invasion; deforestation; environmental damage; land grating
2ac2dabc8409b5c342e0fc1aa29082fe9c807a64: New Pukanu Village was founded in 2016 in part of the area claimed by Funai for demarcation. The demand was formally formulated and presented in 2007, and until today Funai has not opened the Working Group responsible for conducting studies on the identification and delimitation of the territory. In 2019, Funai, following the judicial determination, prepared a brief report characterizing the occupation in the area resumed. The report is conclusive in the recommendation that the entire Gleba São Pedro be destined by the Secretary of the Union Heritage to the exclusive enjoyment of the Kanela community of Araguaia, since only the area where the Village is constituted is insufficient for the physical and cultural survival of the people. This recommendation has not been fulfilled and the area has been going through successive rubble, including surrounded allotments that prevent the free movement of indigenous people. On October 20th and 21st, a team composed of members of the PF of Barra do Garças and Funai members was on site to conduct a review of the complaints reported by the Kanela Indigenous Community Association of Araguaia - Acikan. On October 29, even after the visit of PF and Funai, a member of the community spotted Mr Antonio de Jesus Seixas (named Tanaka) demarcating a fence, near the community, from the road to the forest. At the time of the team's visit, there were only flat green woods; two days later, the fence was pierced and with wire passed. Another breakthrough found by the community was a sting, which was already ready on the date of the visit of PF and Funai; on October 31, she already found it marked. The area surrounded by José Luciman (named Ciman), close to the community, was fenced by him after the team's visit. Acikan has reported several cases to the MPF, Funai, the Federal Police and various human rights agencies and supporters. The community awaits provision and a definitive solution for the people.
410a92f2a00068cbb3bd2c28d157064e3b274f83: Environmental damage; soybean planting; use of pesticides
1c5c08fb89192569c89a24a618a372d5fcf938a1: The Rikbaktsa people traditionally occupy the banks of the Juruena, Blood and Teles Pires rivers. Since the beginning of 2020, the community has presented allergic reactions such as itching and skin spots, as well as diarrhea pictures, after the use of rivers water for bathing, fishing, drinking and preparing food. Indigenous people suspect that these health problems are due to the presence of pesticides in the Blood River. In recent years, soybean crops have extended along the banks of the Blood River, on the right side of the indigenous territory. The pesticide is used in crop sprays, and the waters are contaminated due to the proximity of these crops with rivers and indigenous territory.
588721034e01cddecc22d6e97c3a17d2b1360ca2: Official Forensics and Technical Identification Reports (Politec), as well as the investigations of the Specialized Environmental Police (Dema), pointed out the origin of the outbreaks of fires that devastated the Pantanal in 2020 and identified those responsible for the areas. Several surveys are being finalized with the aim of holding those responsible for the various environmental crimes responsible. According to delegate Alessandra Saturnino, holder of Dema, human action was predominant for fires in Pantanal and Baixada Cuiabana, which resulted in loss of biome and air quality. She reports that even with the identification of those responsible, as there is no violence against people, it is difficult for a request for arrest to be granted, especially during a pandemic period. The deputy assured me that she would act technically to hold the criminals responsible. The expert Alberto Pavan reported that some factors led to the belief that human action was predominant for fires in the Pantanal, because it was a time when there was no incidence of lightning and they were places without electricity, which practically ruled out natural causes.
159af3663e48fcc0a6b3f45ae97e33d2c112a061: In the third week of November 2020, Chief Damião Paridzané and a group of indigenous peoples, when doing a survey by IT, found (before the judicial decision of disintrusion) in the place called Posto da Mata a post with two cameras of capture of images, pointed to the path that goes to Village A’õpá, where the chief Damião resides. No Xavante community leadership was consulted or authorized to install the pole with the cameras. So far, you don't know who put it in, or your boss, or your purpose. Returning to the site two days later, they found that the post with the cameras had been removed. This is an explicit case of violation of indigenous heritage and an attempt to spy or control the movement of the Xavante. The community is investigating the case.
5a5804bbe2f796d9438b5bf476278c829eb512e3: With a lot of effort and unity, the Guató people will rise after the largest burning recorded in the Pantanal biome, since the National Institute of Special Research (Inpe) began to measure the fires in 1998. The side effects are still many: devastated swiddens and medicinal plants, dead animals and almost dry river; in the heads of many people, fire remains alive, according to reports mainly of the elders. In Mato Grosso, fires were banned throughout the state on July 15. But from the month of prohibition until September – the most critical period – what was seen was a record of illegal fires in the three biomes (Amazon, Cerrado and Pantanal), to the point of destroying more than 2 million hectares of the largest flooded plain in the world, only in the part of Mato Grosso. Adding the territory of Mato Grosso Sul, the devastated area reaches 3.9 million hectares, which represents 26% of the entire Pantanal biome. Data are from the Environmental Satellite Applications Laboratory (LASA) of the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ). TI Guató was the last territory demarcated by the federal government in 2018. Former President Michel Temer approved the administrative demarcation made by Funai with an area of 20,000 hectares in the municipality of Barão de Melgaço, in Mato Grosso. The current President of the Republic, Jair Bolsonaro, maintains, from 2019 to the present day, the promise of campaign not to demarcate an indigenous land, in total disrespect to indigenous populations and the Federal Constitution. September was the period that most recorded fires in the Pantanal: 5.859, according to the reference satellite of the Inpe. Of this total, 5,188 outbreaks (88%) emerged in clandestine areas, outside the registers of inspection agencies and real estate registered in the Rural Environmental Certificate (CAR) of the Department of Environment (Sema-MT). The survey is part of the system “Monitor of Burns”, a tool created by the Instituto Centro de Vida de Mato Grosso (ICV). The data goes against the statement of the president of the Jair Bolsonaro Republic and farmers of the region, that most of the biome fires were caused by the indigenous themselves. The causes of burning in private buildings still depend on more specific investigations to determine why. But, according to the ICV, the vast majority is related to the opening of new agricultural fronts, and deforestation is also associated with the logic of expansion of cattle head cultivation. The situation caused the MPF to ask Ibama, in late September, to identify the origin of the biome fires. But after months of the request, Ibama had not yet responded and the MPF investigations had not yet been completed.
a8d0518e15f77241711c3096e68ee64505e2a527: The Rèñoà Bero IT, name Karajá given by the indigenous peoples to the Rio Beleza/Lago Grande, has 4,627 hectares of surface and is located at the confluence of the River Beauty with the Araguaia River, in the northeast end of Mato Grosso, in front of Bananal Island (TO). Almost a decade ago, the work of the Funai Identification and Delimitation GT was initiated. In May 2019, the report identifying and delimiting the area was delivered to the General Coordinator of Funai Identification and Delimitation, but was never published by the agency. While the demarcation is paralyzed, the indigenous see their territory being lotted and sold to third parties. The accused of lotting the indigenous land and selling the lots is the councilman of Santana do Araguaia (PA), Glaucione Silva Costa, known as “Gaguim”. The information was given by a member of the indigenous community, whose name is not revealed for security reasons due to threats suffered. There are reports that the councilman would have already built a summer house within the indigenous land. The demarcation of the Rénõà Bero (Rio Beleza), known as Lake Grande, has been demanded for decades by the Iny-Karajá people, and the lack of provision in the land process leaves the indigenous to the mercy of invaders. A demonstration was held with the MPF of Barra do Garças, requesting investigation and measures to guarantee territorial law and to continue demarcation.
5ec1b9cfbca956588e388ed534c15aed805ecf7f: Invasion of cattle farms; illegal logging
4218cf4a40ae9a4a0f0afd7ee2652a9356492977: Declared in 2008, TI Manoki is constantly invaded by loggers. The halting of the demarcation process allows non-indigenous occupants to continue with their exploratory activities, especially agricultural ones, which are degrading of the environment. According to information from the Manoki leaders, with the pandemic, invasions have increased, especially for cattle breeding within the territory. According to the leaders' testimony, these activities increased during the pandemic, a situation that was not previously observed.
b125b0270da574f80a77037e0138581c6598f31e: Leaders denounce criminal attack, in the village Jaguapiré, with fire of the House of Reza and destruction of sacred objects of their culture, which were over 200 years old and passed from generation to generation. This was the second house of prayer destroyed in 2020 in Mato Grosso do Sul. The first fire was recorded in the Orange Nhanderu community in the municipality of Rio Brilhante, a distance of 163 kilometers from the capital. In July 2019, the target had been the only prayer house of the Goldens Indigenous Reserve in Jaguapiru Village, which was completely destroyed by the flames. With at least 17,000 residents, the reserve is the most populous in the country. The praying woman Roberta Ximenes, from Jaguapiré, reported that, around five o'clock in the morning of March 1, two people invaded the village and set fire to the House of Reza; the fire totally burned the house, which has wooden structure and is covered with grass sapé. Indigenous people report that the region is very violent and ask for security; families live under constant tension and gang threats. A complaint was made to the MPF and the Federal Police, requesting investigation and punishment of criminals.
ec07c4c7176572f19b5d4196d951e39d44fd83d0: Indigenous living on the outskirts of Casa de Reza reports that, just before the attack, early on January 2, he heard noises. Her husband stood up to see what it was and saw a non-indigenous man walking towards the House of Reza. He asked if the man was lost and he told him to leave. The Indian noticed that the man was carrying something that looked like a gun. As the area is very violent, he returned to the house, took his wife and ran off towards the cornfield. From there they observed the movement and the beginning of the fire. Soon after, the men fled and the community put out the fire; the fire consumed part of the House of Reza. Indigenous people in this region live under constant tension and in precarious conditions. The case is being followed by the MPF.
0b6a36997dc83e46b3d19ea786a98a051127b29a: After several complaints about invasions, deforestation, exploitation and damage to the environment, the Federal Police initiated the investigation of these crimes within the indigenous territory, serving search and seizure warrants issued by the Federal Court of Campo Grande. Leaderships denounce that the region has been occupied and devastated for years and that the crimes of invasion and exploitation of indigenous lands intensified in 2019 and 2020. Indigenous people routinely face a hostile climate and situations of the most diverse violence caused by non-indigenous invaders.
dafa4a685f7d6818aa0d0d0f3a83d41e99987372: Major fires that hit the Pantanal National Park of Mato Grosso do Sul, Serra do Amolar and Porto do Indio, in November, also hit IT. Guató, northwest of MS. Fire crews were working in the Pantanal region, in a difficult-to-access location. Reports of firemen realize that Serra do Amolar has become a great black stinger, which is when the vegetation burns completely and there is no more burning, causing the fire to advance to where it has not yet burned.
6cc85fd0ef7280e8ff65a136ff7ec87057c26fbd: Resumptions Guarani and Kaiowá located within the Jaguapiru and Bororó Reserve, also known as the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, continue to suffer constant and uninterrupted violence and pressure in 2020. Indigenous families suffer daily invasions of their territory, facing sieges, threats, attacks on life and burning houses. The attacks against indigenous people on the site are constant and intensified from October 2018. In a single attack, for example, 15 Guarani and Kaiowá were wounded by gunshots from rubber and marble bullets. Since then, the violent actions have left numerous wounded by rubber and firearms, many with gravity, having as a highlight the use of a modified tractor for the purposes of attacks and destruction of homes, called “Caveirão” indigenous people. The indigenous camped, amid all this violence, continue to claim and denounce the subtraction of the indigenous territory, which remains occupied by invaders. The Dourados Indigenous Reserve was demarcated in 1917 with 3.6 thousand hectares. Over time, it suffered a historical process of decreasing its area, being recorded in 1965 with 61 hectares less. The final title of ownership, issued twenty years later, maintained the reduction and the total area was 3.5 thousand hectares – of which less than 3.4 thousand are in the effective possession of the indigenous. The Reserve houses 18,000 indigenous Kaiowá, Guarani and Terena and is considered an area of human confinement and one of the largest humanitarian dramas involving indigenous peoples in history. The indigenous continue to claim to this day about 70 hectares that remain invaded by non-indigenous people.
8ac17fc53db8fc709e273e247d21d6cb5406128e: The Arroio Korá IT, located in the municipality of Paranhos, despite being approved, remains widely invaded, situation without resolution by the authorities until 2020. Of the 7,175 hectares of the territory, the indigenous community effectively occupies only around 4,000 hectares, that is, 55.7% of the total. This situation has caused a series of conflicts and severe violations of human rights, such as hunger, murder, social hypervulnerability, as well as inability to live from their uses, customs and traditions, as governed by the Federal Constitution. In general data, as already reported in the Cimi Violence Report with data from 2018, of the 242.322.33 hectares of indigenous lands already recognized by the Brazilian State in Mato Grosso do Sul, the Guarani and Kaiowá occupy only 70,370,08 of their own territory, about 29%.
81a97168d0b7276805914059ab64acbd8770da28: The IT Dourados Amambai Pegua I, located in the municipality of Caarapó, delimited, continues invaded, without resolution by the authorities. Of the 55,590 hectares of the territory, the Guarani-Kaiowá indigenous community effectively occupies around 4.594.42 hectares, that is, only 8.26% of this total. This situation of slowness and omission of the State in the regularization of the indigenous territory has caused intense conflicts and severe violations of human rights such as hunger, violence of all kinds, murders, social hypervulnerability, as well as inability of the people to live from their uses, customs and traditions, as foreseen in the Magna Charter of the country.
f41e1674d2bfea3ea06334e1f040e5a3f5f25fb5: The Guyraraka IT, located in the municipality of Caarapó, already declared, continues with its territory widely invaded, remaining unresolved by the authorities. Of the 11,440 hectares of the territory, the Guarani-Kaiowá indigenous community effectively occupies about 50 hectares, that is, only 0.44% of the total. While the land situation of the indigenous territory is not treated by the federal government, as provided by the Federal Constitution, families remain surviving in precarious conditions, under constant threats and suffering countless violations of rights. With the Covid-19 pandemic, the situation of the Guarani-Kaiowá, which was already regrettable, worsened. In addition to facing invaders and violence of all kinds, without guarantee of their territory to live with dignity, without effective public policies, hunger and miserability among indigenous families took unacceptable proportions. The indigenous peoples call for effective actions of the protection agencies, guaranteeing them their constitutional rights and dignified life for all.
8fe87293abff69617a776b6a27319451bc1bd7f2: Iguatemi Pegua I – Pyelito Kue/ Mbarakay, located in the municipality of Iguatemi, bounded by Funai, continues with its territory invaded and without any provision by the authorities. The Guarani-Kaiowá indigenous community effectively occupies 98 of the 41,571 hectares of the territory, that is, only 0.24% of the total. Just like the other indigenous families in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, these Iguatemi Pagua TI also wait for measures by the authorities in their obligation to enforce their rights provided for in the Federal Constitution, guaranteeing them their regularized territories and effective public policies. For years, the Guarani-Kaiowá have lived under constant tension and violence by the invaders of their territories, unable to live with dignity in their own land, from their customs and traditions.
e9753a2309931326b757d4ad0bffd7743b995236: The JatayVari IT, located in the municipality of Ponta Porã, declared of traditional indigenous occupation by the Ministry of Justice, continues with its territory widely invaded, without provision by the authorities. Of the 8,800 hectares of this IT, the Guarani-Kaiowá community effectively occupies only 108 hectares, representing 1.23% of the total. Without guarantee of their land rights, the indigenous remain under attacks by the invaders of their territory, suffering all kinds of violence, prejudice, hunger and failure. The indigenous peoples call for justice, and that the responsible authorities and defense and protection bodies enforce their constitutional rights.
08f88f2f8f001ba9aea4575787b7cae82b43b465: The Nhanderu Marangatu IT, located in the municipality of Antônio João, although already approved, remains widely invaded, without provision by the responsible authorities. Of the 9,317 hectares of indigenous land, the Guarani-Kaiowá community occupies around 5,400 hectares, only 57.96% of the total. This situation of insecurity and injustice has generated several conflicts with the invaders and severe violations of human rights such as hunger, murders, social hypervulnerability and prevents the people from living from their uses, customs and traditions, as provided by the Federal Constitution.
3e26458870e3c96205bb9d89f3c87d23564cad90: The Panambi Lagoa Rica IT, located in the municipality of Douradina, delimited, remains widely invaded, without any provision by the authorities. Of the 12,196 hectares of indigenous land, the Guarani-Kaiowá community effectively occupies only about 390, i.e. 3.2% of the total. While justice is not done and the Federal Constitution does not comply with, guaranteeing indigenous rights, the Guarani-Kaiowá families have been living under constant threats and violence of all sorts provoked by the invaders for years. By 2020, the situation that was already precarious became even more serious due to the Covid-19 pandemic. Today, the picture seen in the villages is even more desolating; in addition to the violence caused by the invasion of their territories, the indigenous people have to live with extreme hunger and misery, helplessness, disease and the lack of sensitivity and responsibility of the authorities who should guarantee, at least, decent living conditions for these families.
e2c44d17d44b4e3ccdef03c44d0ce8865c638b55: TI Potrero Guasu, located in the municipality of Paranhos, with a declaratory ordinance issued by the Ministry of Justice, continues with its territory widely invaded, without provision by the authorities. The Guarani Nhandeva community occupies only 1,000 of the 4,025 hectares of indigenous land, corresponding to 24.84% of the total. Meanwhile, in which the authorities of the government fail to fulfil their obligations regarding the regularization of indigenous territories, they continue to be increasingly invaded and the indigenous peoples raped. By 2020, the situation of the Guarani Nhandeva, which was already very serious, became even worse with the arrival of the Covid-19 pandemic. Not enough was all kinds of violence caused by the invaders, the indigenous families are even more impoverished and vulnerable, as well as sick and helpless by the government. The non-guarantee of their territory, free and de-intruded, corroborates the risk to the survival of the Guarani people.
2c9724658da8c617bb1d51c5e6de579139df05f2: The Sombrerito IT, located in the municipality of Sete Quedas, declared, continues with its territory widely invaded, without resolution by the authorities. Of the 12,608 hectares of the indigenous land, the community occupies only 600 hectares, that is, 4.76% of the total. While the government does not comply with what is provided for in the Federal Constitution, regulating and disintruding the indigenous territories, they continue to be invaded, depredated and stripped. In 2020, in the middle of the coronavirus pandemic, in addition to facing all kinds of violence caused by the invaders, the indigenous peoples were even more abandoned by the federal government. The situation in the villages, besides tense and violent, presents a desolating picture, with indigenous families even more vulnerable and impoverished. In addition to violence, hunger and disease are more evident. The indigenous peoples expect the responsible authorities to do their duty and guarantee the rights advocated by the country's largest law.
0ed1ed79d1d303f286a12dd7925bb9f31ba924a9: TI Taquara, located in the municipality of Juti, already declared, continues with its territory widely invaded, without resolution by the authorities. Of the 9.7 thousand hectares of indigenous land, the community actually occupies about 1,881 hectares, only 19.4% of the total territory. While the government, responsible for enforcing the provisions of the Federal Constitution, remains omissive, entire families continue to be assaulted, raped and expelled from their own land by unscrupulous invaders. Without supervision or punishment by the bodies responsible for caring for the indigenous territories, which are the heritage of the Union, the invaders feel free to continue committing their illicits with impunity. The Covid-19 pandemic and the lack of adequate assistance by the federal government in 2020 intensified the situation of severity, violence, hunger and extreme vulnerability among indigenous people in this state. Without the guarantee of their effective territories and public policies, the Guarani-Kaiowá are seriously struggling to maintain their survival, culture and immemorial wealth.
f773bb42c799968c749d42dd17cb69728f2f7fed: In 2020, the Apyka’i IT invaded and the situation experienced by the Guarani-Kaiowá is extremely serious. Despite the demand for demarcation of the Apyka’i IT already last decades, with the effective occupation of the Guarani-Kaiowá in a small range of territory, the qualification for Funai study was established only in 2016 and is paralyzed until today. Even though a commitment was made in 2007, via TAC with the MPF, Funai, arbitraryly, suspended a study ordinance called “Dorados Peguá”, leaving the Apyka’i IT and dozens of territories without provision. This delay, which caused weakness of legal certainty to the territory claimed, ended up consolidating an eviction still in 2016 – another one of many already suffered by this community. To this day, the community is on the banks of the highway, in subhuman conditions of life, and in the territory from which they were evicted there are even two cemeteries of the Kaiowá. After the eviction, a container was provided, where they remain vigilant – private security – with the function of avoiding any access of the indigenous to the territory that is serving today for the private cultivation of sugarcane. In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020, the situation of indigenous peoples is extremely vulnerable. Not enough was the invasion, disrespect and constant violence, the indigenous also faced the harsh reality brought by the disease and the disregard of the federal government. Violence, death, hunger, extreme poverty, diseases and abandonment by the government is the picture experienced today by indigenous people in the state. Fulfilling the constitutional rights of indigenous peoples is a duty that needs to be carried out urgently by the federal government and public bodies, in order to bear responsibility for the decimation of peoples from Brazil.
fbd586cb781b7c6e207f56d2af8bcb0e9bf19ef3: Almost two years after the serious environmental crime committed by Vale Mining, with the breaking of the Bean Dam in Brumadinho (MG), on January 25, 2019, the situation of more than 270 families of dead in that tragedy remains unchanged, including indigenous families. It was families and stories destroyed, human lives, animals, rivers, forests, all the environment in hundreds of miles that perhaps not even in several centuries recover. The Paraopeba River, from which many indigenous and riverside families took their livelihood and survival, is contaminated by the wastes of the mining company Vale, which is not the only one responsible for this which is being considered one of the worst environmental tragedies in the world. The State is also responsible because it approves numerous mega-enterprise projects, but does not supervise them. Repair measures are agreed between MPF and Vale, only this does not comply with them, only postpones them. Meanwhile, without hope of being minimally repaired by so many losses and pains, many families need to leave the region in search of their survival. As if such a picture of horror were imagined to worsen, the region, as well as the entire planet, was hit by the pandemic of coronavirus. And with it, even more difficulties and suffering, due to the apathy and insensitivity also of the federal government, by not helping the indigenous population with a contingency plan, prevention and control that would prevent the spread of the virus and even more deaths.
541b0b264421a8f0c03ef6a8e5921e0abdabd265: Sand extraction; predatory fishing; water removal for irrigation; use of pesticides
cbb6c8dc4e63b70cb7bbead141d82cd9d211c680: The Pará River, which crosses the Kaxixó TI and is one of the sources of spiritual and economic survival of the Kaxixó people, has been greatly assaulted by invaders who remove sand from this river, causing silencing. The Kaxixó are also affected by predatory fishing and by the increase in artisanal fishing, which began to be done by fishermen who were expelled from the region of Córrego do Beanão after the environmental crime of Vale Mineradora, which occurred in 2019, and contaminated the region's watershed. Another problem is cattle farms and agribusiness enterprises, which use irrigation pivots and remove large amounts of water from the river. Para, greatly lowering its natural level, causing serious impacts on fauna, flora and people who depend on the river to survive. In addition, the indiscriminate use of pesticides in farms bordering IT has contaminated the river, causing death of fish and, consequently, diseases in people, especially children and the elderly.
0bb25b258fccf4dc6ce11af45f15e12699007f2a: In 2020, the land situation experienced by the Xakribá people remains unchanged regarding the revision of the boundaries of the traditional territory, claimed and already identified by Funai. The territory identification report was also contested by the National Confederation of Agriculture (CNA). Several invasions are configured as farms within IT. The conflict situation faced by the Xakriabá worsened even more with the pandemic of coronavirus and the lack of adequate control and care by the government.
db03398f6c2a7345ca5e7c8f1d660c0b59ceabfc: Invasion; destruction of indigenous heritage; exploitation of natural resources
74708e2eb93d85207ea54ebdb57a5ff93cd072d7: Claimed as a land of traditional occupation by the indigenous, the area was subtracted from the territory of Krenak and transformed into a conservation unit, the State Park of Seven Halls. While it is not regulated, the territory suffers from the invasion of illegal hunters, illegal extraction of ores, indiscriminate removal of palms and even the theft and destruction of the cave paintings of the sacred territory of the Krenak. Farmers exploit mineral water from the area claimed and even illegally use the name of the people for marketing the product.
96d90f853914a61075a1ed5c4f6020b11268250d: The Red Cinta Jundiba IT, in process of identification by Funai, is being impacted by the power transmission line of the company Mantiqueira, which connects the municipalities of Janaúba to Araçuaí. The 24 high-voltage towers are installed near the traditional territory, and two of them were placed less than 300 metres from the village. Families are very concerned about the consequences of this work. The situation has already been reported by Pankararu and Pataxó to MPF, but remained unchanged in 2020. The pandemic of coronavirus is also a cause of concern for indigenous people, due to the circulation of non-indigenous people in the region. In addition, the northeast region of Minas Gerais and the Jequitinhonha Valley have been targeted by mining companies for lithium extraction. Mineral is being considered as the oil of the future, and can be used in the production of car batteries and electric buses, as well as in cell phone batteries and tablets. However, Brazil has no technology or interest to continue its production chain. Companies today remove crude rock from the region and turn it into lithium concentrate, which is exported and processed in other processes in other countries, especially China. The great concern is with the presence of non-indigenous people in the indigenous territory and throughout the Jequitinhonha Valley region. The mining activity brings immense damage to the environment as a whole, especially to water sources and the survival of the surrounding populations.
32316a317ab45e0114d52f4bbe97289a4f30771e: For the Pankararu of the Apukaré IT, the situation of their territory also remains unchanged in 2020. The land identification process remains paralyzed at Funai. Meanwhile, indigenous peoples suffer various impacts, such as the power transmission line that is being built by Mantiqueira. Cement posts and power towers were built inside and around IT, and indigenous families are concerned about the high-voltage wires that are scattered in the area. One of the high voltage towers was installed in the space used by the Pankararu to collect medicinal plants that are used in their sacred rituals. The delay and omission of the federal government in resolving the land issues of indigenous lands generates conflicts and insecurity to communities, facilitating the invasion of their traditional territories.
393b4a70316909f62fb1580ca24a06771fdc5f11: Arara leaders denounce the invasion of their territory by loggers. Ibama found illegal logging, caught large amounts of cut wood, motorcycles, chainsaws, fuel and truck, as well as a treadmill tractor, used to open clandestine roads to drain the wood. This IT is a constant target of deforestation for illegal exploitation, and also of invaders who sting for possible allotment. The area is also affected by the construction of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Complex. 2020 was even more difficult for the Arara people, due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
2f50aa6b6bead0cd34867f450c63d3381ad21e83: invasion; illegal exploitation of wood; deforestation; land grabbing
62de85a9b7ea6d87951d14c9d689bddd5c6095b9: Leaderships denounce an immense area deforested within the indigenous land. Ibama inspection teams proved the criminal deforestation and seized machines, equipment and fuel used by offenders. The territory is invaded by landowners who have promoted a real environmental devastation, intensified after the election of the Bolsonaro government and its supporters, including senators and deputies who, with their speeches and postures, end up legitimizing environmental crimes.
cace2adcab64dc6942b32d0a1490a3fc72904873: invasion; illegal logging; deforestation; land grating
b7ab6cf53e059eb8102ce4543f32a61ce952b07a: Leaders denounced to the MPF the criminal action of invaders farmers, landowners and loggers, who deforested and still deforested IT Ituna-Itatá, which is today one of the most devastated in the country. The MPF recommends that Ibama continue to combat environmental crimes in the region. The presence of invaders leaves traces of forest devastation and pastures where there are illegal cattle. Even more worrying is that in the area are isolated indigenous, who have no contact with non-indigenous society, which can lead to contamination by diseases that, for them, can be deadly.
e0690c3b5f42d485c2fafed064fe0c38d8467158: After several complaints by indigenous leaders, the Federal Police located more than 2,000 illegal prospectors working in IT. The criminals tried to hide the machinery used within the closed forests of the region, but PF, using drones, located the equipment. Invasions of prospectors have been reported for years, but with no government provision. All the violence and destruction of the environment, pollution of the waters of the rivers, devastation of the forests and forests, with the pandemic of the coronavirus, the invasions increased greatly, and with them the contamination, which has already led many Munduruku to illness and death by Covid-19. According to the MPF, a few indigenous people favorable to mining, co-opted by mining companies, try to force other indigenous peoples to do so and even silence those who are contrary. The situation in the region is very serious.
d37b4522155ca69ff95776e1b3b9acf9e737e3ca: Survey by the Amazon Mine project, InfoAmazonia, found at least 58 research ore mining requirements approved by the National Mining Agency - ANM, even affecting indigenous territories, something that is prohibited by the Federal Constitution. The miner Anglo American Niquel owns almost half of the authorizations; there are 27 valid requests for copper research in indigenous lands of Mato Grosso and Pará. The company's main target is TI Sawré Muybu (Pimental), in southwest Pará, where the Munduruku live, with 13 requests. In addition to these 27 authorizations, the survey found almost 150 requests from the English mining company, made by Anglo American or by smaller companies in which it participates. Anglo states that it is the responsibility of the federal government, because it is up to ANM to demarcate the blocks outside the indigenous territories. The survey also cites as very affected areas TI Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, in Rondônia; TI Arara do Rio Branco, in Acre, and others.
aa28fef07612c96f39f6ac69c64c732c3acae07e: Reports report that, in less than three years, 11% of IT Ituna-Itatá were deforested. They report that, in 2019, this IT was the most deforested in the Amazon, and that in 2020, this same territory concentrated more than 600 fires detected by satellite monitored by Inpe. More than half of these outbreaks were recorded in the first fortnight of October, in the invasion of IT involving schemes of greasing, rearing and “washing” cattle. According to the complaint, the territory through which the fire advances experiences an unprecedented attack of non-indigenous invaders who pressure and affect the entire region of the Middle Xingu and other indigenous lands such as Reach Bacajá, Cachoeira Seca and Apyterewa. One of the main concerns is that the lives of isolated indigenous people living in the region are even more threatened.
927a158774a48b001813cbfc7282b5f86209c8a5: Waterfall Seca was the most deforested indigenous land in Brazil in 2020, according to data from Inpe released at the end of December. Between July 2019 and August 2020 were 72.4 square kilometers of area deforested in this IT. The region has already been greatly affected by the construction of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Plant and indigenous populations have been suffering from the invasion and illegal action of loggers. Six other Indigenous Lands in Pará follow the ranking of the most deforested, after Cachoeira Seca. In order, they are the ITs Apyterewa, Ituna/Itatá, Bacajá Reach, Munduruku and Kayapó.
5ef883b467e36509711a0d5f3caa14033d300011: Water pollution; damage to the environment; illegal greasing and allotment
fc587f7f73ec7ebd9a03f738dbb33c17a78f65cb: The indigenous peoples living on the banks of the Teles Pires River, which covers the states of Pará and Mato Grosso, reported that, after the construction of a hydroelectric plant in the Teles Pires River, the water, previously consumed directly in the river by the populations, was polluted and the supply systems installed are not enough to guarantee access to drinking water. In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, not having guaranteed access to drinking water has been a disaster for the indigenous peoples of the region. In a court hearing on December 2, indigenous peoples were first heard since the plant was installed in the region ten years ago. The hearing is a development of a public civil action proposed by the MPF in 2014, one year before the start of the plant's activities. Hundreds of families of the Apiaká, Kayabí and Munduruku people are directly impacted by the enterprise. In addition to water pollution, the effects of the dam on the flood pulse of the river, with worsening droughts and floods, alter the reproduction of fish and limit navigation. Sacred sites for the indigenous were destroyed, like the Seven Falls rapids, flooded by the dam of the plant. As if all this were not enough, there are still landowners who are armed, making ostensive threats within the indigenous territory, in the intention of batching and selling grilled areas. With precarious supervision by the organs that should control and protect the territory, the invaders feel free to continue their criminal activities within the indigenous lands.
535471faafd6bc8d8a0d801d6823826e549f0b73: Inpe began issuing deforestation alerts in the Amazon through the Real-time Determining Detection System (Deter) in 2015. Since then, the indices detected show that in the last two years there has been a record in deforestation rates, increasing 80.62% in the last quarter compared to the same period of 2019. According to data from the Deter system, mining has deforested 405,36 km2 from the Legal Amazon in the last five years, the equivalent of 40,500 football fields, including advancing on conservation areas. The mining epicenter is between the Tapajós and Xingu rivers, especially in the Munduruku IT, which is one of the most affected peoples by this illegal activity. According to Greenpeace, from January to April 2020 more than 70% of mining in the Amazon occurred within protected areas, and in indigenous lands, the increase in deforestation by mining was 64%, compared to the same period of 2019. Mining in the indigenous lands of Kayapó, Munduruku and Yanomami has been taking place for decades, but the situation has been increasing exponentially in the last two years, especially in 2020. Also according to Inpe, from January 1st to November 20th, 2020, mining was responsible for deforestation of 97.61 km2 throughout the Legal Amazon; Pará alone concentrates 81% of the total, with 79.86 km2; the situation is critical along the Tapajós River, signaling that deforestation is followed by water contamination, especially by mercury, affecting populations living on the banks. Itaituba (40.33 km2) and Jacareacanga (17.29 km2), both in Pará, are the cities most affected by mining throughout the biome. According to Beto Veríssimo, agronomist and co-founder of the Institute of Man and Environment of the Amazon (Imazon), mining activity – especially when illegal and associated with mining – contaminates rivers and people, generates violence against traditional communities and triggers other predatory actions. “The camp in the Amazon is never alone: it paves the way for other illegal activities in the forest. Where mining appears, there is also exploitation of wood, invasion, livestock on the edges and so on. (...) companies are behind, financing the purchase of machinery, co-opting workers, vulnerable people and leaders to act for them in the forests ", complements. In addition to this environmental and social tragedy, illegal mining activity in indigenous lands has compromised the health of communities. A study by Fiocruz in partnership with WWF Brazil on the Munduruku showed that six out of ten participants had high levels of mercury contamination. When the analysis is only in the villages that are on the banks of the rivers affected by the mining, the number of contaminated rises to nine out of ten participants. Children suffer the most from the impact of mercury and other heavy metals used in mining – about 15.8% of them presented problems in neurodevelopment tests.
0585cd8f05d4c0f47e1595ff943c523a9f2ca39d: After complaints, an operation involving Ibama, the State Department of the Environment of Pará and the Armed Forces was carried out, during which nine illegal sawmills that operated around IT Alto Rio Guamá were closed. The gang was engaged in illegal timber trading with other states. A clandestine port on the Gurupi River, used to drain the wood to the Northeast, was also closed.
f0c489f9ee8560ab37ff7f6bb161f5e3f06f7313: In July, the MPF gave a 20-day deadline for Ibama and ICMBio to promote surveillance operations against environmental crimes in ten indigenous lands and conservation units in the middle Xingu region of Pará, also known as Terra do Meio, between the municipalities of Altamira and São Félix do Xingu. Within the areas identified by the MPF as critical, 23 priority targets, sites of criminal activities of mining, sawmills, farms, inns and landing strips were listed. With a deadline to begin, supervision should become permanent. The MPF recalls that the region, with a large volume of criminal activities, is at the epicenter of the impact of large enterprises, such as the Belo Monte plant and the Belo Sun mining project, which increased pressure on protected territories and caused deforestation rates to explode in these areas. The Attorney General of the Republic in Altamira conducts several investigations that establish civil and criminal responsibilities for environmental illicits in the region, mainly in the indigenous lands Cachoeira Seca and Ituna Itatá and in the Ecological Station of the Middle Land. These investigations indicate more than 201 million trees fell in the middle Xingu in 2019, and 23% of the devastation is located within indigenous areas and conservation units. Between 2018 and 2019, there was a 52% increase in deforestation in the so-called Xingu environmental diversity corridor. By 2020, the numbers got worse. The Deforestation Alert System (SAD) detected 188 km2 of deforestation in the Legal Amazon, an increase of 74% compared to January of the previous year. For the seventh month in a row, Pará was among the states that most deforested the Amazon Forest. The devastation occurs for the growth of criminal activities such as illegal mining that, in the first months of 2020, had already deforested 21,340 hectares, according to the MPF. “In the context of confronting the Covid-19 pandemic, there is sufficient evidence to conclude that illegal mining is one of the main vectors of virus spread in communities,” said prosecutors of the Republic who work in Altamira and sign the recommendation.
452501b1ad330a878a148f777606d855ed3558a4: At a meeting of the Environmental Observatory of the Judicial Power, data from the Environmental Action Panel in the Amazon Region were released by the National Council of Justice at the end of November. The panel is an unprecedented mapping of the collection of environmental actions in the Amazon region. Environmental damage, crimes against fauna and flora and pollution are some of the 54,600 cases that have been running in Justice seeking environmental protection in the region since 2000. Only in 2019 nearly 8,000 shares were entered — 14.4% of the total. In 2020, until October, 4.9 thousand lawsuits on the environment in the Amazon were identified. More than half of lawsuits have environmental damage (32.7%) and crimes against flora (22.2%). Pollution follows, with 12% of the processes. Crimes against fauna account for 4% of lawsuits and 6.3% of them refer to requests to revoke or cancel environmental fines. Pará is the state where the largest volume of actions is concentrated — 20.4 thousand, about 37% of the total, being affected several lands and indigenous peoples in the state.
aaf7513bb1a0de60d81328e2103b1badb4979d4d: The MPF of Pará and Mato Grosso forwarded a representation along with the ISA, Aikio Indigenous Association, Atix Indigenous Association, Kabu Institute Indigenous Association, with request for adoption of Cautelary Measure with the TCU due to irregularities practiced by the Union, through the Ministry of Infrastructure and the National Land Transport Agency (ANTT), concerning the project of the EF -170 Railway (Ferrogrão), which involve violations of rights of indigenous peoples and traditional communities. In the representation, it is informed that the survey indicated the presence of 48 indigenous lands, at different stages of regularization, around the railway route. From this set, it was proposed the grouping of “Etnoterritorial Complexes”, through the classification of indigenous lands based on criteria related to ethnic belonging, local and regional ethnic articulation and political mobilization. Three territorial complexes were identified on which there would be evidence of threats and incidence of synergistic and cumulative impacts generated by the implementation of the railway: Complex 1 - Peoples and Indigenous Lands Munduruku, Complex 2 - Indigenous Lands Bau, Menkragnoti and Panará and Complex 3 - Indigenous Lands Capoto Jarina, Indigenous Park of Xingu, Ikpeng, River Arraias, Apiaka/Kayabi and Batalão. If it is carried out, this project will impact the lives of thousands of indigenous people, as well as the entire environment of the region.
5b7bc4d8207f0851a0dc7de37be06d527af5ce5a: At the beginning of August, the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) sent aircraft to Jacareacanga, at the southwest end of Pará, at the request of Ibama, to support an operation to combat environmental crimes – especially illegal mining – within the Munduruku and Sai Gray indigenous lands. The operation did not take place and one of the FAB aircraft was used to transport illegal miners to Brasília (DF). The situation can configure administrative improbity by purpose deviation and began to be investigated by the MPF. The investigation was opened on August 20, in Itaituba (PA), and is based on a document from the FAB itself which, in response to the letter of the MPF, confirmed that it gave way, on August 6, 2020, a plane to transport people indicated as indigenous leaders to Brasilia for meeting with the Minister of the Environment, Ricardo Salles, who the previous day had gone to Jacareaunga and met with the prospectors who were the target of the operation of Ibama. According to FAB's response to the MPF, the determination to surrender an aircraft was accompanied by order to temporarily suspend Operation Verde Brasil 2 in the Jacareacanga region. The operation was subsequently resumed in September, with the performance of PF and logistical support from FAB, Army and Ibama. In the end, 20 machinery used in mining, between shovel loaders, tractors and others, were discarded, and PF estimated the environmental damage identified in approximately R$ 8 million, referring to the six-month period. The ability to combat environmental crimes, however, was compromised by the postponement, because criminals had time to hide most of the heavy machinery they use in the devastation of the forest. The halting of the operation and the transportation of prospectors to Brasília, damaged the effectiveness of the inspection. Leadership Munduruku sent a letter to the MPF denying that the people transported on the FAB plane represented the indigenous people. In fact, the letter says, the caravan taken to Brasilia was formed by seven residents who are defenders of the interests of prospectors and act equally with the illegal exploitation of ores within the Munduruku IT. For the MPF, when transporting criminals, the purpose deviation may have been configured, since the presence of FAB in the region had the objective of supporting operation precisely against environmental crimes committed by the people who would have been transported. “In the present case, there are strong indications of deviation of purpose in the use of FAB aircraft, which, in principle, should be intended for the effectiveness of Operation Green Brazil 2 in the fight against illegal mining,” says the MPF in the order that instituted the investigation of administrative improbity. Under Brazilian laws, all mining within indigenous lands is illegal, so it necessarily commits a crime that admits to being a prospector in indigenous lands.
4073a752ba646a5e91bb8008ebbca53f87cffbe7: The MPF, recognizing the risks and harms that represent the illegal invasions and occupations of the Ituna-Itatá IT, by people who deforest the area and create cattle without authorization from the competent environmental agencies, which pose a risk to the life and physical integrity of the isolated indigenous peoples found in the area and the lack of action of the Public Power to inhibit the illegal settlement in this territory, recommended to Ibama that it promote, within the scope of the surveillance activities in the region of Ituna-Itatá, the effective administrative seizure, transportation and custody of the products and instruments used for the practice of environmental offences, with the exception of the hypothesis of the factual impossibility of guarding or transporting the seized asset; that it carry out the immediate decharacterization, destruction or destruction or destruction of the instruments of environmental crimes committed in the Ituna-Itatá Indigenous Land; and, finally, that it refrains from naming as a faithful depositary of the goods seized administratively responsible for the environmental infringement or persons related to it, in view of the concrete risk of reuse and misuse of the practice of illicit nature. The decision and compliance are awaited.
8f4fde38b86f0ccf3c8a29dad6a01c4dde49d4bd: Damage to the environment; deviation of the river course
8d51f57389207975b7288e4a60b39abbfcb3dd46: Since the construction of the Belo Monte Plant, the indigenous people from all over the region have been harmed in various aspects: invasions of their territories, violence, environmental destruction, among others. One of the most serious problems faced is the use of water to survive both the three indigenous territories and the 25 riverside communities there. Thus, the MPF is charging the Ibama and Belo Monte Plant greater release of hydrogram for these communities. Hydrogram is the amount of water that Ibama determines to be released to bathe the natural course of the river, while the other part is diverted to move the turbines of the Belo Monte plant. Since 2015, the area from which the waters were diverted has been under water stress, and documents from Ibama itself have pointed out, since 2019, damage that can be irreversible and even loss of biodiversity. For the MPF, the Ibama should guarantee the release of more water for the region, since the closed period for Amazonian fish species occurs between November and March and, in the last five years, the reproduction and feeding of fish was prevented in Volta Grande do Xingu, because the Belo Monte plant diverted most of the water from the river, preventing the flooding of forest areas in which spawning occurs and where the most important species are fed for the region, pacu and curimatá. A sixth year without piracema would put at serious risk the survival of ecosystems and indigenous and riverside communities in the region.
c7751401635f4b634bc93c0c2de9428829417030: In view of environmental tragedies throughout the country, especially in the state Pará, the MPF made an order to accompany the action of government organizations in the fight against fires in the Amazon. In the document, the MPF asks INPE to share data collected on the subject in 2020 in relation to the state of Pará, especially regarding areas of federal domain, such as indigenous lands and conservation units. It asks Ibama, ICMBio and the Ministry of the Environment in the state of Pará to provide general clarifications on the subject and to inform, especially: a) records of fires in the state of Pará in the year 2020, with indication, if possible, of extensions, municipalities where they were located and geographical coordinates; b) records of fires in areas of federal domain, such as conservation units and indigenous lands, among others, in the state of Pará in the year 2020; c) how institutions have acted to break down the frame of fires in the state of Pará in the year 2020, what actions were taken, if there are new planned actions, what is the staff framework employed and what are the resources intended for actions. Data from Inpe indicate that, every year, fires and environmental destruction have been increasing alarmingly, compromising the survival of indigenous peoples, other communities and all biodiversity.
53399797f6c8e309558e3911c2de07b751dfc70a: Illegal exploitation of ores; environmental damage
1c904a4def2fb7524e89b77fe0ecc5ec065fe601: For years the Munduruku people have been suffering the serious impacts of illegal - unconstitutional - mining activity within indigenous territory. In 2020, in the midst of the new coronavirus, invasions for illegal mining were greatly intensified, as well as applications for permissions for mining mining with the National Mining Agency (ANM). In the face of the extremely serious situation, the MPF in Pará sent a recommendation to the ANM, in which it explains that the Amazon Forest, the Tapajós River basin and, in particular, the municipality of Itaituba, record an enormous incidence of requests and permissions for the use of mineral resources called Permits of Lavra Garimpeira - PLGs, and that the mismanagement of these mining titles by the ANM has caused direct impacts on public and social heritage, the environment and other diffuse and collective interests; that the indiscriminate proliferation of PLG requirements in the Amazon, the small amount of an effectively regulatory activity by the ANM, has relegated to the exclusive will of the private initiative to affect new areas for mineral exploration, has stimulated pressure by the recategorization of conservation units and the predatory conversion of indigenous lands and forest areas for mining activities. Among several recommendations, the MPF requests the rejection of all requests for mining permission. Provisions are awaited.
9729f1d0d17140dc9fe16fbeb948b742df0217ad: Illegal exploitation of ores; environmental damage
c79fef68cf7d33baca78a35855ce5c80eb65a7a8: The serious impacts of illegal – unconstitutional – mining activity within the territory of the Munduruku people have been taking place for years. As of 2019, invasions for illegal mining have intensified greatly, and even more so in 2020, in the middle of the pandemic. More serious have also been the omissions of the government and the dismantling of federal agencies that should monitor and protect indigenous areas. In this context, and in the face of complaints, the MPF opened an investigation to investigate the leak of Operation Pajé Brabo II, which would be made by Ibama, as well as a video report produced by the program “Fantastic”, Globo Television Network, about mining in indigenous lands. The MPF proposed Public Civil Action against Funai and Ibama, condemning them in the obligation, each within their sphere of assignment, to stop illegal mining in the Munduruku and Sai Gray ITs, in the Jaurizal stream region, areas where the mining has increased very rapidly in recent months, with the aim of containing the socio-environmental damage caused by the intensification of the activity. The Ibama reported that the Brazilian Air Force contradicted the recommendation of the Special Supervisory Group team during the briefing of the operation and logistics planning and, without considering the need to maintain the surprise effect, used the Jacareacanga/PA airport, in advance, to supply the aircraft used during the transport of the aeronautical fuel to the advanced resupply point. This non-observance, according to the environmental authority, implied the leak of the operation on August 4, and resulted in the immediate interruption of mining activities, with the concealment of heavy machinery in the previously established targets. Thus, environmental surveillance actions were not carried out on the main fronts within the Munduruku IT. The MPF requested clarification from the parties.
ce162c520eb7053e1a99a06a2c9afe3d5776467c: In addition to all exploration already carried out by Vale S/A and other companies in the region of TI Xikrin, she is calling for the expansion of the project called “Mina N3 Project – Ferro Carajás Mining Complex”. For this purpose, he planned to hold a public hearing with Ibama in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic on October 8, aiming at environmental licensing of this project. Given the seriousness of the situation, the MPF, MPT and MP/PA recommended to Ibama to suspend the hearing. They also ask: a) that there be formal communication from the licensing body to the MPF, MPT and MP/PA with reasonable time to study the technical documents related to the licensing of the project; b) that there be effective and proven disclosure of the public hearing in press vehicles, with reasonable and adequate time for the population of Parauapebas and surrounding municipalities to be able to appropriate the information available in the EIA-RIMA; c) that there is possibility of effective, safe and face-to-face participation of the communities affected by the enterprise, in particular the indigenous people of the Xikrin IT of Cateté, which will only be possible after the cessation of the state of health emergency resulting from the pandemic caused by the Sars-CoV-2 virus (Covi-19).
8fcd97a549d3dd2183518abeb19bf9d4f785424b: The Union, through the Department of Support for Environmental Licensing and Disappropriation (SALAD) of the Special Secretariat of the Partnership and Investment Program (SE-PPI), without ballast in any procedure to which it has given publicity, elected the indigenous Anderson Painhum, of the Munduruku people, as representative interlocutor to articulate on the interests of its people, in a meeting scheduled to take place in the first week of December 2020, to present the work plan for the Indigenous Component of the Environmental Impact Study (CI-EIA) of Ferrogran. The indigenous was chosen directly by SE-PPI as the potential articulator of the Munduruku people for being president of the Pariri Indigenous Association. As such, he said he was pressured by the Union and issued a public retraction asking the Court of Auditors of the Union (TCU) to suspend the acts of granting Ferrogram. The leadership informed that their association at no time agreed to take part in a meeting on the subject and stressed that the dialogues should observe the Munduruku Protocol and the free, prior and informed consultation procedure, “without pressure”, as well as the ILO Convention 169 (International Labour Organisation). In view of this, the MPF instituted a Public Civil Action against the illegal solicitation of indigenous leaders promoted by SE-PPI, to the extent that the said secretariat, ignoring the specificities of the Munduruku people and without the previous participation of Funai, articulated directly with indigenous leadership to obtain, fraudulently, the consent of all the people Munduruku in relation to the project, disregarding the right and protocol of prior consultation of the people.
082f7b365748303ab29e0631ed2869be89161623: The MPF has judged a Public Civil Action due to the impacts of the paving of BR-163, in its various phases, on the Panará, Bau and Mekragnotire Indigenous Lands, of the Panará/Krenakore and Kayapó Mekrãgnoti/Mebengokrè peoples, whose physical and cultural reproduction is put at risk with the negative of the entrepreneur, the DNIT, in assuming their responsibilities as polluter-payer, and in the face of the deliberate action of Funai contrary to its institutional role. In action, the defendants are Funai, DNIT, Union and Ibama.
5d34e285007a852df79bcfd1a4ab94049004ce94: Illegal exploitation of ores; environmental damage
88989babe1b9642ffc4b0c212a51e64d724dedc3: Leaderships denounce new area being devastated by illegal mining. Although the area is on the Suriname border, the indigenous communities of Brazil, located on the banks of the Paru do Oeste and Marapi rivers, are being affected because the waters of the rivers are dirty and polluted. The mining site is very close to the border and in a central area of the communities. Of the 34 villages in the region, 23 are within a radius of up to 40 km of the mine. The leaders also report that the prospectors carry weapons; the indigenous peoples of both Brazil and Suriname are frightened and fear that, in addition to the destruction of the environment and natural resources, violence will increase on the spot. The indigenous also spotted quadricycles, mowers, motors and chainsaws with the prospectors. The Tiriyó, Kaxuyana and Txikuyana Indigenous Leaders Council gave a letter to the authorities in early October denouncing the situation; they also attached aerial images registered by Suriname indigenous people on September 30, 2020. The photos show the camp of the prospectors next to an airstrip, and the river bed stained with a dark color. The nearest villages, just 8 km from the mine, are Turunkane and Mesepituru, where about ten families live. According to the chief of Mesepituru, Zaqueu Tiriyó, planes often fly over the region. The Suriname Indigenous Organization (OIS) accompanied a Surinamese government delegation to the site. According to OIS, two men were arrested and taken to the capital Paramaribo to testify. The entourage stayed just over an hour at the scene and found no evidence of mining activity. The Brazilian Army claims it went to the site and found no invaders.
2e8bacee41ec0edc6e09114efb182e69122ae121: The situation experienced by the indigenous peoples of TI Waterfall Dry is very serious, due to the presence and harmful action of countless invaders and the inoperance and neglect of the government in carrying out the disintrusion of the territory. The municipality of Uruará entered with a Public Civil Action to paralyze an Ibama supervisory action in IT. For the MPF, which manifested itself to the Federal Court of Santarém on the case, the action of the city defends unnecessary interests of environmental offenders, the same who violently attacked the Ibama inspectors in early May, when servers complied with inspection recommendation. The MPF argues that the real purpose of the action is to prevent the supervision of Ibama on environmental offenders in the indigenous land and its surroundings – which, it should be noted, is essential to safeguard the health of the indigenous and settlers who inhabit the region, before the possible transmission of Covid-19 by environmental offenders. With this, the Municipality of Uruá does not stand beside the indigenous, riverside and colonists who live there, but next to environmental offenders (crickets and loggers) who illegally exploit the area and who have intensified the practice of environmental crimes.
7462cd6bdc234406e79a5384119ba975ac178bab: A foreign company was authorized, in 2019, to carry out logging, with approval of concession for 30 years, through management plan, in the Extractive Reserve (Resex) Tapajós-Arapiuns. Such authorization occurred without prior consultation to the community, which is illegal, in accordance with Brazilian legislation and ILO Convention 169. The reserve is partially superimposed on Tupinambá territory and, although the area under logging concession is not overlapping with the land claimed by Tupinambá, the leaders continue to denounce the impacts suffered by the exploitation. This complaint had already been made in 2019, but the problem remained in 2020, with the worsening of the Covid-19 pandemic. According to the indigenous, an open road for the flow of the extracted wood crosses the traditional occupation area Tupinambá. In addition to the transit of trucks to scare the animals, whose hunting is important to ensure the food sovereignty of the people, the road also generates concern about the possibility of invasions in other areas of the territory claimed by the Tupinambá. This is a very serious situation which requires immediate action from the competent authorities.
61f44dfb23f0437d1e1fc3d415aa94221c13f2e2: Although already reported, the Kayapó people continue to report that the high concentration of illegal mining within the indigenous land has contaminated Rio Branco, especially due to the use of mercury. The river bathes the region, and contamination has greatly affected community food, since fish are its main source of survival. Most of the prospectors have been in full activity since 2014, according to reports from the ICMBio coordination. A survey by MPF points out that national forests in southwest Pará are also being targeted by illegal mining. The MPF reported that the National Mining Agency (ANM) would be issuing licences irregularly, using only authorizations provided by municipal environmental departments, without research or environmental impact studies. The Kayapó community has experienced a tense climate in its own territory, especially in 2020, when all the problems were aggravated by the Covid-19 pandemic situation.
4775f6653675c996a43688576f506f56a7996d39: The Indigenous Associations Porekrô, Kakarekrê and Baypran, of the Xikrin people, through a study by doctor João Paulo Botelho Vieira Filho, have made several warnings to the Brazilian authorities about the serious consequences of mining in indigenous lands and their proximity in the lives of the native peoples. In the territory of Xikrin, the pollution of the Cateté and Itacaiúna rivers by heavy metals such as cadmium, manganese, iron, copper, chromium and nickel from the S11D Eliezer Batista mine and the Onça-Puma plant, both of the Vale mining company, persists without any containment measures, since the first reports presented by the indigenous before 2015. IT is polluted by the mineral wastes of the plant that reach the Cateté river, from which indigenous families survive. The Itacaúnas River receives the waters of the Cateté River with all the pollution it suffers, and flows into the Tocantins River, on the banks of the city of Marabá. Fish, which are the main source of food for families, have disappeared from the river. All water used for drinking, bathing and hygiene and cleaning services is contaminated. The health of this population, as well as the surroundings, is totally compromised, including in future generations. The situation is chaotic, especially in 2020, year worsened by the Covid-19 pandemic. The Xikrin people cry for help.
3417c071711b10626420bd9066eb221eaea1f55b: TI Reach/Bacajá is constantly invaded by landowners, who threaten indigenous leaders. In 2019, the Xikrin returned to the land that was invaded, and appealed to the MPF to remove the invaders. The Xikrin reported that tens of hectares were burned and had already planted pasture in some of the invaded areas. Indigenous lands in the region are under intense pressure from livestock projects. In addition to landowners and farmers, TI Reacheira-Bacajá is also affected by illegal mining activities and deforestation, in addition to having been affected by the construction of the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant. Indians are constantly threatened by gunmen. The climate in the region is very tense and, with the Covid-19 pandemic, the situation has worsened further. An action to reinstate possession against the invaders has been filed in Justice since 2019.
44e7843d14205cd9dfd00fff2457752fa95d50b2: Even being registered since 2007, the Apyterewa IT is invaded, waiting for the disintrusion of the non-indigenous. Indigenous families live under constant tension with the presence of non-indigenous people in IT, as well as large farmers involved in the works of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Complex. There is also illegal mining activity within IT. Environmental damage is immense due to predatory activities carried out by non-indigenous people. As if the whole situation of rights violations were not enough, the Parakanã are experiencing numerous difficulties and risks due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
5df198aa13ba48cd451c2a586a2d73eafc438b10: The Juruna and Arara indigenous people who live in TI Paquiçamba have suffered, for many years, the impacts of the works of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Complex. Most water resources, which should be used and survived by indigenous people, are dammed to the hydroelectric works. In addition, the indigenous population still faces serious situations due to the presence of invaders in their territory, with the large projects of mining companies, such as the Volta Grande do Xingu project of the Canadian company Belo Sun. The MPF monitors the processes. Violations of rights and situations of violence are numerous, even more aggravated by the Covid-19 pandemic.
c026bd7fe5d2cb19257e19aaba755435d5df9f89: In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, the indigenous peoples of Parakanã IT continue to suffer the impacts of ore exploration on their territory. These situations cause serious impacts on indigenous health and environmental damage.
9dac1d5a3394fcdd6cc0429f5126af91ed10c279: Gold mine bales began to act on the Xingu River, both at the time of the Koatinemo IT and above it, on the course of the river. The prospecting practiced by ferries is rustic, using hoses to vacuum the land from the bottom of the river. When discarded, sediments form the “roasts of rafts” – sands that hinder navigation, erod the banks of the river and even chase fish away, generating impacts on the food of the people. The use of mercury by prospectors also impacts the health of indigenous people. In 2019, the Asurini had already captured five prospectors who were working inside the indigenous land.
99b7d4e6580e79bc7f5b933df9901570dfaacd0c: The illegal activity of prospectors in the indigenous territories that make up TI Baixo Tapajós I keep worrying the indigenous and riverside families. The degradation of the environment is immense, especially the pollution of rivers, which are a source of survival of the peoples of the region. With the contamination of the waters, the health of the indigenous, including the future generations, is compromised, because all are affected by the use of mercury and cyanide in the mining activities. The year 2020 was particularly difficult for indigenous populations, because, in addition to living with the invasions, contaminations and degradation of natural wealth, they have still been and are being impacted by the Covid-19 pandemic, still facing the omission of the government due to the lack of contingency plan of the virus.
0ee4f094bc6ca47d3f5a30fa6c6d35e8e6d07a52: Despite the extreme difficulty facing the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020, the indigenous peoples of TI Alto Rio Guamá still live with illegal mining activity and deleterious effects on their lands. The survival of indigenous peoples is compromised due to degradation of the environment and contamination of the waters of the rivers, caused by mining activity.
0a301daf3d3c3672e93a5fffd92264de33b1acf3: In addition to facing an atypical year in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic, the Munduruku of the Santareno Plateau continue to have difficulty accessing drinking water. Farms of monocultures of soybeans and corn, and also cattle raising, have caused the silting of water sources of the indigenous territory, located in Santarém. The silting of Igarapé do Açaí directly affects indigenous families of Açaizal Village. The igarapé is the only natural source of water used for hygiene, household chores, and for food support gardens. In addition to silting, watercourses are also contaminated by pesticides used in farms.
65d8e668509f81aa955de1c92c33ad624005b19f: The year 2020 was very hard for the indigenous populations, due to the pandemic and the lack of effective policies to combat the virus by the federal government. Several indigenous lands that already suffer from invasion problems were even more affected. Even with the forced isolation to avoid the contagion by Covid-19, the IT Asurini will trade, as well as other peoples in the region, continue to have to live with the illegal mining activities that occur within the territory. The serious damage to the environment and the contamination of water sources, caused by illegal activity, threaten daily the health and life of indigenous people.
