a365738ed5e144055fc95d7e432b69d6cd4681dc: The TI Las Casas, of the Kayapó people, remains invaded by the occupants, who refuse to leave, even though they have already received compensation in court. This is a very worrying situation, especially in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic, where it is necessary to be in isolation to avoid infection by the disease. The coexistence of the Kayapó with the non-indigenous is tense, since they feel empowered by the anti-indigenous discourse and practice of the current government.
ec43dd7349c9b664da96ca902f77720cf1ad44cf: Invasion; greasing; exploitation of natural resources
9dca02e075913e7b79c0c20c46df4b969f24dc58: The TI ́s Sawre Apompu and Sawre Jaybu, in the middle Tapajós region, are in the process of identification and delimitation by Funai. However, areas within these territories are being seized by non-indigenous Itaituba, including a cement and brick manufacturing company. In difficult times like these of pandemic, in addition to the disease and its harmful consequences, the Munduruku still have to deal with the threats and aggressions made by the invaders of their traditional lands. The anti-indigenous discourse of the federal government and the lack of effective actions of the control, inspection and protection agencies to the indigenous territories have encouraged the attacks of the invaders.
08e198dba3f89587a31e170b4cb2cd66ad1870cf: Invaders of Apyterewa IT surrounded the base of the federal government, where there were agents of Ibama, Funai and National Force. These teams were notifying IT invaders about the deadline for them to withdraw. The federal agents were coerced by a group of 50 to 70 people, who set up a barricade with tires, nails and pieces of wood on a bridge to prevent access to the base, threatening the physical integrity of public agents who were working on settlement actions against illegal deforestation. One of the invaders was caught with a homemade bomb. The Apyterewa IT was the second most deforested indigenous land in Brazil between 2018 and 2019, according to data from Prodes and Inpe. The MPF entered with reintegration of possession action, aiming to remove the invaders and not obstruction of the Funai base in the indigenous land. The federal court, in response to the request, has determined the immediate cessation of any activity of blocking or threatening to block Funai's headquarters in IT; the removal of all invasive persons from indigenous territory; the seizure of machinery, equipment, vehicles or others that confront the fulfillment of the decision; and the prohibition of a new blockade or threat of blocking the roads that give access to Funai's headquarters in IT.
6a9457f7632326d892fe50ad247974e400c124b9: In addition to all the problems faced daily by the Potiguara - São Miguel people, aggravated by the Covid-19 pandemic period and its consequences, they have still suffered the invasions of their territory. Leaderships denounce that illegal activity of sugar plants continues to occur within the indigenous land. Non-indigenous invaders occupy the territory with sugarcane plantations, causing conflicts with the people, deforesting the native forest that remains, destroying the environment and polluting the rivers. Complaints have already been referred to the government, asking for measures, but nothing has been done so far.
e4a5e719c80b13ed097adff45838be1bb0db69ef: Just like the Potiguara - São Miguel people, the Potiguara - Monte Mor people, in the region of Rio Tinto and Marking, also continues to be impacted by the same difficulties. In addition to all everyday problems, aggravated by the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its consequences, the Potiguara - Monte Mor people have still faced the invasions of their territory. Leaderships report the occurrence of active sugar plant within the indigenous territory. Non-indigenous invaders occupy IT with sugar cane plantations, causing conflicts with the people, deforesting the native forest that remains, destroying the environment and polluting the rivers. Complaints have already been referred to the government, asking for measures, but so far without a favorable solution to the indigenous people.
d53246f56d4b97e1287605e2ba23a1355666eaaa: The indigenous people of Tabajara struggle for the regularization of their traditional territory. People's leaders have denounced that invaders continue to enter their territory to engage in illegal mining activity. They report that this illegal activity is deprecating the environment, polluting the rivers and compromising the health of indigenous people and the population of the region. The indigenous also denounce the performance of companies that produce cement and gravel. The climate in the area is tense, the Tabajara people suffer from conflicts with the invaders and the devastation of the environment. Complaints were made to the government, requesting measures and progress of land issues.
9093ffca4a6a3bd67da062f17acf8f200d7fb7b3: Leadership reports that a pole that signals the location of the demarcation marks of the indigenous land was broken. The pole is located on the right bank of Lake Itaipu, at point 257. The landmarks and poles had been placed recently by Itaipu Binacional, but the non-indigenous do not respect the limits and continue to plant within the indigenous land and destroy the landmarks.
dcf5d4cb4f68615fbe8ff859a377c9663c84594b: Illegal hunting and fishing; illegal logging
9d11520c3ad3118d1e1b890c4c75a59e42b71ced: Leaders denounced to Radio Club de Palmas environmental crimes that are being committed in the territory. According to Ambrózio Luís dos Santos, former chief of the community, there are several cases of environmental crimes, such as hunting and felling trees. In Mato Branco village, machinery was used in the stock of a forest area. According to the leadership, indigenous people from other regions were doing this work. The former chief charges greater performance of the Instituto Terra e Água (formerly IAP – Instituto Ambiental do Paraná) in monitoring and combating these crimes, since the agency has knowledge of the facts, has already made notifications, but the downfall of forests continues.
2a22f36cb2aa2809bbd056ada012d58764e1309f: Leadership reports that on March 14th and August 9th, IT was invaded by strange people, who entered with motorcycles and cars and carried weapons, intimidating the indigenous. Both invasions occurred on weekends and in the same way. The community got scared, and you don't know what this invasion was about. The episodes were reported to the Federal Police.
d5c3d65de35a094f515c9e449f0826842b52c166: Between April and September, more than 300 hectares of IT were illegally destroyed by fire, including subsistence gardens. The health of the indigenous is also affected, especially by respiratory problems. According to a survey by the team of indigenous environmental inspectors, about 12% of the total forest of araucarias of IT no longer exists. Other native forests have also been drastically reduced, such as imbuia, cinnamon and bracatinga; they are classified as endangered or vulnerable species. In addition to forests, wild animals are also being decimated by the action of fire.
1b8c16015cb59f72ac5edc7c5ed9d9317762f5bb: Leaderships reported to Funai and MPF that non-indigenous people built a rubber shop and a garage for cars, near the villas of the Avá-Guarani. The annulment of the I.T. Ordinance has made it difficult to remove non-indigenous people from this site.
d48d38fd53f6386f38ab82a54610e230c9a3fd60: Invasion of loggers; deforestation; illegal hunting
22410e3f5bba6991ccfe466228b9bf856087f5be: In Tarumã territory, near the village Tarumã Mirim, in the place called Ka’Aguy Mirim Porã, which means “Little Beautiful Forest”, where a new village is intended to start, an environmental crime occurred caused by timber invaders, who cut native trees. In addition to deforestation, the invasion of non-indigenous animals in the previous months also occurred for the purpose of hunting forest animals.
197644ef1cf582852720982f7cf86f2b85eb5f37: Leadership reports that a local company entered the Indian area with a truck to dump garbage and debris. The indigenous Wilson Moreira photographed the occurrence, which was communicated to Funai and MPF through a complaint document. He also reported to the organs the occurrence of deforestation in the area and the destruction of an entrance gate at the site. Photos were attached to the document of the logs of cut trees that were placed along the road, the destroyed gate and the truck dumping garbage into IT.
58c60e4b3d55767899e495d080024125a7594caa: Landing of indigenous area; deforestation; use of pesticides
335c413c7b0939a31fa76bc1ad2916a833597a2b: An agricultural company in the city of Espigão Alto rented part of the Indigenous Land, about 50 acres, for the planting of GM cereals. Thus, indigenous people have experienced serious situations in their territory, such as deforestation, fires and pollution of streams and springs due to the use of pesticides, compromising the health of families.
a99577334c960b2144ef579a207a9fb048ca01ee: The MPF received reports of invasions to the indigenous area, with felling of trees considered sacred in the Pankararu tradition, as well as the destruction of fences and subsistence gardens.
fe51c660ca125d63872b5b00b001aaea7e774569: Leadership reports that the Indian school was targeted by criminals, who set fire to the school, burning books and documents and destroying equipment. In addition to the arson, offensive and prejudiced phrases were plotted on the walls. The Civil Police and Funai have been activated for the proper measures and punishment of criminals.
62b0889d770f211dbe17d82e5bb6151a5ab8bdf4: Leaderships of the Kambiwá people denounce that the invaders in the IT, who are farmers and squatters, continue to burn the caatinga for the manufacture of coal and stealing timber for commercialization, especially in the municipality of Ibimirim. Not enough were all the difficulties faced in a year of Covid-19 pandemic and the harsh consequences of it, the indigenous families continue to have to deal with a tense environment in coexistence with the invaders. The environment is deteriorating every day and the entire biome is at risk, harming the indigenous community in its physical, cultural and spiritual survival. IT is registered, but the progress of the land regularization process is paralyzed.
d85ba7b4979fb0312f40f53d0b82115681a41e3d: The invasion of indigenous lands advances amid the pandemic. Gamela Indians had their houses burned down and ravaged gardens in the Barra do Correntim community. According to leaderships, the practice is related to the grilling, common in the region. “Here, the gunman comes from everything that is a place. It's a plague. It spreads more than the coronavirus”, reports James Rodrigues dos Santos Gamela. The community suffers from the severe expansion of the agricultural border of the project called Matopiba – acronym of the initials of the states of Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí and Bahia, which has become, since the 1970s, an area of strong investment of agribusiness, causing serious environmental damage. The Cimi Nordeste requested the Prosecutors measures such as the establishment of a procedure for demarcation of the traditional territory, water supply to the responsible bodies, in addition to the notification of Funai and Sesai, to assume their responsibilities of protecting the Gamela during the pandemic.
52d242d8a0e78e5d9ed52d99e3ae211904cf8f15: The Guarani live in a small area of land, which has been invaded by strange people who have improperly built houses and have been using space for the storage of old cars, machines and equipment, among others. The area Lami/Pindó Poty had the demarcation procedure initiated in 2012 by Funai and, according to information from the indigenous agency, the studies of identification and delimitation of the land were completed and in them the traditionality of land occupation by the Guarani Mbya is proven. In Lami, the place where the Mbyá live was called camp, because the houses were always improvised and without basic sanitation. The government has expressed no concern about attending the families who lived there. Recently, after much pressure from the Mbyá’s struggle and resistance organizations, Funai, Sesai and other bodies began to serve the community minimally. However, the community lives daily with the presence of non-indigenous people in an unhealthy and hostile environment. The indigenous claim the presence of Funai agents on site and immediate removal of the invaders and regularization of the territory.
6b5b190fb9a5cc7b873b8fbd2a5d6ab8dc1e578a: After receiving reports of illegal extraction of sand within the indigenous land, the Military Brigade and the Environmental Squad of the municipality of Camaquã went to the site for investigation. The cops caught a 55-year-old man, who was armed with a shotgun while he was pulling sand out of IT. The perp was arrested and led to the police station.
06b446680eb42ec0ad22ab6bb2f887e7b0fb0ca6: Rent of indigenous land; use of pesticides
07c194354efb42dad62d0d1d35121da7e4ac1d0e: In 2020, internal conflicts ceased. However, invasions of Kaingang territory persist. These invasions occur through the practice of land rental for the planting of monocultures, especially transgenic soybeans. Thus, the soil of the territory is polluted by the use of pesticides, compromising the health of the indigenous population and the surroundings.
9077f607db8ddb22ff36c1041f256eac96ad1b1d: Wood from within the indigenous land was overthrown, transported and marketed illegally. By anonymous tip, a 46-year-old man was arrested by the Environmental Military Police in a truck, carrying a load of timber taken from Igarapé Lage IT.
a7da5888fc9baf4f02b25ea8401bca03460bb90f: After denouncing leaders that there were invaders in the area practicing illegal logging, the Federal Police and Ibama arrested two men, with whom they seized three trucks, one tractor, several logs of wood and three radios of clandestine communication.
c436eded66b42cfac5cb9129350c10960f63095c: Illegal exploitation of ore; environmental damage
5454073808b96a1b34ec44fcbe1c049a05542508: Denunciation of illegal activity of prospectors within IT, exploiting natural resources, mainly diamonds. The Federal Police launched an operation against the illegal exploitation of diamonds, issuing several search and seizure warrants in Rondônia and several other states, such as São Paulo, Roraima, Paraná, Piauí, Mato Grosso, Minas Gerais and Distrito Federal. In addition to prospectors, there are brokers and entrepreneurs who sell diamonds not only in Brazil, but also in European countries. For many years, the indigenous have denounced the invasions of the government, and they have been awaiting supervision, withdrawal and punishment of the invaders. The illegal action devastates forests, pollutes rivers and compromises the health of the indigenous population, especially children and the elderly.
5860874e297b3111b8a07066b4683bcce604864f: After several reports, the Federal Police conducted an IT operation to combat environmental crimes. In addition to trucks and tractors, three clandestine sawmills were found inside the indigenous land, where wood illegally extracted from the forest was processed. According to the Ibama estimate, in only one of the sawmills there were over 4,000 m3 of wood. As if the pandemic of the coronavirus, without control and without assistance, the indigenous communities still face very serious problems caused by the invaders of their lands, which deprecate the environment, pollute the waters of the rivers, carry diseases and all kinds of violence.
4a3df9824611976f3b47a3d9fe9163d93c81ad61: Denunciations of deforestation and invasions in indigenous lands led the Federal Police of Rondônia, accompanied by the Ibama, Funai and Military Police to conduct an operation to combat these crimes. At the site were found several points of deforestation, with many fallen trees, sawmills, tractors, truck loaded with logs, chainsaws, radio communicators and motorcycles. The equipment was discarded by Ibama. Investigations should continue with the aim of identifying and punishing criminals. The indigenous populations in the region live under constant threats and violence committed by the invaders, who ravage the environment, from where the indigenous take their livelihood, practice their way of life, culture and religion.
a9a12cea14a0f550725494c0a200242c8f63e1f2: Since 2011, the Karipuna people have denounced the invasion of their territory. In 2015, a new phase of the invasion began, with the land allotment and greasing inside the demarcated territory. There are 84 lots in the Rural Environmental Registry (CAR) that focus on T I Karipuna, according to data from the government of Rondônia state, through the Department of Development and Environment. There are numerous areas down and the bites made with georeferencing. The lots are marked by the landowners, who move freely in the territory. The lack of effective supervision leaves the territory free for the invasion. There are, therefore, 84 lots, with registration in the CAR, and the state of Rondônia releases the registration number, but does not provide the name of the offender. Leaderships filed a document with complaints to Funai, Ibama, 6th Chamber and MPF, demanding measures.
8126c5ef94191a0a0927a3ce4fd875f569e8be17: Although there has been a decrease in deforestation in the Karipuna IT, there is the practice of maintaining and cleaning the areas already deforested by invaders within the territory. The equivalent of 520 hectares were deforested by October 2020. The invaders feel legitimated by the speech of the current president, and continued to invade the territory in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic and intimidating the people, who cannot move freely to their subsistence activities, such as hunting and collecting chestnuts. Leaderships sent complaint to Funai, Ibama, 6th Chamber and MPF demanding measures.
bdc6d260e517ad85c416dbd63ab3a6f6a4d04f44: Deforestation; soybean monoculture; damage to heritage
282adb3a01c79c2f3140a561fca3d01472360916: Since 2012, the Guarasugwe people have been demanding with Funai the establishment of the working group to identify and demarcate the Guarasugwe Indigenous Land. The territory is totally devastated by the great soy growers, who are in every way eliminating the ancestral evidence of the presence of these people. Many funeral urns were destroyed by farmers who invaded the traditional territory of the people. While awaiting land regularization, the people live in a situation of miserability in the outskirts of the cities of Porto Velho, Costa Marques, Pimenteiras, Guajará Mirim and São Francisco do Guaporé. Leaderships sent complaints to the MPF, Funai/Brasília and the 6th Chamber asking for urgent action.
9a932c1053a073724ba0a5a6c89ae19d4d9c0c0c: Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau TI has been suffering for years with invasions, deforestation, land grating and burning. Leaderships denounce that the Brazilian State never had a serious policy to remove invaders from indigenous land. The organized community conducts territorial monitoring and surveillance of the territory. In one of the monitoring and inspection works carried out by the people, the indigenous seized a motorcycle and a tractor used to invade, deforest and topple the trees. The Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau also kept in the community the owner of the vehicles, a logger, until the arrival of Ibama and the police. The case was reported to Funai, Ibama and the Federal Police, demanding action.
9dd78fa13f055469abd7108969beae1125b2a090: In 2020, IT Karipuna suffered numerous outbreaks of fires, due to the action of the invaders, who continued to invade the territory and maintain illegal possession of the land, a situation aggravated by the pandemic of the new coronavirus and the risk of contamination that its presence means for the Karipuna. Many of the outbreaks of fires were to keep the area deforested; as in previous years, invaders deforest, clean the area and grass for further livestock activity within the indigenous territory. Leaderships sent a complaint document to the MPF and await action.
8390bbd97235c2312080621a15cf5f6401fabafd: Invasion; deforestation; fires; land grabbing; mining
b755d4bd5016572e428e871af4880729048155e1: Leadership denounces the occurrence of invasions of Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau IT and serious environmental crimes such as deforestation, crickets and fires. According to reports from the residents, until October, the entire region surrounding IT was surrounded by an immense fog of smoke, a result of the numerous fires in the surrounding area and within the territory, made by non-indigenous invaders. More than 25 km2 of the interior of the indigenous territory had already been destroyed, leaving the isolated peoples living in the region of the Cautary River even more vulnerable, in addition to threats by the presence of prospectors and landowners working within the IT. According to information from leaders and people in the region, there are three groups of prospectors, who operate armed within the indigenous land, at different points: San Francisco do Guaporé, Seringueiras and São Miguel do Guaporé. The peoples of this region are never at peace on their own land. With the legislative measures that are being approved by Congress and others already approved, invasions have made a significant advance in this IT, as it is one of the largest indigenous lands in the state. The invaders lost fear and respect and circulate in various parts of this territory; they are loggers, squatters, prospectors, hunters and landowners doing allotments within IT. The increase of invaders was observed from 2019 onwards, who feel supported by the anti-indigenous discourse of the federal government. It is estimated that the current number of invaders is more than 1,000 people, directly associated with the increasing rates of deforestation verified in that IT. The risks to the survival of the three isolated peoples within IT have become even greater in the context of Covid-19. The indigenous are forced to do the inspection on their own, because the Etnoenvironmental Front of Funai has a restricted group for such a wide region. There is practically no oversight, which favors the entry of invaders into various access points to this land. The leaders and their allies make constant complaints, but the responsible authorities have not taken steps to curb the invasions. In April 2020, indigenous leader Ari Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau was brutally murdered, probably by invading loggers, due to his territorial surveillance action. A report was forwarded to the MPF requesting action.
f4012eb33d800d236ec44048daf3235dbcb3f6ef: After several reports of invasions, the Federal Police launched an operation against illegal mining activities in IT. Several equipment used to extract ores – mainly diamonds – and wood were destroyed. A bridge built to transport wood from the indigenous land was imploded. So far, no one's been arrested. Leadership expects investigation and punishment from criminals.
185c292836a7c50bc159ed82800ad35fee64dfcd: The Arara people suffer constant attacks by invaders in their traditional territory. These attacks have intensified mainly with the anti-indigenous discourse of the current ruler, which facilitates the action of groups of invaders, loggers and prospectors, who feel authorized in their illegal actions, as well as in coercion and threats against leadership. On December 10, after numerous denunciations of the indigenous to Funai, the Environmental Police and the MPF, there was an operation of the Federal Police in Igarapé Lourdes IT, with seizure of machinery used by the prospectors and arrest of ten invaders. In the same IT, the Gavião people also face serious situations and the recurrent pressure of invaders. In recent years, operations have been carried out by PF, Environmental Police and Funai, with arrests of invaders, but after a while others return and maintain the practice of deforestation and illegal logging. The communities continue to denounce the situation to the competent bodies, but lack permanent supervision and punishment for criminals.
284ad384f2805e87d294cd7145cd15d8c151dd43: The Cassupá people were affected by the construction of the BR-364 highway in 2018, with the overthrow of the front wall, which gives access to the village. This exposes the community to all kinds of vulnerability, considering the violence in the city of Porto Velho. Since the destruction of the wall, the community has been presenting documents to the DER to restore it. The document was also forwarded to the MPF, but so far, no action has been taken.
0f8ff5ef8524b009236c8ca9a1402582f0187a12: After several denunciations of the indigenous reporting invasions in their territory, on December 2, the Federal Police carried out Operation Kawyra, in order to arrest a suspect of deforestation, burning, batching and selling glebas illegally within the IT Karipuna. According to PF, the target of the search and arrest warrant is one of the main suspects of hacking into IT. His name hasn't been released, and so far, there's no information as to whether the suspect was found.
7ce7c7911b1ccadf15fa93da893dff715bc3dc34: With the process of demarcation paralyzed at Funai since 2015, the territory is pressed by the project Terra Legal, through which cattle farmers occupy and deforest the traditional indigenous occupation area. Clandestine fishing also affects one of the main food resources of the indigenous people. The situation of the Miguelenos remains the same, but by the end of 2020, the people triggered the MPF, which moved a Civil Action Public by pressing Funai to complete the demarcation of their lands.
a1ae4a362e6b7502e6935ad6bfd7f0b1c85835f5: According to leaders, even after an operation by the Military Police and Ibama, which culminated in the arrest of eight people involved in deforestation and illegal logging within IT, the invaders were gradually returning into the territory. Funai's lack of oversight and the anti-indigenous discourse of the federal government contribute to the entry of invaders into IT.
80a8223a3ef9004ae06d8444b27834b8f07052c2: Despite PF's operations in IT September 7, in which machinery used in illegal mining and deforestation has been destroyed, loggers always return to their criminal practices. According to leaders and other people in the region, the removal of wood remains and the devastation of the forest only increases. Despite the indigenous complaints, Funai remains absent.
e007755bab430d33536c1b654de9461db33a49e7: Just as the other indigenous lands that have been increasingly invaded by loggers or prospectors, in TI Zoró also continues the exploitation of wood. The inspections only take place when the complaints are made insistently with the responsible bodies. The fact that there is no permanent oversight program facilitates the entry of invaders. It is common to return the invaders a time after operations, especially today, with the anti-indigenous discourse of the federal government. Funai, the supervisory body, has not prioritized these actions lately. Ibama only operates from denunciations, when people insist.
cdb4b51637c79149fb859b45a56122e45274684b: Invasion; Grinding; predatory hunting and fishing
a16af8b1436f379516e9c08b81276dbbf1daa59a: Indigenous people denounce illegal action by landowners, hunters and fishermen who invade their lands, ravage the environment and generate conflicts in the region. The responsible authorities have not taken steps.
7190122631fcce7c98b3f861b265b7ef0b7eae14: For years, the Oro Wari people have been waiting for the authorities to regulate their territories and remove the invaders, which cause conflicts with the indigenous and destroy the environment and livelihoods of families.
6cef6194bac5cc3abd4bbf38fffee3eeaf1143ed: The Rio Negro Ocaia IT had its declaratory ordinance published in 2011. However, the halting of the demarcation process and the fact that the disintrusion and compensation of the occupants were not performed encourage the irregular occupation of the territory, increasing the number of invaders and generating great tension between indigenous and non-indigenous. The Oro Wari people are waiting for the authorities to ensure their right to the regularized land.
5b3dd34697cd41209e0ab4a8a8ef7254b49bf4e8: For a long time, private companies have been withdrawing from the Guaporé river an unidentified ore. The fact has already been reported to the authorities, but there has been no action against companies, which has been causing damage to the Rio Guaporé IT and the environment.
edd755feac4b9996c7ca69200719efe69f961422: Illegal exploitation of ores; deforestation; environmental damage; allotment
577e607fa5ba4adf30b3ab3cfc764db602d28e40: Waimiri-Atroari Indians reported a mining invasion within the Pirititi TI. TI Pirititi is next to TI Waimiri-Atroari and was banned in 2012, by Funai, for protection of the isolated group Pirititi. In addition, according to satellite images analyzed by ISA, since January 2020 the opening of a branch within the land of Pirititi has advanced, with delimitation and opening of lots throughout it. Waimiri expeditions carried out in April and May found and photographed deforested areas, up to 17 canvas and straw camps and a wooden house with ready-made fields. The Pirititi have been mentioned by Waimiri since the 1970s, when the exploitation of Waimiri IT began by the opening of BR-174 and the mining exploration within the territory. It was considered that the Pirititi could have been extinct, but with the ban on the area by Funai in 2012, this group of Pirititi was protected. Since that time, they were already being pressured by timber enterprises in the region. Currently, in the middle of the pandemic, and with the disarticulation of the protection agencies, these indigenous are threatened in their survival, due to the increase of invasions, deforestation and mining activity. Not only the indigenous, but the entire ecosystem is in imminent threat of destruction.
afc11ebe3b76fbb0dc9a662ada861d3645f8a316: The mining and mining bills, promoted by federal and state governments, have become incentives for prospectors to invade indigenous lands. In the case of Raposa Serra do Sol IT, between 2019 and 2020 the mining has been increasing significantly. In the Serras region, the prospectors even entered the most difficult places of access and settled in several points, resuming some areas that were already occupied by the mining decades ago, such as Mutum, Cold Water or Uiramutã or the Campo Formoso region. The social and environmental impact is very serious. In some places, the prospectors report to the indigenous that the new federal government would have already released the mining activity in indigenous lands and that their activity would not be illegal anymore. In the Raposa region, still within the Raposa Serra do Sol IT, an approximate number of 2,000 prospectors settled in Serra do Atola. In 2020, he circulated a video with testimony of Senator Chico Rodrigues (DEM/RR) inside the mining, encouraging activity within the indigenous lands. The presence of sheds covered with canvas, internal markets and a permanent traffic of vehicles that also cross the housing areas of the communities themselves is visible. The installation of mills and machinery for washing the extracted material in the rock causes a serious environmental impact on the region's streams. The indigenous communities established surveillance and protection points of the territory in various places of the indigenous land and some people received threats. In other indigenous lands in the eastern region of Roraima, such as TI Pium, TI Boqueirão and TI Manoá-Pium, among others, there is also the presence of prospectors or the invasion by the prospectors of these territories with access corridors to mining within the Yanomami IT. The Uraricoera River, one of the formators of Rio Branco, is one of the most affected by the mining activity and already presents evidence of contamination by the color of the water, spots on the part of the submerged stones in the waters or decrease the availability of fish, one of the main food sources of the communities and other artisanal fishermen. Complaints were filed with the MPF, Army and Federal Police.
fd6fe167537130e2d8c479f7f95094e16f81c86a: Invasion; illegal exploitation of ores; deforestation; environmental damage
fbc36bc7c4632bf8c44456727009654d567051d3: The massive presence of the prospector remains within the Yanomami IT. Since 2019, the Hutukara Association Yanomami (HAY) has denounced the increase of the mining invasion in the territory, following the messages and incentives that the federal government expresses in favor of illegal activity within indigenous lands. According to HAY, an approximate number of 20,000 prospectors would be installed at Yanomami IT. The Uraricoera, Mucajai, Couto Magalhães, Parima, Apiau and Catrimani rivers would be the areas most affected directly by the mining. The social and environmental impacts are extremely serious. According to reports, during the first half of 2020, the mining presence in the Middle Catrimani region has grown (the presence of prospectors in the Upper Catrimani has been proven, at least, since 2017). Boat and ferry traffic across the river was a constant throughout the year. In February 2020, machinery and groups of prospectors – coming down from Alto Catrimani and being supplied by river, air and land – were already installed and functioning at the time of the waterfall of Poraque, after several treatatives and pressures of the prospectors in the region since 2019. In the lower course of the Catrimani River, since December 2019, prospectors have been making exploratory visits – in order to seek possible agreements, pointing out alleged benefits, but provoking intimidation – in the region of the Waroma and Okarasisi communities. In the successive months, they established temporary camps in the vicinity of those communities to conduct the exploration of the ore. Also since 2019, some prospectors have explored the course of the Pacú river, settling at the confluence of this river with the Catrimani. In the Uraricoera River, regions such as Waikás and Aracaçá concentrated, by December 2020, more than 50% of the environmental degradation observed throughout the Yanomami IT. In September 2020, new mining sites were installed near the Korekorema community, despite attempts at demobilization started months earlier, after complaints. The impacts on the social life of Yanomami are serious. The mining presence is characterized by the circulation of armed people and the spread of alcoholic beverages and illicit drugs, and generates conflicts between indigenous and prospectors, also focusing on the increase of internal conflicts. In this context, one of the conflicts led to the murder of two Yanomami Indians by prospectors in the Parima region in June 2020. The environmental consequences are also severe. In addition to the contamination of the main watercourses, mining means removal of native vegetation, accumulation of garbage and debris, and removal or reduction of animal species. According to ISA data, between January and September 2020, environmental degradation within the Yanomami IT increased by a 20%. It is also necessary to highlight the coincidence of the presence of mining with the worsening of the health situation of the indigenous population. It is notorious that the presence of invaders (including prospectors), who maintain contact with the indigenous, can be configured as the main vector for the entry and transmission of diseases among the inhabitants of the Yanomami IT. The environmental impacts and living conditions on mining cause exponential increases in malaria cases among the population. The data show that the deaths of Yanomami contaminated by the coronavirus often occurred due to comorbidity; among the Yanomami, malaria is the main comorbidity factor. It should be emphasized that the first confirmed case of Covid-19, in comorbidity with malaria, among the Yanomami, led to death a 15-year-old boy from the Helepi community, located on the banks of the Uraricoera River, an area with strong traffic and presence of prospectors. HAY and indigenous entities have been denouncing and qualifying the information about the presence of the mining within the indigenous land, forwarding it to public agencies. The MPF entered with several Public Civil Actions and, resulting from them, there are two judicial decisions within the Federal Court (November 2018 and May 2020) forcing the Union to reactivate EtnoEnvironmental Protection Bases and to immediately withdraw and combat the presence of the mining within the indigenous land. The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (ICHR) complied in 2020 with the request for precautionary measures filed by the National Council on Human Rights (CNDH).
18880bcdd12c89d10ca0106734c0e9f6076e80c7: Denunciation of the action of non-indigenous prospectors, with indigenous participation, led to an action of the Federal Police and the Army within the IT. Five were arrested involved in illegal mining, some of them calling themselves indigenous. Illegal activity takes people related to the trade of inputs for mining, transport and commerce of stones into the indigenous territory, besides causing the incentive to the consumption of alcoholic beverages, generating all kinds of internal violence and compromising the culture and the indigenous way of living. In addition, the situation has the consequences of environmental degradation, deforestation and contamination of water, which causes diseases, especially for children and the elderly.
99d25786359bec9af05cfa61573af23e7e9b2478: In the midst of the historical and frequent complaints by Yanomami of the invasion of prospectors in their territory, punctual actions were carried out and seized some equipment and aircraft used by the IT invaders. In September, an Army action seized four planes that were used in illegal mining activities on a farm that lies within Yanomami territory; in December, another operation carried out in Alto Alegre, north of Roraima, seized two small planes, one car, power generators, fuel and several items used in illegal mining activities inside Yanomami IT. The actions, punctual, are insufficient to ensure the safety of the indigenous peoples living within the IT – and that, according to recurrent complaints from the Hutukara Yanomami Association (HAY), is invaded by about 20,000 prospectors who work illegally within the indigenous land and act, during the Covid-19 pandemic, as vectors of the coronavirus into the indigenous villages.
60adf541b9a210ea1304d47e9cb19c4a47fcf764: Dário Kopenawa, indigenous leader of the Hutukara Yanomami Association (HAY), showed in video published on social networks the devastation caused by the invasion of illegal prospectors within the T.I. The image of the trail of the mining in the Herow River impresses and contradicts the federal government’s assertion that “the Brazilian Amazon remains preserved”. In addition to the numerous damage caused in the indigenous land and all kinds of violence, there is still the contagion, carried by the prospectors, of various diseases and, especially, of Covid-19. Numerous complaints about the serious situation of the invasions have been made by indigenous leaders to the government, but without measures so far.
c1ea50fd886190c732184c5a87580c765c8035c7: A fire destroyed areas of environmental preservation, plantations and pastures of the four villages of the territory, causing damage and health problems to indigenous families, mainly respiratory. According to the Inpe, about 10,000 square meters of native forest were destroyed, as well as over 400 hectares of the indigenous area. According to indigenous professor Tiago Nhandeva, it was not only material damage that they had. He reports that “goes beyond the environmental issue, for us our territory is sacred. Then, when a fire like this happens, it is reaching everything: the soil that is sacred, the area in which we seek raw material to make handicrafts, our medicinal plants. It’s very sad”. Many families survive subsistence farming and market the surplus. The fire hit the swiddens and everything that was invested in them. The cultural center of the villages was also destroyed by fire.
51cc1e0fc59af1f938f5d962ff49bd0713741542: Leaderships reported that a man entered the indigenous land, claiming that he owned a piece of that land and wanted to “resolve” this situation with the indigenous. After two weeks, leaders who protected the territory found an open and deforested area where, days later, they found the same men, who said they would occupy this area because it was theirs. The Guarani make frequent guards in the area in order to monitor attempts at invasion. A representation was made with the MPF and a civil inquiry was opened with Iguape Prefecture.
4d4405668ee33a2824552a6299b88e965e1284bd: During a visit by the Cimi team to the Indigenous Land, community leaders reported that a former occupant of the territory (non-indigenous) sold an area within the IT and, by sale, received the amount of 300,000 reais. The land purchased is ahead of the Régis Bitencourt Highway. The “supposed” new owner surrounded the area, placed a porter (with access to the highway) and hired a householder who lives nearby and does the work of watching the land and, with the help of other employees, began a work of suppression of vegetation (cleanness of the area). At no time were community leaders informed about the sale process. The families were surprised to encounter the fence and the gatekeeper. The hired caretaker passed the information on to the Indians. Indignant, the leaders launched Funai, which held a virtual meeting on August 28, 2020. During the meeting, the regional coordinator of the South-East Coast Funai, Roberto Cortez de Souza, reported that some irregularities were identified in the demarcation process of the indigenous land and that it would have to be reviewed. He also informed that a new anthropological study should be started. According to the leaders who participated in the meeting, when asked about what could be done in relation to the land within the IT, the coordinator said that he would schedule a trip to the territory and would take the opportunity to talk to the “supposed owner”, requesting his permission to allow the indigenous access, if they need to enter the area for extraction of raw material to be used in the production of crafts. The response given by the Funai coordinator generated indignation in the indigenous leaders, who requested support to forward complaint to the MPF.
b6303dc16f204627f46261e1a52d47052852a1a1: The Guarani Mbya people suffer from continuous invasions in their traditional territory, intermediated by local residents who, even knowing that it is indigenous land already delimited, continued to promote deforestation, allotment and sale of the area, actions that have been intensified over the years. Some measures of supervision and investigation by Funai and also the MPF have been referred, under monitoring also by the Cimi team.
6f3c93455c47ca233ef3f169725ddb5ddace551a: As in 2019, a criminal fire inside Xerente IT in 2020 devastated large areas of Cerrado, threatening indigenous people and causing the death of several animals.
bd6e308205534bae960bdb0bd13faa3ce401ebe6: Exploitation of waters for agribusiness irrigation; use of pesticides; damage to the environment
09aa30c1d13d083b4ed558b2123d53ecf88574ea: Several agribusiness projects near Bananal Island use irrigation of river channels to maintain their production. The construction of dams in the rivers, to channel water to the plantations, directly impacts the livelihood of indigenous peoples living in the region, due to the decrease of water and fish. The capture of the waters of the Formoso River Basin and its tributaries by agribusiness has caused devastating consequences for the environment and for the peoples of the region – indigenous, settled and riverside. Indigenous leaders denounce the impacts and environmental damage caused by agribusiness in the region of the municipalities of Formoso do Araguaia, Lagoa da Confusion and around Bananal Island. Lands are being devastated by extensive agribusiness, agriculture irrigated by canals, generating contamination of the springs within the limits of ITs, pollution of rivers, soil degradation, extinction of fish and food, among other damage. The removal of water from streams and rivers is one of the biggest concerns of local residents, because the various pumps and buses operate constantly, damaging everyone. Even facing a critical drought situation in the Formoso and Javaé rivers, on August 26, the judge Ætelvina Maria Sampaio, of the Court of Justice of Tocantins, allowed farmers to recapture waters from the Formoso River basin for irrigation of crops in the region. The deadline for water collection had ended on 15 August and since then the association that represents rural producers has been trying to extend in Justice. The release for capture has caused great violence against the people who live in this region, due to disputes for access to water and the constant drought and pollution of rivers. The judge’s decision contradicts the MPE’s decision to stop the water collection of rivers indefinitely.
ddb0cc99fa81fca51f308ad99773df9e338a6830: Leaderships denounce that some indigenous Xerente das Aldeias Lajeado, Jenipapo, Buritizinho and Traíra and non-indigenous of the cities of Guaraí and Miranorte are involved in the illegal extraction and sale of wood taken from within the indigenous territory. They report that in addition to the exploitation and sale of wood, and all damage to the environment, other indigenous peoples who do not agree with illicit practices suffer intimidation and threats from criminals. Complaints were filed with the MPF, Funai and Federal Police, but so far there have been no arrangements by these agencies. These violations have been repeated year after year and, even more serious, remained in the middle of the coronavirus pandemic. The Environmental Police and Funai conducted an operation in 2019, seizing the wood, but environmental crimes continued in 2020, even during the pandemic. The situation was denounced again to Ibama and the Federal Police.
f215a768f4efada4b8ebd6031223b3eb7f28cf18: As happened in 2019, also in 2020, the indigenous lands located on Bananal Island were punished by large fires. According to indigenous reports, many of the outbreaks originated from the action of cowboys who cleaned pastures. Since October 2019, the Federal Court has determined that Funai, ICMBio and Ibama present a work plan containing what measures would be taken to locate and qualify the records of the existence of the Avá-Canoeiro in Mata do Mamano. He determined that the work plan should include the location of the indigenous people within 12 months, and that measures should be taken to prevent the entry of the fire into the Mamão Forest. Despite the determination of Justice, the plan was not created and the Mata do Mamao suffered again with fires in September 2020, when the fire spread in an extensive area of Mata do Mamao, which encompasses the southern region of TI Inãwébohona and a part of TI Parque do Araguaia, where there is the presence of isolated indigenous people, who were sighted from the flight of a helicopter that was fighting the fire. The fire entered the Mammary Forest for about 10 days, endangering the lives of the isolated Indians. As fire protection actions were not taken as determined by the Justice, the few fire containment measures were not sufficient, and the destruction of the environment and the risk to the lives of the indigenous were incalculable. From the beginning of 2020 until September 23, the reference satellite of Inpe had recorded 1,255 outbreaks of fire in the three indigenous lands of Bananal Island.
468197430086d4b265af995916c3a5b256293692: The surrounding area is occupied by companies and large agribusiness enterprises, which, through bombs, divert water from the Javaé river to their soybean, rice and watermelon plantations. The indigenous people have suffered the consequences of this exploitation, especially in the dry months, between June and November, when the natural volume of water of the river is reduced. However, irrigation projects enhance this decrease. In addition, the use of pesticides ends up contaminating the water that is used by the indigenous, which compromises their physical and cultural survival conditions.
f2f8db25519602b5d30dff82faca0bd684f0f868: Criminal fires; illegal hunting; environmental damage
4028b4f6612b10eaa741cd33e1027a9260a93145: Leaderships reported that the indigenous land suffered several criminal fires, both in 2019 and 2020. In addition to suffering from criminal fires, the Apinajé also face the invasion of hunters in their territory. This year, during the monitoring of protection of their territory, made by the community itself, the indigenous found traces on the roads and spotted hunter camps in the Forest of Ribeirão dos Caboclos. During the night, indigenous people of the village Cocolinho approached a hunter. With it were seized a caliber hunting weapon 28, 15 ammunitions and a motorcycle with Araguatins plate (TO). A police report was recorded in the Civil Police of São Bento. In the middle of the coronavirus pandemic, in addition to all the problems faced by indigenous peoples, invasions in most indigenous territories of the country intensified.
f9689efea1a073a24edb322817f2102543483cb9: After numerous information from the Krahô people about invasions, and at the request of the leaders, a Cimi team accompanied a group of indigenous people to the south of their territory. The group was equipped with precise equipment, with GPS and cameras, until the geographical landmark of the territory. With the GPS coordinates and field investigation, associated with the indigenous testimony, it was possible to compare and verify, superimposed on the official Funai map, that there is the advance of the farmer's about 500 meters inside the IT, for agricultural activity, with presence of cattle and pasture.
48e57d8be0e883527e99b07107b8a4bd2c117cef: TI Parque do Araguaia, located on Bananal Island, continues to be used by non-indigenous people for cattle raising. The territory recorded a large number of fires in 2019 and also in 2020. Burns have again reached the Mata do Mammao region, where isolated indigenous people live, putting their survival at risk. In this IT, indigenous people are also affected by the diversion of the waters of the Javaé and Formoso rivers, dams in various dams for irrigation of agribusiness crops.
22b015d22098a22d7b6250e7e2b4d1cb3d58833d: The Avá-Canoeiro people continue to experience, in 2020, the same problems that have occurred for years, and still aggravated by the coronavirus pandemic. Since the 1970s, when Funai made forced contact with the people, the indigenous have suffered a series of violence and violations, such as the expulsion of their traditional territory known as Mata Azul. To this day they remain outside the area claimed, living in villages of the Javaé and Karajá peoples on Bananal Island. The demarcatory process of its indigenous land, already declared, is in the phase of disintrusion, for the removal of two settlements of the Incra and the Eletroenge farm. Meanwhile, indigenous leaders are threatened by the occupants of their territory.
5648ce4ffc7020ca10995f15b11e4f835eb3a866: With the process of demarcating their land paralyzed by Funai, the Krahô people of Takaywrá village live in a temporary territory, an environmental reserve of the settlement São Judas Tadeu in the municipality of Lagoa da Confusion. The people suffer from the decrease and contamination of the water of the River Formoso, taken from the river by farmers who irrigate their plantations and leave the river dry. In the dry season, from June to November, the rivers of the region suffer from drought and contamination of water, which causes the death of fish. Agribusiness has plotted rivers with dams, impacting river navigation, and the environment, where fish can no longer climb to spawn.
3c85f1a4af835b797372f5a07cab46839256e767: Several agribusiness projects near Bananal Island use irrigation of river canals to maintain their production. The construction of dams in the rivers, to channel water to the plantations, directly impacts the livelihood of indigenous peoples living in the region due to the decrease of water and fish.
b74ac6cd0a6efef6af039074dd971ee19b0906cc: Leaderships denounce the illegal action of non-indigenous married to Xerente woman, in partnership with non-indigenous of the cities of Guaraí and Miranorte involved in the illegal extraction and sale of wood. Tired of the slowness and inoperance of the MPF of Palmas, Funai, Ibama, Federal Police and the abuse of invaders, Xerente leaders organized themselves and carried out the supervision of their territory. This action enabled the flagrant and detention of a non-indigenous man removing wood, and the seizure of chainsaws and truck loaded with logs ready to be transported. The leaders called the Military Police and Funai, who made the arrests. Days later, the wood buyer posted bail on the worker, who was released.
6baab72d3b2dd2386ba4948be7bd103df1dcc4bb: With the absence of indigenous peoples in the House of Students of Araguaína (TO), due to the pandemic of the new coronavirus, and due to the lack of surveillance by public agencies, the house was depredated in its physical structure. In September 2020, a criminal fire burned down the material goods that the indigenous had left at the scene, and the structure of the house was compromised by the fire. Contact was made with Funai de Araguaína and a Police Report. The MPF of Araguaína determined that Funai will reform the House of Students, under penalty of daily fine.
8e6e1af46266890a9d4ad9cdc06e52eaa3c94485: The president of the Health Council, Ervison, was arbitrarily summoned to attend Delmiro Gouveia police station by the coordinator of Funai's CTL, Mr. Jocélio. The reason for the arbitrariness was due to the fact that the community refused to give up a building for the use and operation of Funai's headquarters. In previous years, the building was provided by the community as a support point for Funasa drivers. Ervison Araújo attended Delmiro Gouveia police station and was waiting all morning, but Funai coordinator did not attend. The leadership questioned the police clerk about the subpoena, and he replied that the matter was not of interest to that division but to Funai, and that the police station had already instructed Jocélio to settle with the community itself. So far there have been no more demonstrations, making it clear that this was a way to coerce and intimidate the leaders. Denunciation of the arbitrariness of Funai's server was made to the MPF.
55f67dea8c42c501c5a674bac149c4d968090298: The indigenous were threatened by a Funai server who did not respect the Leadership Surveillance Base. The server also threatened the indians in prison, later presenting an occurrence report against them.
ee5903f18b34570992aa16df9f26408d605ec807: The leaders of the Sateré-Mawé people were surprised by the presence of the Military Police, which entered the assembly being held without prior communication. The Indians felt threatened and coerced, which provoked revolt. At the People's Vigilance Base, the officers entered the boat without asking permission, took objects and tore writings from the Base. The leaders referred this occurrence to the advice of Cimi, because several organs are closed due to the pandemic. In the Act of the Second Extraordinary Assembly of the Sateré-Mawé Leaderships, the truculent acts of the PM appear.
e110754ba0380359f73a264886e0ef46842d679d: As reported by four indigenous Xavante who did not want to be identified, an employee of Funai has done illegally, demanding payment of bribes to issue statements from the agency necessary to obtain social benefits, such as sickness aid, maternity assistance, retirement and others of his own ethnic relatives. They said that the official, after issuing the statements, comes to accompany the Xavante to the bank to demand their illegally charged share. The indigenous fear reprisals of the server to their families and avoid making the complaint.
cdc851992c604685743c5ecd30f53620489f29fe: As the indigenous Frederico suffers from Parkinson’s disease, he accessed the INSS of Good Water in order to obtain the proper benefit. The INSS requested from him a Contribution Time Certificate - CTC, both in the municipality of Campinápolis, and in the state of Mato Grosso, due to its long working time in the area of indigenous education. On 11/01/2020, Fr. Eloir handed over to the local Funai coordinator Isaac Mi’é Ajaw However, Isaac said he would go on vacation on January 16, 2020 and would not have time to elaborate the statement that, according to him, was very complex, and that he could only write it from February 26. It was argued that he would still have four working days before going on vacation and that Frederick needed to forward the benefit. He replied that he would also need the presence of the Social Worker of Sesai to issue the statement (which has been proven not to be necessary). Isaac further added that “if Frederick had waited three years without receiving benefits, he could wait another month.” Only on 02/26/2020 the Funai coordinator delivered the statement. This consisted of only one sheet, nothing complex, with the name of Frederico, the numbers of his RG and CPF and the information that he lived in the village São Pedro, TI Parabubure. It was evident the unnecessary neglect and delay for issuing a simple statement, resulting, consequently, in the delay of the INSS to analyze and assess the case of a sick person in need of the rightful benefit.
d844c4bc5de8019b6707b318908b2c9b03d3b92d: Casualty and delay in document delivery
bbcf2c63621afdc96a071f0c74d3a60d49554188: On October 1, 2020, Mr. Denivaldo Roberto da Rocha, CTL of Funai de Ribeirão Cascalheira, telephoned Chief Damião Paridzané, inviting him to participate in an interrogation that would take place the next day, to deal with the refusal of the leaders of TI Marãiwatsédé to receive the Military Health Force scheduled for August 2020. The CTL said that in the interrogation would be present the attorney Everton Pereira Aguiar Araújo, MPF; Jussielson Gonçalves Silva, Regional Coordinator of Funai; the captain of the Army Gildo Henrique de Azeredo; the coordinator of the DSEI Xavante; and agents of the Federal Police. The chief appeared at the scheduled time, accompanied by his sons Cosme Rite and Elídio Tsõrõné Paridzané. However, there were only two agents from the Federal Police of Barra do Garças, Mr. Jailson and a woman, representing the FUNAI of Ribeirão Cascalheira. No one from MPF or Sesai showed up. The police questioned who guided the Xavante of TI Marãiwatsédé to reject the actions of the Military Health Force in early August. According to Fr Aquilino Tsere’ubu’õ Tsirui’a, Chief Damião replied that he did not accept the Military Health Force because he was suspicious of the government’s actions, distrusted the effectiveness of the drugs and was afraid of the prescription of chloroquine, proven ineffective in the fight against coronavirus, for the Xavante; that the most intense period of contamination and deaths had been the month of May and that, therefore, the aid was already late; and that he was afraid that the military health agents would bring new contamination to the indigenous. He also said that he was aware that no vaccine had yet been discovered; that this vaccine was being investigated and tested in Russia, China and other countries. He said he did not agree with the words written by the MPF prosecutor, Everton Pereira Aguiar Araújo, blaming him and the other chiefs of Marãiwatsédé for future cases of contamination or death that occurred after the refusal (Depacho or Manifestação do MPF de Barra do Garças no 1119/2020/GABPRM1-EPAA, pp. 1011, no 30, letter “b”, no 2, 03/08/2020). The chief reminded the federal police that the Military Health Force had worked in the ITs São Marcos and Parabububure and that, weeks later, new contaminations and even deaths occurred; while in Marãiwatsédé, due to internal organization and isolation, there were no new cases or deaths. The chief wondered why, then, only they should be held accountable? Chief Damian still questioned the feds about who sent them to do that interrogation. Federal agents said it had been Funai's current president, Marcelo Augusto Xavier da Silva.
fa54437760a13f941d23f27902100aa0cb934417: A group of Myky Indians were conducting ritual hunting, within their demarcated and approved territory, near Megacena farm, when they noticed a military police truck leaving the farm. The PM car followed the motorcycle on which two Myky were, who went to meet another companion who was in the Indian association car. The truck approached and demanded that they get off the bike and drop their rifle. The military police said they'd take them to town because they got a report. Without further explanation, the Mykys were taken to the station. One of the indigenous youths went to the village to warn the leaders about what happened and soon they came to the police station to investigate the situation. The deputy demanded bail, but the Mykys stood firm and were finally released. The chief and the leaders prepared a document denouncing the arbitrary act of the police and filed it in the MPF, Funai, Ibama and in the cabinet of Mrs. Rosa Neide.
ab1c9d9b6d8fffa413d47a1143d7dee499b51c3e: According to a complaint from the community, while some indigenous people raised the sanitary barrier at the entrance of the community, a vehicle from the Department of Border Operations (FOD) passed through the site and approached a teenager, only 14 years old, who was sitting next to the highway's burro forest. The police asked where he was from and, upon confirming that he was from the village, they called him closer and began to say that “they did not like Indian”, that Indian was “killer of policemen”. At the same moment, they beat him in the face, and told him to keep his head down; at that moment, one of the officers threatened him, putting a gun to his head. The leaders referred a complaint to the MPF and await action.
43578ed62fff70f4b6aadb5774f872a4ffcaf249: Leadership denounces that, in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, an action of the Military Police, which invaded the territory, making incidences in the villages, put at risk the collective health of about 12,000 indigenous people, especially of elders and elders. Using two winches and several vehicles, the Military Police traveled all the villages, making pressure and having direct contact with the people. The entry of the Military Police caused terror in the familiesPhoto: people Xakriabá the Xakriabá, in Minas Gerais, the PM carried out an ão at risk during the pandemic lia, not only for the action they carried out, without any communication or consultation with the leaders of the people, but also for the danger of contagion by the coronavirus, which could enter the villages with the police coming from various cities of the region. The action carried out by the Military Police in the territory Xakriabá runs counter to Ordinance No. 419 of March 17, 2020, issued by Funai, which suspended the authorizations to enter indigenous lands due to the pandemic. Without any personal protective equipment that would minimize the possibilities of viral infection, the Military Police entered the territory and conducted approaches in indigenous people. According to Chief Santos, the police “used weapons but no equipment not to infect us. We are afraid of what they may have brought.” The leaders issued a complaint document that was forwarded to the MPF, the government of the state of Minas Gerais, the Secretariat of Public Security of Minas Gerais, Funai and human rights agencies.
a9d714c6ba2f2b6a3ac2a192acde65b67c03542c: The MPF judged with the Federal Desembargador of the TRF of the 1st Region an instrument aggravation appeal because of a decision taken by a judge in favor of the Union, to reintegrate possession of the BR-163 road, occupied by protesters of the Kayapó people. The action brought by the Union was against Chief Doto Taca Yre, as well as against the other members of the people and others who met in the kilometer 302 of the highway, claiming rights in the area of health and measures against invaders, as well as measures to preserve the forest and the territory. In the instrument problem, the MPF registered that, on the one hand, there is the Union seeking the clearance of a federal public road, temporarily occupied by indigenous protesters, and on the other, the indigenous people Kayapó claiming conditions worthy of subsistence and protection by the government, before the extreme socio-environmental damage suffered recurrently. The MPF cited that there was police repression against the indigenous who claimed the effective protection of the right to the territory, the environment and health, and that there was no margin for any guarantee of weighting among those involved. The community awaits decision.
a45be953c2663123dd975024955470044df07014: According to leadership information, Chief Crídio Medina was arrested by the local Civil Police and taken to the police station to give a statement about an alleged corn theft. The police accused him of covering up the “crime” committed by the children of the village. After the corn harvest, on a property adjacent to tekoha, the children collected the remaining ears on the ground, not accessed by the harvester. According to the indigenous, the corn ears that the harvester does not reach, close to the ground, are usually not collected by the owners, because it is not worth the cost of the work. Without land to plant and without conditions to leave the village to work on behalf of the pandemic, the children decided to pick up some ears to prepare avati ku’i (fare) and to make the kangui and rora, typical Guarani drink, produced with mature corn. The owner of the property, on realizing the action, triggered the police, who found ten sacks with corn ears inside the community. With that, he took the chief to testify and the deputy decreed his arrest. Two days after his arrest, the chief was released.
038e17ef03b4d1a54e6b7fa47b8ad01f536cb8cd: A PRF vehicle entered IT and purposely dropped a motorcycle carrying two indigenous people. Faced with the aggressive act of the police, the indigenous people retained the vehicle for a few hours, seeking some clarification for the violent action. In reaction, PRF set up an operation defined as “Strength Demonstration”. Dozens of cars and two helicopters have entered IT, terrorizing the Kaingang and tearing the houses apart.
9cd74d860f045fc317802276a2f990c4e323657d: Leaderships denounced that two military police who were traveling along the highway approached the children Mbyá Guarani who were walking on the roadside, in front of the village. One of the officers drew the gun and ran after the children, who went to meet the mother who, at that moment, washed clothes in the creek. The children and the mother were very frightened, because they had never seen such an attitude on the part of those who were to ensure the protection and safety of children. This aggression was denounced to the Citizenship and Human Rights Commission, MPF and Funai for the appropriate measures.
c1cf32645e5b15089d137b25b69d41678e32fbf9: The state deputy Jeferson Alves, PTB-RR, cut with a pliers and a chainsaw the current that controlled the access to the highway BR-174, which cuts the IT Waimiri-Atroari, located between Amazonas and Roraima. The current was installed by the Army, with the aim of protecting the indigenous and wildlife in the area. When this BR was built, the Waimiri-Atroari people were almost decimated and the issue of access is still under discussion in judicial proceedings. The deputy's attack was filmed and released by himself on social media, saying that the highway will never be closed again, exalting his attitude, in a message of support to the President of the Republic. Actions of disrespect to indigenous rights, such as this, have been taking place frequently since the election of Bolsonaro; criminals feel encouraged and protected in the execution of their crimes. Immediate provision was taken by the MPF, which considered unacceptable the arbitrariness of the Member. An injunction of the MPF determined to the Union and Funai the relocation of traffic control currents, and that a policing team be deployed on site, to prevent the practice of new attacks against the indigenous.
2ddd7b749a485b32dedd17aa5e6b3dfb42b6b8f7: On July 25, a group of tourists, in the middle of the pandemic and without the proper licensing of environmental agencies, invaded the territories of the region of the pineapple and Marimari rivers, in the municipalities of Nova Olinda do Norte and Borba (AM), to conduct sports fishing. The action, carried out without consulting or informing the indigenous and riverside communities of the region, triggered a serious conflict. The then executive secretary of the Amazon Social Promotion Fund, Saulo Moysés Rezende Costa, who was part of the group, claimed to have been shot in the shoulder and threatened to return in retaliation. On August 3, indigenous leaders of the Maraguá people denounced that a group of people – who were then known to be undercover military police – on board a speedboat identified by them as “Dona Dora”, were firing shots at residents. The situation unfolded in the murder of two indigenous people of the Munduruku people, residents of the nearby Coatá-Laranjal IT and four riverside people in the region, in the disappearance of two other riverside towns and in a series of human rights violations committed by the PM against local communities, in the case that became known as the “massacre of the pineapple river”. Before that, the Maraguá had already registered several complaints in the MPF against the losses caused by sports fishing in the region of the pineapple river. In August 2018, the MPF promoted a public hearing in the village Terra Preta with the presence of indigenous and settled Incra, who live on the opposite bank of the river. According to leaders of the people, some entrepreneurs and owners of tourism speedboats do not respect the limits of indigenous territory.
8ab7e1a259137b236765c48b6efad12627950528: The indigenous Antonio José de Souza reported verbal aggression and threats suffered in his own village. The aggressor was Councilman Francisco Sales de France, known as “Maprá”. Antonio reports that he was insulted by the councilman, who carried a firearm and threatened him, expelling him from the area, saying that that land was his, showing a document issued by the Union Heritage Secretariat (SPU). It was registered virtual occurrence report at the local police station, and forwarded complaint to Funai and the Amazon MPF. So far, there has been no provision.
99c7632092aebbee15e7d7ba87d7b169aef57eec: For more than 20 years, the Apurinã have been struggling for the demarcation of the Curriã IT area, but so far it is without administrative provisions and is not even registered in Funai databases in Brasilia. According to the chief, invaders entered the indigenous territory through Igarapé Joari, then began to invade the main lake of the village by Igarapé Curriã, which gives entrance to the village Bom Jesus and the village Curriã, challenging the indigenous. The community instructed them to leave with all their equipment and not return. The other day, when returning from an activity in another riverside community, the invaders passed in front of the chief of the community Bom Jesus, drunk, threatening him with death.
fe0f15b27947dae701c757eeff66d0544b8b9782: The Kokama People's Organization of the Javari River – OGIPKORIJA (ex Orinpokovaja) denounced that, on May 28, the indigenous Kokama Daniel Tello Murajari, 25 years old, his four-year-old son and his 16-year-old nephew were threatened with verbal death and a shotgun shot that passed one meter and a half away. The aggressor would be a squatter with the nickname “Miguelzinho”. On June 5, the organization made an occurrence report. The family, which is constantly threatening the residents of São Pedro do Norte, took a bite that divided the gardens (made by the Kokama) that are used to feed the people of this village and is also their main source of income.
464b946694a1fe6b661fc08b3dbeb6272315b317: Cacique Juvenal Tupinambá reports that a landowner, accompanied by 15 heavily armed jagunços, entered the village, claiming to be the owner of the land and stating that they were to leave, because there “he had already killed four others”. The intimidation action was recorded on video, which was forwarded to the Eunápolis MPF, where the complaint was made. The chief also reported that, before leaving the village, the Jaguns fired several shots up in a clear attempt to intimidate them.
7ef83604092a29c5af5b933eee0139c4175607b7: Indigenous leaders report that unknown bikers continue to enter their areas of resumption, especially in the village Cajueiro-Piraí, by highway MA-014, firing shots towards the indigenous and their homes, intimidating and threatening families. Such situations have been denounced several times to the public agencies of the State, but no provision has been made.
35e8c7f0ae9e2ebdffbbab6c9a73912ccc8c68f0: Indigenous people of the Ypoi community reported threats to two leaders who were at the edge of the indigenous land. In January, farmers of the region entered with trucks inside the village and, as they approached, the leaders (not identified by security) were threatened with death by the invaders. The history of murders in the region concerned the leaders who, due to the pandemic period, did not make formal complaint, but informed the chief and warned the community.
ba24b48b9ab9c922bd004a5b9590d3160daa29d3: Leadership reports that unidentified men attacked the indigenous by gunfire and invaded some houses that were emptied by the escape of their residents, who were afraid of the violence and insecurity that prevailed in the region. They also reported that the men walked among the shacks and shouted racist insults while shooting and told the indigenous to leave the place or “that everyone will die”. The previous morning, a House of Reza had been set on fire and partially destroyed by the flames. Several complaints were made to the MPF, the Federal Police and Funai, but the situation in the region remains tense and violent, due to the non-regulation of land.
250da7a4019f4af443256abdeadcf11273583a07: Since the beginning of the year 2020, when there was a serious attack on communities, the more than 180 families Guarani-Kaiowá of resumes Nhu Vera, Nhu Vera Guasu, Aratikuty and Boquerón have been suffering continuous threats. Indigenous people are targeted by attacks and threats from private security, property incidents on indigenous territory and the Border Operations Department (FOD). The Kaiowá and Guarani report that the threats have occurred throughout the year, and that several leaders have already suffered death threats. The situation in the region is daily tense, and families fear that violence worsens even more. Complaints have already been sent to the MPF and the indigenous await measures of the authorities.
ce77ed648ded3bc5ed25452d34e1d05fb8c63c51: According to the community, for the seventh time in the year, armed men who make security of the area claimed as indigenous land, in the region bordering the Golden Reserve, in the region of Nhu Verá, attacked the community violently during the early hours, tearing down the shacks and setting fire to the belongings of the indigenous. In this attack and in the previous six, several indigenous people reported that they were threatened with death by the armed security team. A complaint was forwarded to the MPF, but so far there have been no arrangements.
13a2e3b8118cbcc08435a9cd7aa9dff5ef6c69f4: Indigenous people of the Pyelito Kue community report threats from armed security guards of property incidents on indigenous territory. These security guards reached the entrance of the territory and said that if the indigenous did not leave the land, the main leaders would die. This occurred in mid-May. Indigenous families are afraid that more violence will occur in the region, and they are waiting for measures from the competent authorities.
c425b4bbf59727ebc1f39c624b09f3fcfefa0a5b: A 60-year-old indigenous woman reported to the police that she was threatened with death and aggression. According to her, her neighbor and her husband would have said they would “shoot her, set fire and throw her in the bog.” According to the report, the two already had a previous disagreement because of land dispute in the village. The indigenous woman also reported that her neighbor's husband had a stick in her hands when both threatened her. The police are investigating the case.
fa2fda838c90782a5fa37cabe48c5a8583550cbe: According to leaders, not identified for security reasons, the community has been constantly threatened by private security that points to weapons and threatens death threats to indigenous people. In all, there were more than 10 death threats throughout the year. This situation, further aggravated by the context of the pandemic experienced, leads the indigenous people to a situation of insecurity and despair, generating a cycle of other violence at various levels.
219858a9f4c421b1a89c09ca530a7957aecc7c58: Leaderships denounce that a tenant of lands near this tekoha has an interest in the possession of the indigenous territory, and that made threats to chief Leocinio, through another indigenous. The tenant sent a message, saying that he would “let him eat some more, so he would kill the chief”.
4194a3a0e84733d3a5d66866a418e5c5c8120aff: Leaders denounced death threats to the Pankararu Indians to the Federal Police and MPF. They report that the invaders released a list of the names of the Indians who would “die soon.” Several leaders Pankararu Brejo dos Padres has suffered threats from squatters due to the process of territorial disintrusion, which has caused in recent years a continuous wave of instability and fear in the community, which already has several leaders included in the Program for Protection of Human Rights Defenders and Defenders of the State of Pernambuco (PEPDDH). The attacks and intimidation actions are constant, reports an indigenous unidentified for security reasons: “We wake up and find our crops destroyed, the fruit and sacred trees on the ground. They leave tickets scaring us. We’ve had homes shot at in our villages.”
9a1141c49b2e67958a248f85d2726d3dfdd75ee1: The Pankararu people Opará is in an area resumed in the municipality of Jatobá for five years, fighting for recognition of the area as traditional territory. With this, families have faced conflicts with the local squatters. The Jaguriça pajé (Washington Tenório) and the Valdenúzia Tavares, community leaders, were threatened with death by the squatters who announced that they would hire gunmen from the region to do the job.
