The indigenous people reported to the MPF of Serra Talhada and are included in the Programa de Proteção às Defendores e Defensoras de Direitos Humanos de Pernambuco (PEPDDH).
f34ec1a7c530bb4aa5e44e9d09b52c842890dbd2: The invaders of the Karipuna IT have constantly threatened the indigenous community; they threaten to kill their leaders and set their homes on fire. The community receives these threats through messages from former residents of Resex Jaci Paraná, who also feel threatened by invaders. Leaderships filed complaints and requests for actions in the MPF.
4fb5cd21cec181641e188d0e74a141f291c03f7a: A group of about 25 indigenous families of the Pankariri ethnic group, which just over a year ago resumed land near the village Kariri Xocó, in the São Bento farm, owned by the farmer known as Mario Barreto, was surprised by this, questioning why they were present at the site. The squatter, accompanied by two private security guards, one of whom carrying a gun on his waist, hidden under his shirt, said that the indigenous should not remain on the land, since the judge had determined the reintegration of possession against them, and that he would be with the document. Chief José Raimundo and other members said that they had no knowledge of this document and that they would wait for notification by justice. The Indians sought Funai, who replied that he was unaware of the reintegration of possession. Funai and the MPF were reported, but there were no arrangements.
140caf977a9ee60fccb24908a2bca3b81b8d7907: In February 2020, many indigenous people left their cards with some traders in the municipality of Lábrea (one of these merchants would be Mr. Gugu Teixeira) and the riverside community Foz do Tapauá (trader known as André), but with the arrival of the new coronavirus in the Middle River Purus region, the Madihadeni did not return in these places to follow the process of payment of debts and to seek their cards. The traders benefited from the situation to continue withdrawing the wages and social benefits of the indigenous – even after the debts were paid – and made loans in the bank using the cards of the indigenous. As an example, there are two cases where a trader, in possession of the card of a disabled child of the village Marrecão, made a bank debt in the name of the child, causing the cancellation of its benefit; the same trader was in possession of the card of the Indigenous Health Agent (AI) of Polo Base Marrecão, since February. With a debt of approximately R $ 2,700.00 and being the monthly salary of AIS of approximately R $ 1,500.00, the debt would be settled since the month of May. However, the AIS believes that the merchant continued to withdraw his salary, since the card remained in his possession. Due to such cases, there was a great risk of indigenous people moving to the municipality of Lábrea and Foz de Tapauá in search of their cards in possession of traders, and possibly being infected by the new coronavirus. Funai CR Middle River Purus took action to collect cards that were in the possession of the merchant Gugu Teixeira and other merchants. The Cimi presented a demonstration to the MPF requesting that the necessary measures be taken to return the indigenous cards. The retention of cards is a practice that is known to the MPF, and there are already civil investigations on this practice.
a0bd3f1b74c74aeaa288d16d538de1425f9dce0b: With the pandemic of the coronavirus and the absence of the government, the indigenous people organized themselves and made sanitary barriers in order to avoid the contagion of the community. There were conflicts involving farmers who tried to break down the barriers. In addition to the invasion of the territory of the Mura people, a group of farmers tried to interfere in the internal organization of the indigenous, creating a supposed “directory” to try to replace the Tuxaua, under threats. The government, which should act to protect the barriers and the indigenous against the invasions, did nothing, and the people were forced to remove the barriers. Leaderships filed complaints with the MPF and registered Occurrence Report in the Autazes Police Station. Because of the threats, Francis had to be included in the human rights protection program.
6d63dedf05272f61488b12558caf2cc8bce902ff: The Military Police carried out an operation in the region of the Abacaxis and Marimari rivers, where the TIs Maraguá and Coatá-Laranjal are located, in the municipalities of Borba and Nova Olinda do Norte (AM), which involved about 50 police officers and resulted in the death of two indigenous people of the Munduruku people and four riversides, in addition to the disappearance of two other riversides, in the case that became known as the “massacre of the Abacaxis River”. During the operation, which lasted several days, indigenous people of the Maraguá people, communities of the region and riverside populations reported to the MPF, stating that the PM practiced several abuses. Among the complaints, according to local reports, the use of firearms to intimidate residents, children and the elderly; torture practices, aggressions and threats. Indigenous and riverside were prevented from leaving their communities and villages, forbidden to fish and enter the forest to access their gardens, which generated hunger and thirst. The Tuxaua Joarez da Silva Reis, of the Maraguá people, reports the aggression and truculent action of the PM made to him and his family. In this same episode, military police raided the village Pilão, in TI Maraguá, threatening the people who were there, turning houses and the historical church and stealing material goods. Work equipment and personal effects of health counselor Messiah Miranda, also Maraguá, were thrown into the street, being largely deteriorated. Federal police are investigating the case.
2f18296a023650e938fb1d285703e42d8cc1dbe5: Since the beginning of the pandemic, the Sateré-Mawé people have not received humanitarian aid from municipal authorities. Furthermore, leaders were still the target of persecution by politicians, who wanted to end the sanitary barrier, organized by the leaders themselves, in order to prevent the advance of the coronavirus in the villages. The situation experienced by the Sateré-Mawé was denounced to the MPF in the state of Amazonas.
b0b0b79846dca505a693999bbd318b02fc6f72ad: The Sonia Guajajara leadership and APIB filed a criminal complaint for defamation in the Supreme Court against the chief minister of the Institutional Security Office (GSI), retired general Augusto Heleno. In September, in publications on the social network Twitter, Minister Heleno associated Sonia and APIB with the alleged “crime of lesa-patria”. He accused APIB of “being behind the site defundbolsonaro. org, whose objectives are to publish fake news against Brazil: to impute environmental crimes to the president of the Republic; and to support international boycott campaigns to brazilian products”. Heleno also said that “Emergency APIB is chaired by the indigenous Sônia Guajajara, a PSOL activist and linked to actor Leonardo Di Caprio, a fierce critic of our country.” Heleno wrote that “the Apib website is associated with several others, who work 24 hours a day to stain our image abroad, in a crime of lewd country.” In the complaint-crime filed in the STF, Sonia and APIB stated that they were surprised, on September 18, “by the posts of the dispute that, using its social network, attributed to the plaintiffs acts of extreme gravity”. The STF's response is expected around the opening of the process. In a note, the APIB also repudiated the military statements and stated that “who harms our homeland is the omission of the Bolsonaro government in the face of the destruction of our biomes, protected areas, illegal fires, greasing, deforestation and invasion of our lands and the theft of our wealth”.
f64da73a5b64854ec4e624ebd846655812c4d5fb: About 30 indigenous Warao, aged between 05 and 57 years, who are living in Goiânia, moved to the cities of Catalan, Rio Verde, Itumbiara and Caldas Novas. Upon arriving in these locations, they were expelled and threatened by the Military Police and by people who identified themselves as employees of the social assistance departments of these municipalities. According to information from the Ministry of Migrants, the indigenous were forced to return to Goiânia without any explanation. The case was reported to the MPF of Goiás and provisions are being awaited.
72d02c9d5d7f9a44d8cc459fbb1493782cc5f190: Abuse of authority, threats, expulsion from cities
15a79e9b88e50d4ff5af1a0ebb2511eba0078ac1: The leaders of the Memortumré Canela and Apãnjekra Canela people denounce that traders have retained the cards and passwords of retired and employees. The case is known by Funai's Local Technical Coordination (CTL) in Barra do Corda, but no action was taken.
ef5112764d8d45ee859228d9e12045e37117711a: Leaderships of the Pyhcop people Cati Ji / Hawkeye denounce that traders have retained the cards and passwords of retired and employees. The case is known by Funai's Local Technical Coordination (CTL) in Amarante do Maranhão, but no provision has been made so far.
820caa3fd0f1bdc031baee4d50139ead149a2df5: The indigenous leaders denounce that non-indigenous people are marrying indigenous people, in order to have access to the territory and create conflicts. The leaders claim that they do not want this situation to happen and that they have talked to Funai's Local Technical Coordination (CTL) to help solve the problem.
5d94e413bf2427915de279571330b94ceda5cef1: The indigenous people of Pyhcop Cati Ji/Gavião report that the loggers continue to threaten the indigenous leaders who protect the territory. The leaders denounce that the entry of invaders to illegally remove wood from the territory has been frequent. Even under threats, indigenous leaders themselves maintain surveillance of the territory. The MPF, Funai and other bodies responsible for the surveillance and protection of the territory are always activated by the indigenous peoples, who are waiting for measures.
1ab1b98a3d11db574089c0e38f0fe6f6d66e79f5: The Tremembé people of Engenho denounced that a non-indigenous man lives within the territory threatening the people, destroying and invading swiddens, selling possessions of the territory and taking non-indigenous people into the area Tremembé, endangering the entire community, especially in this year of Covid-19 pandemic. This man declared himself the general chief of the people, without the knowledge of the members of the community.
13085c984290706780cfbea674a685fe75caded2: The Tremembé People's Council of Engenho was created as a legitimate decision-making space for the lives of the people. Non-indigenous who explored the territory were asked to leave the area; after that, they threatened the members of the board of leaders of the Tremembé people.
51b99ff6b2352613408ff8e8c6e04e67e8b8227d: An indigenous from the village of São Domingos Sávio, who asked not to be identified, in a visit of Fr. Eloir Inacio de Oliveira to the House of Indigenous Health (Casai), reported that he had left his Bolsa Família card and the respective password with a lady from a food market in the city. He was sick in Casai, being treated for a severe flu. This is an account not only of this man, but of many indigenous people, who are forced to act in this way to have the right to make their small purchases with social benefit cards, including retirement.
a431d979bf713bb112d6556425da497400b3c0e0: Since 2019 and also in 2020, bank agencies and financial institutions have made loans, beyond the limits permitted by law, for many retired Xavante, causing the drastic decrease of their receipts and compromising the survival of their families. Complaints and complaints were made with the banking and financial agencies, but illegal practice remains.
1003d13ecde9b6e6ff9716f1aa8fddb388029e4a: Leadership reports that a candidate for councilman by the PSL was present in the village - in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, despite the Funai ordinance that prevents the entrances - to make political campaign. The community was worried and frightened by the risks of contamination. Funai has been activated and has awarded the candidate.
fb57096d7605e20baa9d9bb44c60a5f520abd095: Enter the village in the middle of the pandemic
e152be2fffdc1d2e779bec996976a05b5439de8b: Indigenous Guarani and Kaiowá were found working on a farm in the south of Mato Grosso do Sul, in the harvest of cassava, in a situation similar to that of slave labor. A labor inspection by the Department of Labor and Employment rescued 24 indigenous people. The employer did not register the workers, did not provide Personal Protection Equipment, nor even masks, in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic. Among the workers, there were also teenagers. They slept in bed quarters and dirty mattresses, on the floor or in nets. Besides the inhuman conditions, the owner of the farm still discounted the indigenous food, housing and work tools. The supervision defined working conditions as “degrading”. The process is ongoing and the Goldens MPF has opened investigation to investigate the farm. According to Antonio Maria Parron, the labor inspector who coordinated the rescue action, eight other indigenous were on site: two women who accompanied their husbands and six children. The situation was defined by him as “deplorable”.
6d0af3053a587a901f4669ecfbba9449a629eefe: Complaint that non-indigenous residents of Aquidauana and Miranda are using WhatsApp groups to share hate messages and threats against the Terena. In the audios released, there are even proposals to exterminate the indigenous: “Let’s gather everyone together. We will invade the village and kill everyone there. There. Good that already exterminates this useless breed of c*** ", says one of the audios. “You have to close the city and not let them come to the city” and “Since in the village there are people with Covid, they had to stay inside” are other examples of hate demonstrations.
7a553dee0b756d467010cde5b6ed8393009e0d59: In a truculent action, the National Force arrived in the recovery Guarani-Kaiowá pointing weapons to indigenous people. It was 10:00 a.m., when four cars arrived at Tekohá, located in the border area of Golden TI. Retaken by the indigenous peoples, the area is being disputed judicially and, according to local leaders, the owner incited the police action – as she intended a forced and illegal eviction. The police made threats, regardless of the presence of elderly, pregnant women and children at the scene. Very frightened, the indigenous sent a letter of their own to the MPF, asking for security. The document was also presented in an emergency meeting held on 28/08/2020 by Aty Guasu, Great Guarani Kaiowá Assembly. The organization decided to monitor the situation closely, as the conflict involves a family of great political and economic power in the region, placing the indigenous in a situation of greater vulnerability.
83426cc716f47fcade3a36a4aee4ec44275a7e20: Leadership reports that non-indigenous people used social networks and WhatsApp groups to promote attacks on indigenous identity Xakriabá and its internal organization, as well as making false accusations and incitement to violence against communities. Bulletin of Occurrence in the Civil Police was registered and complaints were made to the competent bodies for investigation and investigation of the case, such as Funai, MPF and Human Rights Commission of the Legislative Assembly of Minas Gerais.
d86bf882ff2eb81d232edce71d0fcab82c425722: Celia denounced that, during the period of election campaigns, she received several threats via virtual networks about her political position and actions outside the indigenous territory. According to her, the attacks were slanderous, aggressive, saying that she was not fighting for the rights of her people, but stealing the people. Reported to the MPF and the Human Rights Commission.
c6b61f6bb3b7b41aeaf5c7f52fc830068adfc0b0: The indigenous Ipó received as “donation” of Luiz Carlos Ferreira a long firearm, of the type rifle, generating riots and risks to the community. Upon gaining knowledge, the MPF moved a Criminal Action against Luiz Carlos attributing to him two criminal conducts: a) give free of charge to the indigenous of the name Ipó, belonging to the ethnic Zo’é, the long firearm of the rifle type, which would configure crime; b) disturb the customs and traditions of the Zo’é people, since, in addition to being not common the use of firearms for the practice of hunting, the presence of the artifact would have aroused the interest of the other members of the community, also configuring crime. The Federal Court accepted the action of the MPF and condemned the defendant to provide cash of 20 minimum wages in favor of institution to be defined and provide services to the community.
90bb276e1c1b7225b407914cd58bdee9994df6a7: After denunciations of indigenous leaders and organizations and Funai, the MPF entered a Public Civil Action on three people (Miguel dos Santos Corrêa, Raimundo Ferreira de Sousa and Josael da Penha Luna) who, through the Indigenous Association of the State of Pará (Aiepa), produced “Declarations of Belonging” to indigenous peoples, ideologically false, in order to enable their participation in the Special Indigenous Selection Process of the Federal University of the West of Pará (PSEI/UFOPA), which is an affirmative action aimed exclusively at indigenous candidates. In addition to individual accountability and the dismantling of illegalities, this Public Civil Action seeks to safeguard the policy of affirmative actions of the UFOPA, which is fundamental for the mitigation of inequalities and to remedy the historical exclusion of indigenous peoples from higher education, seeking to preserve the purpose and the target public of affirmative actions.
4074984d603c0fa6c6a5684692b014a4bd0f56ca: The Warao Indians, from Venezuela, when they are in Belém, are generally welcomed in the Tapanã Institutional Reception Space of the Pope John XXIII Foundation. During the stay of the indigenous Fermin Moraleda and Avilio Alvarez, there was a conflict between them and the technical staff of the shelter. Because of this conflict, the indigenous peoples were disconnected from the shelter. The MPF and the Public Defender of the Union (DPU), in the face of the case, issued a recommendation to the Papa João XXIII Foundation, since, according to the MPF, the disengagement of the indigenous peoples occurred in a summary and unilateral way by the shelter team, without any possibility of prior or contradictory defense, and without the transparent communication appropriate to the control bodies that accompany the welcoming policy, such as the DPU, the MPF and civil society organizations. The MPF also stressed that only the two indigenous peoples suffered shutdown, and several others were involved in the conflict. In the recommendation, the MPF and the DPU suggested, among others, the immediate realization of prior consultation, free and informed to the indigenous people; that the broad and contradictory defense be guaranteed, in case of disciplinary measures; that technical analysis be made of the consequences of the disconnection of the host, on the situation of vulnerability experienced by the respective family group (which will also live in the streets, along with the family disconnected, due to the concept of family experienced by the Warao).
1242802d5ddcb3cbd5c73349737f71314bf1998d: Leadership reports that there was a car parked at night, in suspicious attitude, at the entrance of the village; they report that people got out of the car, carrying lanterns and entered the village. Some families got scared, left their homes and went to a house near the Indian school, where they spent the night. Military police have been engaged and have been in the village. Around three o’clock in the morning, the Indians spotted the same car, parked at the entrance of the village. The leaders believe that the fact would be related to the murder of the young Virgínio Benites, which occurred on the 8/03, since the criminals have not yet been arrested. The police are investigating the case.
93805de55dcd2ff12aef30235af7076a421a0c71: Leadership reports that around 23 hours heard gunshots and that then a non-indigenous man entered the tekoha on a motorcycle, screaming, calling by the chief. The man was making alleged accusations against a tekoha resident that he would have been disrespectful to his wife and daughter, and wanted him to turn him in. He threatened that if this were not done, he would set fire to the indigenous houses. The invasion and threats to the MPF of Guaíra were reported.
5c041c8f36af3e2a7e466f763f6bd8b6e4d50d8c: During the program “Tribuna da Massa”, TV Naipi, affiliated with the station SBT, which belongs to the family of the governor of Paraná Ratinho Júnior, the host Luciano Alves acted with discrimination and made threats to the Kaingang people. He gave a speech of discrimination, threats and incitement to violence, endangering more than 800 indigenous families living in New Orange trees. During the show, the host said: “Now there will be more: the police can drop bullet. Now it's rubber bullet, it's bomb, it's gas on top of these Indians. And be punished. You know the rules, you don't walk around naked with your face painted, you don't have those drops of dish. So you guys pay attention. You're going to jail. Gang! The host accused the Kaingang, without proof, of putting oil on the BR-277 track, to cause accidents and plunder drivers, and defended urgent intervention by the authorities. IT residents are suffering discrimination and threats to the death, since four youths in the community were arrested, accused of looting the cargo of a truck. According to Neoli Kafy Olíbio, who was once chief, the climate among indigenous families is of apprehension, because “the press has released what happened so that the community is now afraid to go out on the streets”. According to Neoli, the Kaingang people are the target of attacks on social networks, cursing and intimidation.
7daf2711d719fec3c9a75611086d165c0fe76232: Military officer José Batista dos Santos, captain of the 6th Company of Paraná State Highway Police, defended in an information exchange group between journalists and police officers that agents of the Military Police, Federal Police, Federal Highway Police and Army should beat indigenous people until “leave the loin softer than the belly”. The message was sent after conflicts between indigenous peoples of the Rio das Cobras IT, New Laranjeiras, and Federal Highway Police were registered and received support from a civilian police officer from Pato Branco, Juliano Riboli: “Feel the PRF finger”. Since November 11, a series of conflicts was registered in BR-277, which borders the Rio das Cobras IT, after the arrest of four Kaingang indigenous people accused of involvement in the looting of a truck trunk loaded with tires. In WhatsApp's conversation are made several hateful, prejudiced and racist comments against the indigenous. The Kaingang and Guarani were apprehensive because the non-indigenous population was incited to further hatred and violence against them. They report that the police continue to enter the indigenous territory, with several vehicles, intimidating the families, and there are vehicles in the clover of the two highways, of readiness.
12e08ebf2d86fca277dfabd6df2b14cb166f67fb: After several complaints, PF served two search and seizure warrants in rural establishments in the city of Espigão Alto do Iguaçu. The purpose of the action was to determine whether local traders would be retaining documents and bank cards of indigenous peoples as a guarantee of payment of products sold for later payment (“fiado”). Third party cards and documents were found at the locations.
6518dbdf74a2de702c3b3da959c98169e7192bd3: On the night of 26/11, three 20, 45, and 81-year-old Indians were targeted by bandits for about 12 hours. The youngest among the victims, Bitate Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, reported to the police that night the three were leaving the municipality of Monte Negro for the village, when they were surprised by two hooded and armed suspects on a motorcycle. The bandits surrendered the Indians and had Bitate drive to the bridge of the river Canaan, meaning Cacauland. The victims remained under threat until 4 a.m. the next day, when the criminals fled with the vehicle, a drone, a wagon and a gardener. The case is being cleared at the Ariquemes Heritage Office and the leaders sent a document to the MPF.
f038e00d232dda9b0d6f055402e2566fdadab5ef: Leaderships report receiving intimidating audio from Funai coordinator in Guajará-Mirim. In the message, the coordinator said that, because they were disrespecting the quarantine, “as soon as they pulled over at the port, they would be arrested by the Federal Police”. The leaders expressed their indignation, saying that his role as Funai coordinator should be to guide the indigenous about the severity of the pandemic of the new coronavirus and its consequences. Instead, he used threats and intimidation to the indigenous people of the Guajará-Mirim region.
96dc99916678daf379b17de6272e347c9f4253e1: Complaint that a Xokleng group living in a neighborhood on the banks of the expressway in Blumenau was threatened by eviction by the city. According to the city, there would be a meeting point for drug users and therefore wanted to demolish the house where the Xokleng were living. The neighbors, on the contrary, claim that the presence of the Xokleng in that place has driven away drug users and that they are favorable to the permanence of the indigenous.
c5aba1cc52cc8238d22f32810b5e773a674796b5: The conditions imposed by the merchants of Tocantinia so that the indigenous could buy in time were always that the cards would be held by the merchants and, as the benefits were deposited, the values would be debited from the accounts. In addition to the cards, traders demanded passwords and personal documents from the indigenous. Many indigenous people report that the card owners never made the withdrawals monthly, but the traders always did. The retention of bank cards and benefits has always been the subject of many complaints, for years at a time, of indigenous people from all over the state of Tocantins to MPF-TO. On November 26, 2020, after the MPF sent news crime, the State Civil Police served six search and seizure warrants against Tocantinia traders, suspected of retaining bank cards of indigenous and elderly people in the city. During the operation, the Civil Police seized 134 cards from elderly and indigenous people in the hands of traders. Among them, 83 were from the Bolsa Família program. Police investigate suspicion of swindling, criminal association and retention of magnetic card, which is a crime foreseen in the statute of the elderly, as well as crimes against the consumer.
77cee9bbd269ed46b3c30d76013a7c450fbce1e2: Krahô leaders were at the sanitary barrier installed in the village Kapej, to restrain the Covid-19, when a non-indigenous man appeared in a truck. As he was driving on a road to the territory, they stopped him, and they came across a lot of ammunition for firearms of different calibers inside the truck. The Indians detained the man until the arrival of Funai and the Civil Police. The vehicle was seized and taken to the police station of the municipality of Pedro Afonso, and the owner was indicted. Reported to the MPF, Funai and the Civil Police.
27df820098ba5531e4517ae5845e5d9faa4de207: Illegal carrying of weapons and ammunition
17e5150f70bc01ae8cae60e8f8d99ed25f687024: The bodies of the two adolescents were found by a riverside in the region. In the bodies there were signs of torture and member cuts that, according to the police, indicate that they are practices used by criminal factions. Local authorities have warned of another serious problem faced by indigenous peoples, which is the infiltration of criminal organizations within their traditional territories. They explain that members of the factions seek refuge in remote and difficult places to escape from their enemies or the police.
efda7955db7d292f8bcae7b0859f0cc28873fac8: The indigenous body was found on the banks of the river in Santa Rosa do Purus, and approximately 50 meters from it was an unidentified man, badly injured and with beating marks. Civil police are investigating the case and the delegate reports that the indigenous woman had signs of drowning. The man was hospitalized and is suspected of killing the young woman. The MPF requested your temporary arrest. The delegate responsible for the case has reported that he has heard witnesses and that he will take the opportunity of the photo: Ignatius Werner/CEDH-MT the Chiquitanos brutally murdered by village agents, located on the Bolivian side of the suspicious border, and that he has a history of violence against the woman. The IML is analyzing material collected to assess whether the young woman was also a victim of rape. According to the delegate, the man would have been beaten by other indigenous people after seeing the situation of the young woman. Dsei Alto Rio Purus and Funai follow the investigation. Indigenous leaders told Cimi that the indigenous had gone to the city to receive the benefit of the Bolsa Família program. On the night of that same day, a man who was near the river where many Madija Indians were camped, heavily drunk, ran after Vita, grabbed her by her hair and drowned her in the river until her death.
b29f8b6f5b83ac015da43f70b929ea30f9ea923f: The indigenous youth was found dead on the side of the road, near the municipality of Envira, with signs of aggression. There are no details and the case is being investigated.
292094a8110ddc44715aad324cdc1c29b3806ff1: The only five - year - old child was abducted at dawn while sleeping at home with his mother in the village. Upon missing her daughter, the mother sought help. The child was found lifeless, with signs of asphyxiation and marks of violence by the body and genital organs. Suspects were located in the Ponta Alegre community and contained until the police arrived. The whole community is shaken by the perversity of the case.
79615b280d1fdeb8d803aa24acd051f49a375b60: The murder of the two indigenous peoples occurred in the context of the case that became known as the “massacre of the river Abacaxis”, in the riverside and indigenous communities of the TIs Maraguá and Coatá-Laranjal and the region of the rivers Abacaxis and Marimari, in the municipalities of Borba and Nova Olinda do Norte (AM). In addition to the deaths of the two Munduruku, the case resulted in the murder of four riverside people and the disappearance of two other residents of riverside communities, as well as in several reports of torture and persecution by the Military Police. The conflict began in July, when a group of tourists, in the middle of the pandemic and without proper licensing of environmental agencies, invaded the territories of the region to conduct sport fishing. The then executive secretary of the Amazon Social Promotion Fund, Saulo Moysés Rezende Costa, who was part of the group, claimed to have been shot in the shoulder and threatened to return in retaliation. On August 3, according to reports, policemen entered the rivers using common clothes, carrying heavy weapons and their faces covered. Two police officers were killed during the operation, whose official justification would be the “fight against drug trafficking”. The next day, a contingent of 50 police officers went to the region, carrying out a series of violent actions. The two brothers Munduruku were seen on the night of August 5, going from Rabeta to the headquarters of the municipality, and it is believed that the brothers were executed on the way. On the 7th, Josimar's body was found in the river near the village. The brother's body remains missing, and only the boy's clothing and a skull is supposed to be found. Military police have been spotted in the vicinity of where Josimar's body was found. The following days were marked by several complaints of violence and human rights violations committed by the PM against indigenous and riverside people. The investigation was carried out by the Federal Police, who identified that Josimar was shot in the back of the head. The case ended a year without the people responsible for the action being held accountable and without news of the missing.
74d4f45ffa42d242f9749e5e0be592843cdf3c22: Chief Renato Pataxó reported the murder of the young indigenous, who took place inside the village. The leadership reports that the shooters were on a motorcycle and invaded the village, shooting the young man. The motive for the crime is unknown. The police have been triggered and are investigating the case.
e2244313a17b569dd37e007b1406b37fc73fc84f: The young woman was murdered by her partner, who claimed to be jealous of her. The boy was arrested by the military police the day after the murder and awaiting trial.
2d106518160d575b7249fe634689aa9b1fcc8261: The young Indian was found dead by firearm. There's no information on the case. The murder investigation wasn't completed by the police.
c544168b6bb7ca784f8f4ba0563f5d2a78f981f9: Information indicates that the young man was surprised by a man with a gun, who shot him in the direction, with no chance of reaction. The investigation of the case has not yet been completed by the police.

92cbc3e8ffa8e88211fcaf47d2369ba9b5a1a76f: On August 11, 2020, four chiquitanos were murdered by police officers from the Special Border Group (Gefron), a police center in Mato Grosso that makes the security of the region. The indigenous were hunting in a location near the community of San José de la Frontera, located in San Matías, Bolivia, when they were surprised by Gefron agents. The police reported that Arsino Sunbre García, 53, Pablo Pedraza, 38, Yona Pedraza Tosube, 26, and Ezequiel Pedraza Tosube, 18, would be suspected of drug trafficking and allegedly reacted to the approach. However, it was identified that the indigenous carried only wild animal meat and hunting instruments – that is, nothing that could refer to the commercialization of illicits. The Indians were struck by 29 shots, 27 of which were rifles and two other pistols. Marks of the shootings were recorded in practically a single tree, located inside the São Luiz farm, located 10 km from the indigenous community. Reports of family members, obtained by Cimi and other organizations that conducted an investigation of the case in loco, indicate that there were signs of torture in the bodies, such as victims with broken leg and collarbone, deformed face and body with various abrasions. Hunting is a cultural and subsistence practice of the Chiquitanos, which, in their ancestral territories and traditional occupation, usually transit daily between Brazil and Bolivia, in a region where the dry border is not marked by any delimitation. According to family members, that day, the dogs accompanying the indigenous returned home without their owners, which warned their relatives, who went to look for them. Only after some time were they informed that there were four chiquitans in the morgue of Cáceres (MT), and relatives who were in the city were recognizing the victims. The indigenous also reported that the bodies were only returned to their families almost midnight the following day, after many difficulties in obtaining the coffins and the transfer. The situation generated a situation of terror and destabilization in the community, in addition to the weakening of families directly affected. According to the CNDH, from July to October 2020, there were 17 deaths in Gefron operations, most of them involving chiquitans. The CNDH requested the removal of the officers involved in the operation, but the request was denied by the state Secretary of Public Security of Mato Grosso. MPF and PF are still investigating the case, which, in August 2021, was transferred to the Federal Court.

7505f28021696b72268a4b9a6cd6918599ae30f9: According to information from the Yanomami and Ye ́kuana Indigenous Health District Council (Condisi-Y), the two indigenous youths were attacked in the middle of the forest and shot by prospectors, invaders of the Yanomami land. f42633b24c50eec7a5b64a72ee51dbaf2668c6e0: Leaders denounce the brutal attack on the indigenous area by private security guards of ruralists and also by military police who have already arrived shooting. db0566e13d41ee15f805858251e4ff8543071860: Leaderships denounce that an armed group threatened and shot against the resumption Ñu Verá. 63627fb3063f30b89807b3f395bbc30128672858: Leadership denounces the illegal detention of the indigenous Geraldo Vera, unjustly accused of shooting a private security guard, during a conflict that took place on January 3, 2020 between indigenous and armed security. 01c1aa76925db91ffb5896b86cd6b4cf54a1f8ea: Once again, the President of the Republic, in live video broadcast through social networks, distills his speech of prejudice, racism and hatred against indigenous peoples. By announcing that Vice President Hamilton Mourão would be the head of the Amazon Council, he addresses the Minister of Infrastructure, who was present in the broadcast, and says: “So you know, had contact with the Indians. It's been almost 13, 14 years. I'm sure the Indian has changed. It's evolving. More and more the Indian is a human being like us. So [we need] to get the Indian to join society, and to actually own his land. This is what we want here.” With this anti-indigenous speech, Jair Bolsonaro demonstrates his prejudice and racism by the peoples of this country, who have their rights guaranteed by the Federal Constitution, in Articles 231 and 232, and who need to be respected in their dignity and diversity.
544aa92df2d3a0bd9138d3c54fed9d36a32e7cf3: In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, the President of the Republic vetoed 22 articles of the Bill 1142/2020 on the prevention of infection and the spread of the virus in indigenous territories. Among these articles, it vetoed the supply of drinking water to indigenous peoples, and was supported by the vice president. Hamilton Mourão said that indigenous peoples do not need drinking water, as they “supply water from the rivers in their region”. This speech refers to a prejudice towards indigenous peoples and the entire poor population, and disregards the reality that most rivers are polluted. According to the UN report released in 2019, the consumption and use of untreated and polluted water kills more than all forms of violence. Lack of clean water kills 1.8 million children under the age of 5 annually in the world. Diarrhoea, mainly caused by dirty water, kills about 2.2 million people per year, according to the report, and “more than half of the hospital beds in the world are occupied by people with diseases related to contaminated water.” Not to mention the socioeconomic and environmental impacts linked to water pollution, a hard reality experienced by indigenous and non-indigenous people. One of the ways to prevent Covid-19 is through water hygiene. In addition, with the aforementioned speech, the vice president also ignored that in many indigenous territories there is no drinking water, requiring the supply of carousels.
12e1119dfa8958a2a73785a4cad2c1d8a17c09a9: The Manchinery Association of Great Villages (Matpha) forwarded a complaint to the MPF about alleged irregularities and practice of racism in the choice of edict projects published by the Elias Mansour Culture and Communication Foundation (FEM). The MPF instituted a civil inquiry to investigate alleged irregularities in the selection of projects in the Aldir Blanc Law. Acre received R $ 16 million in aid, and the money is managed by the FEM, which makes the payment in 03 instalments of R $ 600 to farmers of culture. The funds were released from September and were issued so that the cultural professionals would have access to the benefit. The Matpha Association pointed out the following irregularities to the MPF: that the indigenous were not heard in the elaboration of the notice; that the deadlines offered were short; lack of transparency and criteria in the analysis of the proposals. The MPF forwarded letters to the DSEI ́s Alto Rio Purus and Alto Rio Juruá provide clarifications on the situation.
6d1a61f76d9a3bb867e5c6f6f016249d61551232: 2020 was particularly difficult for the indigenous peoples of Brazil. The daily situations of violence and disrespect of all sorts experienced by indigenous people were not enough, the arrival of the Covid-19 pandemic worsened the scenario. Prejudice, racism and ethnic-cultural discrimination of non-indigenous people increased greatly in 2020, in much provoked by the hate and violence speeches of the President of the Republic himself against indigenous peoples. Denunciations of leaders Xavante and Bororo in BBC Brazil report indicate the spread of offensive audios and text messages, with attacks on indigenous people, in the municipality of General Carneiro (MT), for the residents of the city. Among the offensive comments, it stands out that of a man, in audio for a group of WhatsApp: “Oh, mate, that’s only Indian, boy... not people, not (...). Within General himself, the number of infected is very little, thank God. Now the Indians... these people are without culture, without religion, who cares about these people there?” In another message, also in WhatsApp group, one resident says: “This many positive cases (from Covid-19) in General. I see that this 'fuck' of this place will close because of these Indians (...). I can’t stand these devils of these Indians on the door asking for 24 hours of food”. In another audio, a man refers to indigenous people as “bichos”: “You have to close the villages, right? Get there, get the police in there and stop everything. They would have to close the villages for these ‘bichos’“. The Indians prepared a document, which was handed over to the MPF and Funai, making the complaint, asking for investigation and punishment to those responsible for the crime.
364293e1f528b671b38c0ad3d7b4d25cb414779a: Timothy Idjariwa Karajá, former chief of the village Kre-hawã, sought the Municipal Hospital of Luciara for medical care, suspected of Covid-19, and was harassed by officials with statements that the indigenous should not go to the city, because they would be transmitting the coronavirus to the non-indigenous. According to him, the indigenous health agents of the village were warned not to take patients suspected of Covid-19 to the hospital. Mr. Timothy also denounced being prejudiced in the city markets for the same reason. It was made an audio recording of Mr. Timothy and a video, denouncing the episode, and posted on social media. According to Mairu Hakuwi Kuady Karajá, who is master of law by UNB, and who made the recordings of the complaint, the results obtained with the disclosure of the videos were positive, as discriminatory comments ceased.
0f409b0423b80d556e89c8803acb9d90ff188191: Indigenous leaders and indigenous entities denounced to the MPF, through news crime, two broadcasters who disseminated racist and prejudiced comments in the Open Space program, broadcast by Radio Grande FM, Dourados (MS). According to the complaint, the radio reporters commented on more resistant garbage bags, which scare cats that rip the bags, spreading the garbage: “These new bags that are coming out, they have a very strong smell. And this full inhibits the arrival of the cat to rip the garbage bag ", said Cicero. Then he completed that “if it was just cat, Indians also love to tear bags”. In an ironic tone, his colleague Paul said: “If you were to put a scent to scare the Indians away, it will be difficult (laughs)”. In the complaint it was described that “the objective of the presenters was to humiliate, incite hatred to indigenous peoples, spread discourse of subalternization of indigenous peoples, comparing them to the animals that reviewed garbage bags”. Such acts corroborate the prejudice already faced by indigenous people in that region, even worsened in the pandemic period, during which they have struggled to survive without a decent space to live, without food, without drinking water, without the minimum conditions to guarantee their protection and care, given the total absence of the State.
ab65308f56b503cbce5dc5238af7670002cdd55c: In an interview with TV Globo’s “Good morning MS” program, Funai’s then newly appointed coordinator for the Campo Grande region, the reserve military José Magalhães Filho, stated that the “Indian has to be fully integrated into society”. Among other prejudiced and misguided statements, she reports that “india has to start dating black and white, and this integration has automatically emerged, and that is how our policy is implemented”. The “integration policy” that the current government has been trying to implement refers to the military dictatorship, and goes against what is advocated by the 1988 Federal Constitution in its articles 231 and 232. The Terena Council obtained in the Federal Court the suspension, in a preliminary decision, of the appointment of the retired captain, who was later exonerated.
111dca2b2def08b13f57824589ae0ff59ddace9c: The young man was on the highway near the village, trying to answer his cell phone, where there's a signal. He was approached truculently, as happens in the usual way with the indigenous. They report that they are always approached aggressively and intimidatingly by police officers. Usually, according to the reports, they do an interrogation, verbally assault the indigenous and make threats of physical aggression and death.
b973d5cb543d08b64048433b012d3f3734d72286: Abuse of authority; abuse; discriminatory police approach
3a9f9e69d782189b4ec90ae9929a15502fa42dee: The arrival of the Covid-19 pandemic in the villages of the Dourados indigenous reserve, the most populous in the country, generated a wave of prejudiced comments and hatred on social networks. The situation drew the attention of the indigenous pedagogue Michelli Alves Machado, who copied several of these negative manifestations in relation to the communities and posted in his social network with the title “Thus goes inhumanity”. She said the goal of the collage was to draw the attention of society to this rooted prejudice and that the disease is just an excuse for the spread of this hatred. “The problem is not the pandemic, the point is that we are indigenous. If these people could exterminate or erase the indigenous population, they would do so without thinking twice. They're using the virus just to bring out the hatred and prejudice inside them. A lot of Golden people know the Reserve, but they just stick to negative questions about it and generalize. They say there's nothing but ping, that we only live on a basic basket or that we don't like to work. But these same people forget that profiles like those described exist in any community, indigenous or not.” According to her, among the various racist comments, which insinuates that “Indian is not human” was the one that drew the most attention. “What are we? Can't we be considered human? Are we animals? ", emphasized Michelli. The racist and prejudiced comments will all be collected by the legal advice of Cimi and forwarded to the Federal Public Ministry for action, ranging from the opening of investigative procedure in order to investigate the occurrence of crime to the possibility of lawsuits for collective damage against the indigenous population.
4b3813e1cd4e0535c19727421ef1bb3791e41fe2: Mothers and grandmothers of students delivered a document to the MPF of Guaíra, denouncing that their children and grandchildren have long suffered prejudice, discrimination and racism. They report that the municipal Social Assistance Department launched a campaign entitled “Say no to begging” which, according to the document, is another attempt to reinforce the discrimination of indigenous children, as they want to prevent them from going to the city and also prevent traders and other people more sensitive to the reality faced by them from continuing to help them. They also denounce that the municipality is one of those who struggle to prevent the regularization of its traditional occupation territory, a context that is at the origin of the vulnerability situation to which indigenous families are subjected in the region.
cc1b3373d9e1a398ca38da7125574b1508b40f7b: The two Guarani were prevented from buying at the Paulista Supermarket on Friday, July 3. According to the indigenous, the head of the establishment said that she was guided by a city supervisor not to attend them due to a decree that limited the circulation of people from the Covid-19 risk group in the city. One of the indigenous also said he heard that “everyone has disease in the village” and that, therefore, he could not enter. The case has already been reported to the State Prosecutor's Office (MPE), and the Attorney General's Office (PGR) has instituted a procedure to investigate possible crime of racism.
c11bdf612c012098299aee880de8b8f262e74b28: In the middle of the coronavirus pandemic, which in July 2020 had already caused 280 cases of Covid-19 among the Yanomami and Ye’kuana peoples, women of military of the platoons of Suruccus and Auaris carried out a “social action”, with distribution of clothes, candy (which are not part of the people’s food custom) for children and makeup of women within the Yanomami IT. The so-called “social action” was published on social networks in Roraima with messages that asked for donation of coats. In addition to disregarding the basic standards of protection and prevention against the Covid-19, causing agglomeration and distribution of products from outside without any control, the action reflects a colonial mentality, racist and deep disrespect to the culture of indigenous women. The activity took place in the days following the “mission” that led to an expedition from the Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Health to Yanomami IT, in which there was distribution of chloroquine in the communities, as stated in the investigation procedure opened by the MPF/RR. In the same operation, with significant participation of the Army, the Defense Minister said that the pandemic was “controlled in Yanomami IT”. President of the Yanomami and Ye’kwana District Health Council (Condisi-Y), Junior Hekurari Yanomami, reported: “What they did is a total disrespect. This donation of clothes... The Yanomami people are not beggars. Jumper? We don't need jumper. They caused a crowd! The government's action was very wrong. We need government support is to contain the Covid-19, which is entering, spreading in the villages.”
9824a259cc010fab0de0c6f43e91e9181d4a0ba3: Indigenous students from Unicamp report that they suffered several attacks during a “live” entitled “Indigenous Identities at the Public University: Building dialogues in the fight for rights”. The attack occurred around 4:30 p.m., during the speech of a young indigenous woman. Screams, offenses, hate speeches and prejudiced and racist provocations were heard. According to the students, it was clear that it was an attack by an organized group, because in the first speeches, the criminals questioned whether the speakers “were voters of the current president”. Several collectives and organizations signed a letter of repudiation against racist attacks. The dean of Unicamp, Marcelo Knobel, released a repudiation note. So far, no person responsible for the attack has been identified.
661704b4f1e21bf3e900fe2e37dab5eaa440accc: The mayor of the municipality of Formoso do Araguaia, through the Municipal Health Secretariat, decreed by letter that the indigenous people of Javaé people were prevented from entering Formoso do Araguaia for a period of 7 days. On the charge that they were taking the coronavirus to the city, the Indians had their right to come and go restricted. Indigenous leaders were prevented from entering the municipality through a sanitary barrier that was installed on the arrival of the city. When the Indians arrived at the barriers, they were barred by city officials. The MPF was triggered and determined the suspension of the municipal decree.
40e77e89780c9e7b600238f578e89f3bdb2ed180: When the first two patients of the people Xerente contaminated by Covid-19 arrived at the Indigenous Health Base of Tocantinia, there were no health professionals to serve them on site. Inconformity with neglect and disrespect, the daughter of one of the patients, Bento Wakuke Xerente, called the head of Polo Base several times, seeking explanations about why patients were having to wait so long to access the service. Then the Polo professional sent him audio messages mistreating and subalternizing the indigenous. After recovery, the two patients were quarantined by Sesai in a public school in the city. From then on, a series of prejudiced and racist messages were triggered by non-indigenous people in a group of WhatsApp entitled “MOCOTO”. The attacks were against indigenous patients and, consequently, against the entire Xerente people, and their content incited the population of Tocantinia to hate the indigenous who were being treated in the municipality. In a note, the Xerente people expressed “veely repudiation of the manifestations of hatred, prejudice, discrimination and visceral racism”. Leaderships of the people entered with a representation in the MPF against the municipal government, the head of the Indigenous Health Base Pole, the administrator of the WhatsApp group and its members.
fa26351796501b38919c008819b7463e7f94af86: Two armed men raided Piaraçu Village, chief Raoni Metuktire, and shot at the community. The Indians managed to hide and were not injured. 29 shots were fired, endangering the more than 300 indigenous people who live there. According to complaint from the leaders, the men invaded the village after destroying the sanitary barrier built by the indigenous to maintain social isolation in this pandemic period. Report was made, but the community is afraid to be surprised by a new attack.
1cb34dde3b824251b5aa55213094ad34a140f2a4: An indigenous of unidentified people and name was attacked by two men in a hotel in the municipality of Querência. The criminals shot him three times. According to witnesses, the criminals were armed and entered the room, then fleeing. The indigenous was referred to a hospital with injuries to the knee, thigh and waist, where he received care. The police have been triggered and are investigating the attempted murder.
bca7b2f0afdfdfb08bcccacd24f5cc2c7ad5a60d: Rikbaktsa Indians gathered in front of Juína Funai to ask for explanations and punishment in the case of a young indigenous man shot at a rural property in the municipality. According to the leaders, the young man was shot because he went for help in a farm on the side of the road, because the motorcycle he was on
2f83e56ffa16a842857871867f19a609c7072bec: Tupinambá Indians who live in the village Encanto da Patioba, an area located in the municipality of Itapebi, in the extreme south of Bahia, were surprised by firearms. The shots hit a sign that the site is indigenous land; the leaders could not identify the authors of the shots, who were in a boat; the entrance of the village is made by the banks of the river Jequitinhonha. Chief Ron recorded the police report at the local police station.
217b0a2fad1a227e6446cfebc5c274186ad67076: The 23-year-old indigenous man suffered an assassination attempt inside the village. According to the police report, the victim was involved in a fight and was stabbed. Firemen helped him and sent him to the hospital. The assailant escaped and the police are investigating the case.
9cda584d13eaea0a2daa98ee61543f7ad6142f4e: The Indian was found wounded by machete blows. He was rescued by firemen and taken to the Hospital of Life in Dourados. The crime is being found, and the author has not yet been discovered, nor is the motive of the crime known.
cd5dd2d2aff39cffd919f579ae10dcb4016eca7a: According to information from the police report, Silvania was at home, with her son on her lap, when the man entered the house and began arguing with her, beating her with a machete blow to the head. According to the bulletin, the man, named Paulino, is the victim's cousin, and is being sought. Silvania was treated at Mission Hospital, medicated and released.
a8935f6a77e831ccee6cea497497ac81938f0289: The couple were returning from town to their tekoha when a car drove towards them, almost running them over. The driver braked abruptly, opened the window and said: “Ah! You are Paraguayans; if you were Indians, I would go over”. Several complaints have already been made to the MPF reporting prejudice, racism and discrimination of non-indigenous people towards the Guarani people in this region.
c49c2eb007d6027497263ac49c499cf3ac905bb4: Leadership reports that the four indigenous youths had participated in a football championship in a locality near tekoha. Upon returning to their villages by motorcycle, they were attacked by five men, who knocked them down with sticks, machetes and knives. Military police were called in, but they didn't help the wounded. Samu was fired, but he didn't get to the scene for another hour. Three young people were rescued, but one of them, Virgil, upon entering the hospital, died. The police are investigating the case. The attackers are still free.
9007eb9f899c15455965864843154f18f6388626: Between May and August, chief Ilson Soares and the community suffered three gun attacks. All the attacks were at night, coming from vehicles passing by Martin Luther King Avenue, which borders the village. The shots were fired at the beginning of the village, at the gate and at the end of the village. For Ilson “it was an act of provocation. Because there's no justification for firing firearms in front of the village. And it was multiple shots. At the first point, there were about five to seven shots; at the gate, likewise, and at the end, in the same way”, explained the chief. The vehicle passed for the first time and the shots were fired; then the vehicle returned on the same route and more shots were fired at the same points in the village. Twice, the chief recorded a police report, but the third time he didn't do the O.R. because the Civil Police were closed because of the Covid-19 pandemic.
fac7c31d94c0be13716129d899a22deda8dcee20: The PM of Guaíra was informed about a man wounded by the knife, who was attended at the UPA. The nurse on duty reported that the injured man was indigenous. He had been injured with a deep puncture in the abdomen region. It was also informed that the indigenous was medicated and would be transferred to another city, given the severity of the injury. The indigenous identification was being investigated.
6bf0aa2bcc49caff661a825f34da3440b4639108: During the night, the PM was called to the village Tekoha Yhovy to verify a firearm shooting occurrence. At the scene, police were received by an indigenous representative of the chief, who was traveling. She reported that she heard several prints similar to gunshots and then called the police. With the permission of the indigenous leadership, the police team entered the village and conducted searches. One resident told the police that at the time he was in his house, two men approached and called by a name; he went out and said he didn't know anyone by that name. The authors replied “it’s you” and drew two firearms towards you. The Indian reported that he ran off and soon after hearing several shots, but was not shot by any of them. The two shooters were spotted by witnesses when they fled through the woods. Searches were conducted near the site, where the PM found 23 ammunition capsules 9mm. During the search, the perpetrators of the attack were not located. The Guaíra Civil Police are investigating the case.
c70a8826804a903e5dc9e31ac3ff1348c265a648: Early on April 5th, Kaingang Zeca, Candire's grandson, suffered an attack, and was beaten and stabbed. Help took hours to get to the scene. Zeca was hospitalized in a very severe state in a nearby ICU and remained in a coma for several days until discharge. The community expects crime to be investigated and those responsible to be punished in respect to life and its rights to live traditionality and spirituality.
70d802de8797edce35a347b60283744ccb1ed4b6: The Indian woman was raped by her ex-husband and by a non-indigenous man known to her ex-husband. She reported to police that the men drugged her and that she suffered the assaults. The medical team that attended her confirmed that she had signs of sexual violence and physical aggression. The police are investigating the case and looking for the attackers.
a556e37253dc38471a4e19c0dc1888d583c33781: As denunciation by the Council Guardianship of the municipality, the indigenous child was abused repeatedly by the father himself, when he was under the influence of alcohol. In addition to this complaint, the father was also registered for abandonment of incapacitated.
5f68cc4ed451b0bb62359e4aa0f571925fee8526: According to information, the indigenous woman was assaulted and raped by her own son. She was treated at Kaiowá Mission Hospital,
ab5095ae228ab6a7d4f34bd54013aa0668a7a8a7: According to a police report, the adolescent's parents reported that the victim had been raped by his uncle after he was taken to an area behind the Indian House. The mother reports she missed her daughter and found her with the suspect. A restraining order was issued by the Children and Youth Protection Court of Porto Velho and the suspect was arrested.
ef9a9ffa2725c80c66217b11637d82ca4ce66575: A young 20 - year - old Yanomami, admitted to Casai de Roraima, was attacked by an 18 - year - old male of the same ethnicity. According to a nurse's report to the Military Police, the suspect took advantage while everyone was resting and took the young woman by force to an isolated location. They both went into body struggle while the young woman was trying to avoid rape. The boy's been arrested. Sesai had not yet expressed herself on the case.
e638faa56fdd699091e6cef811a43b99e29e90de: According to a complaint made by Apib, the crisis office created in the government by determination of the STF has been decommissioning periodic agendas to deal with issues related to the Covid-19, especially in what affects the isolated indigenous, even more vulnerable facing this pandemic. Apib also reports that the minister of the Presidency’s Institutional Security Office - GSI, Augusto Heleno, had been harsh with participants in a meeting between indigenous people and government representatives.
e2bb2b7c171322666cd45ed98ce2548daca10022: Leaderships denounce that fire prevention in indigenous lands and surrounding areas was not done in a timely manner, and that mobilization of indigenous brigades began three months later than usual. Fruit of a cooperation agreement between Ibama and Funai created in 2013, the Federal Brigades Program is an experience of fire management that uses traditional indigenous knowledge together with the technical and financial support of these organs, in order to prevent fires from the dry season and fight them when they occur. However, leaders report that the resource cuts and the delay in the schedule of activities, in addition to the anti-indigenous policy of the current government, compromised the actions of brigades and aggravated the situation of fires and the destruction caused. Prevention and management actions usually began in April and this year they started only in July, when the flames were already everywhere. The indigenous people fear for the end of the federal brigade program, due to annual cuts in the budget for the Environment and the federal government's own policy, which has committed itself to reducing the surveillance and firefighting actions, as well as persecuting the indigenous peoples.
689e0518fd2a5ffed0b11dd2690b6bfe5e124120: According to data from the Superior Electoral Court, with only a few days left for the municipal elections, 67% of the indigenous candidates had received no donation from either the parties or other candidates or individuals. Among the 2017 indigenous fit to compete for the positions of councilor, mayor and deputy mayor, 1,413 of them had their accounts zeroed.
b274405d47fd661f82c8ddfb6b00d345eae7be86: Complaint to the Acre Public Ministry led him to investigate the situation of an indigenous family that was found living in the middle of a dump in the municipality of Sena Madureira. In the process, there is information that the family would be housed on site, amid animal bones and organic waste, characterizing serious human rights violations. According to the complaint, the indigenous would be in search of food and recyclable in the city dump. Funai and the Social Assistance Department of the municipality were activated. The Social Assistance Department informed the prosecutor that it went to check and found no families living on the site, and that the indigenous people “have the custom of going out through the city turning garbage box”. The situation portrays the neglect and prejudice with which the indigenous people are treated, especially this year, in full pandemic situation, when whole families resort to garbage in search of food and sustenance.
e35dd892c1337c227c14109b18cdc3918538e5dc: After denunciation of the Indigenous Federation of the People Kukami-Kukamiria and the General Organization of the Chiefs of the Indigenous Communities of the Kokama People, the MPF opened civil inquiry to determine the reasons why Funai is not providing services to the Kokama community living in the Greater Victory neighborhood, in the east of Manaus. Tito Menezes, leader of the Sateré-Mawé people, in the Lower Amazon, reported that Funai employees have no autonomy to perform basic actions in the regions.
ef2dd681be51cfbf2c44153cd4bbbb4d4339790f: The indigenous people Mura has been suffering for a long time from the invasion of her territory by farmers, and the government does not take action, not even in this severe period of the coronavirus pandemic. Since the territory is not yet regulated and there is no supervision, invasions have increased. One of the biggest problems faced by the Mura families has been the lack of drinking water. The river that should be used by the indigenous people is completely contaminated and unfit for consumption, due to the large amount of feces and urine of buffaloes that are created by these farmers. Leaderships have reported to the MPF and are awaiting action.
7fc523a6dd4e952c249aff870cb9b06b8eb81ad2: Leaderships of the Federation of Peoples and Indigenous Organizations of Ceará (Fepoince) denounce that Funai referred R$ 137,670.37 for actions aimed at indigenous peoples of Ceará, through the Regional Coordination Northeast II, which also serves the peoples of Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte. The value represents an investment less than R$ 0.05 daily per indigenous, in the period from March 15, when the first cases of coronavirus in the state were officially confirmed, until June 22, a date that marked the 100 days after the first confirmed case of the disease. Proportionally, each of the 35,757 Ceará indigenous people, according to Sesai, had destined R $ 3,82 in Funai actions over the first 100 days of the official period of the pandemic in the state. According to Funai, the resource was used to purchase and distribute food baskets and hygiene kits. According to Weibe Tapeba, legal advisor to Fepoince, the value is insufficient to meet the demand.
2e9b7b5a974c2a8f5f80382634eb49af8dd7b58c: The constant lack of energy in the Tapuia community caused material and financial damage, with the damage of appliances and equipment of the indigenous school and the loss of food stored in refrigerators of the village. The community suffers from the recurrent lack of energy. This time, the Enel de Goiás, which provides electricity, took four days to repair the damage of an energy transformer. There was great damage also in milk production, because without energy, the coolant tank does not work, and several liters of milk that were stored ruined. Enel was activated to replace 25 refrigerators from families who had their appliances burned.
321f75aad09e791a02316e323ce5891947180137: The leaders of the Krepym Cati people Ji have denounced the bad conditions of the roads that give access to the villages, but the municipality and the state have done nothing to solve the problem.
5888b42d41463fc435c2444fac5192cdffe065b5: Indigenous people of the Akroá-Gamella people are not getting access to federal social benefits such as retirement, sickness aid and maternity aid, because the Social Assistance Department of the municipality of Viana does not accept the Funai Declarations and thus refuses to forward the requests for benefits to the INSS.
318a19f904b1f4f67447f6bd640b0fd184a12e5b: Leaderships report that the indigenous make purchases of food and other necessary genres in the municipality of Barra do Corda. The purchased products are usually packed in plastic materials and cans. The municipality of Barra do Corda does not provide garbage collection service in the village, which has been filled with these materials. The leaders are concerned about the accumulation of these wastes within the territory, which is located in the Cerrado, an area under strong environmental pressure that needs to be preserved.
efee5fa95c88e2ab42eca7c00543e17cc078ec48: Leaderships of the various villages of the people Sabanê, Manduca, Idalamarê and others have been claiming for years, together with the public agencies, the repair and restoration of the roads and bridges that connect the communities to the city of Vilhena and the construction of bridges linking the Central village to the village Ikê and the other villages. Students have to travel by bus to schools, and bad road conditions have prevented them from attending classes. In addition to the difficulties faced by the students, families have also failed to drain their agricultural production for commercialization in the city, since the roads do not allow access to the truck used for the transport of banana, pineapple and cassava and for the displacement of the indigenous, who also go to the urban center to receive its benefits and do their shopping. There are over 350 people, approximately 100 families, who are prevented from leaving their villages. Leaderships made a complaint document to the MPF with copies to the responsible agencies, demanding the reform of the roads, the repair of the bridge and also two power posts that fell. The community is waiting for arrangements.
c351b91a62959affeb7648641267a0bc4162cae4: Lack of maintenance on roads, bridges and poles
73fb7694941077a318fc91f3fe6e1b881d9381d4: Leaderships of the Zoró people report that an indigenous woman was injured with an arrow shot by an indigenous living in voluntary isolation in the region, and who appeared in the village of Caneco, in the Amazon region of Mato Grosso. The injured woman was rescued and is not at risk of death. The case reflects the omission of public agencies regarding the need to comply with their obligations to regulate indigenous territories and remove invaders from these territories. Chief Waratan Zoró stated that the isolates have been pressured by invasions and deforestation and, consequently, having their survival threatened. He reports that the invaders threaten and frighten the isolated; they become “crazed”, frightened and run out through the woods, without having to eat, starving and not knowing how to protect themselves. According to Neidinha Suruí, of the Etnoenvironmental Defense Association Kanindé, “the government needs to strengthen the protection fronts of the isolated Indians, survey the occupation areas of these indigenous peoples, interdict these areas and strengthen the teams with experienced personnel to make the protection of these indigenous peoples, because otherwise, it will soon be a genocide”. Zoró leaders fear for the fate of these isolates and believe that they can be attacked or starved.
76543af750b6db4911d688be2e0dc49a6a23495c: At the Parabubure IT, the following bridges are in a precarious state, with serious risks to the Xavante population in their displacements: two bridges over the São Filipe stream, near the villages Santa Clara and São Filipe; three bridges over the Parabubu Stream, near the villages São Jorge, Palmeiras and Santos do Céu; and a bridge over a stream near the Estrela Village. It is clear the neglect of the indigenous, when it is observed that the roads of the ground and the bridges that cross the indigenous lands towards some large farms are very well conserved, with regular maintenance made by the machines of the city. But on the roads whose destinations are only the villages, maintenance is not done. Since 2019, the Xavantes have been denouncing the situation, but so far no provision has been taken by the government.
b1144b48bd2fa0a4dffe5b5e180879f01ba02365: The indigenous Frederico Ruwabzu Tserotomodzatse attended the INSS, accompanied by Fr. Eloir, in the city of Água Boa, where he would have an expertise scheduled to re-confirm his Parkinson's Disease. After the forensics, you were given a password to monitor the results on the INSS website. The INSS employee told him that the following day the result would already be available; however, the result, denying him access to sickness aid, only left a week later. On March 30, Frederico filed an appeal against the rejection of the aid, but so far it appears on the INSS website that the process continues “In analysis”. The social worker of the Casai of Campinápolis reported that there are cases of indigenous people who have been waiting for the result of its benefits for more than six months. He also said that the federal government centralized the analysis of these social benefits in few cities in Brazil and that the number of doctors and employees was very low. The Campinápolis Public Defender entered with injunction in order to regain his INSS insurance status.
5d80afae7c86cf5c58fd51db60bfa25c74ca985b: Since there are no buses making transport lines to the villages, the indigenous are obliged to pay freight in non-indigenous vehicles to travel to the city, do their shopping and return to their homes. The freighters charge very high amounts. The City Council has already been asked to establish a price list, but because there are councilors linked to freighters, the discussion is postponed and there is no decision. Since 2019, this violation has been reported, but there has been no provision.
a4478ca174be5c89842ea128ae6dfde6cfb077f7: The lack of adequate transportation to meet the indigenous communities of the villages to the city worsened this year of pandemic. Funai de Barra do Garças and Funai de Campinápolis tried to regulate the service of freight service providers, but did not succeed. The “freighters” take the Xavante to the cemetery door, at the entrance of the city, or even a bamboo bush, at another entrance of the city. From these points forward, the Xavante walk to the city center. Both on their way to the city and back, indigenous people are transported in vehicles under the same conditions of overcrowding as before the pandemic, in open bodies.
885960967f48b81429df5634888d5d5e54b050a2: The indigenous continue to complain a lot about the attendance of the Funai of Campinápolis in forwarding their demands. Even the simple issuing of statements for the removal of personal documents or the search for social benefits have been delayed or have been denied. The local coordinator of Funai, despite being indigenous, shows no commitment to the demands of relatives or to the fulfillment of his duty as a servant. The situation is worrying, especially in the current pandemic situation.
9f337db31ab47eeb8b962958132099fac919f566: Leaderships denounce that due to the lack of sanitary barriers established by the government to prevent the advance of the Covid-19, several non-indigenous people have addressed the villages, with motorcycles, selling products such as meat and others, which may be contaminated. The harassment only decreased because the leaders mobilized, expelled the sellers and are creating barriers on their own.
9785caec71f9d3bb462d8ad6a0536d385c2eb7b6: Mrs. Rafaela Udzé’a Tsereruremé, widow of Luís Miguel Tseretsu Abhoodi, deceased by Covid-19, was found by Fr. Eloir Oliveira sitting on the sidewalk of Banco do Brasil, in Campinápolis, asking for money to get the second way of the marriage certificate in the local registry. With the certificate, she would claim the pension right of her late husband, who was an employee of Funai. She reported that all government agencies refused to forward the case. She also complained that her husband had orthopedic problems and used crutches; even so, she was not assured the right to have a companion during treatment, since when she was transferred from Campinápolis, first to the hospital of Água Boa and then to the hospital of Cuiabá, where she died, alone, by Covid-19, without any relatives present. This case is yet another one in which the Xavante suffer from the ignorance of their care rights and do not find support from the competent bodies. These bodies also tend to provide undiscounted and contradictory information, forcing the indigenous to make several trips to the city without being able to progress their needs.
847d8868f656740829ad5dd0400cb58cfddde895: In September, Sesai installed water boxes in the village Santa Rita de Cássia, but did not pierce the artesian well. For some time Campinápolis City Hall took water in dump trucks to fill them. Then, he was forced to interrupt this service, after denouncing that that action would be “buying votes”, due to the election year. The community ran out of clean water. On October 7, sensitized to the suffering of the Xavante population by the omission of the government, aggravated by the pandemic period, partners of the Salesian Mission of Mato Grosso and Operation Mato Grosso - OMG perforated an artesian well in the village. Thus, at least the problem of lack of water experienced by indigenous people in this village was solved.
c79a2751edab57f805cb413c9234b46a39d4a80c: A group of leaders Xavante attended the inauguration of the new DSEI Coordinator Xavante, the military Gildo Henrique de Azeredo, in Barra do Garças, to protest against the appointment. The Xavante claimed a lack of prior dialogue with the communities and with the Indigenous Health District Council (Condisi). They also argued that the chosen military, from Rio de Janeiro, knows neither the Xavante culture nor the local reality. No provision has been made so far, and the military remains in office.
eb6fdbbb27a888b38771324432b2737577d262bb: Hire of military to coordinate the DSEI
35aebec4092e8d951eda205dc32f2ee7c933d959: In the middle of the pandemic period, the state of Mato Grosso and the municipality of Campinápolis paid their servers on the same date, causing large agglomerations of indigenous people in the banking agencies, subjecting them to a serious risk of contagion by the coronavirus. Previously, state and county payments were made on different dates.
010585b04e28840321d1a0ff9a86ef35a5678de1: In the days of monthly payments, the Campinápolis Loterical House does not provide the amount of money needed to pay the indigenous people who receive their benefits.
