The establishment starts to serve only people who have payments to make and, only hours later, when “money has entered”, they call the Xavante who will receive. The consequences of such disrespect are hours of waiting, and many indigenous people are elderly who wait standing, clustered at the door of Casa Loterica, with great risk of contamination by coronavirus and great delays until they can make their purchases and return to the villages.
2435d3201e6142165dcef48e47f682fe2ae29098: The indigenous Frederico, who suffers from Parkinson’s disease, accessed the INSS of Good Water to obtain the proper benefit. The INSS requested from him a Contribution Time Certificate, referring to both the municipality of Campinápolis and the state, due to its long working time in indigenous education. On January 11, Fr. Eloir handed over to the coordinator Isaac, from the local Funai, these certificates and asked him for a Funai Declaration to forward the documents required by the INSS. However, the coordinator said he would go on vacation on the 16th and would not have time to elaborate the statement that, according to him, was very complex, and that he could only write it from February 26th. To the argument that he would still have four working days before going on vacation, and that Frederick needed the benefit, he replied that he would also need the presence of the social worker of Sesai to issue the statement – which was proved not necessary. Isaac further added that “if Frederick had waited three years without receiving benefits, he could wait another month.” Only on February 26, coordinator Isaac Mi’é Ajaw This consisted of only one sheet with the name of Frederico, the numbers of his RG and CPF and the information that he lived in the village São Pedro, TI Parabubure. It was evident the unnecessary neglect and delay for issuing a simple statement, resulting, consequently, in the delay of the INSS to analyze and assess the case of a sick person in need of the rightful benefit.
affd412045cd1728b5f3ee9b98ea75a6707c46be: Leaderships denounced to the MPF that they were not receiving basic baskets since November of the previous year, when the president of Funai decided that he would no longer serve indigenous communities that do not live in completely demarcated areas. The delay in the regularization of the territory led the Guarani-Kaiowá to resume close to farms overlapping with their traditional occupation territory. There are dozens of families, with many children and the elderly, living in tiny portions of land, prevented from planting for their own livelihood. Living in precarious and subhuman conditions, in canvas shacks, they are subjected to constant violence, threats, nutritional insecurity and hunger, waiting for the demarcation of their lands. The MPF made a recommendation to Funai and the National Supply Company (Conab) to continue the delivery of basic baskets in the regions not yet demarcated in the south of the state, in the region of Dourados and Ponta-Porã, claiming that the non-demarcation of the lands was caused by the delay of the municipality itself in fulfilling its legal functions.
915f0291eb657eb7b4d3e2683c4a2aaa6d54b333: Lack of food and land regularization
98d13a49510f013ab88451d0a05a3d0a8ca285d5: The MPF in Mato Grosso do Sul denounces delay in the execution of search warrants in homes of those involved in land conflict between besiegers and indigenous people living in the resumptions located in the border area of the Dourados indigenous reserve, occurred in 2018. Due to the delay, the collection of evidence of the conflict can be frustrated, since there was enough time to conceal important evidence for the investigation. Meanwhile, the climate of violence and conflict remain in the region, and indigenous families are the most affected.
c4f8860eeea7328373fa57cd15f9ade8c80ffdb8: Leaderships denounce that the first Indigenous Olympic Village of the country portrays the disregard of the government. The 29,000 m2 complex is depredated and is only used when schools promote few activities per year. What would be a space of sport, culture, leisure, community activities, professionalization of young people and an option to reduce the rates of violence in the indigenous territory is taken by bush and the facilities depredated. There was an expectation that Funai would intermediate with the federal government a partnership with the local government to promote projects. Nine years have passed since the opening and nothing has been done.
48415564cadb999cb86275d71f5280307552836f: Leaderships have been denouncing the bad road conditions of the region for a long time. The lack of road maintenance compromises the displacement of families to the cities, students to go to schools, help reach the villages when necessary, among other problems. In response to the request of the MPF, the Federal Justice of Dourados urged the prefectures of Dourados and Itaporan to carry out maintenance works of the internal routes of the Golden TI, following the municipal borders, and on equal terms with services provided to other rural communities. The MPF reported to the Justice the unequal treatment that is given to indigenous peoples regarding road recovery, compared to the other districts. The community awaits the fulfillment of the judicial decision by the prefectures.
eae4b072eb787e2ae23138368ea2d153802ad402: At the annual meeting on the rights of children at the UN Human Rights Council, the 15-year-old indigenous Roger Ferreira Alegre of the Guarani-Kaiowá people in Amambai denounced the failure of the Brazilian government. In the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic in the villages, he spoke of the lack of food and the climate of insecurity that hangs over indigenous peoples, due to the paralysis of the demarcation of their lands, and the consequent risks to their health, food, safety, physical and mental integrity. He also reported that indigenous children suffer from high malnutrition rates; that 60% of families live under tents of canvas, without access to drinking water, health, education, food, in a “true humanitarian crisis”. Roger also reported that the refrigerators in the region were foci of coronavirus transmission, and that many of the indigenous people were contaminated working in JBS refrigerators. He stressed that “the main measure to protect the rights of indigenous children is to guarantee the demarcation of our territories”.
5b3d8d3a72156cd396eb8ea5f2c7170a6dde9171: Indigenous peoples of Guarani and Kaiowá were victims of the serious lack of working conditions, especially during the pandemic, practiced by the Raizen sugarcane plant. Even in a situation of imminent risk of contamination, the company did not stop its activities and subjected the workers, mostly indigenous Guarani and Kaiowá, to the risk of contracting Covid-19 and taking it to the villages. The government was omitted, since it did not supervise the company in relation to the failure to comply with the measures to prevent infection of the disease. Known for employing extensive indigenous labor, Raizen was responsible for the first cases of contamination of the Tey Kue Reserve, a place that had been identified as extremely risky, if there was contamination, due to the large number of indigenous people living in a tiny space. The first infected of the Reserve were just two indigenous workers of the plant. Since then, the cases have spread. At least 200 indigenous young people (from various regions of the state) were positive from their working relations at the Plant. In Tey Kue, over 2020, 223 indigenous people tested positive for Covid-19. Luckily, there was only one death, which could have been avoided, not so much the negligence of entrepreneurs and the government. The MPF has been notified and is triggering the power plant.
fb9e3ebd17ad59625954c6b9539eb678dd86bb8a: After non-compliance with the Federal Court judgment of October 2020, the MPF requested the blockade of R $ 600,000 of Funai, to ensure the monthly delivery of basic baskets and hygiene products to the indigenous communities of Pará, to assist in the fight against the Covid-19 pandemic. After 60 days of the court order, no measures had been taken by the federal government to deliver the material. Disobedience to the court order is reiterated. Funai had already given its ruling in the same case. Therefore, the MPF filed a request for provisional compliance with the sentence, with a blocking of the amount corresponding to the fine arbitrated by the Court in case of non-compliance, of R $ 10 thousand per day.
91eac7809d4515f03fe2e58f76a558584ca469ba: The DPU, in Belém, filed Civil Action for the conviction of the INSS for denying the granting of maternity pay to indigenous women under the age of 16, on the grounds that there is no minimum age to qualify as insured. The Justice granted the request to injunction arguing that, provided the quality of special insured, the period of absence and the birth of the child has been proven, the age limitation cannot be a hindrance to granting the benefit of the maternity salary. The indigenous peoples are awaiting compliance with the decision.
dd2b32d9978ea828ca96cca13bbd6aca560a4ac3: The MPF of Pará and the DPU made a joint recommendation to several agencies, due to the Venezuelan indigenous Warao who live in the municipality of Itaituba being subjected to unhealthy and degrading conditions, resulting from the lack of shelter and subsistence conditions that should be provided by the government. The Warao Indians are obliged to perform begging activities, which exposes them to the risk of contagion by the coronavirus, since they cannot comply with the essential sanitary measures. According to MPF and DPU, children, elderly and women are in marked vulnerability. In addition, the Warao Indians have no documentation or record, and there are even reports that some of them have had their documents collected by public authorities. The MPF recommended several emergency actions in favor of the Warao, to be carried out by the municipality of Itaituba and by the organs that integrate the Unified Social Assistance System (SUAS) and the Unified Health System (SUS).
77b44c933320c8c728474e63384f7a20e7609331: Indigenous peoples throughout Brazil denounce denial of rights by the INSS, especially with the refusal to accept documents issued by Funai. The DPU has filed Civil Action, with request for emergency protection, to force the INSS to take into account the documents sent by Funai and to ensure that, if the indigenous do not have all the documents necessary for granting the death pension, they are duly informed about the necessary procedures and can produce witness evidence. The MPF issued a favorable opinion to the action of the DPU in the process, which process in the Federal Court of Belém, arguing that the demands made by the INSS violate the rights guaranteed by the Federal Constitution, which recognizes the right of indigenous peoples not to be integrated or assimilated by the non-indigenous society. Thus, the administrative certificates issued by Funai do nothing more than attest “acts and facts referred to indigenous citizens in that document named, occurring within the indigenous communities”, cannot be ignored by the INSS, the MPF argues.
74b0afc0592e8254bdee16bc2365a43485900136: Due to the high flow of indigenous peoples Warao immigrating from Venezuela and arriving in the state of Pará, the DPU, the Public Defender of the State of Pará, the MPF, the municipality of Belém do Pará, the Papa João XXIII Foundation and the state of Pará entered with a Civil Public Action against the Federal Union to make available, immediately, an emergency shelter, temporary and suitable for the indigenous Warao in the capital of Para. The Federal Court accepted the request to force the Union to pass 20 thousand reais monthly to each group of 50 Venezuelan immigrants sheltered by action of the authors in Belém.
de8f67fed68a61205b18b5232a013eb7f1456b4d: Indians charge answers about the murder of 20-year-old Cristian Martins Peres. The young man, resident of the village Aty Mirim, was stabbed to death on 13 March. For chief Natalino, the delay in solving the case involves discrimination against the indigenous population. According to him, “when an Indian dies, it looks like a dog that was killed. You feel these things on your skin a lot. Total discrimination on the part of the judiciary. It is almost a month and everyone is quiet, nobody does anything”. The chief also reports that the police have neglected the demands for speed in solving the murder. The case is under the jurisdiction of the police station of São Miguel do Iguaçu. The Civil Police of Paraná reported that the police inquiry was finalized and forwarded to the prosecutor and to the judiciary. The unsub was indicted for murder, but he's still free.
81afa0a63bcfa4d9abb29cc2beda2454df72d53c: Leaderships denounced to the MPF, in Francisco Beltrão, the lack of drinking water and the interruption in the supply of basic baskets, in the middle of the pandemic of coronavirus, besides charging measures in the demarcation of their traditional territories. The lack of drinking water, aggravated by the drought that plagues the region, compromises the health and life of more than 35 families living in the village, mostly children and the elderly. The indigenous are drinking water directly from Lake Itaipu, without any treatment, contaminated by pesticides used by agribusiness in the region. Without regularization of their territory or access to basic sanitation, indigenous people are unable to cultivate gardens for their survival.
fe7d637c3b02bc932972ee5e4cfd56f197daea87: Indigenous people protested in the 178 kilometer of BR-423, demanding improvements in signaling, with the aim of avoiding accidents. Roads have occurred on site, which is dangerous and is close to the village. The leaders are concerned by the lack of security, especially for children and elderly of the Fulni-O people.
f59f51af8b4d4bad5ccb22dbae56ca9f8260a6bf: Faced with the death of Funai Rieli Franciscato's servant, coordinator of the Etnoenvironmental Protection Front Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, who on September 9, in the Seringueiras region, was struck by an arrow fired by isolated indigenous people, the MPF in Rondônia recommended measures to Funai and Sesai. In the recommendation, the MPF requested that the agencies provide sanitary and safety barriers on the lines giving access to IT in order to protect the isolated peoples of the Cautary River region. Invasions in the indigenous land have caused a change in the behavior of isolated groups, who are frightened and assisted by the ever closer presence of non-indigenous invaders. Funai did not position itself on whether or not to comply with the MPF recommendation.
33a6256185079eab4e5b574191848359536a76d6: The neglect in the maintenance and opening of the access road to the village Panorama leaves the community in a situation of vulnerability, especially in the rainy season and in this period of covid-19 pandemic, because the access by the river Jaci Paraná is very distant for cases of emergency health. The indigenous have already submitted several requests to the State Department of Roads of Rodage and Transport (DER), which during the summer period meets the various lines of Union Bandeirantes and, for political reasons, does not attend or maintain in the territory Karipuna. As an aggravating factor, the only ones using the road are organized crime people, for land grabbing and wood theft. Leaderships made a complaint document and sent it to the MPF and the DER, demanding measures.
66c030c04abd4fb52be1bb0de556ae8cb96c74e5: The Guarasugwe people, since 2012, have been demanding with Funai the issuance of the RANI document (Administrative Register of Indigenous Birth) of some indigenous peoples who do not have any kind of document. Children and adolescents are having difficulty accessing health and education rights due to lack of documents. The lack of the RANI, which must be dispatched by Funai, has prevented indigenous people from accessing and being registered in the Sesai system, to have the right to health. Despite numerous complaints filed at Funai in Brasilia (DF), the situation of denial of this right remains. Few people have been able to include the name of the people in the civil documents. Leaderships made complaint document, which was forwarded to the MPF, the 6th Federal Chamber and Funai of Brasilia.
72ad5073a18d159ab171e152b533598e9efded17: Leaderships denounce that they have long been fighting for immediate public policies in the areas of health and education. The people demand the urgent hiring of teachers and the construction of an appropriate artesian well in the community, because the lack of water generates much suffering and compromises the health of the population, especially in drought periods. Both the river that passes in the village and the artesian well dry completely, leaving the people in precarious conditions of survival. The situation worsens even more with regard to the generator engine, which presents frequent defects and stays longer in repair than in operation in the village. Leaderships and teachers prepared a complaint document and sent it to the MPF, asking for urgent measures.
b428c476d66218a93e60f6bf12b8d02029d10bcc: Leaderships denounce that many indigenous people are unable to receive retirement because there are no specialist doctors to sign reports or support from social workers to forward their processes. In addition, indigenous people also do not have transportation that allows them to move from the villages to the cities, so that they seek to speed up the situation with the responsible bodies.
b995a451512dd76a49e6f1fc57ecfed79106123f: A study published in the Covid Economics newsletter, from the Centre for Economic Policy Research, points out an association between deforestation, illegal mining and Covid-19 cases among indigenous populations in Brazil. The research cross-referenced data from Sesai and the National Institute of Space Research (Inpe), which monitors deforestation in the Amazon. Research results show that an increase in a deforestation unit per 100 km2 is associated, on average, with an increase of 2.4 to 5.5 new cases of Covid-19 daily in indigenous people, 14 days after deforestation. According to the sanitarian doctor Sofia Mendonça, from Unifesp, “in Yanomami, for example, everything indicates that one of the ways of introducing the virus into the villages was through prospectors and illegal mining (...), every time there is a conflict or there are issues in the territory, in the relationship with our society, this mirrors in health”. She warns that “has seen that all these threats to territories such as mining, invasions, deforestation, burnings, all of this added to the Covid-19, have a very great genocidal power.” The doctor still talks about the delay of public agencies such as Funai and Sesai in acting, which worsened the disease.
f13e7dad5475773b48e512691c2e479483c6fdda: Wai-Wai Indians protested in Boa Vista, holding two East Dsei ambulances in the community. The reason for the demonstration was because the East Dsei prevented the indigenous from watching and burying their relatives who died of Covid-19 according to their traditions and culture. Leaderships of the Indigenous Association stated that they had received approval from the MPF for the funeral, but the East Dsei did not follow the recommendation and buried the bodies in Boa Vista, 327 kilometers from IT. Regional coordinator of the region's tuxauas, Valdecir Wai Wai, reported that they only wanted to perform the funeral ritual so that the souls of their relatives could “rest in peace.” He also said that “no need to crowd, let’s not open the coffins. We just want to perform the ritual and pray with family members”. In a letter to the MPF, the Wai Wai said: “We have not been treated as human beings. Authorities have not respected our law, our culture, our mourning at the death of a loved one. We are suffering from institutional racism, because we cannot bury and lament the death of our relatives in a dignified way, according to our culture”. In another passage of the letter, they say: “As if the lack of medicines, qualified professionals, testing and proper care were not enough, neither are we heard! After dead, our relatives are buried away from us. To worsen our suffering in the face of pandemic and tragic death, we also suffer from racism”. Although the MPF issued a recommendation that the East Dsei guarantee the people the right to bury their relatives, respecting the protocols to prevent the spread of the virus, the transfer of the bodies to the community was denied.
53d9225ba6e9f162ed88bd2e865233c53e1ec46e: Since 2015, family groups of the indigenous peoples Warao, E’ñepa and Kariña have crossed the land border between Venezuela and Brazil, entering Roraima and later following other itineraries to other states of the country. In Roraima, where an approximate population of 1,300 indigenous peoples of these peoples is concentrated, most of them lived in 2020 in the two shelters managed by the Hosted Operation – Janokoida, in Pacaraima, and Pintolândia, in Boa Vista – and in the spontaneous occupation of Ka’ Ubanoko, in the city of Boa Vista. According to data from Operation Welcomed, in 2020, among the 13 shelters in Boa Vista to welcome migrants, the two indigenous shelters presented the worst conditions for coping with the Covid-19 pandemic and were categorized as “extreme risk”. Indigenous peoples in a migratory situation are not included within the specific and differentiated public policies and measures within the context of the indigenous policy of the State, despite being covered by Law 14,021 of October 7, 2020, which provides social protection measures to prevent the contagion and spread of Covid-19 in indigenous territories. Funai and Sesai do not operate systematically with these groups and do not play a relevant role in the articulation or coordination of measures adopted by other public authorities. Primary health care is done, with difficulties, within SUS health centers; in shelters or in Ka’ Ubanoko, much of the preventive action was under the care of civil society organizations. In 2020, despite the majority of indigenous people being within institutionalized shelters, no information was provided on the impact of Covid-19 among these groups in relation to confirmed cases of contagion or death. This contributes to the underreporting and invisibility of these peoples and makes it difficult for their situation to be effectively evaluated, so that specific and effective measures can be adopted. There is no state action framework with defined responsibilities for the government in the three spheres – Union, State and Municipalities – the care for this population and even the management of shelters are mainly under the responsibility of civil society organizations and international agencies, even within the sheltered Operation. The Army Task Force continues to coordinate the Operation and having the last word in all decisions, there is no coordinated and stable action plan involving the competent public bodies, whether in the field of health, education, housing or food security. In September 2020, the coordination of the Hosted Operation determined, without any consultation with the residents, the departure of the indigenous families from the spontaneous occupation of Ka’ Ubanoko – an abandoned public space where these families resided since March 2019 in a self-organized way – and their relocation into new institutionalized shelters, a measure rejected by the community that demanded to maintain the space of autonomy and social organization built in Ka’ Ubanoko. The mobilization of the community and the support of social organizations and the MPF allowed to reverse the period of one month initially given by Operation Welcome and carry out, between November and December, a process based on the right of indigenous peoples to prior, free and informed consultation. Although there are no conditions for the proper consultation process, as described in ILO Convention 169, the community has prepared a document with demands for protection and alternatives to institutionalized shelter. The Task Force, coordinator of the Hosted Operation, responded to the document stating that it could not meet these demands, omitting any initiative of articulation with other competent public bodies and reiterating as the only alternative the relocation in institutionalized shelter and exit from the site Ka’ Ubanoko. The Task Force thus maintained the psychological pressure on the community, which was warned about possible measures of forced vacancy by the state of Roraima.
54584fd9674a717b01fd6074ae9e38a8f842374b: Despite the conviction by the Federal Court and the five-day deadline, from September 8th, for the decision to be fulfilled, the Union and the South Interior Dsei did not solve the issue of insufficient electricity for the operation of the motorcycle pumps that supply water to TI Toldo Chimbangue. Prior to this condemnation, the MPF had already made several petitions, requiring urgency in the restoration of water supply to the indigenous. The situation worsens even more in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic, whose risk of transmission is aggravated by the lack of conditions for adequate hygiene of people and residences.
77414f4aabfde063fe305f6d739c126a21b1b0f0: During the Covid-19 pandemic, in several villages the government, in the municipal, state and federal spheres, abandoned the supply of the basic survival needs of the indigenous. Not even basic baskets were provided to suit everyone. The baskets that arrived were insufficient and without monthly planning; the supply could occur or not, leading the community to total food insecurity. If it were not for the donations of the Church, volunteers and other organizations, the indigenous people would have been very hungry and even died, as one of the leaders said. The funding for the maintenance of the activities of the Seai de Araquari did not meet the demands of the demand, requiring food transport campaigns from Joinville to Sesai, for hygiene and distribution in the villages. Sesai's cars needed repairs and there was no resources for it. A collective effort was needed by indigenous leaders, agents of the Social Pastorals and civil society organizations, who provided basic baskets and donations of hygiene, cleaning and other materials, such as mattresses and equipment for the isolation houses built by Funai, who did not have the minimum conditions to welcome sick people.
db15b04ad44b74948dcee545961ae09f23977d4c: Complaint made by the indigenous peoples to the MPF reports the poor state of conservation of the vicinal roads that connect the indigenous land to the state highways. The leaders report that for more than four years they denounce the precariousness of the roads, which compromises the displacement of the indigenous. They are isolated and at risk even if they need to leave their villages in emergency situations. According to the complaint, only one stretch of a road is in better condition, because the farmers themselves performed conservation services, aiming at the disposal of their productions to the city. The MPF held meetings with those involved, seeking the signature of a conduct adjustment term for the restoration of the vicinal roads.
7381d7594849cb69f56c07e68c6867de3b933e24: Leaderships report that the main road of the rural area that gives access to the Krahô IT in Goiatins, 468 km from Palmas, in the northeast of the state, is infegable and leaves residents of the site and isolated villages. The road starts from inside the village Alto Lindo. In response to the requests made by the indigenous people, the city claimed that it could not do maintenance, due to the fact that the only existing machine would be broken, and that there was no date to maintain the road. The case was reported to the MPF, the responsible bodies and the city.
801af16e4fb7a6de07683dc4bbfbe295b13b3926: The Akroá-Gamella people suffer from the lack of indigenous education policy in their territory. Children are forced to attend municipal schools that do not have the specificity of indigenous school education and differentiated political pedagogical project, contemplating the culture and way of life of the indigenous people, as recommended by the legislation. Children have to move to schools in neighboring villages, where they suffer prejudice and discrimination from the local non-indigenous population.
28aee9b9ec0cd65951b212479e4da9657266a8c0: The Municipal Department of Education of Lábrea tried several times to start the school year in the villages during the pandemic of the new coronavirus. In July, the secretary and several teachers visited villages on the Purus River to “consult” the indigenous about the return of classes. According to the secretariat, the indigenous people were in favor of the beginning of the school year. However, the secretariat did not inform Funai – CR MPur and DSEI – MRP about such action, since Ordinance No. 419 of the Presidency of Funai does not allow non-indigenous people to enter IT for services that are not essential during the pandemic of the new coronavirus. He also did not present minutes of meetings and the methodology he used for the consultation, leaving doubts whether this was carried out in accordance with the legislation; it is not known if all sanitary measures were adopted to not take the new coronavirus to the villages (quarantine compliance, use of protective equipment and testing of all before entering the territories). In addition, it is worth highlighting the irregularity in teachers' contracts, because the secretariat claimed that they would only receive their salaries if there was the beginning of classes, using this argument as a form of pressure for indigenous teachers to be in favor of the beginning of the school year. It is worth noting that the professionals had not received for months. The secretary resisted and did not want to hire teachers who refused to enter the area during the pandemic. The indigenous organization Focimp forwarded a complaint to the MPF and triggered Funai and DSEI in the face of non-compliance with security protocols by the secretariat, and SEMEC postponed the beginning of the school year. The teachers then received only the payment for the 5 months that should be in the area, but they did not receive the retroactive value at the late months.
fc0dad85a702935ede0e6252cf3081165e5afac1: Leaderships denounce the poor physical and structural conditions of the building where the school works in the village, where they study more than 600 indigenous students. The building has broken tiles and windows, exposed wiring, damaged fans and chairs, damaged bathrooms, compromising the safety and well-being of children and adolescents who study there. The leaders have charged provisions from the State Department of Education, but have not received a positive response. Given this, the community decided to paralyze the classes for fear that the students would suffer some accident due to the lack of safety of the site.
e448976b06dd553a4b899f87cb2915bf747a48fa: Educators face bad road and river access conditions to deliver handouts to indigenous students from the Figueirinhas community, which is on the banks of the Pisces River. The situation was further aggravated due to the pandemic of the coronavirus. The village has no internet connection, no fixed or mobile telephony.
ee0a18108a712123777069a68b74b6c22c351afc: Leaderships denounce disregard of the State Secretariat of Education of Mato Grosso and the Indigenous School Education Center for the community. They report that for almost 30 years they have claimed the construction of a school in the village, but so far the neglect is total. As classrooms are used the old homes of community families who moved to other villages. The spaces are inadequate, without dignified infrastructure. The cultural aspect of the people has also been disrespected by the State, since the deceased families are buried inside the houses, thus constituting sacred spaces for the indigenous, which should not be used as classrooms. Many students are leaving communities to study in cities and families are apprehensive. A document was drawn up denouncing the situation of negligence, neglect and disrespect of Seduc to the MPF, in which the people demand compliance with their rights.
5fed14b2c0ff1b773837ca2ae901ba72c7994feb: Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, classrooms were suspended in all schools in the state of Mato Grosso, in March. However, in the second semester, the State Department of Education (Seduc-MT) demanded that indigenous schools develop a strategic plan for the resumption of classes, which could be by remote teaching. Given the difficulties and the fact that many schools and students do not have networks and access to the Internet, Seduc proposed that the teaching should be through handouts prepared by non-indigenous people, in Portuguese, ignoring the different sociocultural contexts and the diversity of languages spoken by each people. There were threats of resignation and non-renewal of teachers' contracts that did not comply. The attitude of Seduc-MT hurts the right of indigenous schools to work from their sociocultural realities and the use of their own languages in the learning process. Another complex situation occurred Many people have claimed for years the construction of a school in its Disability in education adds to and aggravates the omission of the State and in cases such as that of the Tapi’itãwa State Indigenous School and other indigenous schools, which were used as sites for the isolation of severe patients and therefore unable to receive teachers and students. Indigenous teachers and indigenous managers discussed the issue through a Whatsapp group. The indigenous members of the Indigenous School Education Council (CEEI) in Mato Grosso also debated and questioned the attitude of Seduc-MT. Cimi Mato Grosso made a Note in this regard, sent to SEDUC MT on August 24. Funai also made a Technical Note, forwarded with Office to Seduc-MT. Even with all the movement and protests, there were no changes by the secretariat, which continued to guide the application of handouts prepared in a massive way to all indigenous schools in the state.
fc1fc4008db2f9de8a217ae2623fa865c8818e2b: The Tapiparanytãwa village has an attached room of the Tapi’itãwa State Indigenous School to meet the demand of four classes of early childhood and elementary school students. The municipal government, however, built only one classroom to attend the various classes of students. Since 2019, due to the lack of adequate space, a class has studied in the school corridor, in precarious conditions. The direction of the Tapi’itãwa State Indigenous School has already forwarded, several times, requests for the construction of another classroom, Photo: Guilherme Cavalli/Cimi the villages, but are not attended. to regulate the indigenous territories both to the State Department of Education (Seduc-MT) and to the Municipality of Confresa. The school's management team was in Cuiabá last year at the meeting of directors, when they delivered a document to Seduc-MT claiming the new classroom for this village. To date, no provision has been made, both by the state department and by the Municipality of Confresa.
f12674d9cd24d50d06883f87e146a8ec86ab4bfe: The Munduruku have long claimed the reform of the José Arlindo Betcel School. However, only in 2020, the City Hall and Municipal Education Secretariat decided to make the reform, in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic. On April 13, the Munduruku Indigenous Council of the Plateau sent a complaint to the MPF about the execution of the works in the village Ipaupixuna, which was increasing the flow of workers between the city and the village and accentuating the risks of contamination of the indigenous by Covid-19. The MPF forwarded action to the Federal Justice, requiring that of the municipality of Santarém the immediate suspension of school reform works, due to the serious period of contamination risk for the indigenous. The agency pointed out that on May 5, an elderly Munduruku had died in the village Ipaupixuna and required the municipality to continue the works as soon as the pandemic or the period of greater social isolation was closed.
a63e24db9f4aef9702c662ecb78b332a25c2ac4d: The MPF moved Public Civil Action to charge government provisions with the Munduruku people, with regard to the performance of surveys in school buildings, the functioning of schools, the hiring of appropriate professionals, the structure of equipment and the provision of quality school meals and high nutritional value, according to the eating habits of indigenous populations. It also charged the National Education Development Fund to supervise the transfers to the Itaituba Prefecture directed to indigenous education in the villages Dace Watpu, Boa-Fé, Sawré Muybu and Sawré Aboy. The Federal Court has granted all the proposals of the action of the MPF.
9fad2a20df74f6d62ce36b1a1ee7e55be3ca30e1: With a view to preventing and repressing fraud in quota systems in vestibulars, competitions and public offices, there are federal, state and municipal laws, and also the Recommendation of no. 41/2016, of the National Council of the Public Ministry. However, the Federal Institute of Education, Science and Technology of Pará (IFPA), by means of a letter, claimed not to have instituted the Committee of Validation of Self-Declaration Racial or Verification Banks and Analysis of color/ethnic self-declared by candidates of selection process to enter their technical courses of secondary or higher graduation level. Therefore, the MPF made a direct recommendation to IFPA, requesting various measures to ensure that the indigenous peoples of Pará have their rights to the quota system.
7f623010085e5b5a72f55048936d49f243da0752: Leaders asked the MPF to intercede with the State Department of Education to build a school within the Tekoá Tajy Poty and Ywyraty Porã, and held the expansion of the school of Tekoá Jevy, since there are almost 250 children who have to move from the village to study in the city. In this case of the expansion, the State Secretariat has the funds, but the city refuses to do the earthing of the land.
fd67e324cb55975b899c00c27e29b01658a9dc87: Leaderships denounce that for years they have been calling for the construction of a school within the village. They report that the only school there is on site works in a room in the house of the chief, which was even burned down in 2018. Since then, indigenous students continue to study in this precarious space. The whole community has been striving to maintain school education, but there is no support from the State Department of Education to comply with constitutional laws, the construction of an equipped school, necessary infrastructure, the provision of school meals and the hiring of teachers. Leaderships have already met with the 12th Regional Coordination of Education, which said that the school would be a priority of the state government, but so far, nothing has been fulfilled.
2fd24530f6ee4364dc4e5fab6d5b16f4f947cb68: The indigenous community denounces the neglect and desistence to which it is always subjected and now, even more, is being harmed due to the difficulties of access faced by teachers to reach the villages to the villages. Professor Keila, quoted in the complaint, is obliged to cross a river swimming to get to school. Every day, the teacher puts her belongings inside a plastic bag and crosses the river. The Indians report that this has happened as a result of a bridge that was broken by a truck belonging to a lumber yard.
452473868915145c13347ad4a34ce74dac547635: Earlier this year, the Puruborá people were surprised by the authoritarian attitude of the State Department of Education (CRE/Seduc/RO), in the municipality of São Francisco do Guaporé. Without dialogue with the community, the Secretariat decided to close the school and redistribute students, teachers and employees in schools in the cities of Seringueira and São Francisco do Guaporé, with an aggravating factor in relation to indigenous knowledge/teacher of the mother tongue, with a change of function, and other employees. The people felt disrespected and discriminated against by the State Department of Education and denounced the arbitrariness to the MPF, through a document. A meeting was also held with the Secretary of State for Education, with the participation of his advisors, the Coordinator of the Indigenous School Education Center/Seduc, the Teaching Manager/Seduc, the chief of the Puruborá people and the teacher of the mother tongue, as well as representatives and the legal advisor of Cimi. It was required that the school be reopened and that the differentiated Indigenous Education be continued.
109ba1032059a6c2d569fd18a24fdcad29bd175a: Leaders denounce that the State Department of Education - CRE/Seduc/RO, in the municipality of São Francisco do Guaporé, is not providing school transportation for indigenous students, who live in nearby farms, to move to the village school. They claim that even having school in the village, indigenous students have been taken to city schools. They report that the bus that takes indigenous students to the city school could take the students who live in the nearby farms and take them to the indigenous school. The leaders assess that the intention of the secretariat is to reduce the number of students in the village to end up closing the indigenous school, as they did in the village Aperoi/Puruborá. They also say that the secretary has already removed high school from the village and is now wanting to reduce the number of students, which will eventually lead to the closure of the indigenous school. The leaders denounced the case to the MPF, demanding measures with the State Department of Education and charging the return of high school in the villages, transportation for the displacement of students to the indigenous school, dialogue and respect for the community.
3bceb9c1b1b5a3ae475a2058f91c47866839762b: Leaderships denounce the cutting of scholarships by the Ministry of Education of indigenous students of the Federal University of Roraima (UFRR). They report that, in the middle of the pandemic, young people, who live in a situation of vulnerability, had their scholarships, worth R $ 900.00, cut. Aids from the Indigenous Collective Health Management course of the Insikiran Institute of Indigenous Higher Education were suspended when classes were no longer held in person.
92778ef838565ee643729c5bccd2c943334f3ad0: The indigenous people of Roraima, after more than 30 years of denouncing the omission and negligence of the federal and state government in relation to indigenous school education, decided to act on their own. In indigenous territories throughout the state of Roraima, schools are improvised in barracks built by residents or in rooms at the health centers of the villages. Most are working on large open malocas, no walls. The lack of structure of schools hinders the concentration of students and prevents the operation during periods of rain. Schools located in community centers are exposed to the noise of machines, mowers, tractors and other everyday disorders. In addition to the rains and external noise, students still suffer from the pests that affect the communities annually, such as the insects pium, carapapanã and maruim, very common in the region. Many of these schools do not receive school meals or have canteens, materials and textbooks. Faced with the chaotic situation, which has lasted for decades, the indigenous families Wapixana, Makuxi, and others decided to join and build a school worthy of their children, which is ongoing and should be ready by the end of the year. The Association of Indigenous Peoples of Roraima continues to denounce the neglect and await compliance with the obligations of public agencies.
eccabfe15be10562b2cacf8e933e09d7eb8f288a: There is a project to build school buildings in the villages Piraí, Tarumã, Morro Alto and Conquista, which has been conducted in the Ministry of Education since 2014 and has already been approved. The State Department of Education of Santa Catarina tries to implement it, but does not go ahead, because the Demarcation Boards are suspended and because there is a strong pressure from the Association of Property Owners and Interested in the municipalities of Araquari and North and Northeast of Santa Catarina, intended for Indigenous Settlement. This association was created by the Municipal Council of Araquari, through the Municipal Ordinary Law no 0014/2009. There was also difficulty of the mayors to grant the permits, and, after they were released and too long, a teacher informed that they had won and needed to be renewed. There are promises that the buildings claimed in the project will be built to the Ministry of Education, but the works are not taking place. Another situation of violation of rights faced by the indigenous is the denial of access to early childhood education by the municipalities Araquari and São Francisco do Sul. Only the Conquista village, in the municipality of Barra do Sul, has this type of education, but lacks adequate physical space. Other schools lack equipment in classrooms, such as desks and desks for teachers, appropriate tables, computers, internet and cooking materials, among others. Teachers also complain about the lack of teaching and pedagogical materials. Another serious situation is lack of lunch; when there is, it is little and arrives late.
022db4e1b1ddc50bd72fa32990c4fbb68d5d63de: Leadership reports that the Indigenous Student House has been invaded by thieves. The crime happened when the students were in the villages, on school holidays. The house was broken into and the bandits took everything inside: appliances, computer, clothes, power generator, television, among others. The indigenous, who study at the Federal University of Tocantins (UFT), report that they had already asked Funai for measures, informing that the house needed reforms and emergency works and that it did not offer security to more than 26 residents, including children. The MPF had filed an action at the end of the previous year forcing Funai to carry out the reforms, but so far nothing had been done.
17cb1bf51ee04dcb62d6bc30c1db853549c5a061: Leaderships have been denouncing, for months, the poor state of conservation of the House of the Indigenous Student of Araguaína, where 26 people reside, among these, 06 children. The house is in ruins, features cracks, leaks, broken tiles and threatening roof collapse on the indigenous. On the day 04/11, the Federal Court determined that the Union and Funai carry out emergency works of renovation or construction in the house, within 90 days. Students should be housed elsewhere safer. The indigenous people are waiting to comply with the decision.
43144d6daed9c518da91031bdf56fd92b7ec5ce8: The school was built in 2003 and delivered to the community without completion of the works, without any comfort for the students. The school attends the first year of elementary school to high school. Since then, the community has been filing documents and denouncing the precariousness of the school. In August 2020, community leaders went to the MPF of Araguaína to file another document, with photos showing the disregard of the Education Secretariat. So far, the community has received no response from the responsible bodies.
f23376b83c59a82023b9e10f2ad0583bfd4b7115: Since 2012, Araguaína university students have been claiming with Funai and denouncing to the MPF the need for reform in the home of students in Araguaína. There are approximately 30 students living in the house, who find themselves without any structure, falling roof, broken windows, fallen wall and many other damages that have been occurring by time and by lack of conservation and reform. The situation is so precarious that young students are at risk of staying under the roof of the house. In 2020, the situation worsened. Due to the pandemic, the students had to return to their villages, and the house was abandoned, susceptible to further destruction. Complaints were made to Funai and the MPF, but without provision.
55a2d46e8e89b07c3c557287d41e471eb1b2e212: With the absence of indigenous peoples in the House of Students of Araguaína, due to the pandemic of the coronavirus, and also due to the lack of surveillance by public agencies, the house was depredated. In September 2020, a criminal fire occurred; the material goods the indigenous had left in the house were burned and the structure of the building was compromised. Contact was made with Funai de Araguaína and a police report. The MPF of Araguaína determined that Funai will reform the House of Students, under penalty of daily fine.
bc721140df0b456c42f1d1758455db62264e6932: Leaderships denounce that the death of elders by Covid-19, in addition to all affective, cultural, and traditional loss, still threatens indigenous languages of the peoples of Brazil. The pandemic leaves the situation of indigenous peoples, which is already precarious, even more serious. The Covid-19 takes the lives of elders who are considered the guardians of maternal languages, forces the isolation of community members, prevents cultural rituals that keep languages alive and impairs their preservation. The omission and negligence of the federal government are factors responsible for the tragedy that has occurred among indigenous peoples, for the lack of prevention, care and control of the pandemic.
89aa719a3a92bae1dfc976912cfd342c8c736c28: According to the report “Our fight is for life: Covid-19 and indigenous peoples”, released by Apib at the end of the year, more than 41,000 indigenous peoples had been contaminated by the coronavirus, affecting more than half of the 305 indigenous peoples living in Brazil and leading 880 lives by November 2020. The report explains that the data systematized by the National Committee for Indigenous Life and Memory, created by Apib, its basic organizations and partners, are higher than the official data of Sesai, which does not record cases of indigenous people living in an urban context. Many indigenous peoples in an urban context, according to the report, are also identified as “pardos” in the news of health systems, which Apib denounces as “an expression of institutional racism”. According to the indigenous organization, the initiative to monitor independently of the Covid-19 cases among the native peoples “was motivated by the recognition that the official numbers of the Sesai did not represent all the cases of indigenous peoples infected and killed by the Covid-19. To mention one of the most evident aspects of data production and discrepancy, the cases of Covid-19 in indigenous people living in urban areas or in indigenous lands not yet approved, not attended by the Subsystem, do not appear in the statistics generated by Sesai”.
159f8b7200f16b15e9e017a0ea8de33d4aa185c4: The vaccination plan against coronavirus presented by the Ministry of Health excluded more than half of the indigenous population in the country by establishing priority groups. The last census conducted by IBGE, 10 years ago, pointed out 896.917 indigenous people, but the indigenous movement considers that today the indigenous population in Brazil exceeds much of 1 million inhabitants. The plan produced by the Ministry of Health said that it would meet only indigenous people living in indigenous lands and not those living in cities in the priority phase. The strategy of restricting indigenous people to what the government has called “villages” – an expression used by government structures during the military dictatorship – is the same used by the government to consider a smaller number of indigenous people infected and killed during the pandemic of the new coronavirus. As the Sesai uses more limited numbers, there is a great divergence between its balance sheet and the numbers raised by the indigenous movement. According to the Sanitarian doctor of Fiocruz, Ana Lúcia Pontes, an indigenous health specialist, indigenous vulnerability is found in different contexts, in the villages and also in the outskirts of the cities. She mentioned a study coordinated by the Federal University of Pelotas, published in July, which revealed that the prevalence of coronavirus among the urban indigenous population is 5.4%, much higher than that found in the white population, which is 1.1%. According to the doctor, the pandemic showed that the prevalence of covid in the indigenous population living in urban areas is much higher.
d212f1a0b82bae8bbf96a474a002b2baeed2eaf6: Since the beginning of the pandemic until the end of the year, the federal government has not implemented the policy of protecting indigenous peoples against Covid-19, which has in the formation of sanitary barriers one of the most effective methods to prevent the entry of diseases into the villages. Even with the pressure of civil society and the determinations of the Supreme Court, the contingency plan did not come out of the role. On the contrary: when indigenous peoples throughout Brazil began to organize, autonomously, barriers to control the entry and circulation of people into their territories, Funai issued an alert, stating that “indigenous people should not block roads during the pandemic.” Months later, in December, when the STF requested, under ADPF 709, information on the fight against pandemic among indigenous peoples, Funai began to ask indigenous peoples for images of the barriers they had previously contraindicated, to send to the STF as if they were the result of their action. “The indigenous movement mobilized to assume the role of the State in the face of its inefficiency. Without having supported the peoples at any time, Funai now wants to appropriate this mobilization through the legal action requiring protection measures from the Union, which fosters health barriers. It was not the initiative of the State at any time”, criticized the legal advisor of Apib, Dinamã Tuxá. In many cases, barriers built by indigenous communities, without State support, were violated or attacked by military police, as occurred in the Xakriabá territory, in Minas Gerais. The barriers implemented months after the start of the pandemic were gradually disappearing, as occurred in the Rio Branco IT, located in Rondônia, annexed to the Massaco IT, where isolated indigenous people live; the barrier was started in June and in October was undone. At the end of the barrier, Covid-19's cases began to escalate. Edmar Aruá, indigenous to Marco village, located in Rio Branco IT, states that there was no support from the responsible institutions. “We didn’t have the leg to maintain the barrier, they didn’t give the necessary support, we had to take on almost everything alone and it got difficult. I believe that almost 50% of the population has already taken the coronavirus. Fishermen and their own staff began to circulate with greater intensity at the end of the year and without monitoring. In December, we started having cases of covid in the reserve ", reported the indigenous. Also within the scope of ADPF 709, the RMP informed in December that the determination of the STF to the government, that barriers would be installed in the ITs Alto Rio Negro (AM), Enawenê-Nawê (MT) and Vale do Javari (AM), considered priority, was abandoned. The government did not verify the application of the measure in these areas and only reported that a “mobile base” with river patrol made up the barrier at IT Alto Rio Negro. In the south of the country, indigenous peoples published a letter denouncing that half of the barriers contained in the Funai report as active did not exist. In Mato Grosso, the indigenous people of the Bororo people of Barra do Garças and General Carneiro were also without barriers. The AGU recognized that the territories of isolated or indigenous people of recent contact of Alto Rio Negro (AM), Alto Turiaçú (MA), Avá-Canoeiro (GO), Enawane Nawê (MT), Juma (AM), Kaxinawá do Rio Humaitá (AC), Mamoate (AC) and Pirahã (AM) also did not have sanitary protection barriers.
03bbff514b8dad71920788ab3ebcbd7bc63338d0: Lack of contingency plan against Covid-19
4981520d8b2f06c1213462a4d55befc4651bbd56: Leaderships denounce that the Pankariri community, which has been in an area resumed for five years, at Fazenda São Bento, awaiting regularization of the territory Kariri-Xocó, has not been included in vaccination campaigns. According to Chief José Raimundo, children and the elderly have had their rights to health care and vaccination (gripe, measles and other diseases) denied by Sesai, for being in a resumption area. The leaders denounced to the MPF the denial of these rights in the middle of the coronavirus pandemic. A video conference was scheduled by the MPF, so that Funai and Sesai could explain the lack of assistance to the community, but the indigenous could not participate, due to the difficulty of access to the internet. The MPF would reschedule the meeting so that everyone could participate and remedy the problem, but so far this has not been accomplished.
9eabb7468954c1aa1959f7a1a54df2fae1b8c870: Indigenous people denounced to the MPF the occurrence of malaria outbreaks in indigenous villages. Leaderships report that outbreaks are caused by invasions of prospectors and increased deforestation in the territory. The MPF recommended to Sesai and DSEI that they provide sufficient specific drugs for the treatment of malaria, as well as the implementation of effective actions to prevent and eradicate malaria vectors. In addition, the agency requires the assistance by a multidisciplinary team in indigenous communities and also the availability of kits to perform tests of the disease.
656e8305a3a94af5359cab466f2383589fea484a: Leaderships of the Coordination of Indigenous Organizations of the Brazilian Amazon - Coiab report that the numbers of cases and deaths of indigenous peoples by Covid-19 in Amazonas, made available by the Amazon Health Surveillance Foundation - FVS, differ in much of those accounted for by Coiab. According to the leaders, this is because the Ministry of Health only accounts for the cases of indigenous villagers. Indigenous people in an urban context are not notified and often not attended, so they are not counted.
f89d659cab56a6ca6210bda3169fa1ae80abe90f: 115 Amazonian institutions and all regions of Brazil, among them Cimi, expressed concern about possible spread of the Covid-19 pandemic and charge emergency actions of the federal government. Historically vulnerable to attacks, violence, diseases and hostages of a precarious structure of health services, especially due to the current disassembly of social protection structures, the more than 800,000 indigenous people in Brazil are one of the weakest links in coping with the virus. The manifesto published by the National Forum Permanent in Amazon Defense required immediate measures of prevention and health care, masks, hygiene kits and rapid tests for virus detection. The institutions also demanded, for the most distant and difficult-to-access areas, equipment for existing hospital boats and the installation of new boats in assisted areas. Another concern expressed was regarding food, since the people contacted were instructed to stay on their land. The manifesto also requested the sending of basic baskets to more vulnerable families in order to avoid displacement. The institutions requested immediate action by the federal government, due to the potential of infection and transmission of the virus, associated with the lack of medical care and necessary inputs.
46282d2089296d90b1b4bd02e370723ca3146052: Leaderships of various indigenous peoples of the Amazon, among them Mura, Tucano, Baré and Murutinga, denounced and made demonstrations in the capital, claiming improvements in the area of health and the exchange of the head of the Indigenous Health District of Manaus. People denounced the neglect and lack of professional care of quality, lack of structure, medicine, equipment, technical support and transportation for medical care.
97235c22e0d5280c5cad5d6a03690d88f6712e3a: The Tson wük Dyapah people, of recent contact with a population of 46 people, were hit by the coronavirus. One adult and two children tested positive for Covid-19, according to information from the Kanamari Javari Valley Association - Akavaja. Due to lack of communication and due to distances, indigenous organizations took days to confirm patients and provide medicines and medical care. The first case was confirmed by Sesai on October 22. The nearest municipality to the village Jarinal is Eirunepé, which is 40 minutes by helicopter; on foot are 25 kilometers and by boat are three days by trip. In addition to contamination by the coronavirus, this recent group and the other peoples of the region live under threat from invaders, illegal prospectors, who have already been denounced to the government.
e7e0a9eabd480222df8b2a6b6a14e84ecef0292c: The advance of the coronavirus among indigenous peoples of Amazonas occurred in an impactful way. On December 14, the number of indigenous people infected by the coronavirus in Amazonas reached 19,134, according to data from Sesai and the Amazon Health Surveillance Foundation (FVS-AM), who also reported the death of 267 indigenous people in the state. The data of the disease among indigenous peoples of the state are separated between the “salted” and “non-salted”, division widely criticized by the indigenous movement and indigenous entities. Cases among “non-aldeates” are included in the information system, filled in the category race and color, of the municipal health departments. On the other hand, the number of indigenous people “salted” with Covid-19 is raised by Sesai, according to notifications by the DSEIs, units of the Subsystem of Indigenous Health Care (Sasi), belonging to the SUS. Despite official data, indigenous organizations indicate that there are underreporting and that the numbers were even higher. Indigenous people also highlight concern with contamination in the Javari Valley region, where there is a greater concentration of indigenous people in a situation of voluntary isolation. Among indigenous people living in indigenous lands, 6,897 cases and 86 deaths have been recorded to date. Among the indigenous peoples in urban context, the number was much higher, with 12,237 registered cases, 456 indigenous hospitalized until that moment and 181 deaths. São Gabriel da Cachoeira was the municipality of Amazonas that concentrated the largest number of cases and deaths among indigenous people in urban context in the period, with 3,812 cases of infection and 57 deaths by the disease, according to official data. Leaderships point out disregard of the Brazilian state in the conduct of the pandemic.
08a58bb8b8a4ece0ae4bed1ce929662ae54f12eb: With the overwhelming arrival of the Covid-19 among the indigenous peoples of Amazonas, and with the availability of emergency aid by the federal government, the MPF sparked public civil action demanding measures of care and preservation of the health of the indigenous. The action was received by the Federal Regional Court – TRF-1 on May 8. The measures were: distribution of basic baskets; extension of the deadline for looting emergency aid; social and social benefits, as well as possibility of access to direct benefits in the villages; adequacy of the Caixa application for granting the benefit, in order for the indigenous to remain in the villages and avoid commuting to urban centers and consequent agglomerations. The Union failed to comply with the decision and the TRF-1 issued a new decision on June 16, with a deadline of 24 hours for the delivery of the basic baskets, providing a fine of R $ 100,000, if not fulfilled. According to the MPF, the second decision was not fulfilled either.
f30caeb34cc90eb485a2b99d6d5dc63bde0c932b: The Matis-Aima Indigenous Association reported, in a public note, that in November the first six cases of Covid-19 were recorded among indigenous peoples of the Kudaya and Tawaya villages. ec1f7565a7fb80452698d709168af7a522d1723c: According to data from the Amazon Health Surveillance Foundation - FVS-AM, until the beginning of December 2020, the number of infected almost tripled in the Lower Amazon region. 8efbd349bc678a7ac3cd05a12086c622e08f04f6: Indigenous people denounce the lack of drinking water in the Alto Solimões region. In total, between 30% and 40% of the population of the 245 villages of the region lives in these conditions, according to the coordinator of the DSEI. In one of them this occurs, but it is a work that needs more planning and resources. For those villages without any water supply, the alternative is to use rainwater (which is constant in the region). Sesai provides sodium hypochlorite for each to put in its water, treating it before drinking. Weydson Pereira, from DSEI Alto Rio Solimões, states that the lack of drinking water supply is the largest bottleneck in the region. According to him, the Sesai would open bidding, later that month, to acquire a drill to open wells in smaller villages, of up to 400 people. In the larger villages, more complex works are needed, with studies and hiring a company. The goal, he said, would be to drill wells in 24 villages the following year.
ccc910b90f032e25117d2b84db47091db52676df: In a letter sent to Sesai, the MPF, DSEI/VJ, Funai and Condisi at the end of December, the Association of Kanamari of the Javari Valley (Akavaja) denounced the lack of health care for indigenous peoples in the region of the Itacoai River gutter, and requested urgent measures. b47fab39026bfac2f1d83f21527e036fab963ece: This year the pandemic exposed all the deficiencies of indigenous health in the undemarcated lands of Barcelos (TI Baixo Rio Negro I and III) and the weaknesses to which the indigenous peoples of the region are exposed. 2474698a12f6f22fd1a861aaf435afaac09dd80f: During the months of May and June 2020, organizations Movement of the General Cacicado Patriarchate of the Kokama Indigenous People of Brazil (MPKK), Indigenous Federation of the Kukami-Kukamiria People From Brazil, Peru and Colombia (TWRK) and General Organization of Chiefs of the Indigenous Communities of the Kokama People (OGCCIPK), all of them organizations Kokama from the Alto Solimões region delivered several documents to the public agencies Sesai, Funai and MPF/TBT on the neglect and omission of the government in the approach of the pandemic in the region, especially regarding the care of indigenous people living in the city and discrimination when they were considered “pards” in the records of deaths granted by the Military Hospital of Tabatinga. 9bb27659894755d1c16c891a2e69a4ddb6731399: The young indigenous woman, aged 26 and pregnant at 38 weeks, had problems during pregnancy and sought care at the José Abreu Luz Regional Hospital in São Félix do Araguaia. 96a2e2c2716a079464f0eea4d08dcaf34af95cd5: The Xavante people are one of the most vulnerable and most affected indigenous peoples by the Covid-19. Retinal tests of 157 were performed. Xavante before the new coronavirus pandemic and the results showed that 60.5% have a high prevalence of type 2 diabetes and ophthalmologic dysfunction caused by the disease, which can lead to blindness. a73500dfac850140524aaf574f486badde38f2af: The very serious fires that occurred in the region, in addition to all environmental destruction, forests, flora, fauna, means of survival of communities, also led dozens of indigenous people to serious respiratory and pulmonary diseases. ac281edad5fb84525d5079f5a9538653b9e199b4: Leaderships of the peoples Sabanê, Manduca, Idalamarê and others that inhabit the IT Pyrenees de Souza denounced lack of service and infrastructure by Sesai regarding the construction of laundries with tanks and baths worthy of the families of the communities. df5d2b98936dec042c9c7e67bf95ebd4cb2a2d35: During the coronavirus pandemic, a structure was set up at the school of Tapi’itãwa village to receive people affected by the disease and who needed isolation. 4c4d8679aae8da71e3e4fcaa02736fc0a2079e73: According to data from Sesai, by December 14, 3,043 indigenous people had been infected and 73 had died due to coronavirus in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul. 70d0bcad8c7f7dfbe8c2b70b169141c1ea8c6155: Both the Sesai and the State Health Departments and the municipalities presented a very deficient policy regarding prevention, identification and care in relation to the Covid-19 epidemic. 63cf41179ead67cc7c564df370738ab6604d4478: A study produced by the doctor João Paulo Botelho Vieira Filho, a professor at Escola Paulista de Medicina - Unifesp, at the request of the Indigenous Associations Xikrin, Pokerô, Kakarekré and Baypran, denounces the serious health risks experienced by indigenous populations that consume fish and water polluted by the activity of mining projects of Vale SA, such as the Onça-Puma power plant, nickel exploration, and the S11D mine, which exploits iron. 8aae1c177d2760efc47e46b0235c3e1491adc8fe: A study conducted by Fiocruz in partnership with WWF-Brasil, at the request of the Pariri Indigenous Association, investigated mercury contamination among indigenous peoples Munduruku of the middle Tapajós region, in Pará. The survey analyzed the situation of three villages of the IT Sawré Muybu over a year. The results indicated that all research participants were affected by the use of mercury in mining activity in and around the indigenous land. About 57.9% of participants had mercury levels well above the maximum safety limit established by health agencies. The communities most affected are those near the banks of the affected rivers. In the village on the banks of the Jamaxim River, nine out of ten residents had high mercury rates. Mercury poisoning can cause respiratory, renal, and mainly attack the nervous system. Children under five years of age underwent neurodevelopment tests; 16% presented motor coordination and speech problems. An 11-month-old baby had mercury levels three times the tolerable. According to researchers from Fiocruz, contamination is related to the advance of illegal mining in the lands of the Munduruku people, because mercury is used in clandestine gold extraction and then dumped into the rivers of the region. All 88 fish caught for the study, which are an important part of the Munduruku people's food base, were contaminated. So scientists have estimated that the indigenous are ingesting up to 18 times the safe limit, which also puts people at risk who are miles away. The main recommendation of the study is the interruption of illegal mining and the withdrawal of invaders from indigenous lands. Indigenous families are being severely affected by mining activity, not only in their health, but in their survival as a whole. The destruction of rivers and forests also compromises the physical, cultural and traditions of the people, among other serious threats. The result of the research in the villages brought concern to leaders of the Munduruku people. “The survival of indigenous peoples is fish. This is serious. We need to denounce, we need to punish these people who are ruining the river and are also, mainly, damaging our health”, as the leadership Alessandra Korap Munduruku said.
72cad4dfd208402e47c7629503be88288c2ab4f4: At the beginning of the pandemic of the new coronavirus, the MPF in Pará proposed public civil action aimed at ensuring, in the municipality of Altamira, the effective implementation of the recommendations of the World Health Organization (WHO) and medical authorities that point to social isolation as the main prevention measure to contain the Covid-19 pandemic. e2174e9c6d60ea299ff5b70ab4af4501514bd55e: According to a report from the Center for Indigenous Work (CTI), the cases of Covid-19 in DSEI Parintins increased 120% between September and October, especially at Andirá Marau IT, after the sanitary barriers were removed. In that month, local indigenous health advisors of the Sateré-Mawé people took a complaint to the MPF about the neglect of the Dsei Parintins in the care of the Nova Esperança community, in them came to death for lack of re (1), Amazonas (36), Mato Grosso (38), nambuco (5), Paraná (4), Rondônia (2), 1), Santa Catarina (1) and Sergipe (1) on the Marau river. The situation ended up causing a sudden increase in cases of coronavirus in IT.
