891566550f426b62c0ddd6f1deb93ab13a0d64a8: The Covid-19 pandemic had caused, until December 9, the death of 889 indigenous peoples and the contamination of 41,250 members of 161 of the 305 native peoples living in Brazil. The mortality rate among the indigenous population, of 991 deaths per million people, was 16% higher than the overall mortality in Brazil due to the disease to date, of 852 deaths per million. The number of indigenous deaths is counted by the National Committee for Indigenous Life and Memory, created by Apib. On the other hand, on this same date, the Sesai bulletin recorded 496 deaths and 35,431 cases of Covid-19 among indigenous peoples. The divergence between the numbers is due to the fact that the Sesai only considers indigenous people living in homologated indigenous lands, leaving out those who are in non-demarcated territories or in urban areas. As if the pandemic were not enough, indigenous peoples had to face in this year actions of the federal government harmful to the indigenous, omission of public agencies in the elaboration and execution of plans to contain the pandemic in communities and increase in invasions of their lands. The first cases of contamination among indigenous peoples were transmitted precisely by health professionals from Sesai. According to Apib, the first infected indigenous woman was an indigenous health agent of the Kokama people in the Alto Solimões region (AM). The infection occurred after a Sesai doctor, who had spent the holidays in São Paulo, returned to the infected region in March, which started a chain of contamination among the Kokama. The last epidemiological bulletin of the Sesai 2020 indicated that the DSEI Alto Rio Solimões registered one of the highest numbers of indigenous deaths by Covid-19 in the country at that time: 35. According to physician Mariana Maleronka, professor of the School of Health Sciences Albert Einstein and consultant of the National Council of Human Rights for indigenous health, state agents ended up serving as one of the main paths of the virus for indigenous peoples due to the lack of a structured prevention policy, requiring PCR tests and quarantine of people on their way to indigenous lands. Apib opposed sending government missions to indigenous territories in order to make public relations. On June 30, an entourage with Defense Minister Fernando Azevedo e Silva, and Sesai's coordinator Robson Santos Silva, traveled to the Yanomami IT, disrespecting the indigenous decision for self-isolation, and attracted about 20 journalists. The mission delivered 33,000 chloroquine tablets to the Yanomami health unit, an unproven drug against Covid-19. In some peoples, contamination occurred through indigenous peoples who work in nearby refrigerators and contracted the disease of coworkers. This was the case of the Oco’y Indigenous Land, in Paraná, the Xapecó Indigenous Land, in Santa Catarina, and the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, in Mato Grosso do Sul. Given the lack of a government plan to protect the peoples from contamination, Apib, together with 6 political parties (PSB, PSOL, PCdoB, Rede, PT and PDT), moved an action in the STF to demand that the government adopt measures to contain the pandemic among indigenous peoples. The minister behind the action, Luís Roberto Barroso, determined that the government set up sanitary barriers to isolate the indigenous, the creation of a situation room to evaluate the evolution of the pandemic in these peoples and the withdrawal of invaders from indigenous lands, among other points. The decision was later confirmed by the Court's plenary. The government, however, did not come up with an effective plan to implement the court order. On July 29, federal management delivered a plan that, according to specialists invited by the STF, had conceptual errors that could accelerate the pandemic rather than contain it, and the text ended up rejected. On August 31, Barroso partially approved a government plan to erect sanitary barriers. The second general version of the plan, however, was rejected by the minister on 22 October, for being “generic and vague”, and he determined the realization of a new text until 23 November. On December 1, Barroso made a new decision, again determining that the government implement sanitary barriers to confront Covid-19 in indigenous territories where they had not yet been erected. Apib reports that the government has not been fulfilling the Supreme's determinations and that some sanitary barriers that had been implemented have already been undone. Dinaman Tuxá of Apib reported: “We were at the mercy of a state policy, and this policy never came. What happened were some mobilizations of the people themselves to alleviate the problem.” He said that inertia “has worsened” the pandemic in indigenous lands and that the government even “has fostered contamination”, by not vehemently opposing invasions of indigenous lands, which also end up exposing people to the virus. He also stated that the rate of contamination among indigenous peoples had no significant reduction throughout the year, as occurred in the country as a whole until the beginning of November, and peoples faced in December a high number of cases due to the loosening of controls.
a3be1bef8f3405393c0d17f5635bf23525d0527a: The young indigenous woman, 38 weeks pregnant, diagnosed with Covid-19, was transferred to the Hospital Regional de Água Boa, after refusal of care of the Hospital Regional José Abreu Luz, in São Félix do Araguaia. The pregnant woman arrived at the first hospital with the baby still alive in her womb. The alleged refusal to attend was because the only surgeon in the hospital would be over 60 years old and, therefore, would be part of the risk group for coronavirus and could not perform delivery. The indigenous woman was transferred to another hospital, more than 500 kilometers, on dirt roads, with her son dead in her womb. The removal of the stillbirth baby occurred only 72 hours after death.
e9d7357ee847438a89869801829f25e2033b471c: Marcelina arrived at the hospital in the municipality of Manga (MG), on February 24, to accompany her brother who had been referred for hospitalization. The next day, Marcelina felt bad, presenting “fatigue”, probably due to the distance from her village. She expressed to hospital staff the need to leave, asking them to make contact with her village and family, but had not met the demand. At the request of the family and yet unaware of the facts, an indigenous driver, service provider for Sesai, went to the hospital and asked for information about the health picture of Marcelina's brother, who was hospitalized there. According to Sesai's driver, not only was access to the patient denied, but he was also not informed about Marcelina's request, who wanted to leave the hospital. In the early hours of the day 26, the hospital’s medical staff diagnosed that Marcelina would be going through a “psychotic outbreak”. Under the guidance of the doctor, the medicines Haldol, Fernegam and Diazepam were applied in the indigenous population. Shortly thereafter, according to the team’s report, she fled, jumping over the hospital wall. The Military Police and the Municipal Guard were activated, but they claimed they could not look for Marcelina, because they did not have a photo or other indigenous references. No hospital employee volunteered to follow the search, even though it was a patient who was under strong psychiatric medications. Days later, with the search carried out by the indigenous themselves and with the help of the Fire Department, the indigenous woman was found lifeless, in a forest, in circumstances not yet clarified. The hospital management denies that there has been medical or hospital negligence and has not taken any steps to open administrative proceedings to investigate the case. The leaders registered a police report and denounced the MPF and the Human Rights Commission of the Legislative Assembly of Minas Gerais.
cc9458a0b747d276f9861b9f4ef52947596509ea: The Mbya Guarani community denounces that the indigenous Cristina Benites, who was pregnant, felt bad and asked for help. The community requested an ambulance, but this one took a while to arrive and Cristina gave birth to a girl. When they were taken to the hospital, the baby presented complications and died. The girl was registered under the name of her mother, Cristiane Benites. The family and community expect clarification about the delay in care and the cause of death of the child.

541df9a76604119146558d561065de531a9db8d0: According to indigenous information, Paulo Kmõrê was diabetic. After his wife died, he became depressed and wandered through the cities of Tocantinia and Miracema, making use of alcoholic beverages. 36bbc08b1918c4e7e354926f419125dd4f14afe8: A study by the Institute of Choices and published in February 2021, entitled Protected Areas or threatened areas? The incessant search for gold in Indigenous Lands and Conservation Units in the Amazon ", reports that more than 6 million hectares within Indigenous Lands and Conservation Units in the Amazon are threatened by the search for gold in the region. The study analyzed the research requests – requirements and authorizations – for gold registered at the National Mining Agency, which indicate the interest in mining in these areas. According to the study, by the end of 2020, Brazil had 6.2 million hectares threatened by the search for gold in protected areas of the Legal Amazon, an area equivalent to 40 times the city of São Paulo. Of this total, 3.8 million hectares are in conservation units and 2.4 million hectares are in indigenous lands. In total, there are 85 territories affected by gold research requests and 64 for conservation units. The Yanomani Indigenous Land, which is located in the states of Amazonas and Roraima, is one of the most vulnerable, with 749 thousand hectares under registration. The Indigenous Land Bau, in Pará, is the second in extension of processes, 471,000 hectares are registered. The study identified that the Raposa Serra do Sol (RR), Kayapó (PA) and Menkragnotí (MT/PA) ITs were also among the lands with the largest area covered by gold research requirements. The survey pointed out that the number of requests in Indigenous Lands has been increasing since 2018, and last year reached its record, with 31 research records. In 2020, the municipalities of the Legal Amazon collected financial compensation for gold extraction 60% higher than all year 2019 and 18 times higher than the amount recorded ten years ago.
5949f8cf9bb2115beaf5f9fe3a394b7d31f5e1c2: The Igarapé Institute published on April 8, 2021 a survey that reveals the size of the destruction caused by illegal gold mining in the Amazon and its impact on the forest, indigenous and population of the region. The document identified 321 illegal mining sites in nine states of the region. The study warns about corruption, deforestation, violence, contamination of rivers ", highlighting that the “illegalities committed in the gold cycle have caused the destruction of forests and lives, especially of indigenous populations in the Brazilian Amazon.” According to the report, gold quotation increased from $400 to $ 1,861.50 per ounce, due to China and India's high demand. Deforestation in indigenous lands caused by mining increased from 4% in 2017 to 23% in June 2020, according to the Deter system. Munduruku territory was the most affected, with satellite images revealing a 58% growth in mining-related deforestation, only in the first four months of 2020. The Igarapé Institute also reports that “hookers use mercury to extract metal, contaminating rivers, fish and who depends on them to live, such as the Yanomami and Munduruku indigenous peoples”. The survey points out, citing the MPF, that “1 kg of gold represents about R$1.7 million in environmental damage, resulting in a cost about ten times higher than the price of the gold market”. The socio-environmental destruction remained on a large scale in 2021, and still with several risks, especially PL 191/2020, that process in the National Congress, and that, if approved, will allow the opening of indigenous lands for mineral exploration.
b13e8f32e030264541ef8fbf180b646baa573522: Acre state politicians held a public hearing and campaigned fiercely to advance the project of building the binational road linking the municipality of Cruzeiro do Sul to Pucallpa, Peru. So far, people have not been consulted and neither has the environmental impact study been done. The MPF began to investigate the steps already undertaken by the government and moves a Civil Action Public to investigate irregularities. The Federal Police itself have already declared that the region is a route for crimes such as deforestation, greasing and drug trafficking.

485b8bba6b28790459fe0c78f9df3e41bf9c5668: In 2020, the MPF/AC had identified several CAR records with overlap to 18 indigenous lands of the state of Acre, causing risk of conflict and undue appropriation of the lands of the native peoples. 56a644a4086234379a58e68d1fffb6859eeb501e: Leadership and social movements denounced predatory activity of the company Mining Vale Verde, due to the implementation of an open-air mine and facilities for processing and production of copper concentrate, directly impacting the territory Xukuru-Kariri and its communities. IT, where approximately 2,600 people live, has a declaratory ordinance, but had its process paralyzed. The reactivation of transnordestine, without activities for more than 25 years, will reach the entire dynamics of the people, since the stretch of the railway passes very close to the sacred area where sacred rituals are performed, such as the Ouricuri.
868e1fe2e2fcdaa85d8bc6ecf96d413605ead7e9: Ibama is holding virtual hearings without participation or prior consultation with the indigenous communities of Lower São Francisco, decompeting and disrespecting what several laws recommend, including the Federal Constitution and the ILO Convention 169. bf5f5b89311bbf53c8f0fe7531366f7058438986: The implementation of the copper mine of the company Mining Vale Verde, which obtained from the state environmental licenses for land use for 27 years, also directly impacts the territory Tingui Botó and its communities. f954d3ebd9811bf7242c60f91d5ac5a67aefa4c5: In the case of the Karapotó people, the project to deploy an open-air mine and facilities for processing and production of copper concentrate by the company Mining Vale Verde will also generate direct and indirect impacts. cd099bcac71325caab774db96fb71fcd11a81a11: The doubling project of BR-101, a highway that cuts the territory of the Wassu Cocal people, began in 2012 and due to a lack of agreement and compliance with the mitigation processes, is paralyzed in the indigenous area. However, this is actually a lack of understanding of the DNIT, which does not accept the decision of the people, since the duplication directly affects two indigenous schools and several houses. The community asks that before the works are started in its territory the government rebuilds the schools and a runway, as well as compensation for families living in the affected area. The MPF has already been activated so that a response on the compensation agreement is collected from DNIT.
1cd55929c4b87a588585c9a296992a6254379ce5: The Karapotó Terra Nova and Karapotó Plaki-ô people suffer the impacts of the BR-101 duplication, which cuts their territory in a stretch of 8 km. The work of duplication remains paralyzed in the passage within IT, due to the failure to comply with the compensatory agreement by the DNIT. The community has charged the protection and inspection agencies, Funai and MPF, to meet their demands for continuity of duplication works.
e4daa1e5413e34470c86485dc776b8050542522e: The Karuazu people occupy a dominial area in the municipality of Pariconha (AL), where for 22 years they have been waiting for the regularization of their territory, which has never been identified. Without the regularization of their land, indigenous families live under tension, especially after the works of the Growth Acceleration Program (CAP), which were implemented without any process of study or consultation with communities, nor proposal to mitigate impacts. The Karuazu people are being hit by the Sertão Canal, an arm of the transposition of the São Francisco River that passes less than 2 km from the Tanque and Campinhos communities. The lack of demarcation is added to the fact that the people were not consulted on the works, disregarding the Federal Constitution and ILO Convention 169.
1d2fea5eea817697e2a02267659834593be03c40: Omission and delay in the demarcation of IT
c56fded61873bdabb5efdac6830de6cd9af0c9aa: Although the Katokinn people have claimed the demarcation of their territory since 2003, Funai has never created a GT to identify indigenous land. Thus, the people live in a dominial land on the outskirts of Pariconha (AL), with a family group living in a resumption area. Indigenous people live in precarious situations in taipa houses, without basic sanitation or access to water. With the lack of territory, the population lives without space for their subsistence and to perform their rituals. Indigenous people face, for example, difficulty in accessing Croá, a plant from which they make the garments of the Praias (enchanted), entities that maintain their entire religious tradition. The situation makes them need to go to another state to get the material for clothing. Exposed to social vulnerability, they often need to leave their communities to seek better living conditions in large centers, works or sugar cane cuts in the southeast.
8c5ccf75f5e68559282ebec80a29feb7f986539d: The MPF entered with public civil action for Funai to better analyze the impacts that the construction of the Tabajara hydroelectric plant in the Machado River can cause to indigenous lands of the region. Funai did research only TI Tenarim Quinces (AM). According to the MPF, the studies should also be conducted in the TIs Diahui (AM), Tenerim Rio Sepoti (AM), Tenerim do Igarapé Preto (AM), Pirahã (AM), Ipixuna (AM), Ninth of January (AM). The action seeks that the current reference term be cancelled and remade, because it excludes other indigenous communities from the same geographical area and ignores the existence of isolated indigenous people who move in areas close to the future reservoir. The MPF points out that the environmental problems caused by hydroelectric plants can reach great distances, and emphasizes that the impacts generated on indigenous communities are only known after specific studies, and cannot be limited to 40 kilometers, as stated in the Interministerial Ordinance 60/2015, published at the time of the construction of the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant in Pará. Indigenous people living in isolation are under a high degree of vulnerability, and the study should detail possible impacts of the plant and the presence of workers in its area of walking. According to the MPF, these groups depend on an ecologically balanced territory, demanding a certain territorial essentiality as a condition of life and physical reproduction”. As for Ibama, the MPF requested a study of the traditional component and that public audiences and advances in relation to the project do not occur before the completion of the studies required by the action. The MPF states that it is Funai’s job to promote, transparently and impartially, the participation of indigenous peoples and traditional communities in data collection and discussion about licensing of enterprises that can cause impacts on these lands.”
626eaf84c40c85e48300dfeb62e2f2d1c7c525a0: There is a social center in the Taquara community, within the TI Reach, of the Mura people, which urgently needs to be reformed. The Walls can't redo the space, because the non-Indians won't allow it. They say it's city hall space, but the Walls built it. Farmers have their meetings there and don't reward the Mura to rebuild the place. They want to carry out the work themselves, so that the use of indigenous peoples is not viable. A person who presents himself as president of the village” would be one of those who would prevent the work in the center. They say that indigenous people are just “named” of the Walls and that, in fact, they would be white. “White people want to humiliate us and not let us do anything in our own territory,” the Mura reported, “but the land is ours and we have the right to overthrow and build the center. According to our consultation protocol, they should consult us to do anything on our land. We're dealing here with a lot of government failures and we can't live and survive that way. It is the duty of the State to carry out these works, it is no kind of favor. We feel that the public bodies lack the will and concern for indigenous lives, because if nothing is done, we ourselves will do everything possible to keep existing.” In the hope that measures will be taken, complaint was made to the MPF by the community.”

4c0df2b19fae169f93925d0860b075bb9441fef6: In September 2021, after several complaints from various indigenous peoples in the region, the MPF recommended to Ibama, DNIT, Funai, Ipaam, ICMBio and Sema-AM to suspend all works related to BR-319 until the indigenous peoples and traditional communities of the region. The agency also requested the emergency construction of a plan of protection, monitoring and permanent supervision in the territories with potential impact of the highway, prioritizing the communities already impacted by the existing pressures, such as the areas located in the municipalities of Canutama, Humaitá, Manicoré and Tapauá. They can only be resumed after the legal questions about the environmental impact studies of the work, which, according to the MPF, were not carried out comprehensively and did not contemplate the entire extension of the road.
f5a88c3a4886a4dcf11971cfb56224baec77bfa8: Land conflict; omission and delay in the demarcation of IT
de558829a8c7fbf844927418c25f7b9d000afa34: In April 2021, the Kokama and Ticuna people carried out the self-demarcation of the Porto Praia de Baixo IT, located in Tefé (AM), in the region of the middle Solimões river. Without provision for Funai, the community, formed by about 500 people, decided to self-demarcate the limits of its territory to try to stop the attacks of invaders and squatters who advance on the land – among them, a gentleman who claims to own a land in the area traditionally occupied by the indigenous, but who did not present to the indigenous titles or documents that prove it. Upon being aware of the self-demarcation of the territory, this owner and his family opened civil proceedings in the 1st Court of the County of Tefé against community leaders for possessive invasion. An audience of the was held, and the indigenous claim that the process be transferred to the federal sphere. Constantly guarded, the indigenous feel threatened and concerned, but they claim that they have followed firm in the struggle for demarcation and preservation, protection and maintenance of their territory.
799e23f01cbe33e7b14677a9405ca06cedc00fed: With the social distancing and the need for people to stay at home, due to the Covid-19 pandemic, many tourists decided to settle in the extreme south of Bahia. Foreigners, mainly of high financial power, have bought lots at TI Barra Velha, on the coast. These lots are often advertised by social networks. Since the demarcatory process does not advance, the Pataxó leaders are threatened by buyers and sellers and thus cannot move to the area to manage the territory and expel the invaders. Complaints were made to Funai and the MPF, which were not answered.

d8641dcb5df1e26bd84f70d3ee88704b64f9751b: TI Taquaritiua dawned on November 18th with the presence of armed gunmen, who said they were police officers and went to the place to help employees of a company in the installation of electric power lines. Already in the afternoon, military police officers went to the Cajueiro Village, in TI Taquaritiua, and forced some leaders into the vehicle. There are reports that mobile phones, among other indigenous communication equipment, were taken by the police. The Gamella observed the movement in the Antero Center Village and were surprised by the invasion of armed officials and gunmen, who threatened the lives of the indigenous. Since 2016, the company has been trying to continue the process of implementing the power line, dividing TI Taquaritua in half. The action disrespects the environmental legislation and the indigenous component of the licensing of the work. In addition to the delay in the demarcatory process, Funai measures such as Normative Instruction 09/2020, which allows the certification of private properties on indigenous lands not yet approved, favor conflicts and actions such as that occurring in Gamella territory.
105fa770ee8d4bc0df609d624866de7d80c1d746: In August 2021, a non-indigenous arrived in the territory of the Krenyê people already demarcated and approved, claiming to have more than 700 hectares within the IT. The alleged owner stated that he would have purchased a lot in 1987, presenting a virtual documentation by mobile phone, registered in the local registry.
40a9576e7bd72623e9093f109681b907a7b09a58: Invasions; allotment; overlapping of properties in indigenous land
d80177b7d91343a205075326fe59a134329ade4a: The Pigs IT, in the process of demarcatory review in the STF, is with the Funai Working Group (GT) paralyzed due to the actions of local politicians, landowners and agribusiness companies in the region and the federal government. With this, the insecurity and threats to the lives of indigenous peoples related to invasions and the presence of squatters, settlements, allotment, deforestation, soybean and corn companies, farmers and loose cattle that destroy the environment and harm the indigenous villages have increased. The climate in the region is tense due to these conflicts. According to a survey by Cimi, after the publication of Normative Instruction 09/2020 by Funai, which released the certification of private properties on unapproved ITs, 26 properties were certified on the IT Pigs, covering almost 30 of the 51.5 thousand hectares of indigenous land. Much of the certifications were made by companies that have large land areas in the state.
a8b7fbd90684e281fa0d856b990c12f050485d2d: Indigenous leaders report invasions by hunters, loggers, farmers and soy and corn companies that are batching and privatizing parts of the territory in areas of rural settlements, soybean fields and corn. In addition, they build roads with transit of trucks to flow commodity production. Many leaders are threatened with death, especially the Guardians of the IT Forest Pigs and the indigenous are forbidden to walk certain roads within the indigenous land itself, at certain times, by the companies and farmers of the region.
0f14051b0876e516267b6dd7802d240f8fdc7acf: The Xavantes of TI Marãiwatsedé, in Mato Grosso, face several conflicts; one of them, at great risk, concerns the BR-158 route. It was elaborated by cutting the indigenous land from north to south, directly affecting cultural and existential aspects of the Xavante people. According to the MPF, in addition to these aspects, the BR-158 tracing causes the internal transit of heavy vehicles that, in addition to causing the death of native fauna species, brings risk of accidents to the indigenous population. The presence of non-indigenous people has also been a factor of great concern, conflicts and risks for the Xavante people, making the free exercise of the land traditionally occupied by indigenous people impossible. After opening the route, the next step would be its paving; the MPF points out, however, that a paved highway within this territory would facilitate the practice of environmental crimes such as deforestation and fires, damaging the indigenous subsistence activities, which predominantly use hunting as food. After numerous conflicts and frustrated attempts at agreements between the parties, the MPF decided Public Civil Action against the Union, Ibama and DNIT, and the Federal Justice determined the closure of the route of this highway and the reforestation of the area. The Xavante people await the fulfillment of judicial determination.
53195bdead0c06b2258f984d5f9b011135bc5314: The Xavante Warã Association published a note denouncing the political use that the federal government is making of the Auwé Xavante people, implementing agricultural cooperatives that work in partnership with agribusiness within the Sangradouro IT in Mato Grosso. The Xavante state that their ancestral and millennial knowledge is not consistent with the discourse that is based on ideas that relate indigenous peoples to ‘misery, poverty, underdevelopment’”. And that “poor is the project of this government for Brazil [ ] failed project developed by Funai in the Military Ditatura as a model of state policy for the indigenous issue”, highlights the note, which also reaffirms the resistance of the people. The “Indigenous Independence Project”, denounced by the Xavante Warã Association, was approved and encouraged by the current management of Funai, in conjunction with the Rural Union of Eastern Spring. “Unlike what his name intends to reveal, the project has nothing of independence or autonomy for the people A’Uwe Xavante”, denounces the indigenous organization. The association Xavante warns that the project is a “stimulus to dependence and lease, with legal air”, and assesses that this is not an isolated case, but a state policy. Leadership and indigenous organizations have denounced similar cases. “The picture is serious, it is our way of life that is threatened”, the note highlights.
ad95ca77413954a0cba2813375660de28cfabcaf: Omission and delay in demarcation of IT; land conflict
56c86d5bbecdebfce21d68917beed6eff464c784: The Chiquitano people, inhabitant of the border region between Brazil and Bolivia, have for years claimed to regulate their territory. 91a63a10ddd9eb2233d0e22dbcaad0b1451b7581: Threats; Grinding; omission and delay in the demarcation of IT
2f4d0c7e81182328d7f73a26751ca640ac5c933f: The Chiquitano people live in a border region between Brazil and Bolivia and demand the demarcation of their traditional territory in different places in Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, from which they are systematically being expelled by agribusiness and politicians. However, Funai only created a GT to identify the Gate of Charming. The village Santa Aparecida (Osbi) is located in the Indigenous Land Pescaria Monte Cristo and has no demarcation referral by Funai, which has generated conflict situations in the region, resulting mainly in threats to the village chief, his Aurélio Rodrigues and family. In September, his grandson, Genisvaldo Rodrigues, was beaten by three non-Indians. Just over a month later, he was found dead, drowned in a dam on the farm where he worked. There are suspicions that his death was a crime, due to land conflicts in the region and the fact that the young man assumed his ethnic identity and claimed traditional territory. Like the village Osbi stays inside the Farm São João do Guaporé, the farmer tries, through the Association of Residents, that the 500 Chiquitanos of Osbi accept lots as if it were private property. Using tractors, he began doing straight streets that year and topple the houses that were not within the neighborhood pattern, because the village follows the distribution of houses around the parents. The family of Vice-Cacique Pascoal Tomichá also suffers constant violence, as they are being forced to share their father's inheritance in the form of private property, when the form of transmission of the parents' property to their children, according to the Chiquitana tradition, is collectively, each child living around their parents. The Chiquitano People's Council of Chiefs has sent documents to the MPF of Cáceres, requesting action on the situation of the territory, the State Human Rights Council and the Human Rights Defenders and Defenders Program, reporting the conflicts, violence and threats suffered by the community.
055d61cb6e62dddeac4b9fc487202a2ce3b9421b: The Chiquitano people, for years, have claimed their territory in Porto Espiridião and other municipalities in the state of Mato Grosso. However, Funai has not yet created the GT to identify Barbecho IT. Such omission and delay of the government in solving this quiestão, has generated situations of conflict in the region and difficulties of Chiquitano survival, which are confined in a few hectares on the roadside, pushed to this place by the farmer occupying the traditional territory.
b946a8f7929c148f05d912adb96892fb2f953781: The Chiquitano people, inhabitant of the border region between Brazil and Bolivia, claim their traditional territory in different places. These Chiquitano Indians, for the most part, come from the Santo Ignacio Village, a territory that was distributed by Incra to the farmers of the region. There in Nova Fortuna they made lots of 50 meters by 80, as if it were a city neighborhood, but they are in the middle of the farms and there they serve as cheap labor, under degrading labor regime, when they find paid work. When they claim to be indigenous Chiquitano, they are no longer accepted for work on farms in the region and are marked as dangerous” for the system of ownership of Chiquitana lands by farmers.”
976870823f940868f7ed3c0d07a7ee93b196f4b1: The Chiquitano people claim their territory, but Funai has not created, until today, the GT to identify this part of the villages near Padre's Bay, which has generated conflict situations in the region. The disregard of the government for the indigenous population has taken on frightening proportions since 2019; the bodies that should protect the indigenous people and their territories are being dismantled, and their institutional duties totally distorted.
eee46e6d5752c245857d171ecf88ae402bce73f6: With the signing of the cooperation agreement between the municipality of Brasnorte and the Incra in the program Titula Brasil, of the federal government, for regularization and titration in the projects of agrarian reform in the municipality of Brasnorte, which began in 05/2021, a serious situation was created in which the indigenous people are confronted with overlapping properties within the Myky's IT, which is identified and delimited. b631f6162d2057bef0f22c191a02e9986683cf94: Construction projects of hydroelectric plant and PCHs
281f59b67333befa9b1c83a77422a4a5ec3115ed: From 2001 to the present day, projects are underway to install Hydroelectric Plants (UHEs) and Small Hydroelectric Plants (PCHs) in the Juruema Basin, in the Papagaio, Sacre, Norato, Membeca, Ponte de Pedra and Cravari rivers, directly impacting the Myky, Paresi, Irantxe/Manoki and Enawenê-Nawê peoples and all natural resources of this region. 21dc6cfd826cbae8f62491480af174a103b49b09: An area of immemorial use of the Apyãwa Tapirapé remained outside the demarcation of the Urubu Branco IT and is pleaded by the Apyãwa people. About three years ago, an entrepreneur occupied this area, building facilities, and made a large ditch, 2 meters deep and about 1.5 meters wide, for drainage of the land – which greatly disturbed the way of the complaining pigs and prevented the access of the Apyãwa to three lakes from where they obtained fish during the time of the camp: Tyxigoo ma’e, Waiwa’i ’Yopãwa and Peinare’ywa. The naming of the area and lakes demonstrates the traditional occupation of this area by the Apyãwa Tapirapé people. 59d19880d9e3962a0450e480fe3aa28eb9c20cf5: According to the MPF, a bridge was built unlawfully by a farmer on the Tarumã River, in the region of Fortuna, hindering access to water by the Chiquitano people of the Indigenous Land Portal do Encantado. bd594d5c9301faf7bd5095860086831dbb308744: The people are still waiting for the developments of the review of IT limits to include, in the demarcation, the region of Adowina (Rio Preto). The request for entry of the community was contrary by the municipality and favorable by the MPF and AGU, and was not yet appreciated by the courts.
d31fcbcc56bbc9fbedf81d8ffd9ce9a438e294fe: Hydropower plant construction project (PCH); violation of prior consultation right
ef2476ac55ef133137c55f9d7d3f0475ce358aa8: Negotiations for the construction of the Jesuit PCH, pleaded by Maggi Energia S.A., and UHE Cachoeirão, both in the Juruena River basin, continued to take place in 2021 without respect to the right Prior Consultation, Free and Informed of indigenous populations, guaranteed by Convention 169 of the ILO. The people continue to fight for the consultation to be carried out according to their protoc.
d2f77fcece07f32b10665ccb65726d341f05f150: After action of the MPF, the Federal Court of Barra do Garças determined that Funai install the specialized GT to carry out the identification and delimitation of Jaguari IT, claimed by the Guarani people. While waiting for the demarcation that has been going on at Funai since at least 2003, the MPF reports that indigenous people are at risk of being permanently expelled from the territory that they have been living for more than five decades, because their lands are occupied by farmers. 1e49904b1e995910a1bbf6237d729988f1d963ef: The Federal Court of Mato Grosso determined a period of 15 days for Funai to constitute a new GT responsible for the review of the limits of the Batovi IT, in the municipalities of Gaúcha do Norte and Paranatinga (MT), the Waujá people. 17f8e69bd1abd23063cdf4ec435d969e811babf1: With legal IT protection Piripkura about to win, exploitation requests fired around the territory where the isolated Piripkura live. A “gold map” released by the federal government drew attention to resources. Newly created cooperative takes advantage of the opportunity to think about becoming the largest in Brazil. Nine months before the expiration of the use restriction ordinance that protects the territory where the isolates live, in December 2020, the federal government chose precisely the region that covers the Pyriplure IT to launch “Letters of Anomalies”, elaborated by the Geological Service of Brazil (CPRM), pointing out the places where there are more chances of finding precious metals throughout the North of Mato Grosso. The “gold map” included the Piripkura IT. As a result, the mining requirements in the region registered at ANM had increased 70% between December and September 2021, according to a survey by InfoAmazônia: the 119 applications registered between 1994 and 2020 rose to 202 after the letters from the Geological Service were published. Only the Guaporé Valley Mining Cooperative, created in 2020, requested ANM to have an area of 575 thousand hectares – twice as large as the Piripkura IT – to explore gold, diamond, manganese and tin in 65 mining requests. The pressure is added to the performance of landowners and loggers within IT. According to Sirad, ISA monitoring system, deforestation between August 2020 and July 2021 in Piripkura IT was 2,000% higher than in the previous two years.”
bd5beccace9480ee4353facf780ab3c2f7c9b446: The permanence of the National Force teams in Dourados and Caarapó was extended, as published on January 15, 2021, in the Official Gazette of the Union. The ordinance was signed by the Executive Secretary of the Ministry of Justice, Tercio Issai Tokano, on grounds of maintaining public order. Among the tasks of the Force National in the municipalities are the prevention of agrarian conflicts, the fight against smuggling, drug trafficking, weapons and ammunition. The contingent is defined by the National Secretariat of Public Security. The National Force has been in Caarapó since 2016, in measure of security taken after the death of indigenous health agent Guarani Clodiodi Aquilleu Rodrigues de Souza, shot at 26 years. In Dourados, the teams were sent from January 2020, also because of conflict between producers and indigenous people. The areas in question are adjacent to Golden TI, the most populous indigenous reserve in the country, which houses the villages Jaguapiru and Bororó. The need for the presence of the National Force by itself already points to the very serious situation of violence suffered by the indigenous peoples in the MH, until the land situation of the indigenous lands is resolved and their demarcations guaranteed.
89e236023c9aa3a9ade509733d3e5e6a77f3597a: The MPF defended the suspension of the process that discusses the demarcation of the territory of the indigenous community Guarani Nandeva de Porto Lindo (MS) until the final decision of the STF on the Theme 1.031, with general repercussions, which will define the legal-constitutional status about the demarcations of traditional indigenous occupation lands. In opinion, the sub-procurator-general of the Wagner Natal Batista Republic recalls that the Supreme Court itself determined the national standstill of all actions on indigenous land ownership until the end of the covid-19 pandemic or until the final trial of Theme 1.031. The case of the Guarani Nhandeva of Porto Beautiful is discussed in Extraordinary Resource 1.103.215/MS. It is an action proposed by a farmer who sought the positive declaration of the possession of the Farm Remanso-Guaçu and the annulment of the ordinance of the Ministry of Justice that had recognized the area as a traditional occupation of the community Guarani Nandeva. The action was joined to others who deal in the first instance. In parallel, the farmer resorted to the STJ and obtained the annulment of the ordinance only with regard to the Farm Remanso-Guaçu. Thus, he asked to give up the declaratory action, with the extinction of the feat. However, Funai and MPF consider it important to continue the action, for the production of expert and anthropological reports capable of attesting the traditional presence of the indigenous community in the region and discussion of issues still open, such as the alleged nullity of the title of the property, the private occupation in indigenous land and the analysis of the benefactories performed. According to article 485, § 4, of the Code of Civil Procedure (Art. 267, VIII, of the CPC 1973), an action can only be extinguished by the author's withdrawal when there is consent from the other parties. Moreover, according to article 3 of Law 9.469/1997, the author would have to expressly waive the right in which the action is founded, which also did not occur. Nevertheless, Justice in the first instance determined the extinction of the feat. Funai and MPF resorted to TRF-3 and STF. Wagner Natal explains that, despite the fact that the case deals with the possibility of extinction of a process – because of the withdrawal of the author, without the consent of the defendants and the MPF – he ends up discussing the possession of indigenous territories. Thus, it must be paralyzed until the end of the pandemic or until the Supreme decides on Theme 1.031, as determined by the Supreme Court itself.
40bd4fb064d6eda0630de17a0237131f485a3b04: A few kilometers from the Federal University of Grande Dourados (UFGD) lives the Guarani Kaiowá community of Tekoha Ava’ete, located in the vicinity of the village Bororó and composed of about twenty families, with elderly people and children, including babies. It happens that rural properties affect the indigenous territory and the owners do not accept the presence of Guarani Kaiowá in that space. The indigenous report that the attacks have happened almost daily, always at night, starting at 6:00 p.m., and usually extend until dawn, being characterized by firearms shooting and use of non-lethal ammunition (rubber bullets). In addition to the shooting, the gunmen” pass with tractors over the shacks of the indigenous, when they do not burn them. In one of these arsons, the burning of belongings and personal documents of the Indians occurred. The situation of the Guarani-Kaiowá is totally unpaired; without access to health and without food, they do not even have food production tools, surviving from a basic basket carried by Funai servants every thirty days, insufficient to feed the entire community. The indigenous people are in the open, exposed to weather and temperature drops, with risks to the health and life of the whole community. Representation was filed in the MPF asking for measures against these human rights violations committed against indigenous people.
6d3028ee04f2d501a0bed8d79bdfb1b8d70c8ba4: The MPF recommended Funai to carry out the physical demarcation of TI Taunay/Ipegue, located in the municipality of Aquidauana (MS). 8b4cdc94dd6e602617a01280b4135aae7251bb8f: Overlay of properties in indigenous land; omission and delay in the demarcation of IT
c55fa35bd529b384abda9e71215925b8d711eb33: The process of demarcation of the Terena people's lands between the Cerrado and the Pantanal of Mato Grosso do Sul has been dragging for at least 40 years. But the registration of a luxurious resort in the same place, requested by Caiman Agrippecuaria, linked to the Klabin family – founder of one of the largest paper manufacturers on the continent – was quickly approved. It took two months between the application and the approval of the court responsible, all with the approval of the federal government. Caiman has as partner one of the heirs and also adviser to the holding company that controls the giant of the paper – which still acts as vice president of the SOS Atlantic Forest Foundation and the SOS Pantanal Institute. Through his company, Klabin asked for land regularization on November 13, 2020, seven months after Funai changed the rules. In January 2021, everything was in the government's Land Management System. While the land situation of the indigenous peoples of the MS is not solved, they remain pushed into tiny spaces, without the least infrastructure, without assistance, without dignity, running all kinds of risks for their survival and all sorts of violence and prejudices. MPF prosecutors entered with several actions throughout the country to annul the practical effects of Funai's IN 09.
2cb7da3fdececf58015986280d962c994a04dc24: Road duplication; threats; omission and delay in the demarcation of IT
8a632f518d48266e864a77be343ab312c30a17c2: Despite the demand for demarcation of the Apyka’i IT already last decades, with the effective occupation of the Guarani-Kaiowá in a small range of territory, the qualification for Funai study was established only in 2016 and has been paralyzed since then. In 2021, the situation of roadside vulnerability caused another death, one of the children of leadership – the tenth in this period of evictions and return to territory, which dates back to the early 2000s. In addition, there was also the decrease – and sometimes the complete interruption – of the delivery of basic baskets by Funai. This worsens the lack of access to land and causes hunger. Another element that aggravates the situation of the community is the duplication of the highway MS-463, which has generated fear among the Kaiowá, since, without legal certainty even in relation to the small area they occupy, they fear suffering new eviction.
f3fcaebc4d507eb24532a1885d105707580810aa: Omission and delay in IT demarcation; threats
6427a08da1cab9decc2d7debc5da9c64ca133b3e: The IT Dourados Amambai Pegua I, located in the municipality of Caarapó (MS), despite being identified and delimited by Funai, in 2016, with 55,590 hectares, remains out of the indigenous possession. d52af7db50e7c1111d8fa99c7e6569e9ef72bd81: In April 2021, the Supreme Court unanimously decided that it will analyze the Guarani Kaiowá action that seeks to annul the decision that invalidated the demarcation of their land. In the rescissory action, the Guarani Kaiowá point out a series of irregularities and unconstitutionalities in the decision of the Second Class of the STF which, in 2014, annulled the decree of the Guyrarooka IT – among them, the fact that the community was not admitted and not even heard in the process. 49f9a01e924e664e9e7f47105f824d77afcc9102: Invasion; threats; omission and delay in the demarcation of IT
f0c3066a830e4a56b1bcf371845e45e3788d4b60: The arrest of the demarcatory procedure of Iguatemi Pegua I – Pyelito Kue/ Mbarakay IT, located in the municipality of Iguatemi (MS) and already identified and delimited by Funai, continued to produce situations of conflict and vulnerability in 2021 for the Guarani and Kaiowá. 09120bcda0edf72c921d5244f2f1d727f1c3b56a: Closing access to the village; threats
03bad9abfd238c20d0721e0c325581185e33a1b9: The village Geru Tucunã is an occupation of the Pataxó people, established by families expelled from Barra Velha (BA) and migrants from the Farm Guarani, in the State Park of the River Current, in Açucena (MG). ed32e38729f81714b0946d6ca20a0289e93236ed: On 14 May, after the situation in Munduruku IT was intensified, the MPF requested the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the National Security Force and the Federal Police to allocate police forces in a state of readiness to combat possible armed conflicts within Munduruku IT in the San Francisco Mission village. 65d3dcbf7c620e70131cd8e3eefbacb6812b1aaa: A group of Indians Munduruku was leaving the city of Jacareacanga (PA), bound for Brasilia (DF), where they would participate in mobilizations to denounce violations of their rights. On the way, the bus the group was on was attacked by prospectors. The driver was threatened with death and the vehicle had flat tires. In a complaint document, the Munduruku said that if I didn't leave town, the bus would be burned. Our entourage is forbidden to travel.” One of the leaders, Alessandra Korap, used her social networks to report the terror scene experienced by the people: “They want to burn the bridge so no one gets out. There is militia on site and no one has done anything.” The Munduruku pointed out in the document that any violence they suffered would be the responsibility of the Brazilian State, which “did not guarantee police reinforcement” and thus continued to be attacked, “even informing, asking for policing and support”. The attack on the bus is not an isolated fact. “These attacks occur due to the lack of federal security forces in the city and the small contingent of the existing PM, which is unable to ensure ostensive peace and security in the city, so much so that this is the sixth attack followed by leaders who oppose illegal mining,” says Munduruku. The Indians report that they suffer continuous threats. According to Greenpeace, Munduruku territory has been suffering from illegal mining for over a decade: from 2008 to 2020, about 61 km2 were destroyed. The indigenous say that the situation is allowed by the federal government. In 2021, aggression and violence intensified absurdly, and the omission of the government favors the invasions and illicits of all kinds within the indigenous territories. The delegation could not follow a trip until days later, after requesting police escort from the MPF/PA and parliamentarians from the Joint Parliamentary Front in Defense of the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
0294f2a91cd3a348f54577b5d3c6a12e3b13caf1: Due to numerous conflicts in Munduruku IT and Sai Ash, originated from the presence of illegal prospectors within indigenous lands, and with the mobilizations planned to take place in Brasilia, the MPF made a recommendation to Funai, ANM, Ibama and other federal government agencies informing that a delegation of 102 indigenous peoples who act associated and funded by hidden entrepreneurs involved and/or interested in the promotion of mining with heavy machinery” within the ITs of the Munduruku people was addressing Brasilia at the Week of Indigenous Peoples in April 2021. According to the MPF, “integrants of the same entourage participated in the attempt of armed invasion of Igarapé Baunilha [...] as well as involved in the depredation and firing at the headquarters of the Wakoburun Women’s Association” and other associations of resistance against mining in indigenous territory. b0b339dedff97cfdef33a222c4ff6d9e7e7ddef2: Although the ITI Paquiçamba has been demarcated and approved since 1991, the Juruna community seeks to review the limits of its area, given that the indigenous peoples had part of their territory directly affected by the drastic reduction of the volume of water in part of the Volta Grande do rio Xingu, due to the construction of the UHE Belo Monte. The identification report of the new limits was published on 23/10/2014, but it has not yet been physically demarcated and they have not yet performed the disintrusion of non-indigenouss.
deec29e622984a9525c1a936cbc5d235b22937b9: The MPF joined with Civil Action against the Union and Funai for the delay of almost 50 years in demarcation of the Karajá Santana IT of Araguaia, in the southeast of Pará. The Karajá IT has already published a declaratory ordinance, which means that demarcation depends only on Funai and the Union to complete the other phases of the demarcation process.”
0d4b58c47039d047ab0833b7d660619cdd9dd1bb: At the end of 2021, TRF-1 suspended the granting of new licenses or authorizations to Chapleau Mineral Exploration for mining in the municipality of Novo Progresso (PA), until the mining company demonstrates the absence of impacts on IT Bau and that prior consultation with indigenous peoples is carried out. fe018d1c561672738c897cd8a596d0b0ffe9e846: Kayapó peoples living in indigenous lands in southeastern Pará are suffering the impact of China's high demand for manganese, metal used in the manufacture of steel that supplies infrastructure works benches by the government of the Asian country. 69fe454b4c4148a3b2713d49598dc41e69e29bc4: The MPF requested, in March 2021, the Federal Court that the Union, Funai and Incra be forced to immediately begin to implement the plan for the withdrawal of non-indigenous people from the area known as Vila Bacajá, located in TI Alto Rio Guamá, in northeastern Pará. eedcd6a603d801dab7973b37efa64ffb31dbdd84: The MPF filed an action asking the Federal Court for the Union and Funai to be forced, urgently, to complete the process of demarcation of the Marakaxi IT, of the Tembé people, located in the municipality of Aurora do Pará, in the northeast of Pará. The situation has generated land conflicts with non-indigenous people and results in insecurity, fear and apprehension among the Tembé.
b9e5be40417ab9072a5f38d324b90ccbaa42cd06: The MPF filed an action in the Federal Court to force Funai and the Union to complete the demarcation of Tuwa Apekuokawera IT, the Suruí people Aikewara. ad76484b9d5c6c9a37860e51afb075f676646e49: Since the start of operations of the Puma Ounce mine, operated by Vale miner, the lives of the Xikrin have been severely affected. In February 2020, the group identified that all the indigenous peoples analyzed in a study were contaminated with at least one heavy metal, with excess lead, mercury, manganese, aluminum and iron, which in some individuals are at frightening levels.” A report produced by Finnish NGO Finnwatch in partnership with Reporter Brasil identified that part of the nickel produced in the region is destined for Europe, acquired from the Valley by Finnish company Outokumpu. d5867dea95f967cd1964532c100cf1bdcca30920: The Federal Court in Santarém (PA) has brought to justice the president of Funai, Marcelo Xavier, in a case in which the MPF accuses him of administrative impropriety for disobeying at least six judicial decisions, in an agreement in which the municipality undertook to advance the demarcation of the indigenous territory of the Munduruku of the Santareno Plateau. With the improbity process, he will also be subject to the penalties provided for in the administrative impropriety law: loss of political rights, prohibition of hiring with the government and fine.
aa799a7219e3dad2db71a5bba4c92789a19c9c38: According to the MPF, there is today a total area of approximately 264 hectares of real estate records in the National System of Rural Environmental Registration (Sicar), superimposed on the protection zone of TI Zo’é, in the west of Pará. The area was created by the government of Paraná in 2008, at the request of the MPF, to prevent the contamination of indigenous people by malaria. The creation of the area also sought to ensure the natural evolution of ecosystems, being prohibited the direct use of natural resources, to prevent the preservation of biological diversity and the indigenous people from being put at risk. 52ade5474bf577233a81723030e8b24e91f8e916: The process of demarcation of the Monte Mor IT was paralyzed in 2021, still waiting for the approval of the President of the Republic. Meanwhile, the Potiguara community continues to face serious and constant conflicts with squatters.

bf769ee3bd68a6915eb34e45e160ca3cf15fa31b: In 2020, the judge Gustavo Chies Cignachi, of the Federal Justice of Guaíra, determined the suspension of any act of demarcation of indigenous lands in the municipalities of Guaíra and Terra Roxa and the annulment of the report of identification and delimitation of TI Tekoha Guasu Guavirá, which comprises 14 Guarani villages located in both cities. 998b742a188e60312625d989b95eead68485b8ad: Since 2008, Pankará do Serrote dos Campos people have been suffering from the attacks by local politicians to build a nuclear power plant in their territory. The project provides for the installation of nuclear power plants in indigenous areas in the municipality of Itacuruba (PE), preventing the demarcation of territories and causing great damage to these peoples. The pro-nuclear campaign is promoted by Senator Fernando Bezerra Coelho (MDB), state deputy Alberto Feitosa (PL) and the department of Nuclear Physics of UFPE, which lobby political and business for the construction of the nuclear park in the state of Pernambuco. Campaigns seek to amend the Federal and State Constitution, especially in Article 216, which prohibits investment in nuclear energy in the state as long as there are other possible energy sources. Due to the pressure and movements of communities and more conscious society, the project has not yet been implemented, but the risk is great, with a view to the involvement of politicians and big businessmen. The community has mobilized with the indigenous peoples Tuxá Campos and Tuxá Pajeú and the social movements in the struggle for the demarcation of their claimed territory.
d8aa26272b9466f84f422fadb8f82fd0371c7190: The Federation of Rural Farmers and Farmers of Piauí (Fetag-PI) denounced and repudiated the eviction committed against the family of the indigenous Karoá-Gamella Adaildo José Alves da Silva, by means of an eviction order issued by the judge of the Gilbués District (PI). 503b5d9cf6f0189e7e089abb230f2f757b8d04aa: After several reports of violence and two murders in TI Serrinha, in Ronda Alta (RS), the Ministry of Justice authorized the sending of the National Force to the site. ffd03367526b8f61ad84232680baf2117a9c3fae: The cacica Cunllung Web informed, through audio, that two men saying themselves of the Federal Police, but without a warrant, without uniform, without any identification and without wearing a protective mask, in the middle of the pandemic, arrived in the community questioning people and looking for an indigenous man named Woie. The cacica reported that it requested from them the judge's warrant for the alleged police action, which was not presented. 8a5247e8f8ffd79ac0769a3cba64942f2a5e7d87: The Mbya Guarani who live in Ponta do Arado, in the Belém Novo neighborhood, in Porto Alegre (RS), denounced that people linked to the economic enterprise Arado Velho, including accompanied by military police, circulated in the land space that was delimited by the TRF-4 as being of exclusive enjoyment of the community. From what they hear and the movement of the representatives of the real estate enterprise, the community leaders say they fear that the company intends to disobey the court order, relocating the electric fence around the community and restricting their right to come and go. According to the information, the attitude of health professionals was to not give any kind of information, including ethical principles. They warn that during the nights they heard shots fired from firearms, probably from people practicing hunting in an area that should be preserved and protected. Given these facts, the Mbya Guarani community called for the attention and support of public agencies, especially the MPF, in the sense of better accompanying them, because of the powerful economic interests in the area, which generates threats to fauna and flora, indigenous rights and all the people who live there.
2c1f22e2951f2ff6dee3bc0cd50a7fd7008ea806: The Pindo Poty area, in Lami, Porto Alegre (RS), of the Mbya Guarani people, is literally being crowded in daylight and under the eyes of the entire population of the neighborhood. The MPF and Funai were informed, but no measures were adopted. Either the responsible bodies act urgently or the families of the community will be driven out of their homes by the invaders. Three complaints have already been made to MPF and Funai, but as incredible as it may seem, the invasion persists and now in a wide-ranging manner. Photos taken by the Cimi Sul team in April 2021 show the invaders plowing, surrounding and building more shacks within the indigenous area. c3370c1512b2da192a9963afa9541c31ea9f0a24: The Kaingang community resumed the area in March 2010. The site is an area of the former State Company of Silos and Warehouses (CESA). Proceed in court with a request for reinstatement in disfavor of the community.
1612ce6d0492d664796d785c821ce4fc58f6bebc: The Guarita indigenous land is the largest indigenous area demarcated in Rio Grande do Sul and has a vast area that can be planted. d5c0351c4d037e8af0af94a90a4fde92cb57805a: About 25 Mbya Guarani families live in this land, which occupy 20 hectares of an area given to the community in 2002 by the state of Rio Grande do Sul. 4aea03321ec916ae0596609ccc4b659d46e77900: This area is considered by the authorities as a camp. It has only seven hectares, provided by the government of the state of Rio Grande do Sul in 2002. The Guarani are reflecting and organizing the map of the earth, with what they consider as the extent necessary and sufficient for their physical and cultural survival. Nearby Estiva there are farms and small rural occupations. The main obstacles to demarcation are farmers, squatters and the state itself, who want to maintain the so-called indigenous camp.
d0ef085cd7e2cfb945aeb3b979969153b617925f: The Mbya camp is located on the banks of RS040, in the municipality of Capivari do Sul. Today, they live on the highway’s banks, between 60 and 62 kilometers, about ten families, in a camp without drinking water, basic sanitation and without adequate housing. The Technical Group to carry out the studies of identification and delimitation of the land was created in 2012 and is paralyzed. There is opposition from farmers and the state against demarcation. In recent years, the state of Rio Grande do Sul, to prevent the demarcation of Capivari, articulated with Funai the creation of a small reserve within a devoid area of the state, called Granja Vargas. A region of soil of low fertility, sandy and degraded. So much so that currently no Guarani family remains in the region. This area was also the subject of a preliminary study in 2006. In 2016, ten families of Capivari do Sul were removed to an IRGA area near Granja Vargas. There they remained in an absolute precarious situation. In 2018, after the sudden death of a two-year-old child, the Karaí and Kunhã Karaí – pajés – said that in the area provided for them to live there were bad spirits and that everyone would die if they stayed in it. From then on, they left the area and returned to Capivari do Sul, where they live in precarious situations – which was aggravated by the increase of the coronavirus pandemic in 2021.
7785afea23380cab2c8ef294c7b0281b58ba50bd: The Irapua is a traditional Guarani occupation land located on the banks of BR-290, at the height of kilometer 298, in the municipality of Caçapava do Sul (RS). aebdf73b93cbd328c0a8cbf9d7192cbae88049dc: On May 10, a group of heavily armed prospectors, on seven vessels, approached the Palimiú indigenous community, in the region of the Uraricoera River, shot the community residents. cd58e744c9870c18b180ece65a862fa91c0bac9c: The armed attacks by prospectors on villages of the Yanomami people and the consolidated invasions in the territory are part of a scenario that is also composed by a large volume of mining requirements incidental to IT, which deal with the MNA and are indicative of the great economic interests involved in the dispute for indigenous land and the omission of the State to curb invasions.
