7a30b17b59a8a73847e80bdd471f9d5c4a99898b: On October 5, 2021, the Maraguá indigenous community denounced the invasion of its territory by a raft in full illegal fishing activity, which took place on the Guarynamã River (Abacaxis), from which the indigenous people withdraw their livelihood. In addition, on the same date and place, the indigenous people also caught the invasion of a tourist boat, called “Mr. Magoo”, traveling the same river. The type of invasion resembles what, in 2020, resulted in a series of killings of indigenous and riverside people in the region, in the case that became known as the “massacre of the pineapple river”. The presence of non-indigenous people in the territory leaves the community vulnerable to various harmful and dangerous situations. The people also denounced, in 2021, the invasion of the territory for the theft of wood and hunting. By the end of the year, no measures to protect the territory and the indigenous people were taken by the responsible bodies.
28ef6177b72730c9a74e894cbc8acf74566ea0d2: Invasion of farmers; greasing; illegal logging; environmental damage
177aa6c2fe5e8f5ccf418d1b0ef2d63a48d29d50: The territory previously claimed separately by the two peoples – Jamamadi and Apurinã – has always been the target of invasions of farmers who occupy the land through the grigrage, with removal of wood both by the landowners, for the formation of pastures, and by loggers. In 2021, two visits were made to the boundaries of the territory; one with the Jamamadi people within the limits of their area (Lourdes) and the other within the limits of the area of the Apurina (Cajueiro), with leaders of the people. The visits followed the local CTL/Funai, the indigenous organization and the Cimi, and in both it was observed an extensive area deforested. In the Cajueiro were found several traces of the saws – gasoline, chainsaw chain, helmet hat, dropped centennial chestnuts and sawn wood. People lament because most of the fallen trees are used for the livelihood of the people through extraction. There are at least 400 indigenous peoples living in the two villages on the Acre border, who denounce, in addition to violence, the destruction of forests and centuries-old trees. In videos and photos, the indigenous recorded the destruction of chestnuts, copaíbas, ipês, cumarus and tucumãs. The fall of centuries-old trees would aim to shock the indigenous and push them further out of the region. They denounce that, at the end of July, the Cajueiro and Floresta villages were burned down by farmers, who also tore down the surrounding forest. Leadership reports that this time the invasion was greater. Since 2019, the first year of the Bolsonaro government, invasions and violence against indigenous people have intensified. Complaints have been made to Funai, MPF and press; the people are awaiting action.
1c20c695766d9b8bd61f81f025cd9a11997c7270: With Funai and the other organs of supervision and protection scrapped, without human and financial resources for inspection actions, the territory of the Kanamari people is a frequent target of the invasion of loggers, fishermen and hunters. The situation creates insecurity for the indigenous, constantly threatened by the invaders.
ee8011c83d5e5a429b7a4b59084b5d9fb580e576: The Federation of Indigenous Organizations of Rio Negro (Fourn) denounced to the MPF intense mining activities at the mouth of the river Cauburis, between the municipalities of Santa Isabel do Rio Negro and Barcelos. At least two dredges were seen operating illegally between the Middle Rio Negro I and II ITs in the first days of April. Illegal activity, in addition to causing high environmental risk in the region and on the planet, also contributes to the spread of coronavirus and other diseases transmitted by non-indigenous people to indigenous and local riverside populations. One of the factors identified by Foirn as facilitators of the advancement of illegal activities is the lack of supervision by public agencies. According to Marivelton Baré, President of Foirn, the population is outraged: We were surprised by this complaint of these dredges entering the territory illegally to extract ore. He had no consultation, no legality, especially because it is an indigenous land. We are outraged.” Foirn also criticizes the federal government and the bills that are under way and aim to withdraw indigenous rights.
b7fadc2c381d76e9cc6140bad345651fd8ffeffd: As occurred in the previous year, in 2021 the Mura of Itaparanã IT Wall, located in the BR-230 (trans-Amazon highway), reported numerous invasions in their territory, with the overthrow of chestnut trees and other species of trees within the area of use of the village. The situation has affected the Itaparanã stream, from which the Mura draw water for consumption, and the subsistence hunting practiced by the indigenous, because the overthrows drive away the animals. The village, surrounded by farms, is in vulnerable location, and the people again denounced the situation to the responsible bodies.
ef0bdafff47e18768240a60b777e71d23ed616c1: The indigenous reported an increase in mining and the presence of prospectors in the region in 2021. The prospectors settled in the river Puré, near the villages Jutaí, Deus Proverá, Jeremiah, Philadelphia and Mount Muriá, the people Maku Nadëb, the village New Canaan, the Kanamari people. The situation had already been reported since at least 2019, and intensified in 2020, in the middle of the pandemic. The municipality of Japurá (AM) is the base for arrival of prospectors seeking to extract gold in the rivers Puré and Joami, in the Ecological Station Federal, for the exit of gold extracted in the region via river and air for Manaus and Porto Velho. There is a true city of open - air prospectors who practice the exploitation of gold and the trading of prostitution. Some indigenous people are enticed by the prospectors to have their dredges and materials hidden inside the lakes in the indigenous lands whenever inspections by the PF and Army take place. The prospectors offer to the indigenous people, in return, favors” such as money, fuel, motor generator and even work in the mining dredges. The prospectors pass wrong information to the indigenous – for example, that the mining had already been legalized in the ITs by the president through the approval of the law (PL 191). The strategy of the prospectors is to hold meetings with the villages separately; they enter with small dredges and take gold samples to show that the land has potential for exploration, with which the indigenous would have many compensations. With the absence of the State, Funai's collapse and fragility in the public policies offered to indigenous peoples, grooming has caused divisions and internal conflicts. Funai that has no logistical conditions to visit the areas, does not seek information with the leaders and the indigenous cannot have contact with employees of the agency, which has only one server to cover eight municipalities. In addition to mining, the indigenous also denounce the invasion of IT by loggers and fishermen.
907d3cc97e6fc3f63edda6dbdc0a27564ce153ca: The Paraná do Paricá IT, Kanamari people, located in the municipality of Maraã, remains invaded by non-indigenouss who enter the territory for predatory fishing practice in preserved lakes. In the two villages that are within IT Paricá, the indigenous peoples mentioned that the invasions that had occurred in previous years for the withdrawal of fish, mining and drug trafficking remained intense in 2021. With the pandemic, the presence of prospectors, traffickers and illegal fishermen around and within indigenous areas was enhanced. The indigenous mention they are without protection and support from Funai, which only makes sporadic visits in the villages of the region, and other environmental agencies to monitor the area and fight the entrance of the invaders. There have already been surveys of two IT communities, São Francisco and Ponta Branca, by prospectors who requested the authorization of the leaders for the search for gold within the area, offering compensation for mining. The question of predatory fishing is another serious problem that has increased within IT, practiced most of the time by people living near the territory or in the city of Maraã (AM). According to the leaders, some indigenous people are also attracted by drug traffickers for sale and consumption. The indigenous people mention that, even knowing that they will not accept and release the mining and sale of drugs, they are constantly approached by people unknown with proposals in this sense, which causes tension and fear in communities. Threats are constant and all this has changed the village's routine in its subsistence activities, such as fishing, because the indigenous are afraid to be approached by illegal fishermen or by traffickers/pirates, who go up and down the Japurá river frequently. Constantly, indigenous and non-indigenous who navigate the river have their belongings – money, gasoline and engines – stolen by pirates, who act violently.
565310426489ce714618e42911e23d62a5456173: Opening of extension near IT; deforestation; burning
ed6034faa4825d742aad24286a67c862ac89d1ac: Since 2019 a coordinated action among entrepreneurs from the municipalities of Lábrea, Canutama and even from other states has orchestrated the opening of a branch linking the district of Belo Monte, in the municipality of Canutama, to BR-319. For such action, a tractor and a team of people are being used. Several lots that are on the banks of the branch are already being marketed. Consequently, the cases of downfall, deforestation and burning are constant in the summer period. This happens very close to TI Pauzinho, which already feels the pressure of some of the owners of lots that are opening stings surrounding their area. There are reports that this branch passes through the area of isolated Indians (catawixi).
488138f707858aad0c960dabb4c1ec1272c9ded3: Invasion; illegal exploitation of natural resources; illegal logging; illegal hunting and fishing
dbf09cf5b3ba520a81e03bb8119a7531b80c5488: In April 2021, the Kokama and Ticuna people carried out the self-demarcation of the Porto Praia de Baixo IT, located in Tefé (AM), in the region of the middle Solimões river. The community, composed of about 500 people, has been facing for decades the conflicts related to land ownership, because there are people who claim the land traditionally occupied by the indigenous without presenting the documentation proving the right about them. They feel the right to send people to withdraw natural resources from the site without asking permission or informing the indigenous. Self-demarcation was a measure to try to stop invasions of the territory, which are recurrent, were already denounced to the public agencies and intensified in 2021. The community suffers pressure from fishermen, large and small loggers, hunters and collectors, who remove wood, sand, pebble, fish, hunts, kelons, above all, wood and sand, which are removed in great quantity and marketed. Even without Funai's answers, we decided to protect and care for our territory, because only we know how important it is to us and to the future of our children and grandchildren ", say the people in the communiqué released after self-demarcation.
1c95d4af0c366b44f77f8e28686c048ebda995df: As already reported in previous years, TI Rio Manicoré continued to be the target of the invasion of ranchers and farmers who make use of a branch coming from the district of Santo Antônio do Matupi in Manicoré (AM). There are several sawmills on site, and the invaders continue to act with impunity, without being harassed by the bodies responsible for environmental and territorial surveillance in the region.
c50a7402c9839d88239408b514a914582ff1cdad: Invasion; road construction within IT; illegal logging
17bd0174078442e01b0c73fca895d34a0f9b80ed: Reports from the indigenous leaders indicate that the invasions followed active inside the Sepoti IT, where, during an expedition carried out by the Madeira do Cimi team and the Tenharim team in 2020, an area was identified with falls and a road opened by loggers, crossing the IT and possibly forming a route between the BR-230 (Transamazônica) and the banks of the Sepoti River. Complaints have already been sent to Funai and PF, but the situation followed in 2021.
8585526b4215663903f2ee9b199d3154012f5130: In November 2021, more than 300 ferries were identified along the course of the Madeira River near the municipalities of Autazes and Nova Olinda do Norte (AM). The dredges were working on gold extraction, however, in the state of Amazonas the mining is considered illegal. The huge concentration of vessels, registered in images that had great repercussions, was called by the media of floating cities”, due to the large number of ferries. Several communities are directly and indirectly affected by the mining in the region, both those located on the banks of the Madeira River and those located on other watercourses nearby, interconnected or affluent of Madeira, such as the areas located on the Black Pantaleão River. The most directly affected ITs are Soares/Urucurituba, Paurú, Maraguá Pajy, Ponciano, Apipica, Patauá, Jauary, Paracuhuba, Cuia, Trencheira, Padre, Miguel/Josefa and Coatá-Orange. The mining in the river contaminates the waters, vegetation, animals and consequently people who enjoy these natural resources, such as the peoples Mura, Maraguá and Munduruku. Some of these lands are still without provision for their demarcation or the paralyzed demarcation process, which makes them even more vulnerable to the pressure of invaders. Mercury, a chemical used to separate gold from the bottom of the river, is highly dangerous and is in the environment for a long time, causing serious damage to the health of the environment and the population. In addition, the presence of prospectors in the region generates risk of conflict and contamination, amid the pandemic. After the great repercussion of the case and the national and international pressure, the PF organized an action to combat mining, exploding and burning several mining vessels – according to the information disclosed, the operation resulted in the destruction of 131 mining ferries and the arrest of three people, seized with 150 grams of gold illegally extracted from the Madeira River rail.
f1d379ada5aed41c96ba3c72dc7330aa582e7a14: Just as in the other ITs of the region, the branches that were opened linking the district of Santo Antônio do Matupi, region of Manicoré (AM) with the presence of several loggers, continued to be used by invaders who entered the Tl Tenarim Marmelos for illegal logging. By 2020, the indigenous had identified that invaders are making allotment In November 2021, more than 300 ferries garming illeg gold on the Madeira River, near the municipalities of Autazes and Nova Olinda do on the banks of the Juqui River, opening clearings and placing landmarks. Despite the complaints, there was no news that in 2021 this situation was investigated or interrupted by the authorities.
2a99e096f8b9bf2b8afa2786143ab201a8b89fc4: Invasion; buffalo farming; water pollution; environmental damage
5ebc02fb6ee692d53997d8f339919de476e6d914: Since 2017, the indigenous people of the Mura people have denounced the creation of buffalo on farms around their territories. In 2021, the problem continued and intensified. This is a great concern of the inhabitants of the village Taquara. The buffaloes are animals that do not support heat, so they live all the time in the water of the river, of which the village has total dependence. There's no fence that holds these animals. Farmers put up electric fences, but it still doesn't. Besides not holding the animals, the electric fences cause risk to the population, especially when they go fishing at night, because they do not see the fence and the person ends up being electrocuted, if already occurred in the village. When farmers enter the village with new buffaloes, they make a point of washing the rafts in front of the community in order to embarrass the indigenous and pollute the waters even more. Until the buffalo entered the region, the Mura report that the waters were clean, transparent; now even the springs are dead. Rather, they say that they could see up to the bottom of the river, the algae and the fish, as they say: we are angry fish by day”. Now they can't even see the branches to divert the canoes. Another problem resulting from dirty water are diseases such as mycoses, stomach problems, diarrhea, vomiting, fever and others. Because of the buffalo, indigenous people are forced to buy food, thus changing their eating habits. The Indians can't plant because the buffalo spoil everything, destroy the swiddens. When they dry the streams it is even more risky, because they approach the Photo: Bruno Kelly/Greenpeace galmente congregated the North (AM) population, entering the community and preventing the circulation of people. Animals also cause material damage: they carry meshes, spoil fences, and eat clothes extended to the poles. In addition to the pollution generated by the habits of these animals, there is the one that stays in the fences made by farmers, who leave remnants of bottles and styrofoam in the water. There is an urgent need to remove these buffalo from the territory, as they have been causing much damage to the indigenous population, generating the need to install a system that cleans the water. Since 2017/2018 complaints have been made; in 2021, again, the case was denounced to the MPF, the Regional Coordinator of Funai, the DSEI, Seduc and IPAM, but no measures were taken.
e077e6d400dbccd3c62a83040d4801b4ec839154: Farmers neighboring TI Reach, near the Taquara Village, deforest and rub several areas; when the bush starts to grow, they spray pesticides. When it rains, these products go into the river, leaving even more contaminated water and fish. The poisons are Tux and DMA, applied together to ensure efficiency, which, for the indigenous, is even worse. The river that bathes the village is the only water that has access and is causing them serious health problems. Farmers don't even perform the correct disposal of the product containers, throwing them directly into the river. In addition to polluting the water, they endanger the health and life of children and uninformed people who can take this material and contaminate themselves, as has happened some years ago. Complaints were made to MPF, Funai, DSEI and IPAM. By the end of the year, no provision was made.
7aa7eb17a48d1b38724b1d91254af4286a2eeb79: Invasion; buffalo farming; illegal hunting and fishing; environmental damage
5143215886aa8deb1cdcfc06a1919b839631be69: For years, the families of the indigenous people Mura have faced problems with the presence of armed invaders in their territory, which is in the process of land regularization, just awaiting approval. The buffalo breeders have floating within the territory of the Mura Indians. In addition to the environmental damage caused by deforestation and pollution, there is theft of fishing and hunting. There are 15 floats that belong to buffalo breeders – among them there are breeders who are employed by other farmers and buffalo owners, too. Complaint has already been made to the MPF, but without result.
97b2460ad65535126804c1e5978e36c5818d5480: The Maku Nadëb people report the increase in the presence of prospectors in the Puré river, in a region close to the village Nova São Joaquim. The practice of illegal mining in the region of the municipality of Japurá (AM) had already been denounced in recent years and intensified further in 2021. Funai’s precariousness and disassembly – with only one server available to serve the entire region of the Middle River Solimões and Afluentes – makes effective supervision actions impossible. With the installation of the mining in the Puré and Joami rivers, the indigenous report that invasions for fish and wood extraction increased significantly in the year 2021. Armed with chainsaws and fishing utensils, invaders enter the areas and remove various species of lawwood and large quantity of fish for sale. The indigenous report that they seek to protect and monitor invasions in the territory, but are threatened and the invaders, who enter the area without any fear, generating conflict and fear.
f55be3627510b9dbe1ccceb318372ed50417a3ba: In 2021, the presence of prospectors continued to be a constant in the Jandiatuba River region, within the Javari Valley IT, putting at risk the lives of indigenous peoples living in IT and even isolated peoples. Jandiatuba's Etnoenvironmental Protection Base (BAPE) - one of the five responsible for IT protection - was reactivated in 2017, after an operation against mining in the region in 2016. In spite of this, she does not count on the presence of any security force and had, in 2021, only one Funai server available for work at the Base, which often ends up being in charge of collaborators and indigenous people. The situation generates vulnerability for indigenous people and servers and reflects the general context of disassembly of the indigenous body, characterized in an internal document of October 2021, obtained by the website Stay Knowing via the Access to Information Law, as of extreme lack as to its own workforce”. According to the document, only in relation to the work linked to people in voluntary isolation, Funai had only 109 effective servants in the 11 Etnoenvironmental Protection Fronts and 24 BAPEs responsible for the protection and supervision of more than 70 ITs – resulting in about 709,000 hectares to be monitored by each server, in regions where death threats occur and there is a context of difficult displacement and communication.
fa3c1944dc237dcceb5e61b9cc6d40b0a59d7432: Between August and September 2021, the Unijava Surveillance Team (EVU) carried out its first mission in the Javari Valley IT, in the region of the Itaquaí, Ituí and Quixito rivers. The EVU was created in order to strengthen the autonomy of the peoples of Javari and, in a scenario of disassembly of the supervisory agencies and Funai, to gather information about the invasions to the territory to support the actions of state protection. According to one of the services of Univaja, the team was created and trained with the help of supporters not to let the systemic and programmed weaknesses of Funai be the way to the destruction” of IT. In addition, Univaja claims, with this practical action, that the State guarantees “the active participation of indigenous peoples and their basic organizations as fundamental elements for any action aimed at protecting our territory.” In this mission, the EVU identified traces of the intense presence of the invaders throughout the length of the rivers and in several lakes and streams searched. The expedition even came across invaders in canoes on one of the mission nights. The indigenous arrested one of the illegal fishermen and took him to the Funai Protection Base of the Ituí River, in a nearby location; despite the presence of National Force police officers, they were informed by the Base's server that he had “superior orders not to carry out seizures of offenders in the indigenous land due to the pandemic” and that the police force “was there to do only the security of Funai servers”. More than 60 points were recorded with these traces along the rivers Ituí, Itaquaí and Quixito. The points indicate the occurrence of illegal camps, poleways opened by fishermen, large and interconnected with each other, traces of fire and even shells of turtle eggs. Fishing equipment and even fiber bags used to transport tracajas, turtles and salt pirarucu were also found. The complaints were forwarded to Funai, PF and MPF, among other organs. Univaja also elaborated, along with indigenous leaders and organizations, Funai employees and indigenists with experience in the region, a Plan for Territorial Protection of the Javari Valley, referred to the Federal Court in the framework of an action moved by the MPF to force the Union and Funai to ensure "humans and minimum materials" for FUNAI BAPEs in the Amazon. Nevertheless, the context of disassembly of the indigenous agency and its operational capacity remained throughout the year.
f00c4e34b6f759609d96432c20131d237917e2cd: Invasion; illegal hunting and fishing; illegal logging; mining
9231331795521c063a18766f7c4545ac5193bd49: In May 2021, the Amazonian Front of Mobilization in Defense of Indigenous Rights (FAMDDI), composed of several indigenous organizations, indigenous and civil society, handed to the president of the CPI of the Pandemic in the Senate a petition denouncing the serious contamination situation by Covid-19 among the indigenous peoples of Amazonas. Among other topics, the petition led the CPI to report a leadership of the Kanamari people on the situation of Javari Valley IT, a region where there is the largest concentration of indigenous peoples in voluntary isolation in the world. The invaders – prospectors, loggers, hunters and fishermen – act with total freedom ", points the leadership. “They are encouraged by the federal government and by the weakening of the protection system of Indians isolated from Funai. The situation is even more critical with the spread of Covid-19 throughout the Javari Valley, which can cause genocide of isolated relatives”.
5324ae91563048aa69a573cfac4525aef25d6dbe: Since 2019, the Association of Kanamari of the Javari Valley (Akavaja) has denounced the advance of mining activity in the Jutaí river, within the indigenous territory. In this region the Kanamari people and the people of recent contact Tsohom Djapa inhabit. To enter the territory, the prospectors attract indigenous and disseminate alcohol. Without supervision and effective actions of the responsible bodies, the situation remained in 2021. In addition to the degradation of the river and the whole area, the activity is a major threat to the way of life of peoples, spreading diseases that endanger the existence of Tsohom Djapa.
699e4386c3c2bcaf7eb3588bebbd39a029465593: Possessory invasion; greasing; illegal logging; illegal hunting and fishing
e6c72aef1e08298955f2e96bb3ca92f83d2cbf6c: The Valparaiso IT is claimed by a group of indigenous people of the Apurinã people who have been fighting for the demarcation of the land since 1991. This area has always been inhabited by these people who, in their simplicity, never imagined that there should be a limit to living. The present generation, having more knowledge of this, began to fight for demarcation. This territory has suffered serious invasions by landowners, fishermen, hunters. The people have kept expeditions on the borders of the territory often and have been faced with ever greater deforestation. In March, even with the flood period, a group of indigenous peoples maintaining the routine of visiting the borders, came across a large area deforested. The people have denounced the MPF and the MPE, as well as the regional Funai, but no action has been taken.
ab2634c4732699cc9d3f5e5772a7581c0fff7e32: A fire in TI Old Village reached eight kilometers of native vegetation in an environmental protection area. About 350 families Pataxó live on site, but the fire occurred far from the houses.
8321f405e804d1b1d94836d374b22c057c4beac4: With the social distancing and the need for people to stay home due to the Covid-19 pandemic, many tourists decided to settle in the southern end of Bahia. Foreigners, mainly of high financial power, have bought lots at TI Barra Velha, on the coast. These lots are often advertised by social networks. Since the demarcatory process does not advance, the Pataxó leaders are threatened by buyers and sellers and thus cannot move to the area to manage the territory and expel the invaders. Complaints were made to Funai and the MPF, which were not answered.
9f3f1e0efdab4dbdda3f31284f7053bc347ecfde: The village Pequi, resumed by the Pataxó people in 2012, has been suffering a series of invasions by tourism-related entrepreneurs and farmers. On December 5, 2021, the leaders denounced a allotment made by an entrepreneur who had already recognized indigenous ownership in the area. With the entrance of machinery and trucks, the invasion threatens the construction of health facilities, church and culture areas of the Pataxó people. Denunciation was sent to the state of Bahia, Funai and MPF for protection of the territory.
c653e94dac71bfecda16c4a8b9aa8d515139655c: The Xakriabá people of Cocos, in addition to facing the slowness of Funai to regulate its territory, still suffer from the progress of projects of Small Hydroelectric Centers (PCH) to explore the rivers of western Bahia, vital for the survival of indigenous and riverside communities. There has been harassment about communities, with the attempt to buy and negotiate land by companies, which circulate drones in communities and carry out markings in the river. The Itaguary River passes through the Xakriabá IT and it is from it that the community withdraws the fish for its livelihood and for activities in general. These are medium- and long-term damage and damage seen in construction movements in the region, in addition to all the environmental and psychosocial impacts that these activities bring with them – not to mention the imminent risk of the dam bursting, such as recent disasters in Minas Gerais. Indigenous leaders have denounced the situation to the responsible bodies and the Movement of People Affected by Dam (MAB) denounced the package of violations in various communities to the MPF, which entered with civil inquiry and met with one of the companies involved. By the end of 2021, the community had not received a return from the organs.
d301062536d1670990a981ee722ac40cb6183d28: Damage to heritage; destruction of tents
241f35749b0feb1804285984ba37edf89b949430: The conflicts faced by the Pataxó in TI Ponta Grande were diverse, with main activity of the hotel and aviation sector, because the area has great tourist appeal. Since the resumption of the land, the situation has become tense. On August 31, 2021, believing that the local leaders would mostly be in Brasilia, following the judgment of the general repercussion process, the City Hall of Porto Seguro brought down eight craft shops Pataxó that were on the edge of the city – which is recognized indigenous land. The action took place without any administrative or judicial decision justifying the operation. An investigation was initiated by the MP, who did not find who was responsible for bringing down the stores.
0bd676b5d949c49359bb0608d3eaf172ebfcc6aa: The city of Caucaia, once again, destroyed two beach tents of the Anacé people, using machines. The site, besides giving access to the beach and being a safety point, is a means of direct subsistence of ten families. The situation impacts the entire Anacé population, of about 3000 people, who use the area to perform their leisure and spirituality practices. The community denounced arbitrariness to the DPU Regional Human Rights Defender (RDH).
ec0ed106b1f75c2f52bb73799a4916087f7e4289: The São Francisco River Integration Project that is being implemented in the region by the state government of Ceará, through the State Department of Water Resources and with federal government resources, has caused serious damage to indigenous peoples and local populations. The project divides the territory, disaggregates the people and suppresses the native forest, impacting directly on the decrease of biodiversity of fauna and flora with equipment and machinery that are building canal for water transposition. The state disorganizes and precarizes the way of living and the cultural and socio-environmental practices of the people through the removal of the population, deforestation (including the riparian forest of the Carás River) and the grounding of cacimbas and wells, hindering access in other reservoirs, besides the excavation and cutting of the territory for the construction of the canal, impacting it directly. Complaints were sent to the MPE, MPF, Iphan to the Municipal and State Departments of Environment and Funai. The community has been mobilized in these complaints and, until the end of the year, it was still waiting for measures.
c4ee09710bb4e2ffe187681b7789e5fd34c880cd: Deforestation of sacred area and cemetery
93d11eea246a2e81a60e1ad6b084745c08c846bd: In a situation of total disrespect, a real estate enterprise destroyed the center of the terreiro, the sacred forest and the indigenous cemetery of the Potiguara people for construction of allotment and pasture of cattle. The site is considered sacred to the spirituality of the Potiguara people and the Pajé Cícero Ponte, being used by the people for more than 30 years. The leaders reported the MPE and the MPF and the case was widely reported in the local press.
96ad7a3028311ad0e58e62f1ab732c7349167afc: Illegal logging; sand removal; IT reduction
57a31fc37eb061a3b6cc72b9e1c9b2ce563722dd: The complaint of illegal extraction of clay, sand and wood at TI Tapeba in Caucaia (CE) revealed a mystery and, at the same time, the focus of a possible fraud. The City, by inspecting the area under complaint, found the illegality of the extraction of ores without licensing” and, when crossing the data on the land where the activity was being carried out, found that Funai shrunk the indigenous land by about 100 hectares. The technicians of the Institute of the Environment of Caucaia (Imac), accompanied by the Civil Guard and the Military Police, carried out the inspection on October 30, in order to find out if the complaint was coming or not. By confirming the illegality of the mineral holding, Imac decided to stop the activities and notified those responsible for the mineral exploitation. The City has also forwarded requests for information to Funai on the Indian area. When investigating whether illegal mineral activities were in the Tapeba lands, the technicians of the Caucaia Prefecture found, in fact, that the map of the area at the disposal of Funai's regional coordination showed differences in relation to the land delimited by the National Mining Agency. The councilman and lawyer Weibe Tapeba (PT) reported how the suppression occurred in 100 hectares of the indigenous area. “We only found that the area had been removed when there was the environmental licensing process of clay mining in the area adjacent to the reserve. Funai's regional coordination said the area was indigenous. It was then that the mining company showed the new maps made by Funai in Brasilia ", reported the leader of TI Tapeba in Caucaia, which houses, in 5.2 thousand hectares, 7,000 indigenous.
af95004d3ab1aa15575862ed745d016258b66374: Fire occurred in TI Tremembé da Barra do Mundaú reached an area used as a sanitary barrier against Covid-19 and also a hut, used as a collective space, very important for the community meetings. The leaders believe it was an attack on the community. Erbene Tremembé reports that cases of violations of indigenous rights are frequent and that punishment is never applied to those responsible for the acts. The people ask the authorities to strengthen actions in defense of the territory, identify criminals and punish those responsible for the crime. Civil police investigate the case and the State Department of Public Security reports that Military Police battalions support community actions with Funai agents.
2f869686686a5cef92430499f1d8454e94a11bc5: Invasion; deforestation; predatory hunting and fishing
167e777b8361470827008bd918dd7d4e94465528: A PF operation arrested seven suspects in invading the Avá-Canoeiro IT in Minaçu, northern Goiás. Several properties have been erected in this IT. Agents destroyed the properties, controlled and supervised by Ibama, aiming at preserving the environment and reducing environmental impacts. About 50 federal police officers served 21 judicial warrants, seven temporary arrest warrants and 14 search and seizure warrants, issued by the Single Court of Federal Justice of Uruaçu. Those investigated may answer for the crimes of invasion of public lands of the Union, criminal association, destruction of permanent preservation area, illegal deforestation, hunting and illegal fishing, and the crime of preventing the regeneration of native vegetation within the indigenous land.
874dd72cca9ccbef8ea57a03040d82e384256acc: In an attempt to contain and prevent the advance of an even greater number of indigenous invaders, the Ka’apor carried out self-defense actions. In November 2021, they closed a branch of loggers and stakers in the indigenous land, and placed a sign at the edge of the territory warning that the people will not accept the entrance of invaders. Natural resources and the whole environment have been exploited and devastated by invaders who, in addition to stealing and destroying, still threaten and commit violence against indigenous people.
bef4b7c30941ff79b810123ef59bc77c5f0012a1: Around 95,000 feet, 11,580 seedlings and 9,000 seeds of cannabis sativa (macogna) were found and destroyed by PF of Maranhão in the indigenous lands of Alto Turiaçu, Alto Rio Guamá and in Union lands. The actions took place in July 2021 and are of the fourth phase of Operation Fusarium ", which aims to disrupt the marketing of drugs. For more than a decade, the indigenous have denounced the invasion of their territories by loggers, farmers, hunters, among others, who commit all kinds of illicits, destroying the entire environment and endangering the safety and life of indigenous families in the region.
7e7de0cfd8d3d6bf54fa18f9b2da8a12d817e2ba: In October 2021, a video released on social media shows hunters invading the Arariboia IT and exhibiting a huge black ounce shot down. In addition, the hunters made a threat to the Guardians of the Forest: if you don’t want to die, don’t risk it in front of me, if I did it with an animal like this, imagine with a guardian”. The “guardion” to which the hunter refers in his speech are the indigenous people of the Guajajara people who created the protection and surveillance group of the indigenous land, the Guardians of the Forest, and who monitor the areas of ethnoenvironmental conservation trying to contain and combat, with much dedication, but little or no financial support, deforestation, fire and invaders. A few days later, the two hunters were arrested by the police in the municipality of Arame. For over a decade, indigenous peoples living in the region have denounced the invasion and depredation of their territories. Deforestation, fires, the presence of illegal hunters and collectors, as well as the advancement of illegal agribusiness activities in these ITs, have culminated in a scenario of environmental collapse, conflict and death.
33d66bebe592ea89a41056b2920d55eb9dfd61fb: The PF destroyed more than 12,000 feet of marijuana and 5,500 seedlings of the plant, cultivated by invaders in the IT Arariboia, in the regions of Amarante and Buriticupu. The operation was named Hefesto and is another unfolding of the combat actions carried out by the PF in the region, in order to expel invaders from indigenous lands, who practice, in addition to deforestation, illegal logging and illegal mining, illegal marijuana planting. The PF also carries out search and seizure warrants against loggers, as it discovered the criminal activity of invaders who knocked down thousands of trees in the preserved area, destining them for timber and furniture. According to the corporation, some loggers were installed on the margins of IT to receive illegal timber.
6a86d67e5da84d23fc562c618a7efa1e227994a0: The invasion of indigenous lands continues at an increasing pace, endangering the lives of indigenous peoples, including isolated peoples, such as the Awá-Guajá. Denunciations of logging raids led the Federal Police to trigger two operations to combat illegal logging in the Arariboia IT region in Maranhão. One action was carried out in Buriticupu and another in Amarante, with the aim of closing clandestine sawmills that operate in regions without permission from environmental agencies. According to PF, illicit activity stimulates invasion of indigenous territory and intensifies deforestation and the practice of other related environmental crimes, exposing the risk of the survival of indigenous communities, especially of isolated groups, the Awá-Guajás.
ae0bb919f440b49c5e7eda32566beca0cf847432: Invasion of farmers; deforestation; illegal logging
ef9dbe33becc49e3627d0664f4a64b6453fead70: After several complaints by leaders Guajajara concerning invaders entering its territory for illegal logging, the Federal Police performed an operation in the region in February 2021. According to the Federal Police, and as reported by the indigenous, several deforestation points were identified, as well as sawmills and furniture. The presence of demastadores represents a constant risk and threats for indigenous people, from the violence suffered, to the risk of infection of diseases, especially Covid-19. For the isolated indigenous Awá-Guajá who live in the region, the risk of this contact is even more serious. The situation has worried the Guajajara people, especially young people, who report that the invasions of hunters, loggers and farmers bring the expansion of soybeans, generate socio-environmental damage and cause the spread of alcoholism and drug use in villages, which is impacting the life and future of indigenous youth.
b5a412a8172a260cd922484b0c430bc1913fa115: The Bacurizinho TI was, along with the Kanela Memortumré TI and Pigs, one of the most affected by Normative Instruction 09, Funai, Maranhão. According to the Cimi survey, almost 30 of the 51.5 thousand hectares of the indigenous land were overlapping by 26 certifications of private properties – most of them from companies that have large land areas in the state. In practice, the area of Cerrado in process of demarcation – already declared of traditional occupation by MJ ordinance – is covered by large soybean crops that are increasingly advancing over the territory, legitimized by certifications. Roads and infrastructure works for grain flow also continued advancing in the Guajajara territory in 2021. In an on-the-spot survey carried out at the end of 2020, the Cimi Regional Maranhão team identified the existence of carvoarias that work in the area already declared of traditional occupation Guajajara. Among the companies that have certified large properties on IT Pigs are steel mills, which use coal in the processing of iron ore for the production of iron ore.
c11840df69d65935900e420327353c7f2c4e5a1b: The IT Geralda/Toco Preto, located in the municipality of Itaipava do Grajaú (MA), has been invaded by loggers for many years, and the situation remained in 2021. The indigenous leaders have denounced the invasion of the responsible bodies, no further action to combat illegal logging in the territory has been carried out.
d882f7e1474f6f5cae9dcc709e2a98b0cc049698: The indigenous people of Pyhcop Cati Ji continue to fight the invasion of loggers in their territory. In 2021, indigenous leaders went to the trawlers to seize trucks and chainsaws used in illegal logging. Complaints have been made to the responsible bodies, but the policy of protecting the territory has not been implemented.
cae3dc5a1b2295b0101360dc4dbe4aa9f284d761: The Kanela IT, in the municipality of Fernando Falcão (MA), has about 125,000 regularized hectares – in addition to another 100,000 hectares identified by Funai study as part of the traditional occupation territory of the people Memortumré Canela, in the process of revision of limits. The indigenous leaders have denounced that farmers are putting fences within the area already demarcated from the territory.
18c969ed6286e98cb36278ab8313bf32a51831d2: The indigenous peoples of the Memortumré Canela people have denounced the illegal exploitation of wood within the demarcated territory of the Memortumré Canela people – a problem that remains over the years, despite the complaints, and continued to occur in 2021. Most wood removed from indigenous territory serves to make coal and also goes furniture. Another recurrent situation in the territory, also in 2021, is the illegal invasion of hunters in the territory, including the occurrence of sexual harassment of invaders against indigenous women. The leaders report that several complaints to the competent bodies are made, but without effective measures.
2e63e921bfcfac4bb635442325ece4e2a3cde79c: The Kanela Memortumré IT, the result of the review of Kanela IT limits, has 100,000 hectares identified and delimited by Funai. With the administrative process affected by the paralyzing of the demarcations of indigenous lands, the area continues to be occupied by soy farms, which deforest the springs of the streams that pass through the indigenous land and are used by the indigenous people to bathe and exercise the cultural practice of fishing. Between 2020 and 2021, after the publication of IN 09/2020 by Funai, which released the certification of private properties on non-approved indigenous lands, a survey by Cimi identified that 22 farms were certified on IT, covering 34.4 thousand hectares of the area and promoting the devastation of the area by farmers and agribusiness entrepreneurs.
eb04b0bf3cbd2235c39ec9c95301b822ed25282a: The Krikati people have been waiting for more than 30 years for the disintrusion of their territory, which has 145,000 hectares and covers the municipalities of Montes Altos, Sitio Novo, Lajeado Novo and Amarante do Maranhão. There are more than 100 non-indigenous families who still live within the territory, making it impossible for the indigenous to enjoy full IT and deepening the degradation of the area that has already been approved as a land of traditional indigenous occupation. The situation is added to the recurrent invasions of hunters, farmers and some farmers within IT.
0a7cd5bcf0b798eacfc4b060cb65ba39bd7868c3: Due to the omission of the government in carrying out its duty to monitor and protect indigenous lands, leaders of the Krikati people created an indigenous forest guard in order to combat illegal logging in their territory. Invaders enter the Indian territory to take down and steal wood. Chain saws, huts and oil used by loggers have been found. In addition, the people denounce the invasion of the territory by illegal hunters year after year.
786dc7da8e222b1ef753eb7eff797a8f21d63b6a: Indigenous leaders of the Tenthar/Guajajara people continue to denounce the invasion of fishermen within their territory – a situation that followed in 2021. In recent years, the people have formed a group of Guardians of the Forest to combat this practice of illegal invasion, which has been happening for many years without provision by the responsible bodies. Illegal fishing is overwhelming because it is being done with nets known as calabous (type of net fishing to fish at the bottom of the river).
a6c8580dff0547b2a46d34985817b55bbd782aa9: The leaders of the Tenthar/Guajajara people denounced some years ago that non-indigenous people had invaded the territory in the place known as Lake Bolivia for cattle raising. In February 2021, women Guajajara who were on vessels recognizing the boundaries of their territory, accompanied by police officers of the 7th Battalion of the PM of Pindaré-Mirim (MA), came to be attacked by shots by settlers using the site. The invasions and conflict followed in early 2021, until, after a judicial decision, Funai was forced to strengthen the milestones that indicate the limits of IT. For now, the action has solved the conflict with non-indigenous people.
e98e640525b12566d7366db5401452c8a89d1db9: The indigenous leaders of the Apánjekra Canela people denounce that non-indigenous people continue to invade their territory to practice illegal hunting – a situation already denounced in previous years, but that remained in 2021. The Apãnjekra claim that the non-indigenous come from other municipalities to hunt within their territory, and report that several complaints to the competent bodies were made, but without effective measures.
c35c540735806436cd1460945420086faa8735a1: Invasion of farmers; greasing; illegal hunting
34a0aa5d91c79fbd99c4399940e793d5040383ab: Indigenous leaders report invasions by hunters, loggers, farmers and soy and corn companies that are batching and privatizing parts of the territory in areas of rural settlements, soybean fields and corn. In addition, they build roads with transit of trucks to flow commodity production. Many leaders are threatened with death, especially the Guardians of the IT Forest Pigs. Indigenous people are forbidden to walk certain roads within the indigenous land itself, at certain times, by the companies and farmers of the region. The situation is aggravated by Normative Instruction 09, published by Funai in 2020, which released the certification of private properties on non-approved ITs. According to a survey conducted by Cimi, 48 properties were certified on the IT Pigs, covering 48% of the 221.8 thousand hectares of the indigenous land.
6255a5aa6cbfb2270e79bc64cecd463bec9feabf: The Taquaritiua IT has not yet been demarcated and the stoppage of the Funai Working Group (GT) activities for the identification and delimitation of the territory has increased the insecurity and threats to the lives of the indigenous, due to the action of invaders and the presence of squatters, farmers and loose cattle that harm the environment and destroy the indigenous villages.
cd8c58046f3452eee58b26b5bbc2f995aedcf397: The Tremembé people of Engenho, whose territory is in the municipality of São José de Ribamar (MA), have already faced nine reintegrations of possession in recent years. In the territory, there are approximately 60 families living exclusively from the planting of vegetable gardens. Although Funai's Working Group (GT) to identify the area has been established, the work remains paralyzed, which enhances the actions of invaders. As in previous years, in 2021 the indigenous leaders denounced the advance of allotment of parts of the territory for the construction of housing project and for planting gardens made by non-indigenous.
ae6d58a8e9f627a23a432d2a34092b6dbe61ea15: On July 22, a forest fire hit the Bay of Guató IT, in the Pantanal region, in Baron of Melgaço (MT). This was the second time, the same month the fire destroyed the vegetation of the region. One of the concerns of the residents of the region with the fires is that there are no teams working on the control of the flames on site. In the first fire, which took place on July 5, the firefighters reported that due to the impossibility of accessing the site by land, the team flew over and found that the fire had self-extinguished due to the humidity of the vegetation of the site. At the time, two kilometers of forest were destroyed. Last year, the fire consumed about 2.1 million hectares of the area. The indigenous land was the only one where fire outbreaks were frequently recorded in the region, which had an 80% reduction in the number of fires compared to the previous year. In the rest of the areas, where the farms are, there are teams of Brigadiers and conditions of access to the Fire Department. In the Bay of Guató, the situation is worrying because of the density of the forest and the lack of roads in conditions of use.
1bda62186f8dc2153b2778272cf55baf2f71d48a: The Chiquitano IT, located 110 km from the municipality of Porto Esperidião, and 460 km from Cuiabá (MT), for decades has been waiting for Funai's identification and regularization. The Chiquitano families have always suffered violence, attempts at expulsion, the destruction of their rice, banana and corn gardens by the cattle of neighboring cattlemen, who freely fed there at the farmer's command. The families also had their ancestral cemetery disrespected and invaded, in addition to seeing contaminated the waters of the Turtle stream, from which they survived. Currently about 20 indigenous families live on site. Inside the small space has traditional houses, gardens, school, chapel, community hall and football field. According to the MPF, in 2006, an agreement signed with the owner of the São Pedro Farm, superimposed on the indigenous territory, guaranteed the Chiquitano community the ownership of an area of 25 hectares. But even after the agreement was concluded, the farmer ended up disrespecting the Chiquitanos' right of possession. Thus, the Posse Maintenance Action was assessed, in which the MPF sought to guarantee the possessive right of the indigenous community. As stated in the judicial decision of the 1st Civil and Criminal Court of Cáceres (MT), recorded videos show that the farmer went to the area of exclusive possession of the indigenous community Chiquitano, in the Village Novo Barbecho, uninvited, hindered the religious rituals of chiquitanos and proceeded to harass them, saying that he would spend the amount needed to remove them from the area [...] even after the judicial agreement was made”. The federal judge accepted the request of the MPF, granting possession protection, and ratified the injunction in favor of the indigenous community and in favor of the farmer, prohibiting him from doing any acts that affect the right of ownership of the indigenous community. If the court order is broken, the farmer must pay a daily fine of R $ 5 thousand.
20430e56ed23d060d458d0e76331b411dc225d29: Environmental damage; soya monoculture; use of pesticides
03c926bba5fe4a0a0f63e20e142147fcf697e0b4: In 2021, Rikbaktsa Indians suffered from a series of health problems that the people thought would occur due to pollution of the Blood River by pesticides. The Rikbaktsa, whose territory extends along the banks of the Juruena, Blood and Teles Pires rivers, have been reporting since 2020 the occurrence of itching, skin spots and diarrhea after the use of rivers water for bathing, fishing, food consumption and preparation. In recent years, soybean crops have extended along the banks of the River Blood, on the right side of the indigenous territory, with spraying of pesticides in crops near the river and territory. The technical report Indigenous Perception of Agrotoxic Contamination, published in 2021 by Opan, brought the following report of a Rikbaktsa, who chose not to identify himself: The fish is decreasing more and more in the river of the Blood, in the river Arinos and also in the river Juruena, because, precisely at the time of the piracema, rainy season, farmers spray the plantations with poison, which runs to the rivers, to the headwaters, killing the newly laid eggs”.
7a74f5a45edda66c33438ea3346bcabd7ad76f0b: Despite being demarcated and regularized, TI Jarudori is still invaded by squatters. In 2019, a federal court decision suspended the process of withdrawal of non-indigenous occupants. Although the MPF appealed and the decision was overthrown, the de-intrusion was not carried out and the process awaits decision in the TRF-1. Meanwhile, the community remains apprehensive about the undefinition of the land situation and the presence of invaders on their lands.
a68014b74f3bc330ec42b1b225b837155f111b09: In November 2021 representatives of the State Human Rights Council (ECDH-MT) were on visits to the Kanela people of Araguaia, checking on site the deforestation actions and pressures on the village Nova Pukanu, which had already been denounced in 2020. The area has been going through successive rubble, including surrounded allotments that prevent the free movement of indigenous people. The situation was denounced to the MPF, Funai, the Federal Police and various human rights agencies and supporters. The village Nova Pukanu was founded in 2016, in a part of the area claimed by Funai since at least 2007. In 2019, after judicial determination, Funai prepared a brief report that recognizes that the area of the village is insufficient for the physical and cultural survival of the people and recommends that the entire area of Gleba São Pedro is intended for the exclusive enjoyment of the Kanela community of Araguaia; the GT for identification and delimitation of the area, however, has not yet been opened. The report of the ECHR-MT was forwarded to the competent bodies, and the community is still awaiting action and a definitive solution for the people.
6f7923fd27f2e76eeec8c71c67e6dd4194211afc: A team of the Brazilian Army and Funai identified invasion and deforestation within the limits of the Kawahiva IT of the Rio Pardo and the Guariba-Roosevelt Extractive Reserve, in Colniza (MT), where there is the presence of isolated indigenous people who live exclusively within the forest, without any contact with the external society. An operation was carried out to combat environmental crimes in these protected areas, with FAB support. During helicopter overflights, Funai agents and Army troops were infiltrated through the aircraft's winch, as the area does not allow landing. According to the Army, illegal camps were found at the scene. The invaders fled as the helicopter approached and were not located. Colniza has the highest rate of deforestation in the state and the presence of invaders in this region puts at risk not only the environment, but also the survival of isolated indigenous peoples.
d72546b261cf0f2cae49ec25fbd331ded8a6e90e: Kayabi, despite being approved, is still occupied by large farmers. The process of IT de-intrusion was interrupted in 2013, when the STF accepted request for guardianship anticipation and suspended the registration in real estate registry of the indigenous land. In 2020, the RMP announced that it would convene the parties for dialogue, but the proposal was suspended due to the pandemic. The then Prosecutor of the 6th Chamber, Antonio Bigonha, stated that the land must be de-intruded. Meanwhile, much of IT remains unavailable for the exclusive enjoyment of the people, as it is occupied by farms of large owners and even a company controlled by the Canadian billionaire Brookfield fund. In 2020, the Public Agency’s investigation identified at least one of these farms the washing” of 3,000 livestock heads, transferred to a property outside the indigenous territory and later sold to JBS.
c615eaebe220f5659c4178c779100d06852d99c8: With the process of demarcation paralyzed by Funai, the Karajá people continue having their territory allotted and sold to third parties, as already denounced in 2020 – including with the performance of a councilman from Santana do Araguaia (PA). The Rèñoà Bero TI, named Karajá given by the indigenous peoples to the Beleza/Lago Grande River, has 4,627 hectares of surface and lies at the confluence of the Beauty and Araguaia rivers, in the northeast end of the state, in front of Bananal Island (TO). Funai's work to identify and delimit the area was started almost a decade ago and, in 2019, the study report was handed over to Funai's General Coordinator of Identification and Delimitation, but was never published. While the demarcation is paralyzed, the indigenous see their territory being appropriate and degraded by invaders. After denouncing the indigenous peoples, the MPF of Barra do Garças moved a Civil Action to try to resolve the situation. By the end of 2021, however, the situation persisted.
8a49200a1a8103c00df33785aceb249e414933f8: Even being declared since 2008, IT Manoki has been constantly invaded by loggers. The stopping of the demarcation process allows non-indigenous occupants to continue with their exploratory and degrading activities of the environment, especially agriculture. According to information from the leaders Manoki/Irantxe, with the Covid-19 pandemic, invasions increased substantially, mainly the activity of cattle farming within the territory. In March, during the search for suspects of farm robbery in the region, the Military Police caught a group of invaders in the Manoki IT. Four men were arrested for illegal logging, exploitation of natural resources in indigenous areas, illegal possession of weapons and others. The invaders even shot the police, but no one was hurt. Some of the men in the group managed to escape by going into the woods.
0832198e1707e1fc5de76c35dfb5f7e63fe439a5: The Mato Grosso Military Police arrested seven men after being caught removing wood from the Parabubure IT, from the Xavante people. They were arrested for the practice of environmental crime in an approach carried out after denunciation of Funai, which informed the illegal extraction of wood within indigenous territory. Police found, at the scene, a mounted camp, trucks, tractors, chainsaws, tools, wood and a 22 caliber revolver.
de5b1abbed80bf3e20f28dc033f948c5f37e2d32: Upon completing 60 years of creation, the Xingu National Park IT is surrounded and threatened by the advance of invasions and deforestation in its surroundings. Studies show that the region has already lost 32% of native vegetation. In addition to sheltering some 7,000 indigenous peoples from 16 different peoples, demarcation also helped protect biodiversity in a transitional area between the Cerrado and the Amazon forest, where 99% of native vegetation within the Park is preserved. But what concerns the peoples of Xingu is deforestation around the indigenous territory. The coordinator of the environmental NGO Instituto Centro de Vida, Vinícius Salgueiro, warns that there are hundreds of springs that today and increasingly are threatened by deforestation and degradation actions that occur in these municipalities. It is important that these areas that are degraded are recovered and that remnant of native vegetation that still exists in the basin is maintained.” Some rivers in the region are already very polluted, which concerns the indigenous peoples of Xingu, such as Jair Kuikuro: “Today we continue our struggle within our community, within our indigenous Xingu territory, knowing that today the fight will not stop here. The most important thing for all of us is the environment. Rio, fish and forests ", says the leadership.
219bd00c94a998383b3f855906985da5ddbc49e8: Satellite images and data show agricultural areas and fires spreading towards the park in 2021, points out material published by Mongabay. The situation occurred despite the ban on burning during the drought – which caused one of the largest droughts in the country in almost a century. Deforestation inside the park – a green island amid agribusiness – increased significantly in 2020, quadrupling the amount of primary forest lost there in 2019, according to Global Forest Watch data analyzed by Mongabay. According to the report, most were caused by forest fires, which probably began in agricultural areas adjacent to the park, in which there was cutting and burning vegetation. Satellite images show an open clearing between April and May 2021 very close to Xingu Indigenous Park – including an area along its border. Data from Deter, INPE system focused on real-time deforestation alerts, show that between June and July 2021, an area of 1,165 hectares had its vegetation degraded west of IT, in an area very close to the Xingu Indigenous Park. The INPE system also recorded, over 2021, large burn scars in the west and northwest portions of IT, in areas close to or overlapping with the boundaries of indigenous land. Some of these scars cover areas of 100, 200 and up to 990 hectares. In September, firefighters met occurrences inside the Xingu Indigenous Park. Site survey The Echo indicated that, in 2021, Ibama began the fire season with only 52% of the firefighting staff. Despite authorization to hire 1,659 temporarys, by the end of June only 869 had been hired by the agency, weakening the fight against fire.
c56d58dd19536697832959f37eb6e4661adc52ae: Between August and November 2021, the Deforestation radar indication system in the Xingu basin (SiradX), maintained by the Xingu+ network and ISA, identified several illegally opened branches in the Xingu Indigenous Park for wood theft. In these four months, the total extension of the illegal branches, located at the western border of IT, reached 26 km. This area, which is located near villages, has been explored since 2019. Lack of supervision and impunity motivate offenders to continue exploiting the natural resources of the territories, endangering indigenous communities.
71bb4d5d98cacf7f2b73e0264c71cc090bba8da2: In the state of Mato Grosso, deforestation has advanced and threatens the lives of the last two Piripikura indigenous peoples in the Piripikura Indigenous Land. Between 2020 and early 2021, IT lost the equivalent of 1,340 football fields. Only two indigenous people – Tamadua and Baita – live on site, in voluntary isolation. They have survived successive massacres against their people in the past decades. The territory is defined by a usage restriction ordinance, which is renewed for periods. In 2018, the ordinance was extended for three more years, and remained valid until September 2021, when it was renewed by Funai, but for only six months. Between August 2020 and July 2021, according to data from Prodes, inpe, more than 2,100 hectares were deforested in the indigenous land.
76f45750364f5e6afa9969c29510012d1f3c2847: The MPF received complaint that a bridge was built unlawfully on the Tarumã River, in the region of Fortuna, in the Portal do Enchanted IT, hindering access to water by the Chiquitano people. It was also denounced to the MPF that the water of the Tarumã river was reaching far below the levels considered normal for the Chiquitano, besides very dirty, getting dry at some points. The Military Police was called to investigate the report of pollution of the river and also illegal deforestation, within the indigenous land, using fire to suppress the forest and land permanent preservation area. All the complaints were confirmed and the MPF asked the Federal Court for the preventive arrest of the farmer, in addition to requesting that he be sentenced to the clearing of the river, through removal of the irregular bridge, the dissorption and unearthing of the area, ensuring the return to normal water flow in favor of indigenous communities, as well as the application of fines and other sanctions.
26c4394ce49e051191bbf905e9be9022a3ac4551: After several reports of invasions of the Sararé IT, mainly of prospectors, the PF and the Army performed an operation on site. Teams left by train from an improvised base in a town near Pontes and Lacerda, where illegal mining was found. Then they went on small boats along the river Sararé. There was a risk of confrontation, but when they arrived in the occupied areas, the prospectors had already fled. The equipment used in illegal exploitation was destroyed. The Sararé IT, where the Nambikwara people live, has just over 67,000 hectares and is close to the border between Brazil and Bolivia. The territory houses species of the Brazilian Cerrado and is rich in minerals. Therefore, it is the target of landowners and groups that invade the region for gold and wood. In addition to the destruction of the forest, these gangs threaten indigenous people and contaminate the environment. Illegal mining opens the crater and uses mercury to extract the gold. Heavy metal spreads through the soil and is then carried by rain and streams to the rivers of the region. An incalculable impact, according to environmentalists. According to Carolina Marçal, of Greenpeace, the expansion of new areas for mining has occurred especially within protected areas, which are indigenous lands and conservation units. This has an impact on the entire ecological chain, not only in the river, but also in the surroundings, on animals that feed on that fish, on humans that feed on those fish. It is a trail of destruction”.
9800f0ca4271dad71645f0ea7ed8628a20ad04f7: After several reports by the Bororo people, reporting the presence of invaders in IT Tadarimana for predatory hunting and fishing, PF performed an IT operation. PF agents and Funai servers served arrest warrants and search and seizure against suspected environmental crimes within the indigenous land. One man was arrested and three firearms, nets and objects used in predatory fishing were seized with him. The one investigated is part of a criminal faction.
78c8d314eac7e805ecd55dd7abe637ad544e348e: Another fire hit Tidarimana IT in Rondonópolis (MT). According to the Fire Department, the fire has been controlled and the causes will be investigated. This is the second time the Indian land has had a fire record in less than a month. The first fire started on August 1, and by the same week it had already been controlled, but another fire occurred at the end of August. In IT, 800 indigenous people live divided into eight villages. According to firemen, 12 military personnel were sent to the scene to carry out the fire fight. Although low relative humidity and high temperatures made it difficult to fight the flames, firemen managed to extinguish the forest fire at the end of the afternoon of the same day.
1039b6ba78e45188d7191ec9e34a3315b3a94026: After many reports of invasion and illegal fishing in Umutina territory by the indigenous people, police began monitoring the site. During monitoring, police noticed suspicious movement of vehicles at the entrance of the village. In the approach, police found and seized 550 kilos of painted in two cars leaving the village. There were also two men, one woman and two teenagers, who were arrested.
68898a93d4e305e67f5da5532f4392c3918674b1: A fire of great proportions destroyed an area of more than 4,100 hectares of native vegetation in TI Umutina, Mato Grosso, where more than 500 indigenous people of the Paresi people live. The dry bush and strong winds contributed to the spread of the flames. About a hundred officers from the Fire Department, Civil Defense, indigenous Brigadiers and the National Force worked in the fight against fire. Town hall machines opened up in the woods to prevent the flames from advancing. With the smoke, the indigenous people got lost in the forest, disoriented, because the open road to facilitate the advancement of combat teams was destroyed by the fire.
b87e424b1df6e3bf8f163f515b937d34fb87659e: The Urubu Branco IT, even before its demarcation and approval (1998), was invaded by illegal occupants from the time the Apyãwa (Tapirapé) began the resumption movement of their ancestral territory in 1993. Since then, these illegal occupants have managed to remain in the northern area of Urubu Branco IT, through successive injunctions that guarantee them the permanence, but not the bust of the indigenous land. However, this prescription has not been fulfilled, and they have not only deforested the region to deploy pastures but have also promoted illegal logging for commercialization. In 2020 and 2021, the Urubu Branco IT continued to suffer from depredation of its natural resources in a much faster way. Since the Bolsonaro government's inauguration, invaders and loggers have felt allowed to carry out more deforestation to implement new pasture areas and more logging for illegal sale of pau-brasil stakes. By 2020, an operation against deforestation and illegal logging had identified that the area was batched” among several bosses, who recruit the “peons”, and the Rural Environmental Register (CAR) of a property was identified by Ibama on site. Deforestation is putting at sacred local risk for the Apyawa, such as Yrywo’ywãwa, Waterfall of the White Urubu. In 2021, deforestation continued, and Ibama and PF launched yet another operation to combat deforestation at Urubu Branco IT. Minister Luiz Fux, on February 21, 2021, confirmed the decision of Minister Dias Tóffoli that had suspended the injunction that prevented the withdrawal of the invaders. However, the process of disintrusion of the area did not happen.
688fc2b09dbc7abbf4edb2081371adb4c5fa4b89: In June 2021, in front of news from illegal fishermen on the Tapirapé River, leaders of the Apyãwa/Tapirapé and Kanela people of Araguaia organized a surveillance operation and seized a speedboat (voider) that was with tourists from Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul. The Civil Police of Porto Alegre do Norte was warned and arrived at the site, where he also seized a pistol and two revolvers 38, in addition to a piarara fish 98 cm long. Tourists were taken to the police station of Porto Alegre do Norte, where a prison record was filed flagrantly for illegal possession of a weapon. Then a tourist from Goiânia and a boy from Confresa (MT) who were also fishing illegally on the Tapirapé River was seized. The scarcity of fish due to illegal fishing directly affects the survival of the Urubu Branco IT communities. The communities are Tapi’itãwa, Tapiparanytãwa, Towajaatãwa, Wiriaotãwa, Inataotãwa, Myryxitãwa and Akara’ytãwa. Likewise, it also affects the communities of Kanela do Araguaia, whose villages are located on the banks of the Tapirapé River: Village Nova Pukanu, Village Tapiraká and Village Porto Velho.
0dd6cb56bc7e4fe072e5c2c7a620d67d00974764: The IT of the Apyãwa/Tapirapé people is one of the indigenous lands that suffer most from invasions, illegal deforestation and theft of timbers. The 44-year-old man, identified as A.L.S., is considered one of the main responsible for the illegal logging of Urubu Branco IT, located between the municipalities of Confresa, Porto Alegre do Norte and Santa Terezinha. Research reports and environmental surveillance in the region indicate that A.L.S. was ahead of numerous wood extractions, including species protected by law, such as the Brazilian wood. In November 2019, even after being arrested in an environmental crime-fighting operation, he continued to act illegally. After being released, he acquired a truck and again removed wood from the indigenous land. In December of the same year, the investigated logger used three trucks to extract wood in the northern part of Urubu Branco. In April 2020, two more trucks were removed from the area loaded with Brazilian wood, a species that is protected by law, with its commercialization prohibited, and that since 2004 has been on the list of endangered Brazilian flora. An action taken by the Confresa Police Department in conjunction with Funai in May 2020 arrested two people extracting wood in the indigenous land at the direction of the investigated. A.L.S. is a defendant in environmental crime proceedings and responds to other criminal actions in progress for the same crimes committed in the region.
f2acd2be6ecaefe78297461bf823ad88c917c243: Satellite images caught a large extension of deforestation in an area adjacent to the Wawi TI, in the municipality of Querência (MT). The images record opening roads to plot preservation area, where it is forbidden to take down forest. The lots would be used for soybean planting and pasture opening. The advance of agribusiness in the region has been threatening the Suyá Indians (Kisêdjê) for at least five years. A farm that is next to IT has been boarded and fined for illegal deforestation last year; even so, the owner of the area says that once he has permission from the competent agencies, he will continue to overthrow the native forest. According to the farmer, they (indians) already have a lot of things, a lot of land, enough”. He, who is also a lawyer for agribusiness entrepreneurs in the state, says he did not deforest and that the cutting of trees was only to build the headquarters and shelters for the workers, “a very small area”. However, images of the Planet satellite, of MapBioma, and drones, reveal large clearings open in the middle of the forest, as well as roads that lead nowhere, serving to delimit three lots, in an area equivalent to 1,300 football fields, making it clear that it is a lot. Illegal deforestation was confirmed by technicians from the Department of the Environment, who embarrassed the area and fined the farmer. According to the indigenous Winti Khisetje, with the deforestation and advance of agribusiness and the use of pesticides very close to IT, “there is a great risk of reducing water resources, fish and animals that we hunt”. The case was also reported to MPF, Funai and PF.

8c86c75b8b3f5f280e76c375d5ad2852aedb1b0e: An operation involving teams of Ibama, Federal Police of Ponta Porã and National Force was carried out to investigate complaints of deforestation and illegal logging in an area of native forest vegetation within the Arroio-Korá IT. The biome is of Atlantic Forest and is considered of special protection, especially because it is within indigenous territory.
2a0e46e8626a39b8583d167f7ed4c2e1981ab485: Rural farmers who rented” areas within indigenous lands for planting GM soybeans and corn are causing major disorders. It is a true “rain of pesticides”, according to indigenous residents close to these areas, since in certain periods of soybean or corn crops are also sprayed with airplanes.
