With the lack of water at some points in the villages, they used the springs, but now they are afraid of contamination caused by pesticides. Some families that have no other alternative still seek to boil the water before consuming, but not all have this knowledge and, consequently, end up drinking water with poison, according to reports of Guarani-Kaiowá people iowá at tekoha Avae’te in Dourados (MS). In addition to housing, at least in Mato Grosso do Sul, and a Guarani Mbya, in Rio Grande do Sul residents of IT. Those who try to plant organic foods are also concerned with the spread of pesticides, especially by air.
a023227bc6a1f447f948987a4d5c104dd165b7db: Tekoha Ava’ete is one of the nine areas of recovery that have formed, over the last few years, on the borders of the Dourados Indian reserve, in the south of the state. It is a piece of land that the Guarani and Kaiowá understand as being theirs, since it was traditionally occupied by their ancestors, but that the Brazilian government never demarcated. It is also an area of conflict. Between the end of August and September, at least three indigenous houses were set on fire, in attacks sometimes accompanied by firearms. Those responsible for the attacks, according to the Guarani and Kaiowá, are private security guards – employees of the farms that dispute the same territory. Many people have been injured in the last four years,” says anthropologist Guarani-Kaiowá Tonico Benites, who follows the situation in Dourados. “Every two months, sometimes more often, a house is burned down. Families live under permanent violence”. The climate of constant violence in the region reflects, at least in part, a decision made by the Brazilian government just over 100 years ago. The Dourados indigenous reserve is now the most populous in Brazil: it houses more than 20,000 indigenous people in just 3.4 thousand hectares. While their territory is not demarcated, conflicts aggravate. The actions of the police authorities are insufficient to stop the clashes. In October 2020, the MPF issued a note pointing out the delay of the police in serving search and seizure warrants. The delay, according to the MPF, hinders the investigations and can “fruit the collection of evidence of the conflict”.
1f3df9bdacda5e404bae0287008b7405aef9d607: On September 6, 2021, private security guards of a besieger set fire to a dwelling of the Guarani and Kaiowá people on the Ava’ete tekoha in Dourados. The action took place around 11 a.m., and was filmed by the Indians. In one week, according to the community, at least three houses of the tekoha Ava’ete were burned by private security. Tekoha is one of the retakes located on the banks of the Dourados Indian reserve, in an area claimed by the Guarani and Kaiowá as part of the indigenous land, but occupied by private properties. Subject to a humanitarian crisis due to the overcrowding of the indigenous reserve, families have taken up the place – and suffered the intense and continuous violence of private security.
e27549f28ddd4ca1d444a3090f12efa8b41e463d: The great fires that hit the Pantanal National Park of Mato Grosso do Sul, Serra do Amolar and Porto do Indio and, in 2020, also affected the Guató IT, in the northwest of Mato Grosso do Sul, left serious consequences for the indigenous people living in the territory. This situation caused the people to face vulnerability and hunger in 2021, since the fires destroyed the plantations and biodiversity of the territory, affecting the livelihoods of the people.
586e2274b16f783baddfc8b905a93fae2e990993: The Kadiwéu IT was the only law protected region in the Pantanal of Mato Grosso do Sul that registered an increase in area burned by forest fires in 2021. In 2012, the MPF had warned of the devastation of this Kadiwéu region, attributing it to the action of local farmers – the same happened in 2018. IT, where about 2,000 indigenous people live, has been demarcated since 1981, but the lack of structure follows in some aspects. The indigenous people suffered from a lack of water supply in 2020. According to data from the Fire Department, there was an increase of approximately 25.2% in the attendance of forest fires. While in the period analyzed in 2020, there were 5,056 occurrences, in 2021 there were 6,332 cases until September. Kadiwéu IT had an increase of approximately 47.4% in the area corrupted by fire. Data from Inpe reinforce the high incidence of fires in the dry months, which usually go up to September.
5a4adc87fca5e733730d4a33f3e1ad75ee9f9f3d: A prayer house of the Tekoha Itay Ka’aguyrusu, of the Guarani and Kaiowá people, was set on fire early on December 29, 2021, in the municipality of Douradina (MS). Indian leaders believe the fire was criminal. According to the police report, the crime occurred around 1:00 a.m., while three teenagers and elderly women slept at the scene. Everyone could leave in a hurry, no injuries. One witness witnessed the crime with family members, and reported having heard people talking at the scene, as well as smelling strong gasoline and hearing gunshot sounds. Then he said that the fire began to take care of the main hut and consumed the entire structure in a few minutes. The witness believes the crime was motivated by religious intolerance. Space, which was straw, was completely destroyed. For the indigenous, the fire in the house of prayer represents an even greater spiritual loss than material loss. The Guarani-Kaiowá have been constant victims of this type of crime, motivated by religious intelligence
f0b67f9e95aa9e5778143702cd2e55a34192b3b3: Religious intolerance has been one of the main reasons for aggression against indigenous populations in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul. Several prayer houses in various ITs have been burned down, especially in recent years. On August 19, the victim was the 92-year-old Guarani Kaiowá Cassiano Romero, who had his prayer house set on fire in the village Rancho Jacaré. At the time of the fire, Romero was at the great meeting of Kaiowá prayerrs for the inauguration of another prayer house in the region. One of the leaders of the traditional culture and religion movement of his people, he lost to the flames objects of religious devotion, documents, appliances, clothes, a bicycle and other belongings. The house of prayer was his dwelling. He just took the clothes off his body. No one's been injured and no information on suspects yet. The indigenous relate the case to religious intolerance. They say that the praying man is the target of several threats and that he was beaten almost to death recently by unidentified people. They relate the episodes of violence to the growth of evangelical churches within indigenous communities. With their advancement, resistance was formed against our traditional religion”, explains indigenous anthropologist Tonico Benites, also Guarani Kaiowá. “Today it shows once again how much the prayerrs are persecuted” denounces Rosicleide Oliveira. The case is under investigation.
1f4beea9d3272ded4f40a820088f4a034b5e85e0: Another episode of violence and intolerance has become a scar in the history of the Guarani and Kaiowá peoples. On the night of October 19, a prayer house – Oga Pysy – in the Tekoha Rancho Jacaré, municipality of Laguna Carapã (MS), was the target of a criminal fire. Space became ashes after less than two months of the inauguration, held on August 29. Tonico Benites, leadership of Aty Guasu, stated that prayerrs and prayerrs are often threatened. They [prayer and preachers] were already suffering threats. They said they wanted to end the prayer houses and kill the praying people ", reports. According to Tonico, they had already tried to burn down the prayer house that was burned down at the Alligator Ranch. Rosicleide Vilhalva Kaiowá, Kuñangue Aty Guasu – Great Assembly of Women Kaiowá and Guarani, also spoke about the context of violence in the tekohas of the Guarani and Kaiowá peoples. “We are being threatened every day. Not only has a house of prayer become ashes, but also the lives of leaders, preachers and children. Today we see the threat and vulnerability within the tekoha, something that Justice does not see”, lamented. Leaderships and witnesses recorded a Report of Occurrence in the Civil Police of Laguna Carapã. The case has also been referred to the MPF and the Federal Police. The suspicion is that the attacks were carried out by farmers and religious groups in the region.
1236f3e99e20abd6d0dbad7724cce292c574fbc0: Indigenous Guarani and Kaiowá of the village Avae’té II, in Dourados, denounced burning of house and belongings, and attack on them. According to local media reports, a rural producer was arrested in Dourados for determination of the Federal Court. He responds to lawsuits due to constant clashes with indigenous people from neighboring areas of the Dourados Indigenous Reserve. He owns property nearby the village and rents lands included in the area claimed by the indigenous. Although the arrest warrant was issued by the Federal Court, it was the Military Police that carried out the order and took the producer to the headquarters of the PF. In September 2019, security guards hired by him were accused of firing shotgun fire in the direction of the Indians surrounding the sites almost three years ago. Addilson Benites, 64, was shot in the arm. In July 2021, Benites recorded a death threat report against the producer. He told me that he was threatened by the besieger at the entrance to the village and that it wouldn't be the first time. In September 2021, the guards of the besieger were accused by the Indians of burning a shack, built in the area that would be leased by him. In an interview with Campo Grande News, he said that he set fire to Kaiowá, in what he described as a moment of fury.” ” I went there and set fire to that shack, it was I who put it, I assume my responsibility, but it (barracus) was within the area that I am renter ", admitted. The MPF requested the pre-trial arrest of the besieger for murder in the attempted form, as it took the risk of killing someone by setting fire to the house.
c4f01f8f5c71f744db47c23204c7a1d75c81b5ff: Mining; lack of water; environmental damage
69d7d9f578a2e978ca2cf1b5d6ac978dab88361a: Since the disaster-crime of the collapse of the dam of rejects in Córrego do Beanão, da Vale, the indigenous community Pataxó that lived on the bank of the Paraopeba river has suffered with lack of water, with the accumulation of garbage in the occupied area and with the lack of assistance of the Valley and the State in the process of repairing the breakup. But in order not to leave the area unprotected, some remained on site, but without access to drinking water. The situation worsened in 2021 with the agreement between the MP/MG, Vale and the state of Minas Gerais, which has made it difficult to fully repair the affected communities. The violations committed against the indigenous population are several: loss of the river and all biodiversity of the surroundings, lack of water for human and cultural use, harassment of the mining company and lack of full repair. It was designated by the MPF independent technical advice to raise the damage caused to the indigenous community by the disaster-crime and facilitate the repair process.
92216d0101aa7411db31940625a44f775d6f3627: The Aranã people, divided into two families, had their territory recognized by Funai in 2013, in two farms: Campo and Tocoiós (an old Maxakali settlement), and remained there working in those two areas that were never requested by their alleged owners. In 2021, however, banana plantation companies began to threaten indigenous families, with surrounding areas, deforestation, pesticide spraying and threats of reintegrating possession.
1c9e940c72065db7aec4a930f6a8284f1bc828a6: Deforestation; works within the territory; environmental damage
b2c60beba287ea2655f81bc2f27a4d791a9cc254: Several companies have threatened the permanence of the Pankararu and Pataxó peoples in the Cinta Vermelha and Jundiba villages in the Jequitinhonha Valley (MG). 2222307f2354d9f9caa1ec168704d9c94a2254ca: The city of Conceição do Mato Inside, he suffers, some years ago, from the mining activity of the Canadian company Anglo American, which has mining activity in the city and the mineroduct Minas-Rio, the largest in the world, which transports the ore to the port in Rio de Janeiro. b497152ba20ac918f08367cdfa1c94cf600af108: Affected by the breakup of the dam of rejects of the Valley in the Córrego do Beanão, in Brumadinho (MG), about 15 families of the peoples Pataxó Hã-Hã-Hãe and Pataxó, faced with the harassment of the miner by individual compensation agreements as a measure to repair the breakup, withdrew from the place they occupied before the disaster-crime and obtained the partial donation of a permanent preservation area, also in the municipality of São Joaquim de Bicas (MG). 3dfac626fbec7bf8b7b3b1793d9271b91058c3c8: The indigenous people of Barreiro Preto Village, located in the Xakriabá TI, in São João das Missões, lived moments of tension and fear in the early morning of June 24, when they perceived a fire of great proportions. According to Chief Domingos Nunes, everything indicates that this is a criminal act, all the files in our school history have been burned. “In addition to the archives of the secretariat, they burned all the computers and our medical home, which is one of the main houses we have of traditional medicine, which we are fighting to preserve”. Military and civilian police were called in to do the investigation, but the Federal Police would take the case.
c410f59f81a239bd1bc5644c1978d8b678747721: In May 2021, on several occasions, the Morro Vermelho Village, in the Xakriabá IT, was invaded by a farmer who claims ownership of the area, threatening the indigenous peoples of death and destruction of houses, fences and plantations. The MPF manifested itself in the action of maintenance of possession, obtaining judicial decision that stipulates daily fine if there are new invasions in the territory Xakriabá. Even so, the climate in the region is very tense and indigenous families feel insecure about so many threats.
721fb2657d04e8acb705c50a43fe906e2f55b44c: An action by the Federal Police has arrested two men for the crime of deforestation at TI Alto Rio Guamá. bcd3f7fc9fc68afc8d732720989995661c97a972: The MPF denounced nine people for environmental crimes committed inside TI Alto Rio Guamá, in northeastern Pará. All those reported were investigated by PF in a police investigation.

6974518078589b1a8b83955869179b95dab49145: In December 2021, the MPF-PA asked the Justice for the Northern Garrafão (PA) to be forced to immediately paralyze the use of indigenous land as a dump and to draw up a plan for the removal of garbage from the area. 29dd9b4ef4327090af8d67b32d470d2ddd604609: In November 2021, the MPF recommended to the prefectures of Nova Esperança do Piriá (PA), Garrafão do Norte (PA) and Viseu (PA) and the company Equatorial Energia to suspend a series of irregular works aimed at benefiting invaders of the indigenous land. 698d204c870cf219c11d981149c1fa523a0c1585: On September 13, a group of 30 Tembé Indians who play the role of protecting the territory received information about an invasion of loggers in the territory and entered the closed forest in search of traces, in an area inside the IT, 12 km from Vila do Cristal, in the municipality of Viseu, on the banks of the river Piriá. According to the report of Fepipa, the indigenous found several In Jacareacanga (PA), one of the various violent activities of prospectors was the destruction of the headquarters of the Munduruku Women's Association Wako logs of wood, as well as a tractor and a truck, which were burned. “At this moment, the indigenous distinguished by the sound of the engine that a boat was approaching. a0afcc75593cf88b80d098fa6218bbb441585712: In October 2021, the MPF/PA presented, again, a request to Justice to determine the urgent withdrawal of the invaders from the Sarauá IT, of the Amanayé people, in Ipixuna do Pará. The first time MPF made this request to the Federal Court in Paragominas (PA) was in November 2018, unsuccessful. Since then, deforestation has followed so intense that wood has become scarce and the area has also become the focus of planting fires. The MPF warned of the risk of conflict, which could generate an unprecedented tragedy.” According to the institution, illegal occupants have been making a series of threats to indigenous people who, in turn, want to remove the invaders on their own. For the MPF, the violation of Amanayé's rights has always been evident and has worsened to the point of causing irreversible damage. In April 2021, the MPF requested information from Ibama on the existence of environmental inspections in IT in 2020 and 2021. Since Ibama did not respond, the MPF sent a recommendation to the municipality to carry out environmental surveillance in the area, whenever possible with the seizure of products and instruments used in the practice of environmental crimes.
6f4f3da4b22502c523c316055b78f649ae04570f: The invasion of indigenous lands for exploitation of natural resources, especially the mining, has caused very serious consequences for the survival of several indigenous peoples in Brazil. Seven studies by the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (Fiocruz) show that women and children are the most vulnerable to mercury poisoning, which affects all 200 people in the villages Sawré Muybu, Poxo Muybu and Sawré Aboy, in the Sawré Muybu Indigenous Land, of the Munduruku people, in western Pará. The source of contamination is gold mining, which has grown almost 500% in indigenous areas since 2010, especially in the Amazon, and today has the Bolsonaro government's encouragement and support. Lands, fish and waters are contaminated and increase risks to rural and urban populations. The average contamination above the tolerable limits is six out of ten indigenous (40% in Sawré Muybu village, 60% in Poxo Muybu and 90% in Sawré Aboy). The territories are on the banks of the Tapajós and Jamanxim rivers, where there has been mining since the 1950s, but it has been intensified in recent years. In April, Cimi's environmentalist and indigenist Cássio Beda died after two years living and consuming fish in the Tapajós River basin, where he supported demands from indigenous peoples. All the natives of the three villages of the IT Sawré Muybu are contaminated at some level. Six out of ten have mercury in their blood above the WHO limit. The villages continue to be affected by contamination of the waters of the basin by illegal mining – especially the Sawré Aboy village, located on the banks of the Jamanxim, tributary of the right bank of Tapajós which is one of the most impacted watercourses by illegal mining.
be0fb10ce80553a737d7cdaee8ffcd9f87fcf018: The invasions in the indigenous territories have intensified every year. Since 2019, the action of these invaders, especially illegal prospectors, has increased with even greater intensity. In order to combat these crimes within the ITs, the Joint Command North carried out an action inside the TI Reach Bacajá, in São Félix do Xingu, in southwest Pará. Facilities that supported illegal activities were not used by the military. Two helicopters were used during the action in support of Funai, Ibama, PF and the National Public Safety Force (FNSP).
db63b5c295c39ecf9e1e376c88b487e604800dac: In November 2021, PF carried out the Parakanã I and II Reach operations, focusing on the fight against deforestation and the withdrawal of invaders from the Reach/Bacajá and Apyterewa ITs. Seven search and seizure warrants were completed in the operations, which involved more than 300 agents and also focused on the deactivation of mining and repression of other environmental crimes related to the illicit extraction of ores. The TI Reacheira/ Bacajá is one of the seven ITs in which the STF determined that a plan for the withdrawal of the invaders was drawn up under ADPF 709, which deals with guarantees for the protection of indigenous peoples amid the Covid-19 pandemic. Despite the specific surveillance actions, TI Reacheira/Bacajá is systematically invaded by landowners and prospectors and has remained among the most deforested in Brazil in recent years, according to data from Inpe. In 2021, data from Prodes, a system for monitoring deforestation in the Legal Amazon of Inpe, indicate that it was the second most deforested indigenous land in the country, with more than 3.5 thousand hectares of devastated forest.
b553e6c04ef348d8d3cdadde14f278f4cd692620: A new report on the health damage of the Xikrin people of Cateté, produced in July 2021 by doctor João Paulo Botelho Vieira Filho, reports the deepening of the health damage caused to the more than 1,600 people living in IT by the mines of the mining company Vale. According to the report, the Cateté and Itacaiúna rivers, used daily by indigenous people for food, fishing, transport, bathing and water consumption, remain visible and proven polluted by heavy metals such as lead, cadmium, iron, copper, chromium, manganese and nickel. The report points out that contamination is caused by wastes from the Onça-Puma and 11D Eliezer Batista mines, exploited by the Valley. Botelho mentions that a study by Professor Reginaldo Saboia de Paiva, UFPA, with 49 indigenous people of the Xikrin people, found in all of them present and high lead”. In addition to the very serious consequences for the health of indigenous peoples, the contamination of rivers seriously affects the traditional way of life of these people and makes some common practices of their culture impossible – such as the consumption of cassava flour. “The Xikrin of the villages Cateté, Djudjê-Kô and Oodjã began to leave the roots of cassava to soften in tonels, because the flour obtained from the softened roots in the rivers were in bad taste of heavy metals”, as lead, whose presence was found in samples of flour. “The roots in sauce in tonels are not so detoxified from cyanic acid, unlike the roots in running water of the river washed by the indigenous custom,” the report continues, reporting that several indigenous people began to present gastric pain and to be referred for endoscopy. The consequent replacement of traditional food by the purchase of industrialized foods favors the increase in cases of obesity, hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, highlights Botelho, and some cases of kidney diseases, cancer and tremors may be a consequence of contamination by heavy metals. The Indigenous Associations Porekrô, Kakarekrê and Baypran, of the Xikrin people, continue to denounce the situation and to charge the authorities.
717a0d6e2aff7c97070b5410c4a7b700886ff40b: The indigenous people of the Tabajara people, in struggle for the regularization of their traditional territory for years, have denounced that invaders continue to enter their territory to engage in illegal mining activity, an activity that is deprecating the environment, polluting the rivers and compromising the health of the indigenous people and the population of the region. The indigenous also denounce the performance of companies that produce cement and gravel. The climate in the area is tense, the Tabajara people suffer from conflicts with the invaders and the devastation of the environment. After complaints made in the previous year, there was an Ibama action in 2021; however, according to the leaders, the mineral extraction activity continued to occur.
6509b54886339c24d03e2a90b3e2bb57eb71f0ae: In 2020, landmarks that signaled the boundaries of the indigenous land on the right bank of Lake Itaipu were broken by non-indigenouss. Despite the complaints, the milestones were not replaced by Funai or Itaipu Binacional, and the non-indigenous continue planting within the limits of the territory.
f59d90b2dc72fc79a117388de53ead8d6d2b5b36: Indigenous people of TI Mangueirinha, in western Paraná, denounce the invasion of soybean and corn producers in their territory and try to articulate to prevent more tragedies from happening. At least a thousand hectares of the reserve have already been taken, according to local indigenous leaders. According to Chief João Santos, the community has been waiting since 2010 for Funai to intervene in returning the land, fulfilling the demarcation. Without part of the territory demarcated and regularized, the community was hostage to the action of farmers around, watching, since the late 1990s, the invasion of space. Today, the invaded territory is about 10 kilometers into IT, in a space known as Canhada Fundo. The territory also received a fence that, according to chief João Santos, was built by the farmers themselves. The Indians went to the invaded lands and protested. A group of indigenous teenagers and youth also wrote on leaves: “Where are the pine trees that were here?”, criticizing the deforestation of the area.
709f133854be09ea63fd1304101b7a00a8019f75: Anonymous denunciation led environmental military police to verify the deforestation that has been taking place within TI Mangueirinha, in the southwest of Paraná. At the time of the survey, a backhoe machine was found falling down the trees, and the devastated area was already 7.1 hectares. According to information, the flagrant result in the apprehension of the machine and acquisition of the owner of the equipment in the amount of R $ 132 thousand. The Federal Court must be notified by the Environmental Police because it is an area of the Union. In addition to a fine, those responsible for deforestation can be prosecuted.
3949b10b9b1cf228b38e3cf007a63ce648a3ac9e: In 2020, an agricultural company in Espigão Alto (PR) leased part of IT for the planting of GM cereals, which caused serious situations, such as deforestation, fires and pollution of streams and springs due to the use of pesticides. In 2021, the lease persisted in the indigenous land. According to a survey by a member of the community, about 400 hectares of the Rio das Cobras IT followed leased.
28b460d377780419e2cce503fad19750ea88b854: In 2020, the Avá-Guarani denounced the construction of a rubber shop near Tekoha Karumbey's chief house to Funai and MPF. Despite the complaints, the rubber shop is still in operation, reducing the freedom of movement and enjoyment of the territory by the indigenous. The situation is aggravated by the fact that, in 2020, Funai invalidated the administrative process of identification and delimitation of IT through ordinance 418 – which is based on a first instance judicial decision, suspended by the TRF-4, and questioned by the MPF.
0ec4b95604be2f461bd7a47ef909ddc5310c2e26: Use of pesticides; damage to the environment
f799ec5da6dc221bf40d1cf3f088319b60290882: Leadership reports that the agrotoxic used by farmers in the region on soybean plantations is contaminating the village and killing small animals, mainly chickens, used in the feeding of families. Environmental Police were in the village last November after the chickens died, but the poison spray in the area continues. The area is claimed by the Avá-Guarani as an indigenous land, but the UHE Itaipu Binacional moves processes of reintegrating possession against the community. In addition to all the difficulties and struggles of the community for its survival, especially in the middle of the pandemic, the people had their health even more compromised, breathing poison thrown by farmers.
ed2cc7a7e1ab087de0f5c664a97580b562e931b5: Leaderships denounce that a farmer performs deforestation and opening of areas within the caatinga, in territory that is pleaded by the Kapinawá people and that is currently inserted in the area of the National Park of the Valley of the Catimbau. The farmer uses machinery, tractor and backhoe to illegally deforest and remove wood from the region, destroying biodiversity. According to information from the community, the farmer received a fine from the ICMBio, recognizing the error and suspending such actions, but the insecurity and risk of the continuity of deforestation remains. The Community has drafted a complaint to the competent bodies and has mobilized itself to give publicity to the case.
c21f524e917f5af3c28dbf5df93e01568cb174e5: The Pankararu people Opará denounced the occurrence of fire and deforestation within the indigenous area during the night. Several native trees that were part of the Environmental Protection Area near the site of the sacred terreiro of the people were destroyed. Part of the caatinga is deforested, damaging the community that needs this biome for its religious activities and sustainability.
31a39f90931c0b949986a193b642deec9b53651a: The leaders of the Gamela people denounce that, due to Funai's omission and delay in proceeding with the regularization of its territory, the people have suffered the action of invaders and crickets in their lands. In addition, the Instituto de Terras do Estado do Piauí (Interpi) held a meeting called a prior consultation”, in Laranjeira Village, in the municipality of Currais. On this occasion a proposal for land titration for the people was presented, without the proper clarification and removing important parts of the traditional territory Gamela, such as the streams and bogs of domination and subsistence of the people. The situation with the MPF was reported.
f1e708913d327962353de88363d1d0b49d247a45: Leaderships denounce the lease of land promoted in traditional area of the Tapuia people. The current tenant makes it impossible for the indigenous community to access the area of Lagoa do Tapará, with the presence of three armed security guards on site. The lagoon was traditionally used by the indigenous people, from where they withdrew their livelihood for their own consumption and collection of fruits such as imbu, coconut, jambo and olive. For decades, the people have been waiting for provisions from the government to regulate their territory.
bdc5160e52ee47d38721eb7eb045e34cef81aaf8: Invasion; fire; monocultures; use of pesticides
fbd4c0ecd5b5f84bc26d9f5d5dba5c2f4ef4c671: Indigenous leaders report invasion and advance of sugarcane monoculture over indigenous territories, with the constant use of burning, deforestation of vegetation and the use of chemicals that cause high incidence of insects in communities and lung diseases in the indigenous population, especially in children and elderly. Such actions also harm animals, who die or need to flee and take refuge in community homes, and cause territorial and environmental loss in the lands. In this region, the most affected indigenous peoples are Tapuia Tarairiú da Lagoa do Tapará, Potiguara do Catu and Potiguara do Sagi/Trabanda. The MPF has been activated and has charged protection measures to these indigenous communities.
4bd1305b372f4701931039af56e15119e309347e: The illegal practice of land leases within IT has fostered a series of conflicts, with the expulsion of families and with the invasion of the territory for GM soybean planting. The territory is also affected by the use of pesticides used in monoculture.
1e219c47c639b8cbf2df13c46672a15d7813fc9d: In 2021, internal conflicts became everyday within this indigenous land. The largest indigenous land in Rio Grande do Sul suffers the intense process of invasion of its territory. These invasions are closely related to the practice of land rental for the planting of monocultures, especially transgenic soybeans. Thus, the soil of the territory is polluted by the use of pesticides, compromising the health of the indigenous population and the surroundings.
47331dc004d4abb76db51c331b6db46e72f6eeec: The Mbya Guarani community of Pindó Poty once again denounced that their land is being invaded and crowded. By 2020, the community had already denounced the invasion of the area to the MPF and Funai. At the time, no measures were taken to prevent further invasions, nor was the withdrawal of those illegally occupying the area promoted. It is worth noting that the land is, since 2012, with the demarcation procedure under way, characterizing it as a land of traditional occupation. The community has already informed Funai about the new invasions, but institutionally they have not received an answer. There was only the manifestation, via WhatsApp, of the anthropologist responsible for the detailed studies of identification and delimitation of the land, who claimed that it was impossible to complete the work while the covid-19 pandemic persisted. The community requested the resumption of studies by Funai, the withdrawal of invaders, the protection and supervision of the land to prevent the systematic process of invasions. It is suspected that they are coordinated by economic groups that want – after illegal occupations are declared as consummated facts – the permanent possession of the entire indigenous area, to promote the construction of commercial units and residential condominiums. The community once again denounces the noise and demands that the authorities take appropriate measures to hold the invaders accountable.
3a22bc13fbb40c30ea224447eaf0a054ba470aad: This is another territory invaded by transgenic soybean growers who carry out illegal land rental practices. Due to this practice, a series of conflicts took place within the indigenous land, culminating in the expulsion of dozens of families from the territory.
0fa67feafd793ccc46b7a285f4e25a4f4420a89c: The Guarani leaders denounce that people linked to the economic enterprise Arado Velho, including accompanied by military police, circulated in the space of land that was delimited by the TRF-4 as an exclusive enjoyment of the community, constantly addressing and questioning the Mbya Guarani about the number of people living there, with insinuations that the indigenous people would be occupying an area greater than that established by the TRF-4. The invaders also cause damage to the environment. During the vaccination of the indigenous against Covid-19, the health team was also ostensibly approached by the management of the project, demanding information about the indigenous, such as the name, age of the people and number of families.
53d37cb32fcf025ac71f33c0647f5a66cdabdcf1: during 2021, internal conflicts became intense and everyday within this indigenous land, including with murders. One of the largest indigenous lands in the gaucho state suffers intense invasion of its territory. These invasions are closely related to the illegal practice of land rental for the planting of monocultures, especially transgenic soybeans. Thus, the soil of the territory is polluted by the use of pesticides, compromising the health of the indigenous population and the surroundings and expelling hundreds of families from traditional territory, invaded by soybean and transgenic wheat.
e080eba44b90a644d3fe6d8a08d1366877bbc50c: Fire; burning of prayer houses; damage to property
be5a1fcb10df8f861d597388fa86da6cf183e5ce: The chief of the area Mbya Guarani de Bonito, Japan Batista, was in the Tenode community and reported that two houses were consumed by fire and that the Opy (house of prayer) was also destroyed by the flames. According to John the Baptist, the firemen were on site, but there was difficulty containing the flames because of the wind. No one was injured, but there was the loss of material possessions, that is, all the belongings of the families ended up consumed by the fire. He's suspected of arson, since this was the third case in the same area. The Mbya report that they saw nothing at the start of the fire, because they were in a dam that is far from the village. The chief's reports point to the possibility of criminal action, since the families were not in the community and there was more than one fire outbreak. If he was a criminal, he is attributed to hate and racism crimes, since in the region there is no dispute over the Tenode area, since it is a land purchased within the compensation programme for doubling the BR-116.
dd489a6387c90fb2258e8029193d8b42bf309e9d: The illegal practice of land lease for planting soybean and GM wheat, with intensive use of pesticides, has caused a series of conflicts with the Kaingang community. Due to this practice, conduct in the Federal Court a Public Civil Action MPF that seeks to curb this practice.
3b3761d4fd2a15fb4fefa48c535b3732ce62d79f: The MPF in Caxias do Sul judged three public civil actions to question the concession of the National Forests (Flonas) of Canela and São Francisco de Paula, in Rio Grande do Sul, without prior appreciation of the land issue involving the indigenous communities Kaingang and Xokleng. In two actions, the agency requires the Union and Funai to carry out an anthropological study for the identification and delimitation of traditional areas within the Flona de Canela, claimed by the indigenous community Kaingang KogunhMág/Jagtyg Fykóg, and the Flona de San Francisco de Paula, of interest to the indigenous community Xokleng Konglui. In the third action, the MPF asks the Federal Court to determine to the ICMBio the performance of prior consultation and consent, free and informed to the Kaingang Kógunh Mág/Jagtyg Fykóg community and the Xokleng Konglui community regarding the concession of the National Forests of Canela and San Francisco de Paula to the private initiative, since these peoples are likely to be directly affected by such concessions. Since 2012, the Xokleng Indians have been waiting for the completion of the qualification phase, a preliminary stage of the demarcatory procedure, therefore prior to the beginning of anthropological studies. The Attorney General of the Republic and author of the actions, Luciana Guarnieri, said that Funai's inertia is intensifying the conflict between the Xokleng and the ICMBio, the managing authority of the National Forest of São Francisco de Paula, which granted a reintegration of possession due to the occupation of the forest by the indigenous peoples in December 2020.” The Kaingang indigenous claim is still in the qualifying phase, and families await the beginning of studies to identify and delimit their traditional land camped within the Canela Flona.
2c14d7f9c63a24f37b5bcec2e1ea218b25d4ab1b: Despite the complaints made by the community to the DER and the MPF, no provision was made to restore the wall that was knocked down for the construction of the BR-364 highway. Without restoration, the Cassupá people continue to feel vulnerable and exposed to violence.
d6048c9d891ef1ffda6c65ee3e38170ea60c9f61: Claiming for almost a decade that Funai has been the working group for the identification and demarcation of Guarasugwe IT, the people continue to see their territory devastated by the great soy growers who, in addition to the degradation caused by monoculture, have destroyed traces of the ancestral presence of the people in the region, as funeral urns. After the people asked ifhan to study the archaeological site, the Institute spoke to the farmer, who denied the existence of the site, and requested a study from the Federal University of Rondônia. While awaiting land regularization, the people live in a situation of miserability in the outskirts of the cities of Porto Velho, Costa Marques, Pimenteiras, Guajará Mirim and São Francisco do Guaporé.
f548a3288cd505424cb526df7bb813d062230325: Deforestation in protected areas of the Amazon located in Rondônia increased considerably after the approval and sanction of the Complementary Law No. 1,089/2021, authored by the governor of the state Marcos Rocha (Union Brazil), which reduced the area of the Reserva (Resex) Extractivist Jaci-Paraná and the State Park (PES) of Guajará-Mirim. The devastation of Resex was estimated at 2700% between May, month in which the decree came into force, and November. The increase in deforestation of the state park corresponds to 300%, when compared to the previous year. The PES of Guajará-Mirim did not suffer any deforestation index between the first months of the year, from January to April, however, with the approval of the law – considered unconstitutional by the Court of Justice of Rondônia (TJ-RO) – trees were knocked down in a perimeter of 40 km2 within the Conservation Unit. The numbers were calculated by WWF-Brazil. The indigenous peoples who are in the Igarapé Lage, Ribeirão, Karipuna, Karitina and Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau ITs are highly impacted by the destruction of their lands, local biodiversity and threatened in their physical and cultural integrity by the presence of an increasing number of invaders. The indigenous organizations sent documents and complaints to the MPF-RO and await measures.
a2cb24f62d9def5e2724f8d39ace9903408bdedb: Even in the face of complaints and an operation carried out by PF at the end of 2020, loggers and prospectors continued to act. With new strategies, invaders remove sawn wood from IT and practice manual mining. Many of them live near the territory, in the district Nova Colina, in the municipality of Ji-Paraná (RO), which facilitates the transit and circulation of information among the invaders. During the pandemic, the Indians erected sanitary barriers, and one of the leaders responsible for this barrier reported that armed men threatened people on their way to the Iteape village to bring personal hygiene and care supplies against Covid-19. The men, according to the account, warned people to leave the village quickly and showed firearms.
d6168c1b8d57c575ced17342192454f4de7cd4a3: In April 2021, numerous complaints by the indigenous and partners led the PF to trigger Operation Crepitus, aimed at preventing and suppressing the entry of invaders into IT. One of the focuses of the operation was the destruction of the bridges built by invaders, who occupy and deforest the territory. There are also cattle and pasture farms in the devastated area. In addition to environmental destruction, the Karipuna are subject to violence and are exposed to diseases caused by the invaders, especially in the last two years, with the Covid-19 pandemic.
daf2446d32f13813d67c1dbd3b6efab891c5101d: Invasion; destruction of IT access bridge
797f037f588f3966cef7848ba6b69308fe11e3b2: Karipuna TI is one of the most invaded and deforested indigenous lands in the region. In August 2021, there were police operations within IT, resulting in the arrest of some invaders. Such operations led the other invaders to a retaliation action, which was the destruction of the access bridge to the village Panorama. The bridge was already in a bad state, but it was completely destroyed by the invaders. The indigenous sent a complaint document and a request to the PF and the MPF.
2b2f624d6710a8e9875c9f55fc2a81739a24b76b: According to the Portal De Olho nas Ruralistas, 84 records were identified, in 2021, in the Rural Environmental Registry (CAR) on IT Karipuna, by the government of Rondônia, through the Department of Development and Environment. There are numerous areas down and the bites made with georeferencing. The lots are marked by the landowners, who move freely in the territory. The lack of effective supervision leaves the territory free for the invasion, beyond the hostile environment, leaving the entire community threatened, weakened and exposed to all kinds of violence. The invaders continued to enter the territory and intimidate the people, who cannot move freely to their subsistence activities, such as chestnut hunting and collecting. In addition to forwarding a complaint document to Funai, Ibama and MPF, where they ask for measures, the community also filed a lawsuit against the invaders.
c72c50bd4c6350a175e09779a0a5e71bf9625a06: Invasion; deforestation; road construction within IT
0932e68121bedc5d0d8a64a3fcaddb1138d3e957: In the year 2021, there was an increase in invasions and deforestation of the Karipuna IT, with practices of maintenance and cleaning of areas already deforested within the territory and the opening of new areas. It was constant the presence of machines working within IT and tractors opening clandestine and illegal roads for the theft of wood and the greasing of land. Many of these roads have access through the farms and, even if there are operations with bridge destruction, the invaders return to enter the indigenous land with improvised bridges. More than 700 hectares of IT were deforested in 2021, according to data from Prodes/ Inpe. The invaders feel legitimated by the speech of the current president and also by the dismantling and lack of supervision of the bodies that should protect the indigenous territories. Complaints and requests of the indigenous peoples were sent to Funai, PF and MPF.
602f9fab62340a410bac7abe36fe6118fa347ea2: With the approval of the Complementary Law 1089/21, which was sanctioned by the governor in May 2021 and reduced the Resex Jaci Paraná and the State Park Guajará Mirim, increased the invasion in the IT Karipuna, on the south side – the River Formoso, where several tents and houses were found, besides planting grass inside the IT. Several fires have been made by these invaders in Resex Jaci Paraná and also inside the IT Karipuna. The level of pollution due to the smoke from these fires Christian Braga/Greenpeace ripuna in the Formoso River region, in the municipality of Nova Mamoré, egg Karipuna, Greenpeace Brazil and Cimi made by the invaders, both near the river and in the village, has caused allergies and respiratory problems in the indigenous. In 2021, several outbreaks of burning were detected by the invaders, with a view to keeping the area clean in the previous years to develop livestock activity within the IT. Documents of complaints and requests for actions were forwarded to Funai, PF and MPF.
96269852265135d6c9e75eebbb87291e42a2b5c4: The increase of invaders in the IT Karipuna has increasingly worried indigenous families. There is a great flow of people with large vessels, and this circulation has become increasingly intense and frequent, with the use of powerful engines and that is no longer restricted to weekends. The community has faced difficulties, with the reduction of fishing availability and/or the difficulty of obtaining the fish for its survival. Similarly, there have been actions by invaders entering IT for illegal hunting. Several complaints were made to Funai, PF and MPF.
40dcbd152f3486682f296108d4ac57b99768d147: The Karipuna report that in the month of September 2021, along the Ramal Panorama, road that gives access to the village Panorama, the invaders tried to legitimize the land, with crops of corn, banana, jerimum, sweet potatoes, peanuts and others, approximately 13 km from the village, inside the IT Karipuna. Through the movement on site and the work of cleaning the swidden, it is evident that the person attends the place almost daily to work in the swidden. The indigenous also saw in this place an armed man, transiting in this newly constituted country, taking away the freedom of the indigenous peoples to move safely in their own territory. The community, concerned and feeling threatened, forwarded documents of complaint and request measures to MPF, PF and Funai.
0fa8020ebe5975b91792659c14fdd9dddd2e4a37: In December 2021, leaders of the people denounced the construction of a bridge inside the Karipuna IT, in the south, linking farm areas to the Karipuna IT. In this place numerous logs of wood have been identified, which are removed and transported illegally to sawmills of the region. Access to this bridge is through the Jacinópolis district. According to Funai's information to the Federal Police, this bridge in the River Formoso was not overturned, because it did not present a great threat to the territory.” Unlike this, in this place the bridge was reinforced, and there the invaders remove the logs of wood stolen from the indigenous land. Complaints have already been and continue to be made, both to the MPF and the PF and Funai, but the measures favorable to the protection of the Karipuna people and the environment have not occurred.
1d6b71e57f48403ea5c574297bf6318e10d257cc: In August 2021, the Karipuna people identified traces of isolated indigenous peoples inside the IT, in a region very threatened by invaders who make logging and land Grinder. In the same month, a document was sent to the sector of isolated Indians of Funai reporting the situation and the risk. Request was made to ensure the presence of the team on site and the protection, supervision and removal of invaders from this area, as well as the removal of invaders from the Formoso River region, to ensure the physical integrity of the two groups identified in the Karipuna IT. By the end of the year, there was no work to curb the action of invaders. The isolated peoples are at great risk of extermination, if no action is taken by the bodies responsible for their protection.
72db12b711c3b2edf640b175fbc78867ec3ee7e2: The Migueleno people also suffer from the pressure of farmers, farmers and fishermen in the territory they claim as a traditional occupation area. The lack of state measures to regulate the area makes the people and the territory even more vulnerable to pressure and environmental degradation. At the end of 2020, the MPF, triggered by the indigenous peoples, moved a Public Civil Action charging Funai to demarcate Migueleno's IT. The federal court decided to continue the proceedings and, on December 1, 2021, through Ordinance MJ/FUNAI no. 439, Funai installed the GT for identification and delimitation of the Migueleno IT.
c8d6c6537f3dcde8175f7e7c44ec5746e708a86d: Invasion; withdrawal of IT limit mark
3dd06fd588297e27b78c7f9b288499a98b7ee312: A farmer located around Ribeirão IT has been advancing the boundaries of indigenous territory. According to indigenous reports, he has already advanced about 15 meters within IT. The farmer started the landmark that delimits the indigenous territory and has also been deforesting the area. The indigenous asked him to put the mark back in place, but this was not done; on the contrary, they have received threats.
8e544694c8477f47f5c6d583684983f8d7bb3b00: Traditionally, in November, the indigenous people of Oro Wari collect chestnuts to support their communities. That's when a group of indigen caught invaders carrying stolen chestnut bags from Ribeirão IT. These were not the only ones caught in full crime; every year, invaders have been bolder in their criminal practices. The lack of supervision by the indigenous protection agencies and the anti-indigenous discourse of the current President of the Republic have contributed to the fact that the invaders of the indigenous lands feel more comfortable in the practice of their crimes.
718e2555541627f965baaca91115b2482642ec07: For years, the Oro Wari people have been waiting for the authorities to regulate their territories and remove the invaders, which cause conflicts and destroy the environment and livelihoods of families. In 2021, without provision from the authorities, the invasions continued. The indigenous are afraid to report the situation to the authorities, as they are threatened by the prospectors and fishermen who roam within the territory.
e7870e11e37cdd6d00df524f67fa7b0c781c9293: After several denunciations, at the end of 2020 PF launched an operation against illegal prospectors and loggers operating within IT, including the destruction of equipment and a bridge used to transport timber. Despite this, no one has been held responsible for the crimes, and leaders report that illegal activities continue in IT. Between May and June 2021, the Deter system, of the Inpe, issued at least two deforestation alerts linked to the practice of mining or mining within the indigenous land.
97cae95692b747b815ff3ffc4404d8bb87b47fc1: With the process of demarcation paralyzed at Funai since 2015, the territory is pressed by federal land regularization programs, through which farmers occupy and deforest the traditional indigenous occupation area. Clandestine fishing also affects one of the people's main food resources. In a situation of vulnerability, the people triggered the MPF at the end of 2020, which moved a Civil Action Public by pressing Funai to complete the demarcation of their lands, and by the end of 2021 still awaited the progress of the process.
d4a3a975959eccdf32c81c01f6a48959399a3b65: Private companies continue to remove ores from the Guaporé river, causing damage to the environment and contamination of the river, which is a source of survival of these peoples. The fact has been reported to the authorities for some years, but there has been no action against the companies, which has been causing damage to the Rio Guaporé IT and the environment. The situation remained in 2021. The indigenous, fearing reprisals and persecution due to the adverse political context, are afraid to make new complaints.
7ae0d1053f490d3f4cc200d0078c46db1e7b2d0b: Despite the operation of the Federal Police against loggers carried out in September 2021, IT continued to be the target of illegal logging. There is no information on new surveillance or repression actions against invaders, who continued to practice illegalities.
089579f906fd5f8dda0b892daf9181a7aba226fe: In 2021, the conflict established in the Rio Negro Ocaia IT remained, without measures of the authorities to ensure the regularization, indemnity and disintrusion of the non-indigenous occupants of the area, which had its declaratory ordinance published in 2011 by the Ministry of Justice. The situation, as reported in previous years, encourages irregular occupation of the territory, increasing the number of invaders and the degradation of the area and generating tension between indigenous and non-indigenous. The Oro Wari people are still waiting for a solution.
2516d523bfbd1f401f5a1dd3b97db5e255b2d591: The Roosevelt IT is located on the border of Rondônia and Mato Grosso and suffers from the invasion of non-indigenous for illegal mining activities. On July 2, 2021, a PF operation was launched in both states to combat a criminal group that was active in the illegal extraction and marketing of diamonds in the territory. From the seizure of 184 diamond stones extracted from IT, PF intensified the investigations and identified the main members of the criminal group, among them a former regional coordinator of Funai, who was arrested. Those investigated will respond by criminal association, usurpation of Union good, illegal extraction of ore without authorization from the competent body, damage to conservation unit and ideological falsehood. Among the seizures are documents, gold and irregular weapons.
4d4bc8e5a05404ff1bf54f425422d408b41bbaa4: In the region near the border with Bolivia, in an area of the municipality of Guajará-Mirim (RO) located between the TIs Pacaas Novas and Sagarana, several plots of land are being opened and deforested by farmers. The devastation reached, in 2021, until the northern border of the Sagaran IT - and, in some points, according to the reports of the leaders, it came to advance on perimeter of the indigenous land - a fact that is also corroborated by warnings of the Deter system, of the Inpe. Between September and October, the fire used to clean the areas deforested by farmers near the IT limit ended up reaching the indigenous land - which, according to Deter, had about 700 hectares covered by burning scars in this period.
7af47aa940db66888ede33d5154cd8848e6c0e03: TI Sete de Setembro, located between the municipalities of Cacoal (RO) and Rondolândia (MT), where the Paiter Suruí people live, faces several threats, mainly the invasion of prospectors and loggers. On July 2, 2021, in a PF operation to combat illegal deforestation in the indigenous land, supported by Funai and the PM, four people were arrested in flagrante and seized at least five chainsaws. Several deforestation points were found with fallen trees, a mobile sawmill point, radios and motorcycles that were used for internal displacement of criminals.
babccfb88c154c896fb2eda55e17a041ce15aff1: In March, the Federal Police carried out an operation aimed at disintegrating a criminal group specializing in the illegal extraction of diamonds that operated in the ITs Seven September and Roosevelt, in the municipalities of Cacoal (RO) and Espigão do Oeste (RO), respectively. The group's performance would have been discovered after a prospector from Espigão do Oeste began looking for internet investors to prospect diamonds in Rondônia. About 35 PF agents participated in the operation, entitled Investor”, and served seven search and seizure warrants in the cities of Espigão do Oeste, Cherry (RO), Clementina (SP), Montenegro (RS), and Domingos Martins (ES). According to PF, investors live in other states and, over several months, sent large amounts of money to finance the extraction of diamonds from indigenous lands. After removing the stones from Rondônia, they were sent out of the country and sold abroad. Also according to the investigation, 60% of the profits obtained from diamonds were divided into equal parts among prospectors, indigenous who combined with mining in the areas and the cost of machinery/production. The remaining 40% were entirely in the hands of investors.
33025daf220b901cea1b07b361642ac9b4e3c877: The Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau IT, demarcated and approved since 1991, is rich in water resources and has fertile land, which is why it is targeted by landowners, loggers and prospectors. As of 2019, invasions intensified, supposedly encouraged by the federal government. Rural producers in the region have organized themselves into associations and use misinformation to promote invasions. According to Neidinha Suruí, of the Etnoenvironmental Defense Association Kanindé, there is a campaign of politicians and producer associations that have begun to emerge now reproducing the discourse of the current government, that the land will be diminished, will be reviewed. This is impossible, because the land is demarcated and approved”. The situation is aggravated by the weakening of control and inspection agencies, such as Ibama, ICMBio and Funai, a strategy that guides the “environmental policy” of the current government. In this context, indigenous peoples themselves have been monitoring their territories at the borders. In one of the surveillance actions, the Indians caught a group of invaders inside the IT. One of the men admitted that he was preparing the land by determination of a person from the municipality of Ji-Paraná, known as “Pé de Louro”, who would have said that the area where they were camped was a rubber plantation reserve that was to be cut. According to the surveillance coordinator, Awapy Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, on site “had tents, mattresses, drums, chainsaws, bales and more bales of rice, lots of game meat, among other things. We explained that the area had nothing to do with the rubber plantation, that they were inside our territory.” Awapy reported that the men said they had been deceived by the boss and that they did not know that area was indigenous territory.
5eeb4dc8abcec86994b8ac0983d7f6c114e79901: According to the Sirad-Isolados Bulletin, released in June 2021 by the Socioenvironmental Institute (ISA), deforestation in Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau IT doubled that month. 57.6 hectares of forest were deforested in 30 days, an increase of 111% compared to the month of May. This reality threatens all the peoples of this territory, especially the isolated peoples, who are exposed to the greatest risk of extermination because they are the most vulnerable. The situation in the region is very serious and requires urgent measures by the government and bodies responsible for the protection of indigenous people, their territories and the environment.
04cb12443dfef604d8a36042d3a170b736a4744d: Invasions of loggers and deforestation at TI Zoró continued in 2021, despite complaints made insistently in recent years. The specific surveillance operations, carried out only by pressure from the indigenous, are insufficient, and it is common for the invaders to return shortly thereafter to illegal activities. Complaints in 2021 are corroborated by the various warnings of deforestation, degradation, burning scars and, especially, disordered cutting of wood inside TI Zoró, issued by the Deter system, of Inpe, in 2021. It is possible to perceive, through the alerts, the advance of deforestation from properties located around IT.
6d54f795ba61a5b45df0c265784078217ebf00ca: A survey carried out by the Socioenvironmental Institute (ISA) and published in the Sirad-Isolados Bulletin, pointed out that in TI Pirititi there was an advance in the invasion of landowners and deforestation, with the overlapping of properties registered in the Rural Environmental Register (CAR) in 47.8% of the territory. The situation is serious, especially due to the presence of isolated indigenous people, who have their survival threatened by environmental degradation and the presence of non-indigenous people. The registration of the CAR is self-declaratory and, although its use is prohibited for the regularization of properties, it is used throughout the country to legitimize the possession of cricket areas. According to the bulletin, the lands most affected by the illegal registration are those with restrictions of use to non-indigenous people.
82fdb4e2cca4ef103429994c77e15d82224930bc: Truculent and illegal reintegration of ownership; destruction of houses; damage to property
03b44015194162c4d44e85e9376d6321737de94a: Contrary to the decision of the Supreme Court, which extended until March 31, 2022 the rules that suspend the evictions and vacancy on account of the Covid-19 pandemic, the State Justice of the District of Alto Alegre (RR) issued a reintegration order against indigenous peoples of TI Pium, authorizing the use of police force. The measure was favorable to a farmer who claims to own the indigenous territory. In the action, carried out on December 1, military police fired tear gas bombs, used pepper spray and threw rubber bullets at community residents. In photos and videos, you can also notice, in the background, a tractor knocking down houses. Men, women, children and animals were present at the time of the assault. According to a note from the CIR, two young people were injured with rubber bullets, even though there was no resistance by the indigenous peoples.” According to information from Cimi Regional North 1, the judge responsible for this case acted in a similar process against the same community, but the author was another farmer. At the time, the judge declined the competence of the State Justice and the process went to the Federal Court. The expectation was that the same decision would be adopted in this most recent episode. According to information from the indigenous people, the site has been preserved by them for years, because there is a stream that “baths the community”. “It is an area in which medicinal herbs predominate, which was not occupied by houses years ago, because our concern was preservation, leaving only animals in space, such as cattle and pigs. [...] His [farm] purpose is to plant soybeans and destroy our Mother Earth”, said one of the leaders. The legal advice of the CIR seeks with appeal against the decision of the County, arguing the lack of competence of the State Justice.
60ef4f2d501ca75389d049e14b8af7b2a22ca9a8: Garimpeiros cross TI Pium to gain access to the Uraricoera River, one of the main rivers of entry to TI Yanomami and one of the most explored regions by the mining. On one occasion, the boats of the prospectors fell into the river and some of their belongings were dragged by the current. The prospectors accused the indigenous people of the Pium community of having appropriate equipment and supplies of the mining and began to make several threats to the people. The illegal action of prospectors in the region is one of the most serious problems faced by the indigenous population, who have their lives and health threatened and the environment completely destroyed. Numerous complaints have been made nationally and internationally, but still without effective measures regarding the care and protection of populations and territories.
1703e456ee4c305172804702a71dedf1df98657c: Leaderships of the Indigenous Council of Roraima (CIR) denounced that invading prospectors formed “favelas” with illegal trade within the Raposa Serra do Sol IT. The Indians claim that there is an illegal bar and market serving the invaders and that there has been an increase of canvas sheds in the region. According to the CIR, the invaders plot the space to sell land to new prospectors arriving in the region. They also claim that there are entrepreneurs, owners of mills and trucks, who work in the region. The leaders also report that there is no supervision by public security agencies and that this has led to insecurity to indigenous families. The CIR reported in its note that there was a significant increase in the flow of people and sheds covered with tarpaulins in the Serra do Atola, located in the Raposa II community in Normandy, where the number of prospectors can exceed 1,000 people. They divide into three areas, and each one has a leader who controls the prospectors who arrive and leave. The environment in the region, especially the streams and small water sources, are contaminated with the wastes of illegal mining activity. In addition to the risks of physical violence, mercury contamination and other diseases brought by non-indigenous people, the presence of invaders aggravates the risks of contamination among the Covid-19 pandemic.
1cd437dcceb1cd113ac10d3292028770ff39e8bf: The Roraima Indigenous Council (CRI) estimates that the presence of illegal prospectors in the Raposa Serra do Sol IT has doubled between 2020 and 2021, reaching approximately 4,000 prospectors on site. The territory is coveted by the existence of gold deposits, diamonds and other minerals. The leaders attribute the problem to the lack of supervision and even by encouragement of the federal government. The vice-coordinator of CIR, Macuxi Edinho Batista de Souza, said that within a year, we saw the result of institutional incentive for the practice of an illegal activity. What already reached other regions now takes over the rivers Maú, Cotingo and Kinô, where activities follow full steam during the pandemic. In addition to pollution of rivers by the use of mercury and the impact on aquatic fauna, illegal mining has already made drug trafficking and slave labor a reality in the indigenous region.” In a live, in 2019, President Bolsonaro said: “You are upon trillions of reais. They cannot continue to be poor upon a rich land.” Air images made by the CIR show the disaster of the mining site known as Serra do Atola. Dozens of tents are scattered around the region where the “barranco gharimpo” is made, a mode in which river gutters are explored in search of gold, resulting in deforestation and contamination of water by mercury. According to the CIR, there are already missing fish that were once the main source of subsistence for indigenous communities. After seeing that the complaints made to Ibama, Army, MPF and other bodies had no effect, the CIR sent a report to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, denouncing the threats suffered by indigenous leaders and environmental invasions and crimes in the Raposa Serra do Sol IT. The CIR awaits returns from the UN.
dba23d962dfa64902e68e53a01ed495f7f6329be: Leaderships denounced the truculent and violent action of the battalions of the Military Police and the Bope against the indigenous community of Tabatinga, in the Serras Region, within the Raposa Serra do Sol IT, in order to promote the facilitation of the entrance of prospectors. According to reports from residents, on November 16, military police force-deactivated the community monitoring post, which served to prevent illicit activities and control the mining invasion in the territory. Cops dropped tear bombs and fired firearms and rubber bullets. Six indigenous people were injured and two of them had to be transferred to the General Hospital of Roraima in Boa Vista, where the medical team also extracted a bullet from the chest of one of the injured. The police also took with them the community radiophony equipment with the clear objective of preventing the information from being disclosed immediately. After the attack, two police units followed to Boa Vista, and two others continued towards the headquarters of the municipality of Uiramutã (RR), without checking the state of the wounded. Later, another group of indigenous people from the village Willimon, in the same region of Serras, who went to provide assistance and support to the residents of Tabatinga, was also violently approached by military police, and two indigenous people had to be hospitalized at the headquarters of the municipality of Uiramutã. The following morning, the indigenous reported that new vehicles from the PM and Bope headed for the site, maintaining the climate of tension and threats. From November 12, the indigenous communities of the region had resumed an action of control and surveillance of their territory in the strategic location where the Tabatinga community is located. In a note addressed to the MPF, Funai and PF, indigenous leaders state that concerned with the increase of invasions, especially of prospectors around our communities, drug trafficking, the entry and sale of alcohol, increased malaria because of mining ( ) we decided to resume surveillance of our indigenous land in the Tabatinga community.” The indigenous leaders claim that they have resumed these protection and monitoring work due to the omission of the federal government and clarify that the Surveillance Post does not in any way prevent the right to come and go of the residents of the nearby indigenous communities. The site where the attack took place is close to the region where President Bolsonaro recently landed without the consent of the communities to publicly defend illegal and criminal activities such as mining within indigenous lands. This police action opens up the true face of the current government of Roraima and the federal government, which act violently against the lives of indigenous peoples while defending, covering up and rewarding crime and illicit activities such as mining and other invasions. On November 19, a commission formed by members of the MPF, PF and Funai moved to the Tabatinga community, listened to the testimonies of the residents and received from the indigenous all the material used by the police and collected in the vicinity of the village, such as projectiles, cashkets and others. While the meeting was taking place, 14 police and Bope vehicles were stationed 2 km from the village, in a clear attitude of intimidation. The PM even proposed its withdrawal from the indigenous land on the condition that the community accepted the definitive deactivation of the inspection post, a proposal rejected by the indigenous people. At the end of the meeting, at the request of the leaders, MPF, PF and Funai went to the location where the PM vehicles were and communicated the decision of the communities to stay in the post and to demand the exit of the PM from the region, which occurred that same afternoon. On December 8, the State Justice declined its competence to prosecute action against the inspection post of communities within its territory.
8c438c23ebc957408302b3483176b0c22e26c848: Leaderships of the Bat community claim that community residents already suffer from the consequences of pesticide discharge by airplanes on the community. Due to the proximity of soybean farms, the Wapixana indigenous people are concerned about the health of the population, as several residents have already presented skin irritations and shortness of breath. The leaders denounced the MPF and Ibama, asking for measures. The Serra da Moça IT is surrounded by soybean farms, which implies the serious health and safety situation of their communities, as well as aggression to the environment, especially to water sources. The Indigenous Council of Roraima (CIR) follows the case through its legal advice and charged the competent authorities an urgent solution.
28f493e26dfa24b4e69e736339ba9f03aa979a9c: In March, the Federal Court of Roraima determined that, in ten days, the Union, Funai, Ibama and ICMBio would start the withdrawal of all thousands of mining raiders of the Yanomami IT, under penalty of a daily fine of R $ 1 million. In the decision made, federal judge Felipe Viana states that there is a risk of indigenous genocide if nothing is done. “The population of non-indigenous prospectors almost permeates that of indigenous people; nothing is being done today, and before the usual news of the abundance of gold in the region, there is no small risk that another ‘Serra Pelada’ will be created in the place, now with even more profound characteristics.” The decision was the result of the mobilization of leaders such as David Kopenawa, Hutukara Yanomami Association (HAY) and civil society organizations that since 2019 have denounced the omission of Bolsonaro's government in the withdrawal of illegal prospectors in the region, mainly in times of transmission of the new coronavirus. With the pandemic, the circulation of prospectors in the territory increased the contamination of the coronavirus, outbreaks of malaria and other diseases, social impacts such as prostitution and sexual violence, as well as the very serious destruction of the environment.
b71acba067ab008e17561d5d3409ea574fb44821: Indigenous organizations of the Yanomami people denounced to the Federal Police that aircraft used to fly over the indigenous land in 2018 is owned by the senator of the Chico Rodrigues Republic. Known as a underwear money senator”, for being caught in 2020 by PF trying to hide R $ 33,000 in his underwear during an operation in his home, in Boa Vista, is a prospector, even though it is generally known that it is an illegal activity in indigenous territories. In January, the senator visited one of the illegal prospectors in the Raposa Serra dos Sol IT, where he recorded a video saying that the prospector on site was “a fabulous job” and that happened “without environmental damage”. The senator reported that at the time he had already transferred the possession of the plane, but did not submit any documents to prove the information. The FP says you don't give information about ongoing investigations. In addition to the PF, the indigenous movement also referred the complaint to the Ministry of Defense, Funai, ICMBio and the Amazon Military Command.
9ce440b2286e539242d40515c50983f088ee6e7f: HAY commissioned a study of a team of researchers in early April to monitor the advance of illegal mining and its destruction of the Amazon. It was found that this illegal activity grows at an absurdly accelerated pace, observed in survey with satellite images and aerial photographs. Only in the first half of 2021, until May, the visible devastation corresponded to 200 hectares, about 10% of all the devastation accumulated in ten years. This study is a continuation of the monitoring done in 2020, when it was revealed a historical record, 500 hectares – which added up to 1,700 hectares of forest destroyed since the beginning of the last decade, within territory inhabited by Yanomami and Ye’kwana in Roraima and Amazonas. Until the study date, the total area occupied by illegal mining corresponded to 2,400 hectares. According to Dário Kopenawa, president of Hutukara, the survey shows that the illegal mining at Yanomami IT is increasing. We are drawing the attention of Brazilian authorities, the federal government, because this is repeating what happened in the 1980s, in 1993, when the Haximu genocide took place. Today we detect the presence of about 20,000 prospectors, growing in the last two years”. The situation of violence in the region is very serious, and has been denounced for years, nationally and internationally, without provision from the competent authorities. The Yanomami people are at imminent risk, with families sick due to contamination of rivers, fish and soil and the constant and threatening circulation of non-indigenous people. The whole tragic picture was even more pronounced in the second year of the Covid-19 pandemic.
2d72bd39d43f8c35f451acdf0bd694b3ce563ab0: In detail, published in June 2021, the NGO Reporter Brasil reported how the gold laundering scheme that is illegally extracted from the Yanomami IT works. Through the Access to Information Act, Reporter Brasil obtained inquiries from the Federal Police that reveal the metal washing scheme, which includes intermediaries, financial companies and international brand jewelry companies involved in the purchase of gold that comes out of IT Yanomami. Legislation in the country has protected buyers and hampered the fight against illegal mining. According to the report, the combined surveys accumulate more than 5,000 revealing pages on how the marketing of metal becomes legal, despite its illegal origin. There are both small gold stores, such as Gold Jewels, DU Gold, Naza Jewels and Itaituba Metals, and larger companies, based in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, involved in the scheme. In addition to Ourominas, irregularities are suspected to Dillon, Carol, FD’Gold and Column, so-called Securities and Securities Distributors (DTVMs) – companies belonging to the financial system and having authorization from the Central Bank to purchase the metal. A great jewelry store, HStern, was also mentioned in at least two moments in the investigations of federal delegates. In the research documents, it is possible to see how the clandestine scheme works: initially, part of the gold illegally extracted from Yanomami IT goes directly to neighbouring countries (Venezuela, Suriname and French Guiana) to be sold. Another part goes to Boa Vista, where it is purchased by the small jewelry stores of Rua do Ouro – even without the Central Bank's permission to purchase the metal. These crossers usually go to Manaus (AM) or Itaituba (PA), where the metal is sold to the DTVMs. Legalization occurs mainly in these two cities in a grotesque way”, in the words of MPF prosecutor in Itaituba, Paulo de Tarso. The traverser, when selling to a DTTM, manually fills a fiscal note stating that that gold came out of a legalized prospect – the so-called “Permissions of Lavras Garimpeiras”, authorized by the National Mining Agency (ANM). As there are no legal prospectors in Roraima, traversadores declare that the gold of the Yanomami IT came out of mining of Pará and Amazonas. With the invoice in hand, with a false origin, the DTVMs are already in possession of a “legalized” gold. From then on, it is freely traded – sold to both financial institutions and large jewelry stores, both domestic and foreign. The destruction of the Yanomami IT, of the whole environment and of the survival of the people is enriching not only the owners of the large and luxurious jewelry companies, but the numerous actors involved in the scheme, including the owners of the DTVMs and their brokers, politicians, entrepreneurs from various branches who, despite responding to inquiries for some years, remain unpunished. Due to the complexity of logistics and the profusion of actors involved in the scheme, the prosecutor of the Republic in Roraima, Alisson Marugal, believes that only “with a real war operation to end illegal mining in indigenous land”.
314472e4372ebeba9c4fa31ca3eb96c2eb116489: According to the publication “Yanomami under attack”, produced by the Hutukara Yanomami Association (HAY) and the Wanassedume Ye’kwana Association, with technical advice from the Socioenvironmental Institute (ISA), a HAY office dated April 30 reported an invasion on the 27th of the same month.
