On the occasion, a Yanomami group intercepted five prospectors who climbed the Uraricoera River towards Korekorema, in a flight loaded with fuel for airplane and helicopter. Ninety liters of fuel were seized. Seven other prospectors coming down the river toward Boa Vista (RR) reacted, firing three shots at the indigenous. There were no injuries. The trade already asked for urgent measures to ensure community security.
fb1063ee895211a2df0b1fdd456ac2eafcfe7bf6: Strongly armed prospectors carried out a brutal attack on the morning of May 10, at Yanomami IT, against the Palimiú community. Leaderships reported that the attack was carried out by invaders linked to the criminal faction originated in São Paulo and known as the First Command of the Capital (PCC), which dominates drug trafficking in Roraima and would be operating in illegal gold mining within IT. The indigenous were surprised by the attack and reported that it was different from everything they had ever experienced in the region; according to the reports, the prospectors were in black and some would even be wearing clothes with the inscription “police”. In the midst of the attack, two children under five fled into the forest. Two days later, according to HAY's account, their bodies were found lifeless in the river. This was the beginning of a systematic set of attacks against the village of Palimiú that lasted at least three months. In a document by the leaders of the community written in July 2021, the indigenous report the routine of terror that was installed throughout the region. The transit of ships through the river and aircraft in the service of the mine increased. The organic structure of the prospector had a profound transformation, with the use of more sophisticated equipment and machinery, with the increase of corrutels, camps and gas stations of the prospector. The community of Palimiú, according to the leadership document, no longer managed to go fishing on the Uraricoera River, afraid of further attacks, since death threats continued to occur. Hunting also decreased in the region because of mining, increased deforestation and plastic waste associated with camping. On the other hand, since the first armed attack against Palimiú, the health team that served the community has left the area and only entered on time in a few moments. Health care decreased and malaria cases increased.
932aa7aec2d93453a38a565b85b8d32fff3b8bad: Attack on the village with firearms and bombs
605c24bb77e7dd7c1e2106459960eab4bfe62946: According to the Hutukara Yanomami Association (HAY) and the Yanomami and Ye’kwana Indigenous Health Council (Condisi-YYY), prospectors once again attacked the Palimiú community in the Yanomami IT after the attack on May 10. The invaders fired with firearms and threw tear gas bombs at the indigenous community, who reported that the invading prospectors were aboard 15 boats. According to Hutukara's office to the federal security agencies, the Yanomami were very distressed and shouted with concern on the phone. Deep down, it was possible to hear the sound of the shots. The situation was serious”. Since May 10th, when there was an armed conflict between prospectors and indigenous peoples, the Palimiú community had been subject to attacks and intimidation. The Federal Court ruled that the Union should send security troops, which, according to the indigenous people, did not occur. Yanomami leaders call for an emergency outpost to be installed in the community of Palimiú, with the aim of maintaining security on the site and on the Uraricoera River and maintaining logistical support for public agencies' actions to maintain security on site. Darlene Yanomami, resident of Palimiú, reports: “We are suffering a lot, we are not having peace. That’s why we women and children are fleeing into the forest to be able to sleep”.
14881dd189ad0aa75ab243efd5c4daacde184893: On May 13, a fourth office of the Palimiú community called for measures against the arrival of 40 prospector boats and warned that the invaders were organizing to initiate new attacks. The day before, another letter had been sent to the Army, requesting logistical support for local security and the installation of an emergency security post in the Palimiú community and in the Uraricoera River, due to another armed confrontation between prospectors, indigenous and agents of the Federal Police. The invasions were denounced in the publication Yanomami under attack”.
3ccf0daf15220191f1a6573bbcf5d8aaf3c582c3: In a fifth letter sent to the government, on May 17, the Yanomami denounced that 15 prospector boats approached the community of Palimiú. The Yanomami said that, in addition to the shots, there was a lot of smoke and that their eyes were burning, indicating the use of tear gas bombs. They were very distressed and were screaming with concern on the phone. In the background, it was possible to hear the sound of the shots”, told HAY to the authorities. The aggressions were reported in the publication “Yanomami under attack”.
42985fd5a850f4a176e9ebbcfb906cea7467fc3d: According to information from the Condisi-YY, for the tenth day of tension followed, in the night of May 19, 2021, prospectors tried again to invade the Palimiú community at the Yanomami IT. The new attack was at night, and the Indians who reside in this community reported that the prospectors were on 12 boats. The invaders only did not advance because they verified the presence of a group of indigenous and returned to the boats. The Condisi-YY expressed itself in a letter asking for support from the Federal Police, the MPF, the Army and the Funai, for fearing the occurrence of a massacre that victimizes the indigenous people”.
50c8166f9b5c7bb33295afaa12f43a1083560233: Invaders of the Yanomami IT are proving even bolder and threatening, not only for the indigenous and their territory, but for the entire surrounding population and the environment. Around 4 p.m. on May 31, eight hooded prospectors entered the base of the Maracá Ecological Station in Roraima, held hostage the three service providers who were at the base and took all the materials that had been seized in the Maracá inspection operation, carried out two weeks earlier at the UC, besides stealing five quadricycles, eight aft engines and other materials seized and property of the unit. In the attack against the unit, the prospectors – heavily armed, including with rifles – sought out ICMBio's surveillance officers and said that if they had found inspectors at the time they would not be spared. During the exit it was said that they were monitoring all the servers and that they would burn the vehicles of the organ if they found any. Brigadiers held hostage were forced to take the materials to the port of access to the unit; after that they were released and the prospectors followed the Uraricoera River, which limits the unit and gives access to the Yanomami IT, directly to the illegal mining regions. After communication with the team, the Brigadiers left the base and fled into the forest, while the head of the ICMBio in Roraima made emergency joints to ensure their integrity. There are audios and reports about monitoring servers, including threats to the families of ICMBio servers. The servants fear for their lives; while the prospectors have spread by the Federal Conservation Units and indigenous lands, the institutional structure does not provide security for the development of the activities and has grown frighteningly the violence against the protection actions of the agency.
20c447594b24d94336db4e2d31d4525952ba1c97: A sixth office of the Yanomami people to the authorities, dated June 7, denounced another attack by prospectors against the Maikohipi community in the Palimiú region, Yanomami land, hit with tear gas bombs. The invasions were denounced in the publication Yanomami under attack”.
093c9bfe463af67157dae9966425d136e39a536c: Once again, in June, the Yanomami IT was attacked by invading prospectors. They shot Indians from the Walomapi community in the Palimiú region on the afternoon of June 8. According to information from the Condisi-YY, the Indians returned from a hunt when they were shot by the prospectors on the banks of the Uraricoera River, and had to dive into the water to escape the attack. It was also reported that the invaders promised to return to the community with weapons and 20 ships. Three days earlier, prospectors who were on four boats threw gas bombs into the Maikohipi community. Condisi-YY president Júnior Hekurari Yanomami forwarded a letter reporting the new attack on Funai, PF, MPF and Army. In 2020, in the middle of a pandemic, illegal mining moved 30% in the Yanomami IT, according to the Scars in the Forest report - Evolution of illegal mining in the Yanomami Indigenous Land in 2020.” The indigenous call for help and ask the authorities to enforce the Federal Constitution. On May 24, 2021, a Supreme Court decision ordered the federal government to take measures to protect Yanomami IT. Prior to this, another judicial measure determined the armed staff, to remain permanent in Palimiú, which did not occur.
4ef6f2fb004319d6c41d10cc3bbf6839f57cdbd3: Reports made by leaders to HAY report that prospectors killed a dog and again made threats to indigenous people living in the Maikohipi community, in the Palimiú region, north of Roraima, on June 10. Hutukara stated that the prospectors were armed and, in its seventh office, denouncing the violence in the Palimiú region and charging the competent bodies, mentioned: At 2:30 p.m., they called for a community leadership shouting “come on faggot, let’s talk, come on” (sic). The prospectors were many and carrying weapons. At 16:25, the prospectors returned again, threatening the indigenous, and killed a Yanomami dog barking on the riverside before they withdrew.” Once again, Hutukara has insisted that authorities prevent the advance of illegal mining within Yanomami IT, and that they ensure security for indigenous communities, including ensuring the constant presence of public security forces in the region and logistical support for operations. MPF, PF, Army and Funai were once again activated.
2e535be7214ed68fadd114ebe0c72cd79fd3ee8e: In an eighth Hutukara trade, released on June 14, the Yanomami reported that a group of prospectors on three boats started a shootout against the Palimiú community. Faced with the new attack, the Yanomami hid in the bush, and then the prospectors followed a journey upriver, towards the Tatuzão's mine. The invasions were denounced in the publication Yanomami under attack”.
7fb82f4b979aebfdb6243a83c993100f155dc405: A ninth letter from HAY on the attacks by prospectors against indigenous peoples in the Palimiú region, inside the Yanomami IT, dated June 17, highlights that a group of hooded prospectors fired fire at the houses of the Korekorema community on the Uraricoera River, forcing the Yanomami to hide in the forest. The aggressions were denounced in the publication Yanomami under attack”.
28e6ffb49734615c01a9cf187c9c5b85577d6466: In another episode of violence, on June 18, illegal prospectors invading the Yanomami IT attacked children and youth. Six children, aged between 10 and 11, and two adolescents who fished in a canoe on the Uriracoera River, near the Typolei community, in the Palimiú region, were knocked out of the canoe by the invaders, according to HAY report. Armed, the aggressors accelerated against the Yanomami and hit the boat against the canoe, causing the Indians to fall into the water and the ship to sink. The young and children managed to escape through the river and through the forest, while listening to the prospectors calling for them, offering cookies and food. Scared of the attack and fearing for their lives, the Yanomami fled to the Yakepraopë community, the first community attacked in the region, on May 10. Dario Kopenawa Yanomami, vice president of the Hutukara Yanomami Association, sent another letter to Funai, PF, MPF and Army. In the document – the tenth on attacks against Yanomami communities only in the Palimiú region – HAY reported that residents of the villages of the region had been unable to sleep, fish or hunt for almost two months due to frequent attacks on their communities and their people.
4aee40d7c041e938b9f56a0544fa28162fb9728e: From 29 June to 2 July, Operation Curarare XIV/Agata by the Army was held at the Yanomami IT. The region had been the scene of several serious attacks by armed prospectors against the Yanomami since June 12, 2020, when two indigenous youths faced two invaders near a clandestine runway for helicopter landing. Since then, several conflicts between indigenous and prospectors, which invade IT in search of gold, have been registered in the region. The Army operation involved Funai, Cipa, PM, PC, PRF, Femarh, Ibama and ICMBio. In total, they were seized: a revolver 38 caliber; a pistol 7.65; a shotgun 20 caliber; 200 ammunition 20, 22, 32 and 38 calibers; 5.2 thousand liters of diesel oil; 750 liters of gasoline; 1.9 thousand liters of kerosene; a speedboat; two boat engines; a pump-type engine; a motor for supply; five chainsaws; three GPS; two radio communicators; two satellite communications antennas; a solar energy panel; a solar power transformer; a motorcycle; an aircraft PT-NDN model; a helicopter; a mobile fuel pump; several spare parts for the helicopter and aircraft. The alarming situation of violence and threats of all sorts suffered by the Yanomami people, caused by the mining invaders, has been worsening since 2019.
f244dbc29353d26a6048e43a55aca44b4f09f580: After a few weeks of relative tranquility with the outbreak of Operation Omama, Hutukara sends its 11th letter of denunciation to the authorities, reporting the resumption of armed attacks on Yanomami in the Palimiú region. According to HAY, on July 8, a mining vessel fired four shots at women seeking a missing relative in the river near the Korekorema community. On July 13, at dawn, the Palimiú community was attacked by two boats of prospectors, who fired ten shots at the indigenous. After the attacks, the prospectors returned to their camp. The reports were reported in the publication Yanomami under attack”.
24e28c254c80ba33885542ca81e091c35ca3bf48: On July 16, at 9 p.m., a group of hooded prospectors fired fire at the houses of the Korekorema community in the Palimiú region, forcing residents to flee into the forest. This attack was another of several systematically occurring in the Yanomami communities of that region from May 2021. The invasion of prospectors in the Yanomami IT has been one of the greatest disasters for the survival of the Yanomami people and for the preservation and balance of the environment. Numerous complaints have been made to the authorities at national and even international levels, but without effective measures to protect the indigenous people and their territory.
bd2c0bc2c894991acebc7527c2124dff5a1df0b1: Anac, with the support of PF, dismantled two clandestine hangars of irregular aircraft at Cataratas Well Artesian Ltda in Boa Vista (RR). Six helicopters were seized and, according to the investigations, they worked in the illegal mining of Yanomami IT. A man was arrested in the operation, but the PF didn't release his name. The owner of the company, who was not present at the time of the operation, was quoted in the special series Gold of the Blood Yanomami ", published by the Real Amazon and Reporter Brazil, as one of the people involved with illegal mining in the indigenous territory. He owns Icaraí Turismo Taxi Air, which signed contracts with the Ministry of Health for care at Yanomami IT during the pandemic. The company received R $ 24.3 million from public coffers, and R $ 17 million were in the Jair Bolsonaro government. PF and MPF in Roraima investigate the aircraft of the entrepreneur as suppliers of the mining scheme known as “Pedro Prancheta”, convicted of genocide of indigenous Yanomami people in the 1990s. According to the MPF, it's still operating in illegal mining.
b1967de324a497c078c7204fd9e29c16bd61c0d1: On August 3, a new HAY office – the 12th denouncing the violence of invaders against the indigenous peoples of the Palimiu region – records the continuity of the circulation of armed prospector vessels up the Uraricoera River. According to the report of local leaders, a group of prospectors would be organizing for a retaliation to the Palimiu communities for their complaints. The information indicated that, despite the recent operation, the mining activity did not cease in the region. The aggressions were denounced in the publication Yanomami under attack”.
a7ea81c51a3434a35b1d2defa739551dbaabb235: In 2021, the destruction caused by mining in Yanomami IT grew 46% compared to 2020, according to the Yanomami report under attack”, produced by HAY and the Wanassedume Ye’kwana Association, with technical advice from ISA. There was an annual increase of 1,038 hectares, reaching a cumulative total of 3,272 hectares. This is possibly the greatest annual growth in environmental degradation since the demarcation of Yanomami IT in 1992. Taking as reference the regional cut by base poles of the Health District, of the 37 existing poles, 18 have records of some deforestation related to the mining. Considering the base poles that do not have record of observable satellite deforestation, but that have information about the performance of ferries or small groups of prospectors, this set would expand to 24 base poles. It is noteworthy that the Xisei region presented a relative growth of more than 1000% of the area degraded by the mining in 2021, with serious consequences for the socio-environmental structure, especially among young people.
5515589de22edcf66db844abefdf9d2cff7cac7a: The impacts of illegal mining on Yanomami IT have also been increasingly harmful to water resources, as pointed out in the study “Yanomami under attack”. Currently, the most affected watershed is that of the Mucajaí River, concentrating on its bed 180 km of destruction (in two stretches), more 50 km of the river Couto Magalhães and 30 km of the headwater of the river Apiaú and 10 km of the river Novo, tributary of the river Apiaú. The Uraricoera basin has also been greatly affected, with 150 km in the bed of its medium course; the impacted stretches in the river Parima (35 km), Igarapé Inajá (10 km) and Igarapé Surucecu (4 km) are added. Thus, the food base of the Yanomami population, which is fish and meat, has been affected by pollution of rivers, with harmful consequences to health after consumption of these foods.
e00fb7861e56f15f53c7294954757b0904f449f8: According to studies presented in the Yanomami Report under attack”, at least 110 Yanomami IT communities are directly affected by the impacts of mining on the biophysical environment (deforestation, habitat destruction, contamination of water and soils, destruction of the natural course of rivers and silting, etc.). These impacts directly affect the health and economy of families. Other impacts of greater reach are the spread of infectious diseases, especially malaria; mercury contamination, used by prospectors in gold extraction, and the overload of the local health system. Observing these other criteria, the number of affected communities rises to 273, covering more than 16,000 people, or 56% of the population of the Yanomami IT.
6f861566c54aaf6ef1d690af48ef45cc56fdf7d7: Part of Ibirama La Klánõ IT is registered. The other part of the land is declared to be traditional possession of the Xokleng La Klánõ people through the MJ Ordinance 1.128 of August 13, 2003, with 23,024 hectares. Indigenous people live in nine villages inside the land. Even so, part of IT is in the possession of non-indigenous people, preventing the Xokleng people from enjoying all their traditional occupation territory.
d382a0a0f344c234d80bf5ceda8e22c50db32962: Morro Alto was declared a traditional possession of the Guarani Mbya people through the MJ Ordinance 2.813 of August 21, 2009, with 893 hectares. The Guarani Mbya live in a village inside the land. Even so, part of the Morro Alto IT is in the possession of non-indigenous people. These invasions prevent indigenous people from exercising the right to the exclusive enjoyment of their traditional land.
a6a7c81bb817959842c0bed8fad2b3fd3a6504f6: The Morro dos Cavalos IT was declared traditional possession of the Guarani Mbya people through the MJ 771 Ordinance of April 18, 2008, with 1,988 hectares. The Guarani Mbya live in two villages inside the land. Even so, part of the Morro dos Cavalos IT is in the possession of non-indigenous people, which prevents indigenous people from exercising the right to the exclusive enjoyment of their traditional land.
d502828d2ba810b19b7fb32f011380b1ee60bd72: The Pindoty/Conquest TI was declared traditional possession of the Guarani Mbya people in 2010, through Ordinance MJ 953, with 3,294 hectares. The Guarani Mbya have four villages within the land. Even so, hundreds of non-indigenous people continue to invade and are in possession of a significant portion of IT, preventing indigenous people from exercising the right to the exclusive enjoyment of their traditional land. There is also practice of allotment and illegal sale of plots of land within that indigenous land.
8ccd50ffe8910018018ebd40ce31c377038009bd: TI Piraí/Tiarajú was declared traditional possession of the Guarani people Mbya by the Ministry of Justice on September 1, 2009, through Ordinance 2.907, with 3,017 hectares. The Guarani Mbya live in a village inside the land. Still, a significant part of TI Piraí is in the possession of non-indigenous people. These invasions prevent indigenous people from exercising the right to the exclusive enjoyment of their traditional land.
da4c92f0afca4c116bf61eb6c979b93f17ce1eb9: Invasion of property; cattle rearing; removal of sand
bb20518dbf0357d7a8ad96f81a5a7c5a6a1c653d: Tarumã TI was declared traditional possession of the Guarani Mbya people in 2009, through Ordinance MJ 2.747 with 2,172 hectares. The Guarani Mbya live in two villages inside the land. Even so, most of IT Tarumã is in possession and being exploited by non-indigenous people, especially with cattle raising and sand mining. These invasions prevent indigenous people from fully exercising the right to the exclusive enjoyment of their traditional land.
88718d8a38fca27f086dfdbffbf72c75773bf2ce: Damage to heritage; destruction of the village entrance gate
ebf6cf7d749a14dd2a1e3ce520401346658da768: A couple of Guarani reported having found the entrance gate of the village knocked down and damaged. This gate was located on the road that gives access to the villas and where a new house was being built. In the middle of the pandemic, this place where the gate was served as a sanitary barrier, for greater security of the indigenous who are building a new village within IT.
26ae65f32b90e9555b3ba452d469055e3d067b32: Monoculture of eucalyptus; pasture; silting of the river; damage to the environment
c580015959e0d8ed906dd5869f06b5c7986dc48b: In all the surroundings of TI Araribá, there is planting of monoculture of eucalyptus, orange and pasture for cattle, generating silting of the river Araribá, drying of springs and environmental damage to the indigenous community. There is no policy of environmental compensation and soil recovery for the community.
47a7412d18c6a83f9a52e2e7e0a4b0769bc94f19: Three highways and a rural road pass within the Araribá IT. The asphalting of the three highways was done without prior consultation of the indigenous community and without compensation for the impact caused. There's no signal and no speed control. The leaders reported the death of two indigenous people hit one of the highways in previous years. In addition, the transit of non-indigenous people within the territory becomes a threat to the way of life of indigenous people, who are vulnerable to all kinds of harassment and interference in their own culture.
66e2691b94dcf5f41f0f2293ccc33add25cfb2f0: Non-indigenous residents who occupy the vicinity of the Ka’aguy Hovy IT surrounded the area where the Yvyty Mirim community is located. The irregular allotment, growing in the region, did not respect the area that includes the indigenous community. The landowner placed his concrete morons with barbed wire surrounding the entire front of the village, as well as making access entrance to the area of the community where about fifteen people, mostly women, live from the Mbya Guarani people.
fae6c29c01b7dfcfed8f4c30a27b7842adff8103: The Itapuã village was invaded on December 18 and 19 by landowners of the region. Itapuã village is one of the communities located in the Kaaguy Hovy IT. The IT population is estimated at around 220 people living in the following tekoá: Itaguá, Jejety, Kaaguy Poty, Yvyty Mirim, Taquaty and Itapuã, where the last invasion of the landowners took place. The attacks by landowners and hunters at the Kaaguy Hovy IT in the municipality of Iguape (SP), has brought fear of more serious conflicts by the inhabitants of the village Tekoa Itapuã. There are reports and videos recorded by the village residents reporting this invasion. A landowner, known as Zé do Bico, along with others, deforested and burned two plots of land for real estate within the limits of the Kaaguy Hovy IT. The invasions intensified in the last three years encouraged by the discriminatory speeches of President Bolsonaro and the mayor of the municipality of Iguape, who does not recognize the rights of the indigenous and still campaign against the demarcation process.
dccb2b7ab81a5c0fdd071d132d23282295854cc8: A farm hotel in Peruíbe, on the coast of São Paulo, was fined more than R $ 500,000 and embarked for operating in the Piaçaguera IT, according to Ibama. In addition, the environmental agency reported that wild animals were found exposed in captivity at the site. Five macaws, one parrot and two pythons were seized, which were sent to the Silvestre Animal Screening Center. There were also exotic fish in a pond, which would also be removed. The action was attended by MPF representatives.
c95c752c1eccdf9344aef07f8aab3a78191950b2: Invasion; house destruction; threats; aggression; damage to property
501dcde53e9273b475b8916fd157c7328d63bc45: Since November 23, Tekoá Kuaray Oua has been threatened by non-Indians who claim to have bought the land in the region and try to coerce the community to leave the site. Non-indigenous people threaten the Guarani Mbya to leave the village that is inside Tenondé Porã IT, which was declared as traditional indigenous occupation by Ordinance 548 of May 6, 2016. There were several threats. They even destroyed one of the houses, saying they'd come back to take down the others. On December 13, some men came shooting up and destroyed tiles and other building materials in order to frighten and intimidate the indigenous. On December 18, accompanied by the Military Police, these men returned with camcorders and drones, saying they were allowed to register images of the village. They haven't filed any papers. Funai, PF and MPF were informed of the situation, but by the end of the year they had taken no steps to protect the indigenous people.
9b9307cb1fa3ef2287ee4ca9060e249767615246: On September 29, 2021, the group of indigenous people who protect the territory found tents, tools and generators of a team, on a trail that arrives at Pico do Corcovado, an area within the indigenous land, superimposed to Parque Piaçaguera, administered by the Forest Foundation. The team was expanding the trail, without any dialogue with the indigenous community or Funai. The indigenous did not allow the continuity of any work or the permanence of the people in the area of the community. The MPF was activated and there were several meetings between the indigenous community and the Forest Foundation, which resulted in an environmental protection project for the area, without expanding the trail and with permanent dialogue with the indigenous leaders.
e14e03ed9e34829ac139778110170bebbaf8e3b9: The leaders Guarani Nandeva of IT Ywyty Guaçu – Renascer state that the territory suffers from the invasion of non-indigenous for mining activities since 2019 in an area located north of the territory. Even with several reports and inspection requests made for Funai and MPF, there are daily presence of people removing sand, stones and land from within the indigenous land, which are marketed in brick factories and buildings and used for the maintenance of existing condominiums in the city. The leaders say that every day there is circulation of trucks that enter the territory to get the material.
799d6ac1c79b251e6c88054494c87b2a95b43a41: The leaders Guarani Nhandeva reported that the northern part of TI Ywyty Guaçu – Renascer is being batched and marketed. In November, the leaders succeeded with Funai identification plates of the Indigenous Land, and placed in this area three plates, which, in the same week, were destroyed by non-indigenous people.
f007ffd3a4c0771787ab81665960a85af6839b8d: With the process of demarcation of their land still paralyzed by Funai, the Krahô people of Takaywrá village continue to live provisionally in an environmental reserve of the settlement São Judas Tadeu, in the municipality of Lagoa da Confusion (TO). As recorded in recent years, the people continue to suffer from the decrease and contamination of the water of the River Formoso and the drought caused by farmers, who draw water from the river to irrigate their crops. In the dry season, from June to November, this situation causes the death of fish and impacts one of the main sources of food for indigenous peoples. Agribusiness has batched the rivers with dams, impacting the navigability of the river and the environment, as the fish can no longer climb to spawn.
e1bef90d59dcfac9291f1dae13ff4f5683077007: Possory invasion; advance of about farm over IT
7e336ecb7730c2fc6ab842542619c53ffba598df: According to reports of indigenous peoples Xerente, the neighboring farmer removed an old fence from the border of the territory, started marks and plates identifying and delimiting the boundaries between Funil IT and private property. Illegal action alters the boundaries of IT's borders, favoring the increase in area for the farmer. The indigenous leaders, when observing the invasion of the territory, communicated to Funai, who, in turn, did not adopt any administrative procedure to determine the facts taken. Only after an attack on the indigenous peoples took place, Funai's coordination decided on a team to go to the site of the invasion and make a previous survey and then adopt procedures. The CR-Araguaia-Tocantins collected GPS points from the site of the invasion and forwarded them to the land sector of Funai/DF for analysis.
6801d35565b50f685bca0ef4b018e5b0ff5f3298: For the third consecutive year, the region of Mata do Mammao, a forest area of Bananal Island, where indigenous peoples isolated from the Avá-Canoeiro people live, was struck by fire. Still in 2019, the Federal Court had determined that Funai, ICMBio and Ibama presented a work plan with measures to locate and qualify records of the existence of isolates in the region and to prevent the entry of fire in the Forest. The studies weren't done. As of July 2021, Brigadiers of Ibama, ICMBio and Funai carried out firefighters and fire lines to prevent fires from reaching Mata do Mammao, which includes the southern region of TI Inãwébohona and a part of TI Parque do Araguaia. Nevertheless, in September 2021, 37,000 hectares of the island had already been hit by fire, including in the forest area where indigenous people live in voluntary isolation. During the 2019 fires, the isolates came to be spotted from a helicopter that made the fire air combat. Throughout the year 2021, Inpe's reference satellite recorded 622 fire outbreaks in the Inãwébohona IT – much of them directly over the Mama Forest.
484bca69093ac35e95d1584e19d01dbb25bc52a3: As has been happening in recent years, in 2021 TI Inãwébohona, on Bananal Island, was also severely affected by the projects of companies and large agribusiness enterprises, which, through bombs, divert water from the Javaé river to their soybean, rice and watermelon plantations. Irrigation projects enhance the natural reduction of the volume of rivers in the dry months, between June and November. The situation is aggravated by the use of pesticides in crops, which end up contaminating the water that is used by the indigenous.
3f20955775acf461930ab1c55c137844afbb1347: The Krahô-Kanela IT continues to be impacted by the various agribusiness projects that use irrigation of river channels to maintain their production near Bananal Island. These projects involve the construction of dams to channel water from rivers to plantations, and directly impact the subsistence of indigenous peoples in the region, due to the decrease in the volume of waters and the availability of fish, the food base of these populations. For at least two years, indigenous leaders have denounced the environmental impacts and damage caused by agribusiness in the region of the municipalities of Formoso do Araguaia, Lagoa da Confusion and around Bananal Island. In 2020, even with the critical drought situation in the Formoso and Javaé rivers, the Court of Justice of Tocantins allowed farmers to keep water capture from the basin. The situation was repeated in 2021, despite a new action by the MP of Tocantins, in July, seeking the suspension of licenses due to severe drought. Bananal Island is now not an island, it is desertion of island. Sand alone”, lamented chief Wagner Krahô-Kanela, in a report that denounced the drought of the rivers in September.
033dca178efc0324616df5ebd9412bdd1f004ef8: For years Cimi has been receiving information from the Krahô people about an invasion of Kraholândia IT, located in the south of the territory, in the municipality of Itacajá. Starting from this complaint, missionaries and missionaries from Cimi Regional Goiás-Tocantins visited Krahô territory, with the intention of investigating and collecting more information about this invasion. According to leadership information, the invasion has been taking place for many years, and it has left the community concerned. After meeting with some leaders, a team moved to the area claimed for investigation. The team provided equipment (GPS, camera) in order to collect more efficient data from IT limits and visit the geographic landmark, so that, after overlapping on Funai's official map, an analysis was made and accurate conclusions were reached. With the GPS coordinates and field survey, added to the indigenous reports, it was observed the advance of the farmer about 500 meters within the IT. As verified, this is an invasion for the use of agricultural activity in this space, with pasture and cattle on site.
5ad99bee5641fe9fdff95364a5213ebb9aa677b3: TI Mata Alagada is an area claimed by the Krahô-Kanela people as part of its traditional territory – most of it, since the State has reserved only 7 of the 31 thousand hectares claimed by the people. Since there is still no administrative procedure to proceed with the review of the limits of the territory Krahô-Kanela, this area is more affected and even more vulnerable to agribusiness projects that use irrigation of river channels to maintain their large areas of monoculture, kidnapping water from the rivers surrounding Bananal Island. The situation remained in 2021, despite the actions of the MP of Tocantins seeking to suspend the licenses that authorized the capture of water from the rivers Formoso and Javaé.
c4a5644cc30bd76d699b4c0f68621b01e41e1507: Between January and October 2021, Inpe registered 1,358 focuses on IT Araguaia Park, 31% more than in the same period of 2020. TI Parque do Araguaia, the one that burned the most in the period of 2021, faces advancement of livestock, deforestation and illegal fishing. Nathanael Karajá, chief of Lariwana Village on Bananal Island, reports: We hear President Bolsonaro say that the Indians are burning in the Amazon. Our people don't do that. The invaders are the ones who set fire to clear the road and can enter more easily. But there's no government support to oversee. We keep thinking, what do they want? Do they want to take [the land] from us, little by little?” In April, the Jair Bolsonaro government approved a 24% cut in the Environment budget for this year. Of the total initially predicted, the actions of control and environmental surveillance lost R $ 11.6 million, while prevention and control of forest fires had a reduction of R $ 6 million. With 1,359 hectares, TI Araguaia Park has 3,502 inhabitants of four peoples: Karajá, Javaé, Tapirapé and Avá-Canoeiro. In addition to the cattle lease, authorized by the competent agencies, the residents live with loggers and illegal fishermen. The largest fires were concentrated in a region known as Mata do Mamao, where isolated indigenous people live. Beyond IT Araguaia Park, the Island houses Inawebohona IT and Araguaia National Park. The presence of loggers and fishermen is increasingly frequent in IT, and indigenous peoples have no tools to monitor and stop these illegal activities. “Bananal Island is very rich in fish. The most wanted is the pirarucu, but they also come after the peacock bass, the painted and the turtle. Her meat is very hot is very expensive. They take and take frozen, especially for Pará ", says the chief. In addition to the destruction of the environment, indigenous families are also being impacted on their own livelihood, as the number of illegal fishermen and hunters within IT has increased.
03be6de9cb25c27cb80515044781e38cc4309456: As occurred in 2019 and 2020, the indigenous lands of Bananal Island were affected by large fires that reached the area of Mata do Mammao, where isolated indigenous people live. In 2021, the Araguaia Park TI was, again, the indigenous land with the highest number of fires registered in the country – between January and December, the INPE reference satellite recorded 1393 heat outbreaks on IT. Despite the work of Brigadiers carried out from July, with the opening of raiders and fire lines, the fires again advanced on the forest area where indigenous people of the Avá-Canoeiro people live in voluntary isolation. Land lease in IT Araguaia Park and the burning of areas to prepare the pastures causes the fire to be widely used within IT and ends up reaching areas until then preserved. In addition, the fires of previous years have weakened the vegetation cover of the Mamáo Forest, reducing the humidity of an area that was closed forest and providing more fuel to fire, which becomes more difficult to control each year.
11d5cf0df2798afd7bebfc8aeffbe5065c10ed84: Teams of the Environmental Police and Funai found areas deforested at points invaded by loggers within the largest island surrounded by river water on the planet – the island of Bananal, in the west of Tocantins. Several centuries old trees have been knocked down. The noble trees are the most sought after by the loggers, for they are the ones with the highest volume and yield. Even a jatob over a hundred years old was overthrown by criminals. According to the inspectors, there are signs that the drop was recent. The island of 20,000 km2 is where are the largest indigenous populations of Tocantins and therefore preserves an untouched nature. It's entering our territory, our home, right? We can't say anything, we can't even ask to withdraw because there can still be violence against us ", says the indigenous Arielly Karajá, who is chief of one of the villages.
2a27731950e2f6d447a769eb15834659c949985e: The Avá-Canoeiro people continued to experience, in 2021, the problems that have been reported for years and that have been aggravated by the coronavirus pandemic. Since the forced contact with the people by Funai in the 1970s, indigenous people have suffered a series of violence and violations, such as the expulsion of their traditional territory known as Mata Azul, and identified by Funai under the name TI Taego Awá. To this day, although the IT has already been declared by the Ministry of Justice, they remain outside the area claimed, living in villages of the Javaé and Karajá peoples on Bananal Island. While waiting for the disintrusion of their land, with the withdrawal of two settlements from the Incra and the Eletroenge farm, the leaders Avá is threatened by the occupants of their territory. In addition, their land continues to be degraded by non-indigenous occupants.
6a5d1ce0c3be67b3cd0f149988f2e425f2b855c5: For years Xerente leaders have denounced the invasion of their territory by non-indigenous people, mainly to do illegal logging. On March 20, two men were registered, 5 km from the entrance of Morro Luau, located in Lajeado, a distant city 55 km from Palmas (TO), carrying wood taken from IT Xerente without environmental license and carrying a chainsaw that did not have the proper License of Port and Use. The Environmental Military Police was informed about a possible environmental crime related to the transportation of forest products. Already at the location of the occurrence, they found a truck loaded with stakes without the Forest Origin Document (DOF). According to the police, when conducting the approach, the military were informed that the product had been purchased within Xerente IT and that they had been hired to carry the cargo. The men were taken to the Federal Police Department (PFD) in Palmas. The police seized three cell phones, one truck and the forest products. Such facts have occurred more frequently, because the public agencies that should supervise and protect indigenous territories are in the process of dismounting and deviating from their constitutional actions, such as Funai and Ibama.

5520b7625a8473a762c2037e83ce4369412fc2de: The Xerente people report invasion of non-indigenous people within the IT to extract, remove and illegally sell timber, which has caused serious damage to the community and the environment. There are reports that some indigenous people are being co-opted and involved in the process of extraction and sale of wood. In February 2021, PF and Funai carried out an on-site action to contain this illegal practice. This time, on February 6, 2021, two men of 43 and 49 years old, who were in a truck and a motorcycle, inside the IT, were arrested red-handedly in the act of deforestation. They also found a firearm and chainsaw. The criminals were taken to the PF headquarters in Palmas. The case is being investigated to see if there are others involved in the case. However, this crime continued to occur throughout the year, as has been repeatedly denounced by the leaders of the Xerente people. The public agencies that should supervise and protect indigenous territories are in the process of dismantling and deviating from their constitutional activities, such as Funai and Ibama. With this, invaders have their criminal actions facilitated within indigenous territories.
1f1004fd40624264e13941804ae98ff55e0cd1ba: Hector Moreira Saldanha does time in semi-open regime and electronic anklet door. In the early hours of January 1st, Hector suffered from stomach pain and needed to go to the hospital; before seeking care, he telephoned the correctional officer to report his departure from his home. As the agent did not answer the call, and as he felt very bad, Hector followed his wife to the hospital. He was attended to, being in observation for about three hours and, after discharge, returned to his home. The criminal officer sent a report to the judge arguing that Hector would have spent the night at a party and, with that, his sentence was increased and Hector returned to the closed regime. His wife requested medical care records from the hospital, but the hospital claims it was lost with the flood that occurred days after the visit. Reported the situation at the State Public Defender's Office. Hector returned to the semi-open, but the sentence was not decrepit. The indigenous claims to be persecuted by the prison agent, who is also a squatter in his territory and anti-indigenous.

aedeb067dde7c13e9f97f631f6152089cca90d38: Military already occupy almost 60% of Funai regional coordination in the Legal Amazon. Of Funai's 24 regional coordinations in the region, 14 are led by military personnel. The positions are occupied by four captains, four lieutenants, a lieutenant colonel, a paratrooper and four marines – one of them from the reserve. The proportion of military personnel in the head of coordination is 58.3% in the nine states of the Legal Amazon. In other regions of the country, the incidence is 26.7%. “In addition to being strategic in the military sense, because it has many international interests, the Legal Amazon is also attractive for exploitation of resources improperly, colluding with large corporations, especially in the extraction of wood, mining and agribusiness,” Dinamam Tuxá, executive coordinator making threats within the territory, analyzes. The server would be carrying basic baskets and distributing them as appropriate, without consulting the leaders and without respecting the way the people organize. He still made threats to cut off the right to assistance. With this, Funai's server has provoked an environment of discord and disharmony within the community. The MPF was triggered and requested explanations from Funai about the server conduct.

7d0734dcfb914a67b0abdaf5ab9ec457b587eb2b: Two Yanomami associations (Ayrca and Kumirayoma) sent a letter to the Army and the MPF demanding the departure of the commander of the 5th Special Border Platoon, on the charge of acting authoritarianly against the indigenous. The Army denies misconduct, but stated it would investigate the complaint. The document accuses Lieutenant Castilho of entering the villages with armed men, without the authority of the leaders, of submitting Military police attacked indigenous people with pepper spray at the demonstration headquarters and expected to be received by the president of the indigenous agency to truculent magazines and threaten to shoot them. The platoon is next to the Maturacá community (AM) at Yanomami IT. In the complaint, the leaders inform that “the apex of this authoritarian and truculent posture happened when our Yanomami warriors were returning from the hunt bringing the already smoked and accommodated fighters, as our cultural tradition sends for the banana party. [The commander] gave a loud shout giving orders for the vessel to stop, for his soldiers to open the volumes that were there and the inspection was done. But in our traditional culture, that is not allowed. Those packages represent the essence of the funeral ritual of our deceased loved ones. There's no way it can be opened. But the lieutenant wanted to open and threatened to shoot the stern motor if it was not obeyed promptly.” The leaders closed the document demanding respect for the community and provisions.
56b7a9d753e807e90304ae95e63a8de5df78819d: The head of Regional Coordination Madeira, Funai, and captain of the Army, Cláudio Rocha, is accused of not delivering five aluminum boats (known as flyers) and five aft engines to the Mura communities of Lake Capanã, in the Amazon. According to the indigenous people, the equipment was purchased in 2018, worth R $ 60 thousand, through a project presented by the chief at the time, Agnaldo Francisco da Costa Leite, Funai. The chief died of Covid-19 in April this year, and his son Ivan Mura took the lead. Ivan reports that “the coordinator is Photo: Mídia NINJA (@midianinja) of Funai, in Brasilia, in June; people refused to deliver the equipment and we denounced it by deviation of the heritage to Funai”. Funai's coordinator denies the charges. Funai states that the aforementioned vessels “are not indigenous heritage, but the heritage of Funai itself, which is given to indigenous people for a determined period of time to carry out activities aimed at environmental management and protection in the indigenous lands of the Madeira River region and its tributaries, state of Amazonas”. Mura leaders have requested that the MPF investigate the case.
3d1222f8c3147b852172278b5aa2c93f8d9de084: The PF opened investigation, after having been triggered by Marcelo Xavier, to investigate indigenous leaders and nine employees of Funai itself, on the charge that these would act to put “diverse barriers and obstacles to approval” of the project that provides for the installation of a high voltage network between Manaus (AM) and Boa Vista (RR), known as “Linhão de Tucuruí”. Of the 721 km planned in the layout of the network planned to be erected next to the BR-174, highway that connects the two capitals, 125 km pass within the Waimiri Atroari IT, where more than two thousand indigenous people live. The indigenous demand that they be consulted on the construction process and charge measures to reduce the impact of the work on their lands. These appointments are in progress. The lawyer who works in the defense of the indigenous, Jonas Carvalho, said that in 30 years of advocacy he had never seen a president of Funai act against the indigenous peoples and the very servants of the foundation, who have the mission to mediate and defend their rights. “I will provide all the necessary clarifications, whatever you want to know. There's absolutely nothing to hide. In all those years when I advocate, I have never seen a president of Funai deliberately request an inquest against indigenous people. That's unqualified. His institutional function is to defend the indigenous. He should be the first to do this”, said the lawyer.

f0b8022524a4a4898f2c7e55527388f312586583: The indigenous Jaminawa Gabriel, Marcelo and Arimar were on the Purus River, fishing and hunting alligator near Kayapuká village, in the indigenous land; they carried two rifles, when they were approached by three police officers and representatives of the ICMBio. The Indians were charged with possession of illegal weapons and predatory hunting. The abusive action represented various types of violence: verbal threats, were handcuffed and arrested within the indigenous territory, without the right to communication with the family, which was in despair, without knowing what would have happened and already having relatives as missing. The family only heard two days later, when Cimi triggered the MPF and obtained information. Three days after the arrest, the Indians were released and answered process in freedom.
b2651a55846653d761225280cd4159d905f32d4d: Indigenous Mura da Aldeia Taquara report that a police officer owns buffalo near the village. According to the people, he passes through the community with his nephews, who are also creators, displaying military uniform and a caliber 22 pistol, in order to intimidate the indigenous. With this intimidating behavior, it aims to frighten the population so that, embarrassed, they walk away and feel powerless. The creation of buffalo creates a number of problems for indigenous peoples, such as the destruction of swiddens and pollution of rivers. Complaints were made to the MPF, Funai, Dsei, Seduc and Ipaam, but by the end of the year there was no provision.
6106eb48a6f95bed340fe4d79b894a185084530a: Report by Reporter Brazil, republished by Folha de São Paulo, shows that the indication of military and political to occupy positions in indigenous health aggravated the health crisis already experienced by indigenous peoples during the Covid-19 pandemic. In at least four of them there were indications of military or political allies who accumulate complaints of inexperience, accusations of truculence in the interaction with communities and poor management amid the pandemic. Among the most serious cases investigated by the Reporter Brazil are that of a coordinator working armed and intimidating indigenous people, diversion of funds to fight the pandemic and suspected distribution of chloroquine in the villages – a drug proven ineffective to fight the coronavirus.

6f863ffbc6e2b12bf1f8d1abeaef83b0479feecc: During the occupation of the Sacred Cross of the Pajé Potiguara, held after the destruction of the terreiro, cemetery and sacred forest of the Potiguara people, the young Francisco Henrique Tabajara, known as Chico, which is a leadership and LGBTQIA+, was camped with relatives in solidarity and support for the struggle. He was arbitrarily arrested by the Military Police because he was carrying a small amount of marijuana, used for medicinal purposes. The young indigenous person undergoes health care due to psychological and neurological disorders. The truculent action led Francisco to present seizure inside the police car. Apoinme was activated in the person of chief and lawyer Jorge Tabajara, to provide legal advice to Francisco. The release license was obtained on October 6, 2021.
b1b8760cf5527d6e2258437d90931b0fb995773a: The city of Caucaia, once again, destroyed two beach tents of the Anacé people, using machines. The site, besides giving access to the beach, security point, is a means of subsistence of direct families. The situation impacts the entire Anacé population, of about 3000 indigenous people, who use the place for their leisure and spirituality practices. The community reported arbitrariness to the Regional Human Rights Defender of the Union Public Defender.
e333125e2531d3d8e50b03444b53f12bef6c57a3: About 800 indigenous peoples of 40 peoples from all regions of the country, who participated in the mobilization entitled “Revante Pela Terra”, performed an act in front of Funai headquarters in Brasilia, and expected to be welcomed by the president of the agency, Marcelo Xavier; leaders denounce truculence and anti-indigenous action of the Military Police, which attacked the demonstration. In addition to not being received at Funai, the Indians were attacked with bombs and pepper spray by the police who blocked the entrance of the building. Since the end of May, the indigenous peoples expressed themselves in defense of their constitutional rights and against anti-indigenous measures such as the Bill (PL) 490/2007, which dealt with the CCJC of the House of Representatives, in addition to following the Supreme Court judgment on the Extraordinary Resource (RE) 1,017,365, which discusses the time frame and the demarcation of lands. The indigenous denounce several measures contrary to their rights taken by Funai under the Bolsonaro government, with the aim of facilitating the exploitation of their territories by non-indigenous people, allowing the certification of private properties on unholy lands, such as Normative Instruction No. 09, and reducing the protection and assistance to communities in struggle for demarcation. In addition, people also denounce the various actions of intimidation and criminalization of indigenous leaders and organizations. In recent months, Funai has denounced indigenous people who are critical of the Bolsonaro government and has provoked investigations to investigate the occurrence of “difference” against the government. The attack by policemen occurred shortly after the approximately 800 indigenous people arrived at the building where Funai's national headquarters are located. On arrival, they found the entrances blocked by a large police contingent. The leaders expected to be received by the president of the indigenist organ, but were not heard – and were also prevented by the police from conducting speeches in a sound car, located on a street opposite the building. The climate became even more tense after this ban, and the Indians were soon surprised by the shock troops, who have already arrived by firing bombs. After the conflict, still surrounded by the police contingent, leaders held a press conference in front of Funai, in which they reinforced the request for Marcelo Xavier to leave the position. In an open letter, the indigenous peoples said that this is “the worst management in the history of the Foundation, which no longer fulfills the function of protecting and promoting the rights of indigenous peoples in order to negotiate our lives and instrumentalize them for the sake of unnecessary and particular interests of agribusiness, illegal mining and other threats that endanger our existence”.
2168b263d7c687a5dc91e9e01ba0b7e68b6fabd3: Truculent police action; attack with pepper spray, gas and rubber bullets
9d3f5deec0f1b83f506b109a326078f90c1cdf7e: The indigenous leader Sônia Guajajara, coordinator of Apib, was subpoenaed by the delegate of the Federal Police, Francisco Vicente Badenes Junior, to give a statement in an inquiry opened by PF at the request of a letter of the president of Funai, Marcelo Augusto Xavier da Silva, made to the director-general of PF, Rolando Alexandre de Sousa. The reason for the subpoena is because of the documentary entitled “Maracá”, which was produced by Apib and released on the internet and which, according to Funai, propagates “lies” against the government. Sonia Guajajara, on social media, said: “The persecution of this government is unacceptable and absurd! They won’t shut us up!” In the documentary, Apib points out a series of violations of the rights of indigenous peoples by the federal government during the Covid-19 pandemic. Note published by Apib reports that “the government seeks to intimidate indigenous peoples in a clear attempt to curtail our freedom of expression, which is the most important tool to denounce human rights violations.” According to the note, at the end of April 2021 “more than half of the indigenous peoples were directly affected by Covid-19, with more than 53,000 confirmed cases and 1,059 killed”.
7c4d7b2fea43108f03f9d443b67d8a1d092b80fb: Abuse of authority; investigation and intimidation of indigenous leadership
61452b5fef5accb6857a8c2ad6aaec8668cff190: A large group of indigenous people, with children and elderly people, was attacked by the Military Police on the afternoon of June 22, in front of Annex 2 of the House of Representatives, during a peaceful protest against the vote of PL 490/2007, which was about to be approved by the Constitution and Justice Commission (CCJ) of the House. The project, voted and approved days after the brutal attack, attacks the territorial rights guaranteed to indigenous peoples by the Federal Constitution, transforms into law the thesis of the time frame and opens the indigenous lands for predatory exploitation. The attacks took place in the parking lot of Annex 2 of the House, with rubber bullets, tear gas bombs and moral effect, after several days of tension by the police, who prevented the use of sound cars and barred the indigenous access to the entrance of the Annex with bars. Two indigenous people (one man and one woman) had to remain under observation at the Base Hospital in Brasília, with serious injuries. In addition to the two, 11 more people, among children, elderly and women, had minor injuries and were attended in the health tent of Camp Levante pela Terra (ALT), next to the National Theatre. Emergency care to the indigenous was hampered by the Shock Corps that was on site, as recorded in videos from the time of the attack. The protesters came from a peaceful march through the Ministries Esplanade when they were received with gas bombs and moral effect, from a barricade mounted by the Shock Battalion at the entrance to Annex 2, where the sessions of the House committees take place. There was no action or incident by the indigenous that justified the violent action of the police. According to information, there were teams from the Legislative, Military and Shock Battalion, with strong repression apparatus, including the presence of a ‘caveirão’ (armored car of the Shock Corps) and cavalry. The indigenous march was part of the program of the camp, which at that time gathered about 850 indigenous peoples from 48 peoples from all regions of Brazil. “The relatives only came to demonstrate not to be approved the PL that will end the demarcation of indigenous lands, and the police have already been shooting bombs. They may gather to take away our rights, but when we try to manifest is treated with truculence ", said Alessandra Korap Munduruku. “We are here with children and elderly people too, many people were affected, they were sick”, added. “We were brutally attacked in a cowardly manner before we arrived to follow the vote. We have injured indigenous people and the police bombed the paramedics making it difficult to provide care,” said Dinam Tuxá, executive coordinator of the Articulation of Indigenous Peoples of Brazil (Apib).
6c1f198de155d88f5f5d12012e5ef64ab7bad8ed: On November 18, 2021, indigenous Akroá-Gamella expelled from their territory officials from an energy company, who were accompanied by armed gunmen who said they were police officers. 590450b8bec4cb5c1208d6e1ed8436899f99376b: On 15/11/2020, a 23-year-old pregnant Xavante, wife of a 21-year-old Xavante, was sexually harassed by a non-indigenous man from Campinápolis. As it was election day, the man offered her a ride on a motorcycle to the school, the place of the vote; however, on the way she realized that he was going out of town, towards a forest, on a nearby farm. Scared, still inside the city, the young woman jumped off the bike, wounding herself in various parts of the body. One of his uncles saw the whole fall scene, because he was standing on his bike, talking on his cell phone. He recognized the assailant, but preferred to help his niece rather than pursue him. On November 15 and 17, 2020, the couple recorded police reports, but the case did not end in an investigation or punishment of the aggressor. On March 17, 2021, a Salesian missionary took the young woman’s uncle (who, at the time, saw her jump off the bike to escape) to testify to the police, accompanied by her father. However, the Civil Police clerk stopped recording two facts of paramount importance for the evidence of the crime, and the uncle, without realizing it, signed the statement without reading its content. The missionaries, reading the testimony, realized the omission of the two facts. On March 19, a Salesian missionary sought out his young uncle in Campinápolis. He said he clearly remembered that he had reported the two facts to the police clerk. He and the missionary then returned to the police station. The clerk apologized, saying that the young deponent had not spoken about the facts. But at the insistence of the missionary and the young man, the scribe agreed to make a supplement in the testimony of the 17th, which, after being read, was signed. After that, everyone was waiting for the delegate to position himself, asking or not for the indictment of the accused with the local prosecutor. However, on August 18, the Salesian went to the police station to learn about the progress of the case, and was surprised by the reply that the delegate had filed the inquiry. The clerk explained that the security cameras of some houses, existing on the route where the accused had passed on November 15, 2020, did not record the passage of his motorcycle. The missionary asked about the possibility of him being with another motorcycle and about the robust facts reported by the young woman's uncle on March 19 not being taken into account. The clerk said the deputy had already given his opinion and filed the case. It is worth noting that even the population of Campinápolis being composed of 55% of Xavante indigenous people, there is no interpreter of the dominant language in the police station, as well as there was no female police officer to take the testimony of the battered young woman; the young woman was twice assaulted, through the embarrassment of reporting the situation experienced to a scribe who, at all times, said that she was contradicting herself. All this neglect, violation of rights and abuse of power against the Xavante Indians was not accompanied by Funai.

6169efcf943d7edfb805e092a72b5929ce3c5470: The indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá Tatiane da Silva Manoel, living in the village Tey Kue, had been in health care for four months, under the care of another indigenous, living in the urban area. Tatiane died on 28 October 2021, and the family was prevented by the First Court of Justice of Caarapó from transferring the body to the village and proceeding with the funeral according to the cultural traditions of the people. The decision was at the request of the person who had been taking care of Tatiane for four months, saying she was a “curator”, responsible for the deceased. Public defender Neyla Ferreira Mendes was triggered by the community and reported that “the burial in the Kaiowá ethnic community, besides being a right of the victim’s family, is linked to indigenous traditions. That's inconceivable. The one who decides where she should be buried is her community and her relatives. It is not the judge who decides that.” And he added: “The state interfered improperly when it received the complaint and assumed family abuse. You didn't hear the community. What link is this that the curator claims four months and that the judicial decision supports that it is greater than the ties she has with the community of origin of the victim, of a lifetime?” In the decision, the judge claims that “in such a context, if, due to prolonged omission and negligence, the parents lost responsibility for Tatiane, while living, there is no reason to understand that, with his death, they would have returned to meet conditions to care for her, or for her body”. At the end of the controversy, the judge's decision prevailed which, without listening to the community, ordered the deceased to be buried in the city.

847bdeb8a96dfe206fd305fcff3642b632656bdb: In the middle of the new coronavirus pandemic, Funai supported Canadian mining company Belo Sun Mining to hold face-to-face meetings with about a hundred indigenous people in two villages in the Amazon. The company, based in Toronto, Canada, wants to accelerate its plans to explore a gold mine that can affect two indigenous lands and riverside communities that already live under the impact of the construction of the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant, in the Xingu River, Pará. The activities planned by Belo Sun would gather about 45 indigenous people in the IT Arara da Volta Grande do Xingu, and 60 to 66 participants in the IT Paquiçamba. Each event would last two days, with morning and afternoon sessions, and about 5:30 a.m. added in each of the villages. The DPU recommended Funai to reject the possibility of any face-to-face meeting during the pandemic and to suspend the effects of a “technical information” that the indigenous agency issued on 10 February, in which it gave some guidance, but did not veto the mining initiative. The document even suggests what the mining company should do “in case there is confirmation or suspicion of any Covid-19 case during the event”, advising that the case detected was immediately isolated from the group and had “the proper referral articulated by the health professional present at the site”. According to Funai, the mining company should request support from private laboratories, scheduled “before the presentation meetings of the CI-EIA (indigenous component of the environmental impact study)”, and hold meetings by video conference, “preferably with the presence of indigenous representatives, to articulate the preparations for the meetings with the region’s DSEI”. According to the data presented by the mining company itself, the disease had killed 7,366 people in Pará by January 2021 – a number that had already risen to 9,000 in March.
