Upon having the proposal refused by the indigenous, the Foundation returned, this time with a subpoena: if the women opposed the reception, the children would be removed and taken by the Guardian Council.
c27d1966397f87a2c69a1d4a0b26affac4dbfd7d: The indigenous leader Almir Suruí was summoned to testify at PF, at Funai's request, in an open inquiry because of the disclosure on the Internet of alleged “lies” against the government. On September 30, 2020, Funai’s president Marcelo Xavier sent a letter to Abin’s general director Alexandre Ramagem, asking him to “monitor” a virtual campaign promoted by two indigenous associations of the Suruí people in Rondônia. Both are related to Almir Narayamoga Suruí, one of the largest indigenous leaders in the country, recognized and internationally awarded. In addition to this investigation, Almir Suruí was also investigated by the Federal Police, also at the request of the president of Funai. Abin's investigation was completed on the last day of May 5, and pointed out that there is no irregularity, suspicion or minimum evidence of crime to be found, deciding on filing. According to Suruí’s lawyer, Ramires Andrade, the office of the president of Funai for the general director of Abin “scans and confirms what we already knew, which is an attempt by the federal government to pressure and coerce the indigenous”. He also said that “the president of Funai, although it is a police career, does not occupy the position as a PF researcher”, and that “his duties there are different from PF. At the base is the PF that helps us when we need support. But the president of Funai has a very clear function, which is to protect the indigenous community. It is the function that justified the creation of Funai. It exists essentially for this, to provide support to indigenous peoples. It cannot be used in the apparatus movement to pressure indigenous movements”.
745a087eed92212e1a3cac8595da8627878edf61: Ana Lúcia Puruborá is an indigenous woman who lives in an urban area in Guajará-Mirim. She was diagnosed with depression and her son went to reside with her to assist in her health care, along with her wife, of the Makurap people, and her 4-year-old son. An acquaintance of Ana Lucia's son asked to spend a few days at her house in a room outside. However, the family had no knowledge that the boy had committed theft and was being sought out by the civilian police. At the time of the robbery, the cops picked him up, and they were on their way to the hospital to perform a body crime test, when the boy took one of the cops' gun and ran away, making them angry. One morning, with only Mrs.Anna Lucia and her four - year - old grandson, the police entered the house violently and struck the wanted boy and also Mrs. Ana Lúcia, claiming she was hiding a criminal in her house. She explained that she knew nothing, tried to call for help on her cell phone, but the cops pulled the device out of her hand and continued to assault her and kick her in front of the child. Cops ransacked the whole house, smashed objects, furniture, and there were blood marks all over the house. The cops took the boy and even Mrs. Ana Lucia, handcuffed. Mrs. Ana Lucia's depression worsened, as did her physical condition; she had problems with her ribs and had to undergo surgery. The Public Defender was triggered and the lawsuit against the police is underway.
48b7b4d6950b07ee5fc3f48df92024d0b29f6cbb: Professor Márcia Nunes Maciel, from the Mura indigenous people, is a doctor in Social History at USP and an indigenous researcher. She taught at EE Professor Francisco Desmoret Passos, and was removed from public school for “insisting on indigenous issues”. According to director Ana Laura Camacho, the decision of her removal “came from above”, with guidance to fill Márcia in a school in Porto Velho, in the city, away from the traditional and originating communities. The indigenous teacher would be being the victim of persecution for her work, evaluates the Workers' Union in Education of Rondônia (Sintero). “There is some persecution for the work of the teacher, which is a rescue of the indigenous tradition,” said Union’s Secretary of Education, Judith Campos. For her, in addition to persecution, the case can set up bullying. “The very case in which the school erased the figure of an Indian on the wall confirms this persecution. The school had other walls and spaces to make new drawings, but it chose to erase the image of the Indian ", says, referring to the episode narrated in the removal document, when Marcia cried when she saw that the school erased the mural in the area of collective use that portrayed an Inca Indian. Marcia is a prominent historian and indigenous leader of Rondônia. It openly criticizes the Bolsonaro government, which advocates the exploitation of territories originating in agribusiness and mining. Since the election of the current president, attacks and violations of the rights of indigenous peoples have intensified, as well as threats to educational institutions and persecution of teachers accused of ideological indoctrination. The current governor of Rondônia, Colonel Marcos Rocha (PSL), Bolsonaro's ally, was famous for censoring books. Besides military, Marcos Rocha is also evangelical and advocate of the exploitation of indigenous lands by agribusiness. In January 2021, the Rondônia government sanctioned the reduction of 161,6 thousand hectares of conservation units Extractive Reserve Jaci-Paraná and State Park Guajará-Mirim to favor cattle raising. The decision directly impacted Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, Karipuna, Igarapé Lage, Igarapé Ribeirão, Karitiana and the people who are in voluntary isolation in the region.
d9d7b11e0665343348e6d66e7b392bbabb829bbf: In January 2021, a group of 55 indigenous Warao, including 32 children, entered Brazil from Venezuela, along the Pacaraima border. They were arrested and conducted by the Federal Police and other bodies in the municipality with the threat of collective and immediate deportation, based on Ordinance 648/20 of the Ministries of Health, Justice and Civil House. The norm, which restricts the entry of foreigners in Brazil because of the epidemic of the new coronavirus, provides for immediate deportation or repatriation, civil, administrative and criminal accountability, and prevents requests for refuge. It is the case that such rules harm the Migration Law (13.445/17), as well as the Refuge Law (9.474/97). Deportation was suspended by determination of Justice, responding to a request for injunction in Public Civil Action of the MPF and the DPU, triggered by Caritas and other civil society entities.
286cc3ecdbba12ce6809212d8f1e8c47ebad8907: Indigenous people denounce the truculent and violent action of the battalions of the Military Police and the Bope against the indigenous community of Tabatinga, in the Serras Region, within the Raposa Serra do Sol IT. According to reports from residents, military police force disabled, on the afternoon of November 16, the community monitoring post that served to prevent illicit activities and control the mining invasion. The police launched tear gas bombs and fired with firearms and also rubber bullets. According to the indigenous testimony, some of the gas bombs were dropped inside the houses, knowing the police who found people in them who were protecting themselves from the shooting. Twelve Indians were injured and two of them had to be transferred to the General Hospital of Roraima in the capital, Boa Vista, where the medical team also extracted a bullet from the chest of one of the wounded. The police also entered the community health center, knocked down shelves where medication was stored, broke the solar panel that supplies the health center and even took the radiophony equipment from the station. They also forced themselves into the community school. That same night, another group of indigenous people from the village of Willimon, in the same region of Serras, who went to provide assistance and support to the residents of Tabatinga, was also violently approached by military police, and two indigenous people had to be hospitalized at the headquarters of the municipality of Uiramutã. The PMs remained in the region, maintaining an environment of terror and threats. On November 19, a commission made up of members of the MPF, PF and Funai moved to the Tabatinga community, heard the testimonies of the residents and received from the indigenous the material that was used by the police and that they collected in the vicinity of the village, such as bullets, purses and others. While the meeting was taking place, 14 police and Bope vehicles were stationed 2 km from the village, in a clear attitude of intimidation. The PM even proposed its withdrawal from the indigenous land on the condition that the community would accept the definitive deactivation of the Supervisory Post, a proposal rejected by the indigenous peoples. At the end of the meeting, and at the request of the leaders, MPF, the PF and Funai went to the location where the PM vehicles were and communicated the decision of the communities to stay at the Post and to demand the withdrawal of the PM from the region. That same afternoon, the PM withdrew from the region. On December 8, the State Justice declined from its competence to prosecute action against the Control Post of the communities within its territory.
88b5715865352693b7a48f088353d0a60644ae69: Abuse of authority; truculent police action; intimidation; physical assault and shooting
9386d4ad3d82d0f80cf0abcb1fade41fd0957db2: On the morning of December 1st, PM and Bope personnel violently attacked an area of resumption of the Pium community at TI Pium. In the action, the police fired tear gas bombs, used pepper spray and threw rubber bullets at the community's residents. In photos and videos, you can also notice, in the background, a tractor knocking down houses. Men, women, children and animals were present at the time of the assault. Two young people were injured with rubber bullets, even though there was no resistance by the indigenous. The PM was executing a reintegration order issued by the Alto Alegre District Court, where the judge authorized the use of the police force. In similar action against the same community, having as author another farmer, the same judge declined the competence of the State Justice. This time, however, he accepted the request and determined the reintegration of possession, contrary to the competence and determination of the Supreme Court not to perform reintegrations of possession during the pandemic. The Pium community resumed an area that remained outside the demarcation of the indigenous land, although it has always been used by the community; there is the source of the Pium creek, and the site is known for the diversity of plants and herbs used by the community as traditional medicine. The area is required by farmers who intend to plant soybeans, where they are contaminating the water sources with pesticides. The CIR Legal Advisory Board will appeal against the county decision, arguing the lack of competence of the State Court in the case.
a8ff1b244610f48b7e1f0d21ba5fd18d274b021b: Abuse of authority; truculent police action; physical assault and shooting
e488b437ae4b7aae81659dcf884642e5ea232c5a: In the matter made by Reporter Brasil, a video was released that shows an area surrounded, approximately two square meters, with a plastic chair and a person lying on ground floor beaten and rubble. The audio says: “Live images of ‘the corner of shame’. I don’t know if you can see it, but they put a wire in the [thanks] business so he wouldn’t escape.” The “sing of shame” is the name that has been given to a space of involuntary confinement where Venezuelan indigenous people are arrested, without a court order, in a condition of alcoholism in the four shelters for indigenous people of Boa Vista (RR) for the reception of refugees and migrants. The images were recorded at the Pintolândia shelter, which is part of Operation Welcome, created in 2018 by Michel Temer, under the responsibility of the Brazilian Army in partnership with non-governmental organizations. Among the indigenous people, the name of the space is “sing of ill-treatment”. One of the Indians Warao sheltered in Boa Vista reported, under anonymity: “They [the military] treat us like criminals, use weapons within shelters. They have no compassion for what we're going through. They leave the person there, dirty, on the floor. And they still record. It hurts a lot.” In addition to the video, a letter of formal notice was issued by health professionals working in shelters of the Hosted Operation. The report interviewed four employees from different shelter-related organizations, who gave interviews in a condition of anonymity for fear of retaliation. Two of them claim to have personally seen the “sink of shame”. “Those who return to the shelter and demonstrate drunkenness are being forced to remain in this confined space, entitled ‘the corner of shame’, until a military member of the shelter coordination team understands that its release is possible,” says the letter, which is signed by “Brazilian government through its public agents”. The servants who sign the document qualify the actions as “practices of violence and torture” and cite cases such as “people who had their arm tied in bars or remained trapped for more than 18 hours on site”. The document details the laws and treaties that are violated, such as Article 5 of the Brazilian Federal Constitution, the American Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and the Resolution of the National Council of Human Rights. The CIR lawyer, Ivo Cípio Aureliano, who confirmed that he received the letter of complaint, as well as a request for help from the Venezuelan indigenous peoples on July 8, when eight leaders would have reported to him about the existence of the confinement space. “What happens there is a serious violation and abuse of power. Hurts the dignity of the human person, honor ", evaluates. The whistleblowers consider that the responsibility for the violation of human rights is the Army, responsible for controlling Operation Welcome.
f602bdec1bf956182b51d419d3e3759483ca98cb: Operation Welcome, particularly the Army, UNHCR and the Ministry of Citizenship decided, without prior consultation with the communities, to unite in one place the indigenous populations Warao, E’ñepa and Kariña, who reside in the Shelters of Pintoland, New Canaan and Tancredo Neves. The new shelter would agglomerate an approximate population of 1,500. The indigenous claim that they have not been notified or consulted in advance on this decision, which they consider arbitrary and without dialogue, affronting the rights recognised in ILO Convention 169: the right to consultation and participation in the measures to be adopted by the government and which may affect the lives of communities. Operation Welcome also did not communicate or consult this decision to the members of the Roraima Indigenous Migration SubGT. After leaking the news, and after denying it several times, stating that it was rumors and rumors, the Army and UNHCR had to make public their decision – which had even a date set for relocation on December 20. For this purpose, they called meetings with the indigenous peoples who characterized, at first, as “assemblies” and consultation spaces. At various times, representatives of the Army and UNHCR doubted that indigenous peoples in mobility were covered by collective rights recognized in ILO Convention 169. The concern of the indigenous peoples is with the insecurity of the new place to which they would be transferred (next to the bus station in Boa Vista, with a high rate of violence), the evident overload in local health and education systems in the neighborhood and the agglomeration of so many people in the covid-19 pandemic period. Indigenous people, along with civil society entities and some UN agencies, have been denouncing for a long time the situation that lives in shelters and presenting demands and proposals for housing solutions, alternatives to shelters, which would require new responses from culturally appropriate public policies. The Hosted Operation, after about four years of operation, failed to create a space for the construction of public policies involving the various federative entities and did not meet, to date, the demands and proposals presented by the indigenous. The leadership document was forwarded to the MPF, DPU, CNDH and Joint Migration and Refugee Commission of the National Congress.
1cc4beec2a787bfd47576c62722e829c2447b870: Abuse of power against refugees; threat of forced removal; violation of the right of prior consultation
c1ff793c7432849f0214f3221e6c94b118cb8776: On August 19, the indigenous community São Mateus, located in the Raposa Serra do Sol IT, was intimidated by the Shock Corps of the PM of Roraima. Some of the cops were wearing no mask, ignoring the prevention measures for Covid-19. The police action took place even with the leaders peacefully complying with the decision of the Justice that determined the unlocking of the highway RR-171, which passes through its territory, in the community St. Matthew. The leaders were mobilized in the fight against the circulation of alcoholic beverages, mining materials, stolen vehicles, among others, in addition to prevention against Covid-19. The indigenous peoples reported that they would demand in the Justice that Union, Funai, Ibama and PF comply with their constitutional obligations of protection and supervision of the indigenous land, especially for the immediate removal of illegal prospectors and the installation of sanitary barriers against Covid-19. They also reported that they would require the MPF to investigate and denounce indigenous peoples and associations that encourage and participate in the mining in the Raposa Serra do Sol IT, demarcated and approved after a struggle that took more than 30 years.
dd4278bea769ed61c5df9f0882acb750ce619cef: Abuse of power; intimidation by police officers
c4db5f67d8be7dbde68bc7c157c0cbcbfbcbcaf4: Two years ago, a group of Deni indigenous families, from the Amazon, lives on the banks of a mangrove in Joinville (SC). In the middle of the pandemic, without any prior notice or court order, military policemen from Santa Catarina invaded the houses and sprayed the indigenous, including children and women. Funai was activated, but decided not to get involved, claiming not to know the existence of the indigenous community in that place. The MPF was also triggered and should take steps to investigate the violent actions of the PM and identify those responsible for the action, which may be characterized as criminal, as well as forward to the Court for due punishment.
675f4e8fd24d6baab0334cd8bf33e344c2e2d3c4: Truculent police action; pepper spray attack
31893bead8050460f69b8ef2a6c9f519362551b2: The indigenous report that police actions in the recovery of Pakurity in Jureia have occurred abusively and violently. The Guarani claim that, daily, the agents of the Forest Foundation and the Environmental Military Police go to the site to take pictures and sometimes even without a mask, in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic period. They also report that the privacy of the community is frequently invaded, which is intimidated, especially children. The case regarding the security and permanence of the community is being followed by the leaders, MPF, Funai, CGY and Cimi.
41030c6c6f165ceb115bbe9757636f8bd68437e1: Evandro dos Santos, a young Pankararu, residing in São Paulo, was arrested and sentenced to nine years in prison after victims suggested that he stole cell phones in the eastern part of the capital of São Paulo. Family and defense say he's innocent and was at a party at the time of the crime, and that his indigenous identity was not respected during almost the entire process. The case occurred on May 26, 2019, when, according to the report of occurrence, around 6:30 a.m. a woman reported that it had been stolen by two men on Avenida Custódio de Sá e Faria, in Sapopemba, eastern São Paulo. According to the victim's report, the men were on a motorcycle carrying a firearm and would have stolen their phones. The woman just described that the bike was “big”. While the BO was plowed, another person arrived at the police station who also said it was stolen by the two men on a large motorcycle. The police were able to verify the location of the two suspects by means of a tracking signal from one of the stolen phones, and they started patrolling. It was then that, according to the police report, the military police found the suspects on a motorcycle on Sapopemba Avenue. There, “the garupa drew a firearm and fired towards the police,” says the document. The alleged robbers fled in the sequence, but the police managed to continue tracking, entered the community of Custódio de Sá e Faria and, in "determinate alley", the police saw the men who supposedly practiced the crime together. According to the police version, the motorbike had “dropped a backpack that was carrying on the back, and fled the place on foot and entered a riot that was in those vicinity, resulting from a party that was taking place in a community alley”, they say in the BO. Then the two men would be tempted to “disguise and disengage from the military police”. That's when Alex Gomes Silva, who was supposedly on the back of the bike, was arrested. He would have appointed Evandro as his partner, saying “I will not hold this BO alone, assumes its BO”, the military police narrate. Meanwhile, Evandro denied participation in the robberies. A personal search was carried out on both and nothing illicit was found, nor was the motorcycle that would have been used in the thefts. Despite this, the police report that Alex would have claimed that he had bought the bike for R$2,000.00 two days earlier. The backpack where the cell phones were found by the cops. According to the BO, the occurrence of the police caused “insurgency against the militiamen, who needed police support, given the imminence of escape and resistance, it was necessary to use progressive physical strength and handcuffs”, they say. However, according to the document, neither Evandro nor Alex claimed that they suffered some kind of physical aggression or embarrassment from the military police. They were both caught red-handed. Called to the police station to recognize the alleged criminals, the victim of a robbery on the 24th claimed that he recognized “without a shadow of doubt” Evandro dos Santos as one of the robbers. One of the victims who claims to have been stolen on May 26 said that “despite the use of the helmet he was able to recognize the pilot Evandro dos Santos” and that he “memorized his look”, according to the self of recognition of the person. On May 27, in a custody hearing, Alex and Evandro claimed that they suffered torture and abuse by the police on the day of the approach, “consisting on: hanging in Evandro and kicking in the legs and arms of Alex”. Lawyers and defenders who act in the case claim that arrests and reconnaissance were made irregularly. According to the lawyer and consultant of the IISC who analyzed the case at the request of the report of the Bridge, the right to self-declaration of a person as belonging to an original people, such as the Pankararu people, is a right that “carts in other guarantees for an indigenous person in the face of criminal justice”, which should be respected in the process, as guaranteed by Resolution 287 of the CNJ, including indigenous people in urban context. In this case, several illegalities were found by the professionals consulted, from the beginning of the police approach; meanwhile, Evandro has been arrested for two years.
7ff8dbd9388362ba379433ac7fcc4e37c21b99e2: On April 5, the young indigenous and a non-indigenous would have been involved in an alleged theft and physical assault on an elderly person, in a rural property located on the left bank of Ribeirão Piabanha. On April 20, the PM served a provisional arrest warrant, and took him from his home in Tocantinia, to the provisional prison in Palmas. The family sought advice and judicial assistance from the Public Defender of the State of Tocantins and Dr. Rogério Xerente, who filed a request to revoke the arrest. On May 21, Charles' release permit was fulfilled. The process remains ongoing in the Tocantins Court.
a486a1e7af202b600aae53f788f0d92bf1fa6bb9: Francis is leadership in his territory and is ahead in the struggle for the demarcation of the land of his people. There is a prohibition to prevent invasions, however, since 2012. The occupying farmers of IT have not respected the judicial decision and every year they increase the overthrows of what remains of the forest. In 2021, two occupants opened up more downfalls in places the Indians intended to make swiddens and one of them planted stakes and made fences. The Indians, tired of reporting and not seeing provisions, decided to destroy the fence. The farmer sent a worker to warn Francisco that if the people continued to destroy the fence “what would remain of the land for Francis would be seven feet”. It was reported to MPF, Funai and PF that by the end of the year they had not taken action, and the farmer completed the construction of the fence in IT.
7b11935fd6523f5df0b239d455c2582c13c4e7e7: Antônio José Apurinã is the general leader of the Valparaíso IT and for 31 years has been fighting for the demarcation of the area, along with its people. The territory claimed suffers many invasions by landowners, loggers and farmers. Constantly Antônio José has denounced the invaders and, because of this, suffers threats. In November, Antônio José went fishing in a creek in the village Maloca and, upon arriving at the site, met two people. One of them is one of the invaders of the territory. They had put in a net blocking the creek. Antônio José asked them to remove the meshworker, because that place is a territory claimed and traditionally used by the Apurinã, and reported that they should not be fishing there. The invader said he wasn't going to take off the mat and, showing off a gun, said if the chief wanted it, he would take it out himself. Antonio José was alone, then only said he wanted no confusion and again insisted that the land belongs to his people. The invader said that Antonio José is “very confident” and that he “is lucky to be still alive”. Antonio Joseph asked why he would be lucky to be still alive and reaffirmed that he had only warned that the land belongs to the Apurinan people. The intruder said the land is his that he has the title of the SPU. The leadership registered a police report and reported it to the MPF.
1d348a8a1c609ed145313fddcd282f600d0e5af7: Threat of death; intimidation with firearm
4070a6fdde1a294c91e0bd2f0ef38bffa87939bf: Francisco is chief general of TI Camicuã. In October, a grandson of his was murdered in a bar in Boca do Acre (AM), which is opposite the indigenous land. The perpetrators are people linked to a criminal faction, in which Francisco's grandson was involved. Francisco registered police reporting the perpetrators of the crime and requesting measures. On account of the complaint, Francisco was threatened with death by his own relatives. With his life at stake, he was removed from the territory, awaiting provision and protection from justice. Reported to MPF and MPE.
7f4b9494b779169e2604cc780d5591df9f1e8afc: Raimundo is a leader and has denounced invasions and deforestation in the territory. 2ccf3544789dc7b196960b5ed6cb54fb9404e622: The Vice-Cacica of the Pataxó people, Erilsa Braz dos Santos, and Chief Welington Ribeiro de Oliveira suffered an attack of intimidation and threat of death in front of their homes on the night of May 17. 50d33fdbe34b5f04d9cac660f0a395c26d0734e9: The Truká-Tupan people have been in a recovery area for 13 years and have been fighting for recognition of indigenous land. 8aa2f50e7826f7fe75190c081b265dedc7ad6895: Maria do Carmo Querino, known as Cacica Cátia, leads the struggle for demarcation of her territory, located in Belmonte, in the southern end of Bahia. 2c8d508ed5f90b3e9dae5f32db3abd07b849dff9: The indigenous Franilson Guajajara recorded an occurrence report in the Civil Police of Grajaú denouncing death threats by an invader of the indigenous land where he lives. ce88dac374f0a19f148fe5f11f8578213a9fddc9: Gunfighters entered the Arariboia IT in November 2021, seeking information on the location of Laércio Guajajara, member of the Guardians of the Forest and witness to the murder of Paulo Paulino Guajajara. 77a28d467894eedc2f62d9ff4e2ec6069fd3f0b2: On November 9, the Robson Tremembé leadership, when arriving in its field, inside the indigenous land, received a written message, anonymous, with death threat. 3a3f3ec76313bc756881c962ed863f8ced3f0dcc: Indigenous leaders report that members of the Guardians of the Forest are threatened with death by gunmen, farmers, hunters and soy and corn companies that invaded the indigenous land. db8e94bc79b8fc5d940ab515745b59264e3d98fa: In October 2021, a video released on social media shows hunters invading the Arariboia IT and displaying a huge black ounce shot down. A few days later, the two hunters were arrested by the police in the municipality of Arame. For over a decade, indigenous peoples living in the region have denounced the invasion and depredation of their territories. Deforestation, fires, the presence of illegal hunters and collectors, as well as the advancement of illegal agribusiness activities in these ITs have culminated in a scenario of environmental collapse, conflict and death.
2279f617e7045b951e0984cde404696c37340271: The Chiquitano people, inhabitant of the border region between Brazil and Bolivia, have for years claimed their territory. e0d5e260da7b1cdb9c964d9f995b3287573859ce: Another episode of violence and intolerance became a scar in the history of the Guarani-Kaiowá peoples of Mato Grosso do Sul. On the night of October 19, a prayer house in the Tekoha Rancho Jacaré, municipality of Laguna Carapã (MS), was the target of a criminal fire. The space became ashes with less than two months of inauguration, which was held on August 29 this year. To Cimi, Tonico Benites, leadership of Aty Guasu, stated that prayerrs and prayerrs are often threatened. “They [prayer and preachers] were already suffering threats. They said they wanted to end the prayer houses and kill the praying people ", reports. According to Tonico, they had already tried to burn down the prayer house that was burned down at the Alligator Ranch. Rosicleide Vilhalva Kaiowá, Kuñangue Aty Guasu – Great Assembly of Women Kaiowá and Guarani, also spoke about the context of violence in the Tekoha Guarani and Kaiowá. “We are being threatened every day. Not only has a house of prayer become ashes, but also the lives of leaders, preachers and children. Today we see the threat and vulnerability within the tekohas, something that Justice does not see”, lamented. “We are dying, being attacked in our own territories, and no one is doing anything. If you're doing it, we're not seeing it. At this moment, the life of the prayerrs, of the Alligator Ranch, is being threatened. We are all in danger of so much threat that we are suffering from religious intolerance”, Rosicleide completed. Leaders and witnesses recorded a Report of Occurrence in the Civil Police of the municipality of Laguna Carapã (MS). The case has also been referred to the MPF and the Federal Police. The suspicion is that the attacks were carried out by farmers and fundamentalist religious groups in the region.
0be9bd8227bcee6d674280b4ae1053bcb6643317: In July 2021, Adilson Benites recorded a death threat report against a besieger in the area claimed by the Guarani Kaiowá. The indigenous reported that he was threatened by the besieger at the entrance of the village and that it would not have been the first time. In September 2021, the guards of the besieger were accused by the indigenous people of burning a shack, built in the area rented by the besieger, named Giovanni. In an interview with Campo Grande News, he recognized having set fire to the shack in a “moment of fury” caused by what he defined as “following attempts at invasion.” “I went there and set fire to that shack, it was I who put it, I assume my responsibility, but it (barracus) was within the area that I am renter”, he admitted. The area, beautiful to the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, a space where the indigenous people live confined and in a humanitarian crisis, is claimed by the Guarani and Kaiowá as part of their traditional occupation territory. The MPF requested Giovanni's pre-trial arrest for murder in the attempted form, as it took the risk of killing someone by setting fire to the shack.
7edddb55db7a44eaea79732a752afb29a88cdaa6: For many years, Maria Leusa and other leaders of the Munduruku people have suffered threats and intimidation due to their opposition and resistance against mining and mining in their territory. The situation worsened even after the election of the current president of the Republic, which openly encourages the invasion and practice of illegal activities in indigenous lands. In March, the threats resulted in an attack on the headquarters of the Munduruku Wakoborun Women's Association, of which Maria Leusa is coordinator. On April 22, the MPF-PA asked the RMP to ask the STF to act to ensure the safety of the Munduruku in Jacareacanga. Maria Leusa reports that the criminals attracted a small group of indigenous, who has been representing the interests of the mining and threatening the Munduruku against the activity. “They [gatherers and supporters] speak whenever we [Munduruku] want the legalization of the prospector, but that is a lie. Our chiefs always speak through the letters that we do not accept the legalization of the mining within our territory ", says, referring to the open documents that Munduruku leaders have disclosed to denounce the prospectors. Maria Leusa reports that the threats come from the relatives themselves who were attracted by the prospectors; that they arm the enticed indigenous people, who “are looking for us, saying they will kill us, because we keep making the complaints”. In June 2021, suspects of threatening and setting fire to Maria Leusa Munduruku's house (and also suspected of attacking a PF base in May) were arrested in an operation involving more than 80 federal police officers and the National Force, with FAB military support. One of the arrest warrants was against the deputy mayor of Jacareacanga, Walmar Kaba Munduruku. Guns and ammunition were seized in his home; the wife and niece of the deputy mayor were also arrested in flagrante for illegal possession of a weapon. The PF also arrested the president of the Jacareacanga mining cooperative, Alan Dias Carneiro, and the indigenous Aldo Cardoso Munduruku. The violent actions were a retaliation of the prospectors after a PF operation that destroyed machines and camps in illegal mining areas on two Munduruku lands. Even with the PF operation in the region, the indigenous continue to live under pressure and threats from the invaders. On this same occasion, the STF determined that the Union should adopt measures to ensure the safety and health of the Munduruku peoples in Pará and Yanomami in Roraima, due to the increase of cases of violence and contagion by Covid-19 caused by prospectors.
de87a8ec87dce119396371ccc5a957c743386141: Alessandra Korap is one of the most active leaders in the defense of Munduruku territory. Due to her engagement in the struggle, she is the victim of threats by those who defend mineral and wood exploration in the indigenous lands of her people. Being one of the most active leaders, he also received an international award for human rights defenders. In the region of the middle Tapajós, where Alessandra lives, the Munduruku people live in urban villages, located in the municipality of Itaituba (PA), and struggle for the demarcation of ITs such as Sawré Bap’in and Sawré Muybu, which was identified and delimited by Funai in 2016 with approximately 178,000 hectares. IT is coveted by prospectors, interested in gold exploration, and loggers, and the people await the publication of the declaratory ordinance of the area by MJ. “We lost a lot of space, because we can’t fish, we can’t hunt. The only space we have guaranteed is the demarcation of territory”, says Alessandra. “I always say: ‘If they kill me one day, I say I tried’. And I tried, I talked, and I screamed. We do not want dam, we do not want mining and no death project ", he stressed.
8f93bd3651f6f850be827dcbe1bb6bd58b28828a: The Pankararu people Opará has been in an area of recovery for five years and struggle for recognition of the area as traditional territory. With this, the squatters have threatened the pajé, the cacica and the community leadership, including hiring gunmen from the region. The indigenous made police reports, complaints to the MPF of Serra Talhada and the Programa de Proteção às Defensores e Defensoras de Direitos Humanos de Pernambuco (PEPDDH), in which the leaders were inserted.
f5bf62659255213bdd8adb7d36a86bb5de59b41c: After the death threats suffered by Vice-Cacique Neusa, resulting from several conflicts that took place in 2020 between the indigenous community of Tekohá Jevy and non-indigenous people who occupy the Guarani IT of Rio Pequeno and who are contrary to the demarcation of the land, the leadership was inserted in the Human Person Protection Program of the State of Rio de Janeiro. However, even in the program, the leadership reports that threats continue to occur. In July, when moving from the village to a meeting in a Sesai vehicle, the indigenous people were approached by a person who threatened the leadership, questioning “how many more Indians” would have to die for them to give up the demarcation. The speech of the man was an allusion to the brother of the vice chief, murdered in 2018.
995afc08cb868f82cb3f2b9d342431c76c7effa2: Families of the Huni Kui people go monthly to the city of Guajará (AM), on the border between Acre and Amazonas, to receive wages, benefits and make their purchases. Most families have acquired the habit of buying “fied” and, in turn, traders, to ensure the payment of the debt, retain the bank cards, including with the password. When the Indian asks for the card or the money, the merchant refuses to give, claiming no balance. This practice has caused abuse by traders, who use cards to make loans and increase the debt value. A campaign is being conducted by the State Department of Social Assistance, Human Rights and Policies for Women, but the pieces reverse the situation and place the victim as a criminal (“delivering the card of its benefit to another person is a crime”). Several complaints have already been made to the MPF.
fca8e82f8ae7dce92c4228191b40883a02224932: To receive wages, benefits and do their shopping, Ashaninka indigenous families go to the city monthly. Most families have acquired the habit of buying “fied”. The merchants, to ensure the receipt of debts, retain the bank cards, including with the password. In most cases, traders use the cards to make loans and increase the value of the debt; when the indigenous asks for the card or the money, the merchant says it has no balance, adding this new debt and generating a constant dependence of families on this
4ef53fa6ceb34ee3e8b31f14d40bd0fa0f211f2c: Reports of leaders report that pastors and evangelical leaders linked to neo-Pentecostal churches acted to influence indigenous peoples not to be vaccinated, using false lies and news. In the Arariboia IT, in Maranhão, pastors and members of local evangelical churches asked the indigenous not to be vaccinated, claiming that the “vaccine comes along with a chip, which has the number of the beast, which turns alligator...”. The disinformation campaign is widespread by audios and videos by mobile phone, the radiophony system between the villages and by in-person cults. In the Amazon, which presented a very serious situation at the beginning of the year, with an increase in the number of cases of contaminated people and lack of oxygen, there are similar reports of disinformation. According to Nara Baré, Coiab coordinator, there were pastors guiding the indigenous not to take the vaccine because it would not be “God’s”. Nara analyzes that the attitude of these religious is aligned with the speech of President Jair Bolsonaro, who speaks ill of the vaccine and delegitimizes science. The facts have been reported to the MPF, asking for measures. Indigenous and indigenous organizations have campaigned to encourage all indigenous people to become vaccinated as a way of preserving their lives.
59d8199092f2368c3e46f54f0a85a9226732750e: Indigenous people of the Madijá people, located in the Jaminawa/Envira, Kulina do Rio Envira and Kulina do Igarapé do Pau, move every month to the city of Feijó to receive their wages, pensions and benefits, and to shop. Most families negotiate with traders to buy “fiado”; with the justification of ensuring the receipt of debts, traders retain the indigenous bank cards with the passwords, often using the cards to make loans and increase the debt value. When the indigenous asks for the card or the money, the merchant says it has no balance, increasing the debt and generating a constant dependence of families on this type of purchase. Complaints were made to the MPF, generating investigation and action of the PF, which recovered cards, notified traders and arrested involved in the crime. Among the prisoners are the councilwoman of Feijó, Aurelinda Portela, her daughter, her husband and an 80-year-old. They worked on this criminal scheme in the municipality of Feijó ten years ago. In the councilwoman's house there were bank cards and Bolsa-Familia, money, bank passwords and notebooks with notes of alleged debts of the indigenous. The indictees will answer for the crimes of indebt appropriation, swindle, criminal association and fraudulent loan.
135b2b18a65bcd3476ab0ea9325e2bda0cb0860d: To receive their salaries, pensions and benefits, as well as to make their purchases, indigenous families move every month to the cities Manoel Urbano and Santa Rosa do Purus. Like other peoples, most families have acquired the habit of buying “fied” and, in turn, traders, with the justification of ensuring the payment of debts, retain the indigenous bank cards with the passwords, using them to make loans and increase the value due. When the indigenous ask for the cards or the money, the merchant says it has no balance, adding the new debts and generating a constant dependence of the families on this type of purchase. Complaints were made to the MPF, generating an investigation and an operation of the PF, called Huni Kuin, in order to combat illegal practice against the indigenous. During the investigations, which began in August 2019, PF identified and arrested three traders in the city of Manoel Urbano, suspected of illegal card retention.
46356408a0461293259d48dd7adbc01c0cad8e23: Even before the Covid-19 vaccines reached the indigenous villages, an anti-vaccine campaign reached these populations, promoted mainly by the President of the Republic and his negative followers. The first indigenous vaccinated against Covid-19 in the Amazon, Vanda Witoto, reports that she received several calls from relatives who wanted to know if she “had turned alligator”. According to doctor Douglas Rodrigues, who has been working with indigenous people in the Amazon for five decades, what is happening “is a very recent phenomenon, leveraged by a lot of false news that the vaccine causes this and that, and coming from various origins, mainly evangelical sectors”, but also “start in Brasilia”. The President of the Republic came to question, in December 2020, the possible side effects of vaccines, saying, in relation to who would vaccinate, that “if you become an alligator, it is your problem”. Health professionals report that they have never seen so much reluctance of indigenous people to vaccinate. Indigenous organizations mobilized to do a contrary job, encouraging relatives to get vaccinated.
027e618c7454f6b0c4f6a54fa93fe1eacf504266: The state deputies of Amazonas, José Neto (Patriota) and Fausto Júnior (MDB), used, without authorization, the image of the indigenous parliamentarian Joênia Wapichana to defend Bolonarist agendas in the Amazon. In a video, they promote proposals such as mining in indigenous lands and casino legalization. Joênia, one of the main opposers to the penitentiary agenda in the area, said: “My work is for the protection of human rights, environmental law and Amazonian peoples. I did not allow my image for any government propaganda, since I have clear and public my position on the Bolsonaro government.”
298a84b559df03d449a3598c04e3a423a9b46af8: An operation of the Civil Police arrested a criminal group that operates in the Village Tribe Park, community that houses indigenous of various peoples, in the west of Manaus. According to the Civil Police, criminals sold lots of land and then charged security, energy and water to the locals; people who did not pay, often due to financial difficulties, were threatened, had stolen goods, houses burned down and were victims of violent attacks by the group. During the operation, the police also arrested a man with about 100 narcotics kits like marijuana, cocaine and oxy. The men will answer for attempted murder, extortion, theft, fire and drug trafficking.
5252da397bff67a31d333a35f786e262bd0d8e41: The PF of Acre conducted an operation at TI Camicuã, in Boca do Acre (AM), following judicial orders for home search and seizure and a preventive arrest warrant. The action was the result of an investigation by the PF, whose target is a criminal group that worked in IT, threatening the indigenous and co-opting children and young people for drug trafficking. The action of PF had a partnership with the Navy, Funai and ICMBio.
1599fead96fed1626bf4451c413fa33dd8798a5b: Families of the Marubo people go monthly to the city of Guajará to receive wages, benefits and do their shopping. Most families have acquired the habit of buying “fiado”, a practice that results in the retention of their bank cards by traders, including with the passwords. The situation has caused abuse on the part of traders, who use the cards to make loans, sell goods with overpriced values and, when the indigenous ask for the cards, do not deliver them, claiming that they still must. One leadership stated that only one merchant in the city would have had more than 150 cards and that he would have threatened to call the police to the indigenous people, because they “would be in debt”. Several complaints were made to the MPF.
d91b115359ed7e9d5c51194d034e138b978da1b9: The Madijá Indians of the Middle Kulina IT Juruá, in the municipalities Eirunepé, Envira and Ipixuna, in Amazonas, move monthly from their villages to receive wages and benefits and make their purchases. As they buy “fied”, by a historical relationship with traders, the cards are retained, including with the passwords, by the owners of the trades. In most cases traders use the cards to make loans and increase the value of debts; when the indigenous asks for the card or the money, the merchant claims there is no balance. The MPF and PF received reports and investigated them. It is estimated that around 600 indigenous people, among retirees, teachers, health agents and beneficiaries of the Bolsa Familia, are affected by this criminal practice.
157b860cb0f087a1eaf438d78de12e2d1db095f4: The Kanamari Indians of the Kulina ITs of the Middle Juruá and Mawetek, in the municipality of Eirunepé, leave their villages monthly to receive wages, benefits and make their purchases in the city. Most families buy “fied” in local businesses and, like other peoples in the region, have their cards and passwords retained by traders. In most cases, merchants use the cards to make loans, which leads to an increase in indigenous debt. The MPF and PF received reports and would be investigating them. It is estimated that around 350 Kanamari indigenous people, among retired, teachers, health agents and beneficiaries of the Bolsa Familia, are affected by this criminal practice.
ac0afc60067e5959871e132de6d56b8e1f870807: The presence of American dogs within the TI Reach, in the Taquara Village, has endangered entire families of the Mura people. Dogs belong to farmers in the region, buffalo breeders, and are taken to the area by a man from Autazes. Farmers release the dogs into the woods with GPS around their necks; they chase away the hunts and kill many animals. They also endanger the lives of the indigenous, because they only know their owner and, if they see the indigenous, they attack them. Dogs take the hunt and then the owner kills them. About three years ago, farmers started bringing these dogs into the area, making it impossible for the Mura to hunt, limiting their circulation within their territory and threatening the physical integrity of children, elderly, women and men. In 2021, the case was denounced to the MPF, the Regional Coordinator of Funai, the DSEI, Seduc and IPAM, but there was no provision except for the entry of the PF in the area only once.
3d0a7567be53780b2a1ad04d3ee7fc6e8f3f8555: Use of dogs to intimidate the indigenous
40c18f5cae53e1a3142734030953a9debe0b86da: The Truká-Tupan people have been in a recovery area for 13 years and have been fighting for recognition of the area as an indigenous reserve. With this, the community and its leaders, over the years, are targets of all kinds of threats. In addition to having their lives threatened daily, indigenous people report that the water pump that supplies the community is often depredated, causing damage and lack of water. They also report that invaders enter the area and cause fire at the entrance of the village, putting all community at risk due to smoke inhalation. The indigenous also denounce that violence affects even the animals of the community, who have been shot to death by the invaders. The community reported to the MPF of Paulo Afonso, the DPU and the Human Rights Protection Program of the State of Bahia, which, with the Cimi team, are following and seeking ways to solve the case.
2a9aae9a6383ca56869a284b53bcb1f56510c35f: Miscellaneous threats; fire; water pump depredation; animal death
c76bb82c7649f4c20e20f842ec3baf63ac15d109: The fact that the Xavantes were one of the people most affected by Covid-19, with 79 deaths confirmed at the end of April 2021, and with a high degree of vulnerability, did not prevent the leaders of the agribusiness of Mato Grosso to promote an event with agglomeration and without wearing masks within the IT Sangraduro, including the participation of the president of Funai, Marcelo Xavier, and Funai servers, also without wearing masks. The event was to promote the opening of the rice harvest in the region and brought together 100 more participants, among federal, state and municipal authorities, Funai servers, leaders of the Rural Union of Eastern Spring and representatives of seven other peoples of the region. Contrary to all the recommendations of immunologists, the president of the Brazilian Association of Soy Producers (Aprosoja Brasil), Gaucho Antônio Galvan, allowed himself to photograph without a mask alongside indigenous people. In another image published on the organization's page, it appears alongside Funai's president, Marcelo Xavier, and two other servants of the indigenist organ, all without facial protection. In addition to those mentioned, some of the main representatives of the ruralist bench in Congress also participated in the event, such as MPs Neri Geller (PP-MT), Nelson Barbudo (PSL-MT) and José Medeiros (We can-MT), as well as state deputies Gilberto Cattani (PSL-MT) and Xuxu Dal Molin (PSC-MT).
c390f84a278774876d8cb9177453e4e6208a3ccc: Unused agglomeration of masks within IT
063000f439225f1e4cdb658047f2c68c1aaecca6: An employee of a Campinápolis market drove a Xavante in a vehicle from the market itself to the Loterica House. They got in line together. When they were attended, the employee verified the balance of the benefit of the Bolsa Família do Xavante and made a withdrawal. Then they returned to the market where Xavante made his purchases. The misuse of bank cards and indigenous passwords by commercial establishments throughout the country has been reported frequently. There are several actions of the MPF in progress, trying to curb this illegal practice, but the indigenous continue to be injured.
7c2c9ef3860749fcd83c910e68c759d834985e11: Even though it is a situation repeatedly reported, the retention of Xavante's social benefits cards by markets continues to occur in Campinápolis (MT). One of the markets that has a vehicle, besides having the cards of the indigenous, also charges the freight service from the city to the village. In this way, the Xavantes are held hostage both from purchases on the market and from freight in the same commercial establishment. Despite the complaints to the responsible bodies, no action was taken to contain these illegalities against the indigenous.
2224fffd2e6a794e8f860bce8bee06ebc1761783: Nine indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá, of which two adolescents aged 14 and 15, were rescued from conditions similar to those of slaves on a cattle ranch in Porto Murtinho (MS). The action included the participation of the Federal Police, which had received a complaint from the Environmental Military Police and fiscal auditors of the work, and also found six Paraguayans and two Brazilians, all in degrading situation – one of the elements that characterize contemporary slave labor. They were housed in precarious canvas sheds, did not count on sanitary facilities and did their physiological needs in the bush, using the water from the stream to cook, wash clothes, bathe and kill the thirst. Acting in the construction of fences and in the cleaning of pasture, they applied pesticides without personal protective equipment, contaminating themselves. The inspection process is underway.
497a45c312b40cfdcbfee279b2ce9180ec69a66e: Indigenous of the village Amambai captured three men, 19, 21 and 24 years old, who practiced theft in the region. The Environmental Military Police were activated and found four marijuana tablets, plus a marijuana plantation in the backyard of the burglars' house. According to reports from indigenous leaders, men are responsible for the sale and distribution of drugs within the village. All three were arrested and the drugs seized.
6f234f429cd75a01183ff0a9006178fff9123549: An indigenous man, after spending 50 days in a farmhouse, denounces slave labor to the MPT. According to his complaint, the shack he lived in has sheltered other people for over 50 years. The MPT investigates the complaint that reports degrading conditions of work offered at Fazenda Morrinho, in Miranda. The place has no light, no water, it's flat ground, and to cook, you need firewood. Lack of infrastructure wasn't the only problem. The execution of the work was accompanied by episodes of humiliation and moral harassment. According to the indigenous, besides him, another boy who still lives in the shack performed the installation service of about between the months of March and April 2021. “His father, who died two months ago, lived there for 52 years,” he said. During the time they were on the farm, workers were not allowed to go out to the city to visit their relatives. The justification was to increase the chances of contracting the coronavirus. The remuneration was also made below the agreed rate. The two would not be the only ones to be kept in this situation on the property. Four other Indians would be working and being housed in an old wooden shed, also without light or water. According to the complaint, the farm belongs to the family of former alderman Ivan Bossay; family members respond to the process at TRE-MS, and were removed from Miranda City Hall in August 2020, including the former alderman. In 2020, the MPT-MS carried out joint rescue operations to several indigenous workers who were in similar conditions to slave labor, and illegal practice remained in 2021.
1970572aeb6ba637e258411f6c9e1ffb086ff934: Indigenous leaders and health professionals in Mato Grosso do Sul are concerned with the circulation of false and prejudiced news about the effect of Covid-19 vaccines. In several villages, such as Jaguapiru and Bororó, there is the resistance of many indigenous people to immunizers. Despite the allocation of more than 20,000 doses to meet this group considered a priority by municipal and state immunization plans, a minority would be spreading false information about the vaccine to discourage indigenous people from going to local health centers. These would be influenced by some religious denominations, which are disinforming the indigenous. Concerned, several health agents are making videos, denying the fake news.
1a31c8efb91782d922252585a2ef566b9a773810: A rescue operation was carried out to free 140 workers, including 25 indigenous workers, who were in conditions similar to those of slavery, on a soybean farm in Sidrolândia (MS). The operation included the Ministry of Labour (MPT), the PF, the Undersecretary of Labour Inspection (SIT) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the MPF and the DPU. The indigenous lived in the village of Bororó, in Dourados, before being enticed to this work. The Environmental Military Police was also part of the action. The 25 indigenous rescued were on a rural property in Sidrolândia, and were found doing weed cleaning activity in a soybean crop. The workers were exposed to various degrading conditions, such as the absence of adequate accommodation and bathrooms; inappropriate places to feed workers; absence of shelter from weather like rain; lack of PPE; absence of first aid materials and absence of portfolio registration.
ca1593a4d7887c7e02317b3fb2f407c6d195b84f: Leaders denounced the attempt to assault the indigenous Márcia Alves Franco by her husband. There are reports that, as her husband failed to assault her, for revenge, he set fire to her house. The police were fired and the man arrested the same day.
834320688a5b67ea0e0edb6a74ea478f6241386e: Eleven indigenous who lived in a situation similar to that of slaves were rescued in Antônio João (MS), near the border with Paraguay, after joint action of the MPT, Regional Labour Superintendence and the Environmental Military Police. According to the investigation, the victims worked in collecting stones under subhuman conditions, without registration and any labor or social security guarantees. Of the 11, four were underage. It was found that all were without drinking water and had to drink, bathe and wash their clothes in a stream. Food was costed by the workers, some rice, sardines or wild animals hunted by the indigenous themselves. They also stayed in plastic canvas huts, which did not protect them from weather like rain and venomous animals. Others slept on dirty old mattresses, placed on the ground and wooden logs, mounted in a shed near the headquarters. Everyone worked without a wallet – much of it doesn't even have a birth certificate. One of them had been on the farm since February 2021, which occupies 4,000 hectares. MPT-MS prosecutor Paulo Douglas Almeida de Moraes said that “reducing a worker to a slave-like condition represents a serious violation of the principle of human dignity, due to the lack of compliance with fundamental rights, especially those related to hygiene, health, safety, housing, rest and others related to personality rights”, and classified the situation as “inadmissible”. After the rescue, the task force will ascertain all the rights of the indigenous who should be paid and compensated by the farmer. The MPT will also apply for compensation for moral damages suffered by the indigenous.
68ec0fb3043ffe90426170ffa61234aa30a7f0e8: Guarani-Kaiowá Indians move from their villages in Paranhos (MS), in search of work in the south of the country. One of the works offered to them is by season, in the apple orchards, in Vacaria (RS), more than a thousand kilometers from the villages in the MS. One of these Indians reported that when he left his village he had no idea of the problems he would face. According to his report, in the accommodation offered by Rasip Agro Pastoril S/A, one of the largest apple producers in Brazil, there were 12 workers per room, divided into six bunk beds. In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, this was a situation that did not allow adequate social distancing. With its strength compromised after infection by the disease due to weakness due to lack of appetite and pain in the body, the working season, which would last from January to May, was only 23 days. The agreed was that he would earn R $70 per day of work, which, in the end, earned him R $ 1,610. When the symptoms manifested, he was taken to an isolation area. “They took me to a dirty place full of mosquitoes, the bathroom was filthy. They didn't even give us a mask. The first day there, they gave me antibiotics. I haven't even had a diagnosis yet. Then I lost my hunger and went about five days without eating”, he says. The indigenous person reports that the care provided by health professionals was also precarious. “There was no doctor, she was just a nurse. She'd show up every two or three days to see who was there. There were about 20 in isolation, and they stayed from one to two people per room”. He told the site report The Joio and the Wheat who was in isolation for about eight days before taking the test to see if he was with Covid-19. “I was weak, they caught me by the arm to take to the car. On the day, they took 12 people to take the test. There were four in each car. It was that quick test on the finger. Only my result was negative”. But the result was false-negative. the MPT-RS reported that they were in their archives “eight procedures in the face of Rasip Foods as a whole, since 2007, for various reasons. Four of them have already been filed. One of them, in 2009, was filed after the conclusion of a Term of Adjustment of Conduct with the company establishing obligations related to the registration of work hours. Two of them are in monitoring waiting for inspections and reports and one is active.”
7f918b4577d9b4edec98dfd2c5f7b805bfe68d4c: The complaint was offered by the MPF in 2016, and the unjustified delay in the process led the ministerial body to ask the 1st Federal Court of Dourados (MS), in May 2021, the inclusion of criminal proceedings related to the fact in the list of cases with trial priority. Subsequently, the petition was sent as a request to the Internal Affairs of the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and to the Committee of Fundamental Rights of the National Council of the Public Prosecutor (CNMP), as well as internal control sectors of the MPF. The complaint relates to the case known as “Massacre de Caarapó”, which occurred on June 14, 2016, and without progress and provision for justice after five years. According to the investigation of the MPF's Avá Guarani Task Force, the five reported rural owners organized, promoted and executed the attack on the Tey Kue community on June 14, 2016. At the time, about 40 trucks, with the help of three loaders and over 100 people, many of whom were heavily armed, forced out a group of approximately 40 Guarani and Kaiowá from a property occupied by them. The indigenous Clodiode Aquileu Rodrigues de Souza was killed with one shot in the abdomen and another in the chest, and six other indigenous, including a 12-year-old child, were shot and seriously injured. Two indigenous people suffered minor injuries and the community was violently embarrassed to leave the area. On October 6, the 1st Federal Court of Dourados received the request for measures forwarded by CNJ and, two days later, issued an order scheduling the instruction hearings for January 2022, for the hearings of the victims and witnesses, in addition to the interrogation of the defendants.
e639d6b56d391b6a9cab48a9ee3e14bef953159d: A 9-year-old Guarani-Kaiowá child living in the village Jaguapiru, in Golden TI, experienced a traumatic experience. A 25-year-old man entered his home, put a plastic bag in his head and tried to kidnap her, along with three other accomplices. The girl caught the uncle's attention, who came to help her when she heard the screams. At that moment, the four criminals ran and managed to escape. Indigenous leaders were triggered to help in the search for the aggressors. In the morning, a bicycle was found in the area; family members reached the suspect and triggered the police. The man was taken to the police station and denied the charges. The girl recognized him by his clothes. He was arraigned for attempted kidnapping and imprisonment.
22e71209267e4fa58818b87ebc1a0698db1c9e4d: As reported in 2020 in the national press (National and Fantastic Newspaper), the undue seizure of Maxakali indigenous benefit cards continued in 2021, being committed by false traders. There are several Indians who have been victims of the crime of extortion of these false traders. On September 14, 2021, the Civil Police were at IT Maxakali, in the villages Água Boa and Pradinho, to investigate the case. On December 6, 2021, police conducted Operation Baba Yaga and arrested drug traffickers involved in the crime. Unfortunately, this is a common practice that occurs with indigenous peoples of various peoples in Brazil, made by local traders in their regions. The indigenous come from the villages to receive the money from the retirement or Bolsa Família in the city, but they do not seek the agencies; they follow directly to the merchant who kept his card. In trade, the indigenous take the products they need and return to the village with the debt balance. The MPF has been active throughout the country, warning about this illegal practice.
d4c550edf4e229a6891c4670764fb60ed43bf4b1: The Tembé-Theneteraha people denounced the involvement of public security agents with private militia for farmers working in IT areas Alto Rio Guamá, Pará. The Tembé released a public note demanding the presence of Funai, the MPF and the Federal Police, and charged urgent forensics and answers from Justice on the murder of young Isac Tembé, killed by military police on February 12. In the police's version, they were called to investigate an alleged cattle theft on a farm, and said they were surprised by gunfire when they arrived at the scene and reacted to defend themselves. The indigenous people contest the version presented by the PMs and indicate that the young indigenous was a victim of execution, in a place that is frequented by the indigenous and claimed as part of their traditional territory. Chief Neto Tembé told G1 “that this story that the police tell is not true, that no one uses a shotgun to kill the hunt.” Isak was considered a leadership among the young Tembé, was formed in history, and would assume the position of teacher. The authorities are investigating the case.
d797aeb8b118fb58aad2bed7cfe689ddd1001857: An indigenous pregnant woman went to the São Miguel do Iguaçu Municipal Hospital to deliver the baby. When the baby was born, it was found to be an intersexual child. Some hospital workers, along with the Guardianship Council, deduced that the child could be killed, due to the condition of her birth, and organized to remove the baby from the mother, without any professional having at any time gone to talk to the mother of the child. An intervention by two anthropologists was necessary to prevent the child from being removed from the mother and placed in the Home of the municipality.
9a1059ef6a28a7348d6eb997dc17a8e4e1204775: Attempted to remove child from mother
c821a28858bbdacc7b77c3cf3950e85bf84bd8e9: As a result of the process of disintrusion of the IT Pankararu Brejo dos Padres, the squatters invade the territory, cut wire fences and continue to put loose animals to pasture in the villages of the indigenous. These squatters physically threaten and intimidate them if the community demonstrates dissatisfaction with the practice. Denunciation was made to the MPF of Serra Talhada, which instituted procedure, and also to the Program of Human Rights Defenders in Pernambuco (PEPDDH). An agenda was constructed between the community, MPF and Cimi to monitor the situation and pressure at Funai, seeking to ensure the protection of the indigenous and the territory; leaderships were inserted in the PEDHR.
b43570d339f293264df1cb55c53b57f46c35c75b: Two men, saying they were PF police officers, but without a warrant, without uniform, without any identification and without wearing a mask of protection in the middle of a pandemic, arrived in the community questioning people and looking for the Woie leadership. They went through the shacks and photographed everything, including the clothes extended on the clothesline. Cacica Cunllugn requested from them the judge's warrant, which was not filed. She reported that the community was waiting for a meeting with MPF, DPU and Federal Justice, and clarified that, in a place where earthmoving was carried out, there will be the construction of a differentiated indigenous school, with the aim of attending the children of the community. The alleged cops, after shooting everything, boarded the vehicle and left. The information reported by Cacica Cunllugn was reported to the MPF and DPU.
76f13d273049447e0fe8025f4bad9be68acedf84: On November 3, when the Casai team brought back patients who were in consultation in the city, there was a roadblock that gives access to the village. The vehicle was only 4 km from the entrance of the Panorama village. Several logs were crossed on the road, preventing the car from moving. This is a strategy used by invaders to intimidate the indigenous in an attempt to ambush. For the indigenous to move forward, it is necessary to get out of the car, to remove the logs placed in the middle of the way. This is one of the many forms of violence that the Karipuna people suffer. It is a message of a clear threat from the criminal invaders who enter IT, with the end of exploitation and greasing of the territory. Complaints were sent to MPF, PF and Funai.
819667fad2b5789269071a81019742a4ca850a1a: Mr. Miguel, one of the last elders to know the culture of the Guarasugwe people, a long time ago, on returning from work in the rural area, suffered a hit-and-run in Costa Marques. He received treatment, but was in a wheelchair and later with a cane. In the region, there is a practice of lawyers from other municipalities that offer their services to indigenous families to work with the INSS. It was Mr. Miguel's case, who hired one of those lawyers. He filed a lawsuit at the INSS, requiring disability retirement. Mr. Miguel reported that the lawyer is from Pimenta Bueno and that he was in his house taking part of the money received in the case, but it was not clarified that money was that and in what situation was the process of his retirement.
fe8b20b9a5c5506187b623f3c4dfdd8bf65f1f27: A 43-year-old indigenous from Warao reported on January 9 that he had fled from a mining site near Vila do Trairão in Amajari (RR), due to the working conditions in which he was, without rest and without food. He was alone and his family were in Venezuela. The case was referred to the International Organization of Migration (IOM), which operates in the region and provides monitoring service to migrants and refugees from Venezuela.
7da114640c716f6c9500854ae3307994238e5440: Some of the attacks by prospectors on the Yanomami Indians in the Palimiú region in May and June 2021, used tear gas bombs, which are restricted and authorized only by the Brazilian Army. According to the Brazilian Military Army Area Command itself, “the tear agents and their launch devices are controlled products of restricted use whose acquisition can only be carried out with the authorization of the Army, through the Controlled Products Surveillance Service (SFPC), according to Decree 10.030/2019”. According to this decree, only public agencies can acquire controlled products of restricted use, that is, only the Armed Forces and public security (Military, Civil and Federal Police) can use tear gas pumps. Asked by the report of the Brazil Fact portal on how the bombs came into the hands of illegal prospectors, the Brazilian Army only reported that “the facts that occurred in the Palimiú Indigenous Community are under investigation by the Federal Police.”
c9e49d254b3d68c992e97b09e37343bf011e7aba: Attack with equipment for restricted use by prospectors
3e9968fe5621055ab230e4cca8579e7be4721de8: The population of the Xisei region lives in a high degree of isolation in the Yanomami IT mountainous area, with very little experience in relation to the surrounding society – and is therefore more vulnerable to pressures and false promises from the mining agents. During 2021, the prospectors of the Xitei community were approached precisely on the basis of the grooming of young people from promises of goods and weapons, and the intimidation of opponents. As payment for the intermediation of prospectors and community, young people receive weapons and ammunition, defending the interest of invaders against the opposing community.
ee907d3c83da3f6cd5d87497581b2e5792938485: Threats, intimidation and grooming of young people
9f8070f77da3b973306a5db50448e1ff6b7ea7ea: The lack of Etnoenvironmental Protection Bases, which should be functioning at the entrances of indigenous areas, has provided new airstrips to be installed inside and close to Yanomami IT, a situation that intensified in the year 2021. With the reduction of surveillance actions in the territory, even clues that were before the exclusive use of the Health District were captured by the mining logistics, as is the case with the Kayanau runway, at the confluence of the Couto de Magalhães river with the Mucajaí river. Twelve clues were mapped within the Yanomami IT at the service of the mining in the macro-region, without considering the clues of Homoxi and Apiaú. In the farms surrounding this region, 40 clues were identified. Second report from the BBC Brazil, preliminary data indicate that at least 277 clandestine landing strips have been identified on the outskirts of all Yanomami IT.
4b3843d8eaf7934afab5d4f2e44e81f890095d74: Underground landing lanes for mining use
80c82921e014ed48335737e63662af2fd699eeed: Wilson Almeida Lima, mayor of the municipality Iguape (SP), in a public hearing held on July 9, 2021, in Espaço Canto do Morro, made speeches that converged with the demonstrations of hatred and slander against residents and leaders of the IT Ka’aguy Hovy, especially against the leadership and teacher Cleo Para Poty. The mayor says against the demarcation of the Ka’aguy Hovy IT and does not recognize the rights of indigenous peoples. It is public knowledge that he, related to entrepreneurs and other actors, has an interest in lots of land that are part of the traditional territory claimed by the Guarani people Mbya that inhabits this region. The mayor tries to co-opt residents who are illegally occupying the IT area, already in the process of disintrusion, inflating disagreements between these occupants against the indigenous peoples and traditional communities of Iguape. This attitude has as main objective to disintegrate the struggle of these peoples for the recognition of their traditional territories, in addition to attacking the peace and harmony of these communities, generating a climate of fear, distrust and disagreements.
287021ef764dbc4701766516d3e5bd0c9b756f03: The son Sinô Kulina, only 12 years old, was killed with cruelty. Sinô was fishing with a 10-year-old cousin on a lake outside Indian territory. On their return to the village, they were approached by a man known as Neto. The man was drunk and shouted at the boys, stating that the lake was his and that it was not for the “caboclos” to fish there. Before the boys reached the riverside, the man took the rifle and shot, hitting Sinô, who, with the shot, fell into the water. The 10-year-old managed to jump out of the canoe and into the woods. The killer went after Sinô's body and dragged him to the beach. On the beach, he took a machete and broke the Indian body in half; one part was thrown in the river and the other part in the bush. The crime was reported by a leadership of the people who are the grandfather of the victim. The informant said they didn't file a police report because the killer is dangerous and they're afraid.
455379658b2a0a6aab7d87ea224ac4d0f18f99b2: Giana Kaxinawá was murdered on May 9 by Claudio Kaxinawá, her husband. According to reports, he had spent the night at a party in a neighboring community located in the neighboring country, Peru. At the party, he would have ingested alcohol mixed with narcotics, and the effect of the drug upset him. When he got home, he took a shotgun and went towards his wife, who was extending clothes in the backyard of the house. Claudius fired three shots to Giana's chest, who died at the scene. Community leaders tied Claudius to deliver him to the police station in Marshal Thaumaturgo. On the way, the leaders stopped in a community to eat, leaving Claudius inside the canoe; he managed to break loose and fled the place.
bb871dfc4afee81f9b25029b9e990c8d311c37ca: Claudio Kaxinawá had murdered his wife, Giana, and was on the run after the leadership attempted to take him to Marshal Thaumaturgo's station. The leaders report that Ciã, Giana's brother, after two months of missing, confessed that he went after Claudius and avenged his sister's death, killing Claudius in the same way he would have killed Giana. The leaders were then in the woods, at the location indicated by Ciã, and only found the bone. Cyan, after the confession, fled and is on the run.
2603e32f4f02cda16c28f195dae268397e813da1: An Indian woman went to the community to spend the day with her parents. She lives in a colony on the border of the territory. The husband, a white man, would have taken alcohol and offered it to the men of the community. Drunk, they started a fight, and the white man took his rifle and shot Kanaú, who soon died. Revolted, the victim's relatives stabbed him to death. Funai's been triggered, but you keep the case a secret. This white man used to bring alcohol to the Indians and trade it for hunting, which he traded.
85ce9c591e9dcc657b3209abf3f7982b6df30f67: Joaquim Kulina, aged 20, was with his family in the city of Feijó. During the stay, the whole family was camped in front of the city, in the Katukina/Kaxinawá IT, of the Shanenawá and Huni Ku. On January 7, Joaquim, drunk, began an argument with his 42 - year - old father, Levi Kulina. In the discussion, Joaquim took a knife and struck his father in the neck, who did not resist and died at the scene, before being rescued. Joaquim's brother Dido Kulina, 12 years old, saw his father dead, hugged him and began to cry, complaining about what happened. Joaquim, still with the knife in his hand, approached his brother and also struck him in the neck. The boy also did not resist and died at the scene. After the facts, Joaquim wanted to run into the woods, but his relatives stopped him and called the police, who arrested him in the act.
61c4713b5ca031c9a791914762133e618d4fe788: The Fransoilton Indian was in a bar with his wife. Around 11 a.m., two men approached the couple, whispered something to Fransoilton and went out with him to the bathroom of the bar, where they murdered him with stab wounds.
