Report of occurrence was registered and reported to the MPF and MPE. The investigation is underway.
0e07bb498f5981264507b08324509ee1da207b03: Indian teenager Hiwô, just 14 years old, was cruelly murdered by five men. The body of Hiwô was found on the edge of the Juruá River, in front of the Bacuri neighborhood in Eirunepé, around five o'clock in the morning of October 25. He had a rope tied around his neck and 29 stab wounds. The family filed a police report. Two days after the murder, the police arrested a suspect who confessed to the crime and reported four others involved. In the testimony, the criminal reported that, around 10:30 p.m., they approached Hiwô, who was going alone to the home of a relative where he was staying in the city; that they grabbed him and dragged him to the riverside and raped him, and that Hiwô resisted with swearing, kicking and spitting, when one of them pierced him using a knife. Then they tied him up with rope around his neck and dragged him until he realized he was dead. Of the five killers, two were arrested and three were on the run.
1306b342179b76e7e671d2476b09a45074df4f95: The victim, Luana Kulina, and her husband were drunk when they started an argument. The husband took a knife and struck her with three blows to the chest. Before the rescue arrived, Luana did not resist and died.
dbc04bf2b4031f69479ad350147bbb16811ca460: Kainá was offering a caiçumada in her home to the people who worked in the mutilão in her swidden. Her 13-year-old niece, who was also her adopted daughter, was already drunk when she asked for a caiçuma. Kaina, seeing the state of her daughter, denied it. The teenager became angry, took a knife and hid it under her blouse; as she approached the mother, who was picking caiçuma in the bucket, struck her in the chest. The teenager ran into the woods. Kaina died before she was rescued.
86ee0fabeb4530e68a56e412ecd91a9315db22f3: The elderly Aniwi was sleeping in the hammock when, around 11:00, the grandson arrived on the boat, drunk, and fell on it. Aniwí knocked him down and started arguing with him. The grandson stood up, pulled Aniwí, hooked his grandmother's head on the handle of the net and hanged her.
a1445e36609a687eb86eda70ff0dd8b5dfcc9eb8: A 17-year-old indigenous girl was stabbed to death in the rural area of Maués, which comprises the territory of the Sateré-Mawé people. Her husband is the prime suspect for the crime. Military police have arrested her husband and civilian police are investigating the case.
7c611bfce609f50cfab5fadac6cfd0836ebcb1b2: The indigenous Pataxó Adilson Neves dos Santos, 44 years old, was killed with several shots. There's no information on the authors, no information about the motive of the crime. Civil Police are investigating the case.
27fe635dbb1978a5d61eb5d18a94eda67af15488: The 41-year-old indigenous Antonio Alves Farias was murdered in Bahetá village with firearms. There's no information on the shooter, no motive for the crime. Civil Police are investigating the case.
58cdee45ff55878ea1ae2aefaeaeb68eb06f2e70: Cleiton Moreira de Jesus, indigenous Pataxó Hã-Hã-Hãe, 40 years old, was killed with several firearms. There's no information on the authorship of the crime. Civil Police are investigating the case.
028dab284a2cccf84990b7ddff07ca9cb21f362c: The 31-year-old Pataxó Crislando Brito Bandeira was killed with several firearms. We still don't know who the shooter is. Civil Police are investigating the case.
4ec370d492c561f9cb5dded7309068e0ac3d52b7: The young Indian Gilcinei Braz dos Santos was murdered with several gunshots. Police are investigating the crime, but there's still no information on the perpetrator or his motive for the crime.
d754b243cc5c3549cdf35201c956ee55ffa1abc0: Pataxó Jackson Silva Amor Divino was shot to death in Cumuruxatiba (BA), a district near his village. Civil Police are investigating the crime, but there's still no more information.
9957fdda3bf0f9ef81577389c8ac9b1880d80594: The indigenous João Dias dos Santos was murdered with several firearms. Police are investigating the crime, but there's still no information on authorship or motivation.
9511dca0a53c28f76f39e786dae6e88fb8d85de9: Leilson Santana Neves, 31-year-old Pataxó indigenous, was shot to death when he was in Cumuruxatiba, a district near his village. There's no more detailed information on the case. The police are investigating the perpetrators and the motive for the crime.
66ddad0754345ec351a790687e7a7455c411d810: The young Pataxó Nivaldo da Conceição Correia Júnior, 22 years old, was murdered in the village Tawá, with a firearm, hit by several shots. There's no more information on the perpetrator or the motive. The police are investigating the case.
64c363255902360c085ca3556efab240e66ddefb: The 22-year-old Pataxó Talis Cruz da Silva was shot by several firearms. The perpetrator has not been identified, nor his motives. The police are investigating the case.
d66f0321ace432ea806ee2f7bdab7a76a4148b8a: The 26-year-old Indian William da Conceição Nascimento was killed by firearms, being shot by several shots. There's no information on the perpetrator. The police are investigating the case.
2ad3f87a347a678db59cd622f89daa82b2761c30: The young indigenous Antonio Carlos was murdered in the interior of his home, at the Caramuru IT Catarina Paraguassu. The young man’s father, Antonio Alves, had also been murdered on February 23. The case is being investigated and we still don't know who the perpetrator was.
abfa73f87042e6ab88b5a7f6360a5ac3d2f9481e: The indigenous Ricardo Brito da Conceição worked as an auto mechanic. He was shot to death in the back while repairing a car in his workshop in the village of Itaporanga, rural area of Porto Seguro. According to the police, a man entered the workshop and shot Ricardo in the head and back. The case is being investigated by the 2nd Territorial Police Station of Arraial d’Ajuda, Porto Seguro district.
c5f3252874f8d8b8514fdaa4c5f9d7abb6e0cc32: The indigenous Gigi Pati Farias do Nascimento was the target of two men who arrived by motorcycle at the gate of the village Boca da Mata, where Gigi was working. He was shot to death. The men fled and the 2nd Territorial Police Department investigates the case.
2bb0de8bc0891bcf7d2bdcba4cee68815803e628: The indigenous child V. G. G., only five years old, was found dead in the region of the municipality of Arame, 478 km from São Luís. The child was missing since the morning of January 25, when she disappeared from the village Barreirinha, in TI Arariboia. According to the child's mother, Regina Guajajara, the girl disappeared in a moment of distraction when they were washing dishes inside the house. The mother triggered the military police, who searched the area. The child was found by the father in a stream near the village with signs of violence. The child had physical disability, speech and locomotion problems. The community is shaken by brutality and demanding justice. Police are investigating the crime.
2cfb9b5e258a23822ba0b36347d892fbf1350b48: One indigenous was murdered and two others were injured during discussion at a party in the village Kolidike, in Tangará da Serra (MT). 60-year-old Jaime Zenezokae was stabbed, shot in the head and had his fingers cut off. The celebration brought together people from various villages of TI Paresi. According to the Civil Police, during the discussion, Jaime would have stabbed two other Indians, 30 and 60 years old. According to the witness report to the police, the two injured men were rescued by employees of the Indigenous Health Pole and taken to the UPA of Tangará da Serra. James, however, remained in the village and was eventually murdered by other participants of the party.
0434c777e1f22dfbd97dfc8f4b2a60e82aec305a: The first case of feminicide registered in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul in 2021 occurred in the village Taquapery. The victim was Maristela Lescano and her murder was confessed by her husband, Anelson Lescano. He claimed that he had been betrayed by the woman and that, as he came home very drunk, he ended up hitting her with a piece of wood. She couldn't resist her injuries and died in her own house. The attacker was arrested and indicted for the crime of feminicide.
838488abc3fa7053117b7a853a133588adc1ec01: According to information from the incident report, the indigenous Salatiel Ramires Aquino was stabbed to death in a forest of the village Bororó, on the banks of a road. He was found by a motorcyclist passing by the scene and warned his family. The victim's wife reported to the police that she noticed people hanging around their house at night and that she was afraid because her husband had enemies. The case is under investigation, but there's still no suspect in custody.
cf7ca035d9167008ca6b1cd142f3536e468a6ffd: According to local press, Vagner and the perpetrator of the crime, a 32-year-old man, were drinking and began a mutual discussion and threats, culminating in an attack on stab wounds. The victim died at the scene. Indian leaders were called and triggered the Civil Police, which stopped the aggressor.
bf796bf558c6ae0241e26c3a92945907af1136c9: The 56-year-old indigenous Rosalia Ferreira was beaten to death in the village Bororó, where she lived. According to police reports, a 17 - year - old teenager was apprehended, suspected of participating in the crime, along with two others, who are on the run. According to indigenous reports, Rosalia was in a house with friends when the three teenagers started the assault against her, giving her punches, kicks and strangling her. Rosalia was still rescued with life by her son, but did not resist the wounds and died. Witnesses reported that one of the teenagers was interested in taking the lead of one of the village groups. One of the indigenous leaders, in a statement to the police, reported that Rosália exercised a kind of informal leadership with the youngest in the village, which may have motivated the envy of the adolescent. However, the leadership reported that this would not be possible, because the village obeys a hierarchy, and she would not have a chance to play this role. The case is being followed by Child Services. Civil Police have opened an investigation for murder.
ada665f2c5990ffa8c7bc3c2a0d819002d43bf5d: An indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá family from the Taquaperi village in Colonel Sapucaia (MS) was the victim of a shooting attempt on July 25. The 11-year-old mother and daughter died after being shot. Another 12-year-old son was also injured. The police were triggered shortly after the attack and moved to the village, with Samu's teams and technical expertise. There, the death of mother and daughter was found and the 12-year-old boy who was conscious, despite being injured, was rescued. He was taken to a hospital in Dourados. His condition hasn't been reported. According to Deputy Edgard Punsky, the father of the family was also in the village at the time of the bombing, but managed to escape. The police are still trying to talk to the man, considered a key to understanding the crime. A village leadership informed the police that the crime may have been for religious reasons. “This leadership told us that another Paraguayan indigenous family would have committed the attack. The family that was victim would have been accused by the suspects of ‘working’ with black magic and would have cast a spell for the death of a relative of them”, reported the delegate, who claimed to have the name of two suspects, wanted in the region. He, however, pointed out that this is only one of the lines of investigation. The case is investigated by Colonel Sapucaia's Civil Police Station.
257cdd4953f67cf8daae46e923cf02d6f3a2d095: The 11-year-old child Raíssa da Silva Cabreira, Guarani-Kaiowá, was found dead at the feet of a quarry disabled in the village Bororó. The first surveys of the Civil Police technical expertise team indicate that the girl was thrown from a height of approximately 20 meters. Civil police officers were already working on the hypothesis that Raissa was still sexually abused, as she was found without clothes, when, the next day, five people confessed to the crime – three adolescents and two adults, including the girl's uncle. According to police information based on statements from the suspects' confession, three teenagers and an adult planned to abuse the girl. In the plan of the crime, police found that two teenagers were responsible for “drinking” the girl and dragging her to the cliff, where the abuse occurred. The youths took the girl to the quarry, where another teenager and an adult were. There, they forced the victim to drink alcohol and, according to what they told the police, they started the collective rape. While the four of them abused the child, the police said that the victim's 34-year-old uncle would have arrived at the scene and also participated in the crime. The accused told the police that the girl screamed for help and that she fainted. As she regained consciousness, the girl screamed again, when the men decided to throw her off the cliff. The whole community was amazed at the brutality of crime, especially because it was a child. The adults have been arrested and will be indicted for the crimes of rape of vulnerable, feminicide and murder, and the adolescents apprehended will respond for infractions similar to the crimes of adults.
9538989cffcb0404d44d866e28b12c142cc2f7e5: A 15-year-old Guarani-Kaiowá teenager, a resident of IT Amambai, was stabbed to death by a 56-year-old man. According to witnesses, the man was drunk and the two had a falling out, starting a fight. The man took a knife that was already with him and struck the adolescent's chest, who did not resist and died at the scene. Civil Police investigators had support from leaders of the indigenous community and managed to locate and arrest the man.
b6d95d02b0c82de1003f09054fa0141ebc7a6322: The 27-year-old Indian Márcio Benites Espíndola was in the company of other men, drinking alcohol, when there was an argument and one of them struck him with a knife and then fled. Marcius couldn't resist his injuries and died. There are reports that three other men would be involved, but they were heard by the police and denied their participation, accusing the fourth suspect. The Japoran Civil Police are following the case and are looking for the accused.
c4f4d32c04a592c0facb1838d533f3d2faec8b54: A 15-year-old Guarani-Kaiowá teenager was murdered in the village located between Ponta Porã and Bela Vista. The young man would have been murdered during a fight in the village Pirakuá Morro, and the case was registered at the police station by indigenous community leader. According to the police report, the adolescent was found already unawakened in the village by the military police, who identified stab marks in the victim's chest. He would have gone into a body struggle with the killer, who was identified by witnesses. The case is being investigated by Ponta Porã police station.
900d8e2cb7e741bf849d6bf1634cac5ef5084e02: The 37-year-old indigenous Edemilson Flores was killed with a stone of about 20 kilos in the village Bororó, in TI Dourados. Edemilson's body was on a road in the village's CRAS region. Two teenagers, 12 and 14 years old, confessed to the crime and were apprehended. They told the police they were passing by the place when they found the Indian and took advantage of it to attack him, due to an old fight.
fb342617d0486a85fd85e68eb9aff041ce4ae5af: The 20-year-old indigenous Charle de Souza Lima was murdered at knife blows in a hut in the village Bororó, in TI Dourados. According to information collected by police officers with village dwellers, Charle would have spent the night drinking with several people on site. Then the friends left, and the next morning, when a couple of friends came to the cabin, they found Charle. The case is being investigated by the Civil Police.
bccfe5a07e74d3d8bab0ac06699f647f36d02b3f: Two indigenous people were executed on the Paraguayan border with Mato Grosso do Sul, when they followed motorcycles by road. The crimes occurred in the Yjhovy Colony in Ybyrarovana district, less than 30 kilometers from Seven Falls (MS). The region where the indigenous people were killed is dominated by drug traffickers and is close to marijuana growing areas. Paraguayan National Police suspect executions have a connection to the drug trade control dispute. The two of them were riding a motorcycle on a vicinal road when they were attacked by gunmen. One of the indigenous was identified as Claudio Agüero Lugo, 36 years old. Still no leads on the perpetrators.
8719506ec4bfd703bd948af57c1f49781f484e51: The 29-year-old body of the indigenous Emerson Rossatti Medina was found on a vicinal road of the village Jaguapirú, near a farming area, in the Golden TI. In his body were signs of stab wounds in the back region. The police are investigating the crime.
102ca31ba9d1edf11edd696481fcbb9c40d53a60: Three people, 38, 35 and 22, were arrested for the death of an 18-year-old indigenous girl in the Yuporan village in Dourados (MS). The young woman's body was found two days after her death, on the banks of the BR-163 highway. According to the Civil Police, one of the investigated women would have put poison in the victim's drink out of jealousy by finding that the young woman had an extramarital affair with her husband. After ingesting the liquid, the indigenous woman had a seizure, fainted and was taken to the backyard of a house where she was left. Upon finding that the young woman had died, those involved decided to hide the corpse so that they would not be held responsible for the crime. The Indian body was only found two days after the crime and forensics confirmed that she had suffered sexual abuse.
c6d4f7bfc6b608c67482f02c4a67523c29bc72f3: Poisoning, sexual abuse and concealment of the corpse
869db545875cf4338f743cb3d01d49f2eb971058: The 19-year-old Genieliston Rosa Gonçalves, resident of the village Bororó, in TI Dourados, was murdered with a knife blow to the back, around 3 a.m. on October 3. According to information from the Civil Police, the victim was in the company of his girlfriend, a 17 - year - old teenager, when they met with two 16 - and 17 - year - old teenagers. One of them took a knife and invested against the teenager, who was injured with a blow to the face. To defend his companion, Genieliston entered the fight and wound up with a knife blow to the back, dying at the scene. The aggressor and the partner fled after the crime, while the adolescent was rescued by a health team and referred to the Hospital da Vida. Indigenous leaders arrested the 17-year-old teenager accused of the crime and reported that the motive may have been for revenge, since the young man is accused of raping the adolescent, who denounced him. The aggressor was referred to the police station and reported in flagrante for simple homicide, and should be transferred to Unei (Education Unit of Internship).
36ea8d7b3e9c3fd31003655a7525c69c5f7f6126: The 19-year-old indigenous Alex Junior Isnarde Machado was murdered in the early hours of October 3, a Sunday. It was the second murder case registered on the same night at Golden T.I. The boy was found wounded about 10 meters from the house where he lived with his mother in the village Jaguapiru. To the police, she told him that she spent part of Saturday night with her son in church, but when they returned, she let him leave the house to play with a friend. He left the residence on his bike, taking only his cell phone. Hours later, at dawn, Alex's mother woke up with the barking of the dogs. She got up to see what was going on and found Alex lying on the floor about 10 meters from home. The help was called, but the boy died in the ambulance before arriving at the hospital. I noticed he had a wound to his abdomen.
d956961f26f12262a1add850b6bcb8c35b6c585b: The indigenous John the Baptist was found dead inside the house. According to the PM, there was a shotgun near the victim's body, suggesting suicide. However, when performing the forensic examination, it was found that the shot did not match the characteristics of the rifle and the weapon had not been used recently. The case is being investigated by the Civil Police.
8c0623d6fe28358c014b96db036438d73a77737d: According to the Indians, Isac and other young Tembé were hunting in an area traditionally frequented by them when they were approached by military police. They report that the young 24-year-old teacher was murdered by the PM. The Temm also refuted the police's claim that there would have been a confrontation; all those who saw the body observed that the shot was fired on the young man's chest and within walking distance. There was no medical examination. According to the PM, a vehicle was triggered to check cattle theft on a farm and, as soon as they arrived, they would have been received with firearms. The PM also said that, in the alleged exchange of shots, the group would have fled, and that the police would have found in the place boned cattle, a revolver next to a person shot, who was later identified as being Isac Tembé. The indigenous accused the police of forging the crime scene and preventing the realization of expertise; evidences that strengthen the position of the indigenous were collected by a diligence of the Human Rights Commission of the Legislative Assembly of Pará, which accompanies the case, and from human rights organizations to the crime scene. The Commission’s report pointed out “flagrant human rights violations” and “possible implementation practice”. The Tembé-Theneteraha people are repeatedly threatened and attacked. In September 2019, the MPF requested the PF and the command of the Army in Belém an urgent operation to avoid attacks by loggers against the indigenous. Shaken, the Tembé-Theneteraha people released a note denouncing the murder as part of this context to which it is subjected in a land that belongs to it. They also report that the police assigned the dead teacher association to criminal activities. “The Military Police murdered twice Isac Tembé: they killed his body and tried to kill his memory when they attacked the character of our young warrior and exemplary leadership,” he says. In the note, the people further reinforce that “our territory suffers daily invasions and attacks by illegal timber explorers or farmers who insist on maintaining the occupation of parts of IT Alto Rio Guamá, through livestock heads and other economic activities.” The MPF asked for information on the case to the Military Police, Federal Police and Funai. The PM's Internal Affairs is investigating the circumstances of the murder. The Paraense Human Rights Defense Society also follows the case.
2a1f7edf745d03f105ab4f1e150567823f6b7b19: Less than a month after the assassination of Isac Tembé, leader of the Tembé Theneteraha people in the municipality of Capt. Poço, in the northeast of Pará, another indigenous was killed in the same region. Benedito Cordeiro de Carvalho was murdered in broad light of March 2. According to prior information, he was followed and shot on the bike he was on. When trying to escape, the Indian was shot in the head. He no longer lived in the village, but was on his way to visit relatives. Known as Didi Tembé, Benedito de Carvalho was of the Municipal Guard of Ourém, a municipality near Captain Well. The circumstances of Didi Tembé's death raised questions among the indigenous peoples of the region. Puyr Tembé, Vice President of Fepipa, explains that there are still many questions to be answered about the motive of the murder. “Some strange things are happening in Captain Well. It is not only in Captain Poço, but the whole of Brazil is going through a very difficult process of criminalizing the leaders, the social segments, not just the indigenous. This has emerged much within the territories,” he says. Nice Gonçalves, journalist and activist Tupinambá, says that out of fear, few indigenous people talk about the murder. Local police officials also began to question Didi Tembé's indigenous identity, only because he went to live in the city. Crime is being investigated.
a06771820ce75b66aef5e85cd56f1ae7058c526f: The 42-year-old indigenous Cleide de Fátima dos Santos was found unconscious in her room next to the bed; she had a deep throat cut. The Fire Department was set up for service, but the victim had already died. The case is being investigated by the Civil Police, which seeks the perpetrator.
848a3921912b31937526d481f8d497f65ae33446: The 28-year-old Aranildo M.N. indigenous was found murdered in Ivaí TI, in the municipality of Manoel Ribas, on January 11. Military and civilian police have been at the scene and are investigating the crime.
3540518b5dfe0eb8f12976b9f8ee7a7f0f442334: Indian father and son, residents of TI Mangueirinha, were found dead in a town square. The occurrence was recorded by the PM, on the street Mauricio Orlando dos Santos, in the square São Basilio. The death of the two was observed by the nurse of the Municipal UBS. On the spot, a woman, their aunt, told them that her nephews do not have personal documents and confirmed that they are residents of the municipality of Mangueirinha. The two Indians were lying on the ground, near a bottle of drink, and had no apparent injury. The case is being investigated. There are suspicions that they would have been poisoned because the tests were not performed at the IML.
e860587149609a778b8e7712a0692cb9d383b097: A 15-year-old indigenous teenager was found dead in Barra Preta. There are suspicions that the teenager was poisoned. They were then activated to the PM and the Civil Police to support the occurrence, which was attended by researchers. The Scientific Police and the IML were also activated. At first, there were no signs of violence in the body, which was directed directly to be buried in the village, without having been taken by the IML to detect the cause of death.
ce2bbce30cc107df834e7674dd03e757f52404e6: A 28-year-old Indian was found dead near a creek in New Orange trees. Civil and military police have been engaged to investigate the case. A nurse in the municipality tried to revive the indigenous, but failed. The boy had a cut on his head and there were blood marks on the scene. Researchers took steps to identify the author and try to ascertain the motive of the crime. The indigenous body underwent necropsy at the Guarapuava IML.
ac2e1b566d265d3382ea56883013dbbfe9565e1e: Three indigenous people were found dead on the banks of a highway in Laranjeiras do Sul. Cops are investigating the case. The bodies were removed to the Cascavel IML and the police are waiting for the autopsy results. Some indigenous people have reported that local traders have sold alcohol mixed with alcohol fuel; they report that they have reported Funai, but that no action has been taken.
03f60b6df16f36a7c7046df5e93aa7b1645ec2ac: An indigenous man, resident of Mata Verde Bonita village in Maricá (RJ), is suspected of raping, impregnation his own daughter and participate in the death of the newborn baby. Her 21-year-old daughter reported the case at the police station, and claimed she was raped by her father since she was 13 years old. According to the police, the young woman reported to the village chief who suffered threats from the father and was forced to leave the newborn baby in a forest area. The baby was found by the village residents, taken to the hospital, but did not resist and died. The case was registered by the police as a vulnerable rape; the man confessed to being the father of the child and admitted to abandoning it, but was not arrested for not being registered in the act.
bcb0fe7c267de57d1a27f3df22ce33918c39d8db: The 23-year-old Indian Cézar Sampaio Benites was found dead on the Orange Road in Many Capões (RS). Family members had already reported her missing. The Civil Police of Vacaria is investigating the case and has already identified two suspects, also indigenous, from Amambai, in Mato Grosso do Sul.
7992e1d6114eee3a521bfcbbeaafa43b4c33596c: According to the local press, since April 4, there has been a conflict over disagreements between indigenous leaders. This conflict was permeated by fights and firearms. Military police were informed of the fighting and shooting in the village, as well as a house fire. On Sunday, day 4, an indigenous was shot and taken to Santo Antônio de Tapejara Hospital. The fights continued on Monday, the 5th, and the police were called again. On Tuesday, the 6th, there was a new exchange of firearms, and another indigenous was shot by firearms. He was taken to the hospital, but he couldn't resist his injuries. According to information from Danilo Braga, Kaingang leadership, there have been two deaths, there is one indigenous missing and the community is looking for the body, as there are reports that it was also shot. According to the leadership, the deaths in the Carreiro IT occurred due to a confrontation of the Military Police with the indigenous community. The police would be in the area to protect the community and avoid an internal conflict, but that's not what happened. Reports show that the two indigenous killed were shot by gunfire, weapons used by the police. The situation is very serious and the Military Police could not be in IT, since it is an assignment of the PF. Funai and PF have been at the scene and are checking out the facts.
ce0f4e5eb9c4be61d31f517dc62def0670798d4e: The 23-year-old indigenous Elizeu Pedroso was shot to death during a demonstration at ERS-324 in Planalto (RS). According to the Civil Police, the investigation indicates that a conflict between indigenous Bananeiras and Pinhalzinho villages led to Pedroso's death. He belonged to Pinhalzinho village. Around 10:30 p.m., a car drove past the demonstration and a passenger shot the group. Elizeu was shot, received care at the Median hospital in Planalto, but did not resist the wound and died. The investigation should be continued by PF.
dfd68c2a4f8670a2cfdfe8c0f5792f7f66bc9f77: The body of Daiane Griá Sales, a 14-year-old teenager Kaingang, was found in the Estiva Sector, in TI Guarita, in the municipality of Redemptora, northwest of Rio Grande do Sul. Resident of the Bananeiras Sector of TI Guarita, Daiane was found in a plantation near a bush area, naked, and with parts of the body from the waist down torn and torn apart – which, according to autopsy report carried out by the Civil Police, would have been caused by animals or birds of prey. In October, the prosecutor filed a complaint against a 33-year-old non-indigenous man accused of raping and asphyxiating young Kaingang. The man, who was arrested preventively, was accused of the crimes of rape of vulnerable and murder with six qualifiers – among them, a lewd motive, characterized by the contempt of the denounced by the Kaingang people. According to the MP, the man was offering a ride to other indigenous people at dances in the region and imagined that, because it is an indigenous woman, the crime would have little repercussions and would go unpunished. There are reports of other cases of attacks against indigenous women and children that would be taking place in the region. With an area of 23.4 thousand hectares, the Guarita TI houses about 6,000 people and is the largest indigenous land in the state, covering the municipalities of Lt. Portela, Redemptora and Herval Seco, in the northwest gaucho. Several factors have been pointed out as possible causes of such violence, such as the failure of the State, especially regarding public policies that favor the social protection of indigenous children and young people, as well as the increased presence of non-indigenous people within the community, generating insecurity and various threats to the population. The proliferation of hate speeches in the country, especially against indigenous peoples and against women, has also favored the increase in cases of violence and cruelty. In a note, the National Articulation of Warrior Women of Ancestrality (Anmiga) states: “We have seen the killing of indigenous people day after day. But it looks like it's not enough to kill. The refinement of cruelty is what tears our souls apart, just as they literally tear down Daiane's young body, just 14 years old. They cut up young bodies, women, people. We understand that the sets of violence committed to us indigenous women since the invasion of Brazil is a cold attempt to exterminate us, with heinous crimes that bleed our souls. The inhumanity exposed in indigenous female bodies needs to stop”.
16473ac881d01ea42cd5f2a12227153d537db706: Illegal lease on indigenous lands has caused serious internal conflicts, generating violence and deaths. In TI Serrinha, a conflict resulted in the deaths of Rosenildo Batista and Lucas Caetano, both Kaingang. It was an episode of much violence, with several wounded beyond the dead, resulting from the encounter between political opponents. The cause of the dispute would be the lease of land for non-indigenous farmers, for the practice of predatory agribusiness, represented by farmers and farmers, who would support leaders, undermining the good coexistence among the Kaingang.
d618328544b1b1c92d65ea3722f671a43befb4c1: After leaving his wife in college, Carlinhos went to meet an acquaintance, not knowing it was a trap. They both met at the barracks, where he was an army corporal. Since the wife had no news of her husband, she called the police in an attempt to locate him. After two days of his disappearance, through the tracker on his motorcycle, his whereabouts and where he had disappeared were discovered. The perp was also found and confessed to killing him for money, for stealing the motorcycle. With him there were also two young accomplices, known to the victim. Carlinhos was also a nursing technician. The population of the municipality felt sensitized and supportive towards the family. After this crime, the population made a demonstration calling for greater security in the city.
62ae808ace835e00f7a709e60e32f9bb0e6ab87e: Ubirajara Canoe's family were looking for him, for he had been missing for two days when a fisherman found him, far from the village. The body had wounds consistent with machete use. The entire community was shaken by the violent murder and the perpetrator has not yet been found.
6fbfe3a3beab562af84da0e35341943a68b6c571: On May 10, a group of heavily armed prospectors attacked the Palimiú indigenous community in the Uraricoera River region. They were on seven ships, from which they shot the residents of the community, who ran and therefore were not hit. Many indigenous people fled the place in the face of panic. Two children under the age of five fled into the forest and two days later their bodies were found lifeless in the river. This was the beginning of a systematic set of attacks against the Palimiú village, which lasted for at least three months. On May 16, 15 prospector vessels arrived again to the site and, in addition to firearms, used tear gas bombs against the community. Three days later, on the 19th, according to information from the Condisi, 12 other vessels attempted to invade the village again. In a document by community leaders in July 2021, three months after the attacks began, the indigenous report the routine of terror that was installed throughout the region. The transit of ships through the river and aircraft in the service of the mine increased. The organic structure of the prospector had a profound transformation, with the use of more sophisticated equipment and machinery, with the increase of corrutels, camps and gas stations of the prospector. The community of Palimiú, according to the leadership document, can no longer go fishing on the Uraricoera River, afraid of further attacks, since death threats continued to occur. Hunting also decreased in the region because of mining and the consequent increase in deforestation and plastic waste. On the other hand, since the first armed attack against Palimiú, the health team that attended the community has left the area and only entered on time, in a few moments. Health care has decreased and malaria is suspected to increase. Leaderships sent a letter of complaint to: 1st Army Jungle Infantry Brigade(1Bis), MPF/RR, Etnoenvironmental Protection Front Yanomami, Funai, and Superintendence of PF in Roraima. The MPF entered with Public Civil Action requesting the presence of state security forces on site to contain the action of the prospectors, and should remain in the region, protecting the communities, until the effective withdrawal of the invaders within 100 km of the village Palimiú and until the implementation of the measures requested in ACP 2020, which required an Emergency Plan for territorial monitoring. On May 13, the Federal Court granted the request of the MPF. In the following weeks there were only a few incursions from small groups of the PF or Army that remained on site for a few hours.
ff68f558bb22d5c6ca2cb221a7a9d01c0dc99131: Around 2:30 p.m. on July 28th, 25-year-old Edgard Yanomami and another Yanomami indigenous were walking in the middle of the mining flight track in the village Homoxi, in the Yanomami IT, towards the health center of the Surucuku region. The monomotor piloted by “Marreco”, nickname of the pilot known in the region, landed, decreased the march because it was approaching the health center that is about 700 meters away and suddenly accelerated the plane, hit the Yanomami and took off. The young man died instantly, shot in the head. After the accident, the prospectors tampered with the crime scene, taking Edgar's body, his wife and the three children, who are still children, to Yamasipiu village, in the neighboring region of Haxiu. The president of Condisi Yanomami and Ye’kuana (Condisi-YYY), Junior Hekurari Yanomami, said that the prospectors stayed between 30 and 40 minutes at the scene of the accident and then decided to take the body to another community, because “they will come police, they will report to Sesai”. But the case was not denounced or communicated to Hekurari by Sesai. The president of Condisi-YY said he received the news almost four hours later by radiophony from Dsei-Y headquarters. To confirm the information, Hekurari called back to Homoxi base and, faced with the silence, decided to request a chartered helicopter flight from Sesai. As the aircraft was in maintenance, he flew to the site. There was trouble getting down. The pilot of the aircraft had to request permission on the radio and Hekurari said they took about ten laps flying over and negotiating with the pilots in order to land. The prospectors didn't want to authorize the plane to come down. The indigenous denounced the case to MPF, Funai, Dsei-YY, Sesai and CDHM of the House of Representatives. Federal Congresswoman Joênia Wapichana (Rede-RR) denounced the murder to the CDHM of the House of Representatives and, on August 5, the President of the Commission, Carlos Veras, sent a request for urgent measures to investigate the murder. The opening of the investigation was communicated on 12 September by the Director-General of PF, Paulo Gustavo Maiurino, who said that the information led to the initiation of the investigation and it was referred for distribution among police authorities. Between August 31 and September 12, an operation against illegal mining at Yanomami IT seized 60 aircraft. In addition to PF, PRF, National Public Safety Force, Funai, Ibama, ICMBio, ANAC, Anatel and ANP participated in the operation.
6db652fcd0d05a172a6cc55f375d5a7fe27159fa: Two Yanomami children from the Macuxi Yano community, aged 5 and 8 years, died on October 12, while playing on the Parima River, next to the dredge of a mining site. According to Hutukara Association Yanomami (HAY), in the publication “Yanomami under attack: illegal mining in the Yanomami Indigenous Land and proposals to fight it”, the children “died drowned while playing on the beach in front of their houses, after being knocked down and swallowed by the current generated by a dredge prospector that operated a few meters from the community. The disappearance of the children was witnessed by their families, without being able to do anything to save them”. The community immediately denounced the disappearance of the children and began the search procedures. The first child’s lifeless body was found by the community the next day, 13. The Roraima Fire Department, which had been triggered by the Condisi-YYY, found the body of the second victim the following day, 14. At the time, HAY stated, in a note, that “the death of the two Yanomami children is yet another sad result of the presence of illegal mining in Yanomami IT, which continues to be invaded by more than 20,000 prospectors. By September 2021, the forest area destroyed by illegal mining at Yanomami IT surpassed the 3,000-hectare mark – a 44% increase from December 2020. Only in the Parima region, where the Macuxi Yano community is located and one of the most affected by illegal activity, a total of 118.96 hectares of degraded forest was reached, an increase of 53% over December 2020. In addition to the already highly impacted regions, such as Waikás, Aracaçá, and Kayanau, the mining progresses over new regions: in Xitei and Homoxi, the activity increased by 1000% between December and September 2021.” The note also reports that, at a meeting held in September, the Yanomami IT Leadership Forum assessed that “the increase in illegal mining activity in the Yanomami IT is reflecting on more insecurity, violence, diseases, and death for Yanomami and Ye’kwana. Brazilian authorities need to continue working to protect the Terra-Floresta, and prevent illegal mining from continuing to threaten our lives.”
5e06d9135efe46ca3a9863826fd55936058616f9: HAY, in a public letter of 2 November, reported two murders to the Etnoenvironmental Protection Front Yanomami of Funai, the Superintendence of PF in Roraima, the 1st Army Jungle Infantry Brigade – 1st BIS and the MPF-RR. According to the complaint, two indigenous isolated Moxihatëtëma were murdered in a confrontation with the prospectors, just over two months before the letter, when they approached the prospect “Black Track”, located in the Upper Apiaú River, in an attempt to expel the prospectors from their territory. In the conflict, the prospectors killed two indigenous men with firearms and the isolated struck with arrows three prospectors. The Moxihatëtëma community is located in the Upper Apiaú River region of Mucajaí, southern Roraima. The Black Strip mining is close to IT. It is a region that attracts prospectors by distance and is difficult to access, about four days by boat with a rabeta engine, according to HAY, which also denounces deforestation in the region: “Satellite image analyses indicate that in the region more than 100 hectares of forest have been destroyed by illegal activity”. The invasion of prospectors at Yanomami IT has been reported for decades, and in the last four years has intensified. In a statement of repudiation, the Cimi presented a history of violence in these territories in recent years and declared its perplexity in the face of the neglect of the authorities, saying that these situations “became frighteningly frequent in the face of the omission of the government, bringing revolt, mourning, fear and food insecurity to the villages”.
de7fb056437cbfd236dddf4ce20c0604a7716b36: Adriano Silva, Guarani Mbya, only 20 years old, was found dead in the Billings Dam on January 12, in Parelheiros, southern São Paulo. He was missing since January 9th. He lived in the village Gwyra Pepó in Tapiraí (SP), and went to TI Tenondé Porã to visit his family. He was last seen getting into a car with a group of young Guarani. After three days gone, the body was seen in the dam at the time of the village Gwyrapaju, in TI Tenondé Porã. The police were fired and the body was taken to the IML of São Paulo. Adriano had signs of physical assault and asphyxiation. The case is being investigated.
fac481e3bdc56c9c000719f97f96ee3f036c0caa: The indigenous Myriwekwde Karajá was beaten by her husband, also indigenous, in the first week of December. She had polytrauma, internal bleeding and was diagnosed positive for Covid-19. On January 10, 2021, after passing two hospitals in two different cities, Myriwekwde died. Only then the police were activated; according to the Public Security Secretariat of Tocantins, the husband remains free. His name hasn't been released. The circumstances and motivations of Myriwekwde Karajá's feminicide remain uncertain, but the lack of support and protection for the victim in the public health network proved alarming. Although Bananal Island is located in Tocantins, the closest city to the community where the crime took place is São Félix do Araguaia, in Mato Grosso, and it was there where the indigenous received the first care, but was soon transferred by plane to the Municipal Hospital of Cuiabá, where she died. The Cuiabana Public Health Company, responsible for administering the hospital, confirmed, by note, that Myriwekwde had been the victim of physical assault, but the police authorities were not notified as expected. According to Eliana Karajá, the coordination of the Collective of Women Iny and the Indigenous Association of Vale do Araguaia (Asiva), “hide that there was beating is a behavior that comes from the fear of the consequences that this may have within the community itself, which often treats the issue as cultural and gives more support to men and aggressors than to victims”.
c02f4cd905df34aabad80a62ab7d4d624c6709c5: Lourenço Rosemar Son of Mello was wanted by the police for crimes committed. He was with his family in the village, when officers from the Special Tactical Operations Group GOTE arrived, along with the Specialized Division of Repression to Organized Crime - DEIC, Paradise (TO), and also with the Civil Police of Mato Grosso. With the approval of Funai, the police officers went to the village to make their arrest. The technical coordinator of Funai Araguaia (TO), Vicente de Paula Rodrigues de Lima, followed the operation. The police say that when a prison voice was given, the indigenous made people of their own family hostage, threatening them. In order not to hurt these people, police officers fired fire to contain it, hitting it mortally before people of the community and their own family, including women and children. Some Indians claim that Lourenço had sketched surrender and yet was shot. The case caused great commotion in the community for the violence with which it was carried out, with the invasion of the village, without previous dialogue with the indigenous leaders. Cimi Goiás/Tocantins and Cimi Mato Grosso issued a note expressing indignation, demanding clarification from Funai and investigation into the police operation.
9dbdcc07ce49441a5bac6fe96a7a1e2dd3f6faea: José Francisco Kiriri, an 84-year-old elder, walked down the road from BA-388, Banzaé, in the northern region of Bahia, when he was hit by a motorcycle. The motorcycle driver fled the scene. José Francisco was rescued, but did not resist his injuries and died. After finishing the period of flagrant, the accused presented himself with a witness in the police station of the municipality of Euclides da Cunha, gave testimony and was released. The case is being conducted by the Civil Police station of the city of Ribeira do Pombal, which has not yet completed the process, and there was no arrest of the accused.
417f9cacc111a67455e7c0918f35f89ecfb12864: Indigenous people of the Guajajara people closed a section of the BR-226, in protest for the death of the only 9-year-old child, known as “Pajezinho”, victim of hit-and-run. The driver fled the scene without providing assistance to the child. According to witnesses, the child was on the roadside, waiting for the delivery of bread to take to his family, when a vehicle went off the road and hit the boy. Leaderships are outraged by so many deaths on the highway in the middle of the indigenous territory. The situation is serious and the local population does not see the authorities taking steps to improve the scenario. “We have no support. Public policies do not reach communities. Nor
f7659d0640d1e26cedf51a2865e52bf92e526201: Enzo Gabriel, an indigenous child of only 4 years old, was accompanied by his family at the door of his home when he was hit by a Toyota Hilux vehicle. The driver was using alcohol and had no experience in driving. Both the driver and the other occupants of the vehicle fled the site without providing assistance. The child did not resist severe injuries and died. Pau Brasil Civil Police has opened an investigation and is investigating the crime.
1732dd8cc68bb31cd8c6be57c581631b990c919b: An indigenous man, appearing to be 30 years old, was hit in BR-070, between Mato Grosso and Goiás, and died on site. Due to the locality of the accident, near Barra do Garças (MT), it is believed that it is of the people Xavante or Bororo. The driver fled without providing assistance to the victim. The PRF is investigating to identify the vehicle involved.
7c6162790f2793e4314007f49884ddfcb46fb4d1: The indigenous Nivaldo Azezonae, 41 years old, died in an accident near the village Rio Verde, in Tangará da Serra (MT). Indigenous community blocked a stretch of the MT358, at the scene of the accident, in protest for the driver's escape. The driver of the vehicle did not provide assistance to Nivaldo, who was on a motorcycle. The highway connects Tangará da Serra to other municipalities of the region such as Nova Lacerda, Campos de Júlio, Comodoro and Cáceres.
ead6b6ea10a864ca39f5dfa3bda4243df85587b0: The indigenous child, only 6 years old, was hit on the highway near the entrance of the Boqueron community. Indigenous people report that the Elian boy lived with his mother and other brothers in the community and that he constantly “escaped”. This time, after he disappeared for a few moments, family members went out to look for him and found the boy's body on the track, torn apart. The vehicle involved has not been identified or located. It is suspected that it was a cart, because the stretch is route of heavy load vehicles. The Indians revolted and promised to close the part Perimetral Norte, close to the clover that gives access to Itaporan and Campo Grande. Gaudêncio Benitez commented: “We are tired of unfulfilled promises. Everyone knows this highway is very dangerous. I'm sure this isn't the first and it won't be the last major accident. Some action needs to be taken.” According to Benitez, the highway should not have been built in that area if the community had been heard at the time. The Samu was triggered, but only found death. Military and Civil Police have also been activated and will request images of cameras installed on property located on the side of the highway to clarify the circumstances of the accident and identify the vehicle that hit the child.
aaf616ce0de39cade7c5b66ca439d303a4c21000: Vehicle collision; driver escape without assistance
8fb6efd45f5176bd6e7132cc19f4cd64bd4378c2: The indigenous Gabriel Benites de Paula, 20 years old, died hit by a car at BR-163, in Dourados (MS). According to witnesses, he was hit by a car and then by a motorcycle. They also said that the young man lived in the community Ñu Porã, on the highway, where he was walking. The drivers of the car and motorcycle escaped from the site without providing assistance, and were not located. Samu was triggered, but found Gabriel's death at the scene of the hit-and-run. The police are investigating the case.
103f94d9eff2ac33afd7c806ec89ce0d95697a86: An 18-year-old Indian boy was hit by a speeding car. The accident occurred on Presidente Vargas Avenue in Dourados (MS), and the driver fled without providing assistance. According to witness reports to the police, the young Indian was on a bicycle, moving in the center direction, when he performed a return maneuver and was hit by a silver-colored vehicle, which passed at high speed. The rescue was triggered, but the young man died at the scene due to the strong impact of the collision. Civilian police have been at the scene and will investigate the case.
395413c626e5222444422b5a24674ab5a90208c0: The PRF of the operating post of Laranjeiras do Sul registered the hit by a 40-year-old indigenous woman on the night of April 12, in the kilometer 476 of BR-277. The driver fled without providing assistance to the victim, who died at the scene.
e3e44e4887c58aa947982862b3e4d8ffea18e019: A car Cruze with Santa Catarina plates hit the indigenous, who received assistance on site. Due to the severity of the injuries, he was first referred to Guaraniaçu, where he was taken with aeromedical care to Cascavel, but did not resist. The PRF will investigate the causes of the accident.
8016216db00a3d426fc11a8bbeef48c9b34bba12: Mário Lourenço, an indigenous Kaingang, was the victim of a hit-and-run at BR-277, which cuts the indigenous territory, and died.
f4c08d175a9c121eab9b4681f9654b1353120d51: The young indigenous Juninho Pého Luiz, only 16 years old, died on the night of December 30, after being hit by the vehicle of an unidentified driver, who fled the place without providing assistance. In this same episode, four other indigenous youths were hit by a car, some with severe injuries and others without information from the health situation. All victims were referred to the municipal hospital of Laranjeiras do Sul (PR).
6dcb49f489e0009a6081813e9c2ee0e04307923c: PRE de Telemaco Borba reported that there was a pedestrian hit in the kilometer 348 of the highway PRC-487, in the city of Cândido de Abreu (PR). At the site, it was found that a motorcycle with a board of the municipality, conducted by a man with initials B. R. S., 44 years old, ran over the indigenous Arlindo, 49 years old, who died at the site and was taken to the IML of Ivaiporã.
00e20d86ee19227e4fe316a28a6bf54f0535022f: An indigenous man died in the Faxinal village of Catanduvas in the first week of September. According to witnesses, he was with three other indigenous people in a place used as shelter for people who commit some infraction in the village. Apparently, the fire that hit the house was accidental, but Funai and PF opened investigation. The other three Indians were rescued and taken to the reference hospital in Telemaco Borba, where the second death was announced on December 15.
734e8a62aa3d84a25f2bffb79b3231380b9f5ac2: A 22-year-old indigenous was located dead in the ERS-330 in Miraguaí, about two o'clock in the morning. According to the PRE of St. Augustus, the evidence is of a hit-and-run. There are no witnesses or information on the vehicle that caused the death.
c86a518cea248e6a13068f30f99b88becf36c40f: The young Breno Mineiro da Silva died after being hit by an accident in the km 6 of the VRS-814, between Flores da Cunha and Nova Padua, around 3:50. The driver of the vehicle fled the site without providing assistance and Breno was already dead when the Samu arrived. According to the DML of Caxias do Sul, where the body was sent, Breno was indigenous and was living in Flores da Cunha to work on the grape harvest.
8b2f6643765cda18fd4ac5a114919fc8dd645f58: The 47-year-old indigenous Kaingang André Pinto hit the ERS-324, a highway that cuts off part of TI Serrinha; he did not resist injuries and died on site. The hit-and-run was in the vicinity of the Caneleira Sector, between the municipalities of Ronda Alta and Três Palmeiras. In contact with indigenous peoples of the community, it was reported to the Cimi Regional Sul that André transited on the banks of the highway and at the time he crossed it he ended up being hit by a cart (of the type “blind”). The indigenous land in question has a large part of its territory being used illegally for rental, with GM soybean and wheat planting. This practice has generated a series of conflicts, leading many families to settle in tiny spaces of land on the highway. A significant part of these families live in exile, even though they are in their own demarcated territory. Another serious situation is that this highway, even crossing an indigenous territory and with many families living close to it, does not have speed reducers and other mechanisms that guarantee pedestrian safety.
0aad6e876b4c1102de981988aa15dec5807613bc: The indigenous Zacqueu da Rosa, 52 years old, was the victim of a hit-and-run on the ERS-330 highway in the Irapua neighborhood of Miraguaí (RS). The driver didn't provide any help and fled the scene. Samu went to the crash site, but the Indian had already died. The Military Brigade and the State Highway Police responded to the occurrence with the Civil Police, which will investigate the causes of the accident.
431173102f7e09b8be18f6faab519740e5d947cd: The indigenous Célia Yanomami died after being hit by a vehicle passing under the viaduct located on Av. Glaycon de Paiva, neighborhood of São Vicente, in Boa Vista (RR). The indigenous woman was with her son, a year old, on her lap. According to the PM, when he arrived at the scene, Celia was attended by a fire ambulance and one by Samu. Resuscitation procedures were performed on the victim, who couldn't resist the injuries and died in the rescue ambulance. The baby was taken to the emergency room of the Child Hospital. Also according to information from the PM, the driver of the car, a 54-year-old accountant, trafficed towards the neighborhood center and, when passing under the viaduct, would have been surprised by the victim, who crossed “repentantly” the right-to-left path, being hit by the car. A breathalyzer test was performed on the driver, who reported negative. The accident occurred around 8:30, when the state suffered a general blackout. Celia's body was taken to the IML and the driver was taken to the police station to record the case and clarify the facts.
1002f06db53f0ffae33475970b207f1803685067: The indigenous João Kulina was in the port of Santa Rosa do Purus, drunk and wanting to fight with his daughter. The police have been called. Upon arriving at the scene, Sergeant Mero invested against the Indian, beating him in the face, arrested him and took him to the police station. Councilman Enio Kulina of the Madija people witnessed the fact and filmed the assaults with his cell phone. The officer, upon hearing that it had been filmed, went to the councilman's house, asked for his cell phone and erased the images. The denunciation of the facts was filed in the MPF, which instituted an inquiry to investigate the police abuses against the indigenous.
3104deb851ce5769d7a7674748b1e821e8e7de5e: Beating; destruction of evidence and illegal imprisonment
cdc50a8e94710097ca55807e6b50f1411c060644: In June, more than 850 indigenous peoples from all over the country participated in Camp Levante pela Terra, mobilization against the dismantling of constitutional rights and anti-indigenous projects that deal with the National Congress, such as PL 490/2007, which prevents land demarcations, institutionalizes the thesis of the so-called “temporal mark” and opens the demarcated areas to predatory economic exploitation. On 22 June, a group of indigenous peoples, including children, met
eb83a36e6eecf94e736fdd4051fc1aa4c02f9787: The Chiquitano IT is located in a region where violence and discrimination against indigenous people occur due to conflicts and claims for land ownership by non-indigenous people. The indigenous are constantly threatened, especially the chief Aurelius. This time, the victim of threats and physical aggression was Genisvaldo Rodrigues, who was approached by three non-indigenous young people. Genisvaldo was beaten violently by the three young men on the way to the indigenous sister's residence. The young people left Genisvaldo unawakened under a hose where he was found by relatives and taken to his sister’s house. Then he was taken to the hospital, where he was treated and medicated. The case is being followed by the State Human Rights Council. Days later, he was found dead in a dam.
cf1980e75faa05f8b03d43b8980bfd54adcbdfd2: An Indian woman was accused of witchcraft and beaten by a group inside her house. She went to the police to make a police report and reported that she was surprised, in her own home, by a group of five people armed with pieces of wood, machete and hammer. The group accused her of witchcraft, and assaulted her with wood, punches and kicks. There are reports that the group is motivated by religious fundamentalists who work in the region and do not respect indigenous culture.
780559a2fb437a3a5a9670d491cff701d90488c2: Three indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá, two adults and one teenager, were approached overnight, while returning to their village by three armed men, who were in two trucks. These men gave them punches, kicks, butts and intimidating shots towards them. According to the indigenous statement to the police, the teenager managed to escape before being assaulted. According to a leadership, “he saw that the car left Querência Farm, already ran towards the direction of our tekoha and stopped about 60 meters, because it was at night, but the men shot towards it.” Aty Guasu attributes the aggressions to Querência Farm employees, located on the outskirts of the village, because there have been several conflicts and attacks over decades. The Guarani-Kaiowá claim the site as part of their traditional territory, from which they were removed in the 1910s. In 2008, Funai started the process of demarcating IT, but its process has been paralyzed since 2012. Leadership of Aty Guasu reports that “it is an area of permanent conflict; farmers want to take the indigenous people away at any cost. And the indigenous insist on staying and demanding demarcation”. The Civil Police of Aral Moreira investigates the case, and the MPF of Ponta Porã is following.
a0cc6ba065430041c2ea41c04993c095c6762c0d: Hooded bandits invaded the residence of the indigenous couple in the village Bororó. According to his 36 - year - old wife, eight hooded people broke into the house about 1:00 a.m. She reported that the invaders were armed with sticks and machetes, announced the robbery and were already assaulting her 48 - year - old husband with blows to the head. He was rescued by the Fire Department and taken to the UPA. The bandits took the stereo from the house.
06b510c45b142cb24677763bff893fbc143480eb: A 20 - year - old indigenous woman living in the Nhu Vera community was violently assaulted by her 23 - year - old husband. The assaults were so serious that she had to be admitted to the Mission Hospital. Leaders had information about where the attacker was and they picked him up to take him to the police station, where he was arrested red-handed.
90b8e75eb98c0cb5a98899b451da8e8eac21974d: A 67-year-old indigenous was hit by a truck in the Perimetral Norte, via which gives access to Avenida Guaicurus, meaning Itaporan, in Dourados. The Indian was on his bike. The victim would be returning from the market to the village, because on the spot there were some purchases such as rice, bread, and sanitary water, among others, that were scattered across the runway. A Samu team was activated to help the elderly, who was referred to the Hospital of Life, with head trauma and breathing with the help of devices.
9ef0ba67aafa83241c71681fc5af7e29a344993b: A 28-year-old Indian assaulted his 28-year-old wife, and his 58-year-old father-in-law beat her. Both were helped and taken to the Hospital of Life by the Samu team. The attacker was arrested, reported for domestic violence.
0b1d6413f228a84451c0b7d7e4d5e538758d9920: Indigenous leaders denounce that agents of the PM and private security in the region of Dourados, in Mato Grosso do Sul, shot at the community of tekoha Avaeté I on November 4. According to reports, the shots hit some people, leaving wounded at the scene. The community is one of the resumptions carried out by the Guarani and Kaiowá on the banks of the Dourados indigenous reserve – an area they claim as part of their traditional territory. The situation of lack of land and confinement in the reserve and conflicts with farmers and besiegers makes the site a conflagrated region, where attacks and threats against indigenous people are frequent.
3bc13403c3569848b06a9d2430e7055ef05fe1fa: A 17-year-old teenager was injured with a stab wound to the face. She was in the company of her 19-year-old boyfriend Genieliston when they met two 16- and 17-year-old teenagers, and one of them seized a knife and invested against the teenager, hurting her. To defend his companion, Genieliston entered the fight, the moment he was wounded with a stab in the back, dying at the scene. The aggressor and his partner fled after the crime, while the adolescent was rescued by a health team and referred to the Hospital of Life. Indigenous leaders arrested the 17-year-old teenager accused of the crimes and reported that the motive may have been for revenge, since the young man is accused of raping the adolescent, who denounced him. The aggressor was referred to the police station and reported in flagrante for simple homicide and should be transferred to Unei (Education Unit of Internship).
07d6b4b5096cda051df9f0ca693c17ebf5b6f965: The Maxakali community denounced violence against Artur Maxakali, a professor of culture of the people, in a case that was widely reported by local and state newspapers. He was brutally beaten in the square of Santa Helena de Minas (MG), before countless people, by the former mayor of this city, Zé Wilson, from Avante (who had his mandate dismissed for abuse of economic power, but appealed in second instance). According to the residents, the motivation for the aggression was that a group of indigenous people went to the city hall to charge improvements in roads that cut Maxakali territory. Arthur was beaten with punches, punches and kicks and fainted; he was totally disfigured. Apoinme entered with a representation with the MPF, requesting the investigation of the aggressions. The Maxakali Justice Observatory, composed of partner institutions (MPE, MPF, PM, PC, District Judge, Funai, among others) is following the case. In addition to the former mayor, there are others involved in the assault against the Maxakali.
8584f8144306c0c643944a23cdf534ce33d6d5ef: Two Indians Ava-Guarani, a lady and her son, were beaten with iron bars. A police team was deployed to move to the UPA 24 hours in Guaíra, in order to assist in a situation of personal injury by a white gun. On the spot, the indigenous youth reported that he was sitting in front of his residence, inside the village Tekoha Marangatu, when the aggressor, for no apparent reason, began to beat him with an iron bar. When the victim's mother saw the attack on her son, she tried to stop him, but she was also assaulted, resulting in severe injuries to both. They could not inform any reason about the assaults. The police are investigating the case.
1b96d86b9c6c8e55aeabdf00154579f49834b20a: After attending a man injured by a gun in the region of the head, Moacir Micheletto Hospital called the PM of Santa Helena to investigate the case. The victim reported to the PM that he is a resident of the indigenous village Ara Porã and that he was in his residence at the time he was assaulted with a machete by several men. The Indian claimed he didn't know what the assault was about. Police conducted searches in the area, but no suspects were found.
df744c1b1db22188d286e3c15d01f1d1f9f1a2e8: Two indigenous men were hit by a car on the night of December 14th. The fact occurred at the time of the km 477 of BR-277, close to the access clover to the highway PR-473, in Nova Laranjeiras. The indigenous people were helped by the health team of the municipality and sent in a serious state to the Hospital São Lucas, in Laranjeiras do Sul. According to information from the PRF, the driver fled the site without providing assistance; the vehicle had not yet been identified.
2e1908c0d6bb31cd477a7133cf7acfc9853e400a: Five indigenous youths were hit on the night of December 30, in the access clover to the municipality of Quedas do Iguaçu, by an unidentified vehicle, whose driver fled the site without providing assistance. One of them, Juninho Pého Luiz, aged only 16 years, died. The other four indigenous young people were referred to the municipal hospital of Laranjeiras do Sul, some with serious injuries and others without information from the health situation.
54754d5f3792ce442fc232278226d2b964548e06: Ana Lúcia Puruborá is an indigenous woman who lives in an urban area in Guajará-Mirim. She was diagnosed with depression and her son went to reside with her to assist in her health care, along with her wife, of the Makurap people, and her 4-year-old son. An acquaintance of Ana Lucia's son asked to spend a few days at her house in a room outside. However, the family had no knowledge that the boy had committed theft and was being sought out by the Civil Police. At the time of the robbery, the cops picked him up, and they were on their way to the hospital to perform a body crime test, when the boy took one of the cops' gun and ran away, making them angry. One morning, with only Mrs. Ana Lucia and her four - year - old grandson at home, the police entered the residence violently and struck the wanted boy and also Mrs. Ana Lúcia, claiming she was hiding a criminal in her house. She explained that she knew nothing, tried to call for help on her cell phone, but the cops pulled the device out of her hand and continued to assault her and kick her in front of the child. Cops ransacked the whole house, broke things and furniture, and there were blood marks all over the house. The cops took the boy and even Mrs. Ana Lucia, handcuffed. Mrs. Ana Lucia's depression worsened, as did her physical condition; she had problems with her ribs and had to undergo surgery. The Public Defender was triggered and the lawsuit against the police is underway.
134099f25846739ba97696a0d5b81a9ba17c8d68: The indigenous people of Macuxi were hit by a vehicle in the neighborhood Jockey Clube, in Boa Vista (RR). According to witnesses, the driver fled the scene without any help. The Samu was triggered and provided first aid to the indigenous, who was taken to the Emergency Room Francisco Elesbon. There's no information that the police and DMV have been triggered.
e8d659baf27aff0ff6dcbd9f353e791a09e36ef4: A 7-year-old Yanomami boy was hit by a vehicle while trying to cross the Glaycon de Paiva Avenue in the São Vicente neighborhood in Boa Vista. The perpetrator of the hit-and-run was a 65-year-old man, civil servant. He informed the police that he was following the avenue towards the neighborhood-center when a group of indigenous people crossed the street and the child was left behind. He also said the child ran through and was hit by his vehicle. The driver fired Samu, who took the child to the Santo Antônio hospital, where she was attended. According to information, the child was “apparently stable”. The accident is being cleared up by the police.
698f4342de2dd638e95d847dfb11cc2517c9a9a6: On the night of November 1, 2021, in São Félix do Araguaia, Ixajuwedu, being drunk, stole a lady's purse. Passersmen saw what happened and ran after Ixajwedu, caught up with him and beat him. The PM arrested the Indian in flagrante. At the custody hearing, held the following day, Judge Ivan Lúcio Amarante constituted Matheus Roos as Ixajuwedu's Dative Lawyer. At this hearing, the judge made the arrest flagrant into pre-trial custody, and the D.A. lawyer demanded nothing. Engaged, the Human Rights Center Dom Pedro Casaldáliga and Cimi Regional Mato Grosso began to act together. They sought assistance from the Public Defender of São Félix do Araguaia. The defender was doing the procedures to take the case, when an indigenous, former chief of Santa Isabel do Morro Village, on behalf of the family, constituted the lawyer Marcos Antônio Miranda Sousa. He manifested himself in the case on November 5, but his petition was only answered on the 26th, when the indigenous received release order.
41df963e70504b22d5755acfab885d5f6196b9a9: Four houses of Fontoura indigenous village on Bananal Island were completely destroyed after a fire. The flames were controlled by the Indians themselves. According to Eliana Karajá, indigenous leadership belonging to the village Santa Isabel, the fire was set in a house after a crime of violence against women. The victim's son would have witnessed the assaults. “We heard that the son saw his father beat his mother and, to try to defend, burned down the house. With the strong wind, the fire spread to three more houses ", told. The injured indigenous woman was taken by a medical team to the hospital of São Félix do Araguaia (MT) with an eye injury. The four families that had their homes hit need help. The leadership states that cases of aggression to indigenous women have been frequent and do not see public interest in protecting these women.
62ef987381e33d508f4166952f78a14d5cf8a9bc: Since the beginning of vaccination in indigenous villages, false and prejudiced news has circulated among indigenous peoples, in order to make them give up vaccination, for fear of its effects. In addition to false news, campaigns are not being conducted with real information about the benefits of Covid-19 vaccine. There are several false information that have circulated, as in the village Tey Kue, in Caarapó (MS), where they say that the indigenous who are vaccinated against Covid-19 will become vampires. Other messages from WhatsApp say that whoever takes a vaccine dies in six months and that the indigenous are “cubaias”, so they are a priority group in the campaign to combat the pandemic. Many indigenous people repeat what they hear from religious fundamentalists – that it is the “mark of the beast” and that the syringe would contain a “liquid chip”. What is heard between the Guarani Kaiowá and Guarani Nhandeva, in Mato Grosso do Sul, are lies, which also reach the peoples of the Amazon and spread in the villages of Xingu. The strong wave of false news causes fear and resistance to vaccination in indigenous peoples throughout Brazil. Many indigenous people report that “if the president (of the Republic) says he will not take the vaccine, because he says he does not need it, why will I take it?” In addition to false news, they still face racist, aggressive and prejudiced messages, through WhatsApp, as one that circulated in the village Tey Kue: “Why do Indians have to be the first to vaccinate, if they have no use?” In an attempt to overcome this situation of misinformation and prejudice, Apib started the campaign “Vaccine, Parent!”, in which it publishes videos with leaders taking the vaccine and stimulating the attitude. Cimi and other organizations have also made campaigns and efforts in this sense, seeking to clarify the importance of vaccination to maintain life.
007f1991efbd82abcfd40f6989e7b6a9311d60de: A prejudiced statement was made by the artist Karol Conká, in a television program, broadcast by Rede Globo. Karol correlated with the colonization of indigenous peoples in Brazil, using a racist phrase: “They (indigenous) accept crumbs. They accept mirrors, hand over lands in exchange for mirrors”. The statement was criticized on social networks, including Ana Patté, an Apib member.
2499991e9d1c099e7392e37219b7dc02fca3e21a: Indigenous leaders who came from all regions of the country to manifest themselves in Brasilia against the anti-indigenous projects that they carry out in the National Congress and against measures of the federal government that weaken their rights were attacked on social networks by then Minister of the Environment, Ricardo Salles. In a post on the minister's account, which then had 344,000 followers, three pictures of indigenous people were released using or carrying cell phones during a demonstration in front of the MMA. One of the photos contained the text: “We received the visit of the iPhone tribe.” The photos have red circles to highlight the phones in the hands of the indigenous. As soon as the racist, prejudiced and discriminatory message was published, Mrs. Joênia Wapichana (Rede-RR) used her space in a virtual session of the House to repudiate the “chacota” made by the minister. The honourable Member said: “I want to say this, your minister: we can use any technology, we can take any position and any position and we will not stop being indigenous. We are aware of our rights and therefore we publicly state that it is the state's duty to defend indigenous peoples and their constitutional rights."
9a6c4d4ad14b28a0b2b5a6179161df497cc94044: The Huni Kui People's Federation of Acre (Fephac) entered a representation against the podcast hosts Underworld, and the MPF-AC opened a civil investigation for the crime of racism against indigenous people. In the complaint, the indigenous informed that the presenters would have made pejorative and racist offenses against the indigenous peoples in a video that circulated on the internet. In the recording, one of the presenters read a report about an indigenous man who was rescued after getting lost in the woods. Then another presenter, identified with Pedro Roi, says: “That’s why Bolsonaro speaks ill of the indigenous. The Indian has one job, he's born, he lives. His only job is to get to know the woods. Even that this bum could not do.” Maikon Jones, who also commented on the report, asks his friend not to call the Indian so and he repeats: “Slut. You don't know the forest is a bum. Strong opinions here. It is vagabond ", reinforces. Jones and Geovany Calegário start laughing. Maikon Jones says he uses it to send a hug to the indigenous peoples and groups of Acre. Then the humorist says: “I will prove that this Indian is nutella”. The indigenous reported that the video was circulating on the internet and that there were several comments also on the same line, but were removed from the air. Presenters already respond to another lawsuit for the crime of homophobia. According to the indigenous people, other people have also been offended and entered with representation. After the controversy and lawsuits in justice, the group of presenters decided to end the activities of the channel. The MPF gathered the material released in the press and launched the inquiry.
824b9b22cf8cfa3acd41ce65da61181ae002a7fc: After a visit by the President of the Republic to indigenous peoples in São Gabriel da Cachoeira (AM), the Federation of Indigenous Organizations of Rio Negro (Foirn) criticized the act of the agent, stating that he ignored the fight against Covid-19, illegal mining in indigenous lands and drug trafficking. Foirn stated that the president still invented an ethnic group by referring to the “People Balaio”, who “does not exist in Brazil and nowhere in the world”. In addition, the president did not wear a protective mask against the coronavirus, endangering everyone he met, who could in turn end up taking the virus to their communities. According to Marivelton Barroso, Baré leadership and Foirn president, “Bolsonaro once again ignores the problems and humiliates the Brazilian people. The president did not meet with the institutions that most helped fight the Covid-19 pandemic here in the region and did not even mention the fight against illegal mining, drug trafficking and other serious issues that plague indigenous lands here in the triple border region with Venezuela and Colombia.” And he said: “The contempt for our indigenous people is so much that the president did not even bother to know our diversity, creating a new ethnic group, that of the Balaio people, which does not exist in Brazil and nowhere in the world.”
