2f325425475666e8dfcdc9d98128bba84ddb1f68: A woman who was a pocketman invaded the camp of the indigenous mobilization in Brasilia and uttered insults, insults and pejorative and prejudiced words to young people who were on the scene, and still pretended that she was being attacked. In the video released on social networks one can hear her say on the phone that she is in the camp surrounded by “Indios with his dick in hand”. The woman is quickly corrected by everyone: “indigenous, indigenous”. Seeing a police car drive past the scene, she runs like she's being attacked. The Indians surround the car by calling it “racist”. The policeman is embraced by one of the indigenous and takes her from the scene. In the same context, allies of the Bolsonaro government have attacked the indigenous since the Supreme Court began the discussion on the demarcation of indigenous lands, in a trial that should bring a court position on the ruralist thesis of the “temporal mark”. An aide to the president, Carla Zambelli and a cousin of the Minister of Agriculture, Tereza Cristina, are some of those involved. Mosart Aragon, who works in the office of the agent, called the indigenous “maneuvering mass” on Twitter. He says the pocketmen were attacked. She also accused indigenous peoples of attacking police officers. “CUT, sickle & hammer and much iPhone marked the ‘protests’ of the ‘indigenous’ in Brasilia”, Zambelli published. Miriam Correa, cousin of the Minister of Agriculture, used the same kind of comment to attack them: “They are indigenous militants. Indian asphalt nutella class” (sic).
f41f7706cb84aae37cc91de8fb2d2164eb9970b9: Verbal aggression and simulation of aggression; prejudiced manifestations in social networks
1cfe961db95f1eaa5c621c6f528a95df96546495: After an episode in the Antero Center Village, in which the indigenous expelled employees from an energy company who were accompanied by armed jagunços trying to implement power lines within the IT, the actions of racism and ethnic-cultural discrimination against the indigenous increased. The population living in the villages and neighboring settlements, which already showed prejudice against the indigenous, began to intensify this behavior.
8e57f0a0fa48201b8b0b36bebaff00b123a499c3: On December 16, 2021, the popular communicator Djalma Guajajara was the victim of racism at a fair in which she participated. A couple of non-Indians used swearing to refer to indigenous paintings and accused the native peoples of committing “land invasions”. Even with the presence of security at the event, which occurred in public square, nothing was done to contain the aggressors.
0bc4301f56427f279d0c65d8419dcb1158c319d2: An OMG missionary waited his turn in line for the cashier of a supermarket in the city of Campinápolis to pay for his purchases. There were three Xavantes in front of you. It was then that, in an act of discrimination and prejudice of the supermarket attendant against the Xavante people, the missionary was called to pass in front of the indigenous people. He refused and said he would wait normally his turn. This episode portrays, in a micro space, the harsh reality of discrimination, racism and prejudice faced during the day not only by the Xavante, but by the indigenous peoples throughout Brazil.
654a04ff25203beaf2b01f46a4d93490385f64ef: According to Apib's complaint in January, even with the increase in cases of Covid-19 in Mato Grosso do Sul, 17 indigenous health professionals were dismissed. Apib classified the situation as “a case of institutional racism, because the professionals dismissed are mainly indigenous who work in indigenous health”. Among the hang-ups is Nurse Indianara Kaiowá, who was the technical coordinator of the Golden Base Pole and was on the front line against the pandemic, attending indigenous people infected by the coronavirus. According to reports from Apib, there is a conflict between health professionals and Dsei-MS coordinator Joe Saccenti Júnior, colonel who was appointed by the Ministry of Health for the post in September 2020. Indigenous people report that “any indigenous health professional who comments or questions the decisions made by Dsei receives warning or resignation”. In the complaint, Apib highlighted that the professionals followed in the fight against coronavirus almost independently, because the Casai (House of Indigenous Health) of the region remained without official leadership during a period of the pandemic.
ad1eff9963ee9b18206f8f15ded06bfd68532576: Due to a series of racist and discriminatory attacks on indigenous people vaccinated against Covid-19, which occurred in several locations in the country, the MPF decided to open investigation to investigate the crimes. There are several attacks that have been suffered against the indigenous, especially on social networks. In one publication, a person comments: “That’s right, immunize this pest that produces nothing... Band of cachaceiro”. In another comment, another person stated: “I find that absurd. For us who go out every day to work and produce, pay taxes, we have to be the last in line. Now, Indian and bandit who only spend money have to be the first. This is Brazil!” On another occasion, an entrepreneur from Dourados (MS) published on social networks a complaint about closed academies due to the Covid-19 pandemic, but with a photo of indigenous people to talk about the spread of the virus in the municipality. In the publication, she reported: “Academias are places of Covid-19 proliferation and need to be closed so that people get their immunities very low. However, these people can walk without a mask and if I am not mistaken, the village was full of Covid-19”. According to the MPF, “the repetition of the argument that ‘Indian only gives expense, does not work, does not produce and does not pay tax’ encourages discrimination and ethnic prejudice against indigenous peoples. Freedom of expression does not shelter the discourse of hatred and intolerance, nor ethnic prejudice and the perpetuation of stereotypes”. In all cases, the MPF investigates hate discourses through the practice of racism, a crime typified in the Brazilian penal code.
2f278f87790621e300eccf021fa6eca6e2892222: Álvaro de Azevedo Gonzaga is indigenous, grandson of Miguel da Costa Kaiowá and professor, and was attacked by hackers during public presentation of the results of his postdoctoral research on indigenous decolonialism, conducted at the Federal University of Grande Dourados (UFGD). The UFGD virtual room was invaded by about 20 profiles and the teacher's speech interrupted by hymns, songs, screams, verbal aggressions and death threats, accompanied by repeated messages from “Bolsonaro 2022”, before being overthrown. The teacher lamented the attacks and positioned himself firmly, in the name of his ancestry, not silent before people who, according to him, use totalitarian instruments to intimidate those who fight for democracy. He evaluates that attacks cannot be thought of in the field of individuality, as they seek to delegitimize a set of voices that have in resistance their strategy of existence.
bbf500fd7ef62b019a64d62f8a0aaefb78ee750e: The PM was activated to move to a pizza place on 11th July street in Maracaju (MS) to contain a 32-year-old woman who was offending indigenous people who were on site. The woman was sitting in the middle of a group of people and said at all times that “the place of bugre is in the village”. Upon seeing the discriminatory offenses, the police asked her to withdraw from the scene, which was not answered. With the negative, the police arrested her and led her to the Civil Police station for appropriate measures.
9e0bf0220b918c3b1d3394a65784dc27d15bc896: Prayers of the indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá people are threatened and insulted by people linked to evangelical churches. Violence has the support of a kind of militia and the “captain” who works in the village Amambai. The traditional medicine house of Kunhã Yvoty dona Lúcia, in the village Amambai, in Mato Grosso do Sul, is a place of prayer and healing. Built from an action of the Kunhangue Aty Guasu (Grand Assembly of Women Guarani and Kaiowá), the space is a demonstration of recognition to the work of midwife and praying lady Lucia. The ñandesy (reveiras) cultivate the herbs in their tekoha, and in the house are made the healing dances. In addition to preserving the tradition of her people, Miss Lucia has denounced the institutional racism and religious intolerance present in the region. And it is precisely for playing this role in her community that Lucia suffers persecution of evangelical people, including family members. The relationship began to be troubled from 2008, when Lucia decided to stop attending the evangelical church, which did not accept traditional Kaiowá practices. The verbal aggressions and attempts to prevent the performance of the ñandesy in the village have intensified since then. According to reports, violence has the support of a kind of militia that acts as “guard” within the villages and that would work together with the figure of the “captain”. On August 8, 2021, new attacks were made by members of the militia and evangelical leaders of the community, who accused the prayers of witchcraft and witchcraft. At the time of the threats, Lucia was singing, praying, and was intimidated by the current “captain” and by a brother-in-law, who promised to return with more people to stop her prayer. Scared, she asked for help from WhatsApp and, with that, mobilized enough people to avoid some more serious situation. However, the threat still persisted.
cf342d62f98c460a7e05adcb219a3ed6b605be2e: A family of indigenous Avá-Guarani went to the headquarters of the Centro de Referência de Assistência Social (CRAS) of Santa Helena to request a basic basket. The CRAS employee treated them with disrespect and prejudice, saying: “Here there is no food for Indian, Indian has to work to eat”. Leadership went to the MPF to report the case. Chief Fernando Lopes, in a document delivered to the organ, complained of the humiliation that this and other families pass to get basic basket of CRAS. The chief said that if they need to order food it is because they do not yet have their land demarcated.
d5b717fc72a878bbfcdaddd49cfc4ad3f61e7f41: Verbal aggression; racism; denial of assistance
7521b3bed6754754ebf8c669a73b65d1cbb9e723: Chief Oscar reported that the Guarani children who study at the João Lorini municipal school were forbidden to speak in the Guarani language by the director and a teacher of that school during the break. The principal and the teacher were afraid that they were speaking ill of the teachers. Chief Oscar went to school to make a complaint, and there they said he could only make the complaint on the day of the parent-teacher meeting. Meanwhile, the children were forbidden to speak in Guarani. Report of the suit was made to the MPF.
bddfed8793cbf398232d728101846d04ef94cf67: Denial of the right to speak the mother tongue
3295cbc50a01abb0cb69c539e660d97db037d07c: When they learned that the city of Campo Mourão (PR) destined a “Terreno de Passagem” in the vicinity of the Araucaria Garden for the Kaingang of Manoel Ribas, who went to the city to sell their crafts, the residents of the neighborhood mobilized against the decision. The people who live in the Araucaria, Botânico I and II gardens, Gutierrez, Casali and Laura, in Campo Mourão, started a petition, with the aim of collecting signatures from residents contrary to the presence of indigenous people in the place, which is close to the Imape headquarters, in the Araucária neighborhood. According to representatives of the Association of Residents of the neighborhood, the document would be forwarded to the Legislative, Executive and Judiciary powers. By mid-May, more than 170 people had already signed the document. In the online petition, the residents declare that they are contrary to the installation of the “Terreno de Passagem” in the neighborhood, claiming “the disorders that the indigenous people caused elsewhere in the city”. “During the last few years we have followed several articles in the press, testimony from residents near the place where the indigenous people were and always said the same thing: they cause disturbances in the neighborhood. Hygiene conditions are always precarious and this hinders the progress and order of the neighborhood ", says the document.
ce51883b7ca29f9d10a96581e12d1ef212e79b8b: Through his work as a photographer, Ubiratan Suruí, who was born in the early 1990s, reports how neopentecostal evangelical missionaries influenced and transformed the original way of living of the Paiter Suruí people. Ubiratan reports that he lived in the village until he was 16 years old and had less contact with the rituals and traditions of his people than he would have liked, because along with the expeditions of sertanists who made the first contacts with So Suruí, foreign evangelical missionaries also arrived, most Protestant Christian countries. Since then, most indigenous people are evangelical, and much of the traditional Suruí culture has been lost. The people changed their way of life, traditions and customs, their clothes, food and drinks, and even the figure of the shaman in the village was “demonized”. According to Ubiratan, “since contact with the whites, the evangelical missionaries have come and converted much of our people. From then on, the church never left I.T. Seven of September, beginning to dominate our culture, our beliefs and even the way we understand the fate of our souls after death. Now, parents almost force their children to go to churches early, because they believe that this is the only way to salvation.”
38b6085b622b0d267edd444c34a7273064413d76: Imposition of non-indigenous customs and religion
c35014bd5726c98713ad8026c432e117e8b74943: Gisele Vaincan Pott, indigenous Xokleng who has been living for five years in the municipality of Blumenau (SC), in urban area, gave birth to a girl. Her wish was to honor her deceased grandmother by naming the girl Larissa Tando Pott. Even though he reported the indigenous origin, the second name, Tando, did not enter the child's certificate. The legislation obliges all notaries of the country to register indigenous names, but there are notaries that, due to the lack of proximity to the theme, end up blocking the right of these parents. According to Gisele, there are still cases of indigenous people who give up registering their children with indigenous names, when they are faced with negatives from clerks. She still relates: “My father’s name is Helmut. It's German, not Indian. So you mean German can (be registered), Indian no? We're all the same. For me it was prejudice”. Gisele made a police report and the case came to the MPF, which is making arrangements.
1c8516f1b4b556926adbc06afb8e0f78c7e815e1: The Icatu village has 169 indigenous inhabitants, from Terena, Kaingang and Guarani Nhandeva. In November, five of them tested positive for Covid-19. By proportion, the State Health Department considered it an outbreak. The situation was reported by local Globo TV. The population of the village was then discriminated against in the city of Braúna. The indigenous people were prevented from entering markets and pharmacies in the city.
6319fd3abcb795867a34cc2354ab10b7c6a65de7: On November 23, 2021, in a meeting at Dsei Araguaia, in São Félix do Araguaia, the Councillor of Condisi, Luiz Flávio Juanahu Karajá, questioned the Dsei coordinator regarding resources sent by the Union to be applied in favor of indigenous health. Faced with the inquiry, Ronalde de Barros Ramos, a retired Navy military officer and Dsei coordinator, began to speak insulting words against Juanahu and the indigenous people Iny Karajá, with the following words: “You don’t know shit. Nothing. You don't even know how to work. A lot of land, nobody produces anything. They just want to live on the misery of the people, the government. You gotta be ashamed of yourself and work. That's what you have to do. Learn to work with ‘tori’, (in reference to non-indigenous). That's what you have to learn. We have to learn, because I'm an Indian too. I'm an Indian, you know that. I'm half-breed. And I learned to work. I don't even have to work anymore, I'm retired, I earn $12,000 from the Navy. And I have two more rented houses. I work day and night, when I get out of here I'll work outside. That's what you, our people, have to learn to do, is work. Which we don't. 500 years ago, we were discovered and we could not work, learn from ‘tori’ (not indigenous) to produce. You weren't supposed to need indigenous health, government health, our people were supposed to be millionaires for the land we have. What we lack is willingness to work, that is what is missing for our people. He has to play on our side.” The indigenous protested in front of the Dsei Araguaia headquarters on November 27, 2021, in repudiation of the racist and prejudiced attitudes of the Dsei coordinator. Condisi, by way of office, reported what happened to the Special Secretary of Indigenous Health, asking for measures.
89b43149ff909c6bca99e394d14f1148c478d7a8: The victim is the leader of the people Madijá/Kulina and fights in the municipality the retention of bank cards from their people by traders. Upon returning from the March of Women, which took place in Brasilia in September, the leadership took advantage that there were many indigenous peoples of its people and met with them in the square, using a screen, in order to pass on what had experienced in the National Mobilization Struggle for Life and in the March of Indigenous Women. He spoke of the struggle for the maintenance of rights and directed the people not to deliver their card to third parties. The next day, around 7:00 p.m., when she was returning from college to her home, she was chased by a black truck that tried to run her over, tossing her car on the sidewalk she was walking through; only it didn't hit her because the indigenous woman was quick and threw herself on the porch of a house. No occurrence was recorded because the indigenous woman could not see the driver or note the license plate; frightened, she is no longer walking alone.
ab43ca57af9a1b77eae819fba77bb075e61b6e91: Francisco Gonçalves, 66 years old, is chief general of TI Camicuã. In recent years, criminal factions have enticed people from their people to drug trafficking and spread. As a leader, Francisco has made complaints, asked for help from the government and forbidden entry into his community of non-indigenous people. On 27 September, leaving a meeting, Francis was approached by two men who claimed that if the chief forbade the entry of people from the city into his land, he also had no right to transit through the city of Boca do Acre. The two men followed the chief and two other indigenous young people who were with him (Henrique Gonçalves, 23 years old and Andrade Carlos, 25 years old) to the port, where they sought to cross the river and reach their community. That's when, in an act of cowardice, using a knife, they attacked the chief's life. The two young people in the community, who were with the chief, in an attempt to defend him, were also injured. Report of occurrence and complaint to the MPF and the MPE was recorded, but so far, there has been no provision.
f64235dc729545f36e7d9966d490c3ece2009bd1: A farmer who has been threatening the indigenous community for years invaded, on October 20, 2021, the area of which he is supposed to own, in order to follow up the allotment he has made. Addressed by Leaders Pataxó, the farmer tried to run over the chief, Ricardo, and then fled. When searching the police station to report the invasion and attempted murder, the leaders of Pataxó were not assisted and learned that the same farmer had just reported them for alleged assault. On the day of the attempt to run over Chief Ricardo, the reinstatement of possession proposed by the farmer had already been suspended by decision of the Supreme Court, given the violence that the Pataxó people have suffered during the pandemic.
7dd80702506e425563daeb762b6778989b2cfb72: Aty Guasu leaders reported to the MPF of Ponta Porã reporting that Jagunços da Fazenda Querência in Aral Moreira (MS) tortured a group of indigenous people. According to Aty Guasu, some of them went deaf due to shots fired near their ears. The leaders reported that the indigenous were approached by armed men who jumped from a truck inside the indigenous area, which is claimed by the Guarani-Kaiowá and awaits regularization by the federal government. In the complaint, Aty Guasu reported that the Jagunços shouted: “You are going to die today”, and that “the indigenous, after being tortured and well-blooded, managed to escape and flee the place”. The MPF activated the Civil and Military Police and requested Funai's participation in investigations and solution of the problem.
de8b6f0d09699c5259493578d98d91e2101d9440: A 27 - year - old Indian was arrested in Dourados after assaulting his own 78 - year - old mother at machetes. The victim was rescued in a health unit. PM teams and Samu were activated to attend an occurrence of injured persons at the UPA. It was found that the elderly woman had wounds from machete blows to the chin and hands. Elson, the elder's son, was appointed by witnesses as the author of the coups. He was found near the old woman's house in the village Bororó, and taken to the police station.
9761ac8688cb8f8bb803f26e92ba6d5c3c9f7d44: The indigenous Silvana Almeida suffered an attempt at feminicide by her former neighbor. Reports show that Silvana witnessed the aggressions against her neighbor, Ana Paula, by her ex-husband, and went to try to defend her. The man assaulted her violently, and only did not consume feminicide because Silvana was rescued. The case occurred at TI Pirakuá in Bela Vista (MS).
2412c10ba78524d23f1cf3df44ed18b91f5aa2b5: The 30-year-old indigenous Mayone de Souza was violently assaulted by her ex-husband in an attempt at feminicide. She is a resident of the village Jaguapiré, in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, and was at home when her ex-husband arrived, on a bicycle, and stabbed her three times, then fleeing. Her ex-husband is 35 and still on the run. Mayone was rescued and taken to Life Hospital, but there is no information on her condition. The police are investigating the case and looking for the attacker.
9602e538b83f53e5eb247db5aa0424c9c3877cf4: A 21-year-old Indian was shot by his own brother during a fight in the village of Jaguapirú in the Dourados Reserve. According to the police report, the 33-year-old shooter was fighting with his sister when the other brother, 21 years old, in order to defend her, entered the middle. The assault didn't end until the father of the three involved arrived and separated the fight. The young man then walked out of the place and was shot in the leg. He was referred to the Emergency Care Unit (UPA) and later to the Hospital of Life.
b042d0cfb7aa43fcd0d8fdc9620c527b5fda4ff7: A 31-year-old indigenous was buried alive in Iguatemi, Mato Grosso do Sul. He managed to escape after the three attackers left him in a shallow grave believing they had killed the victim. The crime occurred after a fight between the Indian and the three men. They worked at a place in the rural area of Iguatemi when there was disagreement. The indigenous man reported: “It was night, I don’t remember anything, but when I went to see the guy kicked me and knocked me down. Then they were in three, beat me, then took me there, buried still there, said I had died and returned to the place running, at night”. The victim told us that he managed to get out of the grave on his own, even though he was stabbed. According to the Indian, two attackers held him while a third used a knife to cut his neck. The Indian spent the night hiding and the next morning he returned to where he worked. He reported what happened to the landowner, who called the ambulance. The case is being investigated by the Mato Grosso do Sul Civil Police.
ad1648ddf908f85e931c924503db903cba85ed5a: Physical assault, use of a gun and burial alive
96bca00a0b0cf5c9c8da30e5f5fcb5338b5e9a22: A 21-year-old indigenous girl lived moments of terror in Ponta Porã (MS). After being beaten with punches and kicks, she was stabbed and raped by two neighbors. Without being able to ask for help, the victim was only rescued the next morning when family members found her at home. The case was registered as a collective rape and attempted feminicide, and took place in Sanga Puitã district. She was rescued and taken with serious injuries to the city's Regional Hospital. The men were arrested red-handed and taken to the police station.
c4e05e2b9adb330793f172711f22b9daea19815c: Collective rape; white weapon; attempted feminicide
4297134692d13d16597fc08fae8a54f0431f369c: A 44-year-old Indian attempted to assassinate his 41-year-old wife with axe blows to the head in the village Jaguapirú, in the Dourados Indian reserve. There are reports that the husband arrived drunk the night of September 25, had an argument with his wife and assaulted her. The indigenous woman went to the family home and returned to her home the next morning. However, the indigenous, knowing of his return, took an axe and struck a blow to the wife's head, who fell to the ground and needed to be rescued by the Samu, who sent her to the hospital. The PM responded to the incident and led the man to the Dourados police station.
c7d6a1ddf459741026d0b9bbdf059166526528d5: On February 25, a boat with eight prospectors docked in the Helepi indigenous community, in the Uraricoera River region, in the Yanomami IT. The prospectors asked for an indigenous Xirixana (as are known the Yanomami of the region). When he found the Indian, the prospector shot him with a gun. The indigenous was wounded, but was helped by the community while waiting for the arrival of a health team. The victim's younger brother, angry, reached the bow and arrow and arched the prospector, who died. From this fact, the Helepi community was threatened by other groups of prospectors. This is another episode of violence caused by the mining invasion of the Yanomami IT, a territory divided between the states of Amazonas and Roraima and where indigenous Yanomami, Ye’kwana and indigenous groups in voluntary isolation live. The Helepi community is the first from the outside limit of IT and, therefore, “all river logistics to supply the mining centers of the region (and, consequently, the prospectors who circulate in it) necessarily passes through it, generating immense environmental and social impacts. According to a document released by Hutukara Association Yanomami (HAY), “the episode of conflict now denounced should not be understood alone. This reflects the serious situation of illegal mining in TIY, and adds to other recent events, which point to an escalation of tension between indigenous communities and prospectors in the TIY countryside.” The indigenous organization demanded that the authorities involved in the episode be identified and punished, and that the free flow of indigenous peoples in the region be guaranteed, now dominated by the invaders. HAY's letter-denunciation was addressed to PF's oversight in Roraima, the MPF-RR and the Yanomami Etnoenvironmental Protection Front of Funai.
6e57a8284bcfacd62f792623ad2357b3066e81ab: On November 15, 2020, a 23-year-old pregnant Xavante, wife of a 21-year-old Xavante, was sexually harassed by a non-indigenous man from Campinápolis. As it was election day, the man offered her a ride on a motorcycle to the school, the place of the vote; however, on the way she realized that he was going out of town, towards a forest, on a nearby farm. Realizing the danger, when they were leaving the asphalt, still inside the city, the young girl jumped off the bike, hurting herself in various parts of the body. One of his uncles saw the whole fall scene, because he was standing on his bike, talking on his cell phone. He recognized the assailant, but preferred to help his niece rather than pursue him. On November 15 and 17, 2020, the couple recorded police reports, but the case did not end in an investigation or punishment of the aggressor. On March 17, 2021, a Salesian missionary took the young woman's uncle (who, at the time, saw her jump off the bike to escape) to give testimony, accompanied by her father. However, the Civil Police clerk stopped recording two facts of paramount importance for the evidence of the crime, and the uncle signed it without reading its content. The missionaries, when reading the copy of the testimony, realized the omission of the facts. On March 19, a Salesian missionary sought out the young uncle in Campinápolis, who claimed to remember clearly that he had reported the facts to the police clerk. He and the missionary then returned to the police station. The clerk apologized, saying that the witness had not spoken the two facts. But at the insistence of the missionary and the young man, the scribe agreed to make a supplement in the testimony of the 17th, which, after being read, was signed. After this complementation, the indigenous family awaits the position of the delegate, who will or will not offer a complaint to the local prosecutor.
2b95dcd970f779c8327bd0d4575c117033428f78: Civil Police are conducting searches to find an elderly person suspected of raping and impregnation a 13-year-old indigenous teenager in Oiapoque, in the northern end of Amapá, on the French Guiana border. There is information that the
7ad0f450f0839f8840ac5c91ccc5e626108ff91b: The case of a 14-year-old indigenous adolescent who was raped by her uncle in 2020 arrived at the Guardian Council (CT). The child was born in July 2020, but the case only came later to the Guardianship Council through complaint. Engaged, the Civil Police did the investigations and requested the arrest of the uncle, which was denied by the Justice. The determination was a protective measure to keep the abuser away from the adolescent. The CT reported that it forwarded the situation to all the competent bodies and that it knew that the protective measure was being disregarded through the press. Thus, on February 18, 2021, the girl and her baby were taken to a reception unit, under the responsibility of the State. For the CT, the right of the children would be protected “by staying under the care of the grandmother, being granted protection measure through the Maria da Penha Law, in which the aggressor would be prevented from maintaining contact”. Faced with the non-compliance of the measure, the Guardianship Council removed the adolescent in an emergency way from family life. It is worth noting that the girl got pregnant at 14 and, in 2021, was 15. The abuses occurred while she lived with her aunt, wife of the abuser and sister of the adolescent's mother, who is already deceased.
fe49fc615991f5f6a6d0b064d9d260c54e28f92d: A 31-year-old man was caught red-handed trying to sexually abuse a 6-year-old indigenous child in a village in Sidrolândia (MS). According to the father's report to the police, he was drinking at a friend's house when he caught him leaving the room where his daughter was sleeping. At that moment, your daughter ran out of the room and hugged her father's legs. In tears, the child said: “He entered the room and lowered my shorts to the knee”. The father struggled with the author, who suffered minor injuries and was immobilized until the arrival of the Military Police.
05751feac3ad5677b7466ca30623f092f011c28b: During the carnival holiday, a 14 - year - old teenager was sexually abused by her uncle. The girl reported to her mother that she was experiencing severe pain in her private parts and reported acts that her uncle did to her, causing pain in the region. The uncle had been living for about four years at the home of his sister, the adolescent's mother. Since the episode occurred, the man has fled and is missing. The family filed a police report and began to investigate the case and look for the accused.
4df72306113afabcccb936812fb8bf902a83097e: A 100-year-old woman was raped in an indigenous community in Amambai (MS). The indigenous woman, who is visually impaired, told the police that this would not be the first time that the 41-year-old perpetrator would have committed abuse against her. According to the testimony of the victim and family members, the elderly woman, who lives with her children in the back of the residence, would have screamed for help, when the daughter and other relatives spotted the suspect fleeing and went to rescue her. The police were fired and the suspect was arrested red-handed. The victim went through a misdemeanor. The investigation continues in secrecy, being cleared by the Amambai Civil Police Station. The assailant must answer for vulnerable rape.
c72304b8f92cfde441e64cf7b426f0b393b70825: On October 1, an indigenous child of only 3 years old disappeared from the village Amambai. She had been raped by two teenagers, 16 and 17 years old, who confessed to the crime. Upon finding her missing, her parents started looking for her, and half an hour later the girl was found by a health agent, who saw her crying a lot and unable to say anything. The child was wet and presented bleeding in the intimate region. Suspicious of rape, the health officer triggered the child's parents, who were taken to the hospital. The mother questioned the health agent about the situation and suspected rape, triggered the village leaders. Suspects were located and police engaged. After tests, the crime was confirmed. The adolescents had the socio-educational hospitalization decreed by the Justice of Mato Grosso do Sul.
3f40974d6c90df9ad8f31ac851e45ce886737824: The 11-year-old child Raíssa da Silva Cabreira, Guarani-Kaiowá, was found dead at the feet of a quarry disabled in the village Bororó. Civil Police technical expertise indicated that she was thrown from a height of about 20 meters after being sexually abused. She was found without clothes. The next day, five people confessed to the crime – three teenagers and two adults, including the girl's uncle. Based on confessional statements, the police reported that the teenagers and an adult planned to abuse the girl after getting her drunk and dragging her to the cliff, where the abuse occurred. There, they would have had to. Root drinking alcohol and practicing collective rape; the uncle of the victim would have arrived later and participated in the crime. Also according to the police, the accused would have reported that the girl screamed for help and fainted; by regaining consciousness and screaming again, the men decided to throw her off the cliff. The entire community was amazed at the brutality of crime, which had national repercussions. The adults have been arrested and will be indicted for the crimes of rape of vulnerable, feminicide and murder, and the adolescents apprehended will respond for infractions similar to the crimes of adults. The crime is added to the serious context of humanitarian crisis experienced within the Dourados Indigenous Reserve.
2be9b19769afa66c32d059779295e6c8a3cc5b70: The Guaíra Military Police was activated to provide support to municipal guards in an attempted rape. The Municipal Guard was passing the BR-272 highway when they spotted an Indian woman naked on public roads. At the scene, the victim informed the police that he was drinking alcohol in the village where he lives next to an acquaintance when they decided to go out and buy more drinks. On the way back, they took a ride and at one point, one of the men attacked the women, started taking off their clothes and tried to rape one of them. Faced with the situation, the victim kicked the author and ran away. The victim said he didn't know the perpetrators. The police contacted and informed Funai's representative about what happened and then triggered Samu, who forwarded the victim to the UPA to perform the medical procedures.
53af6ff1784b06104479a8feb02614c3e83234fb: The Civil Police investigates the case of an indigenous man from Mata Verde Bonita Village in Maricá (RJ), suspected of raping, pregnant his own daughter and participating in the death of the newborn baby. Her 21-year-old daughter reported the case at the police station, and claimed she was raped by her father since she was 13 years old. According to the police, the young woman reported to the village chief who suffered threats from the father and was forced to leave the newborn baby in a forest area. The baby was found by the village residents, taken to the hospital, but did not resist and died. The case was registered by the police as vulnerable rape; the man confessed to being the father of the child, but was not arrested because there was no flagrant.
61808c5ceb6df559fda881362a050d55cba18bd2: In August 2021, the body of Daiane Griá Sales, a 14-year-old Kaingang, was found in the Estiva Sector, Guarita IT, in the municipality of Redemptora (RS), northwest of the state. She lived in the Bananeiras Sector of TI Guarita, and was found in a plantation near a bush area, naked, and with the body parts from the waist down torn and torn. In October, the Public Prosecutor filed a complaint against a 33-year-old man accused of raping and asphyxiating young Kaingang. The man, who was arrested preventively, was accused of the crimes of rape of vulnerable and murder with six qualifiers (mean cruel, foolish motive, dissimulation, a resource that made it difficult to defend the victim, to ensure the concealment of another crime and feminicide). According to the prosecutor, Daiane would have accepted a ride from the man denounced and been conducted to the crime scene, an area close to a place where his family owned property – and therefore well known to him. “She was excessively drunk, unable to resist, raped, strangled and killed,” the prosecutor explains. The denunciation points out as a perverse reason the contempt of man for the original population Kaingang and its members, driven by the false idea that the community and the authorities would react passively to rape due to the fact that it is an indigenous. “The defendant was looking for his victim in events known to be frequented by indigenous young people, having even offered a ride to other girls of the same ethnic group,” the prosecutor points out. The Civil Police investigation concluded, from the autopsy report, that the tearing of the girl's body was caused by animals or birds of prey. There are reports of other cases of attacks against indigenous women and children that would be taking place in the region. With 23.4 thousand hectares, TI Guarita houses about 6,000 people and is the largest indigenous land in the state. Several factors have been identified as possible causes of such violence, such as the failure of the State, especially regarding public policies that favor the social protection of indigenous children and young people, as well as the increased presence of non-indigenous people within the community, generating insecurity and various threats to the population. The proliferation of hate speeches in the country, especially against indigenous peoples and against women, has also favored the increase in cases of violence and cruelty.
a0d4424eba67fcbc27a1fe43b565646d0b3e1a4a: The enormous pressure that mining exerts on communities has left a terrible trail of hunger, death and sexual exploitation of indigenous women. There are reports of situations where prospectors offer food in exchange for sex with indigenous adolescents; sometimes, they attract women with objects for this purpose. One of the strategies most used by prospectors is to give alcohol drink, a situation that leaves them vulnerable, having reports of abuse against women and children in various regions of the Yanomami IT in these circumstances. For most women, prospectors therefore pose a terrible threat. They are luxurious and violent, producing a climate of terror and permanent anguish in the villages. Another problem arising is Sexually Transmitted Infections, which are increasing in several villages. The presence of 20,000 prospectors in IT, according to HAY estimate, indicates the severity of the context and evidences the omission of the State to protect the indigenous.
a2dd7ae93e8bc30c7dab5c9231c9bdab7788f1c7: Complaint by indigenous peoples to the Hutukara Association reports that a prospector working in the Apiaú region offered drinks and drugs to the community and, when everyone was drunk and inert, raped one of the village's children.
5669f60d3013ba2fff1507f046629ef45ca31eb9: Rape and introduction of alcoholic beverages
0c9d284b727d4d8b8f538945ef5681ed2fe39355: According to the Yanomami account, in the publication “Yanomami under attack”, three young people of about 13 years would have died after being repeatedly raped by prospectors, after being forced to consume alcohol. These facts happened in 2020, but they didn't come out until the following year.
963b9a02d6a3093b3b6e2c7f35ae5b63a25cc823: In September 2020, the MP of Acre received a complaint that a family of indigenous Warao would be living in a “junk” in the municipality of Sena Madureira. The episode was also reported in the Cimi Violence Report - Data from 2020. At the time, the Municipal Department of Social Assistance reported that it was on site and did not find the family. The deadline for completion of the investigation of the case expired in March 2021. As it was not concluded, the MP-AC transformed the investigation procedure into a civil investigation. According to the MP, “the established facts deal with alleged violation of human rights, due to the permanence of a family of Indians housed in the lands of the municipal dump of Sena Madureira, the intervention of this ministerial body”. The MP-AC requested measures from Funai and the Municipal Secretary of Social Assistance.
01c8644a0f7a1ca136edd77af3ba36f87aae8663: To comply with a Supreme Court decision regarding ADPF 709, as a response by the federal government to the pandemic's impacts on indigenous peoples, a purchase of 1 million basic baskets was made, but with ultra-processed products. Coconut doughnuts, sugar and ground coffee are in the basic baskets that the federal government purchased for R $ 173 million and should distribute to 233 thousand indigenous families throughout the country for six months. Three indigenous health experts heard through the portal Uol considered the composition of the baskets a “schizophrenia”, “without sense” and improperly formed
e911634a6632fad7ac96f71f53a6e8aec3256c38: The failure of the government to indigenous peoples in Manaus during the pandemic of the coronavirus was stamped in all areas, not only in health. The pain of losses was added to the contempt of the authorities, which forced the indigenous peoples to create their own structures of help, even if precarious. According to communicator Samela Sateré Mawé, activist of the Association of Indigenous Women Sateré Mawé, many indigenous peoples of various peoples lost their lives, indigenous elders died without being able to even have a burial worthy of their culture. The Amazon was the first state to have confirmed infection among indigenous people, and concentrated the highest number of deaths. According to Coiab, by March 2021, 8.674 cases had been registered in the state, reaching 38 people. In Manaus, the Association of Indigenous Women Sateré Mawé lost the main source of income, which is the sale of handicrafts, right at the beginning of the sanitary crisis. Without money to buy food in the city and no information or assistance from the government, the helplessness remained. According to Sônia Sateré Mawé, coordinator of the association, families experienced difficulties: “I didn’t even have money to buy food, let alone mask or alcohol gel,” she recalls, saying that she and her husband took Covid-19. “Without medical attention, it was very difficult.” Through the design of a UK institution, which bought handicrafts and material to produce masks, even without ever having sewn, the women of the association learned the craft and donated the protective equipment for all of the community and other villages in Manaus and the interior Amazon, and still sold some for their livelihood. Without assistance due by the government, the indigenous had to mobilize. According to the communicator, "we indigenous people who live in the city, we are not assisted by Sesai, and during the collapse in Manaus hospitals, many relatives ended up dying and being buried in collective ditches. Organizations and fronts of help, such as the Indigenous Lives Campaigns Import and Breathe Amazon, created mutilations to try to help people who were dying suffocated. In the Tribe Park, indigenous neighborhood of Manaus, leaders like the chief Miqueias Kokama and the nursing technician Vanda Witoto managed, with the help of donations requested via social networks, support to assemble a small health structure, the Support Unit to Indigenous Peoples, which operates in the treatment of patients with covid-19 in Manaus and villages in the vicinity ".
df4e2f6487f3c79f7dd9b37890a59a4e18906c39: The Kariri-Xokó people live with failure in various areas by the State agencies, in particular, Sesai, Funai and Embasa. The people are in a situation of social vulnerability, with lack of water for consumption and planting, food insecurity, undemarcated territory, problems with Funai and the notary for the registration of children as indigenous. The people reported to the MPF of Paulo Afonso, where they conduct administrative procedures in relation to these demands. At a community meeting with the agencies involved and also with Sabeh and Cimi, some issues progressed, such as the difficulties imposed by the notary and Funai regarding the civil registration of indigenous children. The MPF was to publish a recommendation to Funai and the notaries on this issue.
808d8188caf5dba8c97c2d7cd919926aa8976ba1: The Tapeba indigenous people, located in Caucaia (CE), face failure by the state in several areas. The difficulties range from lack of education assistance to difficulties in relation to food security itself. In the report of the portal The People, João Kennedy Tapeba, president of the Association of Indigenous Teachers Tapeba, reported that the technological devices distributed by the state meet the demands of high school students, but the action does not reach the elementary school students, who are being affected by the lack of connectivity and provision of electronic devices. The classes of the state regular high school network began face-to-face at the beginning of August and those of municipal children's education would return hybridly in October. Schools also need reform and infrastructure for the safe face-to-face return of indigenous students. Another problem faced by the indigenous and aggravated during the pandemic is hunger. In many cases, school feeding was the only daily meal of students. The school receives basic baskets from the city and milk donation through the Mesa Brasil program, but are not enough to meet the various situations of extreme vulnerability.
9c6568a4201d2898595eedc984860f6f9f0821ab: The Xavante people, especially the village Paranoá, in Barra do Garças, have long suffered from food shortages. The situation worsened with the Covid-19 pandemic and many indigenous people are starving. The situation is worrying, especially when it involves children and elders, such as the 93 - year - old Heroin Rewanhiré leadership. Risking to be contaminated, she leaves the village to the city of Barra do Garças in search of donations. According to Ana Paula Xavante, who is a journalist and one of SOS coordinators Xavante, the demand of the people for food is a real necessity. With difficulties for production on the land itself, without incentive or public policy that guarantees food security, the indigenous have become dependent on donations of basic baskets that, even when they arrive, are not enough for all villages. Sometimes the hunger is so great that the food doesn't last a week. The location of the village Paranoá is one of the factors that complicate the situation; the village is one of the 58 of IT São Marcos, but it is isolated from the others, not reaching any sign of internet, nor in case they need to communicate in emergencies. Few indigenous people have some income such as retirement or government aid. With the pandemic, what was hard enough got even worse. With extreme gravity, the Xavantes began to call for help.
307e05b7f8116492157fdc4c01ef99a5e4d1a53b: Since February 2019, Salesian missionaries have been assisting in the follow-up to the retirement process of Frederico Ruwabzu Tserotomodzatse, aged 60, but, even with a judicial intervention by the Public Defender, he has been denied it, on the grounds that he has lost his right to Insurance. This was because of his lost skills and lack of social assistance. As of April 2020, under the guidance of the public defender of Campinápolis (MT), they began the search for the Benefit of Continuing Benefit (BPC), in the CRAS of that municipality. Four months were spent so that the CRAS employee could complete the Single Register of Frederico, the Federal Economic Bank (CEF) did not accept the indigenous surname of one of its granddaughters. It took three trips from the village of São Pedro to the city of Barra do Garças, a distance of 390 km each. With the Single Register ready, the Casai Social Worker of Campinápolis included him in the INSS system in February 2021. But, both in CRAS and Casai, the employees made mistakes: the CRAS employee included relatives who should not be in the Single Registry; and the CASAI employee did not mark a point that denied the existence of other positions or salaries received by Frederick. With this, in August 2021, the INSS answered asking for explanations from these misconceptions. The Salesian missionaries once again went to the village of St Peter and sought Frederick for the necessary procedures. The requirements were clarified and forwarded in the INSS system. Right now, we're waiting for the INSS response, which should mark forensics for another medical finding of your Parkinson's disease. In this short narrative there are several violence against Xavante: he was a professor of the state and the municipality, state pedagogical coordinator and director of state school for about 30 years, but, when affected by Parkinson's disease, in 2013, he received no guidance for the measures in view of his retirement. He says that he received the sickness aid only once, in 2016, in the amount of a minimum wage; to that end, the lack of vehicles to take him to government entities that asked for certificates, medical expertise, statements, etc.; the absence of the Funai of Campinápolis throughout the process; the refusal of the CEF to accept the surname of his granddaughter in the computer system; the lack of knowledge about the very service of the CRAS employee, who filled the Single Register with unnecessary names of relatives; and the lack of knowledge about the employee's own service of Casai, which included the Single Register of Frederick in the INSS system without marking the option that denied him to have other positions or that received some value.
681f67a7ad7d11d6b5fb9efa4ead943ac42d75d1: Gustavo, a Terena boy of only 8 years, is a dialysis patient with renal failure, and depends on having piped water at home to be discharged from the University Hospital. Between visits to and from the HU, since March he was hospitalized; he was already intubated due to complications of the disease. In addition to renal dysfunction, Gustavo also developed a cardiac picture of hypertension. Gustavo is in line for kidney transplantation, but, while not coming his turn, he needs to use the dialysis equipment at home, which is provided by SUS. For this, it is necessary to have drinking and piped water inside the house. HU employees are campaigning for donations from water boxes and a pump system.
2b4d6aca7828669ba05cd5bce10831c162781e2d: Lack of piped drinking water and sanitation
cd0a6908ffa22e194ed7508937c3443e7f0880ec: In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, the MPF/MS had to take public civil action against the Union as a matter of urgency, requesting within 72 hours the emergency supply of at least 40 litres of drinking water per person every day until the water supply was established permanently. There are about 489 indigenous families, with approximately 2,000 people, who face a situation of neglect by the government and suffer from the shortage of drinking water in the municipality of Antônio João. They are part of the 11 villages that Foto: Hellen Loures/Cimi Leadership Guarani-Kaiowá – one of the people most affected by the failure and omission of the State – in demonstration of the Camp Struggle for Life, in Brasilia, August 2021 make up the IT Ñande Ru Marangatu and resort to improvisation to get water, often searching in wells in the swamp or in polluted streams and rivers, without the minimum dignity and basic sanitation to which they are entitled. IT Ñande Ru was approved by presidential decree in 2005, but the STF suspended the effects of approval in the same year. While the process of approval still takes place, after more than 16 years, in February 2020 the STF determined the “maintenance of the factual situation of the current occupation”, that is, the maintenance of the indigenous occupation in an area that has already been demarcated. To justify its omission in the supply of water to the community, the DSEI Mato Grosso do Sul claims to be “impeded to operate in unmarked indigenous areas”. The MPF highlights, however, that the Union is required by law to ensure and promote access to water for indigenous populations, including those living in undemarcated lands.
2e031637382d4e548c46907fb3c65116615275b3: Completely desisted by the government, more than 2,500 families of indigenous Guarani-Kaiowá live in Dourados, under tents of canvas. The scenario of the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, which has not had housing programs for 13 years, is totally abandoned. Whole families are exposed to all kinds of weather, violation of rights and dismay. With the Covid-19 pandemic, the situation that was already very serious became even more chaotic. It is practically impossible to comply with minimum health care. They are people living in subhuman conditions, in precarious housing, with lack of food and basic sanitation and in a restricted area, which makes any possibility impossible for indigenous people to live well, according to their traditional ways of life. The humanitarian crisis situation has been denounced for years to the competent bodies, but nothing has been done and the reality experienced by these indigenous people only gets worse every year – a situation directly related to the indigenous struggle for land and the violence suffered by the Guarani and Kaiowá who fight for the demarcation of their lands in the region.
52a0057bb53782a7a8b61dbdc545bab55fb0812b: The Arara Azul and Esperança indigenous communities, located in Aquidauana (MS), have long suffered from the lack of drinking water. During the Covid-19 pandemic, the situation worsened even further, due to the even greater need for constant hygiene and hydration. It is necessary to drill and build artesian wells by the Sesai and the DSEI, which always denied this demand of the Terena people. A public civil action was brought by the MPF, which highlighted that in both areas of recovery, a recommendation had already been sent to the Sesai and the DSEI to adopt the necessary administrative measures for drilling the wells. The argument of the Sesai, the DSEI and the Union was that the land regulation of the areas was lacking, even though they were already in the process of demarcation. Thus, given the request for urgent protection of the MPF, the Federal Justice of Mato Grosso do Sul determined that the Union provide drinking water to the indigenous communities Arara Azul and Hope. The decision determined that the Union should make possible the daily delivery of 50 liters of water per person in both communities, both in areas of recovery, through trucks or delivery of gallons, and that perforations and constructions of artesian wells should be made in both communities to supply 65 litres of water per day, on average, per inhabitant. Water distribution network should also be installed with the drilling wells as its source. The decision reaffirmed the indigenous rights to their fundamental rights, even in a context of conflict and possessive dispute. In the decision of Justice, at the request of the MPF, the Union should also identify all indigenous villages, regularized or not, that do not have access to drinking water in the region of the municipalities of Anastácio, Aquidauana, Bandeirantes, Bodoquena, Bonito, Camapuã, Campo Grande, Corguinho, Two Brothers of Buriti, Figueirão, Jaraguari, Miranda, Nioaque, Paraíso das Águas, Porto Murtinho, Ribas do Rio Pardo, Rochedo, Sidrolândia and Terenos.
16c411a6a9ebba98d0eb8c45bc9c34b66940f082: The Jaguapiru indigenous village, located in the Dourados region of southern Brazil, is one of the most densely populated indigenous reserves in Brazil. At the end of December, the community that has approximately 17,000 inhabitants, held the election to chief. The new leader who will have four-year management will face the challenge of mediating actions to solve the lack of security, domestic, sexual and family violence, basic sanitation deficiency and indigenous problems with alcohol and drugs. For the elementary school teacher in the indigenous community, Cristiane Machado, it is impossible for the indigenous to live well, according to their traditional way of life, in space. “We are destitute of policies, not only of the security issue, but also of the health that is precarious. We have young teenagers who are not involved in socio-educational projects. It is a historically created confinement to shelter an ethnic group, but then new communities came. The village that is destroying itself. We believe there may be a prostitution network here”, he explained. Neglect and slowness in the regularization of indigenous lands and failure by the government are great challenges that have been denounced for decades, but that in recent years have been aggravated with great intensity; they are violence of all sorts experienced by indigenous populations in Mato Grosso do Sul.
d83251bf36fbd094756d9361e8e2c143c3233e7a: The Minister of Women, Family and Human Rights, Damares Alves, was in Dourados to discuss the increase in violence in indigenous villages, specifically gender, in relation to women and children. However, the newspaper Correio do Estado reports that “Damares fulfilled all public commitments, participated in the public hearing to strengthen the fight on the subject, but forgot the name of the victim and the main motivation of the visit, which was to go to the indigenous villages and in particular to Guarani Kaiowá - where there was the collective rape and death of the 11-year-old girl Raíssa”.
db4372e79d8dfdd552e1b51c2863026ebd1d1308: Xikrin leaders denounce the precarious state in which the Support House is located, located in Parauapebas. The Support House is a place of transit of indigenous people who wait for transfer to hospital units, or who recover from health care. About 60 indigenous people circulate in the house and denounce the state of abandonment of the property by the government and also the mining company It is worth noting that, in agreement with the Union, it should assist in complementing the primary responsibility of the State. The indigenous report that, by 2020, the city of Parauapebas (PA) maintained a nursing team on site, but due to the pandemic and the conditions of the house, the care was suspended. It's Sesai's responsibility.
3f3d21ff6f49c6b2934a4dcd0a030f49ec730fd0: The RMP reported to the STF that the absence of the Army in the operation to combat illegal mining occurred at Munduruku IT in May generated concrete damage. The Army pointed out lack of resources and abandoned the site two days before the operation in Jacareacanga (PA), a municipality where IT is located. There was serious conflict between police and prospectors, resulting in ten wounded and arson, practiced by prospectors, in the house of Maria Leusa Kaba, Munduruku leadership with a position contrary to the devastation of the indigenous territory by mining and mining practices. The STF has been activated to ensure security on site. Minister Luís Roberto Barroso ordered PF and PGR to provide information in the case. The operation against the prospectors in the Munduruku IT provided for the participation of the Army, which was responsible for logistical support, protection of the operational base to be mounted at the Jacareacanga aerodrome, as well as air displacements for access to areas of interest identified in preliminary surveys. Two days before the action, the Army left the operation under the argument of lack of resources to meet operational costs. The prosecutors working in the region informed the RMP that “the practical result of the withdrawal of logistical support from the Armed Forces to the Operation was the serious deficiency in maintaining order in Jacareaunga and within the Munduruku IT, which caused concrete damage to the Munduruku indigenous people, such as the invasion of the Tapajós village and burning the residence of the leadership Maria Leusa Cosme Kaba Munduruku, who was forced to leave his village, together with his relatives, to avoid the perpetration of new attacks.” The RMP also states that “another point of special attention, able to explain the situation of serious insecurity that occurred, was the premature withdrawal of all mobilized personnel, leaving to their own luck and with a serious risk of personal security the leaders who oppose illegal mining in indigenous lands.” The RMP also stated that leaking information from the action has damaged the operation and that there has been an increase in violence on the spot, with serious violations of indigenous rights.
e98977107c48519748a31ac1f1eaf734e033571c: The municipality of Garrafão do Norte, Pará, has long been using an area of TI Alto Rio Guamá as municipal garbage dump. Besides, the city is also burying waste at the scene. By the end of November 2021, the MPF had already recommended stopping the dump. The MPF made another request to the Federal Court to be determined that the city's mayor and mayor, Maria Edilma de Lima, are obliged to draw up a plan to remove garbage, which has caused environmental problems and damage to the health of the indigenous community.
b46249adba242c9ef251866017e53c0415a46c46: The indigenous people of the Apucaraninha IT complain about the lack of supply of drinking water from July 18. This was because, due to a fall in the electricity supply, the water pump that supplies the community burned. Maintenance of the water supply network is the responsibility of Sesai, who did not repair the equipment. It is important to remember that problems like this have been happening for a long time in the community; often the bomb burns after a drop in energy or heavy rain. The lack of drinking water supply is a problem that affects several communities in Paraná. Beyond IT Apucaraninha, at least two more communities Photo: Helen Loures/Cimi suffer from lack of water. Faxinal IT and the Rio das Cobras IT have been out of supply for months and the situation remains unresolved by Sesai.
0aa12bfc42ca6eb16ad3544ae7a455da5a237b78: An indigenous family was found in a situation of social vulnerability in Curitiba. The Fykag are Kaingang, one of the three indigenous peoples present in Paraná, besides the Guarani and the Xetá. They traveled almost 400 km from the Rio das Cobras IT, in New Laranjeiras, to the center of the capital, in order to sell the family handicrafts. But with the Indian Pass House (Capai) closed, the Fykag spent the nights under the Colorado Viaduct, next to the city bus station.
aa71b9c2c7a8777f5e6a09f18e21b3023a765fc1: On October 13, a windfall occurred in the region, leaving the indigenous community without electricity. On the same day, the community asked the Paranaense Electric Energy Company (Copel) to reconnect energy. Three days after the request, the company had not switched on the light, which harmed the water supply to the indigenous, due to the failure of the engine that supplies the community. The indigenous families had to drink the contaminated water from Lake Itaipu. In addition, they lost the meat of the school lunch due to the lack of functioning of the freezer. The community had to trigger the MPF to make arrangements. Only after the MPF triggered Copel turned the power back on.
d5a15419a78cbeeeca586d72f7b262d7662b99c2: Disadvantage in electric power supply; lack of water
504babc983323820b8ed23fd7cd7387b70de744b: A situation of extreme neglect and neglect of the government, which refers to a situation of discrimination against indigenous people, has occurred in the municipality of Dois Neighbours. The Protection Network for Children and Adolescents intensified campaigns related to indigenous children in the traffic lights of the municipality. The campaign highlights that children were exposed to danger when they were in the central beds or in the middle of the street. Some tracks were fixed in places where children usually ask for money, guiding drivers not to give alms. The president of the Municipal Council for the Rights of Children and Adolescents (CMDCA) and also of the Municipal Council for Social Assistance, Bruno Lima, stressed that the objective would be to guide the population. “We held several technical meetings with various municipal agencies and authorities to create a network of information and exchange of experiences with indigenous children. We launch this campaign by guiding the population not to give alms to these children, not to contribute money or anything of value. Our advice is to help with food, clothes or buying the crafts of adults.” The situation of vulnerability faced by indigenous peoples in Brazil, in this case the peoples of the south, is a reflection of the neglect, neglect and disrespect of their constitutional rights by the government, especially the regularization and protection of their original territories. If they had their rights guaranteed, indigenous populations would not need to go to other cities in search of food for their survival, work, health care, among others.
44e6b44bcf3f59b67a0349fc4bcce557bccef5ba: Eight indigenous families of various peoples living in the Maracanã Village were threatened with eviction in a pandemic situation. The area was reoccupied in 2016, in the vicinity of Maracanã stadium, in the north of Rio de Janeiro. The families were apprehensive due to a decision by the judge Alcides Martins of the TRF-2, determining on March 10 the subpoena of the state government to inform about “conditions necessary for the execution of the trial”, which, in practice, refers to the reintegration of possession in the context of a troubled judicial process. The indigenous people launched a lawyer, who filed a security warrant in the STJ requesting the annulment of the lawsuit filed by the government of the state of Rio de Janeiro against the indigenous peoples. According to his allegations, not all defendants were cited for knowledge of issues related to the action. In addition, Funai did not participate, although the case involved indigenous people.
604b282d09763c5444245b19c2cb8366d7678435: Indian eviction process in the pandemic
a6579b9dda7b6ab63091fadbfcfa6d17a4f3b392: For the second time in less than two months, amid the coronavirus pandemic, the Afro-Indian Reference Center of Rio Grande do Sul, located in the Baixa neighborhood of Porto Alegre, had the water supply cut off. The first cut took place on November 27, 2020 and the second, in the beginning of 2021, on January 5, when servants of the Municipal Department of Water and Sewage (DMAE), accompanied by vehicles of the Municipal Guard, removed the register from the front of the building that houses the Center, where 12 people currently live. The Reference Center operates in the Lower City and serves as a welcome for indigenous women artisans and children.
07cd45afdc52a69a32bdb2ad0a5c268b5d48c213: Kaingang and Guarani indigenous villages in Rio Great of the South went through complete failure, in the full health crisis that plagues the country. Hunger was one of the serious consequences of the pandemic for these indigenous populations, especially in 2021. Unable to sell their handicrafts, which is one of the survival forms of families, the lack of emergency assistance by the federal government and the lack of assistance from Funai generated a situation of extreme precariousness for indigenous people in Rio Grande do Sul. According to Deoclides de Paula, coordinator Kaingang of the State Council of Indigenous Peoples (CEPI), there was a “play of pushing” between federal, state and municipal governments, on the responsibility of helping indigenous peoples. With the lack of help and hunger, the risk is that the indigenous people leave the villages to try to sell handicrafts in the cities, exposing themselves to the coronavirus, and also that children and elderly people get sick or die of malnutrition. The same dramatic situation has occurred in the Guarani villages. According to the Guarani coordinator of the same Council, Claudio Acosta, they “have no support. The community is going through a lot of trouble, especially in the interior.” He reports that at the beginning of the pandemic there was more support, but it decreased over time. Funai helped with some food, but not enough. Some prefectures also helped, but with the change of governments in 2021, some failed to contribute. The situation was even worse for those who did not have access to the Bolsa-Family aid, since the benefit contributes to the purchase of food. According to Roberto Liebgott, coordinator of the South Regional Cimi, the need for social isolation, since the beginning of the pandemic, put the indigenous people in a situation of food vulnerability, who saw no alternative of how to face this crisis, since there was no government plan for this confrontation. The biggest responsibility for the serious situation is the federal government, due to errors and omissions committed throughout the pandemic. Another aggravating issue of this pitiful situation is the non-regularization of indigenous territories, which prevents them from guaranteeing their livelihood, producing their food and living with dignity, according to their traditional ways of life. The DPU entered with public civil action in the Federal Court of Porto Alegre, charging the federal and state governments to execute care policies in indigenous communities, especially nutritional ones.
6ea308c656cec24ba0059b5ccf6c304e949b557b: Indians Karipuna denounce the neglect of maintaining and opening the access road to the village Panorama, which leaves the community in a vulnerable situation, especially in the rainy season. During the Covid-19 pandemic, the indigenous people faced difficulties, because access by the Jaci-Paraná river is very distant, especially in cases of health emergency. Since 2017, the Karipuna have submitted requests to the DER-RO, which during the summer period meets the various lines of the district of União Bandeirantes and, for political reasons, do not meet and do not maintain roads in Karipuna territory. And yet with the aggravating fact that the only people who use the road are people linked to organized crime, for land-grilling and wood theft. Documents were sent by the indigenous peoples to the DER-RO and the MPF, charging for measures.
dfccbdb04b7625bec76f98b878c83f6ead8d7f37: The Guarasugwe people, since 2012, have been demanding that Funai issue the document Administrative Register of Indigenous Birth (RANI) of some people who do not have any type of document. Few indigenous people have managed to include the name of the people in civil documents. Some children and adolescents are having difficulty accessing their rights in health and education due to lack of documentation. The non-dispatch of documentation by Funai has prevented indigenous people from accessing and being registered in the Sesai system and ensuring specific and differentiated care, if occurred during vaccination against Covid-19. Many indigenous people were prevented from being vaccinated as a priority group. Despite numerous complaints filed at Funai in Brasília (DF), the situation of denial of this right remains. Documents of complaint and request of measures were filed by the indigenous peoples in the MPF and Funai.
23cd629a1e756f6498601c25b5b4036ad883dccf: Denial of ethnic registration; denial of access to vaccine
97bc5f628e12e38a5ab94bdb1f14254d92f63feb: A group of Yanomami families, among men, women and children, improvised camp with tarps and cardboard boxes in the center of Boa Vista, on one of the capital's busiest avenues, and are living in conditions of extreme vulnerability, asking for alms. They said they stayed there because they have nothing to eat. The city of Boa Vista informs that between April 30th and the beginning of June, it made at least three social approaches with the Yanomami, delivering protective masks and personal hygiene items, with guidance from social worker and interpreter of the Yanomami language, and stated that it would provide a basket of food complementation. Funai reported that indigenous people are “residents of the Xexena and Maimasi communities, and are in the city to draw social benefits and accompany family members in health care”. And yet, they were “indigenous of recent contact, so they do not usually stay in shelters, houses or somewhere that restricts locomotion”. The group belongs to the Yawari people, a subgroup of the Yanomami, and Funai reported that it would provide transportation for the group to return to IT. CIR lawyer Ivo Cipio Aureliano reported that since 2019 an investigation has been initiated in the MPF to investigate the numerous complaints of neglect and abandonment with indigenous people living in the city. For him, “it is not only the Yanomami people who are suffering, but society as a whole. This is a consequence of the omission of the government”. Another aggravating factor for indigenous communities is the presence of invaders in the Yanomami IT, the largest in the country; the region is a constant target of prospectors who seek illegal gold exploitation and thus degrade the forest, bring diseases to communities and cause violent conflicts.
6432b7a10319de285d37f3a88c605841ae4f7e80: Young indigenous Warao was arrested in 2019, accused of involvement in illicit border trafficking. Throughout this time, the indigenous family, which resides in shelters institutionalized by Operation Welcomed in Roraima, had no information about the situation of the young person in the process that runs in justice against him. In April 2021, after intervention of legal advice from the CIR and the Pastoral Care of the Diocese of Roraima, information was obtained that the judge decreed the sentence of conviction of more than eight years in prison, one of the highest sentences. The defense would not have claimed the possibility of benefits because it has no background or because of the condition of being an indigenous person. The DPU was activated to follow the case.
767d5f8edbe591950c8636c1897a4aa94697d8a6: Condemnation without clarification and information to the family
5810adaef7f51306dc273bf23802c774ab00b833: The Etnoenvironmental Protection Base (BAPE) located at the entrance of the Uraricoera River is disabled, leaving vulnerable indigenous people in that region, which is the most impacted of the Yanomami IT by illegal mining, for having the access facilitated by river. This region concentrates more than 45% of the total impacts mapped and also has larger camps and the most complex support structures for mining, with several beds, camps and corrutels. In 2017, the MPF filed an action requesting the reactivation of all BAPEs. The decision of the judge was in favour of reopening, but so far the Union has not fully complied with the judgment and the decision is still disabled.
601da04a80d8034d34c7f8e1c324fea975a9d883: At the time of attacks on the Palimiú community that took place from May 2021, leaders of the Yanomami IT filed a complaint to the MPF reporting several impacts caused by the mining to its productive system, in addition to the threats and violence that had been suffering. According to the leaders, before the invasion “fishing was good, hunting was good”, but not now. The river is contaminated and the hunt “has become bigger.” They described areas degraded by the activity, both on the riverbank and inside the forest, which were once part of the area of daily use and which can no longer be accessed by families. Thus, to hunt, fish and collect fruit, they need to move to more distant places, which has compromised the time available for other tasks.
428c9878040c34a5fa74720be29d68dfa994d204: Food insecurity; State omission in the fight against mining invasion
087b1bd773c9abf20702f5d6e0f8e0527e452734: A group of indigenous people, mostly Kaingang, from the west of Santa Catarina, Paraná and Rio Grande do Sul, occupied the bus terminal in Florianópolis (SC). They are pleading from the municipal power a dignified place, in addition to access to drinking water and electricity, for the commercialization of the handicrafts they produce to survive. According to the indigenous Jozileia Daniza Kaingang, who is co-vereador of Florianópolis and anthropologist, with the pandemic and the lack of assistance of the government, the group went through many difficulties in 2020, including lack of food. He reported that they have the need for sales, especially in this emergency period. The city claimed that they could not stay in the city, because they would not have the opportunity to organize reception in the pandemic, and that they were seeing the possibility of supporting them in the villages themselves, through the state government, so that they did not need to move to the capital to make the sales. Judge Marga Inge Barth Tessler, of the TRF-4, suspended the sentence of the 6th Federal Court of Florianópolis that determined adjustments in the terminal of the Sack of Lemons to receive indigenous in the summer. In the decision, the magistrate cited the pandemic and considered “the indigenous population most vulnerable to risks, and it is not prudent to encourage the journey or stay of indigenous people in Florianópolis”. Marga Tessler also stated that “the situation is exceptional in the face of the possibility of contamination of a whole population” and asked for “prudence and caution”.
2fc982c90e7dce88eb3fdcb5889dfdab2c5f4833: After the body of young Guarani Mbya Adriano Silva was found at the Billings Dam on January 12, at Tenondé Porã IT, he was taken to the IML of São Paulo. His mother went to the IML, ran the report and ID on the body. As Adriano's RG had been issued in the state of Paraná, the IML of São Paulo should request the typilloscopy expertise sector of the Paraná Identification Institute to confirm the identification of Adriano (digitais) and release the body for burial.
