This procedure was very time-consuming due to the lack of communication from the IML of São Paulo with Paraná, which only happened because Cimi missionaries made direct contact with the IML of Paraná and it was found that the one from São Paulo had not yet requested the correct sector data in Paraná. After several complaints in the official channels of the Civil Police of São Paulo, they contacted Cimi and, only on January 21, the body was released for burial – ten days after death.
e57fb0da5cd3221bf9a66922523db5871b02032c: The indigenous community of the village Pyaú have been suffering from the lack of drinking water supply in the village by the Basic Sanitation Company of the State of São Paulo (SaESP). The village consists of about 100 families, with approximately 500 indigenous Guarani Mbyá. Requests have already been made to Sesai and Sabesp, but there is no provision. In the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, indigenous people who already suffer all kinds of deprivations and difficulties still live with this further violation of a basic right, which is access to drinking water and sanitation. In addition to neglect in health care, the Guarani Mbya of this village have also faced risks due to the precariousness of electrical installations. There is no position of Funai on the distribution of internal electric energy of the village. There is no sizing of the distribution of electricity to the homes, which causes overheating of electrical wiring, breakers fall, lack of energy in the houses, short circuits and beginnings of fire in houses.
399facfb082ded2b21b2adf2c6a4dec23a9f392d: Lack of drinking water and sanitation; lack of energy
d08ceea3861de01c33ca9a764ba012d2d6af09c7: In 2016, based on the Joint Resolution of the CMNP/CNJ no 03/2012, which establishes standardization on the registration of the indigenous name, the Internal Affairs of the Court near the Tenonde Porã IT began to require that all requests for inclusion of ethnic name in birth certificate documents and general registration be carried out via legal action, generating an accumulation of more than 200 indigenous people who have been waiting since 2016 to include their ethnic name in their documents.
28bcc63ac79d822732e09d748412f7c9c914798a: The vicinal roads that link the city of Itacaja to the Krahô indigenous communities are in a precarious situation, damaging the locomotion of the indigenous people. A meeting was held with the MP-TO, Funai, indigenous representatives and representatives of the municipalities of Itacajá and Goiatins to make urgent arrangements.
47cf649cfdaf9e85eeb56889923dd84de57276fd: After numerous complaints about neglect in the area of indigenous education in the state of Acre, the MPF forwarded a recommendation to the State Department of Education, giving 15 days to present improvements in indigenous education. The improvements concern the infrastructure of schools, and the MPF still requests the school calendars and a list of schools that are in need. According to data from the Pro-Indian Commission, Acre has over 8,000 students and 621 indigenous teachers.
6ea0f47672e61042b6a25b9f09fd3eb4b089c136: Since 2014 there has been no continuity in the training of teachers who attend the indigenous teaching, or in the training processes of those who have already completed. In 2019, the governor determined not to hire indigenous teachers who do not have complete high school, leaving schools without teachers and children and adolescents without classes. The pandemic was two years old and the schools were unable to function. In addition, several communities do not have infrastructure for classes to take place, often being used as “classroom” inadequate spaces, such as the terreiros or ritual places of the villages. There is also a lack of teaching materials necessary for the development of classes, among others. The Ashaninka, Madijá, Huni-Kui and Shanenawá peoples are in this same situation of school failure, located in the Kampa and Isolated ITs of the Envira River, Jaminawá Envira, Kulina do Rio Envira, Kulina do Igarapé Pau, Katukina/Kaxinawá, Kaxinawá Nova Olinda and Kaxinawá do Seringal Curralinho, all in the municipality of Feijó (AC). Complaints were made to the MPF, but there was no provision.
8d38e59a865c9c89b98398c1aea4c59fb5409817: Indigenous leaders of various peoples denounced school failure in various ITs. They report discontinuity in the training of teachers who are still attending the indigenous teaching or in the continued training of those who have already completed. The pandemic crisis, which turned two years old, further aggravated this reality. Most indigenous schools remained closed. In addition, several communities do not have the infrastructure for classes to take place, often being used as “classroom” inadequate spaces, such as ritual spaces of the villages. Educational materials are also lacking for the development of classes, among others. The indigenous peoples Apolima-Arara, Ashaninka, Huni-Kui and Arara do Bagé, who live in the Arara ITs of the Amônia River, Kaxinawá/Ashaninka of the Breu River and Jaminawá-Arara do Bagé, all in the municipality of Marechal Thaumaturgo (AC), are in this same situation of school failure. Complaints were made to the MPF, but there was no provision.
b25bfd04639213ccc500f745bcc9c18a5931e526: Indigenous leaders denounce school failure in the Nawá and Nukini ITs in the municipality of Mâncio Lima. They report discontinuity in the training of teachers who are still attending the indigenous teaching, or lack of continued training of those who have already completed. With the pandemic, schools were completely abandoned and there were no initiatives that favored communities, such as Internet access for online classes. Therefore, the indigenous peoples Nawá and Nukini are in this same situation of school failure. Complaints were made to the MPF.
f4bc2de29c725f485ef9222d4771a3e75018d754: The government of the state of Alagoas, through the State Department of Education, prepared notice for public tender, disregarding the Federal Constitution, Convention 169 and the indigenous peoples for not conducting prior consultation before performing such action. Leaderships report that the notice does not serve the indigenous peoples of Alagoas, because it disrespects their forms of organization. Indigenous teachers have been trying to regularize their category, and during the period, several simplified contests were held for teacher monitor. Indigenous teachers have been working irregularly for over a year. The MPF was triggered and promoted a meeting between the parties to solve the case in question. After this performance of the MPF, the government of the state of Alagoas suspended the notice and invited indigenous teachers to participate in the process of drafting the new notice.
c475b8a08962b2e90f99dd95ea3f938ac72422a6: In the virtual event “Indigenous April 20-30, indigenous leaders of the Amazon made reports of the problems faced in the region. Among others, the situation of the Baniwa people was reported in relation to those that were difficult in the area of indigenous school education. According to one of the leaders, “in São Gabriel da Cachoeira, more than 90% of the population is indigenous. There are 23 peoples, four linguistic families, 18 spoken languages and four co-official languages. There is an Indigenous School Education Subsystem, and the category ‘indigenous teacher’ was created. Currently there is weariness and devaluation of indigenous school education. The new municipal government excluded indigenous language teachers in recent notice and the inclusion of foreign languages (English and Spanish). There was pressure from leaders and organizations and waved with the promise of correction, which did not happen. Schools are important spaces for the implementation of Etno-Territorial Management Plans. In the municipality of Amanã, indigenous languages of indigenous schools were excluded. This exclusion contributes to cultural death. It is a form of genocide”.
9a037a31279811555e3df0fb3b0349a9c8b12f62: Indigenous leaders of various peoples denounce school failure in various ITs in Acre and Amazonas. They report discontinuity in the formation of teachers who still attended the indigenous teaching. The new teachers were also not offered training courses. In addition, several communities do not have the infrastructure for classes to take place, and inadequate spaces such as “classrooms” are often adapted, such as terreiros or ritual spaces of the villages. There is also a lack of teaching materials necessary for the development of classes, among others. The peoples Katukina, Apurinã, Jamamadi, Jaminawá, Manchineri, Madijá and Kanamari are located in the ITs Campinas/Katukina, Rio Gregório, Valparaíso, Camicuã, Massacury Kamapá (Lourdes and Cajueiro), Iquirema/Goiaba/Monte II, Boca do Acre BR-317 - Km 45, Apurinã BR-317 - Km 124, Maracajú, Igarapé Capana, Inauini/ Teuini, Jaminawá do Caiapuca, Mamodate, Riozinho do Iaco, Kulina do Médio Juruá, Cacau do Tarauacá, Mawek and Kanamari do Rio Juruá, distributed in the municipalities of Cruzeiro do Sul, Sena Madureira, Assis Brasil and Tarauacá, in Are, and Boca do Acre, Pauini, Eirunepia, Ixima and Amazon. Complaints were made to the MPF, but there was no provision.
5c3f8fc26694a47db974ddb9635c258619ed86db: The Mura report that the school of the village Taquara, which has high school, serves three communities: Trincheira village, with about 1,600 indigenous people; Taquara village, with 245 people and Flechal village, with about 300. There are approximately 2,145 indigenous people in the region where the school is located. It is frequented by non-indigenouss too, and their families do not allow differentiated education. Some school professionals have ties with the invaders and accumulate functions. It is the case of the manager, who is also a teacher. Her husband is a teacher, watchman, lunch cook, carpenter, and lunch carrier. The luncher is also a cleaner and therefore the preparation of meals is precarious and the quantity is insufficient. The snack is not regionalized and contains many industrialized and processed products. The Mura don't eat those foods. During the dry season, students find it very difficult to get to school. There are reports that the snack is diverted and there is no supervision of where the food that comes to school goes. Complaints were made to the MPF, but without favorable result to the indigenous.
501083798d11c400a2ec7fed713ed8d05a4b27c3: Dissistence and lack of differentiated education
7d64c3e1d614719fec056169b195b372db9dd042: Leaderships and indigenous students report that the concomitance of the Technical Course in Forests offered to the Jarawara people of the village Casa Nova-Nascente, TI Jarawara/Jamadi/ Kanamati, by the Federal Institute of Amazonas (IFAM) – campus Lábrea was broken. The students brought the problem to the discussion during the launch of the Territorial and Environmental Management Plan (PGTA) Jarawara and Apurinã, held in Funai auditorium – CR Médio Purus, in Lábrea, between November 16 and 17, 2021. Seduc's unilateral decision to automatically approve students in the school year 2020 damaged the course's 23 students. In addition, Seduc did not take into account the specificity of indigenous school education and, even more, the specificity of the technical course offered by IFAM in the village Casa Nova-Nascente, as recommended by the Amazon MPF. It is noteworthy that the technical course was suspended because of the Covid-19 pandemic, by collective decision taken at a meeting held on June 1, 2020, in which representatives of the director and NEABI of IFAM campus Lábrea participated, the Rectoria/PROEN/ IFAM, systemic NEABI and Funai – CR Middle Purus. The decision for suspension was based on Ordinance Funai No. 419 of March 17, 2020, as well as on the suspension of classroom academic activities within the IFAM, justified by the duty to safeguard the lives of indigenous students.
58ee554cade2df8ca130ee19d11536c5077981b6: Young indigenous people from the river region Negro made a motion of repudiation for neglect of education and referred to MPF. They complain of lack of lunch and transportation, among other failures. The document listed a series of complaints of mismanagement and execution of Fundeb's public resources. The young people also asked the MPF to visit the communities to investigate all situations of precariousness in the teaching of the region. Many schools still operate in improvised places (community house, chapel, maloca, terreiro, private house, under the trees), without kitchen, cafeteria, library, teachers' room, bathrooms and leisure area. Schools have no furniture, no drinking water and artesian well, no electricity and no internet access in indigenous communities. Another major challenge facing indigenous schools is the lack of adequate river transport, such as 40 HP outboard engines and eight-meter boats, in addition to the need to hire a river driver.
4a83d1f44268adf28955f55e9c8aa25e8df1cd48: Indigenous leaders recorded videos on October 28, 2021 denouncing the precarious structural conditions of the indigenous school General Bandeira de Melo in the village Escalvado. With more than 600 indigenous students enrolled, the school has fallen walls, no doors and windows, with many deteriorated walls and many tiles out of place, no chairs, tables, pictures and no basic operating conditions.
03e11d3d18dcda8199a37cba33ed5d1c066f1f52: The 6th Chamber of Coordination and Review of the MPF decided to convert the News of Fact into a civil inquiry to determine precarious situations of the services provided in the indigenous schools of the State Department of Education (Seduc) of Maranhão. According to the MPF, in the initial representation problems were reported in the Indigenous School El Purume Katuhaw in the village Jacaré, in the municipality of Arame, and in the indigenous school Guajajara Mayrata, in the village Monkey, TI Urucu Juruá, in the municipality of Itaipava do Grajaú. According to the complaint of the MPF, there is no adequate distribution of food, no distribution of teaching material, besides the precarious infrastructure conditions in schools.
b5a9dd61299bd486baa480239628a806ccaea162: The school of the indigenous community in Amarante do Maranhão, which hosts six villages, is in poor infrastructure conditions, endangering the safety of children and adolescents. The walls are cracked and indigenous students need to take their chairs, since there are no chairs in the school. Besides, there's no electricity in the school unit.
9251e2ecf0d0c6ead58a4ebc32f241c82e326a00: The construction of the José Mariano State School, in the indigenous community of Baixius, in Barra do Bugres (MT), has not yet been completed, although the plaque of the work indicates as deadline September 2011. The MPE-MT entered the action requiring injunction that the state complete the construction of the school, in order to meet the quality standards and to offer dignity care to all students and teachers, as well as the conviction in daily fine of R $ 10 thousand in case of non-compliance with the obligation to do. Therefore, the Mato Grosso Court of Justice (TJMT) maintained the decision that determines that the state government builds, installs, teams and puts a school in operation in the community. However, the Justice suspended the daily fine of R $ 10 thousand and increased the deadline of compliance with the judicial determination to 12 months, after the state filed appeal.
7f2241b8302b4d3b55aa8d066618cc1a34b25a6a: Myky leaders report the disrespect of the Mato Grosso State Department of Education to legislation regarding indigenous school education, for not following the norms that guarantee respect for the specificities of indigenous cultures. Seduc deals with indigenous schools in the same way as any school in the city. Some examples of this neglect are: a) during the pandemic the classrooms were suspended and Seduc demanded that the Indigenous Schools organize care by remote teaching; b) there was no less consideration for the problem of internet deficiency in the villages and even the lack of devices such as computers and mobile phones; c) Seduc elaborated handouts that were sent to the villages, however, prepared by non-indigenous people, totally outside the sociocultural context of the Xinui M Some procedures were carried out by the community: a) the indigenous members of the CEEI - Indigenous School Education Council of Mato Grosso, also debated and questioned the attitude of Seduc-MT; b) in the face of the imposition of handouts, the indigenous school received them, but the teachers organized themselves in order to intensify the Indigenous Knowledge and especially the activities of swidden in view of the need for subsistence during the pandemic; c) in relation to representativeness in the CEEI, Councilor M
c10972d23355483ab7a14f1b412c1c1d2592ef9d: In August 2021, the roof of a classroom of the Tapi’itãwa State Indigenous School in Tapi’itãwa Village, TI Urubu Branco, collapsed. The classroom served as a library, and teachers, students and staff were at risk of being injured by the collapse. Many books and equipment have been destroyed. The school management team transferred what was left of the library to the room where the computer lab worked, however, as there were leaks in this room, it was necessary to transfer the library again, to another room. Other parts of the building are in bad condition, the toilets don't work. There are exposed wooden beams with rotted parts that can fall at any time. The electrical part also needs repairs. In addition, a classroom was provided for the operation of the village health center. Due to lack of physical space, several classes of elementary school students are studying in school halls. The Deliberative Council of the School Community sent a document to the Secretary of Education of the State of Mato Grosso exposing the situation and requesting urgent measures. Seduc-MT replied that the school needs to request a decentralized budget, and that it would receive a portion in the first semester and another portion in the second semester. That is, with this bureaucracy and delay, the school would spend another year with the extremely precarious structure, offering risk to the whole community.
91f71f0cf0975a7313e8e5dbbd70756bc4dfb737: In 2021, indigenous schools in the state of Mato Grosso were surprised by the abrupt change in the administrative structure of Seduc-MT. With the change, Pedagogical Advisory in the municipalities will cease to exist in 2022 and the Training and Update Center of Basic Education Professionals of the State of Mato Grosso (CEFAPRO) will be extinguished. With these changes, indigenous schools will be the most affected, because they will no longer be able to count on the administrative collaboration of Pedagogical Advisory that are closer to the schools and that currently act as an administrative support structure. It is the advice that performs, for example, the platform for acquiring school meals. Other changes, such as the nucleation of rural and indigenous schools, extinguishing the attached schools, may also significantly affect the lives of hundreds of indigenous students and teachers, irreparably denying the right to a specific and differentiated indigenous education. These changes occurred without the knowledge of indigenous schools and peoples, thus denying the Free, Previous and Informed Consultation to Indigenous Peoples, guaranteed in Article 6 of the ILO Convention 169, not taking into account that indigenous schools are part of the state education system. These changes directly impact schools, interfering in their administrative and pedagogical functioning. The school community of the Myky people, faced with this threat, launched an Objection Letter from the School Community, rejecting this undemocratic attitude of the government of the state of Mato Grosso.
beb8ec627bd021b85fc4eab8051f7ee5381dc1c6: The MPF recommended to the state of Pará, through the State Department of Education, and to the municipality of Paragominas to take the necessary measures to include in the Articulated Action Plan 4 (PAR-4) of the Ministry of Education the request to make available all the necessary resources for building and acquiring the necessary furniture for the implementation of indigenous schools of the Iarapehu Villages and Tres Furos, including sending the necessary technical documentation to the Integrated Monitoring, Execution and Control System of the Ministry of Education - SIMEC. The villages have no school, and the students need to move for now in river transport to the nearest educational establishment; in addition, the students of these villages are being attended in the classrooms/rooms built by indigenous communities themselves, outside the standards of the polo schools. According to the survey carried out by the Paragominas Prefecture itself, only in the village Três Furos, there are 25 children of school age who would benefit from the construction of the school; however, after four years of the establishment of the procedure, the schools that should attend the children of both villages have not yet been built.
bdd5e1c10de8e47c31bc5acc0ce1e200d1127e0b: The disregard and inefficiency of the state with regard to education, has affected the lives of the peoples Parakanã, Arara, Asurini, Araweté, Kuruaia, Xipaia, Xikrin, Kaiapó and Juruna of the ITs Apyterewa, Arara, Cachoeira Seca, Xipaia, Kuruaia, Reach Bacajá, Paquiçamba, Arara da Volta Grande, Kuatinmo, Ipixuna and Boa Vista km 17. This neglect of education in the villages has caused many losses to the indigenous population, especially to children and young people. Unfortunately, one of the consequences is the emptying of their communities, the distancing of their traditional cultures and ways of life. Another problem faced by indigenous peoples is in relation to the quality of school meals provided, with items of low quality and in little quantity, not meeting the nutritional needs of students. Moreover, the snack is not adequate, as it does not take into account the traditional foods consumed by peoples according to their culture. As for school materials, distribution in the villages is precarious. In general, the government does not comply with what is recommended in the federal legislation regarding the guarantee of an indigenous school education, differentiated and respectful, with the necessary infrastructure, the use of their mother tongues and their own learning modes.
15c6dca764f77ff9ed2b05f76c35df85248e7478: The Pankararu indigenous community Opará denounces the lack of school within IT, although they have been claiming its installation for many years, mainly due to the high illiteracy rate in the locality. d809399ac48751ccfac2479405364ceb54df2777: The cacica Francisca Bezerra Tapuia Tarairiú, coordinator of the Apoinme State Microregion in Rio Grande do Norte, reports the delay in regularizing indigenous schools in the municipalities of Macaíba and Baía Formosa, compromising the school life of indigenous children and adolescents of the Potiguara peoples of Sagi/Trabanda and Tapuia Tarairiú da Lagoa do Tapará. Several requests have already been made to the responsible bodies, but no provision has been made.
ba8c1e3ceaac4bbab4f47f3be098927d27e86bf6: Without adequate infrastructure to operate the Monte Caseros Indigenous EE in Ibiraiaras (RS), the Kaingang community needed to improvise a space to serve 126 students, since the school only has two classrooms. Father of a student and secretary of Indigenous Affairs of the reservation, Nemias Carvalho charges more attention from the authorities to the situation of the school. “We are there crying, asking the authorities to look at it there, so that we can also see our children studying, having good learning, quality”, he says. In 2021, the school began to attend every year of elementary school, increasing the number of students attended. The hall of indigenous land, which was used on a provisional basis, was deactivated because of the risk of collapse. The institution has 15 employees, among teachers, servants and lunchmakers.
a143462aae51ed5be50a70f1e33d1158f1221911: In Igarapé Lage, the Oro Wari indigenous people have reported the disregard of the State for education, which is recurrent and in various ways: lack of teachers, lack of meals, lack of implementation of high school in the community. This situation occurs not only in the community in Distrito Palmeira, but also in others. The community reports that students have spent more than three months without a teacher and that every time they have a teacher they are transferred to another community. For students not to be so damaged, indigenous with a little more knowledge are teaching.
793498bb8d8b15de44e00f07fe5400d41487253d: Reports from an indigenous school principal show that the Roraima State Department of Education and Sports did not give the “minimum conditions” for the return to classes, such as the availability of lunchmakers and school transportation. At least 27 indigenous communities in Roraima were still unable to return to classrooms in November 2021.
4c292db190794ee69ddea71252674b821cb7f840: The indigenous community of Jaraguá, northern São Paulo, has long denounced the lack of school infrastructure, cracks and risk to the physical integrity of students and professionals. The ESS claimed that it had already started some reforms, but that there were problems passing money from the Direct Money Program at School, because the Association of Parents and Masters was blocked by problems with accountability, but that it would already be resolved and that the works of interventions would continue.
da5ac61bc6acc0937043401a0919cf4678d36df9: On November 10, the team of the Cimi Vale do Ribeira was in the village (tekoha) Pakurity to talk with the leaders of IT Cardoso Island. The team realized that the village school was disabled and there were no hired teachers in the village. The village is located on Cardoso Island and the only way to access is by sea, by sea transport. About the school, there was a forecast for hiring teachers for the following year (2022). The community has a motor boat, but the engine has been stolen and the boat is useless. The chief informed that even if the boat was working, the community would not be able to pay for the fuel for the transport of students. The leaders reported that Funai is aware of the situation, but did not signal any provision for solving the problem. They emphasized that Funai made very few visits to IT that year. The community claims support for the repair of the boat and fuel, so that school-aged young people can attend high school, as well as waiting for the hiring of teachers and the structuring of the school that exists in the village so that elementary school students 1 can study.
45dd9eeeb3e88fabcc49a5aae47540a8fd102c38: The school of the village Nova, of the Krahô people, had its construction started in 2003, being handed over to the indigenous without the proper conclusion and without any comfort for the students. In August 2020, the community was in the MPF city of Araguaína to file another document, taking photos that prove the neglect of school education by Seduc. To date, the community has not received any response from the responsible bodies and the school remains in precarious conditions.
7aac1c49aec7236842f375e50e01b03b152458bc: Javaé Indians from Cachoeirinha village, on Bananal Island (TO), report that the Wahuri Indigenous School is in a precarious situation of conservation and at risk of collapse for at least four years. According to the indigenous, one of the roof support beams would be threatening to fall and so it was improvised. “The school is about to fall. He's leaning with a wood. Any minute now, it's gonna fall. Then who's responsible? The chief or the state? We really need the reform of our school”, said Chief Ideberê Javaé. A team from the Department of Education would have gone once again in the village to make surveys for the reform, but the indigenous say it is not the first time that the teams go to the village to perform this type of work and never solve the problem. The indigenous peoples mobilized and withheld a truck from the state, in order to give visibility to the problem faced and to force the measures regarding school reform. There are many indigenous children and young people who are at risk due to the imminent collapse of the school roof.
2d8ddab5e03c40aa00b9204190add999154d041b: From the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic until the beginning of April 2021, 2,569 cases of coronavirus infection were confirmed among indigenous people in the state. 25395db63632a6900b500ad943c52dab3264ac3b: The Ashaninka, Madija and Huni Kui populations living along the Envira River suffer from the lack of drinking water and sanitation in the villages. Several complaints were made to the MPF and the population is awaiting provision.
15fd3b007e24d4c472d4811ca53c93189ebb0245: The Huni Kui, Madija and Jaminawá populations that live along the Purus River suffer from the lack of drinking water and sanitation in the villages. a987f3e75e42858e0c5f69c34fb6fa38bb75e9f1: In addition to the delay of the government in establishing vaccination procedures against Covid-19 with indigenous peoples, the process was also hampered due to the spread of lies. People linked to fundamentalist neo-Pentecostal churches spread lies among the indigenous, spreading that in the vaccine had the chip of the beast, that men would be “skinned”, that the vaccine would kill people. This fact, associated with the low commitment of the federal government to encourage vaccination, generated panic and resistance of the indigenous people to take the vaccine against Covid-19. 82a83894162c3c5a6bcacfd0123a334647c23325: Indigenous people living in an urban context had denied access to vaccination against Covid-19 as a priority public. fd99e31160887058812f1d9f0156965c96625f2f: Denial of vaccines to indigenous people in urban context
6c996db72f4ff1843e98736e8068b70c5f570ad8: Indigenous leaders denounce that missionaries of neo-Pentecostal churches try to convince villages in the Amazon not to take the vaccine against Covid-19. These evangelicals have told the indigenous not to take the vaccine because “it has a chip, which will become an alligator, some crazy excuses”, Claudemir added. Indigenous leaders blame President Jair Bolsonaro and his supporters in the evangelical community for feeding skepticism about coronavirus vaccines, even with the high number of deaths in the country.
8689ecf8baa7bed2abd167f03f5635e02231fea8: The Park of Tribes is a neighborhood of Manaus that was occupied in 2014, with about 700 families, who live under constant threats of eviction, in unhealthy dwellings, without sewage treatment and without water – one of the basic items of protection against the coronavirus. Many Kokama Indians, especially those with more severe symptoms, managed to survive thanks to the Tribe Park Indigenous Campaign Hospital. The federal government promised to set up a hospital for the indigenous in April 2020, but until February 2021 the promise had not come out of the paper. The indigenous report that there is no good will of the government to serve them. Coiab informs that of the 783 indigenous deaths by Covid-19 until February 18, the majority was Amazon, and that the Kokama, which are the largest indigenous population in urban context, are the most affected with deaths. Manaus City Hall has a mobile unit in Tribes Park only to make tests and diagnoses to the indigenous population. The government of Amazonas said that it does not work in the indigenous hospital campaign and that it follows the rule of the Ministry of Health that indigenous "non-salted" should make use of the public network available to the general population. The abandonment by the government in this region is worrying and points to a tragedy.
e8c800d032de9a1fc53a36471c900a64d59d9013: According to data from the federal government, 71% of the indigenous people living in villages in the Amazon until mid-February 2021 had not been vaccinated against Covid-19. More than 431 thousand indigenous people should have been vaccinated by now, as they were included in the first priority groups, but only 164,592 were vaccinated in the first month of the campaign. There are reports that some indigenous people were afraid of vaccination, and refusing to do so, due to the disclosure of false news about vaccines. However, this would not be the only reason; the low vaccination coverage of indigenous peoples was another negative point in the federal management of the pandemic among indigenous peoples. Since July 2020, the STF has determined that the government should adopt measures to protect indigenous communities and prevent mortality from the disease, but the delay and neglect of the federal government has led many indigenous peoples to contamination and death by Covid-19.
80acd80d5f21dfed59f5748654b7a12cd041a8ef: Report by Folha de S. Paulo revealed that in June 2020 large quantities of drugs were distributed in indigenous communities without proven efficacy for Covid-19. According to the report, the Ministry of Health distributed at least 265 thousand chloroquine tablets, azithromycin and ivermectin – proven ineffective drugs for the fight against coronavirus – to several indigenous peoples, located in Amazonas, Acre, Mato Grosso, Rondônia and Roraima. Part of the tablets were purchased directly by DSEIs. According to the report, a technical report from Sesai, June 2020, instructed the DSEIs to “instruct their respective processes of acquisition” of medicines, if municipalities and states refused to provide them.
c09e2cd7a6951f6925776796299eeea6faa3bc66: Failure and connivance of the public authority
e60f3f76835c9465c3f4f22bc4c54b589e40824b: The Madija and Kanamari people of this region are totally abandoned by Sesai – DSEI Tefé. In addition, in most communities there is no basic sanitation, which, in a pandemic period, only worsened the situation. Several complaints were made to the MPF and the population is awaiting provision.
df18fa889b66df7ab702ddd0a626925c13b4f7f0: Lack of assistance, drinking water and sanitation
11075710a231cebf77a48485a8fc72636a59e52d: The indigenous people of the Mura people feel harmed because they do not have a differentiated care at the Health Base Pole of the Reach IT region, to which they are entitled. One of the biggest problems is the lack of indigenous health agents and there is information that no medicine kits are available. Complaints have been made to the MPF and the Mura people are awaiting provision.
7fdef2151072de4bb3b20d8d0162b73c7668e876: The federal government, through the Ministry of Health and Sesai, has omitted data on Covid-19's death statistics of indigenous residents in urban areas. The situation causes a disparity between the data of the federal government and those compiled by entities that assess the impact of the pandemic on the indigenous population. According to Eriki Paiva Terena of Apib, “the underreporting of the Sesai is very large. They do not consider indigenous in an urban context, they do not consider indigenous in unholy lands. The difference, the discrepancy between our data and Sesai's data is so great because we don't have that discrimination. We consider indigenous in any context, because the indigenous territory is the whole of Brazil”. Sesai argues that, according to current legislation, the indigenous population in urban context is attended directly by their respective municipal health departments, and not by the federal government. Besides not registering deaths of urban indigenous peoples, Sesai does not specify cases or deaths by locality, nor does it detail the peoples. Indigenous entities, with criticism of the federal government, launched the International Criminal Court for the third time, denouncing President Jair Bolsonaro for crimes against humanity and genocide. The move reinforces that the president encouraged, facilitated and stopped fighting invasions of indigenous lands, illegal mining, deforestation and contamination – by mercury, ores ores or Covid-19 – affecting the lives, health, integrity and very existence of indigenous peoples in Brazil. “This policy consists of systematic attacks on indigenous peoples, either directly to their bodies or to their lands, resulting in their physical disappearance and the extermination of modes of existence, with a view, in specific cases, to their destruction,” he says.
6b41fcab8103723abc2decaa1a62af14045d2869: Denial of rights in health care
a28c1b1e059dfb6ecf248fab1964f1469bd76370: The Chief Zeca Pataxó and other indigenous leaders of southern Bahia, concerned with the progress of Covid-19, denounced the lack of hygiene and personal protection materials. The only one that was opened was the Red Crown village, which is the largest urban village in the country, and the circulation of people is usually intense. The leaders reported that the lack of masks and gel alcohol was responsible for the increase in the number of contaminated individuals, and that, at the beginning of the pandemic, they received masks and gel alcohol from Sesai and Funai, but for months they have not received the equipment. The Regional Council of Caciques reported that it took the complaints to the MPF, Ministry of Health and the presidency of the Republic.
677660b6fd340dcb481860128b32d585e69d7659: The doctor Alda Regina, who works in the village of Caieiras Velha, in Aracruz (ES), describes a precarious scenario in health care for the indigenous peoples of Espírito Santo. The problems range from lack of input to the scarcity of Personal Protection Equipment (EPIs). “It’s not ethical, it’s not human,” he says. Along with leaders Tupinikim and Guarani, she defends the dismemberment of Governor Valadares' DSEI (MG). For the professional, one of the main problems is the centralization of the management of Indigenous Health in the DSEI of Governor Valadares, which serves both the villages of Minas Gerais and Espírito Santo. “They come here two, three times a year. We do not have a security technician to evaluate the working conditions ", continues. Wellington Moura Pego is Tupinikim and president of the Aracruz Municipal Health Council. He affirms that the dependence of the DSEI of Minas Gerais causes the assistance to reach Espírito Santo in a poor way, with the difficulty of buying medicines and dressings, for example. Alda has been active in this area since September 2020. Since then, he says that he has observed a series of precariousness in the care of the local indigenous population. “Here we lack everything. We don't have a pressure gauge, we have to bring it. We don't have a proper room to separate what respiratory syndrome is. It is all together and mixed”, reports. Paulo Tupinikim, general coordinator of Apoinme, reiterates the lack of assistance caused by the situation.
6999d015c6e56522c42100aa463e52a1e2ec19fd: A lot of masks sent to professionals working in the indigenous villages of Aracruz, in the north of Espírito Santo, was defeated since 2004. The equipment was sent by the DSEI of Governor Valadares (MG), of the Ministry of Health, responsible for the area in the state. For servers on the front line of the fight against the coronavirus pandemic, the episode shows the neglect of the indigenous health service capixaba. For Bruno Joaquim Siqueira, Tupinikim and nursing technician in the village Irajá, it is another neglect with the servants, who already point out the lack of PPE in indigenous health units for some time. “A lack of respect for us, because it is not today that we have been suffering with neglect. I'm an Indian health professional, but first, I'm an Indian too. So, of course I feel disrespected ", reports.
e6de96f9e3942328b9b37d430d9d5d4607600b51: With the process of reviewing the paralyzed demarcation, the indigenous peoples implemented villages on the borders of the land as a strategy to inhibit the invasions of hunters in the territory. The lack of drinking water causes diseases and even greater vulnerability to indigenous people.
b66034745d00ade2370ea9d3b0146c5a1d792c94: For years, the Myky people have faced Sesai's neglect of indigenous health care. The lack of medication, equipment, team of professionals; many prescriptions of medicines are expensive and impossible to achieve; the delay in obtaining care outside the city worsens the patients' health problems. Two cases of Myky brothers from Japuíra Village draw attention to neglect. One, of a nine-year-old child with orthopedic problems, has taken a long time to walk and to this day presents serious problems in the lower limbs and extreme difficulty in locomotion. Since 2018, leaders and supporters, such as Cimi, have tried to obtain adequate care from Sesai to the child, but there has never been an accurate diagnosis of the problem presented, much less systematic treatment of physiotherapy. This child also has speech problems, requiring speech therapy, also without success. The other child, 6 years old, was born with neurological problems, does not talk and does not walk, just crawls on the floor. Since birth, he would need specialized care, but, like his brother, he does not receive any dignified care for the Sesai.
3f61ad3aeb7d74d5b88e0dadeba099306858b25c: The Ministry of Health opened an investigation to investigate a possible loss of 320 doses of Coronavac, one of the vaccines against Covid-19, which would be used in the immunization of indigenous Xingu. Gilberto Figueiredo, Secretary of Health of Mato Grosso, told the local press that the “vaccines were frozen”. To maintain efficacy against coronavirus, the temperature of Coronavac must be between 2oC and 8oC. The bottles with Coronavac were in the Xingu DSEI, located in the municipality of Canarana, 605 km from Cuiabá. To date, Canarana had 24 deaths and 1,566 confirmed cases of Covid-19, in a population of 21,000 people.
e6d4dc9aca86c2f6f4636c9f9e220975f27726a4: The former mayor of the municipality of Santo Antônio de Leverger became a defendant and will be heard in action in the 3rd Federal Court Civil of Mato Grosso that investigates the non-application of R $ 5 million in indigenous health of the region. The action, moved by the MPF, requires that the resources be applied in the Incentive of Primary Care for Indigenous Peoples. According to the MPF, the resources were stopped since 2012, without being applied in the purpose, thus compromising the health situation of indigenous peoples in the region, which is already quite precarious. The MPF stated that even the chaotic pandemic scenario did not raise awareness of the former mayor, who did not seek to serve the indigenous population of his municipality, while the health secretariats, hospital units and DSEIs sought with the MPF and the Judiciary resources to face the severe crisis of Covid-19.
5f772b260b06533c552ecd9d80a5b8ad2a5c0a70: In 2008 resources for indigenous health were released via the city of Santo Antônio do Leverger (MT). These resources should be allocated to the Health District of Cuiabá (DSEI), for the care of the Bororo people of TI Tereza Cristina. However, until September 2021 the appeal had not yet been released by the city. As a result, the community faces problems with the construction and maintenance of health infrastructure (health, sanitation, transportation). The indigenous community has been demanding the release of resources and information on values (bank extract), without answers from the municipal administration. Meanwhile, in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, the Bororo Indians have suffered the harmful consequences of the omission and neglect of the government.
a1caf1f510d6d210835b9409b46c255d2897f4cd: Lack of resources for indigenous health
91e399e8a23797b7785937cdcdd310015c930d70: The village Mother Maria, of the Xavante people, suffers from lack of access to drinking water. In the opinion of the old woman, due to long time without use, the well will need cleaning. At the moment, the community is seeking water for general consumption in a small stream about 500 meters away, with the aggravating fact that this water is not drinking. She also said that seven people in the village have died from diseases caused by the ingestion of contaminated water during the rainy season. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of this village, but there was no provision yet.

All of them urgently need working artesian wells; many are availing themselves of the drinking water of a small stream or rainwater for use in all their needs. In the village Campos do Jordão, for 12 years they live without drinking water, and also use improper water from a small stream and rainwater, causing diseases such as diarrhea, especially in children and elders.
