0ba7f8d939c765d74ded60a46e3db285a47214ab: The Xavante people of Water Village Hot, in Água Boa (MT), suffers from the lack of drinking water and sanitation. Since 2019 the community has requested the drilling of an artesian well in the village. There is a well drilled by Sesai, with facilities of a water box, but it does not work, due to a fault in the water pump and distribution. As a consequence, several families moved temporarily to some neighboring villages. Those who remained seek water in the village Tiripá, 3 km away, with great difficulties. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of this village, but there was no provision yet.
577e855f9f5a1201329f7ff6c79e3b80c8a42802: The village Arimateia, of the Xavante people, has an artesian well perforated by Sesai, with water box facilities and distribution, but in the time of drought, the water decreases greatly, causing the burning of the pump, leaving the community without the water that it so much needs. The community asks that the well be deepened to reach other water sheets. That way, even in the time of drought, drinking water will not be lacking. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Cuiabá denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of this village.
4f6f8756e00b3dae9eaf6aed5925cfce929d11f6: Given the omission and neglect of the government in relation to the health care of the indigenous, volunteers and non-governmental organizations and the Church, they seek to provide assistance in this sector. This is the case of the Pastoral Care of the Indigenous Child and the Personal Parish Xavante São Domingos Sávio, who found that 13 children from the village São Pedro were malnourished and with low weight. Faced with these serious cases, agents of the Pastoral Care of the Child intensified the visits and offered a complementary food (nutritive and multimixture soup) for a period of one month. The initiative resulted and nine children regained adequate weight and nutrition. Four children with more severe conditions remain in malnutrition.
8d5ae5f7e47bbddfe4c86367c240ebe5656fd8fc: The lack of drinking water and sanitation has affected the Xavante indigenous people for many years. In the village Good Luck, the chief reported that his community is suffering from the lack of an artesian well. Ten years ago, he's been asking for arrangements from the competent bodies, with nothing coming. They're looking for drinking water in the nearby village of Campinas. For other uses, they are worth the water of the river Sucuri, distant about 500m. In the village of Brazil, the situation is even more difficult. For 20 years the leaders have been asking for an artesian well for the responsible bodies. The only source closer is a mine that has little flow and is used by three other neighboring villages. In the village of Galilee, inaccessible with a truck, the community needs an artesian well, because it is consuming water from a small course of water that is not drinkable. In Querência village, the community has an old well, pierced by the Salesian Mission of Mato Grosso. But in the months of August or September of each year the water decreases greatly and cannot use it. So they're looking for water in a small stream, about half a mile away. But this drought in the month of July each year. To have quality water they seek it in the village Egypt, about 5km away. Given this situation, the community calls for the deepening of the existing well or the drilling of a new one. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous of these villages, but no provision was made.
73cf1f8825e6dd4290b67db6a813d86d1b5ee082: As in other villages of the Xavante people, communities living in the villages Meribá, New Hope and Blessing Valley experience extreme difficulties due to lack of drinking water and basic sanitation. Even when it came to ancient villages, they never had artesian well or access to drinking water. Families have always had to resort to water from small streams, visibly unfit for consumption. Chief Eliab Tseremoiwe of the Valley of Blessing village informed that he had already sent six documents asking for the installation of an artesian well in his village, but that it had not yet been answered. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Cuiabá denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of these three villages.
59555acf197a50e3f2b1c89aefaac23cd1685161: Various Communities For years Xavante has experienced the neglect and omission of the government in the fulfillment of constitutional rights, especially with regard to indigenous health. The problem of drinking water and sanitation in villages is recurrent in the Parabubure IT: Cachoeira do Couto, Daprabadzé, Hoi’wapredzawi, Independence, Morro da Saudade, Pope Paul VI, Paranoá, Santa Izabel, Santa Luzia, Santa Rita, Santo Expedito, São Miguel, São João Batista, Tsotenho’u and Vassoura. There are no artesian wells perforated in most communities, and when there is, they do not work, due to lack of complementary equipment or lack of maintenance when, for example, bombs burn. The waters for those who have access, for the most part, are considered unfit for human consumption, removed from reduced, dirty and contaminated streams, and far from the communities. The Salesian Mission has even financed the drilling of artesian wells, pipes, water tanks and bombs, but currently has no resources to continue making these contributions or repairs. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of these villages, but there was no provision yet.
99d14d224d99ac01ab1e0ad522a0ca78b04a1d30: The Xavante communities, for the most part, have been experiencing problems with lack of drinking water and sanitation for years. Even though the situation is denounced to the competent bodies, the measures in favor of indigenous families are not taken. In the village Santa Clara, with a population of 398 people, there is an artesian well that was installed by the Salesian Mission of Mato Grosso. Recently, a municipal school was built; but the artesian well intended for it has not yet been pierced. The leaders ask for two more wells to meet the various families of the community, because the well installed by the Salesian Mission is not enough; the water always ends in the afternoon, around 3:00 p.m. The community has also been requesting the drilling of a well to meet the demands of the health center, because it also receives only the water from the main well, installed by the Salesian Mission. When the water in the well runs out, the Xavantes need to find drinking water in a small mine that sprouts in the ravine of the main stream; but in the rainy season, the water from this stream rises and covers the small mine. In the village Three Kings Magos, created ten years ago, there is an artesian well that was also installed by the Salesian Mission of Mato Grosso, but has burned pieces. In the rainy season, the community runs out of water, because there's no sun to make the plate and the bomb work. So the indigenous families use water from a stream near the village, which is not drinkable. Thus, communities have requested the installation of a complete supply system by Sesai. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of these villages, but there was no provision yet.
1350cbc453ec9077907ca8c4d6332a23a94ae0e2: The Xavante communities, for the most part, have been experiencing problems with lack of drinking water and sanitation for years. Even though the situation is denounced to the competent bodies, the measures in favor of indigenous families are not taken. This is also the case of the villages: Cristalina, Lederança, Nossa Senhora do Carmo, Novo Teihidzatsé, Salvador, Santa Maria, Santos Reis, San Francisco de Assis, Ti’irerepá, Três Marias, Vila Maria Santa and Xavante. Most of these villages have no artesian well or other form of access to drinking water. The Salesian Mission of Mato Grosso even drilled artesian wells and equipment for its operation in some villages, however, with the use, several end up having their bombs burned, and there are no resources for repair and maintenance. Communities need to seek inadequate water for human consumption, far from their villages, in dirty and contaminated streams. The communities have already made numerous documents with requests for provision to Sesai, which did not occur. Meanwhile, indigenous families, many children and elderly, are subjected to neglect, becoming ill and dying due to preventable causes such as diarrhea. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of these villages, but there was no provision yet.
79ac255fe38f0c8839f0ee3b1fb1bf3bc84c7508: As occurs in almost all Xavante communities, the disregard of the government regarding health care, access to drinking water and basic sanitation also victim to indigenous families living in the villages Beira da Mata, Cachoeira, São Benedito and Sete Rios. In the village Beira da Mata there is no artesian well. Many were the requests of the community to the responsible bodies, but were not met. Families seek water in a mine for use in all their needs, but some Xavante from another village also use this mine to bathe, which further compromises the quality of water. Many children have diarrhea due to the use of contaminated water. In the Cachoeira village, the chief has already submitted request for drilling of an artesian well to Sesai, but it has not been answered. There's a stream nearby, but your water is unfit for consumption. Families have to get water from bactets with plastic bottles in another faraway village. In the village of São Benedito, in 1998, an artesian well was drilled, with box facilities and taps, by a Cuiabá company. But the well only worked for a month and showed bomb malfunction. The chief went to Barra do Garças and requested the repair, but even after so many years, nothing was done. Today, women take water in a nearby river, but their water is inappropriate for human consumption. In the rainy season it is necessary to strain water several times, so that it can be used. In the village Sete Rios, the chief reported that five years ago, a company went to the village to drill an artesian well. But since there was no water nearby, the well was not pierced and no provision was made. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of these villages, but there was no provision yet.
b28073c7ef2e28f34615428a91539aacad102bfd: The villages Água Viva, Mother of Virgo and Serra Verde are recent, do not have artesian well and do not have access to drinking water for consumption. The Xavante families need to find water in nearby streams, but are contaminated by various substances. The lack of adequate drinking water for consumption has caused various types of diseases in children, mainly diarrhea. The Cimi Regional Mato Grosso protocoled a representation in the MPF of Barra do Garças denouncing the lack of drinking water for the indigenous peoples of these three villages.
c6f5a45eac25034e75b83a0f8533ec6d3795190d: The indigenous Apyãwa/Tapirapé, Urubu Branco IT report that there are no medicines in the health center of the villages and that they need to buy when the doctors prescribe. The tests requested have also been taken by the families of patients, when they are able to buy. An example of this neglect is the situation of an elder Apyãwa, who has a severe leg wound, and needs daily dressings and medications, which also need to be bought by family members. Another situation of neglect and neglect concerns the extremely lengthy reform of the health post of the village Tapi’itãwa by the Municipality of Confresa (MT). Health professionals are attending, improvisedly, in a school classroom. These professionals need to stay overnight in the Tapi’itãwa village and are housed in a house that does not offer enough accommodation for all and does not meet the requirements of the Ministry of Labour, which requires the installation of female and male toilets, so that the servants are not exposed to embarrassing situations. In addition, the toilets of Apyãwa residences are in poor maintenance conditions. Such situations of neglect and neglect occur in the villages Tapi’itãwa, Tapiparanytãwa, Towajaatãwa, Wiriaotãwa, Myryxitãwa, Akara’ytãwa and Inataotãwa.
1da572d2fd3031b2c026f85e470f1e0018570f4e: The Chiquitano people have been fighting for years for the regularization of their traditional territory. Funai has not created, until today, the GT that will carry out studies to identify the territory and proceed to the land regularization process. Meanwhile, the Chiquitano community remains without care and without health care by Sesai; even in a period as painful as the Covid-19 pandemic has been, the government is not aware of the sufferings of these indigenous families. Some meetings have already been held with the Health Council to resolve this demand, but no action has been taken.
399123badf38cd6db70ede52960978c02ff948d2: Almost a hundred indigenous peoples from ten municipalities of Mato Grosso do Sul met in front of the headquarters of the DSEI to protest the neglect of the health of indigenous peoples in the state. There were a total of 80 leaders Guarani-Kaiowá and Terena, representing more than 80 thousand indigenous people of Mato Grosso do Sul. They were calling a meeting with Secretary Robson dos Santos da Silva and, among the requests, was the departure of the DSEI coordinator Joe Saccenti Junior, who's a reserve colonel. The indigenous peoples claim that they cannot engage with him to solve the problems of the villages, especially related to the Covid-19 pandemic and vaccination. According to chief Terena Jânio Rodrigues, 60 years old, they “have gone there other times and are always received with the Federal Police”.
2d8c0643727de00cc26d6e0e4c306383206360fc: The MPF proposed public civil action against the Union demanding that all indigenous people living in urban areas of Campo Grande be registered in the Indigenous Health Care information system and receive SUS card. The action was necessary after disclosure by the federal government that only the indigenous “village” would be vaccinated with priority.
6ae3e186eb6a6b04999b9db509585cc7391ee69f: From the beginning of the pandemic to the beginning of April 2021, 4,322 indigenous people in Mato Grosso do Sul had been infected by the coronavirus. The DSEI in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul was, at that time, the most concentrated cases of Covid-19 in Brazil, and the third among the 34 in the whole country where the coronavirus was more lethal. Every 50 indigenous people who infected themselves with the coronavirus to that point, one died. By early April, 89 indigenous people were killed by Covid-19 in the state.
7dde3f7fce4b51b34f53e44a7f9170b307d7247f: Terena leaders reported that 200 indigenous people living in the Aldeinha community, in undemarcated land, were left out of priority vaccination against Covid-19. According to Terena Edmilson George, “the city has greatly reduced territorial space. We live upstairs, where it's not recognized by Funai, but we're all documented by the organ. And even we voted in the election to chief”. Families on land without demarcation also arrived at the site in 1933, when Aldeinha was founded. The leaders denounced the case to the MPF and the DSEI in Campo Grande. In the region, several indigenous people refused to take the vaccines, believing in the false news that circulates about the effects of immunizers; these 200 and many other indigenous residents in urban areas were deprived of the right to be vaccinated.
97e8a7061e77d0876d43cb6a15751b58e09cb6af: Tired of the omission of the government, especially in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic, a group of indigenous people held a protest against chaos in health in Dourados. Representatives of the Bororó and Jaguapirú communities asked for the resignation of the local coordinator of Sesai, Sidneide Alves, who, according to the leaders, would refuse to attend the indigenous who seek a solution to the serious health situation in the territory. They report suffering due to the lack of supplies, medications and care, including lack of basic equipment for the protection of health workers. Another complaint regarding the administration of the District was related to the misuse of the fleet of vehicles of the base pole of the Sesai, which consists of a true “cemetery” of cars that should meet the indigenous villages, and that are deteriorating to the remote. They are trucks, motorcycles, cars, kombi and ambulances that are abandoned in the courtyard of the DSEI building. According to one of the indigenous leaders, who asked not to identify himself to the report of a local vehicle, the indigenous people “are tired of this omission and this neglect for the lack of vehicles to help the indigenous people, and when we arrive at the base pole we face this cemetery by car in the background, due to incompetence of management”. The MPF was triggered to follow the issue.
d600ef82224889cca18a9562ffd4a1c7e269b29f: Indigenous Guarani and Kaiowá occupied Casai in Amambai in protest for the omission and failure of the government in the face of the serious health situation faced by indigenous peoples in the state. The indigenous asked for the resignation of DSEI coordinator Joe Saccenti Junior, and also local coordinator of Sesai, Sidneide Alves. The indigenous denounced the poor management as a lack of adequate care in the villages, which have more than 18,000 people, lack of medicines and protective materials for health professionals, among other failures, such as abandoning several vehicles in the courtyard of the base polo.
aa0a31cd30ffd256599f945d5ad2c73b87495f4a: Indigenous people reported the disappearance of 1,300 doses of Covid-19 vaccine to the MPF. They reported that on April 23 the technical coordinator of the base pole traveled all the Basic Units of Indigenous Health (UBSI) of Dourados and collected all doses of vaccines, distributing a minimum quantity for each team of the Dourados reserve, an average of 30 doses, to be used in the campaign of the following day, April 24. According to the complaint, from April 26, all UBSI of the indigenous territory were without vaccine. The vaccines were taken to the base of Dourados, and only one nurse, who is coordinator, has access to the key to the refrigerator. The doses are only released according to the request made by the UBSI. However, after collecting information from health professionals in these units, there are indications that about 1,300 vaccines have disappeared, a number evidenced by the difference in the amount of doses applied and those taken to the base pole. The indigenous peoples are waiting to find out the facts and arrangements.
6728b3fb518eac27051614609aa93e66eb48cb5b: According to a survey conducted by the Public Agency in February, the Dourados State Penitentiary led Covid-19's national ranking of positive cases among the penitentiaries analyzed. By the beginning of February 2021, 1,236 cases of Covid-19 had been confirmed in this prison, which then had 2,380 people arrested. It is also in this prison that is the largest contingent of indigenous prisoners in the country – 164 people. Of these, the State Penitentiary Administration Agency confirmed that 86 indigenous people had had the disease in the unit until then. A criminal officer who refused to identify himself believes that contamination reached 90% of the inmates during the outbreak the previous year. He also reported that “the board did not know how to manage things” and that uniforms and protective equipment were missing for police officers, in addition to counting that, for prisoners, it is only mandatory to wear masks in the corridors, so that they are not used in cells and galleries.
5e82a8c739b63e687df2c6f1c1259cc6d63058cd: The MPF reported that the vaccination of indigenous people against Covid-19 failed in Mato Grosso do Sul, reaching only half of the population in some cities. The MPF made joint recommendation with the DPU and the DPE. In the recommendation, the MPF and the Defenders advise that health units should seek indigenous people who did not take the second dose of the vaccine, through mobile teams in the territories of origin and preferably outside the working hours of the indigenous. Failure to adopt the recommended measures may imply administrative measures and actions against public managers who do not.
f15829f19577cc38a9f459ccb0d48020ece856d6: In just 15 days, between December 2020 and January 2021, 410 indigenous people in Mato Grosso do Sul were infected by the coronavirus. In early January, the state already registered 3,453 confirmed cases of Covid-19 among indigenous peoples, according to Sesai data. The case cut-off was 14 to 29 December, when, of the 34 DSEIs, the DSEI Mato Grosso do Sul was the one with the highest number of cases of Covid-19. According to the Covid-19 Bulletin of the Secretariat, 72 deaths of indigenous people of the state caused by the disease had been recorded until the period mentioned.
496d1bb517f147bc3c48ee2f3b4ff3a6326af815: Given the omission and negligence of the government in relation to an adequate and dignified health policy for indigenous peoples, once again, leaders and representatives of these peoples returned to the DSEI in Campo Grande, in an attempt to dialogue with the special secretary of Indigenous Health at the time, Robson Santos da Silva, who traveled from Brasília to hear the demands. The indigenous continued to denounce the neglect of indigenous health and demand measures.
8671aee02366be3b749f79e578f73c1ec5e486d6: The indigenous population in Mato Grosso do Sul faced a serious outbreak of contamination by Covid-19. In the indigenous lands of Dourados, 89 cases of the disease were recorded in early November, representing a number 29 times greater than what is considered an outbreak. Tacuru was the second city with the highest incidence, recording 25 cases. Shortly behind came Paranhos (18), Caarapó (7), Japorã (6) and Amambai (5). In all, in the indigenous villages of Mato Grosso do Sul, a total of 4,725 cases were recorded between the beginning of the pandemic and the beginning of November 2021, with 106 deaths. The vaccination campaign in indigenous youth and adolescents began on September 29, one month after starting in the same public in urban areas of Mato Grosso do Sul. In live on October 29, the state Health Secretary, Geraldo Resende, said that the responsibility of the villages is the Ministry of Health, but that the SES was making itself available to help. “It is important that we say that these outbreaks, within the indigenous reserves, could have been avoided if we had started an immunization process within the indigenous communities at the same time as we started in the community in general,” the secretary said.
02681b70f5597b3f5f48b2c7e5fb4e2728745d56: Denial of rights in access to vaccination against Covid-19
a79606103de2824ae97d1bb81a1ca83122e52855: According to leaders and the MPF, an outbreak of Covid-19 cases took over the Jaguapiru and Bororó villages in Dourados, with a sum of 79 active positive cases by the beginning of November 2021. Of the 79 confirmed cases, ten generated hospitalizations, five in ICU beds and five in ward beds. One of the most serious health conditions was that of a teacher at the Guateka Marçal de Souza Indigenous State School in the village Jaguapiru, admitted to an ICU position in the health unit of Ponta Porã. The case was directly linked to the outbreak that began in reserve schools, with 34 positive cases. A total of 450 tests were performed, with approximately 260 of them directly linked to students, teachers, school servants and their families. Besides the increase in the number of cases, the community faced another serious problem: the vulnerability situation of the vast majority of infected people. This, as reported by indigenous leaders, causes many who tested positive to fail to comply with due and necessary isolation. Without being able to support themselves and without the help of the government, many work for daily lives and those few who have jobs and cannot miss “end up going to work even though they are positive of Covid, because they are in despair of being without money to eat. And we can't control it. We have an environment of total insecurity here”, warned an indigenous leader.
a73010c9be8ef7ff66bfcc10f4d6f7a6ea189647: The MPF set up a civil inquiry to determine the lack of care and insufficient provision of public health services in the Cabeceira and Brejão villages in Nioaque (MS). According to the complaint, the problem has been dragging since 2019 in the villages Taboquinha and Água Branca. Residents report that the most critical situation is in the village Brejão, where there is an urgent need for reform at the health center headquarters. The indigenous say that in the slab part, where the water box is, there are bats, generating strong odors throughout the building.
1e882dec878f2df8e3550ed1a35fd730a64a11a6: Report from the Portal De Olho in Ruralistas reports that former employees of the base pole of Sesai denounced persecution, militarization of the Sesai, moral harassment and lack of basic equipment to combat the pandemic between the Kaiowá and Guarani. The health professionals of Dourados warn that, in addition to layoffs, a series of arbitrary decisions by the management of the pole and the DSEI Mato Grosso do Sul has been damaging the structure of the region, responsible for the largest indigenous population in the country. The polo serves about 18,000 users of the subsystem, spread across villages in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve and three other municipalities. It also serves dozens of indigenous people displaced from its territory by agribusiness, who camp in tents on the roads and in the back of farms. Among the main complaints is the lack of transparency with the data of contamination and deaths of indigenous peoples by Covid-19. Employees and former employees of Sesai reveal that the information is no longer shared internally among professionals at the direction of the head of the pole, after the resignation of technical coordinator Indianara Guarani Kaiowá. A series of documents was prepared by the team that until then worked at the Base Pole of the Sesai in Dourados, to report to the MPF the lack of investment in basic equipment for the functioning of indigenous health. The team fired from the Golden Pole considers that an important part of the problem behind the disinvestment and authoritarian policy of the DSEI is in the organ management exchange, assumed by the reserve colonel Joe Saccenti Junior, appointed by the reserve colonel and then secretary of Sesai, Robson Santos da Silva.
1d625ed9bae1eaf7c189e4f59562339e858003ab: Chief Adenilson of France Santos, of the Kiriri community, denounces that his people were not contemplated with priority vaccination against Covid-19. He reports that the group is small and has been on site for four years, that they are always vaccinated against all other diseases, such as flu, measles and others, but that the state informed them that they were not registered to receive the Covid-19 vaccine. The health department of the municipality of Caldas reported that it had already informed the state health department about the need to send vaccines to the Kiriri, which are a priority group, according to the National Immunization Plan, but by the end of January there had been no return.
efa4e657421a00e37b875bef176820977faeee48: Failure and negligence of the government; denial of access to Covid-19 vaccine
1e6ebaca8109a08e90c689d8d2cddf7b02476cb5: With the lack of regularization of Aranã IT, Sesai recognized them as indigenous in an urban context and thus did not guarantee them vaccination against Covid-19 as a priority group, even if there was a decision by Minister Luís Roberto Barroso of the Supreme Court. According to the leaders, 17 Aranã families were infected with the virus and one person died. In response, Sesai offered basic baskets to families, even though this was not their demand. It was initiated by the MPF in June 2021, without response from Funai and Sesai until the end of the year.
78724652bfbca34430642e862fd465d5d982dec8: The indigenous people of Tembé people of TI Alto Rio Guamá, where young Isak was murdered, are having to live with “rain of poison”. This mechanism has been used by farmers in the region to spray large plantations, which have affected small farmers and the Tembé Indians, since they survive what the land supplies. On January 25, an illegal air dump hit TI Tembé and a camp for landless rural workers located in Santa Luzia do Pará. This “rain of poison” caused damage to the crops and respiratory problems, allergies and itching among indigenous and farmers. According to people who know the product, the sprayed poison is called Tordon, which “kills everything”. Environmental legislation prohibits the aerial application of pesticides in places where there are communities, housing and transit of people, the minimum distance is 500 meters from these environments. Denunciation was forwarded to the competent bodies and the Paraense Society for the Defense of Human Rights, which required measures from the Secretariat of Public Security and lifting of environmental permits.
8cf67b8c497f584e42b943be1ac2a426fdfca93e: Research conducted by neurologist Erik Jennings, physician of Sesai, points out that mercury used in illegal gold mining contaminates 99% of Munduruku villages in Alto Tapajós. According to the doctor, the survey conducted with 109 indigenous people showed that 99% of the population examined had mercury levels in the blood far above the WHO recommended; some had up to 15 times higher than recommended. The damage to the health of indigenous peoples, including future generations, is very serious. The high mercury index in the blood of women of childbearing age is very dangerous, because in a pregnancy it directly affects the neurological system of children. Mercury can cause irreversible damage to the nervous system, heart and thyroid problems, as well as affecting the immune system of babies. For the doctor, “it is a health emergency in Brazil”. Other studies have already been conducted in other regions of Pará, also affected by illegal mining, such as the medium Tapajós, where the research was conducted by the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation in partnership with WWF. In it, of the 200 indigenous people who participated, 58% had mercury levels above the WHO recommended. In one of the villages, the level of contamination reached 87%, and more than 15% of the children under 5 years of age analyzed had neurodevelopment problems. Based on the results of the research, the leadership Alessandra Korap Munduruku has reported against projects that impact Munduruku territory, such as mining – problems aggravated by the policy of the current President of the Republic. According to Alessandra, “this contamination is very serious. The Munduruku people are sick, and we need to take care of them, their children, many pregnant women; it is very sad”. And complete: “There must be punishment, for they (the prospectors) are killing us. (...) The fish are dying contaminated. The women are poisoned. Now we have proof”.
3f16dd358a289af0c05ac535fc352da2b06abdfe: Use of mercury in mining and environmental contamination
fa029e9b060a8e4132fe54df7ed1907968f0e699: In the middle of the new coronavirus pandemic, Funai supported Canadian mining company Belo Sun Mining to hold face-to-face meetings with about a hundred indigenous people in two villages in the Amazon. The company, based in Toronto, Canada, sought to accelerate its plans to explore a gold mine that can directly affect two indigenous lands and riverside communities that already live under the impact of the construction of the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant on the Xingu River, Pará. The activities planned by Belo Sun would gather about 45 indigenous people in the IT Arara da Volta Grande do Xingu, and 60 to 66 participants in the IT Paquiçamba. The DPU recommended Funai to reject the possibility of any face-to-face meeting during the pandemic and to suspend the effects of a technical report that the indigenist agency issued on February 10, in which it gives some guidance, but does not veto the mining initiative. It even suggests what the mining company should do “in case of confirmation or suspicion of any Covid-19 case during the event”, indicating that “the case detected will be immediately isolated from the group and will have the proper referral articulated by the health professional present at the site”. Funai also says that the mining company should request “support to private laboratories” and recommended that, before the presentation meetings of the IC-EIA (indigenous component of the environmental impact study), meetings should be scheduled by videoconferencing, preferably with the presence of indigenous representatives, “to articulate the preparations for meetings with the region’s DSEI”. The indigenist agency suggested that if the support of the DSEI was not possible, the mining company could “request support from private laboratories and/or other professionals”. According to the data presented by the mining company itself, the disease had killed, until last January, 7,366 residents in Pará – data that left out the great wave of the disease that reached, in the beginning of 2021, almost all Brazilian states.
9378516539ad5a4b21e7822a63143d4180727dfb: Omission and connivance of the government; face-to-face meeting with miner in the middle of the pandemic
ae0f0651b43edd808747825cd70641207677c32b: Sesai sent a letter to the Attorney General's Office informing that the spread of false news in Pará villages affected the indigenous decision to take the Covid-19 vaccine. In the letter, Sesai reported that about 70% of the indigenous people in the Tapajós region became undecided or refused to take the vaccine. According to Sesai, the refusal was due to the circulation of false news in the villages about vaccines. The MPF is investigating the case. Prosecutor Gustavo Kenner reports that these false news affects the integrity of indigenous peoples and endangers the health of peoples. He still asks: “We now want to identify exactly who the authors of these messages are and whether it is a ‘mere’ irresponsibility of those who have propagated the information, or worse, if it is a deliberate strategy to endanger the integrity of this group, which could ultimately confirm even genocide.” According to DSEI Tapajós, they had been registered in the region until the beginning of April 2021, 2,082 cases of Covid-19 and 17 deaths.
71974c3f8bcb1673b4e33357d50d718d53beb95b: In mid-2020, Apib and other entities judged ADPF 709 in order to combat the omission of the federal government in confronting the pandemic, demanding that the STF determine measures against the risk of genocide of various peoples. Among other requests, the action required the Supreme Court to determine whether the federal government would install sanitary barriers in more than 30 territories where indigenous peoples live in voluntary isolation or of recent contact, among which is the Zo’é IT – located in an area bordering the Flota Trombetas. The request was received by rapporteur Minister Luís Roberto Barroso and confirmed by the full STF. However, in opposition to the guarantee of isolation of indigenous peoples, on May 31, the Institute of Forest Development and Biodiversity of the State of Pará (Ideflor-Bio) determined the reopening of the State Forest Trombetas. Information obtained by the MPF realizes that the decision on the reopening of this state forest was taken after a meeting between the state government and leaders of the extractive sector of the region. The reopening of Flota Trombetas represents a very serious risk to the Zo’é people, because the activity performed by chestnut collectors, for example, occurs in the region called Jaramacaru, southern region of the limits of TI Zo’É. The decision of Ideflor-Bio expressly contemplates the Zo’é base (called Jaramacaru). Until that moment, measures of social isolation, with due protection to indigenous people, as well as the closure of areas bordering their territories, worked satisfactorily in the region. Therefore, by authorising the opening of Flota Trombetas, the state of Pará could cause the risk of contamination of the Zo’é people and all the consequences arising therefrom. Thus, the MPF-PA requested that the decision to allow access to the region be reviewed and that information be presented on the technical and scientific criteria that supported the decision of the state government to reopen the State Forest Trombetas, and whether there was an assessment of the risks of contamination by coronavirus for the Zo’é people due to the reopening of the Flota.
049cc76037f128051423875e01964ff9447efaa8: Opening area near IT for movement of people in the pandemic
b8e113fe107176c72def76a20199ae86ccde9e46: Due to the federal government's refusal to include indigenous people in the urban context in the emergency vaccination plan against Covid-19, the MPF made a recommendation to the municipality of Belém and the state of Pará regarding the vaccination of the Warao indigenous peoples from Venezuela. The MPF reports that the sociocultural peculiarities experienced by the indigenous group, especially those in an urban environment, as happens in Belém (PA), put them in a situation of greater vulnerability in relation to the transmission of the coronavirus. These indigenous people live most of the time in groups, sharing the same utensils, in a scenario of greater transmission of the virus; in addition, a number of sociocultural, epidemiological and conjunctural particularities of the Warao population intensify the risk of contamination and the impacts of Covid-19, mainly due to the intense circulation in urban centers as a guarantee of survival, as well as the epidemiological fragility of the indigenous people. The MPF-PA recommended that the Street Consultancy Network, a service linked to the Municipal Health Department of Belém, include the Warao population among the priority population for vaccination. The MPF-PA also recommended that all the necessary logistics be offered for vaccination to occur in shelters and rented houses where both the indigenous sheltered and the homeless live; or alternatively, that transportation be organized and made available to send the indigenous to the vaccination sites.
e710d736fa57e583a1ec355038a15f2d22038a7c: The MPF-PA recommended that Sesai complete the bidding process for the hiring of common engineering services to maintain water supply systems in indigenous villages served by the DSEI Guamá-Tocantins. A civil inquiry was initiated based on the communication of lack of maintenance in water supply systems in the villages belonging to the base pole of Captain Poço; lack of maintenance of a car used in patient care logistics; deficiency in the number of professionals of the multidisciplinary team who provide assistance to the community; and lack of inputs and equipment for the administrative team of the area. In a meeting held on March 2 with the MPF, indigenous leaders emphasized that the solution for the maintenance of the sanitary system and water supply in the communities of IT Alto Rio Guamá did not contemplate the expansion of existing networks, necessary to avoid improvisation in water supply.
d953a51e68f3c75e0fd247f49e629bbeb274a044: The indigenous peoples of the Altamira region in Pará denounce serious situations of failure. Absence of water supply systems in the villages; lack of qualified health professionals to endure in the villages; few beds available for indigenous people in the reference hospitals; delays in consultations and difficulties in performing specialized examinations. 31e40da55e3cf25df02e808e6f50ad4526570504: Lack of water and health care
1e8133ee16affea1d68b89ec2d2015c1acf6e36e: Sesai, through the DSEI Potiguara, refused to vaccinate against Covid-19 the indigenous people who live in the cities, claiming that the vaccine was only for the indigenous people living in the villages, highlighting that their vaccination was the responsibility of the municipalities. The Organization of Indigenous Residents in the Urban Zone of the municipality of Baía da Traição (Tab’usuabá) forwarded a representation to the MPF of Paraíba to make arrangements for this neglect. On April 7, 2021, the MPF of Paraíba instituted administrative procedure and provided Sesai and the DSEI Potiguara, requesting the inclusion in the priority vaccination plan of indigenous residents in urban areas, establishing a period of 10 days for the organs to pronounce themselves. However, the indigenous peoples of the city were not included in vaccination by Sesai and had to wait for the vaccination schedule of the municipalities where they live.
f83b9dacc76017b076bf3af364f9dc69608c5397: Denial of the right to vaccination against Covid-19
635fac5a6104fbf621389bdff10e2355ff40a470: The Tabajara Taquara Indigenous Association, which represents the indigenous Tabajara who live in the cities of Conde and Pitimbu, entered with a representation in the MPF of Paraíba requesting that the agency take steps in relation to the Sesai, which refused to include the group in the emergency vaccination plan against Covid-19. 8d0c4ad998e219b978decce4b93864578ac72d10: Denial of vaccination rights against Covid-19
afc289d136964d649040d300d3541eb68bb26772: The leaders of Tekoha Yhovy prepared a document reporting that, due to some indigenous people having contracted the coronavirus, they asked Sesai to hire at least temporarily three nurses and another doctor to meet the demand of the 15 Tekoha in that region. In the document, they also requested the sending of PPE to health workers.
0c00672a8bdc9bd831771fc9e11ca0cdb3fa9f01: The indigenous group Angico Pankararu, resident in Petrolândia (PE), had to resort to the Federal Court to ensure his right to vaccination against Covid-19. Even with the clear determination of Minister Luís Roberto Barroso, of the Supreme Court, on March 17, 2021, that both indigenous villagers and residents in unholy areas had priority in vaccination against Covid-19, the 40 indigenous families Angico Pankararu are not being able to enforce their right to immunization. According to the coordinator of the DSEI in Pernambuco, Antônio Fernandes da Silva, “the Union has no obligation to serve all indigenous peoples by the DSEI, only the villagers, the others must look for SUS in the city halls”. In turn, the mayor of Petrolândia, Fabiano Marques, argues that “what the city can do has done”. The manager avoids any responsibility by stating that the vaccination of indigenous peoples depends on the definition of the DSEI, which tells the Municipal Health Secretariat how many and where the indigenous are, so that the corresponding doses of vaccines are requested. The MPF opened an administrative procedure and notified the coordination of Funai in Paulo Afonso and the DSEI in Pernambuco, asking them to inform the reasons why the indigenous people were not vaccinated and questioning the forecast for this to occur.
e2a9bc03ea4158f768c8c39608f0d8940b666218: Denial of the right to priority vaccination
e81e547351a2e165708f1495ad75783b12c76526: After receiving complaint from Cimi and other organizations that the about 180 indigenous Atikum residents of Agrovila Brigida had not been immunized against Covid-19, the MPF triggered the Federal Justice, and obtained injunction in favor of these indigenous peoples. The justification of DSEI Pernambuco and the municipality of Orocó for not providing vaccination was the non-finalization of the process of demarcation of the indigenous land by the competent authorities. Even after dispatch of recommendation by the MPF, on May 21, to the Orocó Prefecture, the DSEI and the Pernambuco Health Secretariat, vaccination of indigenous people living in the area of the municipality, including the Atikum Brigida people, was not provided. The Attorney of the Republic, Rodolfo Lopes, argues that “although the land occupied by the indigenous people of the Atikum Brigida community is not officially indigenous land or reserve area, the community exists and lives in a traditional way, as the Federal Constitution requires”. As stated in the action, the indigenous peoples of the community are recognized by Funai, appearing on the site of the foundation itself as inhabitants of one of the “Indian Lands of Lower São Francisco”. The MPF highlights that the legislation on social protection measures to prevent the contagion and spread of Covid-19 in indigenous territories covers indigenous peoples isolated and of recent contact, indigenous villagers and indigenous people living outside indigenous lands, in urban or rural areas. In the action, the prosecutor of the Republic also cited the decision of the Supreme Court in the scope of ADPF 709, which determined priority in vaccination also of indigenous peoples located in unapproved lands.
7d9ff9caa2c334cde888ec56403a8ad655ebb284: Failure and negligence of the government; denial of the right to priority vaccination
e881c43dc375366eef7bfb024c7f4add4b99f76e: Sesai cancelled the agreement signed for water supply project to the community, claiming dependence on the verdict in the trial of the time frame in the STF in RE 1,017,365/SC, as well as the vote in the National Congress of PL 490/2007 and its additions. Leaderships report that the fact leaves the community in a situation of risk and vulnerability in the process of food production, subsistence and drinking water consumption. 207cd6b9d9e23feb05a14de65b6726f62b1354f8: The state of Piauí is one of the only ones that do not have DSEI for the care of indigenous peoples, so that people depend on care with the state and municipalities, which weakens health care. Regarding the vaccination of indigenous peoples of Piauí against coronavirus, it only occurred through action of the State Health Secretariat and not by Sesai. 22e910c2fe90cf27e6ed500c2a487d60da90caa2: More than half of the Guarani Mbya indigenous people, who live on the Green Coast of Rio de Janeiro, in Angra dos Reis, were infected by the coronavirus. The Mbya add up to about 350 people and 203 of them have had the disease since the start of the pandemic. According to Angra dos Reis Prefecture, until January 06, 2021, 200 indigenous people recovered from the disease, 1 died and 2 cases are still under investigation. 082af096b0a7a8a426999dde41169c97c26768f6: More than 12,000 indigenous peoples from the states of Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte remained outside the priority vaccination group, provided for in the National Immunization Plan. The Plan defined as a priority group “indigenous living in indigenous lands (i.e. demarcated by Funai) aged 18 years or more, assisted by the Indigenous Health Care Subsystem”, and in accordance with the DSEIs. However, neither Rio Grande do Norte nor Piauí have their own DSEI and no indigenous land has been demarcated. According to Dinaman Tuxá, from Apib, the lack of demarcation of indigenous territories in the northeast is the result of the omission of the State. “The Northeast is the second region with the largest indigenous population in Brazil, behind the North, but the last in terms of demarcation.” What was requested of the Brazilian government” is to ensure vaccination of the indigenous, regardless of the territorial situation”, reinforced Dinaman. The MPF was triggered to intervene in these cases.
a28c8650ce7213f8a542ae185f6a3e185a6fbb96: The absence of DSEI in the State of Rio Grande do Norte for the care of indigenous peoples deepens the situation of social vulnerability, preventing health care, affecting numerous indigenous families of the following peoples: Caboclos de Assu, Potiguara do Catu, Potiguara do Sagi/Trabanda, Potiguara - Mendonça, Potiguara Ibirapi, Tapuia Tarairiú and Warao.
0d71fc774208c7250fe529c24c76d62f106f3bd7: Fundamentalist churches with access to villages have influenced indigenous peoples in the largest territory of the state to reject vaccination against Covid-19. The indigenous claim religious beliefs and claim that the application of the vaccine is not necessary or, even worse, is evil. According to the Municipal Health Department of Lieutenant Portela, around 1.2 thousand indigenous people living in the reserve area corresponding to the municipality should be vaccinated. However, until February, less than half of this group attended health centers to receive the first dose. In an attempt to convince them to vaccinate, Sesai reported that it would send teams to the indigenous homes and apply the doses instead of waiting for them to attend the village health center.
bafdca2e5e12147b4895a6153e87bf3d74320b1f: Due to the fact that the Ministry of Health did not include indigenous peoples in an urban context, who do not live in a village, among the priority groups for immunization against Covid-19, contrary to scientific studies and the principle of equality among indigenous peoples, it was necessary for the MPF to prosecute a public civil action. The objective was to force the Union and the state of Rio Grande do Sul to provide vaccination against Covid-19 of the “non-aldeate” indigenous residents in the state, with the same priority established for the “village” indigenous people. The units of the MPF in the cities of Passo Fundo and Porto Alegre followed in administrative procedures the situation of indigenous people in an urban context to which priority vaccination was denied by the Ministry of Health, under the argument that these indigenous people would be subjected to the same social, environmental and access to health services of other people living in urban areas. They are on a provisional basis, as they maintain a link with the original communities, visiting them when they can. Its immunological and epidemiological specificities remain unchanged in relation to the villagers, including because contact with them is frequent, as confirmed by studies from the Federal University of Pelotas and Fiocruz. Likewise, the distinction between indigenous villagers and non-salted for vaccination purposes is not based on the anthropological and epidemiological approach, as well as the Federal Constitution and the ILO Convention 169 do not allow this differentiation, which violates the principle of equality between indigenous peoples. In practice, the non-aldeates have always had their specific medical care denied by Sesai, being in a situation of institutional invisibility, since they are not registered in the Indigenous Health Care Information System (SIASI), a problem that took on more serious contours with the exclusion of the priority group for vaccination against Covid-19.
c76f22f8383de0be4106c80abaeaed8900cdf956: The DSEI Rondônia questioned the Secretary of Health of Rondônia on the “missing” of 8,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccine in January 2021. According to the DSEI, the state received 11,120 doses of immunizer, but passed only 2,315 doses to indigenous peoples that month. 1e06c5d1f41fde75d81a1fcfa81c0c056ef083f1: According to Coiab, until the beginning of April 2021, the number of indigenous peoples with Covid-19 in Rondônia reached 2,470 and 62 suspected cases, under investigation. In the state, 51 deaths occurred until April, according to Coiab.
3741b893779ee55ca6189fb9d0be144cc79d320b: Several indigenous people who live both in villages and in an urban context report that they have not obtained public health care. They claim that they seek help for health care, without success, and in cases of very urgent need to pay for the consultation and laboratory tests and medications. When the indigenous people who live in the villages get sick and need help, they go through great difficulties, often without getting around, because the villages are very far from the city. When they get care and hospitalizations for a few days, when they are discharged, they go to Casai, and then return to the villages. However, as most of the times the visits are not effective, the patients resume with the symptoms and return to this vicious circle of comings and goings. The indigenous requested measures from the MPF-RO.
4f1e30d084b4ad6d0bf80ed83ee3e18255d248d3: The chief of the village Soterius forwarded a document to the MPF denouncing the neglect of Sesai. The indigenous Diva Oro No and Arlete Oro They are not suffering from much pain in the womb; there are reports that they seek care and are referred to the city for treatment. Later, they return to the village without a more appropriate treatment to the clinical picture presented. Patients complain about returning pain and are referred to the city again. They stay a few days in Casai and return to the village without the treatment completed. It is always a vicious circle, a going and coming exhausting and painful, without adequate treatment for the indigenous. It was diagnosed that they need to perform myoma surgery, however, with Casai's slowness, there is still no result and no referral.
a06179ed41d931d18425cfa8f27f33b86eb4a5be: The various indigenous peoples of the Guajará-Mirim region living in urban context reported being excluded from the priority group for vaccination against Covid-19. 6f4addbc6cb20bf32a07b20a28275ec4ac3a418c: The indigenous Coin’ Oro Mon had been presenting eye problems, with great difficulty to see. On several occasions, he asked Sesai for consultations. Since he could not get care through Sesai, he had to pay to be attended, with the help of friends and the community, as well as to buy the medicines and do the tests. Due to the delay and neglect of the government regarding referrals to their treatment, the indigenous ended up losing sight, and today it depends on the children, family and friends to get around and do daily activities. Several complaints regarding the lack of health care for indigenous peoples have already been made to the MPF and responsible bodies, but without provision.
925b462ee2c649f065be1d92d12c22b1b7905ab3: The indigenous Mijai Oro Mon presented severe intestinal obstruction, but has not been able to obtain specialized consultation by Sesai. The family is concerned about the risk of the situation getting even worse.
7df7732408916e90e4f8f0a7a626bc5eea6beda3: The representatives of 14 indigenous peoples living in the city of Costa Marques (Guarasugwe, Cujubin, Migueleno, Puruborá, Canoé, Wayoro, Cassupá, Aruá, Chiquitano, Kwazá, Sakirabiar, Tupari, Makurap and Parintintin) denounced, once again, that Sesai, the base of Ji-Paraná, continues its practice of abandoning and denying rights in indigenous health care to peoples in urban context, using the same argument of not being able to serve indigenous residents in the cities. The indigenous people have already referred the complaint and claim to the MPF and Sesai, however, no provision has been made.
f9e5d2c335d6c31b1d0501d124e0f8bff9a402cb: The number of cases of malaria increases 66% among indigenous people in Guajará-Mirim, from January to September 2021, compared to the same period of the previous year, according to data from the Epidemiological Surveillance Information System. According to Casai, despite this increase, no death has been recorded for the disease for many years, and despite the high rate among the indigenous, no patient was admitted to the city at the end of this period. Treatment is done in the villages themselves.
12c77229b548b0987338a94b83060848cb7dc90e: Practically abandoned by the government during the Covid-19 pandemic, and experiencing all kinds of suffering, including the psychological, CIR leaders mobilized to seek care for indigenous people. Countless life stories that were interrupted by illness and caused suffering to mothers, children, fathers, wives, husbands, brothers, friends. “All this that we are living has shaken the psychological of indigenous families, especially for those with children. We do not have assistance; I at least did not have psychological assistance, neither I nor my children, our family member died, and no one is caring about what you are going through,” said Rita de Cássia Macuxi, a resident of the Sol Nascente community, in the municipality of Pacaraima, in Roraima. “Who is losing their relatives is staying for that,” he pointed. Sesai and state or municipal governments, with hospital networks and health centers, at best, only offer primary health care. A psychological assistance service for survivors and family members of the pandemic was never considered throughout Brazil. By perceiving the vulnerability of the native peoples, the CIR decided to provide psychological assistance to families affected by the pandemic. The search has been huge. Between April 2020 and March 2021, more than 220 psychological consultations were performed. In addition to psychological care in communities, information leaflets on mental health, in Portuguese and in the Wapichana language are provided. Indigenous psychologists have done this work in the villages, such as Macuxi Iterniza Pereira, who reports: “we work with awareness, we offer this psychological support because they are people who were not able to cope with all this situation, many indigenous families were diagnosed with panic syndrome, became more anxious, had indigenous families who went into depression.” Since the beginning of the pandemic, indigenous peoples have suffered daily and collective mourning. In Roraima, by mid-April, 5,674 cases and 120 deaths had been confirmed among the Macuxi, Pemon, Taurepangue, Wai, Wapichana and Yanomami peoples, as well as Warao, indigenous immigrants from Venezuela. As if the pain of loss were not enough, they still have to fight against the social and cultural impacts that have been affecting their traditions, such as breaking up the farewell ritual, because families were not able to do the wakes. Leadership reports that not even after a year of pandemic, with all deaths and confirmed cases, authorities were able to create a humanized care plan aimed at indigenous peoples.
5177058e8d3016cd5fbabf72bc198f41f67d4a42: The photo of an 8-year-old Yanomami girl, published by Folha de São Paulo on May 9 and reproduced by the national and international press, exposed the cruel lack of assistance to indigenous people in the country. Only five days after the photo was published, the girl was removed from the Maimasi community, a region of difficult access in the Amazon forest, to Hospital Santo Antônio, in Boa Vista. The girl is between 7 and 8 years old and had already been diagnosed with malaria, pneumonia, verminosis and malnutrition. It was Carlo Zacquini of the Catrimani Mission who released the photo, without revealing the authorship to avoid reprisals. According to the missionary, he had been receiving confidences for a few months about the situation of the Yanomami IT, but stated that no one was willing to speak out of fear. He's been in the region assisting the Yanomami since 1968 and says: “These villages are abandoned. All of them without assistance. There are no teams. The team is destitute of people. There are health centers that have been closed for months in the Yanomami Land.” According to Dário Kopenawa Yanomami of HAY, there is an outbreak of malaria in the region, which implies other diseases, such as malnutrition; “the fight against malaria is hampered by a lack of health professionals. This photo of our relative who's circulating shows our vulnerability. The federal government is not concerned with the problems we face today ", completed. Kopenawa reported that malaria and other diseases in the region have been attributed to the advance of illegal mining. Since 2020, indigenous people have reported an increase in Covid-19 infection within Yanomami IT and illegal mining, which causes forest devastation. Numerous complaints have been made to defense and control agencies, but the devastation of the territory and the abandonment of Yanomami people only increases.
e8c8e4e0edbc60321134b6d0bc30cf8c4a918ca0: A study carried out by the GT Saúde Indígena/Abrasco and published on May 17 points out that the number of malaria cases among Yanomami indigenous peoples during the pandemic has increased. The study highlights that this growth of the disease is associated with increased mining activities in the region. In 2020, 19,000 cases were registered in DSEI Yanomami, which means that, in this period, approximately 67% of the population of 28,141 people from DSEI was affected. The technical note was produced at the request of Apib and presented under ADPF 709. According to the data, between 2005 and 2014, 41.6 thousand cases of malaria were recorded in Yanomami territory, with an average of 4.1 thousand cases per year. Growth is impressive: only in the first five months of 2021, 5.1 thousand cases had already been recorded. The researcher and coordinator of the TG Indigenous Health, Ana Lúcia Pontes, sees the situation as worrying given the high vulnerability rate that these populations find themselves, and states: “Malaria, in this case, comes as an aggravating factor, particularly in children’s health, which has already presented an unfavorable health situation. Malaria, malnutrition, worms added to the context of the pandemic worry us enormously.” Another aggravating factor, put in the technical note, reports the complaint of the Pro-Yanomami Network and Ye’kwana that in combat missions to Covid-19, in 2020, the federal government made wide distribution of chloroquine in the Yanomami villages. It is noteworthy that the use of chloroquine does not bring benefits to the prevention or treatment of Covid-19, and that its use for the proper treatment of malaria needs to be done in conjunction with other medications such as primaquine, which has not been distributed in these actions. The document also refers to the impacts of mining activities on the health of indigenous peoples, particularly Yanomami (RR) and Munduruku (PA), regarding exposure to mercury. The note highlights the chronic malnutrition problems found in children and presents an overview of the impacts of the pandemic and vaccination coverage against Covid-19 on Yanomami and Munduruku peoples; in addition, it highlights the conflicts and attacks of prospectors on Yanomami and Munduruku leaders, showing the importance of the removal of invaders and protection of the indigenous population by the competent authorities.
1cc7657425408f1401833ca9f03a309a223661fb: According to complaints from HAY, health team professionals from DSEI-YY would be applying doses of Covid-19 vaccines in prospectors for gold. These facts were recorded in the Homoxi region of the Uxiu community. HAY forwarded a trade to DSEI-YY, Sesai and MPF. The Joint Parliamentary Front in defense of the rights of indigenous peoples presented the complaint to the Senate's ICP that established the responsibilities in confronting Covid-19 in Brazil.
aedc9699c4ee22f04814f98cb8f5a3c86ff57e08: Health care at Yanomami IT, the responsibility of Sesai through DSEI-YY, presents very serious problems of planning, execution of programs and activities, as well as the lack of transparency in the application of resources, supply of medicines and food at health centers and at the base poles and working conditions for health teams. The result is a collapse and abandonment of health care actions and their impacts, associated with the presence of mining in the region, very serious for the Yanomami population. Without a consistent Emergency Plan to confront Covid-19 during the year 2020, the pandemic extended to Yanomami IT regions. According to Sesai data, 22 Yanomami Indians would have died because of Covid-19 in 2020. However, these data may be underreported. According to a survey by a group of entities and supporters of the Yanomami and Ye’kwana peoples, the number of indigenous peoples infected and deceased by Covid-19 in this IT could reach up to twice the official records. From 26 to 31 January 2021, according to Condisi, ten Yanomami children from the Waphuta, Kataroa and Taremou villages died with Covid symptoms. DSEI-Y sent a health team to the scene only a week after the events. The Ministry of Health reported in August that the children had died from diarrhea and vomiting, not from Covid, without presenting evidence of the conclusions. In addition to the Covid-19, other sensitive health indicators have presented worsening data in recent years, related to the increased presence of mining in the region. Malaria cases had quadrupled in the period 2014-2019, according to the report “Cicatrizes da Floresta”, a fact associated with the expansion of forest degradation. According to data from the DSEI-Y Epidemiological Bulletin, 23,293 cases of malaria were registered in 2020. By August 2021 there were 16,982 confirmed cases. The number can be much higher, as there are deficiencies in the application of malaria tests in communities. The health centers (Polos Base and Basic Units of Indigenous Health) are shortages of medicines such as chloroquine, a medicine used by the federal government since 2020 to disseminate false recommendations in the fight against the pandemic. Health teams often do not have fuel to move to the villages and are concentrated in the Base Poles. The treatment of malaria cannot be administered with the regularity and continuity it needs. The indicators of malnutrition in the region also increased. Studies by Unicef and Fiocruz had already pointed out in 2020 that 54% of Yanomami children aged 0 to 5 years had some symptom of malnutrition, a number that could reach 80% in some regions. In March 2021, the MPF-RR judged Public Civil Action requesting Sesai to guarantee food supply for patients and companions within the Base Pole and the Basic Indigenous Health Units. Sesai argued that her responsibility was only to supply Casai with food in Boa Vista. In early November, companies providing air services to DSEI-Y suspended flights on account of a debt of R$ 7 million by Sesai. With regard to resources, the figures are not transparent. Sesai claims to have invested more than R $ 180 million in DSEI-Y. It is evident that this money is not being fully and efficiently invested in health care for Yanomami and Ye’kwana peoples. Despite the widespread chaos in the health care of these peoples, Funai prevented, in November 2021, the entry of a multidisciplinary health team from Fiocruz that intended to verify the situation, support the care and start studies of water contamination by mercury and impacts on the health of Yanomami. In a hearing at the CDHM of the House of Representatives, on November 24, the president of Funai justified this impediment of Fiocruz’s entry saying that “there is already a public body, Sesai, who is doing his work very well”. The MPF-RR entered with Civil Civil Action in March 2021 with a request to injunction for Sesai to ensure the supply of food products at health centers for patient and family care; the agency also issued a recommendation to the Ministry of Health and Sesai, demanding that within 90 days they present a plan to restructure health care for Yanomami and Ye’kwana peoples, resizing the framework of professionals, developing action plans to combat malaria and malnutrition and hiring an air service company. The STF determined, on November 17, that the Ministry of Health offer explanations on the health situation of the Yanomami and Ye’kwana peoples and the government’s action plans. The STF's decisions under ADPF 709 and the IACHR's Citizen's Measure, both of 2020, are still in force, in which they call on the Union to adopt all measures to ensure the health care of Yanomami and Ye'kwana peoples.

José Vane Guajajara was taken to the nearby hospital shortly after the incident, but was transferred to the hospital of Santa Inês, where he was denied care.
