e0e2bccdc43200b3cae1d3f01a431ebcd469377c: According to information from the indigenous leadership Ricardo Memortumré, two indigenous children in the village Escalvado died in November 2021, presenting symptoms of vomiting, diarrhea, mouth wounds and bleeding, and other children also had similar symptoms. The indigenous have not yet discovered the cause of this disease in children.
20563ba1639e03312ba8c997a91526e85f575b90: The 21-year-old indigenous girl died in the Bakairi TI in the Pacuera village. The Civil Police delegate received a call informing about the death and headed to the village in order to investigate the real cause of death. When talking to the young woman's relatives, the delegate was informed that three days earlier, the young woman had gone to the city for medical attention, because she was bleeding. She was medicated and released to return to the village; two days later, she returned to bleeding, resulting in her death. The delegate wondered if he could remove the body for necropsy procedure and identification of the cause of death, but the family did not consent, due to their customs and beliefs. Some family members and the nurse who accompanied the indigenous woman at home were intimidated to testify later. The case was registered with “death to be clarified, no evidence of crime”.
685bd2c4296c16511b5942dad048395e0fe9138e: The omission and negligence of the government in relation to the health care of indigenous populations throughout the country has been increasingly chaotic. This was sadly noted by the Xavante at Campinápolis Municipal Hospital. A baby of only eight months of age needed to be taken to medical care in this hospital. According to a nurse, the doctor orders the indigenous to be observed, most of the times they seek care. This was the procedure performed with the baby, which, even with a severe state of health, was observed. When he was treated, he had to be rushed to the hospital of the city of Água Boa, but unfortunately the baby did not resist the delay of care and died as soon as he arrived in the other municipality.
a14528a87e696009612948a5137690cf62d83c0d: According to Elciney Ciney, he lost his wife, Ruthe, and Raviel, his newborn son, due to alleged negligence at the Aquidauana Regional Hospital. Elciney published an account on social networks and now, in addition to having to deal with the pain of loss, he still needs to console the other four children of the couple, who lost their mother. He told her that his wife was almost 32 weeks pregnant when she had a bleeding and was taken to the hospital at 10:00 p.m. on March 12. Ruthe was 38 and graduated in pedagogy. She was active in the indigenous cause and known in the community for the resumption of traditional lands and the struggle for improvement in indigenous health. Elciney points out that the care failed at the hospital, but that in the village everything was done that was within reach. He says that, arriving at the hospital, the professionals identified that the baby's heartbeat was weak and that Ruthe needed an ultrasound. The problem is that there was no professional who handled the equipment in the hospital, according to the report. Eiciney stated that the professional only arrived the next day, in the morning, to the hospital. When ultrasound was performed, the couple were informed that the pregnant woman needed to undergo a cesarean section urgently, because the baby was dead and she had a clot. Elciney, inconsolable, said: “Here is the cause of the death of my baby and my wife Ruthe. If they had performed the ultrasound at the right time, at the right time, they would prove that the baby was breathing, had a heartbeat, but it was weak due to the rupture or detachment of the umbilical cord. Thus, they would do the cesarean section, saving two indigenous lives, the child and Ruthe”. Elciney will go to court to report the case, and the Aquidauana Regional Hospital has reported that it is investigating what happened. The City Council and a committee of the House may also conduct an investigation to determine whether there has been negligence.
978b99ad6571c2c55c559644c96f22ccdffa4602: The Maxakali community regretted the death of the 55-year-old indigenous, who presented health problems and did not receive adequate care. The information is that the cause of death was severe acute respiratory syndrome and pneumonia.
588203738b53ad2c24d474a8234f859d0bee7512: Several groups of Warao indigenous people, from Venezuela, circulate across various states and cities in Brazil. One of these groups arrived in Belo Horizonte and was welcomed into a shelter for homeless people. There are reports that, due to the poor conditions of this shelter, a child of the Warao group, only 1 year and 7 months, died of Covid-19. The sheltered group consists mostly of children and other cases of Covid-19 contamination have been reported. Refugees and indigenous activists denounce the situation of neglect and abandonment in the city, where pregnant women, children and adolescents live piled up, in an unhealthy place and without prospect of improvement. After the occurrence of this case, a welcoming committee for Warao indigenous people was created by the Belo Horizonte Prefecture.
dc0a15c338f9349996f72506b24c18c43c1e57fb: On returning from the village Ahussehe, around 12 p.m. on July 6, 2021, Awassameu Suruí suffered a motorcycle accident. As she fell, she was rescued by her husband and continued her journey for another seven kilometers until they reached the nearest village. When arriving in the village Ipiray, the husband took her to the health center, being immediately attended by the nurse of the Sesai who applied serum to her and did the first procedures. As the nurse verified the severity of the situation, she informed the Polo Coordinator and asked if she could remove it to the hospital in the city of São Geraldo in a private transport. However, such a request was denied and the victim was waiting for the official transport of the Sesai, which only arrived around 3:00 p.m. During the journey, with 18 km to reach the hospital, the indigenous woman did not resist and died.
5912ecdc28d1668aaee1a842b3ad4c7437979d75: Leadership denounces the lack of health for indigenous peoples in the Altamira region. In November, two indigenous people did not resist the delay of the Sesai to be removed from their villages and led to medical care. The indigenous people who died were the Araweté people, one from the village Ipixuna and the other from the village Aradyti.
3cb485d534d62f1a9ea2f581e714f0361e98f77b: The Piauí Collective denounced, in social network, the death of the baby Warao Euclide Moreno Mendoza, of only one month of life. The baby died due to an intestinal infection, in a shelter for Venezuelans in Teresina, coordinated by the Municipal Department of Citizenship, Social Assistance and Integrated Policies (Semcaspi). According to the Piauí Collective, Venezuelans do not receive medical follow-up; the parents of the baby speak and understand little Portuguese, and went alone to the public hospital. The Collective stated: “In a reference city in health as our capital, in a city with a medical mayor, an indigenous child under the care of his management died from diarrhea. Today, our relatives Warao weep for this life that lived so little time between us. Today, another Indian mother and father cry, because their baby is no longer in their arms”. Semcaspi confirmed the death of Euclide Moreno Mendoza, who was staying at the Emater shelter. The secretary informed that the mother of the baby, Sophia Maria Mendoza, 19, received all the necessary follow-up, including during the gestational period. However, the mother, Sophia, told her that she was not breastfeeding her child and would be offering a milk that was not compatible with her age. With medical advice, Semcaspi said it provided adequate milk and 13 days later the child presented intestinal infection. The parents returned with the baby to the UBS, where they were instructed to give paracetamol and simeticone, in addition to replacing the milk again. Euclid died the next day.
9a49b1337f5bdef3de0534051d0f126f3f6af4d7: One more indigenous child Warao died after a month in the hospital of Urgency of Teresina. Cheito Ramirez Mendonza, only 1 year and 7 months old, had identified as causes of death malnutrition, herpetic meningoencephalitis and bronchopneumonia. The MPF of Piauí instituted a procedure to determine the situation of vulnerability in which Venezuelan indigenous people live sheltered in Teresina. According to complaints, families are not receiving adequate health care, food and hygiene supplies. By June, another baby Warao had also died with the same symptoms due to lack of adequate feeding.
e2aff42e1e54a2e48217ff9879d0c4bd31fe62d9: Pietro, 2 years old, suffered from degenerative muscle disease and died on February 5. Jamila, 3 years old, had an asthma attack, was taken to the hospital, but did not resist and died on the 11th of the same month. Both children were of the Guarani Mbya people and left the entire community dismayed by his death.
ebea855342c0fe5b6cfca8fe006f9dd643556422: Patricia had been ill for more than two weeks and, according to information from the community, was accompanied by a Karai Kunhã. She had a lot of chest and breast pain. It is suspected that the indigenous woman died of breast cancer. This case reflects weaknesses in the care of the Sesai, in the lack of community actions in the prevention and monitoring of patients.
c1ccc5ea28574f7818820fe751aa40a440c92b32: The indigenous Too Tatrao had long been suffering from severe chest pain. She sought care and was sent to the city in Casai, where she remained for a few days. Sometimes she had to be hospitalized and then returned to the village without proper treatment. Several times she needed medication and tests, which she couldn't afford, and who collaborated were people from the community and Cimi. The last time her condition worsened considerably, Too was referred to Porto Velho, but did not resist and died. Failure and neglect in the area of health is one of the serious problems faced by indigenous peoples not only from Rondônia, but from all regions of Brazil.
79800d2d1be1a7ec9a1ee90e239e13009a1a3de6: The indigenous Orowao Pandran Oro Mon, 35 years old, from Sagaran IT, was studying at a university in Porto Velho. Orowao presented health problems and had to be admitted to the ICU of the Campaign Hospital set up in the eastern part of Porto Velho, which does not offer CT or hemodialysis services. Although the kidneys stopped working, for four days in a row the medical report did not mention renal failure. On the 5th day, the attending physician revealed the real picture of the Orowao and did not hide his surprise at the omission in the previous bulletins. The family members then triggered the MPF, which obtained a place in the ICU of the Hospital Samar, which has hemodialysis. However, this service was late. Orowao died a few hours after he was transferred. His mother said: “What killed my son was not only Covid-19, but also medical negligence.”
239c8035efa45d80728cdcddc5ec72e2094a15d8: Parturient Marcilene Oro Mon was already 42 weeks pregnant and arrived at Casai to have the baby. At Casai, they told her it wasn't time to deliver and that she would have to wait. A few days later, Marcilene felt that the baby was not moving and returned for service. Sonar was performed and the baby did not have a heartbeat. Birth of stillbirth was induced only after three days in the maternity ward, and the child was born deformed and smelled. The family and the whole community were outraged by the obvious medical neglect for postponing the induction of childbirth.
085bcbf09ae7a5983b649f64b871b6383de77c6c: Between September and November 2021, five children from 0 to 5 years of age died of malaria at Yanomami IT. All of them died due to the lack of health care provided by DSEI-Y. Many communities are very distant from the Basic Units of Indigenous Health and Base Poles and have not been present or visited by health teams for more than a year. In the case of the deceased child in the Ixaropi community, Hakoma region, the community had requested the presence of the health team for the high number of cases with malaria symptoms, but the team had declined from the visit, arguing that it was not allowed to perform this mission. In the village Xaruna, where two deaths of children from malaria occurred, the community information is that the number of sick children is very large and there is no medical care. On this occasion, the health team justified that the lack of fuel prevented her from moving to the region to monitor the situation. By early September, two children had died of malaria in the Parima region. In the Macuxi Yano community in October 2021, the village pajé died of malaria without care and in the Yaritopi community, a month later, a 17-year-old with falciparum malaria died. On November 30, a 19-year-old Yanomami from the village Paapiu died in labor with a seven-month pregnancy. The young woman had malaria and was not receiving treatment. One element that makes the situation of helplessness even more dramatic is that indigenous people are obliged to resort to illegal camp sites near their communities to communicate with DSEI-Y and request urgent care by health teams. Numerous complaint documents have been submitted by Condisi-Y and HAY to the relevant public bodies.
239a0defe28d56090a2b566d6220512536a467a1: The 26-year-old postnatal Xokleng Daniela Caxias died of Covid-19 in a hospital in Ibirama, in the Itajaí Valley (SC), on August 12. She was buried in Vitor Meireles, Figueira Village, TI Ibirama/La Klánno. Daniela suffered three cardiac arrests until her cerebral death, according to information from Sesai. She had her son on August 3 and the cesarean section occurred within normal limits. According to the secretary, she was discharged and returned home with her family. After five days, she began to experience the first symptoms of the disease. On August 8, she entered a health unit of Vitor Meireles (SC), but according to family members, she was released. At the time, Daniela had a positive result for Covid-19. No other family member of the victim tested for the disease. As soon as the clinical picture worsened, the indigenous woman was referred to Ibirama. The indigenous woman had no comorbidities and there is no information if she had been vaccinated. Daniela left her partner and two children, a newborn and a 6-year-old.
53a8f22aed2ad9826af17abcb07365edcbca9403: The pregnant woman went to the hospital of São Félix do Araguaia for the moment of delivery. At ultrasonography, it was found that the child was lifeless; even so, medication was applied to induce childbirth. After four days, the indigenous woman died.
cc5445b88f97b8a769d626b7bae98dad9e266b94: The iny-karajá community, dismayed, denounces the disregard of the DSEI Araguaia regarding indigenous health in general and the lack of care for a baby, who died at only three months of age in the village Santa Isabel do Morro. For more than 15 days, the baby had diarrhea. Without care, he lost strength and was affected by malnutrition.
